english: In the revealed scriptures, the ultimate object of knowledge is Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Personality of Godhead. The purpose of performing sacrifice is to please Him. Yoga is for realizing Him. All fruitive activities are ultimately rewarded by Him only. He is supreme knowledge, and all severe austerities are performed to know Him. Religion [dharma] is rendering loving service unto Him. He is the supreme goal of life.

sanskrit: saḥ eva idam sasarja agre bhagavān ātma māyayā sat asat rūpayā ca asau guṇa maya aguṇaḥ vibhuḥ
english: In the beginning of the material creation, that Absolute Personality of Godhead [Vāsudeva], in His transcendental position, created the energies of cause and effect by His own internal energy.

sanskrit: tayā vilasiteṣu eṣu guṇeṣu guṇavān iva antaḥ praviṣṭaḥ ābhāti vijñānena vijṛmbhitaḥ
english: After creating the material substance, the Lord [Vāsudeva] expands Himself and enters into it. And although He is within the material modes of nature and appears to be one of the created beings, He is always fully enlightened in His transcendental position.

sanskrit: yathā hi avahitaḥ vahniḥ dāruṣu ekaḥ sva yoniṣu nānā iva bhāti viśva ātmā bhūteṣu ca tathā pumān
english: The Lord, as Supersoul, pervades all things, just as fire permeates wood, and so He appears to be of many varieties, though He is the absolute one without a second.

sanskrit: asau guṇa mayaiḥ bhāvaiḥ bhūta sūkṣma indriya ātmabhiḥ sva nirmiteṣu nirviṣṭaḥ bhuṅkte bhūteṣu tat guṇān
english: The Supersoul enters into the bodies of the created beings who are influenced by the modes of material nature and causes them to enjoy the effects of these modes by the subtle mind.

sanskrit: bhāvayati eṣaḥ sattvena lokān vai loka bhāvanaḥ līlā avatāra anurataḥ deva tiryak nara ādiṣu
english: Thus the Lord of the universes maintains all planets inhabited by demigods, men and lower animals. Assuming the roles of incarnations, He performs pastimes to reclaim those in the mode of pure goodness.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca jagṛhe pauruṣam rūpam bhagavān mahat ādibhiḥ sambhūtam ṣoḍaśa kalam ādau loka sisṛkṣayā
english: Sūta said: In the beginning of the creation, the Lord first expanded Himself in the universal form of the puruṣa incarnation and manifested all the ingredients for the material creation. And thus at first there was the creation of the sixteen principles of material action. This was for the purpose of creating the material universes.

sanskrit: yasya ambhasi śayānasya yoga nidrām vitanvataḥ nābhi hrada ambujāt āsīt brahmā viśva sṛjām patiḥ
english: A part of the puruṣa lies down within the water of the universe, from the navel lake of His body sprouts a lotus stem, and from the lotus flower atop this stem, Brahmā, the master of all engineers in the universe, becomes manifest.

sanskrit: yasya avayava saṁsthānaiḥ kalpitaḥ loka vistaraḥ tat vai bhagavataḥ rūpam viśuddham sattvam ūrjitam
english: It is believed that all the universal planetary systems are situated on the extensive body of the puruṣa, but He has nothing to do with the created material ingredients. His body is eternally in spiritual existence par excellence.

sanskrit: paśyanti adaḥ rūpam adabhra cakṣuṣā sahasra pāda ūru bhuja ānana adbhutam sahasra mūrdha śravaṇa akṣi nāsikam sahasra mauli ambara kuṇḍala ullasat
english: The devotees, with their perfect eyes, see the transcendental form of the puruṣa who has thousands of legs, thighs, arms and faces — all extraordinary. In that body there are thousands of heads, ears, eyes and noses. They are decorated with thousands of helmets and glowing earrings and are adorned with garlands.

sanskrit: etat nānā avatārāṇām nidhānam bījam avyayam yasya aṁśa aṁśena sṛjyante deva tiryak nara ādayaḥ
english: This form [the second manifestation of the puruṣa] is the source and indestructible seed of multifarious incarnations within the universe. From the particles and portions of this form, different living entities, like demigods, men and others, are created.

sanskrit: saḥ eva prathamam devaḥ kaumāram sargam āśritaḥ cacāra duścaram brahmā brahmacaryam akhaṇḍitam
english: First of all, in the beginning of creation, there were the four unmarried sons of Brahmā [the Kumāras], who, being situated in a vow of celibacy, underwent severe austerities for realization of the Absolute Truth.

sanskrit: dvitīyam tu bhavāya asya rasātala gatām mahīm uddhariṣyan upādatta yajñeśaḥ saukaram vapuḥ
english: The supreme enjoyer of all sacrifices accepted the incarnation of a boar [the second incarnation], and for the welfare of the earth He lifted the earth from the nether regions of the universe.

sanskrit: tṛtīyam ṛṣi sargam vai devarṣitvam upetya saḥ tantram sātvatam ācaṣṭa naiṣkarmyam karmaṇām yataḥ
english: In the millennium of the ṛṣis, the Personality of Godhead accepted the third empowered incarnation in the form of Devarṣi Nārada, who is a great sage among the demigods. He collected expositions of the Vedas which deal with devotional service and which inspire nonfruitive action.

sanskrit: turye dharma kalā sarge nara nārāyaṇau ṛṣī bhūtvā ātma upaśama upetam akarot duścaram tapaḥ
english: In the fourth incarnation, the Lord became Nara and Nārāyaṇa, the twin sons of the wife of King Dharma. Thus He undertook severe and exemplary penances to control the senses.

sanskrit: pañcamaḥ kapilaḥ nāma siddheśaḥ kāla viplutam provāca āsuraye sāṅkhyam tattva grāma vinirṇayam
english: The fifth incarnation, named Lord Kapila, is foremost among perfected beings. He gave an exposition of the creative elements and metaphysics to Āsuri Brāhmaṇa, for in course of time this knowledge had been lost.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭham atreḥ apatyatvam vṛtaḥ prāptaḥ anasūyayā ānvīkṣikīm alarkāya prahlāda ādibhyaḥ ūcivān
english: The sixth incarnation of the puruṣa was the son of the sage Atri. He was born from the womb of Anasūyā, who prayed for an incarnation. He spoke on the subject of transcendence to Alarka, Prahlāda and others [Yadu, Haihaya, etc.].

sanskrit: tataḥ saptame ākūtyām ruceḥ yajñaḥ abhyajāyata saḥ yāma ādyaiḥ sura gaṇaiḥ apāt svāyambhuva antaram
english: The seventh incarnation was Yajña, the son of Prajāpati Ruci and his wife Ākūti. He controlled the period during the change of the Svāyambhuva Manu and was assisted by demigods such as His son Yāma.

sanskrit: aṣṭame merudevyām tu nābheḥ jātaḥ urukramaḥ darśayan vartma dhīrāṇām sarva āśrama namaskṛtam
english: The eighth incarnation was King Ṛṣabha, son of King Nābhi and his wife Merudevī. In this incarnation the Lord showed the path of perfection, which is followed by those who have fully controlled their senses and who are honored by all orders of life.

sanskrit: ṛṣibhiḥ yācitaḥ bheje navamam pārthivam vapuḥ dugdha imām oṣadhīḥ viprāḥ tena ayam saḥ uśattamaḥ
english: O brāhmaṇas, in the ninth incarnation, the Lord, prayed for by sages, accepted the body of a king [Pṛthu] who cultivated the land to yield various produce, and for that reason the earth was beautiful and attractive.

sanskrit: rūpam saḥ jagṛhe mātsyam cākṣuṣa udadhi samplave nāvi āropya mahī mayyām apāt vaivasvatam manum
english: When there was a complete inundation after the period of the Cākṣuṣa Manu and the whole world was deep within water, the Lord accepted the form of a fish and protected Vaivasvata Manu, keeping him up on a boat.

sanskrit: sura asurāṇām udadhim mathnatām mandarācalam dadhre kamaṭha rūpeṇa pṛṣṭhe ekādaśe vibhuḥ
english: The eleventh incarnation of the Lord took the form of a tortoise whose shell served as a pivot for the Mandarācala Hill, which was being used as a churning rod by the theists and atheists of the universe.

sanskrit: dhānvantaram dvādaśamam trayodaśamam eva ca apāyayat surān anyān mohinyā mohayan striyā
english: In the twelfth incarnation, the Lord appeared as Dhanvantari, and in the thirteenth He allured the atheists by the charming beauty of a woman and gave nectar to the demigods to drink.

sanskrit: caturdaśam nāra siṁham bibhrat daitya indram ūrjitam dadāra karajaiḥ ūrau erakām kaṭa kṛt yathā
english: In the fourteenth incarnation, the Lord appeared as Nṛsiṁha and bifurcated the strong body of the atheist Hiraṇyakaśipu with His nails, just as a carpenter pierces cane.

sanskrit: pañcadaśam vāmanakam kṛtvā agāt adhvaram baleḥ pada trayam yācamānaḥ pratyāditsuḥ tri piṣṭapam
english: In the fifteenth incarnation, the Lord assumed the form of a dwarf brāhmaṇa [Vāmana] and visited the arena of sacrifice arranged by Mahārāja Bali. Although at heart He was willing to regain the kingdom of the three planetary systems, He simply asked for a donation of three steps of land.

sanskrit: avatāre ṣoḍaśame paśyan brahma druhaḥ nṛpān triḥ sapta kṛtvaḥ kupitaḥ niḥ kṣatrām akarot mahīm
english: In the sixteenth incarnation of the Godhead, the Lord [as Bhṛgupati] annihilated the administrative class [kṣatriyas] twenty-one times, being angry with them because of their rebellion against the brāhmaṇas [the intelligent class].

sanskrit: tataḥ saptadaśe jātaḥ satyavatyām parāśarāt cakre veda taroḥ śākhāḥ dṛṣṭvā puṁsaḥ alpa medhasaḥ
english: Thereafter, in the seventeenth incarnation of Godhead, Śrī Vyāsadeva appeared in the womb of Satyavatī through Parāśara Muni, and he divided the one Veda into several branches and subbranches, seeing that the people in general were less intelligent.

sanskrit: nara devatvam āpannaḥ sura kārya cikīrṣayā samudra nigraha ādīni cakre vīryāṇi ataḥ param
english: In the eighteenth incarnation, the Lord appeared as King Rāma. In order to perform some pleasing work for the demigods, He exhibited superhuman powers by controlling the Indian Ocean and then killing the atheist King Rāvaṇa, who was on the other side of the sea.

sanskrit: ekonaviṁśe viṁśatime vṛṣṇiṣu prāpya janmanī rāma kṛṣṇau iti bhuvaḥ bhagavān aharat bharam
english: In the nineteenth and twentieth incarnations, the Lord advented Himself as Lord Balarāma and Lord Kṛṣṇa in the family of Vṛṣṇi [the Yadu dynasty], and by so doing He removed the burden of the world.

sanskrit: tataḥ kalau sampravṛtte sammohāya sura dviṣām buddhaḥ nāmnā añjana sutaḥ kīkaṭeṣu bhaviṣyati
english: Then, in the beginning of Kali-yuga, the Lord will appear as Lord Buddha, the son of Añjanā, in the province of Gayā, just for the purpose of deluding those who are envious of the faithful theist.

sanskrit: atha asau yuga sandhyāyām dasyu prāyeṣu rājasu janitā viṣṇu yaśasaḥ nāmnā kalkiḥ jagat patiḥ
english: Thereafter, at the conjunction of two yugas, the Lord of the creation will take His birth as the Kalki incarnation and become the son of Viṣṇu Yaśā. At this time almost all the rulers of the earth will have degenerated into plunderers.

sanskrit: avatārāḥ hi asaṅkhyeyāḥ hareḥ sattva nidheḥ dvijāḥ yathā avidāsinaḥ kulyāḥ sarasaḥ syuḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: O brāhmaṇas, the incarnations of the Lord are innumerable, like rivulets flowing from inexhaustible sources of water.

sanskrit: ṛṣayaḥ manavaḥ devāḥ manu putrāḥ mahā ojasaḥ kalāḥ sarve hareḥ eva sa prajāpatayaḥ smṛtāḥ
english: All the ṛṣis, Manus, demigods and descendants of Manu, who are especially powerful, are plenary portions or portions of the plenary portions of the Lord. This also includes the Prajāpatis.

sanskrit: ete ca aṁśa kalāḥ puṁsaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ tu bhagavān svayam indra ari vyākulam lokam mṛḍayanti yuge yuge
english: All of the above-mentioned incarnations are either plenary portions or portions of the plenary portions of the Lord, but Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is the original Personality of Godhead. All of them appear on planets whenever there is a disturbance created by the atheists. The Lord incarnates to protect the theists.

sanskrit: janma guhyam bhagavataḥ yaḥ etat prayataḥ naraḥ sāyam prātaḥ gṛṇan bhaktyā duḥkha grāmāt vimucyate
english: Whoever carefully recites the mysterious appearances of the Lord, with devotion in the morning and in the evening, gets relief from all miseries of life.

sanskrit: etat rūpam bhagavataḥ hi arūpasya cit ātmanaḥ māyā guṇaiḥ viracitam mahat ādibhiḥ ātmani
english: The conception of the virāṭ universal form of the Lord, as appearing in the material world, is imaginary. It is to enable the less intelligent [and neophytes] to adjust to the idea of the Lord’s having form. But factually the Lord has no material form.

sanskrit: yathā nabhasi megha oghaḥ reṇuḥ vā pārthivaḥ anile evam draṣṭari dṛśyatvam āropitam abuddhibhiḥ
english: Clouds and dust are carried by the air, but less intelligent persons say that the sky is cloudy and the air is dirty. Similarly, they also implant material bodily conceptions on the spirit self.

sanskrit: ataḥ param yat avyaktam avyūḍha guṇa bṛṁhitam adṛṣṭa aśruta vastutvāt saḥ jīvaḥ yat punaḥ bhavaḥ
english: Beyond this gross conception of form is another, subtle conception of form which is without formal shape and is unseen, unheard and unmanifest. The living being has his form beyond this subtlety, otherwise he could not have repeated births.

sanskrit: yatra ime sat asat rūpe pratiṣiddhe sva saṁvidā avidyayā ātmani kṛte iti tat brahma darśanam
english: Whenever a person experiences, by self-realization, that both the gross and subtle bodies have nothing to do with the pure self, at that time he sees himself as well as the Lord.

sanskrit: yadi eṣā uparatā devī māyā vaiśāradī matiḥ sampannaḥ eva iti viduḥ mahimni sve mahīyate
english: If the illusory energy subsides and the living entity becomes fully enriched with knowledge by the grace of the Lord, then he becomes at once enlightened with self-realization and thus becomes situated in his own glory.

sanskrit: evam janmāni karmāṇi hi akartuḥ ajanasya ca varṇayanti sma kavayaḥ veda guhyāni hṛt pateḥ
english: Thus learned men describe the births and activities of the unborn and inactive, which is undiscoverable even in the Vedic literatures. He is the Lord of the heart.

sanskrit: saḥ vā idam viśvam amogha līlaḥ sṛjati avati atti na sajjate asmin bhūteṣu ca antarhitaḥ ātma tantraḥ ṣāṭ vargikam jighrati ṣaṭ guṇa īśaḥ
english: The Lord, whose activities are always spotless, is the master of the six senses and is fully omnipotent with six opulences. He creates the manifested universes, maintains them and annihilates them without being in the least affected. He is within every living being and is always independent.

sanskrit: na ca asya kaścit nipuṇena dhātuḥ avaiti jantuḥ kumanīṣaḥ ūtīḥ nāmāni rūpāṇi manaḥ vacobhiḥ santanvataḥ naṭa caryām iva ajñaḥ
english: The foolish with a poor fund of knowledge cannot know the transcendental nature of the forms, names and activities of the Lord, who is playing like an actor in a drama. Nor can they express such things, neither in their speculations nor in their words.

sanskrit: saḥ veda dhātuḥ padavīm parasya duranta vīryasya ratha aṅga pāṇeḥ yaḥ amāyayā santatayā anuvṛttyā bhajeta tat pāda saroja gandham
english: Only those who render unreserved, uninterrupted, favorable service unto the lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa, who carries the wheel of the chariot in His hand, can know the creator of the universe in His full glory, power and transcendence.

sanskrit: atha iha dhanyāḥ bhagavantaḥ ittham yat vāsudeve akhila loka nāthe kurvanti sarva ātmakam ātma bhāvam na yatra bhūyaḥ parivartaḥ ugraḥ
english: Only by making such inquiries in this world can one be successful and perfectly cognizant, for such inquiries invoke transcendental ecstatic love unto the Personality of Godhead, who is the proprietor of all the universes, and guarantee cent-percent immunity from the dreadful repetition of birth and death.

sanskrit: idam bhāgavatam nāma purāṇam brahma sammitam uttama śloka caritam cakāra bhagavān ṛṣiḥ niḥśreyasāya lokasya dhanyam svasti ayanam mahat
english: This Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam is the literary incarnation of God, and it is compiled by Śrīla Vyāsadeva, the incarnation of God. It is meant for the ultimate good of all people, and it is all-successful, all-blissful and all-perfect.

sanskrit: tat idam grāhayām āsa sutam ātmavatām varam sarva veda itihāsānām sāram sāram samuddhṛtam
english: Śrī Vyāsadeva delivered it to his son, who is the most respected among the self-realized, after extracting the cream of all Vedic literatures and histories of the universe.

sanskrit: saḥ tu saṁśrāvayām āsa mahā rājam parīkṣitam prāya upaviṣṭam gaṅgāyām parītam parama ṛṣibhiḥ
english: Śukadeva Gosvāmī, the son of Vyāsadeva, in his turn delivered the Bhāgavatam to the great Emperor Parīkṣit, who sat surrounded by sages on the bank of the Ganges, awaiting death without taking food or drink.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇe sva dhāma upagate dharma jñāna ādibhiḥ saha kalau naṣṭa dṛśām eṣaḥ purāṇa arkaḥ adhunā uditaḥ
english: This Bhāgavata Purāṇa is as brilliant as the sun, and it has arisen just after the departure of Lord Kṛṣṇa to His own abode, accompanied by religion, knowledge, etc. Persons who have lost their vision due to the dense darkness of ignorance in the Age of Kali shall get light from this Purāṇa.

sanskrit: tatra kīrtayataḥ viprāḥ vipra ṛṣeḥ bhūri tejasaḥ aham ca adhyagamam tatra niviṣṭaḥ tat anugrahāt saḥ aham vaḥ śrāvayiṣyāmi yathā adhītam yathā mati
english: O learned brāhmaṇas, when Śukadeva Gosvāmī recited Bhāgavatam there [in the presence of Emperor Parīkṣit], I heard him with rapt attention, and thus, by his mercy, I learned the Bhāgavatam from that great and powerful sage. Now I shall try to make you hear the very same thing as I learned it from him and as I have realized it.

sanskrit: vyāsaḥ uvāca iti bruvāṇam saṁstūya munīnām dīrgha satriṇām vṛddhaḥ kula patiḥ sūtam bahu ṛcaḥ śaunakaḥ abravīt
english: Vyāsadeva said: On hearing Sūta Gosvāmī speak thus, Śaunaka Muni, who was the elderly, learned leader of all the ṛṣis engaged in that prolonged sacrificial ceremony, congratulated Sūta Gosvāmī by addressing him as follows.

sanskrit: śaunakaḥ uvāca sūta sūta mahā bhāga vada naḥ vadatām vara kathām bhāgavatīm puṇyām yat āha bhagavān śukaḥ
english: Śaunaka said: O Sūta Gosvāmī, you are the most fortunate and respected of all those who can speak and recite. Please relate the pious message of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, which was spoken by the great and powerful sage Śukadeva Gosvāmī.

sanskrit: kasmin yuge pravṛttā iyam sthāne vā kena hetunā kutaḥ sañcoditaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ kṛtavān saṁhitām muniḥ
english: In what period and at what place was this first begun, and why was this taken up? From where did Kṛṣṇa-dvaipāyana Vyāsa, the great sage, get the inspiration to compile this literature?

sanskrit: tasya putraḥ mahā yogī sama dṛk nirvikalpakaḥ ekānta matiḥ unnidraḥ gūḍhaḥ mūḍhaḥ iva īyate
english: His [Vyāsadeva’s] son was a great devotee, an equibalanced monist, whose mind was always concentrated in monism. He was transcendental to mundane activities, but being unexposed, he appeared like an ignorant person.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā anuyāntam ṛṣim ātmajam api anagnam devyaḥ hriyā paridadhuḥ na sutasya citram tat vīkṣya pṛcchati munau jagaduḥ tava asti strī pum bhidā na tu sutasya vivikta dṛṣṭeḥ
english: While Śrī Vyāsadeva was following his son, beautiful young damsels who were bathing naked covered their bodies with cloth, although Śrī Vyāsadeva himself was not naked. But they had not done so when his son had passed. The sage inquired about this, and the young ladies replied that his son was purified and when looking at them made no distinction between male and female. But the sage made such distinctions.

sanskrit: katham ālakṣitaḥ pauraiḥ samprāptaḥ kuru jāṅgalān unmatta mūka jaḍavat vicaran gaja sāhvaye
english: How was he [Śrīla Śukadeva, the son of Vyāsa] recognized by the citizens when he entered the city of Hastināpura [now Delhi], after wandering in the provinces of Kuru and Jāṅgala, appearing like a madman, dumb and retarded?

sanskrit: katham vā pāṇḍaveyasya rājarṣeḥ muninā saha saṁvādaḥ samabhūt tāta yatra eṣā sātvatī śrutiḥ
english: How did it so happen that King Parīkṣit met this great sage, making it possible for this great transcendental essence of the Vedas [Bhāgavatam] to be sung to him?

sanskrit: saḥ go dohana mātram hi gṛheṣu gṛha medhinām avekṣate mahā bhāgaḥ tīrthī kurvan tat āśramam
english: He [Śukadeva Gosvāmī] was accustomed to stay at the door of a householder only long enough for a cow to be milked. And he did this just to sanctify the residence.

sanskrit: abhimanyu sutam sūta prāhuḥ bhāgavata uttamam tasya janma mahā āścaryam karmāṇi ca gṛṇīhi naḥ
english: It is said that Mahārāja Parīkṣit is a great first-class devotee of the Lord and that his birth and activities are all wonderful. Please tell us about him.

sanskrit: saḥ samrāṭ kasya vā hetoḥ pāṇḍūnām māna vardhanaḥ prāya upaviṣṭaḥ gaṅgāyām anādṛtya adhirāṭ śriyam
english: He was a great emperor and possessed all the opulences of his acquired kingdom. He was so exalted that he was increasing the prestige of the Pāṇḍu dynasty. Why did he give up everything to sit down on the bank of the Ganges and fast until death?

sanskrit: namanti yat pāda niketam ātmanaḥ śivāya hānīya dhanāni śatravaḥ katham saḥ vīraḥ śriyam aṅga dustyajām yuvā aiṣata utsraṣṭum aho saha asubhiḥ
english: He was such a great emperor that all his enemies would come and bow down at his feet and surrender all their wealth for their own benefit. He was full of youth and strength, and he possessed kingly opulences that were difficult to give up. Why did he want to give up everything, including his life?

sanskrit: śivāya lokasya bhavāya bhūtaye ye uttama śloka parāyaṇāḥ janāḥ jīvanti na ātma artham asau para āśrayam mumoca nirvidya kutaḥ kalevaram
english: Those who are devoted to the cause of the Personality of Godhead live only for the welfare, development and happiness of others. They do not live for any selfish interest. So even though the Emperor [Parīkṣit] was free from all attachment to worldly possessions, how could he give up his mortal body, which was the shelter for others?

sanskrit: tat sarvam naḥ samācakṣva pṛṣṭaḥ yat iha kiñcana manye tvām viṣaye vācām snātam anyatra chāndasāt
english: We know that you are expert in the meaning of all subjects, except some portions of the Vedas, and thus you can clearly explain the answers to all the questions we have just put to you.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca dvāpare samanuprāpte tṛtīye yuga paryaye jātaḥ parāśarāt yogī vāsavyām kalayā hareḥ
english: Sūta Gosvāmī said: When the second millennium overlapped the third, the great sage [Vyāsadeva] was born to Parāśara in the womb of Satyavatī, the daughter of Vasu.

sanskrit: saḥ kadācit sarasvatyāḥ upaspṛśya jalam śuciḥ vivikte ekaḥ āsīnaḥ udite ravi maṇḍale
english: Once upon a time he [Vyāsadeva], as the sun rose, took his morning ablution in the waters of the Sarasvatī and sat alone to concentrate.

sanskrit: para avara jñaḥ saḥ ṛṣiḥ kālena avyakta raṁhasā yuga dharma vyatikaram prāptam bhuvi yuge yuge
english: The great sage Vyāsadeva saw anomalies in the duties of the millennium. This happens on the earth in different ages, due to the unseen force of time.

sanskrit: bhautikānām ca bhāvānām śakti hrāsam ca tat kṛtam aśraddadhānān niḥsattvān durmedhān hrasita āyuṣaḥ durbhagān ca janān vīkṣya muniḥ divyena cakṣuṣā sarva varṇa āśramāṇām yat dadhyau hitam amogha dṛk
english: The great sage, who was fully equipped in knowledge, could see through his transcendental vision the deterioration of everything material due to the influence of the age. He could also see that the faithless people in general would be reduced in duration of life and would be impatient due to lack of goodness. Thus he contemplated for the welfare of men in all statuses and orders of life.

sanskrit: cātuḥ hotram karma śuddham prajānām vīkṣya vaidikam vyadadhāt yajña santatyai vedam ekam catuḥ vidham
english: He saw that the sacrifices mentioned in the Vedas were means by which the people’s occupations could be purified. And to simplify the process he divided the one Veda into four, in order to expand them among men.

sanskrit: ṛg yajuḥ sāma atharva ākhyāḥ vedāḥ catvāraḥ uddhṛtāḥ itihāsa purāṇam ca pañcamaḥ vedaḥ ucyate
english: The four divisions of the original sources of knowledge [the Vedas] were made separately. But the historical facts and authentic stories mentioned in the Purāṇas are called the fifth Veda.

sanskrit: tatra ṛg veda dharaḥ pailaḥ sāma gaḥ jaiminiḥ kaviḥ vaiśampāyanaḥ eva ekaḥ niṣṇātaḥ yajuṣām uta
english: After the Vedas were divided into four divisions, Paila Ṛṣi became the professor of the Ṛg Veda, Jaimini the professor of the Sāma Veda, and Vaiśampāyana alone became glorified by the Yajur Veda.

sanskrit: atharva aṅgirasām āsīt sumantuḥ dāruṇaḥ muniḥ itihāsa purāṇānām pitā me romaharṣaṇaḥ
english: The Sumantu Muni Aṅgirā, who was very devotedly engaged, was entrusted with the Atharva Veda. And my father, Romaharṣaṇa, was entrusted with the Purāṇas and historical records.

sanskrit: te ete ṛṣayaḥ vedam svam svam vyasyan anekadhā śiṣyaiḥ praśiṣyaiḥ tat śiṣyaiḥ vedāḥ te śākhinaḥ abhavan
english: All these learned scholars, in their turn, rendered their entrusted Vedas unto their many disciples, granddisciples and great-granddisciples, and thus the respective branches of the followers of the Vedas came into being.

sanskrit: te eva vedāḥ durmedhaiḥ dhāryante puruṣaiḥ yathā evam cakāra bhagavān vyāsaḥ kṛpaṇa vatsalaḥ
english: Thus the great sage Vyāsadeva, who is very kind to the ignorant masses, edited the Vedas so they might be assimilated by less intellectual men.

sanskrit: strī śūdra dvija bandhūnām trayī na śruti gocarā karma śreyasi mūḍhānām śreyaḥ evam bhavet iha iti bhāratam ākhyānam kṛpayā muninā kṛtam
english: Out of compassion, the great sage thought it wise that this would enable men to achieve the ultimate goal of life. Thus he compiled the great historical narration called the Mahābhārata for women, laborers and friends of the twice-born.

sanskrit: evam pravṛttasya sadā bhūtānām śreyasi dvijāḥ sarvātmakena api yadā na atuṣyat hṛdayam tataḥ
english: O twice-born brāhmaṇas, still his mind was not satisfied, although he engaged himself in working for the total welfare of all people.

sanskrit: na atiprasīdat hṛdayaḥ sarasvatyāḥ taṭe śucau vitarkayan vivikta sthaḥ idam ca uvāca dharma vit
english: Thus the sage, being dissatisfied at heart, at once began to reflect, because he knew the essence of religion, and he said within himself:

sanskrit: dhṛta vratena hi mayā chandāṁsi guravaḥ agnayaḥ mānitāḥ nirvyalīkena gṛhītam ca anuśāsanam bhārata vyapadeśena hi āmnāya arthaḥ ca pradarśitaḥ dṛśyate yatra dharma ādiḥ strī śūdra ādibhiḥ api uta
english: I have, under strict disciplinary vows, unpretentiously worshiped the Vedas, the spiritual masters and the altar of sacrifice. I have also abided by the rulings and have shown the import of disciplic succession through the explanation of the Mahābhārata, by which even women, śūdras and others [friends of the twice-born] can see the path of religion.

sanskrit: tathāpi bata me daihyaḥ hi ātmā ca eva ātmanā vibhuḥ asampannaḥ iva ābhāti brahma varcasya sattamaḥ
english: I am feeling incomplete, though I myself am fully equipped with everything required by the Vedas.

sanskrit: kim vā bhāgavatāḥ dharmāḥ na prāyeṇa nirūpitāḥ priyāḥ paramahaṁsānām te eva hi acyuta priyāḥ
english: This may be because I did not specifically point out the devotional service of the Lord, which is dear both to perfect beings and to the infallible Lord.

sanskrit: tasya evam khilam ātmānam manyamānasya khidyataḥ kṛṣṇasya nāradaḥ abhyāgāt āśramam prāk udāhṛtam
english: As mentioned before, Nārada reached the cottage of Kṛṣṇa-dvaipāyana Vyāsa on the banks of the Sarasvatī just as Vyāsadeva was regretting his defects.

sanskrit: tam abhijñāya sahasā pratyutthāya āgatam muniḥ pūjayām āsa vidhi vat nāradam sura pūjitam
english: At the auspicious arrival of Śrī Nārada, Śrī Vyāsadeva got up respectfully and worshiped him, giving him veneration equal to that given to Brahmājī, the creator.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca atha tam sukham āsīnaḥ upāsīnam bṛhat śravāḥ devarṣiḥ prāha viprarṣim vīṇā pāṇiḥ smayan iva
english: Sūta Gosvāmī said: Thus the sage amongst the gods [Nārada], comfortably seated and apparently smiling, addressed the ṛṣi amongst the brāhmaṇas [Vedavyāsa].

sanskrit: nāradaḥ uvāca pārāśarya mahā bhāga bhavataḥ kaccit ātmanā parituṣyati śārīraḥ ātmā mānasaḥ eva vā
english: Addressing Vyāsadeva, the son of Parāśara, Nārada inquired: Are you satisfied by identifying with the body or the mind as objects of self-realization?

sanskrit: jijñāsitam susampannam api te mahat adbhutam kṛtavān bhāratam yaḥ tvam sarva artha paribṛṁhitam
english: Your inquiries were full and your studies were also well fulfilled, and there is no doubt that you have prepared a great and wonderful work, the Mahābhārata, which is full of all kinds of Vedic sequences elaborately explained.

sanskrit: jijñāsitam adhītam ca brahma yat tat sanātanam tathāpi śocasi ātmānam akṛta arthaḥ iva prabho
english: You have fully delineated the subject of impersonal Brahman as well as the knowledge derived therefrom. Why should you be despondent in spite of all this, thinking that you are undone, my dear prabhu?

sanskrit: vyāsaḥ uvāca asti eva me sarvam idam tvayā uktam tathāpi na ātmā parituṣyate me tat mūlam avyaktam agādha bodham pṛcchāmahe tvā ātma bhava ātma bhūtam
english: Śrī Vyāsadeva said: All you have said about me is perfectly correct. Despite all this, I am not pacified. I therefore question you about the root cause of my dissatisfaction, for you are a man of unlimited knowledge due to your being the offspring of one [Brahmā] who is self-born [without mundane father and mother].

sanskrit: saḥ vai bhavān veda samasta guhyam upāsitaḥ yat puruṣaḥ purāṇaḥ para avara īśaḥ manasā eva viśvam sṛjati avati atti guṇaiḥ asaṅgaḥ
english: My lord! Everything that is mysterious is known to you because you worship the creator and destroyer of the material world and the maintainer of the spiritual world, the original Personality of Godhead, who is transcendental to the three modes of material nature.

sanskrit: tvam paryaṭan arkaḥ iva tri lokīm antaḥ caraḥ vāyuḥ iva ātma sākṣī para avare brahmaṇi dharmataḥ vrataiḥ snātasya me nyūnam alam vicakṣva
english: Like the sun, Your Goodness can travel everywhere in the three worlds, and like the air you can penetrate the internal region of everyone. As such, you are as good as the all-pervasive Supersoul. Please, therefore, find out the deficiency in me, despite my being absorbed in transcendence under disciplinary regulations and vows.

sanskrit: śrī nāradaḥ uvāca bhavatā anudita prāyam yaśaḥ bhagavataḥ amalam yena eva asau na tuṣyeta manye tat darśanam khilam
english: Śrī Nārada said: You have not actually broadcast the sublime and spotless glories of the Personality of Godhead. That philosophy which does not satisfy the transcendental senses of the Lord is considered worthless.

sanskrit: yathā dharma ādayaḥ ca arthāḥ muni varya anukīrtitāḥ na tathā vāsudevasya mahimā hi anuvarṇitaḥ
english: Although, great sage, you have very broadly described the four principles beginning with religious performances, you have not described the glories of the Supreme Personality, Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: na yat vacaḥ citra padam hareḥ yaśaḥ jagat pavitram pragṛṇīta karhicit tat vāyasam tīrtham uśanti mānasāḥ na yatra haṁsāḥ niramanti uśik kṣayāḥ
english: Those words which do not describe the glories of the Lord, who alone can sanctify the atmosphere of the whole universe, are considered by saintly persons to be like unto a place of pilgrimage for crows. Since the all-perfect persons are inhabitants of the transcendental abode, they do not derive any pleasure there.

sanskrit: tat vāk visargaḥ janatā agha viplavaḥ yasmin prati ślokam abaddhavati api nāmāni anantasya yaśaḥ aṅkitāni yat śṛṇvanti gāyanti gṛṇanti sādhavaḥ
english: On the other hand, that literature which is full of descriptions of the transcendental glories of the name, fame, forms, pastimes, etc., of the unlimited Supreme Lord is a different creation, full of transcendental words directed toward bringing about a revolution in the impious lives of this world’s misdirected civilization. Such transcendental literatures, even though imperfectly composed, are heard, sung and accepted by purified men who are thoroughly honest.

sanskrit: naiṣkarmyam api acyuta bhāva varjitam na śobhate jñānam alam nirañjanam kutaḥ punaḥ śaśvat abhadram īśvare na ca arpitam karma yat api akāraṇam
english: Knowledge of self-realization, even though free from all material affinity, does not look well if devoid of a conception of the Infallible [God]. What, then, is the use of fruitive activities, which are naturally painful from the very beginning and transient by nature, if they are not utilized for the devotional service of the Lord?

sanskrit: atho mahā bhāga bhavān amogha dṛk śuci śravāḥ satya rataḥ dhṛta vrataḥ urukramasya akhila bandha muktaye samādhinā anusmara tat viceṣṭitam
english: O Vyāsadeva, your vision is completely perfect. Your good fame is spotless. You are firm in vow and situated in truthfulness. And thus you can think of the pastimes of the Lord in trance for the liberation of the people in general from all material bondage.

sanskrit: tataḥ anyathā kiñcana yat vivakṣataḥ pṛthak dṛśaḥ tat kṛta rūpa nāmabhiḥ na karhicit kvāpi ca duḥsthitā matiḥ labheta vāta āhata nauḥ iva āspadam
english: Whatever you desire to describe that is separate in vision from the Lord simply reacts, with different forms, names and results, to agitate the mind, as the wind agitates a boat which has no resting place.

sanskrit: jugupsitam dharma kṛte anuśāsataḥ svabhāva raktasya mahān vyatikramaḥ yat vākyataḥ dharmaḥ iti itaraḥ sthitaḥ na manyate tasya nivāraṇam janaḥ
english: The people in general are naturally inclined to enjoy, and you have encouraged them in that way in the name of religion. This is verily condemned and is quite unreasonable. Because they are guided under your instructions, they will accept such activities in the name of religion and will hardly care for prohibitions.

sanskrit: vicakṣaṇaḥ asya arhati veditum vibhoḥ ananta pārasya nivṛttitaḥ sukham pravartamānasya guṇaiḥ anātmanaḥ tataḥ bhavān darśaya ceṣṭitam vibhoḥ
english: The Supreme Lord is unlimited. Only a very expert personality, retired from the activities of material happiness, deserves to understand this knowledge of spiritual values. Therefore those who are not so well situated, due to material attachment, should be shown the ways of transcendental realization, by Your Goodness, through descriptions of the transcendental activities of the Supreme Lord.

sanskrit: tyaktvā sva dharmam caraṇa ambujam hareḥ bhajan apakvaḥ atha patet tataḥ yadi yatra kva vā abhadram abhūt amuṣya kim kaḥ vā arthaḥ āptaḥ abhajatām sva dharmataḥ
english: One who has forsaken his material occupations to engage in the devotional service of the Lord may sometimes fall down while in an immature stage, yet there is no danger of his being unsuccessful. On the other hand, a nondevotee, though fully engaged in occupational duties, does not gain anything.

sanskrit: tasya eva hetoḥ prayateta kovidaḥ na labhyate yat bhramatām upari adhaḥ tat labhyate duḥkhavat anyataḥ sukham kālena sarvatra gabhīra raṁhasā
english: Persons who are actually intelligent and philosophically inclined should endeavor only for that purposeful end which is not obtainable even by wandering from the topmost planet [Brahmaloka] down to the lowest planet [Pātāla]. As far as happiness derived from sense enjoyment is concerned, it can be obtained automatically in course of time, just as in course of time we obtain miseries even though we do not desire them.

sanskrit: na vai janaḥ jātu kathañcana āvrajet mukunda sevī anyavat aṅga saṁsṛtim smaran mukunda aṅghri upagūhanam punaḥ vihātum icchet na rasa grahaḥ janaḥ
english: My dear Vyāsa, even though a devotee of Lord Kṛṣṇa sometimes falls down somehow or other, he certainly does not undergo material existence like others [fruitive workers, etc.] because a person who has once relished the taste of the lotus feet of the Lord can do nothing but remember that ecstasy again and again.

sanskrit: idam hi viśvam bhagavān iva itaraḥ yataḥ jagat sthāna nirodha sambhavāḥ tat hi svayam veda bhavān tathā api te prādeśa mātram bhavataḥ pradarśitam
english: The Supreme Lord Personality of Godhead is Himself this cosmos, and still He is aloof from it. From Him only has this cosmic manifestation emanated, in Him it rests, and unto Him it enters after annihilation. Your good self knows all about this. I have given only a synopsis.

sanskrit: tvam ātmanā ātmānam avehi amogha dṛk parasya puṁsaḥ paramātmanaḥ kalām ajam prajātam jagataḥ śivāya tat mahā anubhāva abhyudayaḥ adhigaṇya tām
english: Your Goodness has perfect vision. You yourself can know the Supersoul Personality of Godhead because you are present as the plenary portion of the Lord. Although you are birthless, you have appeared on this earth for the well-being of all people. Please, therefore, describe the transcendental pastimes of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa more vividly.

sanskrit: idam hi puṁsaḥ tapasaḥ śrutasya vā sviṣṭasya sūktasya ca buddhi dattayoḥ avicyutaḥ arthaḥ kavibhiḥ nirūpitaḥ yat uttamaśloka guṇa anuvarṇanam
english: Learned circles have positively concluded that the infallible purpose of the advancement of knowledge, namely austerities, study of the Vedas, sacrifice, chanting of hymns and charity, culminates in the transcendental descriptions of the Lord, who is defined in choice poetry.

sanskrit: aham purā atīta bhave abhavam mune dāsyāḥ tu kasyāścana veda vādinām nirūpitaḥ bālakaḥ eva yoginām śuśrūṣaṇe prāvṛṣi nirvivikṣatām
english: O Muni, in the last millennium I was born as the son of a certain maidservant engaged in the service of brāhmaṇas who were following the principles of Vedānta. When they were living together during the four months of the rainy season, I was engaged in their personal service.

sanskrit: te mayi apeta akhila cāpale arbhake dānte adhṛta krīḍanake anuvartini cakruḥ kṛpām yadyapi tulya darśanāḥ śuśrūṣamāṇe munayaḥ alpa bhāṣiṇi
english: Although they were impartial by nature, those followers of the Vedānta blessed me with their causeless mercy. As far as I was concerned, I was self-controlled and had no attachment for sports, even though I was a boy. In addition, I was not naughty, and I did not speak more than required.

sanskrit: ucchiṣṭa lepān anumoditaḥ dvijaiḥ sakṛt sma bhuñje tat apāsta kilbiṣaḥ evam pravṛttasya viśuddha cetasaḥ tat dharmaḥ eva ātma ruciḥ prajāyate
english: Once only, by their permission, I took the remnants of their food, and by so doing all my sins were at once eradicated. Thus being engaged, I became purified in heart, and at that time the very nature of the transcendentalist became attractive to me.

sanskrit: tatra anu aham kṛṣṇa kathāḥ pragāyatām anugraheṇa aśṛṇavam manaḥ harāḥ tāḥ śraddhayā me anupadam viśṛṇvataḥ priyaśravasi aṅga mama abhavat ruciḥ
english: O Vyāsadeva, in that association and by the mercy of those great Vedāntists, I could hear them describe the attractive activities of Lord Kṛṣṇa. And thus listening attentively, my taste for hearing of the Personality of Godhead increased at every step.

sanskrit: tasmin tadā labdha ruceḥ mahā mate priyaśravasi askhalitā matiḥ mama yayā aham etat sat asat sva māyayā paśye mayi brahmaṇi kalpitam pare
english: O great sage, as soon as I got a taste of the Personality of Godhead, my attention to hear of the Lord was unflinching. And as my taste developed, I could realize that it was only in my ignorance that I had accepted gross and subtle coverings, for both the Lord and I are transcendental.

sanskrit: ittham śarat prāvṛṣikau ṛtū hareḥ viśṛṇvataḥ me anusavam yaśaḥ amalam saṅkīrtyamānam munibhiḥ mahā ātmabhiḥ bhaktiḥ pravṛttā ātma rajaḥ tama upahā
english: Thus during two seasons — the rainy season and autumn — I had the opportunity to hear these great-souled sages constantly chant the unadulterated glories of the Lord Hari. As the flow of my devotional service began, the coverings of the modes of passion and ignorance vanished.

sanskrit: tasya evam me anuraktasya praśritasya hata enasaḥ śraddadhānasya bālasya dāntasya anucarasya ca
english: I was very much attached to those sages. I was gentle in behavior, and all my sins were eradicated in their service. In my heart I had strong faith in them. I had subjugated the senses, and I was strictly following them with body and mind.

sanskrit: jñānam guhyatamam yat tat sākṣāt bhagavatā uditam anvavocan gamiṣyantaḥ kṛpayā dīna vatsalāḥ
english: As they were leaving, those bhakti-vedāntas, who are very kind to poor-hearted souls, instructed me in that most confidential subject which is instructed by the Personality of Godhead Himself.

sanskrit: yena eva aham bhagavataḥ vāsudevasya vedhasaḥ māyā anubhāvam avidam yena gacchanti tat padam
english: By that confidential knowledge, I could understand clearly the influence of the energy of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the creator, maintainer and annihilator of everything. By knowing that, one can return to Him and personally meet Him.

sanskrit: etat saṁsūcitam brahman tāpa traya cikitsitam yat īśvare bhagavati karma brahmaṇi bhāvitam
english: O Brāhmaṇa Vyāsadeva, it is decided by the learned that the best remedial measure for removing all troubles and miseries is to dedicate one’s activities to the service of the Supreme Lord Personality of Godhead [Śrī Kṛṣṇa].

sanskrit: āmayaḥ yaḥ ca bhūtānām jāyate yena suvrata tat eva hi āmayam dravyam na punāti cikitsitam
english: O good soul, does not a thing, applied therapeutically, cure a disease which was caused by that very same thing?

sanskrit: evam nṛṇām kriyā yogāḥ sarve saṁsṛti hetavaḥ te eva ātma vināśāya kalpante kalpitāḥ pare
english: Thus when all a man’s activities are dedicated to the service of the Lord, those very activities which caused his perpetual bondage become the destroyer of the tree of work.

sanskrit: yat atra kriyate karma bhagavat paritoṣaṇam jñānam yat tat adhīnam hi bhakti yoga samanvitam
english: Whatever work is done here in this life for the satisfaction of the mission of the Lord is called bhakti-yoga, or transcendental loving service to the Lord, and what is called knowledge becomes a concomitant factor.

sanskrit: kurvāṇāḥ yatra karmāṇi bhagavat śikṣayā asakṛt gṛṇanti guṇa nāmāni kṛṣṇasya anusmaranti ca
english: While performing duties according to the order of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, one constantly remembers Him, His names and His qualities.

sanskrit: oṁ namaḥ bhagavate tubhyam vāsudevāya dhīmahi pradyumnāya, aniruddhāya and saṅkarṣaṇāya namaḥ ca
english: Let us all chant the glories of Vāsudeva along with His plenary expansions Pradyumna, Aniruddha and Saṅkarṣaṇa.

sanskrit: iti mūrti abhidhānena mantra mūrtim amūrtikam yajate yajña puruṣam saḥ samyak darśanaḥ pumān
english: Thus he is the actual seer who worships, in the form of transcendental sound representation, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Viṣṇu, who has no material form.

sanskrit: imam sva nigamam brahman avetya mat anuṣṭhitam adāt me jñānam aiśvaryam svasmin bhāvam ca keśavaḥ
english: O brāhmaṇa, thus by the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa I was endowed first with the transcendental knowledge of the Lord as inculcated in the confidential parts of the Vedas, then with the spiritual opulences, and then with His intimate loving service.

sanskrit: tvam api adabhra śruta viśrutam vibhoḥ samāpyate yena vidām bubhutsitam prākhyāhi duḥkhaiḥ muhuḥ ardita ātmanām saṅkleśa nirvāṇam uśanti na anyathā
english: Please, therefore, describe the almighty Lord’s activities which you have learned by your vast knowledge of the Vedas, for that will satisfy the hankerings of great learned men and at the same time mitigate the miseries of the masses of common people who are always suffering from material pangs. Indeed, there is no other way to get out of such miseries.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca evam niśamya bhagavān devarṣeḥ janma karma ca bhūyaḥ papraccha tam brahman vyāsaḥ satyavatī sutaḥ
english: Sūta said: O brāhmaṇas, thus hearing all about Śrī Nārada’s birth and activities, Vyāsadeva, the incarnation of God and son of Satyavatī, inquired as follows.

sanskrit: vyāsaḥ uvāca bhikṣubhiḥ vipravasite vijñāna ādeṣṭṛbhiḥ tava vartamānaḥ vayasi ādye tataḥ kim akarot bhavān
english: Śrī Vyāsadeva said: What did you [Nārada] do after the departure of the great sages who had instructed you in scientific transcendental knowledge before the beginning of your present birth?

sanskrit: svāyambhuva kayā vṛttyā vartitam te param vayaḥ katham ca idam udasrākṣīḥ kāle prāpte kalevaram
english: O son of Brahmā, how did you pass your life after initiation, and how did you attain this body, having quit your old one in due course?

sanskrit: prāk kalpa viṣayām etām smṛtim te muni sattama na hi eṣaḥ vyavadhāt kālaḥ eṣaḥ sarva nirākṛtiḥ
english: O great sage, time annihilates everything in due course, so how is it that this subject matter, which happened prior to this day of Brahmā, is still fresh in your memory, undisturbed by time?

sanskrit: nāradaḥ uvāca bhikṣubhiḥ vipravasite vijñāna ādeṣṭṛbhiḥ mama vartamānaḥ vayasi ādye tataḥ etat akāraṣam
english: Śrī Nārada said: The great sages, who had imparted scientific knowledge of transcendence to me, departed for other places, and I had to pass my life in this way.

sanskrit: eka ātmajā me jananī yoṣit mūḍhā ca kiṅkarī mayi ātmaje ananya gatau cakre sneha anubandhanam
english: I was the only son of my mother, who was not only a simple woman but a maidservant as well. Since I was her only offspring, she had no other alternative for protection: she bound me with the tie of affection.

sanskrit: sā asvatantrā na kalpā āsīt yoga kṣemam mama icchatī īśasya hi vaśe lokaḥ yoṣā dāru mayī yathā
english: She wanted to look after my maintenance properly, but because she was not independent, she was not able to do anything for me. The world is under the full control of the Supreme Lord; therefore everyone is like a wooden doll in the hands of a puppet master.

sanskrit: aham ca tat brahma kule ūṣivān tat upekṣayā dik deśa kāla avyutpannaḥ bālakaḥ pañca hāyanaḥ
english: When I was a mere child of five years, I lived in a brāhmaṇa school. I was dependent on my mother’s affection and had no experience of different lands.

sanskrit: ekadā nirgatām gehāt duhantīm niśi gām pathi sarpaḥ adaśat padā spṛṣṭaḥ kṛpaṇām kāla coditaḥ
english: Once upon a time, my poor mother, when going out one night to milk a cow, was bitten on the leg by a serpent, influenced by supreme time.

sanskrit: tadā tat aham īśasya bhaktānām śam abhīpsataḥ anugraham manyamānaḥ prātiṣṭham diśam uttarām
english: I took this as the special mercy of the Lord, who always desires benediction for His devotees, and so thinking, I started for the north.

sanskrit: sphītān jana padān tatra pura grāma vraja ākarān kheṭa kharvaṭa vāṭīḥ ca vanāni upavanāni ca
english: After my departure, I passed through many flourishing metropolises, towns, villages, animal farms, mines, agricultural lands, valleys, flower gardens, nursery gardens and natural forests.

sanskrit: citra dhātu vicitra adrīn ibha bhagna bhuja drumān jalāśayān śiva jalān nalinīḥ sura sevitāḥ citra svanaiḥ patra rathaiḥ vibhramat bhramara śriyaḥ
english: I passed through hills and mountains full of reservoirs of various minerals like gold, silver and copper, and through tracts of land with reservoirs of water filled with beautiful lotus flowers, fit for the denizens of heaven, decorated with bewildered bees and singing birds.

sanskrit: nala veṇu śaraḥ tanba kuśa kīcaka gahvaram ekaḥ eva atiyātaḥ aham adrākṣam vipinam mahat ghoram pratibhaya ākāram vyāla ulūka śiva ajiram
english: I then passed alone through many forests of rushes, bamboo, reeds, sharp grass, weeds and caves, which were very difficult to go through alone. I visited deep, dark and dangerously fearful forests, which were the play yards of snakes, owls and jackals.

sanskrit: pariśrānta indriya ātmā aham tṛṭ parītaḥ bubhukṣitaḥ snātvā pītvā hrade nadyāḥ upaspṛṣṭaḥ gata śramaḥ
english: Thus traveling, I felt tired, both bodily and mentally, and I was both thirsty and hungry. So I took a bath in a river lake and also drank water. By contacting water, I got relief from my exhaustion.

sanskrit: tasmin nirmanuje araṇye pippala upasthe āśritaḥ ātmanā ātmānam ātma stham yathā śrutam acintayam
english: After that, under the shadow of a banyan tree in an uninhabited forest I began to meditate upon the Supersoul situated within, using my intelligence, as I had learned from liberated souls.

sanskrit: dhyāyataḥ caraṇa ambhojam bhāva nirjita cetasā autkaṇṭhya aśru kala akṣasya hṛdi āsīt me śanaiḥ hariḥ
english: As soon as I began to meditate upon the lotus feet of the Personality of Godhead with my mind transformed in transcendental love, tears rolled down my eyes, and without delay the Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, appeared on the lotus of my heart.

sanskrit: premā atibhara nirbhinna pulaka aṅgaḥ ati nirvṛtaḥ ānanda samplave līnaḥ na apaśyam ubhayam mune
english: O Vyāsadeva, at that time, being exceedingly overpowered by feelings of happiness, every part of my body became separately enlivened. Being absorbed in an ocean of ecstasy, I could not see both myself and the Lord.

sanskrit: rūpam bhagavataḥ yat tat manaḥ kāntam śucā apaham apaśyan sahasā uttasthe vaiklavyāt durmanāḥ iva
english: The transcendental form of the Lord, as it is, satisfies the mind’s desire and at once erases all mental incongruities. Upon losing that form, I suddenly got up, being perturbed, as is usual when one loses that which is desirable.

sanskrit: didṛkṣuḥ tat aham bhūyaḥ praṇidhāya manaḥ hṛdi vīkṣamāṇaḥ api na apaśyam avitṛptaḥ iva āturaḥ
english: I desired to see again that transcendental form of the Lord, but despite my attempts to concentrate upon the heart with eagerness to view the form again, I could not see Him any more, and thus dissatisfied, I was very much aggrieved.

sanskrit: evam yatantam vijane mām āha agocaraḥ girām gambhīra ślakṣṇayā vācā śucaḥ praśamayan iva
english: Seeing my attempts in that lonely place, the Personality of Godhead, who is transcendental to all mundane description, spoke to me with gravity and pleasing words, just to mitigate my grief.

sanskrit: hanta asmin janmani bhavān mā mām draṣṭum iha arhati avipakva kaṣāyāṇām durdarśaḥ aham kuyoginām
english: O Nārada [the Lord spoke], I regret that during this lifetime you will not be able to see Me anymore. Those who are incomplete in service and who are not completely free from all material taints can hardly see Me.

sanskrit: sakṛt yat darśitam rūpam etat kāmāya te anagha mat kāmaḥ śanakaiḥ sādhuḥ sarvān muñcati hṛt śayān
english: O virtuous one, you have only once seen My person, and this is just to increase your desire for Me, because the more you hanker for Me, the more you will be freed from all material desires.

sanskrit: sat sevayā adīrghayā api jātā mayi dṛḍhā matiḥ hitvā avadyam imam lokam gantā mat janatām asi
english: By service of the Absolute Truth, even for a few days, a devotee attains firm and fixed intelligence in Me. Consequently he goes on to become My associate in the transcendental world after giving up the present deplorable material worlds.

sanskrit: matiḥ mayi nibaddhā iyam na vipadyeta karhicit prajā sarga nirodhe api smṛtiḥ ca mat anugrahāt
english: Intelligence engaged in My devotion cannot be thwarted at any time. Even at the time of creation, as well as at the time of annihilation, your remembrance will continue by My mercy.

sanskrit: etāvat uktvā upararāma tat mahat bhūtam nabhaḥ liṅgam aliṅgam īśvaram aham ca tasmai mahatām mahīyase śīrṣṇā avanāmam vidadhe anukampitaḥ
english: Then that supreme authority, personified by sound and unseen by eyes, but most wonderful, stopped speaking. Feeling a sense of gratitude, I offered my obeisances unto Him, bowing my head.

sanskrit: nāmāni anantasya hata trapaḥ paṭhan guhyāni bhadrāṇi kṛtāni ca smaran gām paryaṭan tuṣṭa manāḥ gata spṛhaḥ kālam pratīkṣan vimadaḥ vimatsaraḥ
english: Thus I began chanting the holy name and fame of the Lord by repeated recitation, ignoring all the formalities of the material world. Such chanting and remembering of the transcendental pastimes of the Lord are benedictory. So doing, I traveled all over the earth, fully satisfied, humble and unenvious.

sanskrit: evam kṛṣṇa mateḥ brahman na āsaktasya amala ātmanaḥ kālaḥ prādurabhūt kāle taḍit saudāmanī yathā
english: And so, O Brāhmaṇa Vyāsadeva, in due course of time I, who was fully absorbed in thinking of Kṛṣṇa and who therefore had no attachments, being completely freed from all material taints, met with death, as lightning and illumination occur simultaneously.

sanskrit: prayujyamāne mayi tām śuddhām bhāgavatīm tanum ārabdha karma nirvāṇaḥ nyapatat pāñca bhautikaḥ
english: Having been awarded a transcendental body befitting an associate of the Personality of Godhead, I quit the body made of five material elements, and thus all acquired fruitive results of work [karma] stopped.

sanskrit: kalpa ante idam ādāya śayāne ambhasi udanvataḥ śiśayiṣoḥ anuprāṇam viviśe antaḥ aham vibhoḥ
english: At the end of the millennium, when the Personality of Godhead, Lord Nārāyaṇa, lay down within the water of devastation, Brahmā began to enter into Him along with all creative elements, and I also entered through His breathing.

sanskrit: sahasra yuga paryante utthāya idam sisṛkṣataḥ marīci miśrāḥ ṛṣayaḥ prāṇebhyaḥ aham ca jajñire
english: After 4,300,000,000 solar years, when Brahmā awoke to create again by the will of the Lord, all the ṛṣis like Marīci, Aṅgirā, Atri and so on were created from the transcendental body of the Lord, and I also appeared along with them.

sanskrit: antaḥ bahiḥ ca lokān trīn paryemi askandita vrataḥ anugrahāt mahā viṣṇoḥ avighāta gatiḥ kvacit
english: Since then, by the grace of the almighty Viṣṇu, I travel everywhere without restriction both in the transcendental world and in the three divisions of the material world. This is because I am fixed in unbroken devotional service of the Lord.

sanskrit: deva dattām imām vīṇām svara brahma vibhūṣitām mūrcchayitvā hari kathām gāyamānaḥ carāmi aham
english: And thus I travel, constantly singing the transcendental message of the glories of the Lord, vibrating this instrument called a vīṇā, which is charged with transcendental sound and which was given to me by Lord Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: pragāyataḥ sva vīryāṇi tīrtha pādaḥ priya śravāḥ āhūtaḥ iva me śīghram darśanam yāti cetasi
english: The Supreme Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, whose glories and activities are pleasing to hear, at once appears on the seat of my heart, as if called for, as soon as I begin to chant His holy activities.

sanskrit: etat hi ātura cittānām mātrā sparśa icchayā muhuḥ bhava sindhu plavaḥ dṛṣṭaḥ hari carya anuvarṇanam
english: It is personally experienced by me that those who are always full of cares and anxieties due to desiring contact of the senses with their objects can cross the ocean of nescience on a most suitable boat — the constant chanting of the transcendental activities of the Personality of Godhead.

sanskrit: yama ādibhiḥ yoga pathaiḥ kāma lobha hataḥ muhuḥ mukunda sevayā yadvat tathā ātmā addhā na śāmyati
english: It is true that by practicing restraint of the senses by the yoga system one can get relief from the disturbances of desire and lust, but this is not sufficient to give satisfaction to the soul, for this [satisfaction] is derived from devotional service to the Personality of Godhead.

sanskrit: sarvam tat idam ākhyātam yat pṛṣṭaḥ aham tvayā anagha janma karma rahasyam me bhavataḥ ca ātma toṣaṇam
english: O Vyāsadeva, you are freed from all sins. Thus I have explained my birth and activities for self-realization, as you asked. All this will be conducive for your personal satisfaction also.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca evam sambhāṣya bhagavān nāradaḥ vāsavī sutam āmantrya vīṇām raṇayan yayau yādṛcchikaḥ muniḥ
english: Sūta Gosvāmī said: Thus addressing Vyāsadeva, Śrīla Nārada Muni took leave of him, and vibrating on his vīṇā instrument, he left to wander at his free will.

sanskrit: aho devarṣiḥ dhanyaḥ ayam yat kīrtim śārṅga dhanvanaḥ gāyan mādyan idam tantryā ramayati āturam jagat
english: All glory and success to Śrīla Nārada Muni because he glorifies the activities of the Personality of Godhead, and so doing he himself takes pleasure and also enlivens all the distressed souls of the universe.

sanskrit: śaunakaḥ uvāca nirgate nārade sūta bhagavān bādarāyaṇaḥ śrutavān tat abhipretam tataḥ kim akarot vibhuḥ
english: Ṛṣi Śaunaka asked: O Sūta, the great and transcendentally powerful Vyāsadeva heard everything from Śrī Nārada Muni. So after Nārada’s departure, what did Vyāsadeva do?

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca brahma nadyām sarasvatyām āśramaḥ paścime taṭe śamyāprāsaḥ iti proktaḥ ṛṣīṇām satra vardhanaḥ
english: Śrī Sūta said: On the western bank of the river Sarasvatī, which is intimately related with the Vedas, there is a cottage for meditation at Śamyāprāsa which enlivens the transcendental activities of the sages.

sanskrit: tasmin sve āśrame vyāsaḥ badarī ṣaṇḍa maṇḍite āsīnaḥ apaḥ upaspṛśya praṇidadhyau manaḥ svayam
english: In that place, Śrīla Vyāsadeva, in his own āśrama, which was surrounded by berry trees, sat down to meditate after touching water for purification.

sanskrit: bhakti yogena manasi samyak praṇihite amale apaśyat puruṣam pūrṇam māyām ca tat apāśrayam
english: Thus he fixed his mind, perfectly engaging it by linking it in devotional service [bhakti-yoga] without any tinge of materialism, and thus he saw the Absolute Personality of Godhead along with His external energy, which was under full control.

sanskrit: yayā sammohitaḥ jīvaḥ ātmānam tri guṇa ātmakam paraḥ api manute anartham tat kṛtam ca abhipadyate
english: Due to this external energy, the living entity, although transcendental to the three modes of material nature, thinks of himself as a material product and thus undergoes the reactions of material miseries.

sanskrit: anartha upaśamam sākṣāt bhakti yogam adhokṣaje lokasya ajānataḥ vidvān cakre sātvata saṁhitām
english: The material miseries of the living entity, which are superfluous to him, can be directly mitigated by the linking process of devotional service. But the mass of people do not know this, and therefore the learned Vyāsadeva compiled this Vedic literature, which is in relation to the Supreme Truth.

sanskrit: yasyām vai śrūyamāṇāyām kṛṣṇe parama pūruṣe bhaktiḥ utpadyate puṁsaḥ śoka moha bhaya apahā
english: Simply by giving aural reception to this Vedic literature, the feeling for loving devotional service to Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, sprouts up at once to extinguish the fire of lamentation, illusion and fearfulness.

sanskrit: saḥ saṁhitām bhāgavatīm kṛtvā anukramya ca ātma jam śukam adhyāpayām āsa nivṛtti niratam muniḥ
english: The great sage Vyāsadeva, after compiling the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam and revising it, taught it to his own son, Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī, who was already engaged in self-realization.

sanskrit: śaunakaḥ uvāca saḥ vai nivṛtti nirataḥ sarvatra upekṣakaḥ muniḥ kasya vā bṛhatīm etām ātma ārāmaḥ samabhyasat
english: Śrī Śaunaka asked Sūta Gosvāmī: Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī was already on the path of self-realization, and thus he was pleased with his own self. So why did he take the trouble to undergo the study of such a vast literature?

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca ātmārāmāḥ ca munayaḥ nirgranthāḥ api urukrame kurvanti ahaitukīm bhaktim ittham bhūta guṇaḥ hariḥ
english: Sūta Gosvāmī said: All different varieties of ātmārāmas [those who take pleasure in the ātmā, or spirit self], especially those established on the path of self-realization, though freed from all kinds of material bondage, desire to render unalloyed devotional service unto the Personality of Godhead. This means that the Lord possesses transcendental qualities and therefore can attract everyone, including liberated souls.

sanskrit: hareḥ guṇa ākṣipta matiḥ bhagavān bādarāyaṇiḥ adhyagāt mahat ākhyānam nityam viṣṇu jana priyaḥ
english: Śrīla Śukadeva Gosvāmī, son of Śrīla Vyāsadeva, was not only transcendentally powerful. He was also very dear to the devotees of the Lord. Thus he underwent the study of this great narration [Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam].

sanskrit: parīkṣitaḥ atha rājarṣeḥ janma karma vilāpanam saṁsthām ca pāṇḍu putrāṇām vakṣye kṛṣṇa kathā udayam
english: Sūta Gosvāmī thus addressed the ṛṣis headed by Śaunaka: Now I shall begin the transcendental narration of the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa and topics of the birth, activities and deliverance of King Parīkṣit, the sage amongst kings, as well as topics of the renunciation of the worldly order by the sons of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: yadā mṛdhe kaurava sṛñjayānām vīreṣu atho vīra gatim gateṣu vṛkodara āviddha gadā abhimarśa bhagna uru daṇḍe dhṛtarāṣṭra putre bhartuḥ priyam drauṇiḥ iti sma paśyan kṛṣṇā sutānām svapatām śirāṁsi upāharat vipriyam eva tasya jugupsitam karma vigarhayanti
english: When the respective warriors of both camps, namely the Kauravas and the Pāṇḍavas, were killed on the Battlefield of Kurukṣetra and the dead warriors obtained their deserved destinations, and when the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra fell down lamenting, his spine broken, being beaten by the club of Bhīmasena, the son of Droṇācārya [Aśvatthāmā] beheaded the five sleeping sons of Draupadī and delivered the heads as a prize to his master, foolishly thinking that he would be pleased. Duryodhana, however, disapproved of the heinous act, and he was not pleased in the least.

sanskrit: mātā śiśūnām nidhanam sutānām niśamya ghoram paritapyamānā tadā arudat vāṣpa kala ākula akṣī tām sāntvayan āha kirīṭamālī
english: Draupadī, the mother of the five children of the Pāṇḍavas, after hearing of the massacre of her sons, began to cry in distress with eyes full of tears. Trying to pacify her in her great loss, Arjuna spoke to her thus:

sanskrit: tadā śucaḥ te pramṛjāmi bhadre yat brahma bandhoḥ śiraḥ ātatāyinaḥ gāṇḍīva muktaiḥ viśikhaiḥ upāhare tvā ākramya yat snāsyasi dagdha putrā
english: O gentle lady, when I present you with the head of that brāhmaṇa, after beheading him with arrows from my Gāṇḍīva bow, I shall then wipe the tears from your eyes and pacify you. Then, after burning your sons’ bodies, you can take your bath standing on his head.

sanskrit: iti priyām valgu vicitra jalpaiḥ saḥ sāntvayitvā acyuta mitra sūtaḥ anvādravat daṁśitaḥ ugra dhanvā kapi dhvajaḥ guru putram rathena
english: Arjuna, who is guided by the infallible Lord as friend and driver, thus satisfied the dear lady by such statements. Then he dressed in armor and armed himself with furious weapons, and getting into his chariot, he set out to follow Aśvatthāmā, the son of his martial teacher.

sanskrit: tam āpatantam saḥ vilakṣya dūrāt kumāra hā udvigna manāḥ rathena parādravat prāṇa parīpsuḥ urvyām yāvat gamam rudra bhayāt yathā kaḥ
english: Aśvatthāmā, the murderer of the princes, seeing from a great distance Arjuna coming at him with great speed, fled in his chariot, panic stricken, just to save his life, as Brahmā fled in fear from Śiva.

sanskrit: yadā aśaraṇam ātmānam aikṣata śrānta vājinam astram brahma śiraḥ mene ātma trāṇam dvija ātma jaḥ
english: When the son of the brāhmaṇa [Aśvatthāmā] saw that his horses were tired, he considered that there was no alternative for protection outside of his using the ultimate weapon, the brahmāstra [nuclear weapon].

sanskrit: atha upaspṛśya salilam sandadhe tat samāhitaḥ ajānan api saṁhāram prāṇa kṛcchre upasthite
english: Since his life was in danger, he touched water in sanctity and concentrated upon the chanting of the hymns for throwing nuclear weapons, although he did not know how to withdraw such weapons.

sanskrit: tataḥ prāduṣkṛtam tejaḥ pracaṇḍam sarvataḥ diśam prāṇa āpadam abhiprekṣya viṣṇum jiṣṇuḥ uvāca ha
english: Thereupon a glaring light spread in all directions. It was so fierce that Arjuna thought his own life in danger, and so he began to address Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: arjunaḥ uvāca kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa mahā bāho bhaktānām abhayaṅkara tvam ekaḥ dahyamānānām apavargaḥ asi saṁsṛteḥ
english: Arjuna said: O my Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, You are the almighty Personality of Godhead. There is no limit to Your different energies. Therefore only You are competent to instill fearlessness in the hearts of Your devotees. Everyone in the flames of material miseries can find the path of liberation in You only.

sanskrit: tvam ādyaḥ puruṣaḥ sākṣāt īśvaraḥ prakṛteḥ paraḥ māyām vyudasya cit śaktyā kaivalye sthitaḥ ātmani
english: You are the original Personality of Godhead who expands Himself all over the creations and is transcendental to material energy. You have cast away the effects of the material energy by dint of Your spiritual potency. You are always situated in eternal bliss and transcendental knowledge.

sanskrit: saḥ eva jīva lokasya māyā mohita cetasaḥ vidhatse svena vīryeṇa śreyaḥ dharma ādi lakṣaṇam
english: And yet, though You are beyond the purview of the material energy, You execute the four principles of liberation characterized by religion and so on for the ultimate good of the conditioned souls.

sanskrit: tathā ayam ca avatāraḥ te bhuvaḥ bhāra jihīrṣayā svānām ca ananya bhāvānām anudhyānāya ca asakṛt
english: Thus You descend as an incarnation to remove the burden of the world and to benefit Your friends, especially those who are Your exclusive devotees and are constantly rapt in meditation upon You.

sanskrit: kim idam svit kutaḥ vā iti deva deva na vedmi aham sarvataḥ mukham āyāti tejaḥ parama dāruṇam
english: O Lord of lords, how is it that this dangerous effulgence is spreading all around? Where does it come from? I do not understand it.

sanskrit: śrī bhagavān uvāca vettha idam droṇa putrasya brāhmam astram pradarśitam na eva asau veda saṁhāram prāṇa bādhe upasthite
english: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: Know from Me that this is the act of the son of Droṇa. He has thrown the hymns of nuclear energy [brahmāstra], and he does not know how to retract the glare. He has helplessly done this, being afraid of imminent death.

sanskrit: na hi asya anyatamam kiñcit astram prati avakarśanam jahi astra tejaḥ unnaddham astra jñaḥ hi astra tejasā
english: O Arjuna, only another brahmāstra can counteract this weapon. Since you are expert in the military science, subdue this weapon’s glare with the power of your own weapon.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca śrutvā bhagavatā proktam phālgunaḥ para vīra hā spṛṣṭvā āpaḥ tam parikramya brāhmam brāhma astram sandadhe
english: Śrī Sūta Gosvāmī said: Hearing this from the Personality of Godhead, Arjuna touched water for purification, and after circumambulating Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, he cast his brahmāstra weapon to counteract the other one.

sanskrit: saṁhatya anyonyam ubhayoḥ tejasī śara saṁvṛte āvṛtya rodasī kham ca vavṛdhāte arka vahni vat
english: When the rays of the two brahmāstras combined, a great circle of fire, like the disc of the sun, covered all outer space and the whole firmament of planets.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā astra tejaḥ tu tayoḥ trīn lokān pradahat mahat dahyamānāḥ prajāḥ sarvāḥ sāṁvartakam amaṁsata
english: All the population of the three worlds was scorched by the combined heat of the weapons. Everyone was reminded of the sāṁvartaka fire which takes place at the time of annihilation.

sanskrit: prajā upadravam ālakṣya loka vyatikaram ca tam matam ca vāsudevasya sañjahāra arjunaḥ dvayam
english: Thus seeing the disturbance of the general populace and the imminent destruction of the planets, Arjuna at once retracted both brahmāstra weapons, as Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa desired.

sanskrit: tataḥ āsādya tarasā dāruṇam gautamī sutam babandha amarṣa tāmra akṣaḥ paśum raśanayā yathā
english: Arjuna, his eyes blazing in anger like two red balls of copper, dexterously arrested the son of Gautamī and bound him with ropes like an animal.

sanskrit: śibirāya ninīṣantam rajjvā baddhvā ripum balāt prāha arjunam prakupitaḥ bhagavān ambuja īkṣaṇaḥ
english: After binding Aśvatthāmā, Arjuna wanted to take him to the military camp. The Personality of Godhead Śrī Kṛṣṇa, looking on with His lotus eyes, spoke to Arjuna in an angry mood.

sanskrit: mā enam pārtha arhasi trātum brahma bandhum imam jahi yaḥ asau anāgasaḥ suptān avadhīt niśi bālakān
english: Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O Arjuna, you should not show mercy by releasing this relative of a brāhmaṇa [brahma-bandhu], for he has killed innocent boys in their sleep.

sanskrit: mattam pramattam unmattam suptam bālam striyam jaḍam prapannam viratham bhītam na ripum hanti dharma vit
english: A person who knows the principles of religion does not kill an enemy who is careless, intoxicated, insane, asleep, afraid or devoid of his chariot. Nor does he kill a boy, a woman, a foolish creature or a surrendered soul.

sanskrit: sva prāṇān yaḥ para prāṇaiḥ prapuṣṇāti aghṛṇaḥ khalaḥ tat vadhaḥ tasya hi śreyaḥ yat doṣāt yāti adhaḥ pumān
english: A cruel and wretched person who maintains his existence at the cost of others’ lives deserves to be killed for his own well-being, otherwise he will go down by his own actions.

sanskrit: pratiśrutam ca bhavatā pāñcālyai śṛṇvataḥ mama āhariṣye śiraḥ tasya yaḥ te mānini putra hā
english: Furthermore, I have personally heard you promise Draupadī that you would bring forth the head of the killer of her sons.

sanskrit: tat asau vadhyatām pāpaḥ ātatāyī ātma bandhu hā bhartuḥ ca vipriyam vīra kṛtavān kula pāṁsanaḥ
english: This man is an assassin and murderer of your own family members. Not only that, but he has also dissatisfied his master. He is but the burnt remnants of his family. Kill him immediately.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca evam parīkṣatā dharmam pārthaḥ kṛṣṇena coditaḥ na aicchat hantum guru sutam yadyapi ātma hanam mahān
english: Sūta Gosvāmī said: Although Kṛṣṇa, who was examining Arjuna in religion, encouraged Arjuna to kill the son of Droṇācārya, Arjuna, a great soul, did not like the idea of killing him, although Aśvatthāmā was a heinous murderer of Arjuna’s family members.

sanskrit: atha upetya sva śibiram govinda priya sārathiḥ nyavedayat tam priyāyai śocantyai ātma jān hatān
english: After reaching his own camp, Arjuna, along with his dear friend and charioteer [Śrī Kṛṣṇa], entrusted the murderer unto his dear wife, who was lamenting for her murdered sons.

sanskrit: tathā āhṛtam paśu vat pāśa baddham avāk mukham karma jugupsitena nirīkṣya kṛṣṇā apakṛtam guroḥ sutam vāma svabhāvā kṛpayā nanāma ca
english: Śrī Sūta Gosvāmī said: Draupadī then saw Aśvatthāmā, who was bound with ropes like an animal and silent for having enacted the most inglorious murder. Due to her female nature, and due to her being naturally good and well-behaved, she showed him due respects as a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: uvāca ca asahantī asya bandhana ānayanam satī mucyatām mucyatām eṣaḥ brāhmaṇaḥ nitarām guruḥ
english: She could not tolerate Aśvatthāmā’s being bound by ropes, and being a devoted lady, she said: Release him, release him, for he is a brāhmaṇa, our spiritual master.

sanskrit: sa rahasyaḥ dhanuḥ vedaḥ sa visarga upasaṁyamaḥ astra grāmaḥ ca bhavatā śikṣitaḥ yat anugrahāt
english: It was by Droṇācārya’s mercy that you learned the military art of throwing arrows and the confidential art of controlling weapons.

sanskrit: saḥ eṣaḥ bhagavān droṇaḥ prajā rūpeṇa vartate tasya ātmanaḥ ardham patnī āste na anvagāt vīrasūḥ kṛpī
english: He [Droṇācārya] is certainly still existing, being represented by his son. His wife Kṛpī did not undergo a satī with him because she had a son.

sanskrit: tat dharma jña mahā bhāga bhavadbhiḥ gauravam kulam vṛjinam na arhati prāptum pūjyam vandyam abhīkṣṇaśaḥ
english: O most fortunate one who know the principles of religion, it is not good for you to cause grief to glorious family members who are always respectable and worshipful.

sanskrit: mā rodīt asya jananī gautamī pati devatā yathā aham mṛta vatsā ārtā rodimi aśru mukhī muhuḥ
english: My lord, do not make the wife of Droṇācārya cry like me. I am aggrieved for the death of my sons. She need not cry constantly like me.

sanskrit: yaiḥ kopitam brahma kulam rājanyaiḥ ajita ātmabhiḥ tat kulam pradahati āśu sa anubandham śucā arpitam
english: If the kingly administrative order, being unrestricted in sense control, offends the brāhmaṇa order and enrages them, then the fire of that rage burns up the whole body of the royal family and brings grief upon them all.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca dharmyam nyāyyam sa karuṇam nirvyalīkam samam mahat rājā dharma sutaḥ rājñyāḥ pratyanandat vacaḥ dvijāḥ
english: Sūta Gosvāmī said: O brāhmaṇas, King Yudhiṣṭhira fully supported the statements of the Queen, which were in accordance with the principles of religion and were justified, glorious, full of mercy and equity, and without duplicity.

sanskrit: nakulaḥ sahadevaḥ ca yuyudhānaḥ dhanañjayaḥ bhagavān devakī putraḥ ye ca anye yāḥ ca yoṣitaḥ
english: Nakula and Sahadeva [the younger brothers of the King] and also Sātyaki, Arjuna, the Personality of Godhead Lord Sri Kṛṣṇa, son of Devakī, and the ladies and others all unanimously agreed with the King.

sanskrit: tatra āha amarṣitaḥ bhīmaḥ tasya śreyān vadhaḥ smṛtaḥ na bhartuḥ na ātmanaḥ ca arthe yaḥ ahan suptān śiśūn vṛthā
english: Bhīma, however, angrily disagreed with them and recommended killing this culprit, who had murdered sleeping children for no purpose and for neither his nor his master’s interest.

sanskrit: niśamya bhīma gaditam draupadyāḥ ca catuḥ bhujaḥ ālokya vadanam sakhyuḥ idam āha hasan iva
english: Caturbhuja [the four-armed one], or the Personality of Godhead, after hearing the words of Bhīma, Draupadī and others, saw the face of His dear friend Arjuna, and He began to speak as if smiling.

sanskrit: śrī bhagavān uvāca brahma bandhuḥ na hantavyaḥ ātatāyī vadha arhaṇaḥ mayā eva ubhayam āmnātam paripāhi anuśāsanam kuru pratiśrutam satyam yat tat sāntvayatā priyām priyam ca bhīmasenasya pāñcālyāḥ mahyam eva ca
english: The Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: A friend of a brāhmaṇa is not to be killed, but if he is an aggressor he must be killed. All these rulings are in the scriptures, and you should act accordingly. You have to fulfill your promise to your wife, and you must also act to the satisfaction of Bhīmasena and Me.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca arjunaḥ sahasā ājñāya hareḥ hārdam atha asinā maṇim jahāra mūrdhanyam dvijasya saha mūrdhajam
english: Sūta Gosvāmī said: Just then Arjuna could understand the motive of the Lord by His equivocal orders, and thus with his sword he severed both hair and jewel from the head of Aśvatthāmā.

sanskrit: vimucya raśanā baddham bāla hatyā hata prabham tejasā maṇinā hīnam śibirāt nirayāpayat
english: He [Aśvatthāmā] had already lost his bodily luster due to infanticide, and now, moreover, having lost the jewel from his head, he lost even more strength. Thus he was unbound and driven out of the camp.

sanskrit: vapanam draviṇa adānam sthānāt niryāpaṇam tathā eṣaḥ hi brahma bandhūnām vadhaḥ na anyaḥ asti daihikaḥ
english: Cutting the hair from his head, depriving him of his wealth and driving him from his residence are the prescribed punishments for the relative of a brāhmaṇa. There is no injunction for killing the body.

sanskrit: putra śoka āturāḥ sarve pāṇḍavāḥ saha kṛṣṇayā svānām mṛtānām yat kṛtyam cakruḥ nirharaṇa ādikam
english: Thereafter, the sons of Pāṇḍu, and Draupadī, overwhelmed with grief, performed the proper rituals for the dead bodies of their relatives.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca atha te samparetānām svānām udakam icchatām dātum sa kṛṣṇāḥ gaṅgāyām puraskṛtya yayuḥ striyaḥ
english: Sūta Gosvāmī said: Thereafter the Pāṇḍavas, desiring to deliver water to the dead relatives who had desired it, went to the Ganges with Draupadī. The ladies walked in front.

sanskrit: te ninīya udakam sarve vilapya ca bhṛśam punaḥ āplutāḥ hari pādābja rajaḥ pūta sarit jale
english: Having lamented over them and sufficiently offered Ganges water, they bathed in the Ganges, whose water is sanctified due to being mixed with the dust of the lotus feet of the Lord.

sanskrit: tatra āsīnam kuru patim dhṛtarāṣṭram saha anujam gāndhārīm putra śoka artām pṛthām kṛṣṇām ca mādhavaḥ
english: There sat the King of the Kurus, Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira, along with his younger brothers and Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gāndhārī, Kuntī and Draupadī, all overwhelmed with grief. Lord Kṛṣṇa was also there.

sanskrit: sāntvayām āsa munibhiḥ hata bandhūn śucārpitān bhūteṣu kālasya gatim darśayan na pratikriyām
english: Citing the stringent laws of the Almighty and their reactions upon living beings, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa and the munis began to pacify those who were shocked and affected.

sanskrit: sādhayitvā ajāta śatroḥ svam rājyam kitavaiḥ hṛtam ghātayitvā asataḥ rājñaḥ kaca sparśa kṣata āyuṣaḥ
english: The clever Duryodhana and his party cunningly usurped the kingdom of Yudhiṣṭhira, who had no enemy. By the grace of the Lord, the recovery was executed, and the unscrupulous kings who joined with Duryodhana were killed by Him. Others also died, their duration of life having decreased for their rough handling of the hair of Queen Draupadī.

sanskrit: yājayitvā aśvamedhaiḥ tam tribhiḥ uttama kalpakaiḥ tat yaśaḥ pāvanam dikṣu śata manyoḥ iva atanot
english: Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa caused three well-performed aśvamedha-yajñas [horse sacrifices] to be conducted by Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira and thus caused his virtuous fame to be glorified in all directions, like that of Indra, who had performed one hundred such sacrifices.

sanskrit: āmantrya pāṇḍu putrān ca śaineya uddhava saṁyutaḥ dvaipāyana ādibhiḥ vipraiḥ pūjitaiḥ pratipūjitaḥ
english: Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa then prepared for His departure. He invited the sons of Pāṇḍu, after having been worshiped by the brāhmaṇas, headed by Śrīla Vyāsadeva. The Lord also reciprocated greetings.

sanskrit: gantum kṛtamatiḥ brahman dvārakām ratham āsthitaḥ upalebhe abhidhāvantīm uttarām bhaya vihvalām
english: As soon as He seated Himself on the chariot to start for Dvārakā, He saw Uttarā hurrying toward Him in fear.

sanskrit: uttarā uvāca pāhi pāhi mahā yogin deva deva jagat pate na anyam tvat abhayam paśye yatra mṛtyuḥ parasparam
english: Uttarā said: O Lord of lords, Lord of the universe! You are the greatest of mystics. Please protect me, protect me, for there is no one else who can save me from the clutches of death in this world of duality.

sanskrit: abhidravati mām īśa śaraḥ tapta ayasaḥ vibho kāmam dahatu mām nātha mā me garbhaḥ nipātyatām
english: O my Lord, You are all-powerful. A fiery iron arrow is coming towards me fast. My Lord, let it burn me personally, if You so desire, but please do not let it burn and abort my embryo. Please do me this favor, my Lord.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca upadhārya vacaḥ tasyāḥ bhagavān bhakta vatsalaḥ apāṇḍavam idam kartum drauṇeḥ astram abudhyata
english: Sūta Gosvāmī said: Having patiently heard her words, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is always very affectionate to His devotees, could at once understand that Aśvatthāmā, the son of Droṇācārya, had thrown the brahmāstra to finish the last life in the Pāṇḍava family.

sanskrit: tarhi eva atha muni śreṣṭha pāṇḍavāḥ pañca sāyakān ātmanaḥ abhimukhān dīptān ālakṣya astrāṇi upādaduḥ
english: O foremost among the great thinkers [munis] [Śaunaka], seeing the glaring brahmāstra proceeding towards them, the Pāṇḍavas took up their five respective weapons.

sanskrit: vyasanam vīkṣya tat teṣām ananya viṣaya ātmanām sudarśanena sva astreṇa svānām rakṣām vyadhāt vibhuḥ
english: The almighty Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, having observed that a great danger was befalling His unalloyed devotees, who were fully surrendered souls, at once took up His Sudarśana disc to protect them.

sanskrit: antaḥsthaḥ sarva bhūtānām ātmā yoga īśvaraḥ hariḥ sva māyayā āvṛṇot garbham vairāṭyāḥ kuru tantave
