english: The Lord of supreme mysticism, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, resides within everyone’s heart as the Paramātmā. As such, just to protect the progeny of the Kuru dynasty, He covered the embryo of Uttarā by His personal energy.

sanskrit: yadyapi astram brahma śiraḥ tu amogham ca apratikriyam vaiṣṇavam tejaḥ āsādya samaśāmyat bhṛgu udvaha
english: O Śaunaka, glory of Bhṛgu’s family, although the supreme brahmāstra weapon released by Aśvatthāmā was irresistible and without check or counteraction, it was neutralized and foiled when confronted by the strength of Viṣṇu [Lord Kṛṣṇa].

sanskrit: mā maṁsthāḥ hi etat āścaryam sarva āścarya maye acyute yaḥ idam māyayā devyā sṛjati avati hanti ajaḥ
english: O brāhmaṇas, do not think this to be especially wonderful in the activities of the mysterious and infallible Personality of Godhead. By His own transcendental energy He creates, maintains and annihilates all material things, although He Himself is unborn.

sanskrit: brahma tejaḥ vinirmuktaiḥ ātma jaiḥ saha kṛṣṇayā prayāṇa abhimukham kṛṣṇam idam āha pṛthā satī
english: Thus saved from the radiation of the brahmāstra, Kuntī, the chaste devotee of the Lord, and her five sons and Draupadī addressed Lord Kṛṣṇa as He started for home.

sanskrit: kuntī uvāca namasye puruṣam tvā ādyam īśvaram prakṛteḥ param alakṣyam sarva bhūtānām antaḥ bahiḥ avasthitam
english: Śrīmatī Kuntī said: O Kṛṣṇa, I offer my obeisances unto You because You are the original personality and are unaffected by the qualities of the material world. You are existing both within and without everything, yet You are invisible to all.

sanskrit: māyā javanikā ācchannam ajñā adhokṣajam avyayam na lakṣyase mūḍha dṛśā naṭaḥ nāṭya dharaḥ yathā
english: Being beyond the range of limited sense perception, You are the eternally irreproachable factor covered by the curtain of deluding energy. You are invisible to the foolish observer, exactly as an actor dressed as a player is not recognized.

sanskrit: tathā paramahaṁsānām munīnām amala ātmanām bhakti yoga vidhāna artham katham paśyema hi striyaḥ
english: You Yourself descend to propagate the transcendental science of devotional service unto the hearts of the advanced transcendentalists and mental speculators, who are purified by being able to discriminate between matter and spirit. How then can we women know You perfectly?

sanskrit: kṛṣṇāya vāsudevāya devakī nandanāya ca nanda gopa kumārāya govindāya namaḥ namaḥ
english: Let me therefore offer my respectful obeisances unto the Lord, who has become the son of Vasudeva, the pleasure of Devakī, the boy of Nanda and the other cowherd men of Vṛndāvana, and the enlivener of the cows and the senses.

sanskrit: namaḥ paṅkaja nābhāya namaḥ paṅkaja māline namaḥ paṅkaja netrāya namaḥ te paṅkaja aṅghraye
english: My respectful obeisances are unto You, O Lord, whose abdomen is marked with a depression like a lotus flower, who are always decorated with garlands of lotus flowers, whose glance is as cool as the lotus and whose feet are engraved with lotuses.

sanskrit: yathā hṛṣīkeśa khalena devakī kaṁsena ruddhā ati ciram śuca arpitā vimocitā aham ca saha ātma jā vibho tvayā eva nāthena muhuḥ vipat gaṇāt
english: O Hṛṣīkeśa, master of the senses and Lord of lords, You have released Your mother, Devakī, who was long imprisoned and distressed by the envious King Kaṁsa, and me and my children from a series of constant dangers.

sanskrit: viṣāt mahā agneḥ puruṣa ada darśanāt asat sabhāyāḥ vana vāsa kṛcchrataḥ mṛdhe mṛdhe aneka mahā ratha astrataḥ drauṇi astrataḥ ca āsma hare abhirakṣitāḥ
english: My dear Kṛṣṇa, Your Lordship has protected us from a poisoned cake, from a great fire, from cannibals, from the vicious assembly, from sufferings during our exile in the forest and from the battle where great generals fought. And now You have saved us from the weapon of Aśvatthāmā.

sanskrit: vipadaḥ santu tāḥ śaśvat tatra tatra jagat guro bhavataḥ darśanam yat syāt apunaḥ bhava darśanam
english: I wish that all those calamities would happen again and again so that we could see You again and again, for seeing You means that we will no longer see repeated births and deaths.

sanskrit: janma aiśvarya śruta śrībhiḥ edhamāna madaḥ pumān na eva arhati abhidhātum vai tvām akiñcana gocaram
english: My Lord, Your Lordship can easily be approached, but only by those who are materially exhausted. One who is on the path of [material] progress, trying to improve himself with respectable parentage, great opulence, high education and bodily beauty, cannot approach You with sincere feeling.

sanskrit: namaḥ akiñcana vittāya nivṛtta guṇa vṛttaye ātma ārāmāya śāntāya kaivalya pataye namaḥ
english: My obeisances are unto You, who are the property of the materially impoverished. You have nothing to do with the actions and reactions of the material modes of nature. You are self-satisfied, and therefore You are the most gentle and are master of the monists.

sanskrit: manye tvām kālam īśānam anādi nidhanam vibhum samam carantam sarvatra bhūtānām yat mithaḥ kaliḥ
english: My Lord, I consider Your Lordship to be eternal time, the supreme controller, without beginning and end, the all-pervasive one. In distributing Your mercy, You are equal to everyone. The dissensions between living beings are due to social intercourse.

sanskrit: na veda kaścit bhagavan cikīrṣitam tava īhamānasya nṛṇām viḍambanam na yasya kaścit dayitaḥ asti karhicit dveṣyaḥ ca yasmin viṣamā matiḥ nṛṇām
english: O Lord, no one can understand Your transcendental pastimes, which appear to be human and so are misleading. You have no specific object of favor, nor do You have any object of envy. People only imagine that You are partial.

sanskrit: janma karma ca viśva ātman ajasya akartuḥ ātmanaḥ tiryak nṛ ṛṣiṣu yādaḥsu tat atyanta viḍambanam
english: Of course it is bewildering, O soul of the universe, that You work, though You are inactive, and that You take birth, though You are the vital force and the unborn. You Yourself descend amongst animals, men, sages and aquatics. Verily, this is bewildering.

sanskrit: gopī ādade tvayi kṛtāgasi dāma tāvat yā te daśā aśru kalila añjana sambhrama akṣam vaktram ninīya bhaya bhāvanayā sthitasya sā mām vimohayati bhīḥ api yat bibheti
english: My dear Kṛṣṇa, Yaśodā took up a rope to bind You when You committed an offense, and Your perturbed eyes overflooded with tears, which washed the mascara from Your eyes. And You were afraid, though fear personified is afraid of You. This sight is bewildering to me.

sanskrit: kecit āhuḥ ajam jātam puṇya ślokasya kīrtaye yadoḥ priyasya anvavāye malayasya iva candanam
english: Some say that the Unborn is born for the glorification of pious kings, and others say that He is born to please King Yadu, one of Your dearest devotees. You appear in his family as sandalwood appears in the Malaya hills.

sanskrit: apare vasudevasya devakyām yācitaḥ abhyagāt ajaḥ tvam asya kṣemāya vadhāya ca sura dviṣām
english: Others say that since both Vasudeva and Devakī prayed for You, You have taken Your birth as their son. Undoubtedly You are unborn, yet You take Your birth for their welfare and to kill those who are envious of the demigods.

sanskrit: bhāra avatāraṇāya anye bhuvaḥ nāvaḥ iva udadhau sīdantyāḥ bhūri bhāreṇa jātaḥ hi ātma bhuvā arthitaḥ
english: Others say that the world, being overburdened like a boat at sea, is much aggrieved, and that Brahmā, who is Your son, prayed for You, and so You have appeared to diminish the trouble.

sanskrit: bhave asmin kliśyamānānām avidyā kāma karmabhiḥ śravaṇa smaraṇa arhāṇi kariṣyan iti kecana
english: And yet others say that You appeared for the sake of rejuvenating the devotional service of hearing, remembering, worshiping and so on in order that the conditioned souls suffering from material pangs might take advantage and gain liberation.

sanskrit: śṛṇvanti gāyanti gṛṇanti abhīkṣṇaśaḥ smaranti nandanti tava īhitam janāḥ te eva paśyanti acireṇa tāvakam bhava pravāha uparamam pada ambujam
english: O Kṛṣṇa, those who continuously hear, chant and repeat Your transcendental activities, or take pleasure in others’ doing so, certainly see Your lotus feet, which alone can stop the repetition of birth and death.

sanskrit: api adya naḥ tvam sva kṛta īhita prabho jihāsasi svit suhṛdaḥ anujīvinaḥ yeṣām na ca anyat bhavataḥ pada ambujāt parāyaṇam rājasu yojita aṁhasām
english: O my Lord, You have executed all duties Yourself. Are you leaving us today, though we are completely dependent on Your mercy and have no one else to protect us, now when all kings are at enmity with us?

sanskrit: ke vayam nāma rūpābhyām yadubhiḥ saha pāṇḍavāḥ bhavataḥ adarśanam yarhi hṛṣīkāṇām iva īśituḥ
english: As the name and fame of a particular body is finished with the disappearance of the living spirit, similarly if You do not look upon us, all our fame and activities, along with the Pāṇḍavas and Yadus, will end at once.

sanskrit: na iyam śobhiṣyate tatra yathā idānīm gadādhara tvat padaiḥ aṅkitā bhāti sva lakṣaṇa vilakṣitaiḥ
english: O Gadādhara [Kṛṣṇa], our kingdom is now being marked by the impressions of Your feet, and therefore it appears beautiful. But when You leave, it will no longer be so.

sanskrit: ime jana padāḥ svṛddhāḥ supakva auṣadhi vīrudhaḥ vana adri nadī udanvantaḥ hi edhante tava vīkṣitaiḥ
english: All these cities and villages are flourishing in all respects because the herbs and grains are in abundance, the trees are full of fruits, the rivers are flowing, the hills are full of minerals and the oceans full of wealth. And this is all due to Your glancing over them.

sanskrit: atha viśva īśa viśva ātman viśva mūrte svakeṣu me sneha pāśam imam chindhi dṛḍham pāṇḍuṣu vṛṣṇiṣu
english: O Lord of the universe, soul of the universe, O personality of the form of the universe, please, therefore, sever my tie of affection for my kinsmen, the Pāṇḍavas and the Vṛṣṇis.

sanskrit: tvayi me ananya viṣayā matiḥ madhu pate asakṛt ratim udvahatāt addhā gaṅgā iva ogham udanvati
english: O Lord of Madhu, as the Ganges forever flows to the sea without hindrance, let my attraction be constantly drawn unto You without being diverted to anyone else.

sanskrit: śrī kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa sakha vṛṣṇi ṛṣabha avani dhruk rājanya vaṁśa dahana anapavarga vīrya govinda go dvija sura arti hara avatāra yoga īśvara akhila guro bhagavan namaḥ te
english: O Kṛṣṇa, O friend of Arjuna, O chief amongst the descendants of Vṛṣṇi, You are the destroyer of those political parties which are disturbing elements on this earth. Your prowess never deteriorates. You are the proprietor of the transcendental abode, and You descend to relieve the distresses of the cows, the brāhmaṇas and the devotees. You possess all mystic powers, and You are the preceptor of the entire universe. You are the almighty God, and I offer You my respectful obeisances.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca pṛthayā ittham kala padaiḥ pariṇūta akhila udayaḥ mandam jahāsa vaikuṇṭhaḥ mohayan iva māyayā
english: Sūta Gosvāmī said: The Lord, thus hearing the prayers of Kuntīdevī, composed in choice words for His glorification, mildly smiled. That smile was as enchanting as His mystic power.

sanskrit: tām bāḍham iti upāmantrya praviśya gajasāhvayam striyaḥ ca sva puram yāsyan premṇā rājñā nivāritaḥ
english: Thus accepting the prayers of Śrīmatī Kuntīdevī, the Lord subsequently informed other ladies of His departure by entering the palace of Hastināpura. But upon preparing to leave, He was stopped by King Yudhiṣṭhira, who implored Him lovingly.

sanskrit: vyāsa ādyaiḥ īśvara īhā jñaiḥ kṛṣṇena adbhuta karmaṇā prabodhitaḥ api itihāsaiḥ na abudhyata śucā arpitaḥ
english: King Yudhiṣṭhira, who was much aggrieved, could not be convinced, despite instructions by great sages headed by Vyāsa and the Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself, the performer of superhuman feats, and despite all historical evidence.

sanskrit: āha rājā dharma sutaḥ cintayan suhṛdām vadham prākṛtena ātmanā viprāḥ sneha moha vaśam gataḥ
english: King Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Dharma, overwhelmed by the death of his friends, was aggrieved just like a common, materialistic man. O sages, thus deluded by affection, he began to speak.

sanskrit: aho me paśyata ajñānam hṛdi rūḍham durātmanaḥ pārakyasya eva dehasya bahvyaḥ me akṣauhiṇīḥ hatāḥ
english: King Yudhiṣṭhira said: O my lot! I am the most sinful man! Just see my heart, which is full of ignorance! This body, which is ultimately meant for others, has killed many, many phalanxes of men.

sanskrit: bāla dvi ja suhṛt mitra pitṛ bhrātṛ guru druhaḥ na me syāt nirayāt mokṣaḥ hi api varṣa ayuta āyutaiḥ
english: I have killed many boys, brāhmaṇas, well-wishers, friends, parents, preceptors and brothers. Though I live millions of years, I will not be relieved from the hell that awaits me for all these sins.

sanskrit: na enaḥ rājñaḥ prajā bhartuḥ dharma yuddhe vadhaḥ dviṣām iti me na tu bodhāya kalpate śāsanam vacaḥ
english: There is no sin for a king who kills for the right cause, who is engaged in maintaining his citizens. But this injunction is not applicable to me.

sanskrit: strīṇām mat hata bandhūnām drohaḥ yaḥ asau iha utthitaḥ karmabhiḥ gṛhamedhīyaiḥ na aham kalpaḥ vyapohitum
english: I have killed many friends of women, and I have thus caused enmity to such an extent that it is not possible to undo it by material welfare work.

sanskrit: yathā paṅkena paṅka ambhaḥ surayā vā surākṛtam bhūta hatyām tathā eva ekām na yajñaiḥ mārṣṭum arhati
english: As it is not possible to filter muddy water through mud, or purify a wine-stained pot with wine, it is not possible to counteract the killing of men by sacrificing animals.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca iti bhītaḥ prajā drohāt sarva dharma vivitsayā tataḥ vinaśanam prāgāt yatra deva vrataḥ apatat
english: Sūta Gosvāmī said: Being afraid for having killed so many subjects on the Battlefield of Kurukṣetra, Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira went to the scene of the massacre. There, Bhīṣmadeva was lying on a bed of arrows, about to pass away.

sanskrit: tadā te bhrātaraḥ sarve sat aśvaiḥ svarṇa bhūṣitaiḥ anvagacchan rathaiḥ viprāḥ vyāsa dhaumya ādayaḥ tathā
english: At that time all his brothers followed him on beautiful chariots drawn by first-class horses decorated with gold ornaments. With them were Vyāsa and ṛṣis like Dhaumya [the learned priest of the Pāṇḍavas] and others.

sanskrit: bhagavān api vipra ṛṣe rathena sa dhanañjayaḥ saḥ taiḥ vyarocata nṛpaḥ kuvera iva guhyakaiḥ
english: O sage amongst the brāhmaṇas, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Personality of Godhead, also followed, seated on a chariot with Arjuna. Thus King Yudhiṣṭhira appeared very aristocratic, like Kuvera surrounded by his companions [the Guhyakas].

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā nipatitam bhūmau divaḥ cyutam iva amaram praṇemuḥ pāṇḍavāḥ bhīṣmam sa anugāḥ saha cakriṇā
english: Seeing him [Bhīṣma] lying on the ground, like a demigod fallen from the sky, the Pāṇḍava King Yudhiṣṭhira, along with his younger brothers and Lord Kṛṣṇa, bowed down before him.

sanskrit: tatra brahma ṛṣayaḥ sarve deva ṛṣayaḥ ca sattama rāja ṛṣayaḥ ca tatra āsan draṣṭum bharata puṅgavam
english: Just to see the chief of the descendants of King Bharata [Bhīṣma], all the great souls in the universe, namely the ṛṣis amongst the demigods, brāhmaṇas and kings, all situated in the quality of goodness, were assembled there.

sanskrit: parvataḥ nāradaḥ dhaumyaḥ bhagavān bādarāyaṇaḥ bṛhadaśvaḥ bharadvājaḥ sa śiṣyaḥ reṇukā sutaḥ vasiṣṭhaḥ indrapramadaḥ tritaḥ gṛtsamadaḥ asitaḥ kakṣīvān gautamaḥ atriḥ ca kauśikaḥ atha sudarśanaḥ
english: All the sages like Parvata Muni, Nārada, Dhaumya, Vyāsa the incarnation of God, Bṛhadaśva, Bharadvāja and Paraśurāma and disciples, Vasiṣṭha, Indrapramada, Trita, Gṛtsamada, Asita, Kakṣīvān, Gautama, Atri, Kauśika and Sudarśana were present.

sanskrit: anye ca munayaḥ brahman brahmarāta ādayaḥ amalāḥ śiṣyaiḥ upetāḥ ājagmuḥ kaśyapa āṅgirasa ādayaḥ
english: And many others like Śukadeva Gosvāmī and other purified souls, Kaśyapa and Āṅgirasa and others, all accompanied by their respective disciples, arrived there.

sanskrit: tān sametān mahā bhāgān upalabhya vasu uttamaḥ pūjayām āsa dharma jñaḥ deśa kāla vibhāga vit
english: Bhīṣmadeva, who was the best amongst the eight Vasus, received and welcomed all the great and powerful ṛṣis who were assembled there, for he knew perfectly all the religious principles according to time and place.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇam ca tat prabhāva jñaḥ āsīnam jagat īśvaram hṛdi stham pūjayām āsa māyayā upātta vigraham
english: Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa is situated in everyone’s heart, yet He manifests His transcendental form by His internal potency. This very Lord was sitting before Bhīṣmadeva, and since Bhīṣmadeva knew of His glories, he worshiped Him duly.

sanskrit: pāṇḍu putrān upāsīnān praśraya prema saṅgatān abhyācaṣṭa anurāga aśraiḥ andhībhūtena cakṣuṣā
english: The sons of Mahārāja Pāṇḍu were sitting silently nearby, overtaken with affection for their dying grandfather. Seeing this, Bhīṣmadeva congratulated them with feeling. There were tears of ecstasy in his eyes, for he was overwhelmed by love and affection.

sanskrit: aho kaṣṭam aho anyāyyam yat yūyam dharma nandanāḥ jīvitum na arhatha kliṣṭam vipra dharma acyuta āśrayāḥ
english: Bhīṣmadeva said: Oh, what terrible sufferings and what terrible injustices you good souls suffer for being the sons of religion personified. You did not deserve to remain alive under those tribulations, yet you were protected by the brāhmaṇas, God and religion.

sanskrit: saṁsthite ati rathe pāṇḍau pṛthā bāla prajā vadhūḥ yuṣmat kṛte bahūn kleśān prāptā toka vatī muhuḥ
english: As far as my daughter-in-law Kuntī is concerned, upon the great General Pāṇḍu’s death, she became a widow with many children, and therefore she suffered greatly. And when you were grown up she suffered a great deal also because of your actions.

sanskrit: sarvam kāla kṛtam manye bhavatām ca yat apriyam sa pālaḥ yat vaśe lokaḥ vāyoḥ iva ghana āvaliḥ
english: In my opinion, this is all due to inevitable time, under whose control everyone in every planet is carried, just as the clouds are carried by the wind.

sanskrit: yatra dharma sutaḥ rājā gadā pāṇiḥ vṛkodaraḥ kṛṣṇaḥ astrī gāṇḍivam cāpam suhṛt kṛṣṇaḥ tataḥ vipat
english: Oh, how wonderful is the influence of inevitable time! It is irreversible — otherwise, how can there be reverses in the presence of King Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of the demigod controlling religion; Bhīma, the great fighter with a club; the great bowman Arjuna with his mighty weapon Gāṇḍīva; and above all, the Lord, the direct well-wisher of the Pāṇḍavas?

sanskrit: na hi asya karhicit rājan pumān veda vidhitsitam yat vijijñāsayā yuktāḥ muhyanti kavayaḥ api hi
english: O King, no one can know the plan of the Lord [Śrī Kṛṣṇa]. Even though great philosophers inquire exhaustively, they are bewildered.

sanskrit: tasmāt idam daiva tantram vyavasya bharata ṛṣabha tasya anuvihitaḥ anāthāḥ nātha pāhi prajāḥ prabho
english: O best among the descendants of Bharata [Yudhiṣṭhira], I maintain, therefore, that all this is within the plan of the Lord. Accepting the inconceivable plan of the Lord, you must follow it. You are now the appointed administrative head, and, my lord, you should now take care of those subjects who are now rendered helpless.

sanskrit: eṣaḥ vai bhagavān sākṣāt ādyaḥ nārāyaṇaḥ pumān mohayan māyayā lokam gūḍhaḥ carati vṛṣṇiṣu
english: This Śrī Kṛṣṇa is no other than the inconceivable, original Personality of Godhead. He is the first Nārāyaṇa, the supreme enjoyer. But He is moving amongst the descendants of King Vṛṣṇi just like one of us, and He is bewildering us with His self-created energy.

sanskrit: asya anubhāvam bhagavān veda guhya tamam śivaḥ deva ṛṣiḥ nāradaḥ sākṣāt bhagavān kapilaḥ nṛpa
english: O King, Lord Śiva, Nārada the sage amongst the demigods, and Kapila, the incarnation of Godhead, all know very confidentially about His glories through direct contact.

sanskrit: yam manyase mātuleyam priyam mitram suhṛt tamam akaroḥ sacivam dūtam sauhṛdāt atha sārathim
english: O King, that personality whom, out of ignorance only, you thought to be your maternal cousin, your very dear friend, well-wisher, counselor, messenger, benefactor, etc., is that very Personality of Godhead Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: sarva ātmanaḥ sama dṛśaḥ hi advayasya anahaṅkṛteḥ tat kṛtam mati vaiṣamyam niravadyasya na kvacit
english: Being the Absolute Personality of Godhead, He is present in everyone’s heart. He is equally kind to everyone, and He is free from the false ego of differentiation. Therefore whatever He does is free from material inebriety. He is equibalanced.

sanskrit: tathāpi ekānta bhakteṣu paśya bhū pa anukampitam yat me asūn tyajataḥ sākṣāt kṛṣṇaḥ darśanam āgataḥ
english: Yet, despite His being equally kind to everyone, He has graciously come before me while I am ending my life, for I am His unflinching servitor.

sanskrit: bhaktyā āveśya manaḥ yasmin vācā yat nāma kīrtayan tyajan kalevaram yogī mucyate kāma karmabhiḥ
english: The Personality of Godhead, who appears in the mind of the devotee by attentive devotion and meditation and by chanting of the holy name, releases the devotee from the bondage of fruitive activities at the time of his quitting the material body.

sanskrit: saḥ deva devaḥ bhagavān pratīkṣatām kalevaram yāvat idam hinomi aham prasanna hāsa aruṇa locana ullasat mukha ambujaḥ dhyāna pathaḥ catur bhujaḥ
english: May my Lord, who is four-handed and whose beautifully decorated lotus face, with eyes as red as the rising sun, is smiling, kindly await me at that moment when I quit this material body.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca yudhiṣṭhiraḥ tat ākarṇya śayānam śara pañjare apṛcchat vividhān dharmān ṛṣīṇām ca anuśṛṇvatām
english: Sūta Gosvāmī said: Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira, after hearing Bhīṣmadeva speak in that appealing tone, asked him, in the presence of all the great ṛṣis, about the essential principles of various religious duties.

sanskrit: puruṣa sva bhāva vihitān yathā varṇam yathā āśramam vairāgya rāga upādhibhyām āmnāta ubhaya lakṣaṇān
english: At Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira’s inquiry, Bhīṣmadeva first defined all the classifications of castes and orders of life in terms of the individual’s qualifications. Then he systematically, in twofold divisions, described counteraction by detachment and interaction by attachment.

sanskrit: dāna dharmān rāja dharmān mokṣa dharmān vibhāgaśaḥ strī dharmān bhagavat dharmān samāsa vyāsa yogataḥ
english: He then explained, by divisions, acts of charity, the pragmatic activities of a king and activities for salvation. Then he described the duties of women and devotees, both briefly and extensively.

sanskrit: dharma artha kāma mokṣān ca saha upāyān yathā mune nānā ākhyāna itihāseṣu varṇayām āsa tattva vit
english: Then he described the occupational duties of different orders and statuses of life, citing instances from history, for he was himself well acquainted with the truth.

sanskrit: dharmam pravadataḥ tasya saḥ kālaḥ pratyupasthitaḥ yaḥ yoginaḥ chanda mṛtyoḥ vāñchitaḥ tu uttarāyaṇaḥ
english: While Bhīṣmadeva was describing occupational duties, the sun’s course ran into the northern hemisphere. This period is desired by mystics who die at their will.

sanskrit: tadā upasaṁhṛtya giraḥ sahasraṇīḥ vimukta saṅgam manaḥ ādi pūruṣe kṛṣṇe lasat pīta paṭe catur bhuje puraḥ sthite amīlita dṛk vyadhārayat
english: Thereupon that man who spoke on different subjects with thousands of meanings, and who fought on thousands of battlefields and protected thousands of men, stopped speaking and, being completely freed from all bondage, withdrew his mind from everything else and fixed his wide-open eyes upon the original Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who stood before him, four-handed, dressed in yellow garments that glittered and shined.

sanskrit: viśuddhayā dhāraṇayā hata aśubhaḥ tat īkṣayā eva āśu gatā yudha śramaḥ nivṛtta sarva indriya vṛtti vibhramaḥ tuṣṭāva janyam visṛjan janārdanam
english: By pure meditation, looking at Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, he at once was freed from all material inauspiciousness and was relieved of all bodily pains caused by the arrow wounds. Thus all the external activities of his senses at once stopped, and he prayed transcendentally to the controller of all living beings while quitting his material body.

sanskrit: śrī bhīṣmaḥ uvāca iti matiḥ upakalpitā vitṛṣṇā bhagavati sātvata puṅgave vibhūmni sva sukham upagate kvacit vihartum prakṛtim upeyuṣi yat bhava pravāhaḥ
english: Bhīṣmadeva said: Let me now invest my thinking, feeling and willing, which were so long engaged in different subjects and occupational duties, in the all-powerful Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa. He is always self-satisfied, but sometimes, being the leader of the devotees, He enjoys transcendental pleasure by descending to the material world, although from Him only the material world is created.

sanskrit: tri bhuvana kamanam tamāla varṇam ravi kara gaura varāmbaram dadhāne vapuḥ alaka kula āvṛta anana abjam vijaya sakhe ratiḥ astu me anavadyā
english: Śrī Kṛṣṇa is the intimate friend of Arjuna. He has appeared on this earth in His transcendental body, which resembles the bluish color of the tamāla tree. His body attracts everyone in the three planetary systems [upper, middle and lower]. May His glittering yellow dress and His lotus face, covered with paintings of sandalwood pulp, be the object of my attraction, and may I not desire fruitive results.

sanskrit: yudhi turaga rajaḥ vidhūmra viṣvak kaca lulita śramavāri alaṅkṛta āsye mama niśita śaraiḥ vibhidyamāna tvaci vilasat kavace astu kṛṣṇe ātmā
english: On the battlefield [where Śrī Kṛṣṇa attended Arjuna out of friendship], the flowing hair of Lord Kṛṣṇa turned ashen due to the dust raised by the hoofs of the horses. And because of His labor, beads of sweat wetted His face. All these decorations, intensified by the wounds dealt by my sharp arrows, were enjoyed by Him. Let my mind thus go unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: sapadi sakhi vacaḥ niśamya madhye nija parayoḥ balayoḥ ratham niveśya sthitavati para sainika āyuḥ akṣṇā hṛtavati pārtha sakhe ratiḥ mama astu
english: In obedience to the command of His friend, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa entered the arena of the Battlefield of Kurukṣetra between the soldiers of Arjuna and Duryodhana, and while there He shortened the life spans of the opposite party by His merciful glance. This was done simply by His looking at the enemy. Let my mind be fixed upon that Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: vyavahita pṛtanā mukham nirīkṣya sva jana vadhāt vimukhasya doṣa buddhyā kumatim aharat ātma vidyayā yaḥ caraṇa ratiḥ paramasya tasya me astu
english: When Arjuna was seemingly polluted by ignorance upon observing the soldiers and commanders before him on the battlefield, the Lord eradicated his ignorance by delivering transcendental knowledge. May His lotus feet always remain the object of my attraction.

sanskrit: sva nigamam apahāya mat pratijñām ṛtam adhi kartum avaplutaḥ ratha sthaḥ dhṛta ratha caraṇaḥ abhyayāt caladguḥ hariḥ iva hantum ibham gata uttarīyaḥ
english: Fulfilling my vow and sacrificing His own promise, He got down from the chariot, took up its wheel, and ran towards me hurriedly, just as a lion goes to kill an elephant. He even dropped His outer garment on the way.

sanskrit: śita viśikha hataḥ viśīrṇa daṁśaḥ kṣataja pariplutaḥ ātatāyinaḥ me prasabham abhisasāra mat vadha artham saḥ bhavatu me bhagavān gatiḥ mukundaḥ
english: May He, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Personality of Godhead, who awards salvation, be my ultimate destination. On the battlefield He charged me, as if angry because of the wounds dealt by my sharp arrows. His shield was scattered, and His body was smeared with blood due to the wounds.

sanskrit: vijaya ratha kuṭumbe ātta totre dhṛta haya raśmini tat śriyā īkṣaṇīye bhagavati ratiḥ astu me mumūrṣoḥ yam iha nirīkṣya hatāḥ gatāḥ sva rūpam
english: At the moment of death, let my ultimate attraction be to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Personality of Godhead. I concentrate my mind upon the chariot driver of Arjuna who stood with a whip in His right hand and a bridle rope in His left, who was very careful to give protection to Arjuna’s chariot by all means. Those who saw Him on the Battlefield of Kurukṣetra attained their original forms after death.

sanskrit: lalita gati vilāsa valgu hāsa praṇaya nirīkṣaṇa kalpita urumānāḥ kṛtam anukṛtavatyaḥ unmada andhāḥ prakṛtim agan kila yasya gopa vadhvaḥ
english: Let my mind be fixed upon Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, whose motions and smiles of love attracted the damsels of Vrajadhāma [the gopīs]. The damsels imitated the characteristic movements of the Lord [after His disappearance from the rāsa dance].

sanskrit: muni gaṇa nṛpa varya saṅkule antaḥ sadasi yudhiṣṭhira rāja sūye eṣām arhaṇam upapeda īkṣaṇīyaḥ mama dṛśi gocaraḥ eṣaḥ āviḥ ātmā
english: At the Rājasūya-yajña [sacrifice] performed by Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira, there was the greatest assembly of all the elite men of the world, the royal and learned orders, and in that great assembly Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa was worshiped by one and all as the most exalted Personality of Godhead. This happened during my presence, and I remembered the incident in order to keep my mind upon the Lord.

sanskrit: tam imam aham ajam śarīra bhājām hṛdi hṛdi dhiṣṭhitam ātma kalpitānām pratidṛśam iva na ekadhā arkam ekam samadhigataḥ asmi vidhūta bheda mohaḥ
english: Now I can meditate with full concentration upon that one Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, now present before me because now I have transcended the misconceptions of duality in regard to His presence in everyone’s heart, even in the hearts of the mental speculators. He is in everyone’s heart. The sun may be perceived differently, but the sun is one.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca kṛṣṇe evam bhagavati manaḥ vāk dṛṣṭi vṛttibhiḥ ātmani ātmānam āveśya saḥ antaḥ śvāsaḥ upāramat
english: Sūta Gosvāmī said: Thus Bhīṣmadeva merged himself in the Supersoul, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, with his mind, speech, sight and actions, and thus he became silent, and his breathing stopped.

sanskrit: sampadyamānam ājñāya bhīṣmam brahmaṇi niṣkale sarve babhūvuḥ te tūṣṇīm vayāṁsi iva dina atyaye
english: Knowing that Bhīṣmadeva had merged into the unlimited eternity of the Supreme Absolute, all present there became silent like birds at the end of the day.

sanskrit: tatra dundubhayaḥ neduḥ deva mānava vāditāḥ śaśaṁsuḥ sādhavaḥ rājñām khāt petuḥ puṣpa vṛṣṭayaḥ
english: Thereafter, both men and demigods sounded drums in honor, and the honest royal order commenced demonstrations of honor and respect. And from the sky fell showers of flowers.

sanskrit: tasya nirharaṇa ādīni samparetasya bhārgava yudhiṣṭhiraḥ kārayitvā muhūrtam duḥkhitaḥ abhavat
english: O descendant of Bhṛgu [Śaunaka], after performing funeral rituals for the dead body of Bhīṣmadeva, Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira was momentarily overtaken with grief.

sanskrit: tuṣṭuvuḥ munayaḥ hṛṣṭāḥ kṛṣṇam tat guhya nāmabhiḥ tataḥ te kṛṣṇa hṛdayāḥ sva āśramān prayayuḥ punaḥ
english: All the great sages then glorified Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who was present there, by confidential Vedic hymns. Then all of them returned to their respective hermitages, bearing always Lord Kṛṣṇa within their hearts.

sanskrit: tataḥ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ gatvā saha kṛṣṇaḥ gajāhvayam pitaram sāntvayām āsa gāndhārīm ca tapasvinīm
english: Thereafter, Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira at once went to his capital, Hastināpura, accompanied by Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, and there he consoled his uncle and aunt Gāndhārī, who was an ascetic.

sanskrit: pitrā ca anumataḥ rājā vāsudeva anumoditaḥ cakāra rājyam dharmeṇa pitṛ paitāmaham vibhuḥ
english: After this, the great religious King, Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira, executed the royal power in the kingdom strictly according to the codes of royal principles approved by his uncle and confirmed by Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: śaunakaḥ uvāca hatvā svariktha spṛdhaḥ ātatāyinaḥ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ dharma bhṛtām variṣṭhaḥ saha anujaiḥ pratyavaruddha bhojanaḥ katham pravṛttaḥ kim akāraṣīt tataḥ
english: Śaunaka Muni asked: After killing his enemies who desired to usurp his rightful inheritance, how did the greatest of all religious men, Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira, assisted by his brothers, rule his subjects? Surely he could not freely enjoy his kingdom with unrestricted consciousness.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca vaṁśam kuroḥ vaṁśa dava agni nirhṛtam saṁrohayitvā bhava bhāvanaḥ hariḥ niveśayitvā nija rājye īśvaraḥ yudhiṣṭhiram prīta manāḥ babhūva ha
english: Sūta Gosvāmī said: Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is the maintainer of the world, became pleased after reestablishing Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira in his own kingdom and after restoring the Kuru dynasty, which had been exhausted by the bamboo fire of anger.

sanskrit: niśamya bhīṣma uktam atha acyuta uktam pravṛtta vijñāna vidhūta vibhramaḥ śaśāsa gām indra iva ajita āśrayaḥ paridhi upāntām anuja anuvartitaḥ
english: Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira, after being enlightened by what was spoken by Bhīṣmadeva and Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the infallible, engaged himself in matters of perfect knowledge because all his misgivings were eradicated. Thus he ruled over the earth and seas and was followed by his younger brothers.

sanskrit: kāmam vavarṣa parjanyaḥ sarva kāma dughā mahī siṣicuḥ sma vrajān gāvaḥ payasā udhasvatīḥ mudā
english: During the reign of Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira, the clouds showered all the water that people needed, and the earth produced all the necessities of man in profusion. Due to its fatty milk bag and cheerful attitude, the cow used to moisten the grazing ground with milk.

sanskrit: nadyaḥ samudrāḥ girayaḥ savanaspati vīrudhaḥ phalanti oṣadhayaḥ sarvāḥ kāmam anvṛtu tasya vai
english: The rivers, oceans, hills, mountains, forests, creepers and active drugs, in every season, paid their tax quota to the King in profusion.

sanskrit: na ādhayaḥ vyādhayaḥ kleśāḥ daiva bhūta ātma hetavaḥ ajāta śatrau abhavan jantūnām rājñi karhicit
english: Because of the King’s having no enemy, the living beings were not at any time disturbed by mental agonies, diseases, or excessive heat or cold.

sanskrit: uṣitvā hāstinapure māsān katipayān hariḥ suhṛdām ca viśokāya svasuḥ ca priya kāmyayā
english: Śrī Hari, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, resided at Hastināpura for a few months to pacify His relatives and please His own sister [Subhadrā].

sanskrit: āmantrya ca abhyanujñātaḥ pariṣvajya abhivādya tam āruroha ratham kaiścit pariṣvaktaḥ abhivāditaḥ
english: Afterwards, when the Lord asked permission to depart and the King gave it, the Lord offered His respects to Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira by bowing down at his feet, and the King embraced Him. After this the Lord, being embraced by others and receiving their obeisances, got into His chariot.

sanskrit: subhadrā draupadī kuntī virāṭa tanayā tathā gāndhārī dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ ca yuyutsuḥ gautamaḥ yamau vṛkodaraḥ ca dhaumyaḥ ca striyaḥ matsya sutā ādayaḥ na sehire vimuhyantaḥ viraham śārṅga dhanvanaḥ
english: At that time Subhadrā, Draupadī, Kuntī, Uttarā, Gāndhārī, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Yuyutsu, Kṛpācārya, Nakula, Sahadeva, Bhīmasena, Dhaumya and Satyavatī all nearly fainted because it was impossible for them to bear separation from Lord Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: sat saṅgāt mukta duḥsaṅgaḥ hātum na utsahate budhaḥ kīrtyamānam yaśaḥ yasya sakṛt ākarṇya rocanam tasmin nyasta dhiyaḥ pārthāḥ saheran viraham katham darśana sparśa saṁlāpa śayana āsana bhojanaiḥ
english: The intelligent, who have understood the Supreme Lord in association with pure devotees and have become freed from bad materialistic association, can never avoid hearing the glories of the Lord, even though they have heard them only once. How then could the Pāṇḍavas tolerate His separation, for they had been intimately associated with His person, seeing Him face to face, touching Him, conversing with Him, and sleeping, sitting and dining with Him?

sanskrit: sarve te animiṣaiḥ akṣaiḥ tam anu druta cetasaḥ vīkṣantaḥ sneha sambaddhāḥ viceluḥ tatra tatra ha
english: All their hearts were melting for Him on the pot of attraction. They looked at Him without blinking their eyes, and they moved hither and thither in perplexity.

sanskrit: nyarundhan udgalat bāṣpam autkaṇṭhyāt devakī sute niryāti agārāt naḥ abhadram iti syāt bāndhava striyaḥ
english: The female relatives, whose eyes were flooded with tears out of anxiety for Kṛṣṇa, came out of the palace. They could stop their tears only with great difficulty. They feared that tears would cause misfortune at the time of departure.

sanskrit: mṛdaṅga śaṅkha bheryaḥ ca vīṇā paṇava gomukhāḥ dhundhurī ānaka ghaṇṭā ādyāḥ neduḥ dundubhayaḥ tathā
english: While the Lord was departing from the palace of Hastināpura, different types of drums — like the mṛdaṅga, dhola, nagra, dhundhurī and dundubhi — and flutes of different types, the vīṇā, gomukha and bherī, all sounded together to show Him honor.

sanskrit: prāsāda śikhara ārūḍhāḥ kuru nāryaḥ didṛkṣayā vavṛṣuḥ kusumaiḥ kṛṣṇam prema vrīḍā smita īkṣaṇāḥ
english: Out of a loving desire to see the Lord, the royal ladies of the Kurus got up on top of the palace, and smiling with affection and shyness, they showered flowers upon the Lord.

sanskrit: sita ātapatram jagrāha muktā dāma vibhūṣitam ratna daṇḍam guḍākeśaḥ priyaḥ priyatamasya ha
english: At that time Arjuna, the great warrior and conqueror of sleep, who is the intimate friend of the most beloved Supreme Lord, took up an umbrella which had a handle of jewels and was embroidered with lace and pearls.

sanskrit: uddhavaḥ sātyakiḥ ca eva vyajane parama adbhute vikīryamāṇaḥ kusumaiḥ reje madhu patiḥ pathi
english: Uddhava and Sātyaki began to fan the Lord with decorated fans, and the Lord, as the master of Madhu, seated on scattered flowers, commanded them along the road.

sanskrit: aśrūyanta āśiṣaḥ satyāḥ tatra tatra dvija īritāḥ na anurūpa anurūpāḥ ca nirguṇasya guṇa ātmanaḥ
english: It was being heard here and there that the benedictions being paid to Kṛṣṇa were neither befitting nor unbefitting because they were all for the Absolute, who was now playing the part of a human being.

sanskrit: anyonyam āsīt sañjalpaḥ uttama śloka cetasām kaurava indra pura strīṇām sarva śruti manaḥ haraḥ
english: Absorbed in the thought of the transcendental qualities of the Lord, who is sung in select poetry, the ladies on the roofs of all the houses of Hastināpura began to talk of Him. This talk was more attractive than the hymns of the Vedas.

sanskrit: saḥ vai kila ayam puruṣaḥ purātanaḥ yaḥ ekaḥ āsīt aviśeṣaḥ ātmani agre guṇebhyaḥ jagat ātmani īśvare nimīlita ātman niśi supta śaktiṣu
english: They said: Here He is, the original Personality of Godhead as we definitely remember Him. He alone existed before the manifested creation of the modes of nature, and in Him only, because He is the Supreme Lord, all living beings merge, as if sleeping at night, their energy suspended.

sanskrit: saḥ eva bhūyaḥ nija vīrya coditām sva jīva māyām prakṛtim sisṛkṣatīm anāma rūpa ātmani rūpa nāmanī vidhitsamānaḥ anusasāra śāstra kṛt
english: The Personality of Godhead, again desiring to give names and forms to His parts and parcels, the living entities, placed them under the guidance of material nature. By His own potency, material nature is empowered to re-create.

sanskrit: saḥ vai ayam yat padam atra sūrayaḥ jita indriyāḥ nirjita mātariśvanaḥ paśyanti bhakti utkalita amala ātmanā nanu eṣaḥ sattvam parimārṣṭum arhati
english: Here is the same Supreme Personality of Godhead whose transcendental form is experienced by the great devotees who are completely cleansed of material consciousness by dint of rigid devotional service and full control of life and the senses. And that is the only way to purify existence.

sanskrit: saḥ vai ayam sakhi anugīta sat kathaḥ vedeṣu guhyeṣu ca guhya vādibhiḥ yaḥ ekaḥ īśaḥ jagat ātma līlayā sṛjati avati atti na tatra sajjate
english: O dear friends, here is that very Personality of Godhead whose attractive and confidential pastimes are described in the confidential parts of Vedic literature by His great devotees. It is He only who creates, maintains and annihilates the material world and yet remains unaffected.

sanskrit: yadā hi adharmeṇa tamaḥ dhiyaḥ nṛpāḥ jīvanti tatra eṣaḥ hi sattvataḥ kila dhatte bhagam satyam ṛtam dayām yaśaḥ bhavāya rūpāṇi dadhat yuge yuge
english: Whenever there are kings and administrators living like animals in the lowest modes of existence, the Lord in His transcendental form manifests His supreme power, the Truth Positive, shows special mercy to the faithful, performs wonderful activities and manifests various transcendental forms as is necessary in different periods and ages.

sanskrit: aho alam ślāghya tamam yadoḥ kulam aho alam puṇya tamam madhoḥ vanam yat eṣaḥ puṁsām ṛṣabhaḥ śriyaḥ patiḥ sva janmanā caṅkramaṇena ca añcati
english: Oh, how supremely glorified is the dynasty of King Yadu, and how virtuous is the land of Mathurā, where the supreme leader of all living beings, the husband of the goddess of fortune, has taken His birth and wandered in His childhood.

sanskrit: aho bata svaḥ yaśasaḥ tiraskarī kuśasthalī puṇya yaśaskarī bhuvaḥ paśyanti nityam yat anugraha iṣitam smita avalokam sva patim sma yat prajāḥ
english: Undoubtedly it is wonderful that Dvārakā has defeated the glories of the heavenly planets and has enhanced the celebrity of the earth. The inhabitants of Dvārakā are always seeing the soul of all living beings [Kṛṣṇa] in His loving feature. He glances at them and favors them with sweet smiles.

sanskrit: nūnam vrata snāna huta ādinā īśvaraḥ samarcitaḥ hi asya gṛhīta pāṇibhiḥ pibanti yāḥ sakhi adhara amṛtam muhuḥ vraja striyaḥ sammumuhuḥ yat āśayāḥ
english: O friends, just think of His wives, whose hands He has accepted. How they must have undergone vows, baths, fire sacrifices and perfect worship of the Lord of the universe to constantly relish now the nectar from His lips [by kissing]. The damsels of Vrajabhūmi would often faint just by expecting such favors.

sanskrit: yā vīrya śulkena hṛtāḥ svayaṁvare pramathya caidya pramukhān hi śuṣmiṇaḥ pradyumna sāmba amba suta ādayaḥ aparāḥ yāḥ ca āhṛtāḥ bhauma vadhe sahasraśaḥ
english: The children of these ladies are Pradyumna, Sāmba, Amba, etc. Ladies like Rukmiṇī, Satyabhāmā and Jāmbavatī were forcibly taken away by Him from their svayaṁvara ceremonies after He defeated many powerful kings, headed by Śiśupāla. And other ladies were also forcibly taken away by Him after He killed Bhaumāsura and thousands of his assistants. All of these ladies are glorious.

sanskrit: etāḥ param strītvam apāstapeśalam nirasta śaucam bata sādhu kurvate yāsām gṛhāt puṣkara locanaḥ patiḥ na jātu apaiti āhṛtibhiḥ hṛdi spṛśan
english: All these women auspiciously glorified their lives despite their being without individuality and without purity. Their husband, the lotus-eyed Personality of Godhead, never left them alone at home. He always pleased their hearts by making valuable presentations.

sanskrit: evaṁvidhāḥ gadantīnām saḥ giraḥ pura yoṣitām nirīkṣaṇena abhinandan sa smitena yayau hariḥ
english: While the ladies of the capital [Hastināpura] were greeting Him and talking in this way, the Lord, smiling, accepted their good greetings, and casting the grace of His glance over them, He departed from the city.

sanskrit: ajāta śatruḥ pṛtanām gopīthāya madhu dviṣaḥ parebhyaḥ śaṅkitaḥ snehāt prāyuṅkta catuḥ aṅginīm
english: Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira, although no one’s enemy, engaged four divisions of defense [horse, elephant, chariot and army] to accompany Lord Kṛṣṇa, the enemy of the asuras [demons]. The Mahārāja did this because of the enemy, and also out of affection for the Lord.

sanskrit: atha dūrāgatān śauriḥ kauravān virahāturān sannivartya dṛḍham snigdhān prāyāt sva nagarīm priyaiḥ
english: Out of profound affection for Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Pāṇḍavas, who were of the Kuru dynasty, accompanied Him a considerable distance to see Him off. They were overwhelmed with the thought of future separation. The Lord, however, persuaded them to return home, and He proceeded towards Dvārakā with His dear companions.

sanskrit: kuru jāṅgala pāñcālān śūrasenān sa yāmunān brahmāvartam kurukṣetram matsyān sārasvatān atha maru dhanvam ati kramya sauvīra ābhīrayoḥ parān ānartān bhārgava upāgāt śrānta vāhaḥ manāk vibhuḥ
english: O Śaunaka, the Lord then proceeded towards Kurujāṅgala, Pāñcālā, Śūrasenā, the land on the bank of the river Yamunā, Brahmāvarta, Kurukṣetra, Matsya, Sārasvata, the province of the desert and the land of scanty water. After crossing these provinces He gradually reached the Sauvīra and Ābhīra provinces, then, west of these, reached Dvārakā at last.

sanskrit: tatra tatra ha tatratyaiḥ hariḥ pratyudyata arhaṇaḥ sāyam bheje diśam paścāt gaviṣthaḥ gām gataḥ tadā
english: On His journey through these provinces He was welcomed, worshiped and given various presentations. In the evening, in all places, the Lord suspended His journey to perform evening rites. This was regularly observed after sunset.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca ānartān saḥ upavrajya svṛddhān jana padān svakān dadhmau daravaram teṣām viṣādam śamayan iva
english: Sūta Gosvāmī said: Upon reaching the border of His most prosperous metropolis, known as the country of the Ānartas [Dvārakā], the Lord sounded His auspicious conchshell, heralding His arrival and apparently pacifying the dejection of the inhabitants.

sanskrit: saḥ uccakāśe dhavala udaraḥ daraḥ api urukramasya adharaśoṇa śoṇimā dādhmāyamānaḥ kara kañja sampuṭe yathā abja khaṇḍe kala haṁsaḥ utsvanaḥ
english: The white and fat-bowled conchshell, being gripped by the hand of Lord Kṛṣṇa and sounded by Him, appeared to be reddened by the touch of His transcendental lips. It seemed that a white swan was playing in the stems of red lotus flowers.

sanskrit: tam upaśrutya ninadam jagat bhaya bhaya āvaham prati udyayuḥ prajāḥ sarvāḥ bhartṛ darśana lālasāḥ
english: The citizens of Dvārakā, having heard that sound which threatens fear personified in the material world, began to run towards Him fast, just to have a long desired audience with the Lord, who is the protector of all devotees.

sanskrit: tatra upanīta balayaḥ raveḥ dīpam iva ādṛtāḥ ātma ārāmam pūrṇa kāmam nija lābhena nitya dā prīti utphulla mukhāḥ procuḥ harṣa gadgadayā girā pitaram sarva suhṛdam avitāram iva arbhakāḥ
english: The citizens arrived before the Lord with their respective presentations, offering them to the fully satisfied and self-sufficient one, who, by His own potency, incessantly supplies others. These presentations were like the offering of a lamp to the sun. Yet the citizens began to speak in ecstatic language to receive the Lord, just as wards welcome their guardian and father.

sanskrit: natāḥ sma te nātha sadā aṅghri paṅkajam viriñca vairiñcya sura indra vanditam parāyaṇam kṣemam iha icchatām param na yatra kālaḥ prabhavet paraḥ prabhuḥ
english: The citizens said: O Lord, You are worshiped by all demigods like Brahmā, the four Sanas and even the King of heaven. You are the ultimate rest for those who are really aspiring to achieve the highest benefit of life. You are the supreme transcendental Lord, and inevitable time cannot exert its influence upon You.

sanskrit: bhavāya naḥ tvam bhava viśva bhāvana tvam eva mātā atha suhṛt patiḥ pitā tvam sat guruḥ naḥ paramam ca daivatam yasya anuvṛttyā kṛtinaḥ babhūvima
english: O creator of the universe, You are our mother, well-wisher, Lord, father, spiritual master and worshipable Deity. By following in Your footsteps we have become successful in every respect. We pray, therefore, that You continue to bless us with Your mercy.

sanskrit: aho sa nāthāḥ bhavatā sma yat vayam traiviṣṭa pānām api dūra darśanam prema smita snigdha nirīkṣaṇa ānanam paśyema rūpam tava sarva saubhagam
english: Oh, it is our good luck that we have come again today under Your protection by Your presence, for Your Lordship rarely visits even the denizens of heaven. Now it is possible for us to look into Your smiling face, which is full of affectionate glances. We can now see Your transcendental form, full of all auspiciousness.

sanskrit: yarhi ambuja akṣa apasasāra bho bhavān kurūn madhūn vā atha suhṛt didṛkṣayā tatra abda koṭi pratimaḥ kṣaṇaḥ bhavet ravim vinā akṣṇoḥ iva naḥ tava acyuta
english: O lotus-eyed Lord, whenever You go away to Mathurā-Vṛndāvana or Hastināpura to meet Your friends and relatives, every moment of Your absence seems like millions of years. O infallible one, at that time our eyes become useless, as if bereft of sun.

sanskrit: katham vayam nātha ciroṣite tvayi prasanna dṛṣṭyā akhila tāpa śoṣaṇam jīvema te sundara hāsa śobhitam apaśyamānāḥ vadanam manoharam iti ca udīritāḥ vācaḥ prajānām bhakta vatsalaḥ śṛṇvānaḥ anugraham dṛṣṭyā vitanvan prāviśat puram
english: O master, if You live abroad all the time, then we cannot look at Your attractive face, whose smiles vanquish all our sufferings. How can we exist without Your presence?Upon hearing their speeches, the Lord, who is very kind to the citizens and the devotees, entered the city of Dvārakā and acknowledged all their greetings by casting His transcendental glance over them.

sanskrit: madhu bhoja daśārha arha kukura andhaka vṛṣṇibhiḥ ātma tulya balaiḥ guptām nāgaiḥ bhogavatīm iva
english: As Bhogavatī, the capital of Nāgaloka, is protected by the Nāgas, so was Dvārakā protected by the descendants of Vṛṣṇi — Bhoja, Madhu, Daśārha, Arha, Kukura, Andhaka, etc. — who were as strong as Lord Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: sarva ṛtu sarva vibhava puṇya vṛkṣa latā āśramaiḥ udyāna upavana ārāmaiḥ vṛta padma ākara śriyam
english: The city of Dvārakāpurī was filled with the opulences of all seasons. There were hermitages, orchards, flower gardens, parks and reservoirs of water breeding lotus flowers all over.

sanskrit: gopura dvāra mārgeṣu kṛta kautuka toraṇām citra dhvaja patākā agraiḥ antaḥ pratihata ātapām
english: The city gateway, the household doors and festooned arches along the roads were all nicely decorated with festive signs like plantain trees and mango leaves, all to welcome the Lord. Flags, garlands and painted signs and slogans all combined to shade the sunshine.

sanskrit: sammārjita mahā mārga rathya āpaṇaka catvarām siktām gandha jalaiḥ uptām phala puṣpa akṣata aṅkuraiḥ
english: The highways, subways, lanes, markets and public meeting places were all thoroughly cleansed and then moistened with scented water. And to welcome the Lord, fruits, flowers and unbroken seeds were strewn everywhere.

sanskrit: dvāri dvāri gṛhāṇām ca dadhi akṣata phala ikṣubhiḥ alaṅkṛtām pūrṇa kumbhaiḥ balibhiḥ dhūpa dīpakaiḥ
english: In each and every door of the residential houses, auspicious things like curd, unbroken fruits, sugarcane and full waterpots with articles for worship, incense and candles were all displayed.

sanskrit: niśamya preṣṭham āyāntam vasudevaḥ mahā manāḥ akrūraḥ ca ugrasenaḥ ca rāmaḥ ca adbhuta vikramaḥ pradyumnaḥ cārudeṣṇaḥ ca sāmbaḥ jāmbavatī sutaḥ praharṣa vega ucchaśita śayana āsana bhojanāḥ
english: On hearing that the most dear Kṛṣṇa was approaching Dvārakā-dhāma, magnanimous Vasudeva, Akrūra, Ugrasena, Balarāma (the superhumanly powerful), Pradyumna, Cārudeṣṇa and Sāmba the son of Jāmbavatī, all extremely happy, abandoned resting, sitting and dining.

sanskrit: vāraṇa indram puraskṛtya brāhmaṇaiḥ sa sumaṅgalaiḥ śaṅkha tūrya ninādena brahma ghoṣeṇa ca ādṛtāḥ prati ujjagmuḥ rathaiḥ hṛṣṭāḥ praṇayāgata sādhvasāḥ
english: They hastened toward the Lord on chariots with brāhmaṇas bearing flowers. Before them were elephants, emblems of good fortune. Conchshells and bugles were sounded, and Vedic hymns were chanted. Thus they offered their respects, which were saturated with affection.

sanskrit: vāramukhyāḥ ca śataśaḥ yānaiḥ tat darśana utsukāḥ lasat kuṇḍala nirbhāta kapola vadana śriyaḥ
english: At the same time, many hundreds of well-known prostitutes began to proceed on various vehicles. They were all very eager to meet the Lord, and their beautiful faces were decorated with dazzling earrings, which enhanced the beauty of their foreheads.

sanskrit: naṭa nartaka gandharvāḥ sūta māgadha vandinaḥ gāyanti ca uttamaśloka caritāni adbhutāni ca
english: Expert dramatists, artists, dancers, singers, historians, genealogists and learned speakers all gave their respective contributions, being inspired by the superhuman pastimes of the Lord. Thus they proceeded on and on.

sanskrit: bhagavān tatra bandhūnām paurāṇām anuvartinām yathā vidhi upasaṅgamya sarveṣām mānam ādadhe
english: Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Personality of Godhead, approached them and offered due honor and respect to each and every one of the friends, relatives, citizens and all others who came to receive and welcome Him.

sanskrit: prahvā abhivādana āśleṣa kara sparśa smita īkṣaṇaiḥ āśvāsya ca āśvapākebhyaḥ varaiḥ ca abhimataiḥ vibhuḥ
english: The almighty Lord greeted everyone present by bowing His head, exchanging greetings, embracing, shaking hands, looking and smiling, giving assurances and awarding benedictions, even to the lowest in rank.

sanskrit: svayam ca gurubhiḥ vipraiḥ sadāraiḥ sthaviraiḥ api āśīrbhiḥ yujyamānaḥ anyaiḥ vandibhiḥ ca aviśat puram
english: Then the Lord personally entered the city accompanied by elderly relatives and invalid brāhmaṇas with their wives, all offering benedictions and singing the glories of the Lord. Others also praised the glories of the Lord.

sanskrit: rāja mārgam gate kṛṣṇe dvārakāyāḥ kula striyaḥ harmyāṇi āruruhuḥ vipra tat īkṣaṇa mahā utsavāḥ
english: When Lord Kṛṣṇa passed over the public roads, all the ladies from the respectable families of Dvārakā went up to the roofs of their palaces just to have a look at the Lord. They considered this to be the greatest festival.

sanskrit: nityam nirīkṣamāṇānām yat api dvārakā okasām na vitṛpyanti hi dṛśaḥ śriyaḥ dhāma aṅgam acyutam
english: The inhabitants of Dvārakā were regularly accustomed to look upon the reservoir of all beauty, the infallible Lord, yet they were never satiated.

sanskrit: śriyaḥ nivāsaḥ yasya uraḥ pāna pātram mukham dṛśām bāhavaḥ loka pālānām sāraṅgāṇām pada ambujam
english: The Lord’s chest is the abode of the goddess of fortune. His moonlike face is the drinking vessel for eyes which hanker after all that is beautiful. His arms are the resting places for the administrative demigods. And His lotus feet are the refuge of pure devotees who never talk or sing of any subject except His Lordship.

sanskrit: sita ātapatra vyajanaiḥ upaskṛtaḥ prasūna varṣaiḥ abhivarṣitaḥ pathi piśaṅga vāsāḥ vana mālayā babhau ghanaḥ yathā arka uḍupa cāpa vaidyutaiḥ
english: As the Lord passed along the public road of Dvārakā, His head was protected from the sunshine by a white umbrella. White feathered fans moved in semicircles, and showers of flowers fell upon the road. His yellow garments and garlands of flowers made it appear as if a dark cloud were surrounded simultaneously by sun, moon, lightning and rainbows.

sanskrit: praviṣṭaḥ tu gṛham pitroḥ pariṣvaktaḥ sva mātṛbhiḥ vavande śirasā sapta devakī pramukhā mudā
english: After entering the house of His father, He was embraced by the mothers present, and the Lord offered His obeisances unto them by placing His head at their feet. The mothers were headed by Devakī [His real mother].

sanskrit: tāḥ putram aṅkam āropya sneha snuta payodharāḥ harṣa vihvalita ātmānaḥ siṣicuḥ netrajaiḥ jalaiḥ
english: The mothers, after embracing their son, sat Him on their laps. Due to pure affection, milk sprang from their breasts. They were overwhelmed with delight, and the tears from their eyes wetted the Lord.

sanskrit: atha aviśat sva bhavanam sarva kāmam anuttamam prāsādāḥ yatra patnīnām sahasrāṇi ca ṣoḍaśa
english: Thereafter, the Lord entered His palaces, which were perfect to the fullest extent. His wives lived in them, and they numbered over sixteen thousand.

sanskrit: patnyaḥ patim proṣya gṛha anupāgatam vilokya sañjāta manaḥ mahā utsavāḥ uttasthuḥ ārāt sahasā āsanā āśayāt sākam vrataiḥ vrīḍita locana ānanāḥ
english: The queens of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa rejoiced within their minds to see their husband home after a long period abroad. The queens got up at once from their seats and meditations. As was socially customary, they covered their faces shyly and looked about coyly.

sanskrit: tam ātma jaiḥ dṛṣṭibhiḥ antara ātmanā duranta bhāvāḥ parirebhire patim niruddham api āsravat ambu netrayoḥ vilajjatīnām bhṛgu varya vaiklavāt
english: The insuperable ecstasy was so strong that the queens, who were shy, first embraced the Lord in the innermost recesses of their hearts. Then they embraced Him visually, and then they sent their sons to embrace Him [which is equal to personal embracing]. But, O chief amongst the Bhṛgus, though they tried to restrain their feelings, they inadvertently shed tears.

sanskrit: yadi api asau pārśva gataḥ rahaḥ gataḥ tathāpi tasya aṅghri yugam navam navam pade pade kā virameta tat padāt calāpi yat śrīḥ na jahāti karhicit
english: Although Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa was constantly by their sides, as well as exclusively alone, His feet appeared to them to be newer and newer. The goddess of fortune, although by nature always restless and moving, could not quit the Lord’s feet. So what woman can be detached from those feet, having once taken shelter of them?

sanskrit: evam nṛpāṇām kṣiti bhāra janmanām akṣauhiṇībhiḥ parivṛtta tejasām vidhāya vairam śvasanaḥ yathā analam mithaḥ vadhena uparataḥ nirāyudhaḥ
english: The Lord was pacified after killing those kings who were burdensome to the earth. They were puffed up with their military strength, their horses, elephants, chariots, infantry, etc. He Himself was not a party in the fight. He simply created hostility between the powerful administrators, and they fought amongst themselves. He was like the wind which causes friction between bamboos and so sparks a fire.

sanskrit: saḥ eṣaḥ nara loke asmin avatīrṇaḥ sva māyayā reme strī ratna kūṭasthaḥ bhagavān prākṛtaḥ yathā
english: That Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, out of His causeless mercy, appeared on this planet by His internal potency and enjoyed Himself amongst competent women as if He were engaging in mundane affairs.

sanskrit: uddāma bhāva piśuna amala valgu hāsa vrīḍa avaloka nihataḥ madanaḥ api yāsām sammuhya cāpam ajahāt pramada uttamāḥ tā yasya indriyam vimathitum kuhakaiḥ na śekuḥ
english: Although the queens’ beautiful smiles and furtive glances were all spotless and exciting, and although they could conquer Cupid himself by making him give up his bow in frustration, and although even the tolerant Śiva could fall victim to them, still, despite all their magical feats and attractions, they could not agitate the senses of the Lord.

sanskrit: tam ayam manyate lokaḥ hi asaṅgam api saṅginam ātma aupamyena manujam vyāpṛṇvānam yataḥ abudhaḥ
english: The common materialistic conditioned souls speculate that the Lord is one of them. Out of their ignorance they think that the Lord is affected by matter, although He is unattached.

sanskrit: etat īśanam īśasya prakṛti sthaḥ api tat guṇaiḥ na yujyate sadā ātma sthaiḥ yathā buddhiḥ tat āśrayā
english: This is the divinity of the Personality of Godhead: He is not affected by the qualities of material nature, even though He is in contact with them. Similarly, the devotees who have taken shelter of the Lord do not become influenced by the material qualities.

sanskrit: tam menire abalāḥ mūḍhāḥ straiṇam ca anuvratam rahaḥ apramāṇa vidaḥ bhartuḥ īśvaram matayaḥ yathā
english: The simple and delicate women truly thought that Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, their beloved husband, followed them and was dominated by them. They were unaware of the extent of the glories of their husband, as the atheists are unaware of Him as the supreme controller.

sanskrit: śaunakaḥ uvāca aśvatthāmna upasṛṣṭena brahma śīrṣṇā uru tejasā uttarāyāḥ hataḥ garbhaḥ īśena ājīvitaḥ punaḥ
english: The sage Śaunaka said: The womb of Uttarā, mother of Mahārāja Parīkṣit, was spoiled by the dreadful and invincible brahmāstra weapon released by Aśvatthāmā. But Mahārāja Parīkṣit was saved by the Supreme Lord.

sanskrit: tasya janma mahā buddheḥ karmāṇi ca mahā ātmanaḥ nidhanam ca yathā eva āsīt saḥ pretya gatavān yathā
english: How was the great emperor Parīkṣit, who was a highly intelligent and great devotee, born in that womb? How did his death take place, and what did he achieve after his death?

sanskrit: tat idam śrotum icchāmaḥ gaditum yadi manyase brūhi naḥ śraddadhānānām yasya jñānam adāt śukaḥ
english: We all respectfully want to hear about him [Mahārāja Parīkṣit] to whom Śukadeva Gosvāmī imparted transcendental knowledge. Please speak on this matter.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca apīpalat dharma rājaḥ pitṛ vat rañjayan prajāḥ niḥspṛhaḥ sarva kāmebhyaḥ kṛṣṇa pāda anusevayā
english: Śrī Sūta Gosvāmī said: Emperor Yudhiṣṭhira administered generously to everyone during his reign. He was exactly like his father. He had no personal ambition and was freed from all sorts of sense gratification because of his continuous service unto the lotus feet of the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: sampadaḥ kratavaḥ lokāḥ mahiṣī bhrātaraḥ mahī jambu dvīpa ādhipatyam ca yaśaḥ ca tri divam gatam
english: News even reached the celestial planets about Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira’s worldly possessions, the sacrifices by which he would attain a better destination, his queen, his stalwart brothers, his extensive land, his sovereignty over the planet earth, his fame, etc.

sanskrit: kim te kāmāḥ sura spārhāḥ mukunda manasaḥ dvijāḥ adhijahruḥ mudam rājñaḥ kṣudhitasya yathā itare
english: O brāhmaṇas, the opulence of the King was so enchanting that the denizens of heaven aspired for it. But because he was absorbed in the service of the Lord, nothing could satisfy him except the Lord’s service.

sanskrit: mātuḥ garbha gataḥ vīraḥ saḥ tadā bhṛgu nandana dadarśa puruṣam kañcit dahyamānaḥ astra tejasā
english: O son of Bhṛgu [Śaunaka], when the child Parīkṣit, the great fighter, was in the womb of his mother, Uttarā, and was suffering from the burning heat of the brahmāstra [thrown by Aśvatthāmā], he could observe the Supreme Lord coming to him.

sanskrit: aṅguṣṭha mātram amalam sphurat puraṭa maulinam apīvya darśanam śyāmam taḍit vāsasam acyutam
english: He [the Lord] was only thumb high, but He was all transcendental. He had a very beautiful, blackish, infallible body, and He wore a dress of lightning yellow and a helmet of blazing gold. Thus He was seen by the child.

sanskrit: śrīmat dīrgha catuḥ bāhum tapta kāñcana kuṇḍalam kṣataja akṣam gadā pāṇim ātmanaḥ sarvataḥ diśam paribhramantam ulkābhām bhrāmayantam gadām muhuḥ
english: The Lord was enriched with four hands, earrings of molten gold and eyes blood red with fury. As He loitered about, His club constantly encircled Him like a shooting star.

sanskrit: astra tejaḥ sva gadayā nīhāram iva gopatiḥ vidhamantam sannikarṣe paryaikṣata kaḥ iti asau
english: The Lord was thus engaged in vanquishing the radiation of the brahmāstra, just as the sun evaporates a drop of dew. He was observed by the child, who thought about who He was.

sanskrit: vidhūya tat ameyātmā bhagavān dharma gup vibhuḥ miṣataḥ daśamāsasya tatra eva antaḥ dadhe hariḥ
english: While thus being observed by the child, the Supreme Lord Personality of Godhead, the Supersoul of everyone and the protector of the righteous, who stretches in all directions and who is unlimited by time and space, disappeared at once.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarva guṇa udarke sa anukūla grahodaye jajñe vaṁśa dharaḥ pāṇḍoḥ bhūyaḥ pāṇḍuḥ iva ojasā
english: Thereupon, when all the good signs of the zodiac gradually evolved, the heir apparent of Pāṇḍu, who would be exactly like him in prowess, took birth.

sanskrit: tasya prīta manāḥ rājā vipraiḥ dhaumya kṛpa ādibhiḥ jātakam kārayām āsa vācayitvā ca maṅgalam
english: King Yudhiṣṭhira, who was very satisfied with the birth of Mahārāja Parīkṣit, had the purificatory process of birth performed. Learned brāhmaṇas, headed by Dhaumya and Kṛpa, recited auspicious hymns.

sanskrit: hiraṇyam gām mahīm grāmān hasti aśvān nṛpatiḥ varān prādāt su annam ca viprebhyaḥ prajā tīrthe saḥ tīrtha vit
english: Upon the birth of a son, the King, who knew how, where and when charity should be given, gave gold, land, villages, elephants, horses and good food grains to the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: tam ūcuḥ brāhmaṇāḥ tuṣṭāḥ rājānam praśraya anvitam eṣaḥ hi asmin prajā tantau purūṇām paurava ṛṣabha
english: The learned brāhmaṇas, who were very satisfied with the charities of the King, addressed him as the chief amongst the Pūrus and informed him that his son was certainly in the line of descent from the Pūrus.

sanskrit: daivena apratighātena śukle saṁsthām upeyuṣi rātaḥ vaḥ anugraha arthāya viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā
english: The brāhmaṇas said: This spotless son has been restored by the all-powerful and all-pervasive Lord Viṣṇu, the Personality of Godhead, in order to oblige you. He was saved when he was doomed to be destroyed by an irresistible supernatural weapon.

sanskrit: tasmāt nāmnā viṣṇu rātaḥ iti loke bhaviṣyati na sandehaḥ mahā bhāga mahā bhāgavataḥ mahān
english: For this reason this child will be well known in the world as one who is protected by the Personality of Godhead. O most fortunate one, there is no doubt that this child will become a first-class devotee and will be qualified with all good qualities.

sanskrit: śrī rājā uvāca api eṣaḥ vaṁśyān rāja ṛṣīn puṇya ślokān mahā ātmanaḥ anuvartitā svit yaśasā sādhu vādena sat tamāḥ
english: The good King [Yudhiṣṭhira] inquired: O great souls, will he become as saintly a king, as pious in his very name and as famous and glorified in his achievements, as others who appeared in this great royal family?

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāḥ ūcuḥ pārtha prajā avitā sākṣāt ikṣvākuḥ iva mānavaḥ brahmaṇyaḥ satya sandhaḥ ca rāmaḥ dāśarathiḥ yathā
english: The learned brāhmaṇas said: O son of Pṛthā, this child shall be exactly like King Ikṣvāku, son of Manu, in maintaining all those who are born. And as for following the brahminical principles, especially in being true to his promise, he shall be exactly like Rāma, the Personality of Godhead, the son of Mahārāja Daśaratha.

sanskrit: eṣaḥ dātā śaraṇyaḥ ca yathā hi auśīnaraḥ śibiḥ yaśaḥ vitanitā svānām dauṣyantih iva yajvanām
english: This child will be a munificent donor of charity and protector of the surrendered, like the famous King Śibi of the Uśīnara country. And he will expand the name and fame of his family like Bharata, the son of Mahārāja Duṣyanta.

sanskrit: dhanvinām agraṇīḥ eṣaḥ tulyaḥ ca arjunayoḥ dvayoḥ hutāśaḥ iva durdharṣaḥ samudraḥ iva dustaraḥ
english: Amongst great bowmen, this child will be as good as Arjuna. He will be as irresistible as fire and as unsurpassable as the ocean.

sanskrit: mṛgendraḥ iva vikrāntaḥ niṣevyaḥ himavān iva titikṣuḥ vasudhā iva asau sahiṣṇuḥ pitarau iva
english: This child will be as strong as a lion, and as worthy a shelter as the Himālaya Mountains. He will be forbearing like the earth, and as tolerant as his parents.

sanskrit: pitāmaha samaḥ sāmye prasāde giriśa upamaḥ āśrayaḥ sarva bhūtānām yathā devaḥ ramā āśrayaḥ
english: This child will be like his grandfather Yudhiṣṭhira or Brahmā in equanimity of mind. He will be munificent like the lord of the Kailāsa Hill, Śiva. And he will be the resort of everyone, like the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Nārāyaṇa, who is even the shelter of the goddess of fortune.

sanskrit: sarva sat guṇa māhātmye eṣaḥ kṛṣṇam anuvrataḥ rantidevaḥ iva udāraḥ yayātiḥ iva dhārmikaḥ
english: This child will be almost as good as Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa by following in His footsteps. In magnanimity he will become as great as King Rantideva. And in religion he will be like Mahārāja Yayāti.

sanskrit: dhṛtyā bali samaḥ kṛṣṇe prahrāda iva sat grahaḥ āhartā eṣaḥ aśvamedhānām vṛddhānām paryupāsakaḥ
english: This child will be like Bali Mahārāja in patience, a staunch devotee of Lord Kṛṣṇa like Prahlāda Mahārāja, a performer of many aśvamedha [horse] sacrifices and a follower of the old and experienced men.

sanskrit: rāja ṛṣīṇām janayitā śāstā ca utpatha gāminām nigrahītā kaleḥ eṣaḥ bhuvaḥ dharmasya kāraṇāt
english: This child will be the father of kings who will be like sages. For world peace and for the sake of religion, he will be the chastiser of the upstarts and the quarrelsome.

sanskrit: takṣakāt ātmanaḥ mṛtyum dvija putra upasarjitāt prapatsyate upaśrutya mukta saṅgaḥ padam hareḥ
english: After hearing about his death, which will be caused by the bite of a snakebird sent by a son of a brāhmaṇa, he will get himself freed from all material attachment and surrender unto the Personality of Godhead, taking shelter of Him.

sanskrit: jijñāsita ātma yāthārthyaḥ muneḥ vyāsa sutāt asau hitvā idam nṛpa gaṅgāyām yāsyati addhā akutaḥ bhayam
english: After inquiring about proper self-knowledge from the son of Vyāsadeva, who will be a great philosopher, he will renounce all material attachment and achieve a life of fearlessness.

sanskrit: iti rājñe upādiśya viprāḥ jātaka kovidāḥ labdha apacitayaḥ sarve pratijagmuḥ svakān gṛhān
english: Thus those who were expert in astrological knowledge and in performance of the birth ceremony instructed King Yudhiṣṭhira about the future history of his child. Then, being sumptuously remunerated, they all returned to their respective homes.

sanskrit: saḥ eṣaḥ loke vikhyātaḥ parīkṣit iti yat prabhuḥ pūrvam dṛṣṭam anudhyāyan parīkṣeta nareṣu iha
english: So his son would become famous in the world as Parīkṣit [examiner] because he would come to examine all human beings in his search after that personality whom he saw before his birth. Thus he would come to constantly contemplate Him.

sanskrit: saḥ rāja putraḥ vavṛdhe āśu śukle iva uḍupaḥ āpūryamāṇaḥ pitṛbhiḥ kāṣṭhābhiḥ iva saḥ anvaham
english: As the moon, in its waxing fortnight, develops day after day, so the royal prince [Parīkṣit] very soon developed luxuriantly under the care and full facilities of his guardian grandfathers.

sanskrit: yakṣyamāṇaḥ aśvamedhena jñāti droha jihāsayā rājā labdha dhanaḥ dadhyau na anyatra kara daṇḍayoḥ
english: Just at this time, King Yudhiṣṭhira was considering performing a horse sacrifice to get freed from sins incurred from fighting with kinsmen. But he became anxious to get some wealth, for there were no surplus funds outside of fines and tax collection.

sanskrit: tat abhipretam ālakṣya bhrātaraḥ acyuta coditāḥ dhanam prahīṇam ājahruḥ udīcyām diśi bhūriśaḥ
english: Understanding the hearty wishes of the King, his brothers, as advised by the infallible Lord Kṛṣṇa, collected sufficient riches from the north [left by King Marutta].

sanskrit: tena sambhṛta sambhāraḥ dharma putraḥ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ vājimedhaiḥ tribhiḥ bhītaḥ yajñaiḥ samayajat harim
english: By those riches, the King could procure the ingredients for three horse sacrifices. Thus the pious King Yudhiṣṭhira, who was very fearful after the Battle of Kurukṣetra, pleased Lord Hari, the Personality of Godhead.

sanskrit: āhūtaḥ bhagavān rājñā yājayitvā dvijaiḥ nṛpam uvāsa katicit māsān suhṛdām priya kāmyayā
english: Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Personality of Godhead, being invited to the sacrifices by Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira, saw to it that they were performed by qualified [twice-born] brāhmaṇas. After that, for the pleasure of the relatives, the Lord remained a few months.

sanskrit: tataḥ rājñā abhyanujñātaḥ kṛṣṇayā saha bandhubhiḥ yayau dvāravatīm brahman sa arjunaḥ yadubhiḥ vṛtaḥ
english: O Śaunaka, thereafter the Lord, having bade farewell to King Yudhiṣṭhira, Draupadī and other relatives, started for the city of Dvārakā, accompanied by Arjuna and other members of the Yadu dynasty.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca viduraḥ tīrtha yātrāyām maitreyāt ātmanaḥ gatim jñātvā āgāt hāstinapuram tayā avāpta vivitsitaḥ
english: Śrī Sūta Gosvāmī said: While traveling on a pilgrimage, Vidura received knowledge of the destination of the self from the great sage Maitreya and then returned to Hastināpura. He became as well versed in the subject as he desired.

sanskrit: yāvataḥ kṛtavān praśnān kṣattā kauṣārava agrataḥ jāta eka bhaktiḥ govinde tebhyaḥ ca upararāma ha
english: After asking various questions and becoming established in the transcendental loving service of Lord Kṛṣṇa, Vidura retired from putting questions to Maitreya Muni.

sanskrit: tam bandhum āgatam dṛṣṭvā dharma putraḥ saha anujaḥ dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ yuyutsuḥ ca sūtaḥ śāradvataḥ pṛthā gāndhārī draupadī brahman subhadrā ca uttarā kṛpī anyāḥ ca jāmayaḥ pāṇḍoḥ jñātayaḥ sa sutāḥ striyaḥ
english: When they saw Vidura return to the palace, all the inhabitants — Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira, his younger brothers, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Sātyaki, Sañjaya, Kṛpācārya, Kuntī, Gāndhārī, Draupadī, Subhadrā, Uttarā, Kṛpī, many other wives of the Kauravas, and other ladies with children — all hurried to him in great delight. It so appeared that they had regained their consciousness after a long period.

sanskrit: prati ujjagmuḥ praharṣeṇa prāṇam tanvaḥ iva āgatam abhisaṅgamya vidhi vat pariṣvaṅga abhivādanaiḥ
english: With great delight they all approached him, as if life had returned to their bodies. They exchanged obeisances and welcomed each other with embraces.

sanskrit: mumucuḥ prema bāṣpa ogham viraha autkaṇṭhya kātarāḥ rājā tam arhayām cakre kṛta āsana parigraham
english: Due to anxieties and long separation, they all cried out of affection. King Yudhiṣṭhira then arranged to offer sitting accommodations and a reception.

sanskrit: tam bhuktavantam viśrāntam āsīnam sukham āsane praśraya avanataḥ rājā prāha teṣām ca śṛṇvatām
english: After Vidura ate sumptuously and took sufficient rest, he was comfortably seated. Then the King began to speak to him, and all who were present there listened.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraḥ uvāca api smaratha naḥ yuṣmat pakṣa chāyā samedhitān vipat gaṇāt viṣa agni ādeḥ mocitāḥ yat sa mātṛkāḥ
english: Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira said: My uncle, do you remember how you always protected us, along with our mother, from all sorts of calamities? Your partiality, like the wings of a bird, saved us from poisoning and arson.

sanskrit: kayā vṛttyā vartitam vaḥ caradbhiḥ kṣiti maṇḍalam tīrthāni kṣetra mukhyāni sevitāni iha bhūtale
english: While traveling on the surface of the earth, how did you maintain your livelihood? At which holy places and pilgrimage sites did you render service?

sanskrit: bhavat vidhāḥ bhāgavatāḥ tīrtha bhūtāḥ svayam vibho tīrthī kurvanti tīrthāni sva antaḥ sthena gadā bhṛtā
english: My lord, devotees like your good self are verily holy places personified. Because you carry the Personality of Godhead within your heart, you turn all places into places of pilgrimage.

sanskrit: api naḥ suhṛdaḥ tāta bāndhavāḥ kṛṣṇa devatāḥ dṛṣṭāḥ śrutāḥ vā yadavaḥ sva puryām sukham āsate
english: My uncle, you must have visited Dvārakā. In that holy place are our friends and well-wishers, the descendants of Yadu, who are always rapt in the service of the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa. You might have seen them or heard about them. Are they all living happily in their abodes?

sanskrit: iti uktaḥ dharma rājena sarvam tat samavarṇayat yathā anubhūtam kramaśaḥ vinā yadu kula kṣayam
english: Thus being questioned by Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira, Mahātmā Vidura gradually described everything he had personally experienced, except news of the annihilation of the Yadu dynasty.

sanskrit: nanu apriyam durviṣaham nṛṇām svayam upasthitam na āvedayat sakaruṇaḥ duḥkhitān draṣṭum akṣamaḥ
english: Compassionate Mahātmā Vidura could not stand to see the Pāṇḍavas distressed at any time. Therefore he did not disclose this unpalatable and unbearable incident because calamities come of their own accord.

sanskrit: kañcit kālam atha avātsīt sat kṛtaḥ deva vat sukham bhrātuḥ jyeṣṭhasya śreyaḥ kṛt sarveṣām sukham āvahan
english: Thus Mahātmā Vidura, being treated just like a godly person by his kinsmen, remained there for a certain period just to rectify the mentality of his eldest brother and in this way bring happiness to all the others.

sanskrit: abibhrat aryamā daṇḍam yathāvat agha kāriṣu yāvat dadhāra śūdratvam śāpāt varṣa śatam yamaḥ
english: As long as Vidura played the part of a śūdra, being cursed by Maṇḍūka Muni, Aryamā officiated at the post of Yamarāja to punish those who committed sinful acts.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraḥ labdha rājyaḥ dṛṣṭvā pautram kulam dharam bhrātṛbhiḥ loka pālābhaiḥ mumude parayā śriyā
english: Having won his kingdom and observed the birth of one grandson competent to continue the noble tradition of his family, Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira reigned peacefully and enjoyed uncommon opulence in cooperation with his younger brothers, who were all expert administrators to the common people.

sanskrit: evam gṛheṣu saktānām pramattānām tat īhayā atyakrāmat avijñātaḥ kālaḥ parama dustaraḥ
english: Insurmountable eternal time imperceptibly overcomes those who are too much attached to family affairs and are always engrossed in their thought.

sanskrit: viduraḥ tat abhipretya dhṛtarāṣṭram abhāṣata rājan nirgamyatām śīghram paśya idam bhayam āgatam
english: Mahātmā Vidura knew all this, and therefore he addressed Dhṛtarāṣṭra, saying: My dear King, please get out of here immediately. Do not delay. Just see how fear has overtaken you.

sanskrit: pratikriyā na yasya iha kutaścit karhicit prabho saḥ eṣaḥ bhagavān kālaḥ sarveṣām naḥ samāgataḥ
english: This frightful situation cannot be remedied by any person in this material world. My lord, it is the Supreme Personality of Godhead as eternal time [kāla] that has approached us all.

sanskrit: yena ca eva abhipannaḥ ayam prāṇaiḥ priya tamaiḥ api janaḥ sadyaḥ viyujyeta kim uta anyaiḥ dhana ādibhiḥ
english: Whoever is under the influence of supreme kāla [eternal time] must surrender his most dear life, and what to speak of other things, such as wealth, honor, children, land and home.

sanskrit: pitṛ bhrātṛ suhṛt putrāḥ hatāḥ te vigatam vayam ātmā ca jarayā grastaḥ para geham upāsase
english: Your father, brother, well-wishers and sons are all dead and passed away. You yourself have expended the major portion of your life, your body is now overtaken by invalidity, and you are living in the home of another.

sanskrit: andhaḥ purā eva vadhiraḥ manda prajñāḥ ca sāmpratam viśīrṇa dantaḥ manda agniḥ sa rāgaḥ kapham udvahan
english: You have been blind from your very birth, and recently you have become hard of hearing. Your memory is shortened, and your intelligence is disturbed. Your teeth are loose, your liver is defective, and you are coughing up mucus.

sanskrit: aho mahīyasī jantoḥ jīvita āśā yathā bhavān bhīma apavarjitam piṇḍam ādatte gṛha pāla vat
english: Alas, how powerful are the hopes of a living being to continue his life. Verily, you are living just like a household dog and are eating remnants of food given by Bhīma.

sanskrit: agniḥ nisṛṣṭaḥ dattaḥ ca garaḥ dārāḥ ca dūṣitāḥ hṛtam kṣetram dhanam yeṣām tat dattaiḥ asubhiḥ kiyat
english: There is no need to live a degraded life and subsist on the charity of those whom you tried to kill by arson and poisoning. You also insulted their married wife and usurped their kingdom and wealth.

sanskrit: tasya api tava dehaḥ ayam kṛpaṇasya jijīviṣoḥ paraiti anicchataḥ jīrṇaḥ jarayā vāsasī iva
english: Despite your unwillingness to die and your desire to live even at the cost of honor and prestige, your miserly body will certainly dwindle and deteriorate like an old garment.

sanskrit: gata sva artham imam deham viraktaḥ mukta bandhanaḥ avijñāta gatiḥ jahyāt saḥ vai dhīraḥ udāhṛtaḥ
english: He is called undisturbed who goes to an unknown, remote place and, freed from all obligations, quits his material body when it has become useless.

sanskrit: yaḥ svakāt parataḥ vā iha jāta nirvedaḥ ātmavān hṛdi kṛtvā harim gehāt pravrajet saḥ nara uttamaḥ
english: He is certainly a first-class man who awakens and understands, either by himself or from others, the falsity and misery of this material world and thus leaves home and depends fully on the Personality of Godhead residing within his heart.

sanskrit: atha udīcīm diśam yātu svaiḥ ajñāta gatiḥ bhavān itaḥ arvāk prāyaśaḥ kālaḥ puṁsām guṇa vikarṣaṇaḥ
