english: 55-56. “O girl of splendid features, you are delicate in body. Why do you sweep yourself, O girl of bright smiles? O gentle lady, you have in front of you many men and women servants. At your bidding they will do all the sweeping work etc.”

sanskrit: ṛṣestadvacanaṃ śrutvā prahasyedamuvāca ha || 57 ||
english: 57. On hearing those words of the sage, she laughingly said thus:

sanskrit: śivasevāṃ prakurvāṇāḥ śivabhaktipuraskṛtāḥ | ye narāścaiva nāryyaśca śivalokaṃ vrajaṃti vai || 58 || saṃmārjanaṃ ca pāṇibhyāṃ padbhyāṃ yānaṃ śivālaye | tasmānmayā ca kriyate saṃmārjanamataṃdritam || 59 ||
english: 58-60a. “The men and women who render service to Śiva, those who are prompted by devotion to Śiva, do go to the world of Śiva. The sweeping must be done by one’s own hands. One should go to the temple on one’s own foot. Hence, sweeping is done by me unweariedly. I do not know anything else, excepting the single act of sweeping.”[10]

sanskrit: anayā kiṃ kṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ keyaṃ kasya prasādataḥ | tadā jñānaṃ ca ṛṣiṇā tatsarvaṃ jñānacakṣuṣā | vismayena samāviṣṭastūṣṇīṃbhūto'bhavattadā || 61 ||
english: 60b-62. On hearing her words, the sage pondered: ‘Who is she? What has been done by her previously? By whose favour (did she get all these)?’ Then everything was understood by the sage through the eye of (the power of his) spiritual knowledge.

sanskrit: savismayo'bhūdatha tadviditvā uddālako jñānavatāṃ variṣṭhaḥ | śivaprabhāvaṃ manasā viciṃtya jñānātparaṃ bodhamavāpa śāṃtaḥ || 62 ||
english: 63. Struck with wonder, he became silent. After knowing it, he became surprised. Thinking about the power of Śiva, Uddālaka, the most excellent among the learned ones, attained the greatest enlightenment. He became calm and quiescent. FOOTNOTES AND REFERENCES: This is how Purāṇas tried to bring together followers of Śaivism and Vaiṣṇavism.

sanskrit: | lomaśa uvāca | taskaro'pi purā brahmansarvadharmabāhiṣkṛtaḥ | brahmaghno'sau surāpaśca suvarṇasya ca taskaraḥ || 1 ||
english: Or, was Vīrabhadra worshipped by them? The next verse shows that Vīrabhadra was worshipped by Suras.

sanskrit: laṃpaṭohi mahāpāpa uttamastrīṣu sarvadā | dyūtakārī sadā maṃdaḥ kitavaiḥ saha saṃgataḥ || 2 ||
english: In Mantra Śāstra, Oṃkāra Bīja is called Prāsāda.

sanskrit: ekadā krīḍatā tena hāritaṃ dyūtamadbhutam | kitavairmardyamāno hi tadā novāca kiñcana || 3 ||
english: 1-3. O Brāhmaṇas, once there was a great sinner[1] He was a thief. He was excommunicated from all religious rites. He was a Brāhmaṇa-slayer, a drink-addict and a thief of gold. He sought the company of excellent women in an illicit way. He was stupid and slow and always engaged in gambling along with gamblers and cunning fellows. Once while playing, he lost wonderfully (large amount). Smashed and hit by rogues and gamblers, he did not speak anything.

sanskrit: pīḍito'pyabhavattūṣṇīṃ tairuktaḥ pāpakṛttamaḥ | dyūte tvayā ca taddravyaṃ hāritaṃ kiṃ prayacchasi || 4 || no vā tatkathyatāṃ śīghraṃ yāthātathyena durmate | yaddhāritaṃ prayacchāmi rātrāvityabravīcca saḥ || 5 ||
english: 4-5. Though he was harassed and tormented, he kept quiet. Then that great sinner was asked thus by them: “You have lost this much wealth in the game of dice. Are you going to give it or not? O wicked fellow, let this be told immediately and precisely.” Then he said: “What has been lost by me, I shall give at night.”

sanskrit: tairmuktastena vākyena gatāste kitavādayaḥ | tadā niśīthasamaye gato'sau śivamaṃdiram || 6 ||
english: 6. Thanks to that statement, he was released by them. Those gamblers and rogues then went away. Then at mid-night he went to the temple of Śiva.

sanskrit: śirodhiruhya śambhośca ghaṇṭāmādātumudyataḥ | tāvatkailāsaśikhare śaṃbhuḥ provāca kiṃkarān || 7 ||
english: 7. Climbing on to the head of Śaṃbhu, he attempted to take the bell. At that time on the peak of Kailāsa, Śaṃbhu said to his servants:

sanskrit: anena yatkṛtaṃ cādya sarveṣāmadhikaṃ bhuvi | sarveṣāmeva bhaktānāṃ variṣṭho'yaṃ ca matpriyaḥ || 8 ||
english: 8. “What has been done by this fellow today is far superior to anything done by anyone on the earth. He is the most excellent one among all my devotees, hence he is my great favourite.”

sanskrit: iti proktvāna yāmāsa vīrabhadrādibhirgaṇaiḥ | te sarve tvaritā jagmuḥ kailāsācchivavallabhāt || 9 ||
english: 9. After saying this, he commanded the Gaṇas beginning with Vīrabhadra to bring him (the thief-gambler). They hurriedly started from Kailāsa, the favourite (resort) of Śiva.

sanskrit: sarvairḍamarunādena nāditaṃ bhuvanatrayam | tāndṛṣṭvā sahasottīrya taskarosau durātmavān | liṃgasya mastakātsadyaḥ palāyanaparo'bhavat || 10 ||
english: 10. The three worlds were filled with the sound of Ḍamarus by all of them. On seeing them, the evil-minded thief got down suddenly from the top of the Liṅga and took to his heels immediately.

sanskrit: palāyamānaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā vīrabhadraḥ samāhvayat || 11 || kasmādvibhepi re manda devadevo mahesvaraḥ | prasannastava jātodya udāracarito hyasau || 12 ||
english: 11-14. On seeing him fleeing, Vīrabhadra called him: “Whom do you fear, O stupid fellow? Maheśvara, the lord of Devas, has been pleased with you, as he is very liberal-minded.”

sanskrit: ityuktvā taṃ vimāne ca kṛtvā kailāsamāyayau | pārṣado hi kṛtastena taskaro hi mahātmanā || 13 ||
english: After saying thus and placing him in the aerial chariot, he came to Kailāsa. The thief was made an attendant by that noble-souled (lord).

sanskrit: tasmādbhāvyā śive bhaktiḥ sarveṣāmapi dehinām | paśavo'pi hi pūjyāḥ syuḥ kiṃ punarmānavābhuvi || 14 || ye tārkikāstarkaparāstatha mīmāṃsakāśca ye | anyonyavādinaścānye cānye vātmavitarkakāḥ || 15 ||
english: Hence, devotion to Śiva must be preserved and cultivated by all embodied beings. Even animals will be worthy of being worshipped thereby. What to say of men on the earth?

sanskrit: ekavākyaṃ na kurvaṃti śivārcanabahiṣkṛtāḥ | tarko hi kriyate yaiśca tesarve kiṃ śivaṃ vinā || 16 ||
english: 15-16. The followers of Tarka-śāstra are engaged in abstract reasoning and arguments.[2] So are the followers of the Mīmāṃsā School. They go on arguing and disputing among themselves. And there are others who deliberate on and discuss about the existence, nature etc. of the Soul, but never reach any unanimity, or reconciliation of (their) differences. They are excluded from the worship of Śiva. Without Śiva, of what significance are they, by whom only arguments are forwarded?

sanskrit: tathā kiṃ bahunoktena sarve'pi sthirajaṃgamāḥ | prāṇino'pi hi jāyaṃte kevalaṃ liṃgadhāriṇaḥ || 17 ||
english: 17. Of what avail is much talk? All mobile and immobile beings, all animals too, are born bearing the Liṅga.

sanskrit: piṇḍīyuktaṃ yatā liṃgaṃ sthāpitaṃ ca yathā'bhavat | tathā narā liṃgayuktāḥ piṇḍībhūtāstatā striyaḥ || 18 ||
english: 18. Just as the Liṅga is placed (and consecrated) in conjunction with the Piṇḍī (globular solid pedestal), so also men are endowed with Liṅgas and women afe Piṇḍīs.

sanskrit: śivaśaktiyutaṃ sarvaṃ jagadetaccarācaram | taṃ śivaṃ mauḍhyatastyaktvā mūḍhāścānyaṃ bhajaṃti ye || 19 ||
english: 19. The entire universe consisting of the mobile and immobile beings is endowed with (the union of) Śiva and Śakti. Those are foolish fellows who, out of delusion, eschew devotion to such Śiva and worship others.

sanskrit: dharmamātyaṃtikaṃ tucchaṃ naśvaraṃ kṣaṇabhaṃguram | yo viṣṇuḥ sa śivo jñeyo yaḥ śivo viṣṇureva saḥ || 20 ||
english: 20. Their Dharma is extremely insignificant, perishable and momentary. He who is Viṣṇu should be known as Śiva. He who is Śiva is Viṣṇu alone.[3]

sanskrit: pīṭhikā viṣṇurūpaṃ syālliṃgarūpī maheśvaraḥ | tasmālliṃgārcanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ sarveṣāmapi vai dvijāḥ || 21 ||
english: 21. The pedestal is the form of Viṣṇu and Maheśvara is in the form of Liṅga. Hence the worship of Liṅga, O Brāhmaṇas, is excellent for everyone.

sanskrit: brahmā maṇimayaṃ liṃgaṃ pūjayatyaniśaṃ śubham | indro ratnamayaṃ liṃgaṃ candro muktāmayaṃ tathā || 22 ||
english: 22. Brahmā worships a Ruby-Liṅga always, Indra worships a Liṅga made of gems and Candra (the Moon-god) one of pearls.

sanskrit: bhānustāmramayaṃ liṃgaṃ pūjayatyaniśaṃ śubham | raukmaṃ liṃgaṃ kuberaśca pāśī cāraktameva ca || 23 ||
english: 23. Bhānu (the Sun-god) always worships a splendid copper (-coloured) Liṅga. Kubera worships a golden Liṅga and Varuṇa a Liṅga red in colour.

sanskrit: yamo nīlamayaṃ liṃgaṃ rājataṃ nairṛtastathā | kāśmīraṃ pavano liṃgamarcayatyaniśaṃ vibhoḥ || 24 ||
english: 24. Yama worships a sapphire Liṅga, Nairṛta worships a silver Liṅga, Pavana (Wind-god) always worships a saffron Liṅga of the lord.

sanskrit: evaṃ te liṃgitāḥ sarve lokapālāḥ savāsavāḥ | tathā sarve'pi pātāle gaṃdharvāḥ kiṃnaraiḥ saha || 25 ||
english: 25. Thus, all Guardians of the Quarters including Indra have been characterised as worshippers of Liṅga. So are all (persons) in the nether world and also Gandharvas and Kinnaras.

sanskrit: daityānāṃ vaiṣṇavāḥ kecitprahlādapramukhā dvijāḥ | tathāhi rākṣasānāṃ ca vibhīṣaṇapurogamāḥ || 26 || baliśca namuciścaiva hiraṇyakaśipustathā | vṛṣaparvā vṛṣaścaiva saṃhrādo bāṇa eva ca || 27 ||
english: 26-27. Among Daityas, O Brāhmaṇas, there are certain devotees of Viṣṇu, the chief of whom was Prahlāda.[4] So also among Rākṣasas, those having Vibhīṣaṇa as their leader. So also (were) Bali, Namuci, Hiraṇyakaśipu, Vṛṣaparvan, Vṛṣa, Saṃhrāda and Bāṇa.

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavaḥ śiṣyāḥ śukrasya dhīmataḥ | evaṃ śivārcanaratāḥ sarve te daityadānavāḥ || 28 || rākṣasā eva te sarve śivapūjānvitāḥ sadā | hetiḥ prahetiḥ saṃyātirvighasaḥ praghasastathā || 29 ||
english: 28. These and many others who were the disciples of the intelligent Śukra were engaged in worshipping Śiva. All these Daityas and Dānavas (were devotees of Śiva).

sanskrit: vidyujjihvastīkṣṇadaṃṣṭro dhūmrākṣo bhīmavikramaḥ | mālī caiva sumālī ca mālyavānatibhīṣamaḥ || 30 || vidyutkaiśastaḍijjihvo rāvaṇaśca mahābalaḥ | kuṃbhakarṇo durādharṣo vegadarśī pratāpavān || 31 || ete hi rākṣasāḥ śreṣṭhā śivārcanaratāḥ sadā | liṃgamabhyarcya ca sadā siddhiṃ prāptāḥ purā tu te || 32 ||
english: 29-32. All the following were Rākṣasas and they were always engaged in the worship of Śiva. They were: Heti, Praheti, Saṃyāti, Vighasa, Praghasa, Vidyujjihva, Tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭra, Dhūmrākṣa of terrible valour, Mālī, Sumālī and the extremely terrible Mālyavān, Vidyutkeśa, Tadijjihva, Rāvaṇa of great strength, the invincible Kuṃbhakarṇa and Vegadarśī of great valour. These were great Rākṣasas, who were always engaged in worshipping Śiva. After worshipping the Liṅga formerly, they had always attained Siddhi.

sanskrit: rāvaṇena tapastaptaṃ sarveṣāmapi duḥkhaham | tapodhipo mahādevastutoṣa ca tadā bhṛśam || 33 ||
english: 33. A severe penance unbearable to all was performed by Ṛāvaṇa. Then Mahādeva, the lord of penance, became much pleased.

sanskrit: varānprāyacchata tadā sarveṣāmapi durlabhān | jñānaṃ vijñānasahitaṃ labdhaṃ tena sadāśivāt || 34 || ajeyatvaṃ ca saṃgrāme dvaiguṇyaṃ śirasāmapi | paṃcavaktro mahā devo daśavaktro'tha rāvaṇaḥ || 35 ||
english: 34-35. He granted him boons very difficult to be achieved by all others. Wisdom with perfect knowledge was obtained by him from Sadāśiva. He further obtained (invinicibility) in battle and twice the number of heads (as those of god Śiva), for Mahādeva had only five faces, whereas Rāvaṇa had ten faces.

sanskrit: devānṛṣīnpitṝṃścaiva nirjitya tapasā vibhuḥ | maheśasya prasādācca sarveṣāmadhiko'bhavat || 36 ||
english: 36. Thanks to the grace of Maheśa, that powerful (Rākṣasa) defeated Devas, sages and manes by means of his penance and became superior to all.

sanskrit: rājā trikūṭādhipatirmaheśena kṛto mahān | sarveṣāṃ rākṣasānāṃ ca paramāsanamāstitaḥ || 37 ||
english: 37. He was made the great king and ruler of Trikūṭa by Maheśa. He occupied the greatest and most excellent position (seat) among Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: tapasvināṃ parīkṣāyai yadṛṣīṇāṃ vihiṃsanam | kṛtaṃ tena tadā viprā rāvaṇena tapasvinā || 38 ||
english: 38. It was for testing (the enduring capacity of) the sages that he harassed them. Violence towards the sages was indulged in, O Brāhmaṇas, by Rāvaṇa who was himself an ascetic, only because he wanted to test them.

sanskrit: ajeyo hi mahāñjāto rāvaṇo lokarāvaṇaḥ | sṛṣṭyaṃtaraṃ kṛtaṃ yena prasādācchaṃkarasya ca || 39 ||
english: 39. Rāvaṇa who made the whole world cry and scream, became great and invincible. Thanks to the grace and favour of Śaṅkara, another creation was evolved by him.

sanskrit: lokapālā jitāstena pratāpena tapasvinā | brahmāpi vijito yena tapasā parameṇa hi || 40 ||
english: 40. The guardians of the worlds were conquered by that ascetic by means of his valour. Brahmā too was subdued by him only through great penance.

sanskrit: amṛtāṃśukaro bhūtvā jito yena śaśī dvijāḥ | dāhakatvājjito vahnirīśaḥ kailāsatolanāt || 41 ||
english: 41. By becoming the nectar-rayed one, he conquered the Moon, O Brāhmaṇas. Through the power of burning, the Fire-god was conquered and Īśa (himself) was conquered by lifting up Kailāsa (mountain).

sanskrit: aiśvaryeṇa jitaścendro viṣṇuḥ sarvagatastathā | liṃgārcanaprasādena trailokyaṃ ca vaśīkṛtam || 42 ||
english: 42. Indra was conquered by means of his Aiśvarya (power and prosperity). So also Viṣṇu, the omnipresent one. By worshipping and propitiating the Liṅga, all the three worlds were controlled by him.

sanskrit: tadā sarve suragaṇā brahmaviṣṇupurogamāḥ | merupṛṣṭhaṃ samāsādya sumaṃtraṃ cakrire tadā || 43 ||
english: 43. At that time, all the groups of Suras, with Brahmā and Viṣṇu as their leaders, gathered together on the top of Mem and began their deliberation and discussion:

sanskrit: pīḍitāḥ smo rāvaṇena tapasā duṣkareṇa vai | gokarṇākhye girau devāḥ śrūyatāṃ paramādbhutam || 44 || sākṣālliṃgārcanaṃ yena kṛtamasti mahātmanā | jñānajñeyaṃ jñānagamyaṃ yadyatparamamadbhutam | tatkṛtaṃ rāvaṇenaiva sarveṣāṃ duratikramam || 45 ||
english: 44-45. “We have been tormented by Rāvaṇa through his penance, very difficult to be performed (by others). O Devas, let this wonderful story be listened to. On the mountain named Gokarṇa, worship of the Liṅga itself was performed by that noble-souled (hero). What could be known only through knowledge, what could be achieved only through knowledge, whatever.great miracle was there, that which is very difficult to be surpassed by everyone—all these were done by Rāvaṇa alone.

sanskrit: vairāgyaṃ paramāsthāya audāryaṃ ca tato'dhikam | tenaiva mamatā tyaktā rāvaṇena mahātmanā || 46 ||
english: 46. He had adopted the greatest vairāgya (detachment) as well as liberal-midedness [mindedness/mindness?] greater even than that (vairāgya). The feeling of mamatā (mineness [mindness?]) was eschewed by the noble-souled Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: saṃvatsarasahasrācca svaśiro hi mahābhujaḥ | kṛttvā kareṇa liṃgasya pūjanārthaṃ samarpayat || 47 ||
english: 47. After a period of a thousand years, that (hero) of great arms cut one of his own head and offered it with his own hand, for the sake of worshipping the Liṅga.

sanskrit: rāvaṇasya kabaṃdhaṃ ca tadagre ca samīpataḥ | yogadhāraṇayā yuktaṃ parameṇa samādhinā || 48 ||
english: 48. Ṛāvaṇa’s body short of one head stood in front of it in the vicinity. īt was endowed with Yogic dhāraṇā (steady abstraction) and the greatest samādhi (concentration).

sanskrit: liṃge layaṃ samādhāya kayāpi kalayā sthitam | anyacchirovivṛścyaivaṃ tenāpi śivapūjanam | kṛtaṃ naivānyamuninā tathā caivāpareṇahi || 49 ||
english: 49. Fixing his attention deeply on the Liṅga after about a kalā, he cut off another head and worshipped Śiva with it. Such (performance of) worship was never done by any sage nor by anyone else.

sanskrit: evaṃ śirāṃsyeva bahūni tena samarpitānyeva śivārcanārthe | bhūtvā kabaṃdho hi punaḥ punaśca śivo'sau varado babhūva || 50 ||
english: 50. Thus many heads were chopped off and offered by him in worshipping Śiva. Again and again he became a headless body. Then Śiva became a bestower of boons.

sanskrit: mayā vināsurastatra piṃḍībhūtena vai purā | varānvaraya paulastya yatheṣṭaṃ tāndadāmyaham || 51 ||
english: 51. ‘Formerly without being myself transformed into a Piṇḍī...[5] O descendant of Pulastya, choose boons as you please. I shall grant you the same.’

sanskrit: rāvaṇena tadā coktaḥ śivaḥ paramamaṃgalaḥ | yadi prasanno bhagavandeyo me vara uttamaḥ || 52 || na kāmaye'nyaṃ ca varamāśraye tvatpadāṃbujam | yathā tathā pradātavyaṃ yadyasti ca kṛpā mayi || 53 ||
english: 52-53. Then Śiva of greatest auṣpiciousness was requested by Rāvaṇa: ‘If Your Lordship are pleased, the excellent boon should be given to me. I do not wish to seek any other boon. If you have merciful favour towards me, you should give me such a boon whereby I (always) resort to your feet.’

sanskrit: tadā sadāśivenokto rāvaṇo lokarāvaṇaḥ | matprasādācca sarvaṃ tvaṃ prāpsyase manasepsitam || 54 ||
english: 54. Then Rāvaṇa who made the world cry and scream was told by Sādāśiva: ‘By my favour, you will obtain everything mentally desired by you.’

sanskrit: evaṃ prāptaṃ śivātsarvaṃ rāvaṇena sureśvarāḥ | tasmātsarvairbhavadbhiśca tapasā parameṇa hi || 55 ||
english: 55-59. It was thus, O leading Suras, that everything was. obtained by Rāvaṇa from Śiva. Hence this Rāvaṇa should be subdued by you all only through great penance. This is what I think.”

sanskrit: ciṃtāmāpedire sarve ciraṃ te viṣayānvitāḥ | brahmāpi ceṃdriyagrastaḥ sutā ramitumudyataḥ || 57 ||
english: On hearing the words of Acyuta, the groups of Devas beginning with Brahmā became anxious, because all of them had been addicted to sensual pleasures.

sanskrit: iṃdro hi jārabhāvācca caṃdro hi gurutalpagaḥ | yamaḥ kadaryabhāvācca caṃcalatvātsadāgatiḥ || 58 || pāvakaḥ sarvabhakṣitvāttathānye devatāgaṇāḥ | aśaktā rāvaṇaṃ jetuṃ tapasā ca vijṛṃbhitam || 59 ||
english: Brahmā was overpowered by sexual desire and he attempted sexual act with his own daughter. Indra was an adulterer. Candra (the Moon-god) defiled the bed of his Guru (preceptor Bṛhaspati). Yama has been avaricious and stingy. Sadāgati (the Wind-god) has been fickle. Pāvaka has been indiscriminate in eating anything and everything. The others among the groups of Devas (had similar defects). Hence, all these were incapable of conquering Rāvaṇa who had become very great by means of penance.

sanskrit: śailādo hi mahātejā gaṇaśreṣṭhaḥ purātanaḥ | buddhi mānnītinipuṇo mahābalaparākramī || 60 ||
english: 60. Śailāda was an elderly excellent Gaṇa of great splendour. He was intelligent, an expert in adopting the right course of action, highly powerful and very valorous.

sanskrit: śivapriyo rudrarūpī mahātmā hyuvāca sarvānatha ceṃdramukhyān | kasmādyūyaṃ saṃbhramādāgatāśca etatsarvaṃ kathyatāṃ vistareṇa || 61 ||
english: 61-62. He was a favourite of Śiva and was identical with Rudra. The noble-souled one asked all of them led by Indra, “Why have you all come here in great excitement? Let the whole thing be reported in detail.”

sanskrit: naṃdinā ca tadā sarve pṛṣṭāḥ procustvarānvitāḥ || 62 || devā ūcuḥ | rāvaṇena vayaṃ sarve nirjitā munibhiḥ saha | prasādayitumāyātāḥ śivaṃ lokeśvareśvaram || 63 ||
english: On being asked by Nandi, all of them hurriedly said then: Devas said: 63. All of us along with the sages have been conquered by Rāvaṇa. We have come to propitiate Śiva, the lord of the lords, of the worlds.

sanskrit: prahasya bhagavānnaṃdī brahmāṇaṃ vai hyuvāca ha | kva yūyaṃ kva śivaḥ śaṃbhustapasā parameṇa hi | draṣṭavyo hṛdi madhyasthaḥ so'dya draṣṭuṃ na pāryate || 64 ||
english: 64. Lord Nandī laughed and said to Brahmā: “Where are you? Where is auspicious Śaṃbhu? (There is a world of difference between you two.) By means of great penance, he should be seen seated in the middle of the heart. He cannot be seen today.

sanskrit: yāvadbhāvā hyanekāśca iṃdriyārthāstathaiva ca | yāvacca mamatābhāvastāvadīśo hi durlabhaḥ || 65 ||
english: 65. As long as the emotional attitudes are too many, the objects of senses are plentiful and there is the feeling of mineness, so long Īśa is very difficult to be attained.

sanskrit: jiteṃdriyāṇāṃ śāṃtānāṃ tanniṣṭhānāṃ mahātmanām | sulabho liṃgarūpī syādbhavatāṃ hi sudurlabhaḥ || 66 ||
english: 66. Śiva in the form of the Liṅga is easy of access to those noble-souled ones who have subdued the senses, are quiescent and have stabilized themselves in him. He is very difficult to be obtained by you all.”

sanskrit: tadā brahmādayo devā ṛṣayaśca vipaścitaḥ | praṇamya naṃdinaṃ prāhuḥ kasmāttvaṃ vānarānanaḥ | tatsarvaṃ kathayānyaṃ ca rāvaṇasya tapobalam || 67 ||
english: 67. Then Brahma and other Devas as well as the learned sages bowed down to Nandī and said: “Why do you have the face of a monkey?[6] Tell us everything about it. Tell us about the power of the penance of Rāvaṇa.” Nandīśvara said:

sanskrit: naṃdīśvara uvāca | kubero'dhikṛtastena śaṃkareṇa mahātmanā | dhanānāmādipatye ca taṃ draṣṭuṃ rāvaṇo'tra vai || 68 || āgacchattvarayā yuktaḥ samāruhya svavāhanam | māṃ dṛṣṭvā cābravītkruddhaḥ kubero hyatra āgataḥ || 69 ||
english: 68-70a. Kubera had been made by the noble-souled Śaṅkara the over-lord of wealth and assets. Rāvaṇa came here to see him, riding in his own vehicle. He was in a hurry. On seeing me, he said furiously: “Did Kubera come here? Was he seen by you here? Let this be told immediately.”

sanskrit: tvayā dṛṣṭo'tha vātrāsau kathyatāmavilaṃbitam | kiṃ kāryaṃ dhanadenādya iti pṛṣṭo mayā hi saḥ || 70 ||
english: 70b-72. He was asked by me: “What have you to do with Dhanada (Kubera) today?”

sanskrit: tadovāca mahātejā rāvaṇo lokarāvaṇaḥ | mayyaśraddhānvito bhūtvā viṣayātmā sudurmadaḥ || 71 || śikṣāpayitumārabdho maivaṃ kāryamiti prabho | yathāhaṃ ca śriyā yukta āḍhyo'haṃ balavānaham | tathā tvaṃ bhava re mūḍha mā mūḍhatvamupārjaya || 72 ||
english: Then Rāvaṇa of great splendour, who made the world scream, said: “At the outset he (Kubera) had been indifferent towards me. He did not care for me. Addicted to sensual pleasures, as he is, he has been highly arrogant. He began to teach me saying, ‘O lord, it should not be done like this. Just as I am endowed with glory and splendour, just as I am rich and strong, so also you do become, O fool. Do not get into delusion and stupidity.’

sanskrit: ahaṃ mūḍhaḥ kṛtastena kubereṇa mahātmanā | mayā nirākṛto roṣāttapastepe sa guhyakaḥ || 73 ||
english: 73. I have been made a fool and a deluded person by the noble-souled Kubera. On being turned out by me angrily, that Guḥyaka (i.e. Kubera) performed penance.

sanskrit: kuberaḥ sa hi naṃdinkimāgatastava maṃdiram | dīyatāṃ ca kuberodya nātra kāryā vicāraṇā || 74 ||
english: 74. Did that Kubera come, O Nandī, to your abode? Let that Kubera be handed over (to me). You need not hesitate in this matter.”

sanskrit: rāvaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā hyavocaṃ tvarito'pyaham | liṃgakosi mahābhāga tvamahaṃ ca tathāvidhaḥ || 75 || ubhayoḥ samanāṃ jñātvā vṛthā jalpasi durmate | yathoktaḥ sa tvavādīnmāṃ vadanārthe baloddhataḥ || 76 ||
english: 75-79. On hearing the words of Rāvaṇa, I hurriedly replied: “You are a Liṅgaka (worshipper of Liṅga), an exalted one. I too am one like that. Knowing the equality between us both you are prattling in vain, O vicious one.”

sanskrit: manum ekāgram āsīnam abhigamya maharṣayaḥ / pratipūjya yathānyāyam idaṃ vacanam abruvan //
english: The great sages approached Manu, who was seated with a collected mind, and, having duly worshipped him, spoke as follows:

sanskrit: bhagavan sarvavarṇānāṃ yathāvad anupūrvaśaḥ / antaraprabhavānāṃ ca dharmān no vaktum arhasi //
english: 'Deign, divine one, to declare to us precisely and in due order the sacred laws of each of the (four chief) castes (varna) and of the intermediate ones.

sanskrit: tvam eko hy asya sarvasya vidhānasya svayaṃbhuvaḥ / acintyasyāprameyasya kāryatattvārthavit prabho //
english: 'For thou, O Lord, alone knowest the purport, (i.e.) the rites, and the knowledge of the soul, (taught) in this whole ordinance of the Self-existent (Svayambhu), which is unknowable and unfathomable.'

sanskrit: sa taiḥ pṛṣṭas tathā samyag amitaujā mahātmabhiḥ / pratyuvācārcya tān sarvān maharṣīñ śrūyatām iti //
english: He, whose power is measureless, being thus asked by the high-minded great sages, duly honoured them, and answered, 'Listen!'

sanskrit: āsīd idaṃ tamobhūtam aprajñātam alakṣaṇam / apratarkyam avijñeyaṃ prasuptam iva sarvataḥ //
english: This (universe) existed in the shape of Darkness, unperceived, destitute of distinctive marks, unattainable by reasoning, unknowable, wholly immersed, as it were, in deep sleep.

sanskrit: tataḥ svayaṃbhūr bhagavān avyakto vyañjayann idam / mahābhūtādi vṛttaujāḥ prādur āsīt tamonudaḥ //
english: Then the divine Self-existent (Svayambhu, himself) indiscernible, (but) making (all) this, the great elements and the rest, discernible, appeared with irresistible (creative) power, dispelling the darkness.

sanskrit: yo 'sāv atīndriyagrāhyaḥ sūkṣmo 'vyaktaḥ sanātanaḥ / sarvabhūtamayo 'cintyaḥ sa eva svayam udbabhau //
english: He who can be perceived by the internal organ (alone), who is subtile, indiscernible, and eternal, who contains all created beings and is inconceivable, shone forth of his own (will).

sanskrit: so 'bhidhyāya śarīrāt svāt sisṛkṣur vividhāḥ prajāḥ / apa eva sasarjādau tāsu vīryam avāsṛjat //
english: He, desiring to produce beings of many kinds from his own body, first with a thought created the waters, and placed his seed in them.

sanskrit: tad aṇḍam abhavad dhaimaṃ sahasrāṃśusamaprabham / tasmiñ jajñe svayaṃ brahmā sarvalokapitāmahaḥ //
english: That (seed) became a golden egg, in brilliancy equal to the sun; in that (egg) he himself was born as Brahman, the progenitor of the whole world.

sanskrit: āpo narā iti proktā āpo vai narasūnavaḥ / tā yad asyāyanaṃ pūrvaṃ tena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ //
english: The waters are called narah, (for) the waters are, indeed, the offspring of Nara; as they were his first residence (ayana), he thence is named Narayana.

sanskrit: yat tat kāraṇam avyaktaṃ nityaṃ sadasadātmakaṃ / tadvisṛṣṭaḥ sa puruṣo loke brahmeti kīrtyate //
english: From that (first) cause, which is indiscernible, eternal, and both real and unreal, was produced that male (Purusha), who is famed in this world (under the appellation of) Brahman.

sanskrit: tasminn aṇḍe sa bhagavān uṣitvā parivatsaram / svayam evātmano dhyānāt tad aṇḍam akarod dvidhā //
english: The divine one resided in that egg during a whole year, then he himself by his thought (alone) divided it into two halves;

sanskrit: tābhyāṃ sa śakalābhyāṃ ca divaṃ bhūmiṃ ca nirmame / madhye vyoma diśaś cāṣṭāv apāṃ sthānaṃ ca śāśvataṃ //
english: And out of those two halves he formed heaven and earth, between them the middle sphere, the eight points of the horizon, and the eternal abode of the waters.

sanskrit: udbabarhātmanaś caiva manaḥ sadasadātmakam / manasaś cāpy ahaṃkāram abhimantāram īśvaram //
english: From himself (atmanah) he also drew forth the mind, which is both real and unreal, likewise from the mind egoism, which possesses the function of self-consciousness (and is) lordly;

sanskrit: mahāntam eva cātmānaṃ sarvāṇi triguṇāni ca / viṣayāṇāṃ grahītṝṇi śanaiḥ pañcendriyāṇi ca //
english: Moreover, the great one, the soul, and all (products) affected by the three qualities, and, in their order, the five organs which perceive the objects of sensation.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tv avayavān sūkṣmān ṣaṇṇām apy amitaujasām / saṃniveśyātmamātrāsu sarvabhūtāni nirmame //
english: But, joining minute particles even of those six, which possess measureless power, with particles of himself, he created all beings.

sanskrit: yan mūrtyavayavāḥ sūkṣmās tānīmāny āśrayanti ṣaṭ / tasmāc charīram ity āhus tasya mūrtiṃ manīṣiṇaḥ //
english: Because those six (kinds of) minute particles, which form the (creator's) frame, enter (a-sri) these (creatures), therefore the wise call his frame sarira, (the body.)

sanskrit: tad āviśanti bhūtāni mahānti saha karmabhiḥ / manaś cāvayavaiḥ sūkṣmaiḥ sarvabhūtakṛd avyayam //
english: That the great elements enter, together with their functions and the mind, through its minute parts the framer of all beings, the imperishable one.

sanskrit: teṣām idaṃ tu saptānāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ mahaujasām / sūkṣmābhyo mūrtimātrābhyaḥ saṃbhavaty avyayād vyayam //
english: But from minute body (-framing) particles of these seven very powerful Purushas springs this (world), the perishable from the imperishable.

sanskrit: ādyādyasya guṇaṃ tv eṣām avāpnoti paraḥ paraḥ / yo yo yāvatithaś caiṣāṃ sa sa tāvad guṇaḥ smṛtaḥ //
english: Among them each succeeding (element) acquires the quality of the preceding one, and whatever place (in the sequence) each of them occupies, even so many qualities it is declared to possess.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ tu sa nāmāni karmāṇi ca pṛthak pṛthak / vedaśabdebhya evādau pṛthak saṃsthāś ca nirmame //
english: But in the beginning he assigned their several names, actions, and conditions to all (created beings), even according to the words of the Veda.

sanskrit: karmātmanāṃ ca devānāṃ so 'sṛjat prāṇināṃ prabhuḥ / sādhyānāṃ ca gaṇaṃ sūkṣmaṃ yajñaṃ caiva sanātanam //
english: He, the Lord, also created the class of the gods, who are endowed with life, and whose nature is action; and the subtile class of the Sadhyas, and the eternal sacrifice.

sanskrit: agnivāyuravibhyas tu trayaṃ brahma sanātanam / dudoha yajñasiddhyartham ṛgyajuḥsāmalakṣaṇam //
english: But from fire, wind, and the sun he drew forth the threefold eternal Veda, called Rik, Yagus, and Saman, for the due performance of the sacrifice.

sanskrit: kālaṃ kālavibhaktīś ca nakṣatrāṇi grahāṃs tathā / saritaḥ sāgarāñ śailān samāni viṣamāni ca //
english: Time and the divisions of time, the lunar mansions and the planets, the rivers, the oceans, the mountains, plains, and uneven ground.

sanskrit: tapo vācaṃ ratiṃ caiva kāmaṃ ca krodham eva ca / sṛṣṭiṃ sasarja caivemāṃ sraṣṭum icchann imāḥ prajāḥ //
english: Austerity, speech, pleasure, desire, and anger, this whole creation he likewise produced, as he desired to call these beings into existence.

sanskrit: karmaṇāṃ ca vivekārthaṃ dharmādharmau vyavecayat / dvandvair ayojayac cemāḥ sukhaduḥkhādibhiḥ prajāḥ //
english: Moreover, in order to distinguish actions, he separated merit from demerit, and he caused the creatures to be affected by the pairs (of opposites), such as pain and pleasure.

sanskrit: aṇvyo mātrā vināśinyo daśārdhānāṃ tu yāḥ smṛtāḥ / tābhiḥ sārdham idaṃ sarvaṃ saṃbhavaty anupūrvaśaḥ //
english: But with the minute perishable particles of the five (elements) which have been mentioned, this whole (world) is framed in due order.

sanskrit: yaṃ tu karmaṇi yasmin sa nyayuṅkta prathamaṃ prabhuḥ / sa tad eva svayaṃ bheje sṛjyamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ //
english: But to whatever course of action the Lord at first appointed each (kind of beings), that alone it has spontaneously adopted in each succeeding creation.

sanskrit: hiṃsrāhiṃsre mṛdukrūre dharmādharmāv ṛtānṛte / yad yasya so 'dadhāt sarge tat tasya svayam āviśat //
english: Whatever he assigned to each at the (first) creation, noxiousness or harmlessness, gentleness or ferocity, virtue or sin, truth or falsehood, that clung (afterwards) spontaneously to it.

sanskrit: yathā rtuliṅgāny ṛtavaḥ svayam eva rtuparyaye / svāni svāny abhipadyante tathā karmāṇi dehinaḥ //
english: As at the change of the seasons each season of its own accord assumes its distinctive marks, even so corporeal beings (resume in new births) their (appointed) course of action.

sanskrit: lokānāṃ tu vivṛddhyarthaṃ mukhabāhūrupādataḥ / brāhmaṇaṃ kṣatriyaṃ vaiśyaṃ śūdraṃ ca niravartayat //
english: But for the sake of the prosperity of the worlds he caused the Brahmana, the Kshatriya, the Vaisya, and the Sudra to proceed from his mouth, his arms, his thighs, and his feet.

sanskrit: dvidhā kṛtvātmano deham ardhena puruṣo 'bhavat / ardhena nārī tasyāṃ sa virājam asṛjat prabhuḥ // tapas taptvāsṛjad yaṃ tu sa svayaṃ puruṣo virāṭ / taṃ māṃ vittāsya sarvasya sraṣṭāraṃ dvijasattamāḥ //
english: Dividing his own body, the Lord became half male and half female; with that (female) he produced Virag. But know me, O most holy among the twice-born, to be the creator of this whole (world), whom that male, Virag, himself produced, having performed austerities.

sanskrit: ahaṃ prajāḥ sisṛkṣus tu tapas taptvā suduścaram / patīn prajānām asṛjaṃ maharṣīn ādito daśa //
english: Then I, desiring to produce created beings, performed very difficult austerities, and (thereby) called into existence ten great sages, lords of created beings,

sanskrit: marīcim atryaṅgirasau pulastyaṃ pulahaṃ kratum / pracetasaṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ ca bhṛguṃ nāradam eva ca //
english: Mariki, Atri, Angiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Praketas, Vasishtha, Bhrigu, and Narada.

sanskrit: ete manūṃs tu saptān yān asṛjan bhūritejasaḥ / devān devanikāyāṃś ca maharṣīṃś cāmitaujasaḥ //
english: They created seven other Manus possessing great brilliancy, gods and classes of gods and great sages of measureless power,

sanskrit: yakṣarakṣaḥpiśācāṃś ca gandharvāpsaraso 'surān / nāgān sarpān suparṇāṃś ca pitṝṇāṃś ca pṛthaggaṇam //
english: Yakshas (the servants of Kubera, the demons called) Rakshasas and Pisakas, Gandharvas (or musicians of the gods), Apsarases (the dancers of the gods), Asuras, (the snake-deities called) Nagas and Sarpas, (the bird-deities called) Suparnas and the several classes of the manes,

sanskrit: kinnarān vānarān matsyān vividhāṃś ca vihaṅgamān / paśūn mṛgān manuṣyāṃś ca vyālāṃś cobhayatodataḥ // kṛmikīṭapataṅgāṃś ca yūkāmakṣikamatkuṇam / sarvaṃ ca daṃśamaśakaṃ sthāvaraṃ ca pṛthagvidham //
english: Lightnings, thunderbolts and clouds, imperfect (rohita) and perfect rainbows, falling meteors, supernatural noises, comets, and heavenly lights of many kinds,39 (Horse-faced) Kinnaras, monkeys, fishes, birds of many kinds, cattle, deer, men, and carnivorous beasts with two rows of teeth, Small and large worms and beetles, moths, lice, flies, bugs, all stinging and biting insects and the several kinds of immovable things.

sanskrit: evam etair idaṃ sarvaṃ manniyogān mahātmabhiḥ / yathākarma tapoyogāt sṛṣṭaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam //
english: Thus was this whole (creation), both the immovable and the movable, produced by those high-minded ones by means of austerities and at my command, (each being) according to (the results of) its actions.

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ tu yādṛṣaṃ karma bhūtānām iha kīrtitam / tat tathā vo 'bhidhāsyāmi kramayogaṃ ca janmani //
english: But whatever act is stated (to belong) to (each of) those creatures here below, that I will truly declare to you, as well as their order in respect to birth.

sanskrit: paśavaś ca mṛgāś caiva vyālāś cobhayatodataḥ / rakṣāṃsi ca piśācāś ca manuṣyāś ca jarāyujāḥ // aṇḍājāḥ pakṣiṇaḥ sarpā nakrā matsyāś ca kacchapāḥ / yāni caivaM: prakārāṇi sthalajāny audakāni ca //
english: Cattle, deer, carnivorous beasts with two rows of teeth, Rakshasas, Pisakas, and men are born from the womb. From eggs are born birds, snakes, crocodiles, fishes, tortoises, as well as similar terrestrial and aquatic (animals). From hot moisture spring stinging and biting insects, lice, flies, bugs, and all other (creatures) of that kind which are produced by heat.

sanskrit: udbhijjāḥ sthāvarāḥ sarve bījakāṇḍaprarohiṇaḥ / oṣadhyaḥ phalapākāntā bahupuṣpaphalopagāḥ // apuṣpāḥ phalavanto ye te vanaspatayaḥ smṛtāḥ / puṣpiṇaḥ phalinaś caiva vṛkṣās tūbhayataḥ smṛtāḥ // gucchagulmaṃ tu vividhaṃ tathaiva tṛṇajātayaḥ / bījakāṇḍaruhāṇy eva pratānā vallya eva ca //
english: All plants, propagated by seed or by slips, grow from shoots; annual plants (are those) which, bearing many flowers and fruits, perish after the ripening of their fruit; (Those trees) which bear fruit without flowers are called vanaspati (lords of the forest); but those which bear both flowers and fruit are called vriksha. But the various plants with many stalks, growing from one or several roots, the different kinds of grasses, the climbing plants and the creepers spring all from seed or from slips.

sanskrit: tamasā bahurūpeṇa veṣṭitāḥ karmahetunā / antaḥsaṃjñā bhavanty ete sukhaduḥkhasamanvitāḥ //
english: These (plants) which are surrounded by multiform Darkness, the result of their acts (in former existences), possess internal consciousness and experience pleasure and pain.

sanskrit: etadantās tu gatayo brahmādyāḥ samudāhṛtāḥ / ghore 'smin bhūtasaṃsāre nityaṃ satatayāyini //
english: The (various) conditions in this always terrible and constantly changing circle of births and deaths to which created beings are subject, are stated to begin with (that of) Brahman, and to end with (that of) these (just mentioned immovable creatures).

sanskrit: evaṃ sarvaṃ sa sṛṣṭvedaṃ māṃ cācintyaparākramaḥ / ātmany antardadhe bhūyaḥ kālaṃ kālena pīḍayan //
english: When he whose power is incomprehensible, had thus produced the universe and men, he disappeared in himself, repeatedly suppressing one period by means of the other.

sanskrit: yadā sa devo jāgarti tad evaṃ ceṣṭate jagat / yadā svapiti śāntātmā tadā sarvaṃ nimīlati //
english: When that divine one wakes, then this world stirs; when he slumbers tranquilly, then the universe sinks to sleep.

sanskrit: tasmin svapiti tu svasthe karmātmānaḥ śarīriṇaḥ / svakarmabhyo nivartante manaś ca glānim ṛcchati //
english: But when he reposes in calm sleep, the corporeal beings whose nature is action, desist from their actions and mind becomes inert.

sanskrit: yugapat tu pralīyante yadā tasmin mahātmani / tadāyaṃ sarvabhūtātmā sukhaṃ svapiti nirvṛtaḥ //
english: When they are absorbed all at once in that great soul, then he who is the soul of all beings sweetly slumbers, free from all care and occupation.

sanskrit: tamo 'yaṃ tu samāśritya ciraṃ tiṣṭhati sendriyaḥ / na ca svaṃ kurute karma tadotkrāmati mūrtitaḥ //
english: When this (soul) has entered darkness, it remains for a long time united with the organs (of sensation), but performs not its functions; it then leaves the corporeal frame.

sanskrit: yadāṇumātriko bhūtvā bījaṃ sthāsnu cariṣṇu ca / samāviśati saṃsṛṣṭas tadā mūrtiṃ vimuñcati //
english: When, being clothed with minute particles (only), it enters into vegetable or animal seed, it then assumes, united (with the fine body), a (new) corporeal frame.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa jāgratsvapnābhyām idaṃ sarvaṃ carācaram / saṃjīvayati cājasraṃ pramāpayati cāvyayaḥ //
english: Thus he, the imperishable one, by (alternately) waking and slumbering, incessantly revivifies and destroys this whole movable and immovable (creation).

sanskrit: idaṃ śāstraṃ tu kṛtvāsau mām eva svayam āditaḥ / vidhivad grāhayām āsa marīcyādīṃs tv ahaṃ munīn //
english: But he having composed these Institutes (of the sacred law), himself taught them, according to the rule, to me alone in the beginning; next I (taught them) to Mariki and the other sages.

sanskrit: etad vo 'yaṃ bhṛguḥ śāstraṃ śrāvayiṣyaty aśesataḥ / etad dhi matto 'dhijage sarvam eṣo 'khilaṃ muniḥ //
english: Bhrigu, here, will fully recite to you these Institutes; for that sage learned the whole in its entirety from me.

sanskrit: tatas tathā sa tenokto maharṣimanunā bhṛguḥ / tān abravīd ṛṣīn sarvān prītātmā śrūyatām iti //
english: Then that great sage Bhrigu, being thus addressed by Manu, spoke, pleased in his heart, to all the sages, 'Listen!'

sanskrit: svāyaṃbhuvasyāsya manoḥ ṣaḍvaṃśyā manavo 'pare / sṛṣṭavantaḥ prajāḥ svāḥ svā mahātmāno mahaujasaḥ //
english: Six other high-minded, very powerful Manus, who belong to the race of this Manu, the descendant of the Self-existent (Svayambhu), and who have severally produced created beings,

sanskrit: svārociṣaś cottamaś ca tāmaso raivatas tathā / cākṣuṣaś ca mahātejā vivasvatsuta eva ca //
english: (Are) Svarokisha, Auttami, Tamasa, Raivata, Kakshusha, possessing great lustre, and the son of Vivasvat.

sanskrit: svāyaṃbhuvādyāḥ saptaite manavo bhūritejasaḥ / sve sve 'ntare sarvam idam utpādyāpuś carācaram //
english: These seven very glorious Manus, the first among whom is Svayambhuva, produced and protected this whole movable and immovable (creation), each during the period (allotted to him).

sanskrit: nimeṣā daśa cāṣṭau ca kāṣṭhā triṃśat tu tāḥ kalā / triṃśat kalā muhūrtaḥ syād ahorātraṃ tu tāvataḥ //
english: Eighteen nimeshas (twinklings of the eye, are one kashtha), thirty kashthas one kala, thirty kalas one muhurta, and as many (muhurtas) one day and night.

sanskrit: ahorātre vibhajate sūryo mānuṣadaivike / rātriḥ svapnāya bhūtānāṃ ceṣṭāyai karmaṇām ahaḥ //
english: The sun divides days and nights, both human and divine, the night (being intended) for the repose of created beings and the day for exertion.

sanskrit: pitrye rātryahanī māsaḥ pravibhāgas tu pakṣayoḥ / karmaceṣṭāsv ahaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ śuklaḥ svapnāya śarvarī //
english: A month is a day and a night of the manes, but the division is according to fortnights. The dark (fortnight) is their day for active exertion, the bright (fortnight) their night for sleep.

sanskrit: daive rātryahanī varṣaṃ pravibhāgas tayoḥ punaḥ / ahas tatrodagayanaṃ rātriḥ syād dakṣiṇāyanam //
english: A year is a day and a night of the gods; their division is (as follows): the half year during which the sun progresses to the north will be the day, that during which it goes southwards the night.

sanskrit: brāhmasya tu kṣapāhasya yat pramāṇaṃ samāsataḥ / ekaikaśo yugānāṃ tu kramaśas tan nibodhata //
english: But hear now the brief (description of) the duration of a night and a day of Brahman and of the several ages (of the world, yuga) according to their order.

sanskrit: catvāry āhuḥ sahasrāṇi varsāṇāṃ tat kṛtaṃ yugam / tasya tāvac chatī saṃdhyā saṃdhyāṃśaś ca tathāvidhaḥ //
english: They declare that the Krita age (consists of) four thousand years (of the gods); the twilight preceding it consists of as many hundreds, and the twilight following it of the same number.

sanskrit: itareṣu sasaṃdhyeṣu sasaṃdhyāṃśeṣu ca triṣu / ekāpāyena vartante sahasrāṇi śatāni ca //
english: In the other three ages with their twilights preceding and following, the thousands and hundreds are diminished by one (in each).

sanskrit: yad etat parisaṃkhyātam ādāv eva caturyugam / etad dvādaśasāhasraṃ devānāṃ yugam ucyate //
english: These twelve thousand (years) which thus have been just mentioned as the total of four (human) ages, are called one age of the gods.

sanskrit: daivikānāṃ yugānāṃ tu sahasraṃ parisaṃkhyayā / brāhmam ekam ahar jñeyaṃ tāvatīṃ rātrim eva ca // tad vai yugasahasrāntaṃ brāhmaṃ puṇyam ahar viduḥ / rātriṃ ca tāvatīm eva te 'horātravido janāḥ //
english: But know that the sum of one thousand ages of the gods (makes) one day of Brahman, and that his night has the same length. Those (only, who) know that the holy day of Brahman, indeed, ends after (the completion of) one thousand ages (of the gods) and that his night lasts as long, (are really) men acquainted with (the length of) days and nights.

sanskrit: tasya so 'harniśasyānte prasuptaḥ pratibudhyate / pratibuddhaś ca sṛjati manaḥ sadasadātmakam //
english: At the end of that day and night he who was asleep, awakes and, after awaking, creates mind, which is both real and unreal.

sanskrit: manaḥ sṛṣṭiṃ vikurute codyamānaṃ sisṛkṣayā / ākāśaṃ jāyate tasmāt tasya śabdaṃ guṇaṃ viduḥ //
english: Mind, impelled by (Brahman's) desire to create, performs the work of creation by modifying itself, thence ether is produced; they declare that sound is the quality of the latter.

sanskrit: ākāśāt tu vikurvāṇāt sarvagandhavahaḥ śuciḥ / balavāñ jāyate vāyuḥ sa vai sparśaguṇo mataḥ //
english: But from ether, modifying itself, springs the pure, powerful wind, the vehicle of all perfumes; that is held to possess the quality of touch.

sanskrit: vāyor api vikurvāṇād virociṣṇu tamonudam / jyotir utpadyate bhāsvat tad rūpaguṇam ucyate //
english: Next from wind modifying itself, proceeds the brilliant light, which illuminates and dispels darkness; that is declared to possess the quality of colour;

sanskrit: jyotiṣaś ca vikurvāṇād āpo rasaguṇāḥ smṛtāḥ / adbhyo gandhaguṇā bhūmir ity eṣā sṛṣṭir āditaḥ //
english: And from light, modifying itself, (is produced) water, possessing the quality of taste, from water earth which has the quality of smell; such is the creation in the beginning.

sanskrit: yad prāg dvādaśasāhasram uditaṃ daivikaṃ yugam / tad ekasaptatiguṇaṃ manvantaram ihocyate //
english: The before-mentioned age of the gods, (or) twelve thousand (of their years), being multiplied by seventy-one, (constitutes what) is here named the period of a Manu (Manvantara).

sanskrit: manvantarāṇy asaṃkhyāni sargaḥ saṃhāra eva ca / krīḍann ivaitat kurute parameṣṭhī punaḥ punaḥ //
english: The Manvantaras, the creations and destructions (of the world, are) numberless; sporting, as it were, Brahman repeats this again and again.

sanskrit: catuṣpāt sakalo dharmaḥ satyaṃ caiva kṛte yuge / nādharmeṇāgamaḥ kaś cin manuṣyān prati vartate // itareṣv āgamād dharmaḥ pādaśas tv avaropitaḥ / caurikānṛtamāyābhir dharmaś cāpaiti pādaśaḥ //
english: In the Krita age Dharma is four-footed and entire, and (so is) Truth; nor does any gain accrue to men by unrighteousness. In the other (three ages), by reason of (unjust) gains (agama), Dharma is deprived successively of one foot, and through (the prevalence of) theft, falsehood, and fraud the merit (gained by men) is diminished by one fourth (in each).

sanskrit: arogāḥ sarvasiddhārthāś caturvarṣaśatāyuṣaḥ / kṛte tretādiṣu hy eṣāṃ āyur hrasati pādaśaḥ //
english: (Men are) free from disease, accomplish all their aims, and live four hundred years in the Krita age, but in the Treta and (in each of) the succeeding (ages) their life is lessened by one quarter.

sanskrit: vedoktam āyur martyānām āśiṣaś caiva karmaṇām / phalanty anuyugaṃ loke prabhāvaś ca śarīriṇām //
english: The life of mortals, mentioned in the Veda, the desired results of sacrificial rites and the (supernatural) power of embodied (spirits) are fruits proportioned among men according to (the character of) the age.

sanskrit: anye kṛtayuge dharmās tretāyāṃ dvāpare 'pare / anye kaliyuge nṝṇāṃ yugahrāsānurūpataḥ //
english: One set of duties (is prescribed) for men in the Krita age, different ones in the Treta and in the Dvapara, and (again) another (set) in the Kali, in a proportion as (those) ages decrease in length.

sanskrit: tapaḥ paraṃ kṛtayuge tretāyāṃ jñānam ucyate / dvāpare yajñam evāhur dānam ekaṃ kalau yuge //
english: In the Krita age the chief (virtue) is declared to be (the performance of) austerities, in the Treta (divine) knowledge, in the Dvapara (the performance of) sacrifices, in the Kali liberality alone.

sanskrit: sarvasyāsya tu sargasya guptyarthaṃ sa mahādyutiḥ / mukhabāhūrupajjānāṃ pṛthakkarmāṇy akalpayat //
english: But in order to protect this universe He, the most resplendent one, assigned separate (duties and) occupations to those who sprang from his mouth, arms, thighs, and feet.

sanskrit: adhyāpanam adhyayanaṃ yajanaṃ yājanaṃ tathā / dānaṃ pratigrahaṃ caiva brāhmaṇānām akalpayat //
english: To Brahmanas he assigned teaching and studying (the Veda), sacrificing for their own benefit and for others, giving and accepting (of alms).

sanskrit: prajānāṃ rakṣaṇaṃ dānam ijyādhyayanam eva ca / viṣayeṣv aprasaktiś ca kṣatriyasya samāsataḥ //
english: The Kshatriya he commanded to protect the people, to bestow gifts, to offer sacrifices, to study (the Veda), and to abstain from attaching himself to sensual pleasures;

sanskrit: paśūnāṃ rakṣaṇaṃ dānam ijyādhyayanam eva ca / vaṇikpathaṃ kusīdaṃ ca vaiśyasya kṛṣim eva ca //
english: The Vaisya to tend cattle, to bestow gifts, to offer sacrifices, to study (the Veda), to trade, to lend money, and to cultivate land.

sanskrit: ekam eva tu śūdrasya prabhuḥ karma samādiśat / eteṣām eva varṇānāṃ śuśrūṣām anasūyayā //
english: One occupation only the lord prescribed to the Sudra, to serve meekly even these (other) three castes.

sanskrit: ūrdhvaṃ nābher medhyataraḥ puruṣaḥ parikīrtitaḥ / tasmān medhyatamaṃ tv asya mukham uktaṃ svayaṃbhuvā //
english: Man is stated to be purer above the navel (than below); hence the Self-existent (Svayambhu) has declared the purest (part) of him (to be) his mouth.

sanskrit: yasyāsyena sadāśnanti havyāni tridivaukasaḥ / kavyāni caiva pitaraḥ kiṃ bhūtam adhikaṃ tataḥ //
english: What created being can surpass him, through whose mouth the gods continually consume the sacrificial viands and the manes the offerings to the dead?

sanskrit: bhūtānāṃ prāṇinaḥ śreṣṭhāḥ prāṇināṃ buddhijīvinaḥ / buddhimatsu narāḥ śreṣṭhā nareṣu brāhmaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ //
english: Of created beings the most excellent are said to be those which are animated; of the animated, those which subsist by intelligence; of the intelligent, mankind; and of men, the Brahmanas;

sanskrit: brāhmaṇeṣu ca vidvāṃso vidvatsu kṛtabuddhayaḥ / kṛtabuddhiṣu kartāraḥ kartṛṣu brahmavedinaḥ //
english: Of Brahmanas, those learned (in the Veda); of the learned, those who recognise (the necessity and the manner of performing the prescribed duties); of those who possess this knowledge, those who perform them; of the performers, those who know the Brahman.

sanskrit: utpattir eva viprasya mūrtir dharmasya śāśvatī / sa hi dharmārtham utpanno brahmabhūyāya kalpate //
english: The very birth of a Brahmana is an eternal incarnation of the sacred law; for he is born to (fulfil) the sacred law, and becomes one with Brahman.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo jāyamāno hi pṛthivyām adhijāyate / īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ dharmakośasya guptaye //
english: A Brahmana, coming into existence, is born as the highest on earth, the lord of all created beings, for the protection of the treasury of the law.

sanskrit: sarvaṃ svaṃ brāhmaṇasyedaṃ yat kiṃ cij jagatīgataṃ / śraiṣṭhyenābhijanenedaṃ sarvaṃ vai brāhmaṇo 'rhati //
english: Whatever exists in the world is, the property of the Brahmana; on account of the excellence of his origin The Brahmana is, indeed, entitled to all.

sanskrit: svam eva brāhmaṇo bhuṅkte svaṃ vaste svaṃ dadāti ca / ānṛśaṃsyād brāhmaṇasya bhuñjate hītare janāḥ //
english: The Brahmana eats but his own food, wears but his own apparel, bestows but his own in alms; other mortals subsist through the benevolence of the Brahmana.

sanskrit: tasya karmavivekārthaṃ śeṣāṇām anupūrvaśaḥ / svāyaṃbhuvo manur dhīmān idaṃ śāstram akalpayat //
english: In order to clearly settle his duties those of the other (castes) according to their order, wise Manu sprung from the Self-existent, composed these Institutes (of the sacred Law).

sanskrit: viduṣā brāhmaṇenedam adhyetavyaṃ prayatnataḥ / śiśyebhyaś ca pravaktavyaṃ samyaṅ nānyena kena cit //
english: A learned Brahmana must carefully study them, and he must duly instruct his pupils in them, but nobody else (shall do it).

sanskrit: idaṃ śāstram adhīyāno brāhmaṇaḥ śaṃsitavrataḥ / manovāggehajair nityaṃ karmadoṣair na lipyate //
english: A Brahmana who studies these Institutes (and) faithfully fulfils the duties (prescribed therein), is never tainted by sins, arising from thoughts, words, or deeds.

sanskrit: punāti paṅktiṃ vaṃśyāṃś ca saptasapta parāvarān / pṛthivīm api caivemāṃ kṛtsnām eko 'pi so 'rhati //
english: He sanctifies any company (which he may enter), seven ancestors and seven descendants, and he alone deserves (to possess) this whole earth.

sanskrit: idaṃ svastyayanaṃ śreṣṭham idaṃ buddhivivardhanam / idaṃ yaśasyam āyuṣyam idaṃ niḥśreyasaṃ param //
english: (To study) this (work) is the best means of securing welfare, it increases understanding, it procures fame and long life, it (leads to) supreme bliss.

sanskrit: asmin dharmo 'khilenokto guṇadoṣau ca karmaṇām / caturṇām api varṇānām ācāraś caiva śāśvataḥ //
english: In this (work) the sacred law has been fully stated as well as the good and bad qualities of (human) actions and the immemorial rule of conduct, (to be followed) by all the four castes (varna).

sanskrit: ācāraḥ paramo dharmaḥ śrutyuktaḥ smārta eva ca / tasmād asmin sadā yukto nityaṃ syād ātmavān dvijaḥ //
english: The rule of conduct is transcendent law, whether it be taught in the revealed texts or in the sacred tradition; hence a twice-born man who possesses regard for himself, should be always careful to (follow) it.

sanskrit: ācārād vicyuto vipro na vedaphalam aśnute / ācāreṇa tu saṃyuktaḥ sampūrṇaphalabhāj bhavet //
english: A Brahmana who departs from the rule of conduct, does not reap the fruit of the Veda, but he who duly follows it, will obtain the full reward.

sanskrit: evam ācārato dṛṣṭvā dharmasya munayo gatiṃ / sarvasya tapaso mūlam ācāraṃ jagṛhuḥ param //
english: The sages who saw that the sacred law is thus grounded on the rule of conduct, have taken good conduct to be the most excellent root of all austerity.

sanskrit: jagataś ca samutpattiṃ saṃskāravidhim eva ca / vratacaryopacāraṃ ca snānasya ca paraṃ vidhim //
english: The creation of the universe, the rule of the sacraments, the ordinances of studentship, and the respectful behaviour (towards Gurus), the most excellent rule of bathing (on return from the teacher's house),

sanskrit: dārādhigamanaṃ caiva vivāhānāṃ ca lakṣaṇam / mahāyajñavidhānaṃ ca śrāddhakalpaṃ ca śāśvatam //
english: (The law of) marriage and the description of the (various) marriage-rites, the regulations for the great sacrifices and the eternal rule of the funeral sacrifices,

sanskrit: vṛttīnāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ caiva snātakasya vratāni ca / bhakṣyābhakṣyaṃ ca śaucaṃ ca dravyāṇāṃ śuddhim eva ca //
english: The description of the modes of (gaining) subsistence and the duties of a Snataka, (the rules regarding) lawful and forbidden food, the purification of men and of things,

sanskrit: strīdharmayogaṃ tāpasyaṃ mokṣaṃ saṃnyāsam eva ca / rājñaś ca dharmam akhilaṃ kāryāṇāṃ ca vinirṇayam //
english: The laws concerning women, (the law) of hermits, (the manner of gaining) final emancipation and (of) renouncing the world, the whole duty of a king and the manner of deciding lawsuits,

sanskrit: sākṣipraśnavidhānaṃ ca dharmaṃ strīpuṃsayor api / vibhāgadharmaṃ dyūtaṃ ca kaṇṭakānāṃ ca śodhanam // vaiśyaśūdropacāraṃ ca saṃkīrṇānāṃ ca saṃbhavam / āpaddharmaṃ ca varṇānāṃ prāyaścittavidhiṃ tathā //
english: The rules for the examination of witnesses, the laws concerning husband and wife, the law of (inheritance and) division, (the law concerning) gambling and the removal of (men nocuous like) thorns, (The law concerning) the behaviour of Vaisyas and Sudras, the origin of the mixed castes, the law for all castes in times of distress and the law of penances,

sanskrit: saṃsāragamanaṃ caiva trividhaṃ karmasaṃbhavam / niḥśreyasaṃ karmaṇāṃ ca guṇadoṣaparīkṣaṇam //
english: The threefold course of transmigrations, the result of (good or bad) actions, (the manner of attaining) supreme bliss and the examination of the good and bad qualities of actions,

sanskrit: deśadharmāñ jātidharmān kuladharmāṃś ca śāśvatān / pāṣaṇḍagaṇadharmāṃś ca śāstre 'sminn uktavān manuḥ //
english: The primeval laws of countries, of castes (gati), of families, and the rules concerning heretics and companies (of traders and the like)- (all that) Manu has declared in these Institutes.

sanskrit: yathedam uktavāñ śāstraṃ purā pṛṣṭo manur mayā / tathedaṃ yūyam apy adya matsakāśān nibodhata //
english: As Manu, in reply to my questions, formerly promulgated these Institutes, even so learn ye also the (whole work) from me.

sanskrit: vidvadbhiḥ sevitaḥ sadbhir nityam adveṣarāgibhiḥ / hṛdayenābhyanujñāto yo dharmas taṃ nibodhata //
english: Learn that sacred law which is followed by men learned (in the Veda) and assented to in their hearts by the virtuous, who are ever exempt from hatred and inordinate affection.

sanskrit: kāmātmatā na praśastā na caivehāsty akāmatā / kāmyo hi vedādhigamaḥ karmayogaś ca vaidikaḥ //
english: To act solely from a desire for rewards is not laudable, yet an exemption from that desire is not (to be found) in this (world): for on (that) desire is grounded the study of the Veda and the performance of the actions, prescribed by the Veda.

sanskrit: saṃkalpamūlaḥ kāmo vai yajñāḥ saṃkalpasaṃbhavāḥ / vratāni yamadharmāś ca sarve saṃkalpajāḥ smṛtāḥ //
english: The desire (for rewards), indeed, has its root in the conception that an act can yield them, and in consequence of (that) conception sacrifices are performed; vows and the laws prescribing restraints are all stated to be kept through the idea that they will bear fruit.

sanskrit: akāmasya kriyā kā cid dṛśyate neha karhi cit / yad yad dhi kurute kiṃ cit tat tat kāmasya ceṣṭitam //
english: Not a single act here (below) appears ever to be done by a man free from desire; for whatever (man) does, it is (the result of) the impulse of desire.

sanskrit: teṣu samyag vartamāno gacchaty amaralokatām / yathā saṃkalpitāṃś ceha sarvān kāmān samaśnute //
english: He who persists in discharging these (prescribed duties) in the right manner, reaches the deathless state and even in this (life) obtains (the fulfilment of) all the desires that he may have conceived.

sanskrit: vedo 'khilo dharmamūlaṃ smṛtiśīle ca tadvidām / ācāraś caiva sādhūnām ātmanas tuṣṭir eva ca //
english: The whole Veda is the (first) source of the sacred law, next the tradition and the virtuous conduct of those who know the (Veda further), also the customs of holy men, and (finally) self-satisfaction.

sanskrit: yaḥ kaś cit kasya cid dharmo manunā parikīrtitaḥ / sa sarvo 'bhihito vede sarvajñānamayo hi saḥ //
english: Whatever law has been ordained for any (person) by Manu, that has been fully declared in the Veda: for that (sage was) omniscient.

sanskrit: sarvaṃ tu samavekṣyedaṃ nikhilaṃ jñānacakṣuṣā / śrutiprāmāṇyato vidvān svadharme niviśeta vai //
english: But a learned man after fully scrutinising all this with the eye of knowledge, should, in accordance with the authority of the revealed texts, be intent on (the performance of) his duties.

sanskrit: śrutismṛtyuditaṃ dharmam anutiṣṭhan hi mānavaḥ / iha kīrtim avāpnoti pretya cānuttamaṃ sukham //
english: For that man who obeys the law prescribed in the revealed texts and in the sacred tradition, gains fame in this (world) and after death unsurpassable bliss.

sanskrit: śrutis tu vedo vijñeyo dharmaśāstraṃ tu vai smṛtiḥ / te sarvārtheṣv amīmāṃsye tābhyāṃ dharmo hi nirbabhau // yo 'vamanyeta te mūle hetuśāstrāśrayād dvijaḥ / sa sādhubhir bahiṣkāryo nāstiko vedanindakaḥ //
english: But by Sruti (revelation) is meant the Veda, and by Smriti (tradition) the Institutes of the sacred law: those two must not be called into question in any matter, since from those two the sacred law shone forth. Every twice-born man, who, relying on the Institutes of dialectics, treats with contempt those two sources (of the law), must be cast out by the virtuous, as an atheist and a scorner of the Veda.

sanskrit: vedaḥ smṛtiḥ sadācāraḥ svasya ca priyam ātmanaḥ / etac caturvidhaṃ prāhuḥ sākṣād dharmasya lakṣaṇam //
english: The Veda, the sacred tradition, the customs of virtuous men, and one's own pleasure, they declare to be visibly the fourfold means of defining the sacred law.

sanskrit: arthakāmeṣv asaktānāṃ dharmajñānaṃ vidhīyate / dharmaṃ jijñāsamānānāṃ pramāṇaṃ paramaṃ śrutiḥ //
english: The knowledge of the sacred law is prescribed for those who are not given to the acquisition of wealth and to the gratification of their desires; to those who seek the knowledge of the sacred law the supreme authority is the revelation (Sruti).

sanskrit: śrutidvaidhaṃ tu yatra syāt tatra dharmāv ubhau smṛtau / ubhāv api hi tau dharmau samyag uktau manīṣibhiḥ //
english: But when two sacred texts (Sruti) are conflicting, both are held to be law; for both are pronounced by the wise (to be) valid law.

sanskrit: udite 'nudite caiva samayādhyuṣite tathā / sarvathā vartate yajña itīyaṃ vaidikī śrutiḥ //
english: (Thus) the (Agnihotra) sacrifice may be (optionally) performed, at any time after the sun has risen, before he has risen, or when neither sun nor stars are visible; that (is declared) by Vedic texts.

sanskrit: niṣekādiśmaśānānto mantrair yasyodito vidhiḥ / tasya śāstre 'dhikāro 'smiñ jñeyo nānyasya kasya cit //
english: Know that he for whom (the performance of) the ceremonies beginning with the rite of impregnation (Garbhadhana) and ending with the funeral rite (Antyeshti) is prescribed, while sacred formulas are being recited, is entitled (to study) these Institutes, but no other man whatsoever.

sanskrit: sarasvatīdṛśadvatyor devanadyor yad antaram / taṃ devanirmitaṃ deśaṃ brahmāvartaṃ pracakṣate //
english: That land, created by the gods, which lies between the two divine rivers Sarasvati and Drishadvati, the (sages) call Brahmavarta.

sanskrit: tasmin deśe ya ācāraḥ pāramparyakramāgataḥ / varṇānāṃ sāntarālānāṃ sa sadācāra ucyate //
english: The custom handed down in regular succession (since time immemorial) among the (four chief) castes (varna) and the mixed (races) of that country, is called the conduct of virtuous men.

sanskrit: kurukṣetraṃ ca matsyāś ca pañcālāḥ śūrasenakāḥ / eṣa brahmarṣideśo vai brahmāvartād anantaraḥ //
english: The plain of the Kurus, the (country of the) Matsyas, Pankalas, and Surasenakas, these (form), indeed, the country of the Brahmarshis (Brahmanical sages, which ranks) immediately after Brahmavarta.

sanskrit: etad deśaprasūtasya sakāśād agrajanmanaḥ / svaṃ svaṃ caritraṃ śikṣeran pṛthivyāṃ sarvamānavāḥ //
english: From a Brahmana, born in that country, let all men on earth learn their several usages.

sanskrit: himavadvindhyayor madhyaṃ yat prāg vinaśanād api / pratyag eva prayāgāc ca madhyadeśaḥ prakīrtitaḥ //
english: That (country) which (lies) between the Himavat and the Vindhya (mountains) to the east of Prayaga and to the west of Vinasana (the place where the river Sarasvati disappears) is called Madhyadesa (the central region).

sanskrit: ā samudrāt tu vai pūrvād ā samudrāc ca paścimāt / tayor evāntaraṃ giryor āryāvartaṃ vidur budhāḥ //
english: But (the tract) between those two mountains (just mentioned), which (extends) as far as the eastern and the western oceans, the wise call Aryavarta (the country of the Aryans).

sanskrit: kṛṣṇasāras tu carati mṛgo yatra svabhāvataḥ / sa jñeyo yajñiyo deśo mlecchadeśas tv ataḥ paraḥ //
english: That land where the black antelope naturally roams, one must know to be fit for the performance of sacrifices; (the tract) different from that (is) the country of the Mlekkhas (barbarians).

sanskrit: etāṇ dvijātayo deśān saṃśrayeran prayatnataḥ / śūdras tu yasmin kasmin vā nivased vṛttikarśitaḥ //
english: Let twice-born men seek to dwell in those (above-mentioned countries); but a Sudra, distressed for subsistence, may reside anywhere.

sanskrit: eṣā dharmasya vo yoniḥ samāsena prakīrtitā / saṃbhavaś cāsya sarvasya varṇadharmān nibodhata //
english: Thus has the origin of the sacred law been succinctly described to you and the origin of this universe; learn (now) the duties of the castes (varna).

sanskrit: vaidikaiḥ karmabhiḥ puṇyair niṣekādir dvijanmanām / kāryaḥ śarīrasaṃskāraḥ pāvanaḥ pretya ceha ca //
english: With holy rites, prescribed by the Veda, must the ceremony on conception and other sacraments be performed for twice-born men, which sanctify the body and purify (from sin) in this (life) and after death.

sanskrit: gārbhair homair jātakarma- cauḍamauñjīnibandhanaiḥ / baijikaṃ gārbhikaṃ caino dvijānām apamṛjyate //
english: By burnt oblations during (the mother's) pregnancy, by the Gatakarman (the ceremony after birth), the Kauda (tonsure), and the Maungibandhana (the tying of the sacred girdle of Munga grass) is the taint, derived from both parents, removed from twice-born men.

sanskrit: svādhyāyena vratair homais traividyenejyayā sutaiḥ / mahāyajñaiś ca yajñaiś ca brāhmīyaṃ kriyate tanuḥ //
english: By the study of the Veda, by vows, by burnt oblations, by (the recitation of) sacred texts, by the (acquisition of the) threefold sacred science, by offering (to the gods, Rishis, and manes), by (the procreation of) sons, by the great sacrifices, and by (Srauta) rites this (human) body is made fit for (union with) Brahman.

sanskrit: prāṅ nābhivardhanāt puṃso jātakarma vidhīyate / mantravat prāśanaṃ cāsya hiraṇyamadhusarpiṣām //
english: Before the navel-string is cut, the Gatakarman (birth-rite) must be performed for a male (child); and while sacred formulas are being recited, he must be fed with gold, honey, and butter.

sanskrit: nāmadheyaṃ daśamyāṃ tu dvādaśyāṃ vāsya kārayet / puṇye tithau muhūrte vā nakṣatre vā guṇānvite //
english: But let (the father perform or) cause to be performed the Namadheya (the rite of naming the child), on the tenth or twelfth (day after birth), or on a lucky lunar day, in a lucky muhurta, under an auspicious constellation.

sanskrit: maṅgalyaṃ brāhmaṇasya syāt kṣatriyasya balānvitam / vaiśyasya dhanasaṃyuktaṃ śūdrasya tu jugupsitam // śarmavad brāhmaṇasya syād rājño rakṣāsamanvitam / vaiśyasya puṣṭisaṃyuktaṃ śūdrasya preṣyasaṃyutam //
english: Let (the first part of) a Brahmana's name (denote something) auspicious, a Kshatriya's be connected with power, and a Vaisya's with wealth, but a Sudra's (express something) contemptible. (The second part of) a Brahmana's (name) shall be (a word) implying happiness, of a Kshatriya's (a word) implying protection, of a Vaisya's (a term) expressive of thriving, and of a Sudra's (an expression) denoting service.

sanskrit: strīṇāṃ sukhodyam akrūraṃ vispaṣṭārthaṃ manoharam / maṅgalyaṃ dīrghavarṇāntam āśīrvādābhidhānavat //
english: The names of women should be easy to pronounce, not imply anything dreadful, possess a plain meaning, be pleasing and auspicious, end in long vowels, and contain a word of benediction.

sanskrit: caturthe māsi kartavyaṃ śiśor niṣkramaṇaṃ gṛhāt / ṣaṣṭhe 'nnaprāśanaṃ māsi yad veṣṭaṃ maṅgalaṃ kule //
english: In the fourth month the Nishkramana (the first leaving of the house) of the child should be performed, in the sixth month the Annaprasana (first feeding with rice), and optionally (any other) auspicious ceremony required by (the custom of) the family.

sanskrit: cūḍākarma dvijātīnāṃ sarveṣām eva dharmataḥ / prathame 'bde tṛtīye vā kartavyaṃ śruticodanāt //
english: According to the teaching of the revealed texts, the Kudakarman (tonsure) must be performed, for the sake of spiritual merit, by all twice-born men in the first or third year.

sanskrit: garbhāṣṭame 'bde kurvīta brāhmaṇasyopanāyanam / garbhād ekādaśe rājño garbhāt tu dvādaśe viśaḥ //
english: In the eighth year after conception, one should perform the initiation (upanayana) of a Brahmana, in the eleventh after conception (that) of a Kshatriya, but in the twelfth that of a Vaisya.

sanskrit: brahmavarcasakāmasya kāryo viprasya pañcame / rājño balārthinaḥ ṣaṣṭhe vaiśyasyehārthino 'ṣṭame //
english: (The initiation) of a Brahmana who desires proficiency in sacred learning should take place in the fifth (year after conception), (that) of a Kshatriya who wishes to become powerful in the sixth, (and that) of a Vaisya who longs for (success in his) business in the eighth.

sanskrit: ā ṣodaśād brāhmaṇasya sāvitrī nātivartate / ā dvāviṃśāt kṣatrabandhor ā caturviṃśater viśaḥ //
english: The (time for the) Savitri (initiation) of a Brahmana does not pass until the completion of the sixteenth year (after conception), of a Kshatriya until the completion of the twenty-second, and of a Vaisya until the completion of the twenty-fourth.

sanskrit: ata ūrdhvaṃ trayo 'py ete yathākālam asaṃskṛtāḥ / sāvitrīpatitā vrātyā bhavanty āryavigarhitāḥ //
english: After those (periods men of) these three (castes) who have not received the sacrament at the proper time, become Vratyas (outcasts), excluded from the Savitri (initiation) and despised by the Aryans.

sanskrit: naitair apūtair vidhivad āpady api hi karhi cit / brāhmān yaunāṃś ca saṃbandhān nācared brāhmaṇaḥ saha //
english: With such men, if they have not been purified according to the rule, let no Brahmana ever, even in times of distress, form a connexion either through the Veda or by marriage.

sanskrit: kārṣṇarauravabāstāni carmāṇi brahmacāriṇaḥ / vasīrann ānupūrvyeṇa śāṇakṣaumāvikāni ca //
english: Let students, according to the order (of their castes), wear (as upper dresses) the skins of black antelopes, spotted deer, and he-goats, and (lower garments) made of hemp, flax or wool.

sanskrit: mauñjī trivṛt samā ślakṣṇā kāryā viprasya mekhalā / kṣatriyasya tu maurvī jyā vaiśyasya śaṇatāntavī //
english: The girdle of a Brahmana shall consist of a of a triple cord of Munga grass, smooth and soft; (that) of a Kshatriya, of a bowstring, made of Murva fibres; (that) of a Vaisya, of hempen threads.

sanskrit: muñjālābhe tu kartavyāḥ kuśāśmantakabalvajaiḥ / trivṛtā granthinaikena tribhiḥ pañcabhir eva vā //
english: If Munga grass (and so forth) be not procurable, (the girdles) may be made of Kusa, Asmantaka, and Balbaga (fibres), with a single threefold knot, or with three or five (knots according to the custom of the family).

sanskrit: kārpāsam upavītaṃ syād viprasyordhvavṛtaṃ trivṛt / śaṇasūtramayaṃ rājño vaiśyasyāvikasautrikam //
english: The sacrificial string of a Brahmana shall be made of cotton, (shall be) twisted to the right, (and consist) of three threads, that of a Kshatriya of hempen threads, (and) that of a Vaisya of woollen threads.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo bailvapālāśau kṣatriyo vāṭakhādirau / pailavāudumbarau vaiśyo daṇḍān arhanti dharmataḥ //
english: A Brahmana shall (carry), according to the sacred law, a staff of Bilva or Palasa; a Kshatriya, of Vata or Khadira; (and) a Vaisya, of Pilu or Udumbara.

sanskrit: keśāntiko brāhmaṇasya daṇḍaḥ kāryaḥ pramāṇataḥ / lalāṭasammito rājñaḥ syāt tu nāsāntiko viśaḥ //
english: The staff of a Brahmana shall be made of such length as to reach the end of his hair; that of a Kshatriya, to reach his forehead;(and) that of a Vaisya, to reach (the tip of his) nose.

sanskrit: ṛjavas te tu sarve syur avraṇāḥ saumyadarśanāḥ / anudvegakarā nṝṇāṃ satvaco 'nagnidūṣitāḥ //
english: Let all the staves be straight, without a blemish, handsome to look at, not likely to terrify men, with their bark perfect, unhurt by fire.

sanskrit: pratigṛhyepsitaṃ daṇḍam upasthāya ca bhāskaram / pradakṣiṇaṃ parītyāgniṃ cared bhaikṣaṃ yathāvidhi //
english: Having taken a staff according to his choice, having worshipped the sun and walked round the fire, turning his right hand towards it, (the student) should beg alms according to the prescribed rule.

sanskrit: bhavatpūrvaṃ cared bhaikṣam upanīto dvijottamaḥ / bhavanmadhyaṃ tu rājanyo vaiśyas tu bhavaduttaram //
english: An initiated Brahmana should beg, beginning (his request with the word) lady (bhavati); a Kshatriya, placing (the word) lady in the middle, but a Vaisya, placing it at the end (of the formula).

sanskrit: mātaraṃ vā svasāraṃ vā mātur vā bhaginīṃ nijām / bhikṣeta bhikṣāṃ prathamaṃ yā cainaṃ nāvamānayet //
english: Let him first beg food of his mother, or of his sister, or of his own maternal aunt, or of (some other) female who will not disgrace him (by a refusal).

sanskrit: samāhṛtya tu tad bhaikṣaṃ yāvadannam amāyayā / nivedya gurave 'śnīyād ācamya prāṅmukhaḥ śuciḥ //
english: Having collected as much food as is required (from several persons), and having announced it without guile to his teacher, let him eat, turning his face towards the east, and having purified himself by sipping water.

sanskrit: āyuṣyaṃ prāṅmukho bhuṅkte yaśasyaṃ dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ / śriyaṃ pratyaṅmukho bhuṅkte ṛtaṃ bhuṅkte hy udaṅmukhaḥ //
english: (His meal will procure) long life, if he eats facing the east; fame, if he turns to the south; prosperity, if he turns to the west; truthfulness, if he faces the east.

sanskrit: upaspṛśya dvijo nityam annam adyāt samāhitaḥ / bhuktvā copaspṛśet samyag adbhiḥ khāni ca saṃspṛśet //
english: Let a twice-born man always eat his food with concentrated mind, after performing an ablution; and after he has eaten, let him duly cleanse himself with water and sprinkle the cavities (of his head).

sanskrit: pūjayed aśanaṃ nityam adyāc caitad akutsayan / dṛṣṭvā hṛṣyet prasīdec ca pratinandec ca sarvaśaḥ //
english: Let him always worship his food, and eat it without contempt; when he sees it, let him rejoice, show a pleased face, and pray that he may always obtain it.

sanskrit: pūjitaṃ hy aśanaṃ nityaṃ balam ūrjaṃ ca yacchati / apūjitaṃ tu tad bhuktam ubhayaṃ nāśayed idam //
english: Food, that is always worshipped, gives strength and manly vigour; but eaten irreverently, it destroys them both.

sanskrit: nocchiṣṭaṃ kasya cid dadyān nādyād etat tathāntarā / na caivātyaśanaṃ kuryān na cocchiṣṭaḥ kva cid vrajet //
english: Let him not give to any man what he leaves, and beware of eating between (the two meal-times); let him not over-eat himself, nor go anywhere without having purified himself (after his meal).

sanskrit: anārogyam anāyuṣyam asvargyaṃ cātibhojanam / apuṇyaṃ lokavidviṣṭaṃ tasmāt tat parivarjayet //
english: Excessive eating is prejudicial to health, to fame, and to (bliss in) heaven; it prevents (the acquisition of) spiritual merit, and is odious among men; one ought, for these reasons, to avoid it carefully.

sanskrit: brāhmeṇa vipras tīrthena nityakālam upaspṛśet / kāyatraidaśikābhyāṃ vā na pitryeṇa kadā cana //
english: Let a Brahmana always sip water out of the part of the hand (tirtha) sacred to Brahman, or out of that sacred to Ka (Pragapati), or out of (that) sacred to the gods, never out of that sacred to the manes.

sanskrit: aṅguṣṭhamūlasya tale brāhmaṃ tīrthaṃ pracakṣate / kāyam aṅgulimūle 'gre devaṃ pitryaṃ tayor adhaḥ //
english: They call (the part) at the root of the thumb the tirtha sacred to Brahman, that at the root of the (little) finger (the tirtha) sacred to Ka (Pragapati), (that) at the tips (of the fingers, the tirtha) sacred to the gods, and that below (between the index and the thumb, the tirtha) sacred to the manes.

sanskrit: trir ācāmed apaḥ pūrvaṃ dviḥ pramṛjyāt tato mukham / khāni caiva spṛśed adbhir ātmānaṃ śira eva ca //
english: Let him first sip water thrice; next twice wipe his mouth; and, lastly, touch with water the cavities (of the head), (the seat of) the soul and the head.

sanskrit: anuṣṇābhir aphenābhir adbhis tīrthena dharmavit / śaucepsuḥ sarvadācāmed ekānte prāgudaṅmukhaḥ //
english: He who knows the sacred law and seeks purity shall always perform the rite of sipping with water neither hot nor frothy, with the (prescribed) tirtha, in a lonely place, and turning to the east or to the north.

sanskrit: hṛdgābhiḥ pūyate vipraḥ kaṇṭhagābhis tu bhūmipaḥ / vaiśyo 'dbhiḥ prāśitābhis tu śūdraḥ spṛṣṭābhir antataḥ //
english: A Brahmana is purified by water that reaches his heart, a Kshatriya by water reaching his throat, a Vaisya by water taken into his mouth, (and) a Sudra by water touched with the extremity (of his lips).

sanskrit: uddhṛte dakṣine pāṇāv upavīty ucyate dvijaḥ / savye prācīnāvītī nivītī kaṇṭhasajjane //
english: A twice-born man is called upavitin when his right arm is raised (and the sacrificial string or the dress, passed under it, rests on the left shoulder); (when his) left (arm) is raised (and the string, or the dress, passed under it, rests on the right shoulder, he is called) prakinavitin; and nivitin when it hangs down (straight) from the neck.

sanskrit: mekhalām ajinaṃ daṇḍam upavītaṃ kamaṇḍalum / apsu prāsya vinaṣṭāni gṛhṇītānyāni mantravat //
english: His girdle, the skin (which serves as his upper garment), his staff, his sacrificial thread, (and) his water-pot he must throw into water, when they have been damaged, and take others, reciting sacred formulas.

sanskrit: keśāntaḥ ṣoḍaśe varṣe brāhmaṇasya vidhīyate / rājanyabandhor dvāviṃśe vaiśyasya dvyadhike mataḥ //
english: (The ceremony called) Kesanta (clipping the hair) is ordained for a Brahmana in the sixteenth year (from conception); for a Kshatriya, in the twenty-second; and for a Vaisya, two (years) later than that.

sanskrit: amantrikā tu kāryeyaṃ strīṇām āvṛd aśeṣataḥ / saṃskārārthaṃ śarīrasya yathākālaṃ yathākramam //
english: This whole series (of ceremonies) must be performed for females (also), in order to sanctify the body, at the proper time and in the proper order, but without (the recitation of) sacred texts.

sanskrit: vaivāhiko vidhiḥ strīṇāṃ saṃskāro vaidikaḥ smṛtaḥ / patisevā gurau vāso gṛhārtho 'gniparikriyā //
english: The nuptial ceremony is stated to be the Vedic sacrament for women (and to be equal to the initiation), serving the husband (equivalent to) the residence in (the house of the) teacher, and the household duties (the same) as the (daily) worship of the sacred fire.

sanskrit: eṣa prokto dvijātīnām aupanāyaniko vidhiḥ / utpattivyañjakaḥ puṇyaḥ karmayogaṃ nibodhata //
english: Thus has been described the rule for the initiation of the twice-born, which indicates a (new) birth, and sanctifies; learn (now) to what duties they must afterwards apply themselves.

sanskrit: upanīya guruḥ śiṣyaṃ śikṣayec chaucam āditaḥ / ācāram agnikāryaṃ ca saṃdhyopāsanam eva ca //
english: Having performed the (rite of) initiation, the teacher must first instruct the (pupil) in (the rules of) personal purification, of conduct, of the fire-worship, and of the twilight devotions.

sanskrit: adhyeṣyamāṇas tv ācānto yathāśāstram udaṅmukhaḥ / brahmāñjalikṛto 'dhyāpyo laghuvāsā jitendriyaḥ //
english: But (a student) who is about to begin the Study (of the Veda), shall receive instruction, after he has sipped water in accordance with the Institutes (of the sacred law), has made the Brahmangali, (has put on) a clean dress, and has brought his organs under due control.

sanskrit: brahmārambhe 'vasāne ca pādau grāhyau guroḥ sadā / saṃhatya hastāv adhyeyaṃ sa hi brahmāñjaliḥ smṛtaḥ //
english: At the beginning and at the end of (a lesson in the) Veda he must always clasp both the feet of his teacher, (and) he must study, joining his hands; that is called the Brahmangali (joining the palms for the sake of the Veda).

sanskrit: vyatyastapāṇinā kāryam upasaṃgrahaṇaṃ guroḥ / savyena savyaḥ spraṣṭavyo dakṣiṇena ca dakṣiṇaḥ //
english: With crossed hands he must clasp (the feet) of the teacher, and touch the left (foot) with his left (hand), the right (foot) with his right (hand).

sanskrit: adhyeṣyamāṇaṃ tu gurur nityakālam atandritaḥ / adhīṣva bho iti brūyād virāmo 'stv iti cāramet //
english: But to him who is about to begin studying, the teacher always unwearied, must say: Ho, recite! He shall leave off (when the teacher says): Let a stoppage take place!

sanskrit: brahmanaḥ praṇavaṃ kuryād ādāv ante ca sarvadā / sravaty anoṃkṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ parastāc ca viśīryati //
english: Let him always pronounce the syllable Om at the beginning and at the end of (a lesson in) the Veda; (for) unless the syllable Om precede (the lesson) will slip away (from him), and unless it follow it will fade away.

sanskrit: prākkūlān paryupāsīnaḥ pavitraiś caiva pāvitaḥ / prāṇāyāmais tribhiḥ pūtas tata oṃkāram arhati //
english: Seated on (blades of Kusa grass) with their points to the east, purified by Pavitras (blades of Kusa grass), and sanctified by three suppressions of the breath (Pranayama), he is worthy (to pronounce) the syllable Om.

sanskrit: akāraṃ cāpy ukāraṃ ca makāraṃ ca prajāpatiḥ / vedatrayān niraduhad bhūr bhuvaḥ svar itīti ca //
english: Pragapati (the lord of creatures) milked out (as it were) from the three Vedas the sounds A, U, and M, and (the Vyahritis) Bhuh, Bhuvah, Svah.

sanskrit: tribhya eva tu vedebhyaḥ pādaṃ pādam adūduhat / tad ity ṛco 'syāḥ sāvitryāḥ parameṣṭhī prajāpatiḥ //
english: Moreover from the three Vedas Pragapati, who dwells in the highest heaven (Parameshthin), milked out (as it were) that Rik-verse, sacred to Savitri (Savitri), which begins with the word tad, one foot from each.

sanskrit: etad akṣaram etāṃ ca japan vyāhṛtipūrvikām / saṃdhyayor vedavid vipro vedapuṇyena yujyate //
