english: A Brahmana, learned in the Veda, who recites during both twilights that syllable and that (verse), preceded by the Vyahritis, gains the (whole) merit which (the recitation of) the Vedas confers.

sanskrit: sahasrakṛtvas tv abhyasya bahir etat trikaṃ dvijaḥ / mahato 'py enaso māsāt tvacevāhir vimucyate //
english: A twice-born man who (daily) repeats those three one thousand times outside (the village), will be freed after a month even from great guilt, as a snake from its slough.

sanskrit: etayā rcā visaṃyuktaḥ kāle ca kriyayā svayā / brahmakṣatriyaviśyonir garhaṇāṃ yāti sādhuṣu //
english: The Brahmana, the Kshatriya, and the Vaisya who neglect (the recitation of) that Rik-verse and the timely (performance of the) rites (prescribed for) them, will be blamed among virtuous men.

sanskrit: oṃkārapūrvikās tisro mahāvyāhṛtayo 'vyayāḥ / tripadā caiva sāvitrī vijñeyaṃ brahmaṇo mukham //
english: Know that the three imperishable Mahavyahritis, preceded by the syllable Om, and (followed) by the three-footed Savitri are the portal of the Veda and the gate leading (to union with) Brahman.

sanskrit: yo 'dhīte 'hany ahany etāṃ trīṇi varṣāṇy atandritaḥ / sa brahma param abhyeti vāyubhūtaḥ khamūrtimān //
english: He who daily recites that (verse), untired, during three years, will enter (after death) the highest Brahman, move as free as air, and assume an ethereal form.

sanskrit: ekākṣaraṃ paraṃ brahma prāṇāyāmaḥ paraṃ tapaḥ / sāvitryās tu paraṃ nāsti maunāt satyaṃ viśiṣyate //
english: The monosyllable (Om) is the highest Brahman, (three) suppressions of the breath are the best (form of) austerity, but nothing surpasses the Savitri truthfulness is better than silence.

sanskrit: kṣaranti sarvā vaidikyo juhotiyajatikriyāḥ / akṣaraṃ duṣkaraṃ jñeyaṃ brahma caiva prajāpatiḥ //
english: All rites ordained in the Veda, burnt oblations and (other) sacrifices, pass away; but know that the syllable (Om) is imperishable, and (it is) Brahman, (and) the Lord of creatures (Pragapati).

sanskrit: vidhiyajñāj japayajño viśiṣṭo daśabhir guṇaiḥ / upāṃśuḥ syāc chataguṇaḥ sāhasro mānasaḥ smṛtaḥ //
english: An offering, consisting of muttered prayers, is ten times more efficacious than a sacrifice performed according to the rules (of the Veda); a (prayer) which is inaudible (to others) surpasses it a hundred times, and the mental (recitation of sacred texts) a thousand times.

sanskrit: ye pākayajñās catvāro vidhiyajñasamanvitāḥ / sarve te japayajñasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm //
english: The four Pakayagnas and those sacrifices which are enjoined by the rules (of the Veda) are all together not equal in value to a sixteenth part of the sacrifice consisting of muttered prayers.

sanskrit: japyenaiva tu saṃsidhyed brāhmaṇo nātra saṃśayaḥ / kuryād anyan na vā kuryān maitro brāhmaṇa ucyate //
english: But, undoubtedly, a Brahmana reaches the highest goal by muttering prayers only; (whether) he perform other (rites) or neglect them, he who befriends (all creatures) is declared (to be) a (true) Brahmana.

sanskrit: indriyāṇāṃ vicaratāṃ viṣayeṣv apahāriṣu / saṃyame yatnam ātiṣṭhed vidvān yanteva vājinām //
english: A wise man should strive to restrain his organs which run wild among alluring sensual objects, like a charioteer his horses.

sanskrit: ekādaśendriyāṇy āhur yāni pūrve manīṣiṇaḥ / tāni samyak pravakṣyāmi yathāvad anupūrvaśaḥ //
english: Those eleven organs which former sages have named, I will properly (and) precisely enumerate in due order,

sanskrit: śrotraṃ tvak cakṣuṣī jihvā nāsikā caiva pañcamī / pāyūpasthaṃ hastapādaṃ vāk caiva daśamī smṛtā //
english: (Viz.) the ear, the skin, the eyes, the tongue, and the nose as the fifth, the anus, the organ of generation, hands and feet, and the (organ of) speech, named as the tenth.

sanskrit: buddhīndriyāṇi pañcaiṣāṃ śrotrādīny anupūrvaśaḥ / karmendriyāṇi pañcaiṣāṃ pāyvādīni pracakṣate //
english: Five of them, the ear and the rest according to their order, they call organs of sense, and five of them, the anus and the rest, organs of action.

sanskrit: ekādaśaṃ mano jñeyaṃ svaguṇenobhayātmakam / yasmin jite jitāv etau bhavataḥ pañcakau gaṇau //
english: Know that the internal organ (manas) is the eleventh, which by its quality belongs to both (sets); when that has been subdued, both those sets of five have been conquered.

sanskrit: indriyāṇāṃ prasaṅgena doṣam ṛcchaty asaṃśayam / saṃniyamya tu tāny eva tataḥ siddhiṃ nigacchati //
english: Through the attachment of his organs (to sensual pleasure) a man doubtlessly will incur guilt; but if he keep them under complete control, he will obtain success (in gaining all his aims).

sanskrit: na jātu kāmaḥ kāmānām upabhogena śāmyati / haviṣā kṛṣṇavartmeva bhūya evābhivardhate //
english: Desire is never extinguished by the enjoyment of desired objects; it only grows stronger like a fire (fed) with clarified butter.

sanskrit: yaś caitān prāpnuyāt sarvān yaś caitān kevalāṃs tyajet / prāpaṇāt sarvakāmānāṃ parityāgo viśiṣyate //
english: If one man should obtain all those (sensual enjoyments) and another should renounce them all, the renunciation of all pleasure is far better than the attainment of them.

sanskrit: na tathaitāni śakyante saṃniyantum asevayā / viṣayeṣu prajuṣṭāni yathā jñānena nityaśaḥ //
english: Those (organs) which are strongly attached to sensual pleasures, cannot so effectually be restrained by abstinence (from enjoyments) as by a constant (pursuit of true) knowledge.

sanskrit: vedās tyāgaś ca yajñāś ca niyamāś ca tapāṃsi ca / na vipraduṣṭabhāvasya siddhiṃ gacchati karhi cit //
english: Neither (the study of) the Vedas, nor liberality, nor sacrifices, nor any (self-imposed) restraint, nor austerities, ever procure the attainment (of rewards) to a man whose heart is contaminated (by sensuality).

sanskrit: śrutvā spṛṣṭvā ca dṛṣṭvā ca bhuktvā ghrātvā ca yo naraḥ / na hṛṣyati glāyati vā sa vijñeyo jitendriyaḥ //
english: That man may be considered to have (really) subdued his organs, who on hearing and touching and seeing, on tasting and smelling (anything) neither rejoices nor repines.

sanskrit: indriyāṇāṃ tu sarveṣāṃ yady ekaṃ kṣaratīndriyam / tenāsya kṣarati prajñā dṛteḥ pādād ivodakam //
english: But when one among all the organs slips away (from control), thereby (man's) wisdom slips away from him, even as the water (flows) through the one (open) foot of a (water-carrier's) skin.

sanskrit: vaśe kṛtvendriyagrāmaṃ saṃyamya ca manas tathā / sarvān saṃsādhayed arthān akṣiṇvan yogatas tanum //
english: If he keeps all the (ten) organs as well as the mind in subjection, he may gain all his aims, without reducing his body by (the practice) of Yoga.

sanskrit: pūrvāṃ saṃdhyāṃ japāṃs tiṣṭhet sāvitrīm ārkadarśanāt / paścimāṃ tu samāsīnaḥ samyag ṛkṣavibhāvanāt //
english: Let him stand during the morning twilight, muttering the Savitri until the sun appears, but (let him recite it), seated, in the evening until the constellations can be seen distinctly.

sanskrit: pūrvāṃ saṃdhyāṃ japaṃs tiṣṭhan naiśam eno vyapohati / paścimāṃ tu samāsīno malaṃ hanti divākṛtam //
english: He who stands during the morning twilight muttering (the Savitri), removes the guilt contracted during the (previous) night; but he who (recites it), seated, in the evening, destroys the sin he committed during the day.

sanskrit: na tiṣṭhati tu yaḥ pūrvāṃ nopāste yaś ca paścimām / sa śūdravad bahiṣkāryaḥ sarvasmād dvijakarmaṇaḥ //
english: But he who does not (worship) standing in the morning, nor sitting in the evening, shall be excluded, just like a Sudra, from all the duties and rights of an Aryan.

sanskrit: apāṃ samīpe niyato naityakaṃ vidhim āsthitaḥ / sāvitrīm apy adhīyīta gatvāraṇyaṃ samāhitaḥ //
english: He who (desires to) perform the ceremony (of the) daily (recitation), may even recite the Savitri near water, retiring into the forest, controlling his organs and concentrating his mind.

sanskrit: vedopakaraṇe caiva svādhyāye caiva naityake / nānurodho 'sty anadhyāye homamantreṣu caiva hi //
english: Both when (one studies) the supplementary treatises of the Veda, and when (one recites) the daily portion of the Veda, no regard need be paid to forbidden days, likewise when (one repeats) the sacred texts required for a burnt oblation.

sanskrit: naityake nāsty anadhyāyo brahmasattraṃ hi tat smṛtam / brahmāhutihutaṃ puṇyam anadhyāyavaṣaṭkṛtam //
english: There are no forbidden days for the daily recitation, since that is declared to be a Brahmasattra (an everlasting sacrifice offered to Brahman); at that the Veda takes the place of the burnt oblations, and it is meritorious (even), when (natural phenomena, requiring) a cessation of the Veda-study, take the place of the exclamation Vashat.

sanskrit: yaḥ svādhyāyam adhīte 'bdaṃ vidhinā niyataḥ śuciḥ / tasya nityaṃ kṣaraty eṣa payo dadhi ghṛtaṃ madhu //
english: For him who, being pure and controlling his organs, during a year daily recites the Veda according to the rule, that (daily recitation) will ever cause sweet and sour milk, clarified butter and honey to flow.

sanskrit: agnīndhanaṃ bhaikṣacaryām adhaḥśayyāṃ guror hitam / ā samāvartanāt kuryāt kṛtopanayano dvijaḥ //
english: Let an Aryan who has been initiated, (daily) offer fuel in the sacred fire, beg food, sleep on the ground and do what is beneficial to this teacher, until (he performs the ceremony of) Samavartana (on returning home).

sanskrit: ācāryaputraḥ śuśrūṣur jñānado dhārmikaḥ śuciḥ / āptaḥ śakto 'rthadaḥ sādhuḥ svo 'dhyāpyā daśa dharmataḥ //
english: According to the sacred law the (following) ten (persons, viz.) the teacher's son, one who desires to do service, one who imparts knowledge, one who is intent on fulfilling the law, one who is pure, a person connected by marriage or friendship, one who possesses (mental) ability, one who makes presents of money, one who is honest, and a relative, may be instructed (in the Veda).

sanskrit: nāpṛṣṭaḥ kasya cid brūyān na cānyāyena pṛcchataḥ / jānann api hi medhāvī jaḍaval loka ācaret //
english: Unless one be asked, one must not explain (anything) to anybody, nor (must one answer) a person who asks improperly; let a wise man, though he knows (the answer), behave among men as (if he were) an idiot.

sanskrit: adharmeṇa ca yaḥ prāha yaś cādharmeṇa pṛcchati / tayor anyataraḥ praiti vidveṣaṃ vādhigacchati //
english: Of the two persons, him who illegally explains (anything), and him who illegally asks (a question), one (or both) will die or incur (the other's) enmity.

sanskrit: dharmārthau yatra na syātāṃ śuśrūṣā vāpi tadvidhā / tatra vidyā na vaptavyā śubhaṃ bījam ivoṣare //
english: Where merit and wealth are not (obtained by teaching) nor (at least) due obedience, in such (soil) sacred knowledge must not be sown, just as good seed (must) not (be thrown) on barren land.

sanskrit: vidyayaiva samaṃ kāmaṃ martavyaṃ brahmavādinā / āpady api hi ghorāyāṃ na tv enām iriṇe vapet // vidyā brāhmaṇam etyāha śevadhis te 'smi rakṣa mām / asūyakāya māṃ mādās tathā syāṃ vīryavattamā // yam eva tu śuciṃ vidyān niyatabrahmacāriṇam / tasmai māṃ brūhi viprāya nidhipāyāpramādine //
english: Even in times of dire distress a teacher of the Veda should rather die with his knowledge than sow it in barren soil. Sacred Learning approached a Brahmana and said to him: 'I am thy treasure, preserve me, deliver me not to a scorner; so (preserved) I shall become supremely strong.' 'But deliver me, as to the keeper of thy treasure, to a Brahmana whom thou shalt know to be pure, of subdued senses, chaste and attentive.'

sanskrit: brahma yas tv ananujñātam adhīyānād avāpnuyāt / sa brahmasteyasaṃyukto narakaṃ pratipadyate //
english: But he who acquires without permission the Veda from one who recites it, incurs the guilt of stealing the Veda, and shall sink into hell.

sanskrit: laukikaṃ vaidikaṃ vāpi tathādhyātmikam eva vā / ādadīta yato jñānaṃ taṃ pūrvam abhivādayet //
english: (A student) shall first reverentially salute that (teacher) from whom he receives (knowledge), referring to worldly affairs, to the Veda, or to the Brahman.

sanskrit: sāvitrīmātrasāro 'pi varaṃ vipraḥ suyantritaḥ / nāyantritas trivedo 'pi sarvāśī sarvavikrayī //
english: A Brahmana who completely governs himself, though he know the Savitri only, is better than he who knows the three Vedas, (but) does not control himself, eats all (sorts of) food, and sells all (sorts of goods).

sanskrit: śayyāsane 'dhyācarite śreyasā na samāviśet / śayyāsanasthaś caivainaṃ pratyutthāyābhivādayet //
english: One must not sit down on a couch or seat which a superior occupies; and he who occupies a couch or seat shall rise to meet a (superior), and (afterwards) salute him.

sanskrit: ūrdhvaṃ prāṇā hy utkrāmanti yūnaḥ sthavira āyati / pratyutthānābhivādābhyāṃ punas tān pratipadyate //
english: For the vital airs of a young man mount upwards to leave his body when an elder approaches; but by rising to meet him and saluting he recovers them.

sanskrit: abhivādanaśīlasya nityaṃ vṛddhopasevinaḥ / catvāri tasya vardhante āyur dharmo yaśo balam //
english: He who habitually salutes and constantly pays reverence to the aged obtains an increase of four (things), (viz.) length of life, knowledge, fame, (and) strength.

sanskrit: abhivādāt paraṃ vipro jyāyāṃsam abhivādayan / asau nāmāham asmīti svaṃ nāma parikīrtayet //
english: After the (word of) salutation, a Brahmana who greets an elder must pronounce his name, saying, 'I am N. N.'

sanskrit: nāmadheyasya ye ke cid abhivādaṃ na jānate / tān prājño 'ham iti brūyāt striyaḥ sarvās tathaiva ca //
english: To those (persons) who, when a name is pronounced, do not understand (the meaning of) the salutation, a wise man should say, 'It is I;' and (he should address) in the same manner all women.

sanskrit: bhoḥśabdaṃ kīrtayed ante svasya nāmno 'bhivādane / nāmnāṃ svarūpabhāvo hi bhobhāva ṛṣibhiḥ smṛtaḥ //
english: In saluting he should pronounce after his name the word bhoh; for the sages have declared that the nature of bhoh is the same as that of (all proper) names.

sanskrit: āyuṣmān bhava saumyeti vācyo vipro 'bhivādane / akāraś cāsya nāmno 'nte vācyaḥ pūrvākṣaraḥ plutaḥ //
english: A Brahmana should thus be saluted in return, 'May'st thou be long-lived, O gentle one!' and the vowel 'a' must be added at the end of the name (of the person addressed), the syllable preceding it being drawn out to the length of three moras.

sanskrit: yo na vetty abhivādasya vipraḥ pratyabhivādanam / nābhivādyaḥ sa viduṣā yathā śūdras tathaiva saḥ //
english: A Brahmana who does not know the form of returning a salutation, must not be saluted by a learned man; as a Sudra, even so is he.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaṃ kuśalaṃ pṛcchet kṣatrabandhum anāmayam / vaiśyaṃ kṣemaṃ samāgamya śūdram ārogyam eva ca //
english: Let him ask a Brahmana, on meeting him, after (his health, with the word) kusala, a Kshatriya (with the word) anamaya, a Vaisya (with the word) kshema, and a Sudra (with the word) anarogya.

sanskrit: avācyo dīkṣito nāmnā yavīyān api yo bhavet / bhobhavatpūrvakaṃ tv enam abhibhāṣeta dharmavit //
english: He who has been initiated (to perform a Srauta sacrifice) must not be addressed by his name, even though he be a younger man; he who knows the sacred law must use in speaking to such (a man the particle) bhoh and (the pronoun) bhavat (your worship).

sanskrit: parapatnī tu yā strī syād asaṃbandhā ca yonitaḥ / tāṃ brūyād bhavatīty evaṃ subhage bhaginīti ca //
english: But to a female who is the wife of another man, and not a blood-relation, he must say, 'Lady' (bhavati) or 'Beloved sister!'

sanskrit: mātulāṃś ca pitṛvyāṃś ca śvaśurān ṛtvijo gurūn / asāv aham iti brūyāt pratyutthāya yavīyasaḥ //
english: To his maternal and paternal uncles, fathers-in-law, officiating priests, (and other) venerable persons, he must say, 'I am N. N.,' and rise (to meet them), even though they be younger (than himself).

sanskrit: mātṛśvasā mātulānī śvaśrūr atha pitṛśvasā / saṃpūjyā gurupatnīvat samās tā gurubhāryayā //
english: A maternal aunt, the wife of a maternal uncle, a mother-in-law, and a paternal aunt must be honoured like the wife of one's teacher; they are equal to the wife of one's teacher.

sanskrit: pitur bhaginyāṃ mātuś ca jyāyasyāṃ ca svasary api / mātṛvad vṛttim ātiṣṭhen mātā tābhyo garīyasī //
english: Towards a sister of one's father and of one's mother, and towards one's own elder sister, one must behave as towards one's mother; (but) the mother is more venerable than they.

sanskrit: daśābdākhyaṃ paurasakhyaṃ pañcābdākhyaṃ kalābhṛtām / tryabdapūrvaṃ śrotriyāṇāṃ svalpenāpi svayoniṣu //
english: Fellow-citizens are called friends (and equals though one be) ten years (older than the other), men practising (the same) fine art (though one be) five years (older than the other), Srotriyas (though) three years (intervene between their ages), but blood-relations only (if the) difference of age be very small.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaṃ daśavarṣaṃ tu śatavarṣaṃ tu bhūmipam / pitāputrau vijānīyād brāhmaṇas tu tayoḥ pitā //
english: Know that a Brahmana of ten years and Kshatriya of a hundred years stand to each other in the relation of father and son; but between those two the Brahmana is the father.

sanskrit: vittaṃ bandhur vayaḥ karma vidyā bhavati pañcamī / etāni mānyasthānāni garīyo yad yad uttaram //
english: Wealth, kindred, age, (the due performance of) rites, and, fifthly, sacred learning are titles to respect; but each later-named (cause) is more weighty (than the preceding ones).

sanskrit: pañcānāṃ triṣu varṇeṣu bhūyāṃsi guṇavanti ca / yatra syuḥ so 'tra mānārhaḥ śūdro 'pi daśamīṃ gataḥ //
english: Whatever man of the three (highest) castes possesses most of those five, both in number and degree, that man is worthy of honour among them; and (so is) also a Sudra who has entered the tenth (decade of his life).

sanskrit: cakriṇo daśamīsthasya rogiṇo bhāriṇaḥ striyāḥ / snātakasya ca rājñaś ca panthā deyo varasya ca //
english: Way must be made for a man in a carriage, for one who is above ninety years old, for one diseased, for the carrier of a burden, for a woman, for a Snataka, for the king, and for a bridegroom.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu samāvetānāṃ mānyau snātakapārthivau / rājasnātakayoś caiva snātako nṛpamānabhāk //
english: Among all those, if they meet (at one time), a Snataka and the king must be (most) honoured; and if the king and a Snataka (meet), the latter receives respect from the king.

sanskrit: upanīya tu yaḥ śiṣyaṃ vedam adhyāpayed dvijaḥ / sakalpaṃ sarahasyaṃ ca tam ācāryaṃ pracakṣate //
english: They call that Brahmana who initiates a pupil and teaches him the Veda together with the Kalpa and the Rahasyas, the teacher (akarya, of the latter).

sanskrit: ekadeśaṃ tu vedasya vedāṅgāny api vā punaḥ / yo 'dhyāpayati vṛttyartham upādhyāyaḥ sa ucyate //
english: But he who for his livelihood teaches a portion only of the Veda, or also the Angas of the Veda, is called the sub-teacher (upadhyaya).

sanskrit: niṣekādīni karmāṇi yaḥ karoti yathāvidhi / saṃbhāvayati cānnena sa vipro gurur ucyate //
english: That Brahmana, who performs in accordance with the rules (of the Veda) the rites, the Garbhadhana (conception-rite), and so forth, and gives food (to the child), is called the Guru (the venerable one).

sanskrit: agnyādheyaṃ pākayajñān agniṣṭomādikān makhān / yaḥ karoti vṛto yasya sa tasya rtvig ihocyate //
english: He who, being (duly) chosen (for the purpose), performs the Agnyadheya, the Pakayagnas, (and) the (Srauta) sacrifices, such as the Agnishtoma (for another man), is called (his) officiating priest.

sanskrit: ya āvṛṇoty avitathaṃ brahmaṇā śravaṇāv ubhau / sa mātā sa pitā jñeyas taṃ na druhyet kadā cana //
english: That (man) who truthfully fills both his ears with the Veda, (the pupil) shall consider as his father and mother; he must never offend him.

sanskrit: upādhyāyān daśācārya ācāryāṇāṃ śataṃ pitā / sahasraṃ tu pitṝn mātā gauraveṇātiricyate //
english: The teacher (akarya) is ten times more venerable than a sub-teacher (upadhyaya), the father a hundred times more than the teacher, but the mother a thousand times more than the father.

sanskrit: utpādakabrahmadātror garīyān brahmadaḥ pitā / brahmajanma hi viprasya pretya ceha ca śāśvatam //
english: Of him who gives natural birth and him who gives (the knowledge of) the Veda, the giver of the Veda is the more venerable father; for the birth for the sake of the Veda (ensures) eternal (rewards) both in this (life) and after death.

sanskrit: kāmān mātā pitā cainaṃ yad utpādayato mithaḥ / saṃbhūtiṃ tasya tāṃ vidyād yad yonāv abhijāyate //
english: Let him consider that (he received) a (mere animal) existence, when his parents begat him through mutual affection, and when he was born from the womb (of his mother).

sanskrit: ācāryas tv asya yāṃ jātiṃ vidhivad vedapāragaḥ / utpādayati sāvitryā sā satyā sājarāmarā //
english: But that birth which a teacher acquainted with the whole Veda, in accordance with the law, procures for him through the Savitri, is real, exempt from age and death.

sanskrit: alpaṃ vā bahu vā yasya śrutasyopakaroti yaḥ / tam apīha guruṃ vidyāc chrutopakriyayā tayā //
english: (The pupil) must know that that man also who benefits him by (instruction in) the Veda, be it little or much, is called in these (Institutes) his Guru, in consequence of that benefit (conferred by instruction in) the Veda.

sanskrit: brāhmasya janmanaḥ kartā svadharmasya ca śāsitā / bālo 'pi vipro vṛddhasya pitā bhavati dharmataḥ //
english: That Brahmana who is the giver of the birth for the sake of the Veda and the teacher of the prescribed duties becomes by law the father of an aged man, even though he himself be a child.

sanskrit: adhyāpayām āsa pitṝn śiśur āṅgirasaḥ kaviḥ / putrakā iti hovāca jñānena parigṛhya tān //
english: Young Kavi, the son of Angiras, taught his (relatives who were old enough to be) fathers, and, as he excelled them in (sacred) knowledge, he called them 'Little sons.'

sanskrit: te tam artham apṛcchanta devān āgatamanyavaḥ / devāś caitān sametyocur nyāyyaṃ vaḥ śiśur uktavān //
english: They, moved with resentment, asked the gods concerning that matter, and the gods, having assembled, answered, 'The child has addressed you properly.'

sanskrit: ajño bhavati vai bālaḥ pitā bhavati mantradaḥ / ajñaṃ hi bālam ity āhuḥ pitety eva tu mantradam //
english: "'For (a man) destitute of (sacred) knowledge is indeed a child, and he who teaches him the Veda is his father; for (the sages) have always said ""child"" to an ignorant man, and ""father"" to a teacher of the Veda.'"

sanskrit: na hāyanair na palitair na vittena na bandhubhiḥ / ṛṣayaś cakrire dharmaṃ yo 'nūcānaḥ sa no mahān //
english: Neither through years, nor through white (hairs), nor through wealth, nor through (powerful) kinsmen (comes greatness). The sages have made this law, 'He who has learnt the Veda together with the Angas (Anukana) is (considered) great by us.'

sanskrit: viprāṇāṃ jñānato jyaiṣṭhyaṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ tu vīryataḥ / vaiśyānāṃ dhānyadhanataḥ śūdrāṇām eva janmataḥ //
english: The seniority of Brahmanas is from (sacred) knowledge, that of Kshatriyas from valour, that of Vaisyas from wealth in grain (and other goods), but that of Sudras alone from age.

sanskrit: na tena vṛddho bhavati yenāsya palitaṃ śiraḥ / yo vai yuvāpy adhīyānas taṃ devāḥ sthaviraṃ viduḥ //
english: A man is not therefore (considered) venerable because his head is gray; him who, though young, has learned the Veda, the gods consider to be venerable.

sanskrit: yathā kāṣṭhamayo hastī yathā carmamayo mṛgaḥ / yaś ca vipro 'nadhīyānas trayas te nāma bibhrati //
english: As an elephant made of wood, as an antelope made of leather, such is an unlearned Brahmana; those three have nothing but the names (of their kind).

sanskrit: yathā ṣaṇḍho 'phalaḥ strīṣu yathā gaur gavi cāphalā / yathā cājñe 'phalaṃ dānaṃ tathā vipro 'nṛco 'phalaḥ //
english: As a eunuch is unproductive with women, as a cow with a cow is unprolific, and as a gift made to an ignorant man yields no reward, even so is a Brahmana useless, who (does) not (know) the Rikas.

sanskrit: ahiṃsayaiva bhūtānāṃ kāryaṃ śreyo 'nuśāsanam / vāk caiva madhurā ślakṣṇā prayojyā dharmam icchatā //
english: Created beings must be instructed in (what concerns) their welfare without giving them pain, and sweet and gentle speech must be used by (a teacher) who desires (to abide by) the sacred law.

sanskrit: yasya vāṅganasī śuddhe samyaggupte ca sarvadā / sa vai sarvam avāpnoti vedāntopagataṃ phalam //
english: He, forsooth, whose speech and thoughts are pure and ever perfectly guarded, gains the whole reward which is conferred by the Vedanta.

sanskrit: nāruṃtudaḥ syād ārto 'pi na paradrohakarmadhīḥ / yayāsyodvijate vācā nālokyāṃ tām udīrayet //
english: Let him not, even though in pain, (speak words) cutting (others) to the quick; let him not injure others in thought or deed; let him not utter speeches which make (others) afraid of him, since that will prevent him from gaining heaven.

sanskrit: sammānād brāhmaṇo nityam udvijeta viṣād iva / amṛtasyeva cākāṅkṣed avamānasya sarvadā //
english: A Brahmana should always fear homage as if it were poison; and constantly desire (to suffer) scorn as (he would long for) nectar.

sanskrit: sukhaṃ hy avamataḥ śete sukhaṃ ca pratibudhyate / sukhaṃ carati loke 'sminn avamantā vinaśyati //
english: For he who is scorned (nevertheless may) sleep with an easy mind, awake with an easy mind, and with an easy mind walk here among men; but the scorner utterly perishes.

sanskrit: anena kramayogena saṃskṛtātmā dvijaḥ śanaiḥ / gurau vasan sañcinuyād brahmādhigamikaṃ tapaḥ // tapoviśeṣair vividhair vrataiś ca vidhicoditaiḥ / vedaḥ kṛtsno 'dhigantavyaḥ sarahasyo dvijanmanā //
english: A twice-born man who has been sanctified by the (employment of) the means, (described above) in due order, shall gradually and cumulatively perform the various austerities prescribed for (those who) study the Veda. An Aryan must study the whole Veda together with the Rahasyas, performing at the same time various kinds of austerities and the vows prescribed by the rules (of the Veda).

sanskrit: vedam eva sadābhyasyet tapas tapsyan dvijottamaḥ / vedābhyāso hi viprasya tapaḥ param ihocyate //
english: Let a Brahmana who desires to perform austerities, constantly repeat the Veda; for the study of the Veda is declared (to be) in this world the highest austerity for a Brahmana.

sanskrit: ā haiva sa nakhāgrebhyaḥ paramaṃ tapyate tapaḥ / yaḥ sragvy api dvijo 'dhīte svādhyāyaṃ śaktito 'nvaham //
english: Verily, that twice-born man performs the highest austerity up to the extremities of his nails, who, though wearing a garland, daily recites the Veda in private to the utmost of his ability.

sanskrit: yo 'nadhītya dvijo vedam anyatra kurute śramam / sa jīvann eva śūdratvam āśu gacchati sānvayaḥ //
english: A twice-born man who, not having studied the Veda, applies himself to other (and worldly study), soon falls, even while living, to the condition of a Sudra and his descendants (after him).

sanskrit: mātur agre 'dhijananaṃ dvitīyaṃ mauñjibandhane / tṛtīyaṃ yajñadīkṣāyāṃ dvijasya śruticodanāt //
english: According to the injunction of the revealed texts the first birth of an Aryan is from (his natural) mother, the second (happens) on the tying of the girdle of Munga grass, and the third on the initiation to (the performance of) a (Srauta) sacrifice.

sanskrit: tatra yad brahmajanmāsya mauñjībandhanacihnitam / tatrāsya mātā sāvitrī pitā tv ācārya ucyate //
english: Among those (three) the birth which is symbolised by the investiture with the girdle of Munga grass, is his birth for the sake of the Veda; they declare that in that (birth) the Sivitri (verse) is his mother and the teacher his father.

sanskrit: vedapradānād ācāryaṃ pitaraṃ paricakṣate / na hy asmin yujyate karma kiñ cid ā mauñjibandhanāt //
english: They call the teacher (the pupil's) father because he gives the Veda; for nobody can perform a (sacred) rite before the investiture with the girdle of Munga grass.

sanskrit: nābhivyāhārayed brahma svadhāninayanād ṛte / śūdreṇa hi samas tāvad yāvad vede na jāyate // kṛtopanayanasyāsya vratādeśanam iṣyate / brahmaṇo grahaṇaṃ caiva krameṇa vidhipūrvakam //
english: (He who has not been initiated) should not pronounce (any) Vedic text excepting (those required for) the performance of funeral rites, since he is on a level with a Sudra before his birth from the Veda. The (student) who has been initiated must be instructed in the performance of the vows, and gradually learn the Veda, observing the prescribed rules.

sanskrit: yady asya vihitaṃ carma yat sūtraṃ yā ca mekhalā / yo daṇḍo yac ca vasanaṃ tat tad asya vrateṣv api //
english: Whatever dress of skin, sacred thread, girdle, staff, and lower garment are prescribed for a (student at the initiation), the like (must again be used) at the (performance of the) vows.

sanskrit: sevetemāṃs tu niyamān brahmacārī gurau vasan / sanniyamyendriyagrāmaṃ tapovṛddhyartham ātmanaḥ //
english: But a student who resides with his teacher must observe the following restrictive rules, duly controlling all his organs, in order to increase his spiritual merit.

sanskrit: nityaṃ snātvā śuciḥ kuryād devarṣipitṛtarpaṇam / devatābhyarcanaṃ caiva samidādhānam eva ca //
english: Every day, having bathed, and being purified, he must offer libations of water to the gods, sages and manes, worship (the images of) the gods, and place fuel on (the sacred fire).

sanskrit: varjayen madhu māṃsaṃ ca gandhaṃ mālyaṃ rasān striyaḥ / śuktāni yāni sarvāṇi prāṇināṃ caiva hiṃsanam //
english: Let him abstain from honey, meat, perfumes, garlands, substances (used for) flavouring (food), women, all substances turned acid, and from doing injury to living creatures.

sanskrit: abhyaṅgam añjanaṃ cākṣṇor upānacchatradhāraṇam / kāmaṃ krodhaṃ ca lobhaṃ ca nartanaṃ gītavādanam // dyūtaṃ ca janavādaṃ ca parivādaṃ tathānṛtam / strīṇāṃ ca prekṣaṇālambham upaghātaṃ parasya ca //
english: From anointing (his body), applying collyrium to his eyes, from the use of shoes and of an umbrella (or parasol), from (sensual) desire, anger, covetousness, dancing, singing, and playing (musical instruments), From gambling, idle disputes, backbiting, and lying, from looking at and touching women, and from hurting others.

sanskrit: ekaḥ śayīta sarvatra na retaḥ skandayet kva cit / kāmād dhi skandayan reto hinasti vratam ātmanaḥ //
english: Let him always sleep alone, let him never waste his manhood; for he who voluntarily wastes his manhood, breaks his vow.

sanskrit: svapne siktvā brahmacārī dvijaḥ śukram akāmataḥ / snātvārkam arcayitvā triḥ punar mām ity ṛcaṃ japet //
english: A twice-born student, who has involuntarily wasted his manly strength during sleep, must bathe, worship the sun, and afterwards thrice mutter the Rik-verse (which begins), 'Again let my strength return to me.'

sanskrit: udakumbhaṃ sumanaso gośakṛnmṛttikākuśān / āhared yāvad arthāni bhaikṣaṃ cāharahaś caret //
english: Let him fetch a pot full of water, flowers, cowdung, earth, and Kusa grass, as much as may be required (by his teacher), and daily go to beg food.

sanskrit: vedayajñair ahīnānāṃ praśastānāṃ svakarmasu / brahmacāry āhared bhaikṣaṃ gṛhebhyaḥ prayato 'nvaham // guroḥ kule na bhikṣeta na jñātikulabandhuṣu / alābhe tv anyagehānāṃ pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ vivarjayet //
english: A student, being pure, shall daily bring food from the houses of men who are not deficient in (the knowledge of) the Veda and in (performing) sacrifices, and who are famous for (following their lawful) occupations. Let him not beg from the relatives of his teacher, nor from his own or his mother's blood-relations; but if there are no houses belonging to strangers, let him go to one of those named above, taking the last-named first;

sanskrit: sarvaṃ vāpi cared grāmaṃ pūrvoktānām asaṃbhave / niyamya prayato vācam abhiśastāṃs tu varjayet //
english: Or, if there are no (virtuous men of the kind) mentioned above, he may go to each (house in the) village, being pure and remaining silent; but let him avoid Abhisastas (those accused of mortal sin).

sanskrit: dūrād āhṛtya samidhaḥ sannidadhyād vihāyasi / sāyaM: prātaś ca juhuyāt tābhir agnim atandritaḥ //
english: Having brought sacred fuel from a distance, let him place it anywhere but on the ground, and let him, unwearied, make with it burnt oblations to the sacred fire, both evening and morning.

sanskrit: akṛtvā bhaikṣacaraṇam asamidhya ca pāvakaṃ / anāturaḥ saptarātram avakīrṇivrataṃ caret //
english: He who, without being sick, neglects during seven (successive) days to go out begging, and to offer fuel in the sacred fire, shall perform the penance of an Avakirnin (one who has broken his vow).

sanskrit: bhaikṣeṇa vartayen nityaṃ naikānnādī bhaved vratī / bhaikṣeṇa vratino vṛttir upavāsasamā smṛtā //
english: He who performs the vow (of studentship) shall constantly subsist on alms, (but) not eat the food of one (person only); the subsistence of a student on begged food is declared to be equal (in merit) to fasting.

sanskrit: vratavad devadaivatye pitrye karmaṇy atha rṣivat / kāmam abhyarthito 'śnīyād vratam asya na lupyate //
english: At his pleasure he may eat, when invited, the food of one man at (a rite) in honour of the gods, observing (however the conditions on his vow, or at a (funeral meal) in honor of the manes, behaving (however) like a hermit.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇasyaiva karmaitad upadiṣṭaṃ manīṣibhiḥ / rājanyavaiśyayos tv evaṃ naitat karma vidhīyate //
english: This duty is prescribed by the wise for a Brahmana only; but no such duty is ordained for a Kshatriya and a Vaisya.

sanskrit: codito guruṇā nityam apracodita eva vā / kuryād adhyayane yatnam ācāryasya hiteṣu ca //
english: Both when ordered by his teacher, and without a (special) command, (a student) shall always exert himself in studying (the Veda), and in doing what is serviceable to his teacher.

sanskrit: śarīraṃ caiva vācaṃ ca buddhīndriyamanāṃsi ca / niyamya prāñjalis tiṣṭhed vīkṣamāṇo guror mukham //
english: Controlling his body, his speech, his organs (of sense), and his mind, let him stand with joined hands, looking at the face of his teacher.

sanskrit: nityam uddhṛtapāṇiḥ syāt sādhvācāraḥ susaṃvṛtaḥ / āsyatām iti coktaḥ sann āsītābhimukhaṃ guroḥ // hīnānnavastraveṣaḥ syāt sarvadā gurusannidhau / uttiṣṭhet prathamaṃ cāsya caramaṃ caiva saṃviśet //
english: Let him always keep his right arm uncovered, behave decently and keep his body well covered, and when he is addressed (with the words), 'Be seated,' he shall sit down, facing his teacher. In the presence of his teacher let him always eat less, wear a less valuable dress and ornaments (than the former), and let him rise earlier (from his bed), and go to rest later.

sanskrit: pratiśrāvaṇasaṃbhāṣe śayāno na samācaret / nāsīno na ca bhuñjāno na tiṣṭhan na parāṅmukhaḥ //
english: Let him not answer or converse with (his teacher), reclining on a bed, nor sitting, nor eating, nor standing, nor with an averted face.

sanskrit: āsīnasya sthitaḥ kuryād abhigacchaṃs tu tiṣṭhataḥ / pratyudgamya tv āvrajataḥ paścād dhāvaṃs tu dhāvataḥ // parāṅmukhasyābhimukho dūrasthasyaitya cāntikam / praṇamya tu śayānasya nideśe caiva tiṣṭhataḥ //
english: Let him do (that), standing up, if (his teacher) is seated, advancing towards him when he stands, going to meet him if he advances, and running after him when he runs; Going (round) to face (the teacher), if his face is averted, approaching him if he stands at a distance, but bending towards him if he lies on a bed, and if he stands in a lower place.

sanskrit: nīcaṃ śayyāsanaṃ cāsya nityaṃ syād gurusannidhau / guros tu cakṣurviṣaye na yatheṣṭāsano bhavet //
english: When his teacher is nigh, let his bed or seat be low; but within sight of his teacher he shall not sit carelessly at ease.

sanskrit: nodāhared asya nāma parokṣam api kevalam / na caivāsyānukurvīta gatibhāṣitaceṣṭitam //
english: Let him not pronounce the mere name of his teacher (without adding an honorific title) behind his back even, and let him not mimic his gait, speech, and deportment.

sanskrit: guror yatra parivādo nindā vāpi pravartate / karṇau tatra pidhātavyau gantavyaṃ vā tato 'nyataḥ //
english: Wherever (people) justly censure or falsely defame his teacher, there he must cover his ears or depart thence to another place.

sanskrit: parīvādāt kharo bhavati śvā vai bhavati nindakaḥ / paribhoktā kṛmir bhavati kīṭo bhavati matsarī //
english: By censuring (his teacher), though justly, he will become (in his next birth) an ass, by falsely defaming him, a dog; he who lives on his teacher's substance, will become a worm, and he who is envious (of his merit), a (larger) insect.

sanskrit: dūrastho nārcayed enaṃ na kruddho nāntike striyāḥ / yānāsanasthaś caivainam avaruhyābhivādayet //
english: He must not serve the (teacher by the intervention of another) while he himself stands aloof, nor when he (himself) is angry, nor when a woman is near; if he is seated in a carriage or on a (raised) seat, he must descend and afterwards salute his (teacher).

sanskrit: prativāte 'nuvāte ca nāsīta guruṇā saha / asaṃśrave caiva guror na kiṃ cid api kīrtayet //
english: Let him not sit with his teacher, to the leeward or to the windward (of him); nor let him say anything which his teacher cannot hear.

sanskrit: go'śvoṣṭrayānaprāsāda- prastareṣu kaṭeṣu ca / āsīta guruṇā sārdhaṃ śilāphalakanauṣu ca //
english: He may sit with his teacher in a carriage drawn by oxen, horses, or camels, on a terrace, on a bed of grass or leaves, on a mat, on a rock, on a wooden bench, or in a boat.

sanskrit: guror gurau sannihite guruvad vṛttim ācaret / na cānisṛṣṭo guruṇā svān gurūn abhivādayet //
english: If his teacher's teacher is near, let him behave (towards him) as towards his own teacher; but let him, unless he has received permission from his teacher, not salute venerable persons of his own (family).

sanskrit: vidyāguruṣv evam eva nityā vṛttiḥ svayoniṣu / pratiṣedhatsu cādharmād dhitaṃ copadiśatsv api //
english: This is likewise (ordained as) his constant behaviour towards (other) instructors in science, towards his relatives (to whom honour is due), towards all who may restrain him from sin, or may give him salutary advice.

sanskrit: śreyaḥsu guruvad vṛttiṃ nityam eva samācaret / guruputreṣu cāryeṣu guroś caiva svabandhuṣu //
english: Towards his betters let him always behave as towards his teacher, likewise towards sons of his teacher, born by wives of equal caste, and towards the teacher's relatives both on the side of the father and of the mother.

sanskrit: bālaḥ samānajanmā vā śiṣyo vā yajñakarmaṇi / adhyāpayan gurusuto guruvan mānam arhati //
english: The son of the teacher who imparts instruction (in his father's stead), whether younger or of equal age, or a student of (the science of) sacrifices (or of other Angas), deserves the same honour as the teacher.

sanskrit: utsādanaṃ ca gātrāṇāṃ snāpanocchiṣṭabhojane / na kuryād guruputrasya pādayoś cāvanejanam //
english: (A student) must not shampoo the limbs of his teacher's son, nor assist him in bathing, nor eat the fragments of his food, nor wash his feet.

sanskrit: guruvat pratipūjyāḥ syuḥ savarṇā guruyoṣitaḥ / asavarṇās tu sampūjyāḥ pratyutthānābhivādanaiḥ //
english: The wives of the teacher, who belong to the same caste, must be treated as respectfully as the teacher; but those who belong to a different caste, must be honoured by rising and salutation.

sanskrit: abhyañjanaṃ snāpanaṃ ca gātrotsādanam eva ca / gurupatnyā na kāryāṇi keśānāṃ ca prasādhanam //
english: Let him not perform for a wife of his teacher (the offices of) anointing her, assisting her in the bath, shampooing her limbs, or arranging her hair.

sanskrit: gurupatnī tu yuvatir nābhivādyeha pādayoḥ / pūrṇaviṃśativarṣeṇa guṇadoṣau vijānatā //
english: (A pupil) who is full twenty years old, and knows what is becoming and unbecoming, shall not salute a young wife of his teacher (by clasping) her feet.

sanskrit: svabhāva eṣa nārīṇāṃ narāṇām iha dūṣaṇam / ato 'rthān na pramādyanti pramadāsu vipaścitaḥ //
english: It is the nature of women to seduce men in this (world); for that reason the wise are never unguarded in (the company of) females.

sanskrit: avidvāṃsam alaṃ loke vidvāṃsam api vā punaḥ / pramadā hy utpathaṃ netuṃ kāmakrodhavaśānugam //
english: For women are able to lead astray in (this) world not only a fool, but even a learned man, and (to make) him a slave of desire and anger.

sanskrit: mātrā svasrā duhitrā vā na viviktāsano bhavet / balavān indriyagrāmo vidvāṃsam api karṣati //
english: One should not sit in a lonely place with one's mother, sister, or daughter; for the senses are powerful, and master even a learned man.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ tu gurupatnīnāṃ yuvatīnāṃ yuvā bhuvi / vidhivad vandanaṃ kuryād asāv aham iti bruvan //
english: But at his pleasure a young student may prostrate himself on the ground before the young wife of a teacher, in accordance with the rule, and say, 'I, N. N., (worship thee, O lady).'

sanskrit: viproṣya pādagrahaṇam anvahaṃ cābhivādanam / gurudāreṣu kurvīta satāṃ dharmam anusmaran //
english: On returning from a journey he must clasp the feet of his teacher's wife and daily salute her (in the manner just mentioned), remembering the duty of the virtuous.

sanskrit: yathā khanan khanitreṇa naro vāry adhigacchati / tathā gurugatāṃ vidyāṃ śuśrūṣur adhigacchati //
english: As the man who digs with a spade (into the ground) obtains water, even so an obedient (pupil) obtains the knowledge which lies (hidden) in his teacher.

sanskrit: muṇḍo vā jaṭilo vā syād atha vā syāc chikhājaṭaḥ / nainaṃ grāme 'bhinimlocet sūryo nābhyudiyāt kva cit //
english: A (student) may either shave his head, or wear his hair in braids, or braid one lock on the crown of his head; the sun must never set or rise while he (lies asleep) in the village.

sanskrit: taṃ ced abhyudiyāt sūryaḥ śayānaṃ kāmacārataḥ / nimloced vāpy avijñānāj japann upavased dinam //
english: If the sun should rise or set while he is sleeping, be it (that he offended) intentionally or unintentionally, he shall fast during the (next) day, muttering (the Savitri).

sanskrit: sūryeṇa hy abhinirmuktaḥ śayāno 'bhyuditaś ca yaḥ / prāyaścittam akurvāṇo yuktaḥ syān mahatainasā //
english: For he who lies (sleeping), while the sun sets or rises, and does not perform (that) penance, is tainted by great guilt.

sanskrit: ācamya prayato nityam ubhe saṃdhye samāhitaḥ / śucau deśe japañ japyam upāsīta yathāvidhi //
english: Purified by sipping water, he shall daily worship during both twilights with a concentrated mind in a pure place, muttering the prescribed text according to the rule.

sanskrit: yadi strī yady avarajaḥ śreyaḥ kiṃ cit samācaret / tat sarvam ācared yukto yatra cāsya ramen manaḥ //
english: If a woman or a man of low caste perform anything (leading to) happiness, let him diligently practise it, as well as (any other permitted act) in which his heart finds pleasure.

sanskrit: dharmārthāv ucyate śreyaḥ kāmārthau dharma eva ca / artha eveha vā śreyas trivarga iti tu sthitiḥ //
english: (Some declare that) the chief good consists in (the acquisition of) spiritual merit and wealth, (others place it) in (the gratification of) desire and (the acquisition of) wealth, (others) in (the acquisition of) spiritual merit alone, and (others say that the acquisition of) wealth alone is the chief good here (below); but the (correct) decision is that it consists of the aggregate of (those) three.

sanskrit: ācāryaś ca pitā caiva mātā bhrātā ca pūrvajaḥ / nārtenāpy avamantavyā brāhmaṇena viśeṣataḥ //
english: The teacher, the father, the mother, and an elder brother must not be treated with disrespect, especially by a Brahmana, though one be grievously offended (by them).

sanskrit: ācāryo brahmaṇo mūrtiḥ pitā mūrtiḥ prajāpateḥ / mātā pṛthivyā mūrtis tu bhrātā svo mūrtir ātmanaḥ //
english: The teacher is the image of Brahman, the father the image of Pragipati (the lord of created beings), the mother the image of the earth, and an (elder) full brother the image of oneself.

sanskrit: yaṃ mātāpitarau kleśaṃ sahete saṃbhave nṛṇām / na tasya niṣkṛtiḥ śakyā kartuṃ varṣaśatair api //
english: That trouble (and pain) which the parents undergo on the birth of (their) children, cannot be compensated even in a hundred years.

sanskrit: tayor nityaṃ priyaṃ kuryād ācāryasya ca sarvadā / teṣv eva triṣu tuṣṭeṣu tapaḥ sarvaṃ samāpyate //
english: Let him always do what is agreeable to those (two) and always (what may please) his teacher; when those three are pleased, he obtains all (those rewards which) austerities (yield).

sanskrit: teṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ śuśrūṣā paramaṃ tapa ucyate / na tair anabhyanujñāto dharmam anyaṃ samācaret //
english: Obedience towards those three is declared to be the best (form of) austerity; let him not perform other meritorious acts without their permission.

sanskrit: ta eva hi trayo lokās ta eva traya āśramāḥ / ta eva hi trayo vedās ta evoktās trayo 'gnayaḥ //
english: For they are declared to be the three worlds, they the three (principal) orders, they the three Vedas, and they the three sacred fires.

sanskrit: pitā vai gārhapatyo 'gnir mātāgnir dakṣiṇaḥ smṛtaḥ / gurur āhavanīyas tu sāgnitretā garīyasī //
english: The father, forsooth, is stated to be the Garhapatya fire, the mother the Dakshinagni, but the teacher the Ahavaniya fire; this triad of fires is most venerable.

sanskrit: triṣv apramādyann eteṣu trīn lokān vijayed gṛhī / dīpyamānaḥ svavapuṣā devavad divi modate //
english: He who neglects not those three, (even after he has become) a householder, will conquer the three worlds and, radiant in body like a god, he will enjoy bliss in heaven.

sanskrit: imaṃ lokaṃ mātṛbhaktyā pitṛbhaktyā tu madhyamam / guruśuśrūṣayā tv evaṃ brahmalokaṃ samaśnute //
english: By honouring his mother he gains this (nether) world, by honouring his father the middle sphere, but by obedience to his teacher the world of Brahman.

sanskrit: sarve tasyādṛtā dharmā yasyaite traya ādṛtāḥ / anādṛtās tu yasyaite sarvās tasyāphalāḥ kriyāḥ //
english: All duties have been fulfilled by him who honours those three; but to him who honours them not, all rites remain fruitless.

sanskrit: yāvat trayas te jīveyus tāvan nānyaṃ samācaret / teṣv eva nityaṃ śuśrūṣāṃ kuryāt priyahite rataḥ //
english: As long as those three live, so long let him not (independently) perform any other (meritorious acts); let him always serve them, rejoicing (to do what is) agreeable and beneficial (to them).

sanskrit: teṣām anuparodhena pāratryaṃ yad yad ācaret / tat tan nivedayet tebhyo manovacanakarmabhiḥ //
english: He shall inform them of everything that with their consent he may perform in thought, word, or deed for the sake of the next world.

sanskrit: triṣv eteṣv itikṛtyaṃ hi puruṣasya samāpyate / eṣa dharmaḥ paraḥ sākṣād upadharmo 'nya ucyate //
english: By (honouring) these three all that ought to be done by man, is accomplished; that is clearly the highest duty, every other (act) is a subordinate duty.

sanskrit: śraddadhānaḥ śubhāṃ vidyām ādadītāvarād api / anyād api paraṃ dharmaṃ strīratnaṃ duṣkulād api //
english: He who possesses faith may receive pure learning even from a man of lower caste, the highest law even from the lowest, and an excellent wife even from a base family.

sanskrit: viṣād apy amṛtaṃ grāhyaṃ bālād api subhāṣitam / amitrād api sadvṛttam amedhyād api kāñcanam //
english: Even from poison nectar may be taken, even from a child good advice, even from a foe (a lesson in) good conduct, and even from an impure (substance) gold.

sanskrit: striyo ratnāny atho vidyā dharmaḥ śaucaṃ subhāṣitam / vividhāni ca śīlpāni samādeyāni sarvataḥ //
english: Excellent wives, learning, (the knowledge of) the law, (the rules of) purity, good advice, and various arts may be acquired from anybody.

sanskrit: abrāhmaṇād adhyāyanam āpatkāle vidhīyate / anuvrajyā ca śuśrūṣā yāvad adhyāyanaṃ guroḥ //
english: It is prescribed that in times of distress (a student) may learn (the Veda) from one who is not a Brahmana; and that he shall walk behind and serve (such a) teacher, as long as the instruction lasts.

sanskrit: nābrāhmaṇe gurau śiṣyo vāsam ātyantikaṃ vaset / brāhmaṇe vānanūcāne kāṅkṣan gatim anuttamām //
english: He who desires incomparable bliss (in heaven) shall not dwell during his whole life in (the house of) a non-Brahmanical teacher, nor with a Brahmana who does not know the whole Veda and the Angas.

sanskrit: yadi tv ātyantikaṃ vāsaṃ rocayeta guroḥ kule / yuktaḥ paricared enam ā śarīravimokṣaṇāt //
english: But if (a student) desires to pass his whole life in the teacher's house, he must diligently serve him, until he is freed from this body.

sanskrit: ā samāpteḥ śarīrasya yas tu śuśrūṣate gurum / sa gacchaty añjasā vipro brahmaṇaḥ sadma śāśvatam //
english: A Brahmana who serves his teacher till the dissolution of his body, reaches forthwith the eternal mansion of Brahman.

sanskrit: na pūrvaṃ gurave kiṃ cid upakurvīta dharmavit / snāsyaṃs tu guruṇājñaptaḥ śaktyā gurvartham āharet //
english: He who knows the sacred law must not present any gift to his teacher before (the Samavartana); but when, with the permission of his teacher, he is about to take the (final) bath, let him procure (a present) for the venerable man according to his ability,

sanskrit: kṣetraṃ hiraṇyaṃ gām aśvaṃ chatropānaham āsanam / dhānyaṃ śākaṃ ca vāsāṃsi gurave prītim āvahet //
english: (Viz.) a field, gold, a cow, a horse, a parasol and shoes, a seat, grain, (even) vegetables, (and thus) give pleasure to his teacher.

sanskrit: ācārye tu khalu prete guruputre guṇānvite / gurudāre sapiṇḍe vā guruvad vṛttim ācaret //
english: (A perpetual student) must, if his teacher dies, serve his son (provided he be) endowed with good qualities, or his widow, or his Sapinda, in the same manner as the teacher.

sanskrit: eteṣv avidyamāneṣu sthānāsanavihāravān / prayuñjāno 'gniśuśrūṣāṃ sādhayed deham ātmanaḥ //
english: Should none of these be alive, he must serve the sacred fire, standing (by day) and sitting (during the night), and thus finish his life.

sanskrit: evaṃ carati yo vipro brahmacaryam aviplutaḥ / sa gacchaty uttamasthānaṃ na ceha jāyate punaḥ //
english: A Brahmana who thus passes his life as a student without breaking his vow, reaches (after death) the highest abode and will not be born again in this world.

sanskrit: ṣaṭtriṃśadābdikaṃ caryaṃ gurau traivedikaṃ vratam / tadardhikaṃ pādikaṃ vā grahaṇāntikam eva vā //
english: The vow (of studying) the three Vedas under a teacher must be kept for thirty-six years, or for half that time, or for a quarter, or until the (student) has perfectly learnt them.

sanskrit: vedān adhītya vedau vā vedaṃ vāpi yathākramam / aviplutabrahmacaryo gṛhasthāśramam āvaset //
english: (A student) who has studied in due order the three Vedas, or two, or even one only, without breaking the (rules of) studentship, shall enter the order of householders.

sanskrit: taṃ pratītaṃ svadharmeṇa brahmadāyaharaṃ pituḥ / sragviṇaṃ talpa āsīnam arhayet prathamaṃ gavā // guruṇānumataḥ snātvā samāvṛtto yathāvidhi / udvaheta dvijo bhāryāṃ savarṇāṃ lakṣaṇānvitām //
english: He who is famous for (the strict performance of) his duties and has received his heritage, the Veda, from his father, shall be honoured, sitting on a couch and adorned with a garland, with (the present of) a cow (and the honey-mixture). Having bathed, with the permission of his teacher, and performed according to the rule the Samavartana (the rite on returning home), a twice-born man shall marry a wife of equal caste who is endowed with auspicious (bodily) marks.

sanskrit: asapiṇḍā ca yā mātur asagotrā ca yā pituḥ / sā praśastā dvijātīnāṃ dārakarmaṇi maithune //
english: A damsel who is neither a Sapinda on the mother's side, nor belongs to the same family on the father's side, is recommended to twice-born men for wedlock and conjugal union.

sanskrit: mahānty api samṛddhāni go'jāvidhanadhānyataḥ / strīsaṃbandhe daśaitāni kulāni parivarjayet //
english: In connecting himself with a wife, let him carefully avoid the ten following families, be they ever so great, or rich in kine, horses, sheep, grain, or (other) property,

sanskrit: hīnakriyaṃ niṣpuruṣaṃ niśchando romaśārśasam / kṣayāmayāvyapasmāri- śvitrikuṣṭhikulāni ca //
english: (Viz.) one which neglects the sacred rites, one in which no male children (are born), one in which the Veda is not studied, one (the members of) which have thick hair on the body, those which are subject to hemorrhoids, phthisis, weakness of digestion, epilepsy, or white or black leprosy.

sanskrit: nodvahet kapilāṃ kanyāṃ nādhikāṅgīṃ na rogiṇīm / nālomikāṃ nātilomāṃ na vācāṭāṃ na piṅgalām // na rkṣavṛkṣanadīnāmnīṃ nāntyaparvatanāmikām / na pakṣyahipreṣyanāmnīṃ na ca bhīṣananāmikām //
english: Let him not marry a maiden (with) reddish (hair), nor one who has a redundant member, nor one who is sickly, nor one either with no hair (on the body) or too much, nor one who is garrulous or has red (eyes), Nor one named after a constellation, a tree, or a river, nor one bearing the name of a low caste, or of a mountain, nor one named after a bird, a snake, or a slave, nor one whose name inspires terror.

sanskrit: avyaṅgāṅgīṃ saumyanāmnīṃ haṃsavāraṇagāminīm / tanulomakeśadaśanāṃ mṛdvaṅgīm udvahet striyam //
english: Let him wed a female free from bodily defects, who has an agreeable name, the (graceful) gait of a Hamsa or of an elephant, a moderate (quantity of) hair on the body and on the head, small teeth, and soft limbs.

sanskrit: yasyās tu na bhaved bhrātā na vijñāyeta vā pitā / nopayaccheta tāṃ prājñaḥ putrikādharmaśaṅkayā //
english: But a prudent man should not marry (a maiden) who has no brother, nor one whose father is not known, through fear lest (in the former case she be made) an appointed daughter (and in the latter) lest (he should commit) sin.

sanskrit: savarṇāgre dvijātīnāṃ praśastā dārakarmaṇi / kāmatas tu pravṛttānām imāḥ syuḥ kramaśo 'varāḥ //
english: For the first marriage of twice-born men (wives) of equal caste are recommended; but for those who through desire proceed (to marry again) the following females, (chosen) according to the (direct) order (of the castes), are most approved.

sanskrit: śūdraiva bhāryā śūdrasya sā ca svā ca viśaḥ smṛte / te ca svā caiva rājñaś ca tāś ca svā cāgrajanmanaḥ //
english: It is declared that a Sudra woman alone (can be) the wife of a Sudra, she and one of his own caste (the wives) of a Vaisya, those two and one of his own caste (the wives) of a Kshatriya, those three and one of his own caste (the wives) of a Brahmana.

sanskrit: na brāhmaṇakṣatriyayor āpady api hi tiṣṭhatoḥ / kasmiṃś cid api vṛttānte śūdrā bhāryopadiśyate //
english: A Sudra woman is not mentioned even in any (ancient) story as the (first) wife of a Brahmana or of a Kshatriya, though they lived in the (greatest) distress.

sanskrit: hīnajātistriyaṃ mohād udvahanto dvijātayaḥ / kulāny eva nayanty āśu sasantānāni śūdratām //
english: Twice-born men who, in their folly, wed wives of the low (Sudra) caste, soon degrade their families and their children to the state of Sudras.

sanskrit: śūdrāvedī pataty atrer utathyatanayasya ca / śaunakasya sutotpattyā tadapatyatayā bhṛgoḥ //
english: According to Atri and to (Gautama) the son of Utathya, he who weds a Sudra woman becomes an outcast, according to Saunaka on the birth of a son, and according to Bhrigu he who has (male) offspring from a (Sudra female, alone).

sanskrit: śūdrāṃ śayanam āropya brāhmaṇo yāty adhogatim / janayitvā sutaṃ tasyāṃ brāhmaṇyād eva hīyate //
english: A Brahmana who takes a Sudra wife to his bed, will (after death) sink into hell; if he begets a child by her, he will lose the rank of a Brahmana.

sanskrit: daivapitryātitheyāni tatpradhānāni yasya tu / nāśnanti pitṛdevās tan na ca svargaṃ sa gacchati //
english: The manes and the gods will not eat the (offerings) of that man who performs the rites in honour of the gods, of the manes, and of guests chiefly with a (Sudra wife's) assistance, and such (a man) will not go to heaven.

sanskrit: vṛṣalīphenapītasya niḥśvāsopahatasya ca / tasyāṃ caiva prasūtasya niṣkṛtir na vidhīyate //
english: For him who drinks the moisture of a Sudra's lips, who is tainted by her breath, and who begets a son on her, no expiation is prescribed.

sanskrit: caturṇām api varṇānaṃ pretya ceha hitāhitān / aṣṭāv imān samāsena strīvivāhān nibodhata //
english: Now listen to (the) brief (description of) the following eight marriage-rites used by the four castes (varna) which partly secure benefits and partly produce evil both in this life and after death.

sanskrit: brāhmo daivas tathaivārṣaḥ prājāpatyas tathāsuraḥ / gāndharvo rākṣasaś caiva paiśācaś cāṣṭamo 'dhamaḥ //
english: (They are) the rite of Brahman (Brahma), that of the gods (Daiva), that of the Rishis (Arsha), that of Pragapati (Pragapatya), that of the Asuras (Asura), that of the Gandharvas (Gandharva), that of the Rhashasas (Rakshasa), and that of the Pisakas (Paisaka).

sanskrit: yo yasya dharmyo varṇasya guṇadoṣau ca yasya yau / tad vaḥ sarvaṃ pravakṣyāmi prasave ca guṇāguṇān //
english: Which is lawful for each caste (varna) and which are the virtues or faults of each (rite), all this I will declare to you, as well as their good and evil results with respect to the offspring.

sanskrit: ṣaḍ ānupūrvyā viprasya kṣatrasya caturo 'varān / viṭśūdrayos tu tān eva vidyād dharmyān arākṣasān //
english: One may know that the first six according to the order (followed above) are lawful for a Brahmana, the four last for a Kshatriya, and the same four, excepting the Rakshasa rite, for a Vaisya and a Sudra.

sanskrit: caturo brāhmaṇasyādyān praśastān kavayo viduḥ / rākṣasaṃ kṣatriyasyaikam āsuraṃ vaiśyaśūdrayoḥ //
english: The sages state that the first four are approved (in the case) of a Brahmana, one, the Rakshasa (rite in the case) of a Kshatriya, and the Asura (marriage in that) of a Vaisya and of a Sudra.

sanskrit: pañcānāṃ tu trayo dharmyā dvāv adharmyau smṛtāv iha / paiśācaś cāsuraś caiva na kartavyau kadā cana //
english: But in these (Institutes of the sacred law) three of the five (last) are declared to be lawful and two unlawful; the Paisaka and the Asura (rites) must never be used.

sanskrit: pṛthak pṛthag vā miśrau vā vivāhau pūrvacoditau / gāndharvo rākṣasaś caiva dharmyau kṣatrasya tau smṛtau //
english: For Kshatriyas those before-mentioned two rites, the Gandharva and the Rakshasa, whether separate or mixed, are permitted by the sacred tradition.

sanskrit: ācchādya cārcayitvā ca śrutaśīlavate svayam / āhūya dānaṃ kanyāyā brāhmo dharmaḥ prakīrtitaḥ //
english: The gift of a daughter, after decking her (with costly garments) and honouring (her by presents of jewels), to a man learned in the Veda and of good conduct, whom (the father) himself invites, is called the Brahma rite.

sanskrit: yajñe tu vitate samyag ṛtvije karma kurvate / alaṅkṛtya sutādānaṃ daivaṃ dharmaṃ pracakṣate //
english: The gift of a daughter who has been decked with ornaments, to a priest who duly officiates at a sacrifice, during the course of its performance, they call the Daiva rite.

sanskrit: ekaṃ gomithunaṃ dve vā varād ādāya dharmataḥ / kanyāpradānaṃ vidhivad ārṣo dharmaḥ sa ucyate //
english: When (the father) gives away his daughter according to the rule, after receiving from the bridegroom, for (the fulfilment of) the sacred law, a cow and a bull or two pairs, that is named the Arsha rite.

sanskrit: sahobhau caratāṃ dharmam iti vācānubhāṣya ca / kanyāpradānam abhyarcya prājāpatyo vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ //
english: The gift of a daughter (by her father) after he has addressed (the couple) with the text, 'May both of you perform together your duties,' and has shown honour (to the bridegroom), is called in the Smriti the Pragapatya rite.

sanskrit: jñātibhyo draviṇaṃ dattvā kanyāyai caiva śaktitaḥ / kanyāpradānaṃ svācchandyād āsuro dharma ucyate //
english: When (the bridegroom) receives a maiden, after having given as much wealth as he can afford, to the kinsmen and to the bride herself, according to his own will, that is called the Asura rite.

sanskrit: icchayānyonyasaṃyogaḥ kanyāyāś ca varasya ca / gāndharvaḥ sa tu vijñeyo maithunyaḥ kāmasaṃbhavaḥ //
english: The voluntary union of a maiden and her lover one must know (to be) the Gandharva rite, which springs from desire and has sexual intercourse for its purpose.

sanskrit: hatvā chittvā ca bhittvā ca krośantīṃ rudantīṃ gṛhāt / prasahya kanyāharaṇaṃ rākṣaso vidhir ucyate //
english: The forcible abduction of a maiden from her home, while she cries out and weeps, after (her kinsmen) have been slain or wounded and (their houses) broken open, is called the Rakshasa rite.

sanskrit: suptāṃ mattāṃ pramattāṃ vā raho yatropagacchati / sa pāpiṣṭho vivāhānāṃ paiśācaś cāṣṭamo 'dhamaḥ //
english: When (a man) by stealth seduces a girl who is sleeping, intoxicated, or disordered in intellect, that is the eighth, the most base and sinful rite of the Pisakas.

sanskrit: adbhir eva dvijāgryāṇāṃ kanyādānaṃ viśiṣyate / itareṣāṃ tu varṇānām itaretarakāmyayā //
english: The gift of daughters among Brahmanas is most approved, (if it is preceded) by (a libation of) water; but in the case of other castes (it may be performed) by (the expression of) mutual consent.

sanskrit: yo yasyaiṣāṃ vivāhānāṃ manunā kīrtito guṇaḥ / sarvaṃ śṛṇuta taṃ viprāḥ sarvaṃ kīrtayato mama //
english: Listen now to me, ye Brahmanas, while I fully declare what quality has been ascribed by Manu to each of these marriage-rites.

sanskrit: daśa pūrvān parān vaṃśyān ātmānaṃ caikaviṃśakam / brāhmīputraḥ sukṛtakṛn mocayaty enasaḥ pitṝn //
english: The son of a wife wedded according to the Brahma rite, if he performs meritorious acts, liberates from sin ten ancestors, ten descendants and himself as the twenty-first.

sanskrit: daivoḍhājaḥ sutaś caiva sapta sapta parāvarān / ārṣoḍhājaḥ sutas trīṃs trīn ṣaṭ ṣaṭ kāyoḍhajaḥ sutaḥ //
english: The son born of a wife, wedded according to the Daiva rite, likewise (saves) seven ancestors and seven descendants, the son of a wife married by the Arsha rite three (in the ascending and descending lines), and the son of a wife married by the rite of Ka (Pragapati) six (in either line).

sanskrit: brāhmādiṣu vivāheṣu caturṣv evānupūrvaśaḥ / brahmavarcasvinaḥ putrā jāyante śiṣṭasammatāḥ //
english: From the four marriages, (enumerated) successively, which begin with the Brahma rite spring sons, radiant with knowledge of the Veda and honoured by the Sishtas (good men).

sanskrit: rūpasattvaguṇopetā dhanavanto yaśasvinaḥ / paryāptabhogā dharmiṣṭhā jīvanti ca śataṃ samāḥ //
english: Endowded with the qualities of beauty and goodness, possessing wealth and fame, obtaining as many enjoyments as they desire and being most righteous, they will live a hundred years.

sanskrit: itareṣu tu śiṣṭeṣu nṛśaṃsānṛtavādinaḥ / jāyante durvivāheṣu brahmadharmadviṣaḥ sutāḥ //
english: But from the remaining (four) blamable marriages spring sons who are cruel and speakers of untruth, who hate the Veda and the sacred law.

sanskrit: aninditaiḥ strīvivāhair anindyā bhavati prajā / ninditair ninditā nṝṇāṃ tasmān nindyān vivarjayet //
english: In the blameless marriages blameless children are born to men, in blamable (marriages) blamable (offspring); one should therefore avoid the blamable (forms of marriage).

sanskrit: pāṇigrahaṇasaṃskāraḥ savarṇāsūpadiśyate / asavarṇāsv ayaṃ jñeyo vidhir udvāhakarmaṇi //
english: The ceremony of joining the hands is prescribed for (marriages with) women of equal caste (varna); know that the following rule (applies) to weddings with females of a different caste (varna).

sanskrit: śaraḥ kṣatriyayā grāhyaḥ pratodo vaiśyakanyayā / vasanasya daśā grāhyā śūdrayotkṛṣṭavedane //
english: On marrying a man of a higher caste a Kshatriya bride must take hold of an arrow, a Vaisya bride of a goad, and a Sudra female of the hem of the (bridegroom's) garment.

sanskrit: ṛtukālābhigāmī syāt svadāranirataḥ sadā / parvavarjaṃ vrajec caināṃ tadvrato ratikāmyayā //
english: Let (the husband) approach his wife in due season, being constantly satisfied with her (alone); he may also, being intent on pleasing her, approach her with a desire for conjugal union (on any day) excepting the Parvans.

sanskrit: ṛtuḥ svābhāvikaḥ strīṇāṃ rātrayaḥ ṣoḍaśa smṛtāḥ / caturbhir itaraiḥ sārdham ahobhiḥ sadvigarhitaiḥ //
english: Sixteen (days and) nights (in each month), including four days which differ from the rest and are censured by the virtuous, (are called) the natural season of women.

sanskrit: tāsām ādyāś catasras tu ninditaikādaśī ca yā / trayodaśī ca śeṣās tu praśastā daśarātrayaḥ //
english: But among these the first four, the eleventh and the thirteenth are (declared to be) forbidden; the remaining nights are recommended.

sanskrit: yugmāsu putrā jāyante striyo 'yugmāsu rātriṣu / tasmād yugmāsu putrārthī saṃviśed ārtave striyam //
english: On the even nights sons are conceived and daughters on the uneven ones; hence a man who desires to have sons should approach his wife in due season on the even (nights).

sanskrit: pumān puṃso 'dhike śukre strī bhavaty adhike striyāḥ / same 'pumān puṃ striyau vā kṣīṇe 'lpe ca viparyayaḥ //
english: A male child is produced by a greater quantity of male seed, a female child by the prevalence of the female; if (both are) equal, a hermaphrodite or a boy and a girl; if (both are) weak or deficient in quantity, a failure of conception (results).

sanskrit: nindyāsv aṣṭāsu cānyāsu striyo rātriṣu varjayan / brahmacāry eva bhavati yatra tatrāśrame vasan //
english: He who avoids women on the six forbidden nights and on eight others, is (equal in chastity to) a student, in whichever order he may live.

sanskrit: na kanyāyāḥ pitā vidvān gṛhṇīyāc chulkam aṇv api / gṛhṇañ śulkaṃ hi lobhena syān naro 'patyavikrayī //
english: No father who knows (the law) must take even the smallest gratuity for his daughter; for a man who, through avarice, takes a gratuity, is a seller of his offspring.

sanskrit: strīdhanāni tu ye mohād upajīvanti bāndhavāḥ / nārī yānāni vastraṃ vā te pāpā yānty adhogatim //
english: But those (male) relations who, in their folly, live on the separate property of women, (e.g. appropriate) the beasts of burden, carriages, and clothes of women, commit sin and will sink into hell.

sanskrit: ārṣe gomithunaṃ śulkaṃ ke cid āhur mṛṣaiva tat / alpo 'py evaṃ mahān vāpi vikrayas tāvad eva saḥ //
english: Some call the cow and the bull (given) at an Arsha wedding 'a gratuity;' (but) that is wrong, since (the acceptance of) a fee, be it small or great, is a sale (of the daughter).

sanskrit: yāsāṃ nādadate śulkaṃ jñātayo na sa vikrayaḥ / arhaṇaṃ tat kumārīṇām ānṛśaṃsyaṃ ca kevalam //
english: When the relatives do not appropriate (for their use) the gratuity (given), it is not a sale; (in that case) the (gift) is only a token of respect and of kindness towards the maidens.

sanskrit: pitṛbhir bhrātṛbhiś caitāḥ patibhir devarais tathā / pūjyā bhūṣayitavyāś ca bahukalyāṇam īpsubhiḥ //
english: Women must be honoured and adorned by their fathers, brothers, husbands, and brothers-in-law, who desire (their own) welfare.

sanskrit: yatra nāryas tu pūjyante ramante tatra devatāḥ / yatraitās tu na pūjyante sarvās tatrāphalāḥ kriyāḥ //
english: Where women are honoured, there the gods are pleased; but where they are not honoured, no sacred rite yields rewards.

sanskrit: śocanti jāmayo yatra vinaśyaty āśu tat kulam / na śocanti tu yatraitā vardhate tad dhi sarvadā //
english: Where the female relations live in grief, the family soon wholly perishes; but that family where they are not unhappy ever prospers.

sanskrit: jāmayo yāni gehāni śapanty apratipūjitāḥ / tāni kṛtyāhatānīva vinaśyanti samantataḥ //
english: The houses on which female relations, not being duly honoured, pronounce a curse, perish completely, as if destroyed by magic.

sanskrit: tasmād etāḥ sadā pūjyā bhūṣaṇācchādanāśanaiḥ / bhūtikāmair narair nityaṃ satkareṣūtsaveṣu ca //
english: Hence men who seek (their own) welfare, should always honour women on holidays and festivals with (gifts of) ornaments, clothes, and (dainty) food.

sanskrit: saṃtuṣṭo bhāryayā bhartā bhartrā bhāryā tathaiva ca / yasminn eva kule nityaṃ kalyāṇaṃ tatra vai dhruvam //
english: In that family, where the husband is pleased with his wife and the wife with her husband, happiness will assuredly be lasting.

sanskrit: yadi hi strī na roceta pumāṃsaṃ na pramodayet / apramodāt punaḥ puṃsaḥ prajanaṃ na pravartate //
english: For if the wife is not radiant with beauty, she will not attract her husband; but if she has no attractions for him, no children will be born.

sanskrit: striyāṃ tu rocamānāyāṃ sarvaṃ tad rocate kulaṃ / tasyāṃ tv arocamānāyāṃ sarvam eva na rocate //
english: If the wife is radiant with beauty, the whole house is bright; but if she is destitute of beauty, all will appear dismal.

sanskrit: kuvivāhaiḥ kriyālopair vedānadhyayanena ca / kulāny akulatāṃ yānti brāhmaṇātikrameṇa ca //
english: By low marriages, by omitting (the performance of) sacred rites, by neglecting the study of the Veda, and by irreverence towards Brahmanas, (great) families sink low.

sanskrit: śilpena vyavahāreṇa śūdrāpatyaiś ca kevalaiḥ / gobhir aśvaiś ca yānaiś ca kṛṣyā rājopasevayā // ayājyayājanaiś caiva nāstikyena ca karmaṇām / kulāny āśu vinaśyanti yāni hīnāni mantrataḥ //
english: By (practising) handicrafts, by pecuniary transactions, by (begetting) children on Sudra females only, by (trading in) cows, horses, and carriages, by (the pursuit of) agriculture and by taking service under a king, By sacrificing for men unworthy to offer sacrifices and by denying (the future rewards for good) works, families, deficient in the (knowledge of the) Veda, quickly perish.

sanskrit: mantratas tu samṛddhāni kulāny alpadhanāny api / kulasaṃkhyāṃ ca gacchanti karṣanti ca mahad yaśaḥ //
english: But families that are rich in the knowledge of the Veda, though possessing little wealth, are numbered among the great, and acquire great fame.

sanskrit: vaivāhike 'gnau kurvīta gṛhyaṃ karma yathāvidhi / pañcayajñavidhānaṃ ca paktiṃ cānvāhikīṃ gṛhī //
english: With the sacred fire, kindled at the wedding, a householder shall perform according to the law the domestic ceremonies and the five (great) sacrifices, and (with that) he shall daily cook his food.

sanskrit: pañca sūnā gṛhasthasya cullī peṣaṇy upaskaraḥ / kaṇḍanī codakumbhaś ca badhyate yās tu vāhayan //
english: A householder has five slaughter-houses (as it were, viz.) the hearth, the grinding-stone, the broom, the pestle and mortar, the water-vessel, by using which he is bound (with the fetters of sin).

sanskrit: tāsāṃ krameṇa sarvāsāṃ niṣkṛtyarthaṃ maharṣibhiḥ / pañca kḷptā mahāyajñāḥ pratyahaṃ gṛhamedhinām //
english: In order to successively expiate (the offences committed by means) of all these (five) the great sages have prescribed for householders the daily (performance of the five) great sacrifices.

sanskrit: adhyāpanaṃ brahmayajñaḥ pitṛyajñas tu tarpaṇam / homo daivo balir bhauto nṛyajño 'tithipūjanam //
english: Teaching (and studying) is the sacrifice (offered) to Brahman, the (offerings of water and food called) Tarpana the sacrifice to the manes, the burnt oblation the sacrifice offered to the gods, the Bali offering that offered to the Bhutas, and the hospitable reception of guests the offering to men.

sanskrit: pañcaitān yo mahāayajñān na hāpayati śaktitaḥ / sa gṛhe 'pi vasan nityaṃ sūnādoṣair na lipyate //
english: He who neglects not these five great sacrifices, while he is able (to perform them), is not tainted by the sins (committed) in the five places of slaughter, though he constantly lives in the (order of) house (-holders).

sanskrit: devatātithibhṛtyānāṃ pitṝṇām ātmanaś ca yaḥ / na nirvapati pañcānām ucchvasan na sa jīvati //
english: But he who does not feed these five, the gods, his guests, those whom he is bound to maintain, the manes, and himself, lives not, though he breathes.

sanskrit: ahutaṃ ca hutaṃ caiva tathā prahutam eva ca / brāhmyaṃ hutaṃ prāśitaṃ ca pañcayajñān pracakṣate //
english: They call (these) five sacrifices also, Ahuta, Huta, Prahuta, Brahmya-huta, and Prasita.

sanskrit: japo 'huto huto homaḥ prahuto bhautiko baliḥ / brāhmyaṃ hutaṃ dvijāgryārcā prāśitaṃ pitṛtarpaṇam //
english: Ahuta (not offered in the fire) is the muttering (of Vedic texts), Huta the burnt oblation (offered to the gods), Prahuta (offered by scattering it on the ground) the Bali offering given to the Bhutas, Brahmya-huta (offered in the digestive fire of Brahmanas), the respectful reception of Brahmana (guests), and Prasita (eaten) the (daily oblation to the manes, called) Tarpana.

sanskrit: svādhyāye nityayuktaḥ syād daive caiveha karmaṇi / daivakarmaṇi yukto hi bibhartīdaṃ carācaram //
english: Let (every man) in this (second order, at least) daily apply himself to the private recitation of the Veda, and also to the performance of the offering to the gods; for he who is diligent in the performance of sacrifices, supports both the movable and the immovable creation.

sanskrit: agnau prāstāhutiḥ samyag ādityam upatiṣṭhate / ādityāj jāyate vṛṣṭir vṛṣṭer annaṃ tataḥ prajāḥ //
english: An oblation duly thrown into the fire, reaches the sun; from the sun comes rain, from rain food, therefrom the living creatures (derive their subsistence).

sanskrit: yathā vāyuṃ samāśritya vartante sarvajantavaḥ / tathā gṛhastham āśritya vartante sarva āśramāḥ //
english: As all living creatures subsist by receiving support from air, even so (the members of) all orders subsist by receiving support from the householder.

sanskrit: yasmāt trayo 'py āśramiṇo jñānenānnena cānvaham / gṛhasthenaiva dhāryante tasmāj jyeṣṭhāśramo gṛhī //
english: Because men of the three (other) orders are daily supported by the householder with (gifts of) sacred knowledge and food, therefore (the order of) householders is the most excellent order.

sanskrit: sa saṃdhāryaḥ prayatnena svargam akṣayam icchatā / sukhaṃ cehecchatātyantaṃ yo 'dhāryo durbalendriyaiḥ //
english: (The duties of) this order, which cannot be practised by men with weak organs, must be carefully observed by him who desires imperishable (bliss in) heaven, and constant happiness in this (life).

sanskrit: ṛṣayaḥ pitaro devā bhūtāny atithayas tathā / āśāsate kuṭumbibhyas tebhyaḥ kāryaṃ vijānatā // svādhyāyenārcayeta rṣīn homair devān yathāvidhi / pitṝñ śrāddhaiś ca nṝn annair bhūtāni balikarmaṇā //
english: The sages, the manes, the gods, the Bhutas, and guests ask the householders (for offerings and gifts); hence he who knows (the law), must give to them (what is due to each). Let him worship, according to the rule, the sages by the private recitation of the Veda, the gods by burnt oblations, the manes by funeral offerings (Sraddha), men by (gifts of) food, and the Bhutas by the Bali offering.

sanskrit: kuryād aharahaḥ śrāddham annādyenodakena vā / payomūlaphalair vāpi pitṛbhyaḥ prītim āvahan //
english: Let him daily perform a funeral sacrifice with food, or with water, or also with milk, roots, and fruits, and (thus) please the manes.

sanskrit: ekam apy āśayed vipraṃ pitrarthe pāñcayajñike / na caivātrāśayet kiṃ cid vaiśvadevaṃ prati dvijam //
english: Let him feed even one Brahmana in honour of the manes at (the Sraddha), which belongs to the five great sacrifices; but let him not feed on that (occasion) any Brahmana on account of the Vaisvadeva offering.

sanskrit: vaiśvadevasya siddhasya gṛhye 'gnau vidhipūrvakam / ābhyaḥ kuryād devatābhyo brāhmaṇo homam anvaham //
english: A Brahmana shall offer according to the rule (of his Grihya-sutra a portion) of the cooked food destined for the Vaisvadeva in the sacred domestic fire to the following deities:

sanskrit: agneḥ somasya caivādau tayoś caiva samastayoḥ / viśvebhyaś caiva devebhyo dhanvantaraya eva ca //
english: First to Agni, and (next) to Soma, then to both these gods conjointly, further to all the gods (Visve Devah), and (then) to Dhanvantari,

sanskrit: kuhvai caivānumatyai ca prajāpataya eva ca / saha dyāvāpṛthivyoś ca tathā sviṣṭakṛte 'ntataḥ //
english: Further to Kuhu (the goddess of the new-moon day), to Anumati (the goddess of the full-moon day), to Pragapati (the lord of creatures), to heaven and earth conjointly, and finally to Agni Svishtakrit (the fire which performs the sacrifice well).

sanskrit: evaṃ samyagg havir hutvā sarvadikṣu pradakṣiṇam / indrāntakāppatīndubhyaḥ sānugebhyo baliṃ haret //
english: After having thus duly offered the sacrificial food, let him throw Bali offerings in all directions of the compass, proceeding (from the east) to the south, to Indra, Yama, Varuna, and Soma, as well as to the servants (of these deities).

sanskrit: marudbhya iti tu dvāri kṣiped apsv adbhya ity api / vanaspatibhya ity evaṃ musalolūkhale haret //
english: Saying, '(Adoration) to the Maruts,' he shall scatter (some food) near the door, and (some) in water, saying, '(Adoration to the waters;' he shall throw (some) on the pestle and the mortar, speaking thus, '(Adoration) to the trees.'

sanskrit: ucchīrṣake śriyai kuryād bhadrakālyai ca pādataḥ / brahmavāstoṣpatibhyāṃ tu vāstumadhye baliṃ haret //
english: Near the head (of the bed) he shall make an offering to Sri (fortune), and near the foot (of his bed) to Bhadrakali; in the centre of the house let him place a Bali for Brahman and for Vastoshpati (the lord of the dwelling) conjointly.

sanskrit: viśvebhyaś caiva devebhyo balim ākāśa utkṣipet / divācarebhyo bhūtebhyo naktaṃcāribhya eva ca //
english: Let him throw up into the air a Bali for all the gods, and (in the day-time one) for the goblins roaming about by day, (and in the evening one) for the goblins that walk at night.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhavāstuni kurvīta baliṃ sarvātmabhūtaye / pitṛbhyo baliśeṣaṃ tu sarvaṃ dakṣiṇato haret //
english: In the upper story let him offer a Bali to Sarvatmabhuti; but let him throw what remains (from these offerings) in a southerly direction for the manes.

sanskrit: śūnāṃ ca patitānāṃ ca śvapacāṃ pāparogiṇām / vayasānāṃ kṛmīṇāṃ ca śanakair nirvaped bhuvi //
english: Let him gently place on the ground (some food) for dogs, outcasts, Kandalas (Svapak), those afflicted with diseases that are punishments of former sins, crows, and insects.

sanskrit: evaṃ yaḥ sarvabhūtāni brāhmaṇo nityam arcati / sa gacchati paraṃ sthānaṃ tejomūrtiḥ pathā rjunā //
english: That Brahmana who thus daily honours all beings, goes, endowed with a resplendent body, by a straight road to the highest dwelling-place (i.e. Brahman).

sanskrit: kṛtvaitad balikarmaivam atithiṃ pūrvam āśayet / bhikṣāṃ ca bhikṣave dadyād vidhivad brahmacāriṇe //
english: Having performed this Bali offering, he shall first feed his guest and, according to the rule, give alms to an ascetic (and) to a student.

sanskrit: yat puṇyaphalam āpnoti gāṃ dattvā vidhivad guroḥ / tat puṇyaphalam āpnoti bhikṣāṃ dattvā dvijo gṛhī //
english: A twice-born householder gains, by giving alms, the same reward for his meritorious act which (a student) obtains for presenting, in accordance with the rule, a cow to his teacher.

sanskrit: bhikṣām apy udapātraṃ vā satkṛtya vidhipūrvakam / vedatattvārthaviduṣe brāhmaṇāyopapādayet //
english: Let him give, in accordance with the rule, to a Brahmana who knows the true meaning of the Veda, even (a small portion of food as) alms, or a pot full of water, having garnished (the food with seasoning, or the pot with flowers and fruit).

sanskrit: naśyanti havyakavyāni narāṇām avijānatām / bhasmībhūteṣu vipreṣu mohād dattāni dātṛbhiḥ //
english: The oblations to gods and manes, made by men ignorant (of the law of gifts), are lost, if the givers in their folly present (shares of them) to Brahmanas who are mere ashes.
