sanskrit: vidyātapaḥsamṛddheṣu hutaṃ vipramukhāgniṣu / nistārayati durgāc ca mahataś caiva kilbiṣāt //
english: An offering made in the mouth-fire of Brahmanas rich in sacred learning and austerities, saves from misfortune and from great guilt.

sanskrit: saṃprāptāya tv atithaye pradadyād āsanodake / annaṃ caiva yathāśakti satkṛtya vidhipūrvakam //
english: But let him offer, in accordance with the rule, to a guest who has come (of his own accord) a seat and water, as well as food, garnished (with seasoning), according to his ability.

sanskrit: śilān apy uñchato nityaṃ pañcāgnīn api juhvataḥ / sarvaṃ sukṛtam ādatte brāhmaṇo 'narcito vasan //
english: A Brahmana who stays unhonoured (in the house), takes away (with him) all the spiritual merit even of a man who subsists by gleaning ears of corn, or offers oblations in five fires.

sanskrit: tṛṇāni bhūmir udakaṃ vāk caturthī ca sūnṛtā / etāny api satāṃ gehe nocchidyante kadā cana //
english: Grass, room (for resting), water, and fourthly a kind word; these (things) never fail in the houses of good men.

sanskrit: ekarātraṃ tu nivasann atithir brāhmaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ / anityaṃ hi sthito yasmāt tasmād atithir ucyate //
english: But a Brahmana who stays one night only is declared to be a guest (atithi); for because he stays (sthita) not long (anityam), he is called atithi (a guest).

sanskrit: naikagrāmīṇam atithiṃ vipraṃ sāṅgatikaṃ tathā / upasthitaṃ gṛhe vidyād bhāryā yatrāgnayo 'pi vā //
english: One must not consider as a guest a Brahmana who dwells in the same village, nor one who seeks his livelihood by social intercourse, even though he has come to a house where (there is) a wife, and where sacred fires (are kept).

sanskrit: upāsate ye gṛhasthāḥ parapākam abuddhayaḥ / tena te pretya paśutāṃ vrajanty annādidāyinaḥ //
english: Those foolish householders who constantly seek (to live on) the food of others, become, in consequence of that (baseness), after death the cattle of those who give them food.

sanskrit: apraṇodyo 'tithiḥ sāyaṃ sūryoḍho gṛhamedhinā / kāle prāptas tv akāle vā nāsyānaśnan gṛhe vaset //
english: A guest who is sent by the (setting) sun in the evening, must not be driven away by a householder; whether he have come at (supper-) time or at an inopportune moment, he must not stay in the house without entertainment.

sanskrit: na vai svayaṃ tad aśnīyād atithiṃ yan na bhojayet / dhanyaṃ yaśasyam āyuṣyaṃ svargyaṃ vātithipūjanam //
english: Let him not eat any (dainty) food which he does not offer to his guest; the hospitable reception of guests procures wealth, fame, long life, and heavenly bliss.

sanskrit: āsanāvasathau śayyām anuvrajyām upāsanām / uttameṣūttamaṃ kuryād dhīne hīnaṃ same samam //
english: Let him offer (to his guests) seats, rooms, beds, attendance on departure and honour (while they stay), to the most distinguished in the best form, to the lower ones in a lower form, to equals in an equal manner.

sanskrit: vaiśvadeve tu nirvṛtte yady anyo 'tithir āvrajet / tasyāpy annaṃ yathāśakti pradadyān na baliṃ haret //
english: But if another guest comes after the Vaisvadeva offering has been finished, (the householder) must give him food according to his ability, (but) not repeat the Bali offering.

sanskrit: na bhojanārthaṃ sve vipraḥ kulagotre nivedayet / bhojanārthaṃ hi te śaṃsan vāntāśīty ucyate budhaiḥ //
english: A Brahmana shall not name his family and (Vedic) gotra in order to obtain a meal; for he who boasts of them for the sake of a meal, is called by the wise a foul feeder (vantasin).

sanskrit: na brāhmaṇasya tv atithir gṛhe rājanya ucyate / vaiśyaśūdrau sakhā caiva jñātayo gurur eva ca //
english: But a Kshatriya (who comes) to the house of a Brahmana is not called a guest (atithi), nor a Vaisya, nor a Sudra, nor a personal friend, nor a relative, nor the teacher.

sanskrit: yadi tv atithidharmeṇa kṣatriyo gṛham āvrajet / bhuktavatsu ca vipreṣu kāmaṃ tam api bhojayet //
english: But if a Kshatriya comes to the house of a Brahmana in the manner of a guest, (the house-holder) may feed him according to his desire, after the above-mentioned Brahmanas have eaten.

sanskrit: vaiśyaśūdrāv api prāptau kuṭumbe 'tithidharmiṇau / bhojayet saha bhṛtyais tāv ānṛśaṃsyaṃ prayojayan //
english: Even a Vaisya and a Sudra who have approached his house in the manner of guests, he may allow to eat with his servants, showing (thereby) his compassionate disposition.

sanskrit: itarān api sakhyādīn samprītyā gṛham āgatān / prakṛtyānnaṃ yathāśakti bhojayet saha bhāryayā //
english: Even to others, personal friends and so forth, who have come to his house out of affection, he may give food, garnished (with seasoning) according to his ability, (at the same time) with his wife.

sanskrit: suvāsinīḥ kumārīś ca rogiṇo garbhiṇīḥ striyaḥ / atithibhyo 'gra evaitān bhojayed avicārayan //
english: Without hesitation he may give food, even before his guests, to the following persons, (viz.) to newly-married women, to infants, to the sick, and to pregnant women.

sanskrit: adattvā tu ya etebhyaḥ pūrvaṃ bhuṅkte 'vicakṣaṇaḥ / sa bhuñjāno na jānāti śvagṛdhrair jagdhim ātmanaḥ //
english: But the foolish man who eats first without having given food to these (persons) does, while he crams, not know that (after death) he himself will be devoured by dogs and vultures.

sanskrit: bhuktavatsv atha vipreṣu sveṣu bhṛtyeṣu caiva hi / bhuñjīyātāṃ tataḥ paścād avaśiṣṭaṃ tu dampatī //
english: After the Brahmanas, the kinsmen, and the servants have dined, the householder and his wife may afterwards eat what remains.

sanskrit: devān ṛṣīn manuṣyāṃś ca pitṝn gṛhyāś ca devatāḥ / pūjayitvā tataḥ paścād gṛhasthaḥ śeṣabhug bhavet //
english: Having honoured the gods, the sages, men, the manes, and the guardian deities of the house, the householder shall eat afterwards what remains.

sanskrit: aghaṃ sa kevalaṃ bhuṅkte yaḥ pacaty ātmakāraṇāt / yajñaśiṣṭāśanaṃ hy etat satām annaṃ vidhīyate //
english: He who prepares food for himself (alone), eats nothing but sin; for it is ordained that the food which remains after (the performance of) the sacrifices shall be the meal of virtuous men.

sanskrit: rājartviksnātakagurūn priyaśvaśuramātulān / arhayen madhuparkeṇa parisaṃvatsarāt punaḥ //
english: Let him honour with the honey-mixture a king, an officiating priest, a Snataka, the teacher, a son-in-law, a father-in-law, and a maternal uncle, (if they come) again after a full year (has elapsed since their last visit).

sanskrit: rājā ca śrotriyaś caiva yajñakarmaṇy upasthitau / madhuparkeṇa saṃpūjyau na tv ayajña iti sthitiḥ //
english: A king and a Srotriya, who come on the performance of a sacrifice, must be honoured with the honey-mixture, but not if no sacrifice is being performed; that is a settled rule.

sanskrit: sāyaṃ tv annasya siddhasya patny amantraṃ baliṃ haret / vaiśvadevaṃ hi nāmaitat sāyaṃ prātar vidhīyate //
english: But the wife shall offer in the evening (a portion) of the dressed food as a Bali-oblation, without (the recitation of) sacred formulas; for that (rite which is called the) Vaisvadeva is prescribed both for the morning and the evening.

sanskrit: pitṛyajñaṃ tu nirvartya vipraś candrakṣaye 'gnimān / piṇḍānvāhāryakaṃ śrāddhaṃ kuryān māsānumāsikam //
english: After performing the Pitriyagna, a Brahmana who keeps a sacred fire shall offer, month by month, on the new-moon day, the funeral sacrifice (Sraddha, called) Pindanvaharyaka.

sanskrit: pitṝṇāṃ māsikaṃ śrāddham anvāhāryaṃ vidur budhāḥ / tac cāmiṣeṇā kartavyaṃ praśastena prayatnataḥ //
english: The wise call the monthly funeral offering to the manes Anvaharya (to be offered after the cakes), and that must be carefully performed with the approved (sorts of) flesh (mentioned below).

sanskrit: tatra ye bhojanīyāḥ syur ye ca varjyā dvijottamāḥ / yāvantaś caiva yaiś cānnais tān pravakṣyāmy aśeṣataḥ //
english: I will fully declare what and how many (Brahmanas) must be fed on that (occasion), who must be avoided, and on what kinds of food (they shall dine).

sanskrit: dvau daive pitṛkārye trīn ekaikam ubhayatra vā / bhojayet susamṛddho 'pi na prasajjeta vistare //
english: One must feed two (Brahmanas) at the offering to the gods, and three at the offering to the manes, or one only on either occasion; even a very wealthy man shall not be anxious (to entertain) a large company.

sanskrit: satkriyāṃ deśakālau ca śaucaṃ brāhmaṇasaṃpadaḥ / pañcaitān vistaro hanti tasmān neheta vistaram //
english: A large company destroys these five (advantages) the respectful treatment (of the invited, the propriety of) place and time, purity and (the selection of) virtuous Brahmana (guests); he therefore shall not seek (to entertain) a large company.

sanskrit: prathitā pretakṛtyaiṣā pitryaṃ nāma vidhukṣaye / tasmin yuktasyaiti nityaṃ pretakṛtyaiva laukikī //
english: Famed is this rite for the dead, called (the sacrifice sacred to the manes (and performed) on the new-moon day; if a man is diligent in (performing) that, (the reward of) the rite for the dead, which is performed according to Smarta rules, reaches him constantly.

sanskrit: śrotriyāyaiva deyāni havyakavyāni dātṛbhiḥ / arhattamāya viprāya tasmai dattaṃ mahāphalam //
english: Oblations to the gods and manes must be presented by the givers to a Srotriya alone; what is given to such a most worthy Brahmana yields great reward.

sanskrit: ekaikam api vidvāṃsaṃ daive pitrye ca bhojayet / puṣkalaṃ phalam āpnoti nāmantrajñān bahūn api //
english: Let him feed even one learned man at (the sacrifice) to the gods, and one at (the sacrifice) to the manes; (thus) he will gain a rich reward, not (if he entertains) many who are unacquainted with the Veda.

sanskrit: dūrād eva parīkṣeta brāhmaṇaṃ vedapāragam / tīrthaṃ tad dhavyakavyānāṃ pradāne so 'tithiḥ smṛtaḥ //
english: Let him make inquiries even regarding the remote (ancestors of) a Brahmana who has studied an entire (recension of the) Veda;(if descended from a virtuous race) such a man is a worthy recipient of gifts (consisting) of food offered to the gods or to the manes, he is declared (to procure as great rewards as) a guest (atithi).

sanskrit: sahasraṃ hi sahasrāṇām anṛcāṃ yatra bhuñjate / ekas tān mantravit prītaḥ sarvān arhati dharmataḥ //
english: Though a million of men, unaquainted with the Rikas, were to dine at a (funeral sacrifice), yet a single man, learned in the Veda, who is satisfied (with his entertainment), is worth them all as far as the (production of) spiritual merit (is concerned).

sanskrit: jñānotkṛṣṭāya deyāni kavyāni ca havīṃṣi ca / na hi hastāv asṛgdigdhau rudhireṇaiva śudhyataḥ // yāvato grasate grāsān havyakavyeṣv amantravit / tāvato grasate preto dīptaśūlarṣṭyayoguḍān //
english: Food sacred to the manes or to the gods must be given to a man distinguished by sacred knowledge; for hands, smeared with blood, cannot be cleansed with blood. As many mouthfuls as an ignorant man swallows at a sacrifice to the gods or to the manes, so many red-hot spikes, spears, and iron balls must (the giver of the repast) swallow after death.

sanskrit: jñānaniṣṭhā dvijāḥ ke cit taponiṣṭhās tathāpare / tapaḥsvādhyāyaniṣṭhāś ca karmaniṣṭhās tathāpare //
english: Some Brahmanas are devoted to (the pursuit of) knowledge, and others to (the performance of) austerities; some to austerities and to the recitation of the Veda, and others to (the performance of) sacred rites.

sanskrit: jñānaniṣṭheṣu kavyāni pratiṣṭhāpyāni yatnataḥ / havyāni tu yathānyāyaṃ sarveṣv eva caturṣv api //
english: Oblations to the manes ought to be carefully presented to those devoted to knowledge, but offerings to the gods, in accordance with the reason (of the sacred law), to (men of) all the four (above-mentioned classes).

sanskrit: aśrotriyaḥ pitā yasya putraḥ syād vedapāragaḥ / aśrotriyo vā putraḥ syāt pitā syād vedapāragaḥ //
english: If there is a father ignorant of the sacred texts whose son has learned one whole recension of the Veda and the Angas, and a son ignorant of the sacred texts whose father knows an entire recension of the Veda and the Angas,

sanskrit: jyāyāṃsam anayor vidyād yasya syāc chrotriyaḥ pitā / mantrasaṃpūjanārthaṃ tu satkāram itaro 'rhati //
english: Know that he whose father knows the Veda, is the more venerable one (of the two); yet the other one is worthy of honour, because respect is due to the Veda (which he has learned).

sanskrit: na śrāddhe bhojayen mitraṃ dhanaiḥ kāryo 'sya saṃgrahaḥ / nāriṃ na mitraṃ yaṃ vidyāt taṃ śrāddhe bhojayed dvijam //
english: Let him not entertain a personal friend at a funeral sacrifice; he may gain his affection by (other) valuable gifts; let him feed at a Sraddha a Brahmana whom he considers neither as a foe nor as a friend.

sanskrit: yasya mitrapradhānāni śrāddhāni ca havīṃṣi ca / tasya pretya phalaṃ nāsti śrāddheṣu ca haviḥṣu ca //
english: He who performs funeral sacrifices and offerings to the gods chiefly for the sake of (gaining) friends, reaps after death no reward for Sraddhas and sacrifices.

sanskrit: yaḥ saṃgatāni kurute mohāc chrāddhena mānavaḥ / sa svargāc cyavate lokāc chrāddhamitro dvijādhamaḥ //
english: That meanest among twice-born men who in his folly contracts friendships through a funeral sacrifice, loses heaven, because he performed a Sraddha for the sake of friendship.

sanskrit: saṃbhojāni sābhihitā paiśācī dakṣiṇā dvijaiḥ / ihaivāste tu sā loke gaur andhevaikaveśmani //
english: A gift (of food) by twice-born men, consumed with (friends and relatives), is said to be offered to the Pisakas; it remains in this (world) alone like a blind cow in one stable.

sanskrit: yatheriṇe bījam uptvā na vaptā labhate phalam / tathānṛce havir dattvā na dātā labhate phalam //
english: As a husbandman reaps no harvest when he has sown the seed in barren soil, even so the giver of sacrificial food gains no reward if he presented it to a man unacquainted with the Rikas.

sanskrit: dātṝn pratigrahītṝṃś ca kurute phalabhāginaḥ / viduṣe dakṣiṇāṃ dattvā vidhivat pretya ceha ca //
english: But a present made in accordance with the rules to a learned man, makes the giver and the recipient partakers of rewards both in this (life) and after death.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ śrāddhe 'rcayen mitraṃ nābhirūpam api tv arim / dviṣatā hi havir bhuktaṃ bhavati pretya niṣphalam //
english: (If no learned Brahmana be at hand), he may rather honour a (virtuous) friend than an enemy, though the latter may be qualified (by learning and so forth); for sacrificial food, eaten by a foe, bears no reward after death.

sanskrit: yatnena bhojayec chrāddhe bahvṛcaṃ vedapāragam / śākhāntagam athādhvaryuṃ chandogaṃ tu samāptikam //
english: Let him (take) pains (to) feed at a Sraddha an adherent of the Rig-veda who has studied one entire (recension of that) Veda, or a follower of the Yagur-veda who has finished one Sakha, or a singer of Samans who (likewise) has completed (the study of an entire recension).

sanskrit: eṣām anyatamo yasya bhuñjīta śrāddham arcitaḥ / pitṝṇāṃ tasya tṛptiḥ syāc chāśvatī sāptapauruṣī //
english: If one of these three dines, duly honoured, at a funeral sacrifice, the ancestors of him (who gives the feast), as far as the seventh person, will be satisfied for a very long time.

sanskrit: eṣa vai prathamaḥ kalpaḥ pradāne havyakavyayoḥ / anukalpas tv ayaṃ jñeyaḥ sadā sadbhir anuṣṭhitaḥ //
english: This is the chief rule (to be followed) in offering sacrifices to the gods and manes; know that the virtuous always observe the following subsidiary rule.

sanskrit: mātāmahaṃ mātulaṃ ca svasrīyaṃ śvaśuraṃ gurum / dauhitraṃ viṭpatiṃ bandhum ṛtvig yājyau ca bhojayet //
english: One may also entertain (on such occasions) one's maternal grandfather, a maternal uncle, a sister's son, a father-in-law, one's teacher, a daughter's son, a daughter's husband, a cognate kinsman, one's own officiating priest or a man for whom one offers sacrifices.

sanskrit: na brāhmaṇaṃ parīkṣeta daive karmaṇi dharmavit / pitrye karmaṇi tu prāpte parīkṣeta prayatnataḥ //
english: For a rite sacred to the gods, he who knows the law will not make (too close) inquiries regarding an (invited) Brahmana; but when one performs a ceremony in honour of the manes, one must carefully examine (the qualities and parentage of the guest).

sanskrit: ye stenapatitaklībā ye ca nāstikavṛttayaḥ / tān havyakavyayor viprān anarhān manur abravīt //
english: Manu has declared that those Brahmanas who are thieves, outcasts, eunuchs, or atheists are unworthy (to partake) of oblations to the gods and manes.

sanskrit: jaṭilaṃ cānadhīyānaṃ durbālaṃ kitavaṃ tathā / yājayanti ca ye pūgāṃs tāṃś ca śrāddhe na bhojayet //
english: Let him not entertain at a Sraddha one who wears his hair in braids (a student), one who has not studied (the Veda), one afflicted with a skin-disease, a gambler, nor those who sacrifice for a multitude (of sacrificers).

sanskrit: cikitsakān devalakān māṃsavikrayiṇas tathā / vipaṇena ca jīvanto varjyāḥ syur havyakavyayoḥ //
english: Physicians, temple-priests, sellers of meat, and those who subsist by shop-keeping must be avoided at sacrifices offered to the gods and to the manes.

sanskrit: preṣyo grāmasya rājñaś ca kunakhī śyāvadantakaḥ / pratiroddhā guroś caiva tyaktāgnir vārdhuṣis tathā //
english: A paid servant of a village or of a king, man with deformed nails or black teeth, one who opposes his teacher, one who has forsaken the sacred fire, and a usurer;

sanskrit: yakṣmī ca paśupālaś ca parivettā nirākṛtiḥ / brahmadviṭ parivittiś ca gaṇābhyantara eva ca //
english: One suffering from consumption, one who subsists by tending cattle, a younger brother who marries or kindles the sacred fire before the elder, one who neglects the five great sacrifices, an enemy of the Brahmana race, an elder brother who marries or kindles the sacred fire after the younger, and one who belongs to a company or corporation,

sanskrit: kuśīlavo 'vakīrṇī ca vṛṣalīpatir eva ca / paunarbhavaś ca kāṇaś ca yasya copapatir gṛhe // bhṛtakādhyāpako yaś ca bhṛtakādhyāpitas tathā / śūdraśiṣyo guruś caiva vāgduṣṭaḥ kuṇḍagolakau //
english: An actor or singer, one who has broken the vow of studentship, one whose (only or first) wife is a Sudra female, the son of a remarried woman, a one-eyed man, and he in whose house a paramour of his wife (resides); He who teaches for a stipulated fee and he who is taught on that condition, he who instructs Sudra pupils and he whose teacher is a Sudra, he who speaks rudely, the son of an adulteress, and the son of a widow,

sanskrit: akāraṇe parityaktā mātāpitror guros tathā / brāhmair yaunaiś ca saṃbandhaiḥ saṃyogaṃ patitair gataḥ //
english: He who forsakes his mother, his father, or a teacher without a (sufficient) reason, he who has contracted an alliance with outcasts either through the Veda or through a marriage,

sanskrit: agāradāhī garadaḥ kuṇḍāśī somavikrayī / samudrayāyī bandī ca tailikaḥ kūṭakārakaḥ //
english: An incendiary, a prisoner, he who eats the food given by the son of an adulteress, a seller of Soma, he who undertakes voyages by sea, a bard, an oil-man, a suborner to perjury,

sanskrit: pitrā vivadamānaś ca kitavo madyapas tathā / pāparogy abhiśastaś ca dāmbhiko rasavikrayī //
english: He who wrangles or goes to law with his father, the keeper of a gambling-house, a drunkard, he who is afflicted with a disease (in punishment of former) crimes, he who is accused of a mortal sin, a hypocrite, a seller of substances used for flavouring food,

sanskrit: dhanuḥśarāṇāṃ kartā ca yaś cāgredidhiṣūpatiḥ / mitradhrug dyūtavṛttiś ca putrācāryas tathaiva ca //
english: A maker of bows and of arrows, he who lasciviously dallies with a brother's widow, the betrayer of a friend, one who subsists by gambling, he who learns (the Veda) from his son,

sanskrit: yataḥ sarvāṇi bhūtānipratibhānti sthitāni ca /  yatraivopaśamaṃ yānti tasmaisatyātmane namaḥ //
english: Hail The Eternal. Om, salutation to the self-same Reality, from whom all beings proceed, by whom they are manifest, upon whom they depend, and in whom they become extinct.

sanskrit: jñātā jñānaṃ tathā jñeyaṃ draṣṭādarśanadṛśyabhūḥ / kartā hetuḥ kriyā yasmāttasmai jñasyātmane namaḥ //
english: He is the knower, the knowledge and all that is to be known. He is the seer, the (act of) seeing, and all that is to be seen. He is the actor, the cause and the effect: therefore salutation to Him (who is all) knowledge himself.

sanskrit: sphuranti sīkarā yasmādānandasyāmbare'vanau / sarveṣāṃ jīvanaṃ tasmai brahmānandātmane namaḥ //
english: Salutation to Him (who is) supreme bliss itself, from whom flow the dews of delight (as water springs from a fountain) both in heaven and earth, and who is the life of all.

sanskrit: sutīkṣṇo brāhmaṇaḥ kaścitsaṃśayākṛṣṭamānasaḥ / agasterāśramaṃ gatvā muniṃ papraccha sādaram //
english: One Sutikshna, a Brahmana, whose mind was full of doubts, went to the hermitage of Agasti and asked the sage respectfully:—

sanskrit: sutīkṣṇa uvāca / bhagavandharmatattvajña sarvaśāstraviniścita / saṃśayo'sti mahānekastvametaṃ kṛpayā vada //
english: Oh great sage! that art informed in all the ways and truths of virtue, and knowest with certainty all the Sastras, I am in a great doubt (about something) which I pray you will kindly remove.

sanskrit: mokṣasya kāraṇaṃ karma jñānaṃ vā mokṣasādhanam / ubhayaṃ vā viniścitya ekaṃ kathaya kāraṇam //
english: Tell me whether a man's acts or his knowledge or both of these, is in your opinion, the cause of his emancipation.

sanskrit: agastiruvāca / ubhābhyāmeva pakṣābhyāṃ yathā khe pakṣiṇāṃ gatiḥ / tathaiva jñānakarmabhyāṃ jāyate paramaṃ padam //
english: Agasti replied:—As the flight of birds in the air is effected by means of both their wings, so the highest state of emancipation is attained through the instrumentality of both knowledge and acts.

sanskrit: kevalātkarmaṇo jñānānnahi mokṣo'bhijāyate / kiṃtūbhābhyāṃ bhavenmokṣaḥ sādhanaṃ tūbhayaṃ viduḥ //
english: It is neither our acts nor knowledge alone that produces emancipation, but both together are known as the means of it.

sanskrit: asminnarthe purāvṛttamitihāsaṃ vadāmi te / kāruṇyākhyaḥ purā kaścidbrāhmaṇo'dhītavedakaḥ //
english: I will recite to you an instance on this subject from the old traditions, relating a Brahman named Karunya, who was learned in the Vedas in days of yore.

sanskrit: agniveśyasya putro'bhūdvedavedāṅgapāragaḥ / guroradhītavidyaḥ sannājagāma gṛhaṃ prati //
english: He was the son of Agnivesya and accomplished in the Vedas and all their branches, and after finishing his studies at the preceptor's, returned to his own abode.

sanskrit: tasthāvakarmakṛttūṣṇīṃ saṃśayāno gṛhe tadā / agniveśyo vilokyātha putraṃ karmavivarjitam //
english: He remained a sceptic at home, holding his taciturnity and inertness to acts: when his father Agnivesya saw his son so slack in his duties, he upbraided him thus for his good.

sanskrit: agniveśya uvāca / prāha etadvaco nindyaṃ guruḥ putraṃ hitāya ca / kimetatputra kuruṣe pālanaṃ na svakarmaṇaḥ //
english: Agnivesya said:—Why my son do you not discharge your duties, tell me how can you succeed (in anything) if you remain inactive, and tell me also the reason of your cessation from acts.

sanskrit: akarmanirataḥ siddhiṃ kathaṃ prāpsyasi tadvada / karmaṇo'smānnivṛtteḥ kiṃ kāraṇaṃ tannivedyatām //
english: Agnivesya said:—Why my son do you not discharge your duties, tell me how can you succeed (in anything) if you remain inactive, and tell me also the reason of your cessation from acts.

sanskrit: kāruṇya uvāca / yāvajjīvamagnihotraṃ nityaṃ saṃdhyāmupāsayet / pravṛttirūpo dharmo'yaṃ śrutyā smṛtyā ca coditaḥ //
english: Karunya replied:—The offering of daily oblations, and performance of morning and evening devotions during life, are inculcated in the Veda and law as the active duties.

sanskrit: na dhanena bhavenmokṣaḥ karmaṇā prajayā na vā / tyāgamātreṇa kiṃtveke yatayo'śnanti cāmṛtam //
english: But it is neither by acts or riches, nor by means of progeny, that one obtains his liberation, it is solely by self-denial that Stoics taste the ambrosia.

sanskrit: iti śrutyordvayormadhye kiṃ kartavyaṃ mayā guro / iti saṃdigdhatāṃ gatvā tūṣṇīṃbhūto'smi karmaṇi //
english: Tell me my father! which of these two ordinances is to be observed by me? Doubtful of this I have become indifferent to acts.

sanskrit: agastiruvāca / ityuktvā tāta vipro'sau kāruṇyo maunamāgataḥ / tathāvidhaṃ sutaṃ dṛṣṭvā punaḥ prāha guruḥ sutam //
english: Agasti said:—Hear me my son, that Karunya after saying so held his silence; when his father seeing him thus, rejoined his speech.

sanskrit: agniveśya uvāca / śṛṇu putra kathāmekāṃ tadarthaṃ hṛdaye'khilam / matto'vadhārya putra tvaṃ yathecchasi tathā kuru //
english: Agnivesya said:—Hear me relate a narrative (to you) my son, and you having fully considered its purport in your mind, may do as you may choose.

sanskrit: surucirnāma kācitstrī apsarogaṇauttamā / upaviṣṭā himavataḥ śikhare śikhisaṃvṛte //
english: There was a damsel named Suruchi, the best of the Apsara nymphs, who was seated on the mountain peak of Himalaya, beset by peacocks around.

sanskrit: ramante kāmasaṃtaptāḥ kinnaryo yatra kinnaraiḥ / svardhunyoghena saṃsṛṣṭe mahāghaughavināśinā //
english: Here Kinnaras inflamed by love sported with their mates, and the fall of heavenly streams (Ganga and Yamuna), served to expurgate the gravest sins.

sanskrit: dūtamindrasya gacchantamantarikṣe dadarśa sā / tamuvāca mahābhāgā suruciścāpsarovarā //
english: She beheld a messenger of Indra making his way through the sky; and then this most fortunate and best of Apsaras, addressed him thus:

sanskrit: suruciruvāca / devadūta mahābhāga kuta āgamyate tvayā / adhunā kutra gantāsi tatsarvaṃ kṛpayā vada //
english: Suruchi said:—O thou herald of gods, tell me kindly whence thou comest and whither art thou destined at present.

sanskrit: devadūta uvāca / sādhu pṛṣṭaṃ tvayā subhru yathāvatkathayāmi te / ariṣṭanemī rājarṣirdattvā rājyaṃ sutāya vai //
english: The divine ariel replied:—Well hast thou asked Oh pretty browed maid, and I will tell thee all as it is. Know, Arishtanemi the royal sage, who has made over his realm to his son.

sanskrit: vītarāgaḥ sa dharmātmā niryayau tapase vanam / tapaścaratyasau rājā parvate gandhamādane //
english: He has (now) with religious indifference (to the world), set out to the forest for (practice of) asceticism, and is performing his austerities on the Gandha Madana mountains.

sanskrit: kāryaṃ kṛtvā mayā tatra tata āgamyate'5dhunā / gantāsmi pārśve śakrasya taṃ vṛttāntaṃ niveditum //
english: I am now returning from there after discharge of my errand, and repairing to Sakra's (palace) to report the matter.

sanskrit: apsarā uvāca / vṛttāntaḥ ko'bhavattatra kathayasva mama prabho / praṣṭukāmā vinītāsmi nodvegaṃ kartumarhasi //
english: Suruchi said:—Tell me, my Lord, what matter has taken place there. I am with submission (much) inquisitive after it, nor shouldest thou cause me (the pain of) anxiety.

sanskrit: devadūta uvāca / śṛṇu bhadre yathāvṛttaṃ vistareṇa vadāmi te / tasminrājñi vane tatra tapaścarati dustaram //
english: The messenger replied:—Hear me gentle maid, relate to thee in length (everything) as it has occurred.

sanskrit: ityahaṃ devarājena subhrūrājñāpitastadā / dūta tvaṃ tatra gacchāśu gṛhītvedaṃ vimānakam //
english: On hearing that the king was practising the utmost rigors of asceticism in that forest, Indra, the lord of Gods, desired me to take this heavenly car and repair at once to the spot.

sanskrit: apsarogaṇasaṃyuktaṃ nānāvāditraśobhitam / gandharvasiddhayakṣaiśca kinnarādyaiśca śobhitam //
english: “Take this car,” said he, “bearing the (dancing) Apsaras equipped with all their musical instruments, and furnished with a band of Gandharvas, Siddhas, Yakshas and Kinnaras.”

sanskrit: tālaveṇumṛdaṅgādi parvate gandhamādane / nānāvṛkṣasamākīrṇe gatvā tasmingirau śubhe //
english: “Convey them,” said he, “with all their wired instruments, flutes and drums to the auspices of the Sylvan mount of Gandha Madana.”

sanskrit: ariṣṭanemiṃ rājānaṃ dūtāropya vimānake / ānaya svargabhogāya nagarīmamarāvatīm //
english: “There having placed the Prince Aristanemi in the vehicle, bring him to the enjoyment of heavenly delight in this city of Amaravati (the seat of immortals).”

sanskrit: dūta uvāca / ityājñāṃ prāpya śakrasya gṛhītvā tadvimānakam / sarvopaskarasaṃyuktaṃ tasminnadrāvahaṃ yayau //
english: The messenger added:—Receiving this injunction of Indra and taking the car with all its equipments, I proceeded to that mountain.

sanskrit: āgatya parvate tasminrājño gatvā''śramaṃ mayā / niveditā mahendrasya sarvājñā'riṣṭanemaye //
english: Having arrived at the mountain and advancing to the hermitage of the king, I delivered to him the orders of the great Indra.

sanskrit: iti madvacanaṃ śrutvā saṃśayāno'vadacchubhe / rājovāca / praṣṭumicchāmi dūta tvāṃ tanme tvaṃ vaktumarhasi //
english: Hearing my words, Oh happy damsel! the king spoke to me with reluctance and said: “I wish to ask thee something O messenger, which (I hope) thou wilt deign to answer.”

sanskrit: guṇā doṣāśca ke tatra svarge vada mamāgrataḥ / jñātvā sthitiṃ tu tatratyāṃ kariṣye'haṃ yathāruci //
english: “Tell me what good and what evils there are in heaven, that knowing them (beforehand), I may think of settling there as I may choose.”

sanskrit: dūta uvāca / svarge puṇyasya sāmagryā bhujyate paramaṃ sukham / uttamena tu puṇyena prāpnoti svargamuttamam //
english: I answered, saying:—In heaven there is ample reward for merit, conferring perfect bliss (to all); but it is the degree of meritoriousness that leads one to higher heavens.

sanskrit: madhyamena tathā madhyaḥ svargo bhavati nānyathā / kaniṣṭhena tu puṇyena svargo bhavati tādṛśaḥ //
english: By moderate virtue, one is certainly entitled to a middle station, and virtue of an inferior order, leads a person to a lower position.

sanskrit: parotkarṣāsahiṣṇutvaṃ spardhā caiva samaiśca taiḥ / kaniṣṭheṣu ca saṃtoṣo yāvatpuṇyakṣayo bhavet //
english: But one's virtue is destroyed by his impatience at the excellence of his betters, by his haughtiness to his equals, and by his joy at the inferiority of others.

sanskrit: kṣīṇe puṇye viśantyetaṃ martyalokaṃ ca mānavāḥ / ityādiguṇadoṣāśca svarge rājannavasthitāḥ //
english: When one's virtue is thus destroyed, he must enter the abode of mortals. These and the like are the effects of merit and demerit (with us) in heaven.

sanskrit: iti śrutvā vaco bhadre sa rājā pratyabhāṣata / rājovāca / necchāmi devadūtāhaṃ svargamīdṛgvidhaṃ phalam //
english: Hearing this, Oh good maiden, the king answered and said: “I do not, Oh divine messenger! like the heaven that is of such like conditions.”

sanskrit: ataḥ paraṃ mahograṃ ca tapaḥ kṛtvā kalevaram / tyakṣyāmyahamaśuddhaṃ hi jīrṇāṃ tvacamivoragaḥ //
english: "I will henceforth practise the most austere form of devotion, and abandon this my unhallowed human frame in the same way, as the snake abandons his time-worn-skin.

sanskrit: devadūta vimānedaṃ gṛhītvā tvaṃ yathāgataḥ / tathā gaccha mahendrasya saṃnidhau tvaṃ namo'stu te //
english: “Be thou pleased, Oh delegate of the Gods! to return with thy heavenly car to the presence of the great Indra whence thou comest, and fare thee well.”

sanskrit: devadūta uvāca / ityukto'haṃ gato bhadre śakrasyāgre nivedituma / yathāvṛttaṃ nivedyātha mahadāścaryatāṃ gataḥ //
english: The celestial emissary resumed:—Thus being bid, I went Oh goodly dame to the presence of Sakra to report the matter. Who upon my rehearsal of the matter, was struck with great wonder.

sanskrit: indra uvāca / punaḥ prāha mahendro māṃ ślakṣṇaṃ madhurayā girā / dūta gaccha punastatra taṃ rājānaṃ nayāśramam //
english: Then the great Indra again spoke to me with a sweet voice and said: “Go you my herald again to that king, and take him to the hermitage of Valmiki.”

sanskrit: vālmīkerjñātatattvasya svabodhārthaṃ virāgiṇam / saṃdeśaṃ mama vālmīkermaharṣestvaṃ nivedaya //
english: He is well acquainted with every truth, tell him my errand for the instruction of the dispassionate prince, saying:—  "

sanskrit: maharṣe tvaṃ vinītāya rājñe'smai vītarāgiṇe / nasvargamicchate tattvaṃ prabodhaya mahāmune //
english: "Oh thou great sage! remonstrate with this prince who is humble and dispassionate, and dislikes the enjoyments of heaven.

sanskrit: tena saṃsāraduḥkhārto mokṣameṣyati ca kramāt / ityuktvā devarājena preṣito'haṃ tadantike //
english: “So that this prince who is aggrieved at the miseries of the world, may gradually come to attain his emancipation.”

sanskrit: mayāgatya punastatra rājā valmīkajanmane / nivedito mahendrasya rājñā mokṣasya sādhanam //
english: I then went and explained my mission to the royal hermit, took him to the sage Valmiki (who had grown amidst the ant-hills), and to whom I delivered great Indra's charge for the king's practice (of the means) for his final liberation.

sanskrit: tato valmīkajanmāsau rājānaṃ samapṛcchata / anāmayamatiprītyā kuśalapraśnavārtayā //
english: Then the sage (named after the ant-hill in which he had grown), welcomed the King with gentle inquiries regarding his welfare.

sanskrit: rājovāca / bhagavandharmatattvajña jñātajñeya vidāṃvara / kṛtārtho'haṃ bhavaddṛṣṭyā tadeva kuśalaṃ mama //
english: The prince replied:—Oh great seer, that art informed in all the truths of religion, and art the greatest of them that know the knowable, thy very sight has given me all that I desired, and therein is all my welfare.  "

sanskrit: bhagavanpraṣṭumicchāmi tadavighnena me vada / saṃsārabandhaduḥkhārteḥ kathaṃ muñcāmi tadvada //
english: “Great sire, I wish to learn from thee how I may escape the miseries which arise from one's connection with this world, and which (I hope) thou wilt reveal to me without reserve.”

sanskrit: vālmīkiruvāca / śrṛṇu rājanpravakṣyāmi rāmāyaṇamakhaṇḍitam / śrutvāvadhārya yatnena jīvanmukto bhaviṣyasi //
english: Valmiki said:—Hear me Oh king! I will relate to you the entire Ramayana, by the hearing and understanding of which you will be saved even while in this life.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭharāmasaṃvādaṃ mokṣopāyakathāṃ śubhāma / jñātasvabhāvo rājendra vadāmi śrūyatāṃ budha //
english: Hear me Oh great and intelligent king, repeat to you the sacred conversation which took place between Rama and Vasishtha relating the way to liberation, and which I well know from my knowledge.

sanskrit: rājovāca / ko rāmaḥ kīdṛśaḥ kasya baddho vā mukta eva vā / etanme niścitaṃ brūhi jñānaṃ tattvavidāṃ vara //
english: The prince said:—“O thou best of sages, tell me precisely who and what this Rama was, what was his bondage and how he got freed from it.”

sanskrit: vālmīkiruvāca / śāpavyājavaśādeva rājaveṣadharo hariḥ / āhṛtājñānasaṃpannaḥ kiṃcijjño'sau bhavatprabhuḥ //
english: Valmiki said:—Hari was proscribed under an imprecation to take upon himself the form of a prince, with an assumed ignorance as that of a man of little understanding.

sanskrit: rājovāca / cidānandasvarūpe hi rāme caitanyavigrahe / śāpasya kāraṇaṃ brūhi kaḥ śaptā ceti me vada //
english: The prince said: “Tell me who was the author of that imprecation, and how it could befall on Rama, who was the personification of consciousness and felicity, and the very image of wisdom.”

sanskrit: vālmīkiruvāca / sanatkumāro niṣkāma avasadbrahmasadmani / vaikuṇṭhādāgato viṣṇustrailokyādhipatiḥ prabhuḥ //
english: Valmiki replied: Sanat-kumara, who was devoid of desires, had been residing at the abode of Brahma, to which Vishnu, the Lord of the three worlds, was a visitor from Vaikuntha.

sanskrit: brahmaṇā pūjitastatra salyalokanivāsibhiḥ / vinā kumāraṃ taṃ dṛṣṭrā hyuvāca prabhurīśvaraḥ //
english: The Lord God was welcomed by all the inhabitants of the Brahmaloka as well as by Brahma himself, except by Sanat-kumara who was thus beheld and addressed to by the god.

sanskrit: sanatkumāra stabdho'si niṣkāmo garvaceṣṭayā / atastvaṃ bhava kāmārtaḥ śarajanmeti nāmataḥ //
english: “Sanat-kumar, it is ignorance that makes thee forsake thy desires for fear of regeneration (on earth), therefore must thou be born under the name of Sara-janma to be troubled with desires.”

sanskrit: tenāpi śāpito viṣṇuḥ sarvajñatvaṃ tavāsti yat / kiṃcitkālaṃ hi tattyaktvā tvamajñānī bhaviṣyasi //
english: Sanat-kumara in return denounced Vishnu by saying:—“Even all discerning as thou art, thou shalt have to sacrifice thine omniscience for some time, and pass as an ignorant mortal (on earth).”

sanskrit: bhṛgurbhāryāṃ hatāṃ dṛṣṭrā hyuvāca krodhamūrcchitaḥ / viṣṇo tavāpi bhāryāyā viyogo hi bhaviṣyati //
english: There was another anathema pronounced upon Vishnu by the sage Bhrigu, who seeing his wife killed (by him), became incensed with anger and said: “Vishnu thou shalt have also to be bereft of thy wife.”

sanskrit: vṛndayā śāpito viṣṇuśchalanaṃ yattvayā kṛtam / atastvaṃ strīviyogaṃ tu vacanānmama yāsyasi //
english: He was again cursed by Vrinda to be deprived of his wife, on account of his beguiling her.

sanskrit: bhāryā hi devadattasya payoṣṇītīrasa~sthitā / nṛsiṃhaveṣadhṛgviṣṇuṃ dṛṣṭvā pañcatvamāgatā //
english: Again when the pregnant wife of Deva-datta was killed (with fear) on seeing the man-lion figure of Vishnu;

sanskrit: tena śapto hi nṛharirduḥkhārtaḥ strīviyogataḥ / tavāpi bhāryayā sārdhaṃ viyogo hi bhaviṣyati //
english: The leonine Hari was denounced by the husband, who was sorely afflicted at the loss of his consort, to be thus separated from his wife also.

sanskrit: bhṛguṇaivaṃ kumāreṇa śāpito devaśarmaṇā / vṛndayā śāpito viṣṇustena mānuṣyatāṃ gataḥ //
english: Thus denounced by Bhrigu, by Sanat-kumara, Deva-datta and Vrinda, he was obliged (to be born in this earth) in the figure of a human being.

sanskrit: etatte kathitaṃ sarve śāpavyājasya kāraṇam / idānīṃ vacmi tatsarve sāvadhānamatiḥ śṛṇu //
english: I have thus explained to you the causes of all the imprecations (which were passed on Vishnu), and will now relate to you all other things which you shall have carefully to attend to.

sanskrit: divi bhūmau tathākāśe bahirantaśca me vibhuḥ / yo vibhātyavabhāsātmā tasmai sarvātmane namaḥ //
english: Salutation to the Lord, the universal soul, shining manifest in heaven, earth and the sky, and both within and without myself.

sanskrit: vālmīkiruvāca / ahaṃ baddho vimuktaḥ syāmiti yasyāsti niścayaḥ / nātyantamajño nota jñaḥ so'smiñchāstre'dhikāravān //
english: One convinced of his constraint (in this mortal world), and desiring his liberation from it, and, who is neither wholly ignorant of, nor quite conversant with divine knowledge, is entitled to (the perusal of) this work.

sanskrit: kathopāyānvicāryādau mokṣopāyānimānatha / yo vicārayati prājño na sa bhūyo'bhijāyate //
english: The wise man, who having well considered the narrative (of Rama) as the first step, comes afterwards to think on the means of liberation (as are expounded herein), he shall verily be exempt from transmigration.

sanskrit: asminrāmāyaṇe rāmakathopāyānmahābalān / etāṃstu prathamaṃ kṛtvā purāhamarimardana //
english: Know, O destroyer of thy enemies! that I have first embodied the history of Rama in this Ramayana.

sanskrit: śiṣyāyāsmi vinītāya bharadvājāya dhīmate / ekāgro dattavāṃstasmai maṇimabdhirivārthine //
english: And I have given the same to my attentive pupil the obedient and intelligent Bharadwaja, as the sea yields his gems to their seeker.

sanskrit: tata ete kathopāyā bharadvājena dhīmatā / kasmiṃścinmerugahane brahmaṇo'gra udāhṛtāḥ //
english: These historical preparatories were rehearsed by the learned Bharadwaja in the presence of Brahma, seated in a certain forest of the Sumeru Mountain.

sanskrit: athāsya tuṣṭo bhagavānbrahmā lokapitāmahaḥ / varaṃ putra gṛhāṇeti tamuvāca mahāśayaḥ //
english: "Then the lord Brahma, the great grandfather of the inhabitants (of the three worlds), was so highly pleased with him that he addressed him saying: ""Oh my son! ask the best boon that thou wishest for.""  "

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca / bhagavanbhūtabhavyeśa varo'yaṃ me'dya rocate / yeneyaṃ janatā duḥkhānmucyate tadudāhara //
english: "Bharadwaja said:—""Oh thou lord, that art master of the past and future times, grant me the desired boon of communicating to me the means whereby people are liberated from their miseries.""  "

sanskrit: śrībrahmovāca / guruṃ vālmīkimatrāśu prārthayasva prayatnataḥ / tenedaṃ yatsamārabdhaṃ rāmāyaṇamaninditam //
english: "Brahma said:—""Go ask diligently of thy preceptor Valmiki, to complete the faultless Ramayana that he has undertaken.  "

sanskrit: tasmiñchrute naro mohātsamagrātsaṃtariṣyati / setunevāmbudheḥ pāramapāraguṇaśālinā //
english: By the hearing of which men will get over their manifold errors, in the same manner as they pass over the sea by the bridge built over it by the great Rama, who was fraught with all good qualities.

sanskrit: śrīvālmīkiruvāca / ityuktvā sa bharadvājaṃ parameṣṭhī madāśramam / abhyāgacchatsamaṃ tena bharadvājena bhūtakṛt //
english: Valmiki said:—Saying this to Bharadwaja, the supreme maker of all beings (Brahma) accompanied him to my hermitage.

sanskrit: tūrṇaṃ saṃpūjito devaḥ so'rghyapādyādinā mayā / avocanmāṃ mahāsattvaḥ sarvabhūtahite rataḥ //
english: In right earnest was the god welcomed by me with the argha and offerings of water and the like, when the lord of truth spoke to me for the good of all creatures.

sanskrit: rāmasvabhāvakathanādasmādvaramune tvayā / nodvegātsa parityājya āsamāpteraninditāt //
english: "Brahma spake to me saying said:—""Do not Oh sage! give up your undertaking until its final completion. No pains ought to be spared to make the history of Rama as faultless as it ought to be.  "

sanskrit: granthenānena loko'yamasmātsaṃsārasaṃkaṭāt / samuttariṣyati kṣipraṃ potenevāśu sāgarāt //
english: By this work of yours men will forthwith pass over this hazardous world, in the same manner as one crosses the sea in a vessel.

sanskrit: vaktuṃ tadevamevārthamahamāgatavānayam / kuru lokahitārthaṃ tvaṃ śāstramityuktavānajaḥ //
english: "Again said the increate brahma to me said:—""I come to tell this very thing to you, that you complete the work for the benefit of mankind.""  "

sanskrit: mama puṇyāśramāttasmātkṣaṇādantarddhimāgataḥ / muhūrtābhyutthitaḥ proccaistaraṅga iva vāriṇaḥ //
english: Then Oh king, the God disappeared from my sacred hermitage in a moment, just as the wave subsides in the water no sooner it has heaved itself.

sanskrit: tasminprayāte bhagavatyahaṃ vismayamāgataḥ / punastatra bharadvājamapṛcchaṃ svasthayā dhiyā //
english: I was struck with wonder at the disappearance of that (deity), and then being composed in my mind, I inquired of Bharadwaja, saying:—

sanskrit: kimetadbrahmaṇā proktaṃ bharadvāja vadāśu me / ityuktena punaḥ proktaṃ bharadvājena tena me //
english: Tell me, Bharadwaja, what Brahma spoke (to me) in the hermitage; to which he answered saying:—

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca / etaduktaṃ bhagavatā yathā rāmāyaṇaṃ kuru / sarvalokahitārthāya saṃsārārṇavatārakam //
english: The God commanded you to complete the Ramayana for the good of men, and as a means of their crossing over the gulf of the world.

sanskrit: mahyaṃ ca bhagavanbrūhi kathaṃ saṃsārasaṃkaṭe / rāmo vyavahṛto hyasminbharataśca mahāmanāḥ //
english: "Now Sir said Bharadwaja, ""explain to me how the great minded Rama and Bharata conducted themselves amidst the troubles of this world.  "

sanskrit: śatrughno lakṣmaṇaścāpi sītā cāpi yaśasvinī / rāmānuyāyinaste vā mantriputrā mahādhiyaḥ //
english: "Tell me also how did Satrughna, Lakshmana, and the renowned Sita, and all those who followed Rama, as also the ministers and their highly intelligent sons, conduct themselves.

sanskrit: nirduḥkhitāṃ yathaite nu prāptāstadbrūhi me sphuṭam / tathaivāhaṃ bhaviṣyāmi tato janatayā saha //
english: Tell me clearly how they escaped all its miseries, that I may do the same with the rest of mankind: (for our salvation).""  "

sanskrit: bharadvājena rājendra vadetyukto'smi sādaram / tadā kartuṃ vibhorājñāmahaṃ vaktuṃ pravṛttavān //
english: Being thus respectfully addressed by Bharadwaja, I was led, Oh great King! to carry out the behest of my lord (Brahma), and to narrate the Ramayana to him; saying:—

sanskrit: śṛṇu vatsa bharadvāja yathāpṛṣṭaṃ vadāmi te / śrutena yena saṃmohamalaṃ dūre kariṣyasi //
english: Hear my son Bharadwaja, I will tell you all that you have asked, and by the hearing of which you shall be enabled to cast away the dross of errors.

sanskrit: tathā vyavahara prājña yathā vyavahṛtaḥ sukhī / sarvāsaṃsaktayā buddhyā rāmo rājīvalocanaḥ //
english: You are wise and have to manage yourself in the manner of the felicitous and lotus-eyed Rama, with a mind free from (worldly) attachments,

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇo bharataścaiva śatrughnaśca mahāmanāḥ / kausalyā ca sumitrā ca sītā daśarathastathā //
english: (Know that) Lakshmana, Bharata, the great minded Satrughna, Kausalya, Sita, Sumitra as well as Dasaratha;—

sanskrit: kṛtāstraścā'virodhaśca bodhapāramupāgatāḥ / vasiṣṭho vāmadevaśca mantriṇo'ṣṭau tathetare //
english: With Kritastra and the two friends of Rama, and Vasishtha and Vamadeva, and the eight ministers of state as well as many others, had reached the summit of knowledge.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭirjayanto bhāsaśca satyo vijaya eva ca / vibhīṣaṇaḥ suṣeṇaśca hanumānindrajittathā //
english: Their names are Dhrishta, Jayanta, Bhasa, Satya, Vijaya, Vibishanah, Sushena and Hanumana. And also Indrajita.

sanskrit: ete'ṣṭau mantriṇaḥ proktāḥ samanīrāgacetasaḥ / jīvanmuktā mahātmāno yathāprāptānuvartinaḥ //
english: These were the eight ministers of Rama, who are said to have been equally dispassionate in their minds, and content with what was their lot. They were great souls, and free in their lives.

sanskrit: etairyathā hutaṃ dattaṃ gṛhītamuṣitaṃ smṛtam / tathā cedvartase putra mukta evāsi saṃkaṭāt //
english: Well my son, if you follow the manner in which these men observed sacrificial rites, gave and received their offerings, and how they lived and thought, you are at once freed from the turmoils.

sanskrit: apārasaṃsārasamudrapātī labdhvā parāṃ yuktimudārasattvaḥ / na śokamāyāti na dainyameti gatajvarastiṣṭhati nityatṛptaḥ //
english: One fallen in this boundless ocean of the world, may enjoy (the bliss of) liberation by the magnanimity of his soul. He shall not come across grief or destitution, but remain ever satisfied by being freed from the fever of anxiety.

sanskrit: bharadvāja uvāca / jīvanmuktasthitiṃ vrahmankṛtvā rāghavamāditaḥ / kramātkathaya me nityaṃ bhaviṣyāmi sukhī yathā //
english: Bharadwaja said, O Brahman! relate to me first about Rama, and then enlighten me by degrees with the conditions of attaining liberation in this life, that I may be happy for ever.

sanskrit: śrīvālmīkiruvāca / bhramasya jāgatasyāsya jātasyākāśavarṇavat / apunaḥsmaraṇaṃ manye sādho vismaraṇaṃ varam //
english: "Valmiki replied:—""Know, holy Saint! all worldly conceptions to be as erroneous as the various hues that taint the clear firmament. It is better therefore to efface them in oblivion, rather than revive their reminiscence.  "

sanskrit: dṛśyātyantābhāvabodhaṃ vinā tannānubhūyate / kadācitkenacinnāma svabodho'nviṣyatāmataḥ //
english: All visible objects are absolute negation; we have no idea of them save from sensation. Inquire into these apprehensions, and you will never find them as real.

sanskrit: sa ceha saṃbhavatyeva tadarthamidamātatam / śāstramākarṇayasi cettattvamāpsyasi nānyathā //
english: It is possible here (on earth) to attain to this knowledge (of worldly vanities) which is fully expounded herein: if you will listen to it attentively, you shall get at the truth and not otherwise.

sanskrit: jagadbhramo'yaṃ dṛśyo'pi nāstyevetyanubhūyate / varṇo vyomna ivākhedādvicāreṇāmunā'nagha //
english: The conception of this world is a mistake, and though we actually see it, it is never in existence. It appears in the same light, O sinless saint, as the variegated colours in the sky.

sanskrit: dṛśyaṃ nāstīti bodhena manaso dṛśyamārjanam / saṃpannaṃ cettadutpannā parā nirvāṇanirvṛtiḥ //
english: The conviction of the non-existence of the objects of vision, leads to efface their impressions from the mind. Thus perfected, there springs in it the supreme and eternal bliss of self-extinction.

sanskrit: anyathā śāstragarteṣu luṭhatāṃ bhavatāmiha / bhavatyakṛtrimājñānāṃ kalpairapi na nirvṛtiḥ //
english: Otherwise there is no quietism to be had herein by men like you, rolling in the depths of science for thousands of years and unacquainted with the true knowledge.

sanskrit: aśeṣeṇa parityāgo vāsanānāṃ ya uttamaḥ / mokṣaṃ ityucyate brahmansa eva vimalakramaḥ //
english: Complete abandonment of desires, styled as the best state of liberation, is the only pure step towards beatitude.

sanskrit: kṣīṇāyāṃ vāsanāyāṃ tu ceto galati satvaram / kṣīṇāyāṃ śītasaṃtatyāṃ brahmanhimakaṇo yathā //
english: The absence of desires leads to the extinction of mental actions, in the same manner as the absence of cold conduces to the dissolution of small particles of ice.

sanskrit: ayaṃ vāsanayā deho dhriyate bhūtapañjaraḥ / tanunāntarniviṣṭena muktaughastantunā yathā //
english: Our desires which uphold our living bodies (and minds), bind us fast as by strings to our bodily prison. These being loosened, the inward soul is liberated.

sanskrit: vāsanā dvividhā proktā śuddhā ca malinā tathā / malinā janmano hetuḥ śuddhā janmavināśinī //
english: Desires are of two kinds, pure and impure. The impure ones are the cause of transmigration, while the pure ones serve to destroy it.

sanskrit: ajñānasughanākārā ghanāhaṃkāraśālinī / punarjanmakarī proktā malinā vāsanā budhaiḥ //
english: An impure desire is of the form of a mist of ignorance, consisting in the feeling of an obdurate egoism. This is said by the wise to be the cause of birth.

sanskrit: punarjanmāṅkuraṃ tyaktvā sthitā saṃbhṛṣṭabījavat / dehārthaṃ dhriyate jñātajñeyā śuddheti cocyate //
english: A pure desire is like a parched seed incapable to bring forth the germ of transmigration, and only supports the present body.

sanskrit: apunarjanmakaraṇī jīvanmukteṣu dehiṣu / vāsanā vidyate śuddhā dehe cakra iva bhramaḥ //
english: The pure desires which are unattended with transmigration, reside in the bodies of living-liberated men, like unmoving wheels.

sanskrit: ye śuddhavāsanā bhūyo na janmānarthabhājanam / jñātajñeyāsta ucyante jīvanmuktā mahādhiyaḥ //
english: Those that have the pure desires are not liable to transmigration, and are said to be knowing in all things that ought to be known. These are called the living-liberated and are of superior intelligence.

sanskrit: jīvanmuktipadaṃ prāpto yathā rāmo mahāmatiḥ / tatte'haṃ śṛṇu vakṣyābhi jarāmaraṇaśāntaye //
english: I will explain to you how the high minded Rama attained the state of liberation in life, hear you this that old age and death may not come upon you.

sanskrit: bharadvāja mahābuddhe rāmakramamimaṃ śubham / śṛṇu vakṣyāmi tenaiva sarvaṃ jñāsyasi sarvadā //
english: Hear Oh highly intelligent Bharadawaja, the auspicious course and conduct of Rama's life: whereby you shall be enabled to understand everything at all times.

sanskrit: vidyāgṛhādviniṣkramya rāmo rājīvalocanaḥ / divasānyanayadgehe līlābhirakutobhayaḥ //
english: The lotus-eyed Rama after coming out of his school, remained for many days at home in his diversions, and without anything to fear.

sanskrit: atha gacchati kāle tu pālayatyavaniṃ nṛpe / prajāsu vītaśokāsu sthitāsu vigatajvaram //
english: In the course of time as he took the reins of the Government, (in his hand), his people enjoyed all the bliss that absence of grief and diseases could impart.

sanskrit: tīrthapuṇyāśramaśreṇīrdraṣṭumutkaṇṭhitaṃ manaḥ / rāmasyābhūdbhṛśaṃ tatra kadācidguṇaśālinaḥ //
english: At one time Rama's mind virtuous as he was, became anxious to see the different places of pilgrimage, the cities and hermitages.

sanskrit: rāghavaścintayitvaivamupetya caraṇau pituḥ / haṃsaḥ padmāviva navau jagrāha nakhakesarau //
english: So Raghava with this view, approached his father's feet, he touched the nails (of his toes) as a swan lays hold on the buds of lotus.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / tīrthāni devasadmāni vanānyāyatanāni ca / draṣṭumutkaṇṭhitaṃ tāta mamedaṃ nātha mānasam //
english: "Oh my father he said, ""my mind is desirous to see the different places of pilgrimage, temples of gods, forests and abodes.  "

sanskrit: tadetāmarthitāṃ pūrvāṃ saphalāṃ kartumarhasi / na so'sti bhuvane nātha tvayā yo'rthī na mānitaḥ //
english: Grant me my lord this my petition, as there is no petitioner of thine on earth whom didst thou ever dishonor.

sanskrit: iti saṃprārthito rājā vasiṣṭhena samaṃ tadā / vicāryāmuñcadevainaṃ rāmaṃ prathamamarthinam //
english: Thus solicited (by Rama), the king consulted with Vasishtha, and after much reflection granted him the first request he ever made.

sanskrit: śubhe nakṣatradivase bhrātṛbhyāṃ saha rāghavaḥ / maṅgalālaṃkṛtavapuḥ kṛtasvastyayano dvijaiḥ //
english: On a day of lucky stars Rama set out (on his journey) with his two brothers (Lakshmana and Satrughna), having his body adorned with auspicious marks, and (receiving the) benedictions which were pronounced on him by the priests.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhaprahitairvipraiḥ śāstrajñaiśca samanvitaḥ / snigdhaiḥ katipayaireva rājaputravaraiḥ saha //
english: Accompanied also by a body of learned Brahmans whom Vasishtha had chosen on the occasion, and a select party of his associate princes;

sanskrit: ambābhirvihitāśībhirāliṅgyāliṅgya bhūṣitaḥ / niragātsvagṛhāttasmāttīrthayātrārthamudyataḥ //
english: He started from home towards his pilgrimage after he received the benedictions and embraces of his mothers.

sanskrit: nirgataḥ svapurātpauraistūryaghoṣeṇa vāditaḥ / pīyamānaḥ purastrīṇāṃ netrairbhṛṅgaughabhaṅguraiḥ //
english: As he went out of his city, the citizens welcomed him with the sounds of trumpets, while the bee-like fickle eyes of the city ladies were fixed upon his lotus like face.

sanskrit: grāmīṇalalanālolahastapadmāpanoditaiḥ / lājavarṣairvikīrṇātmā himairiva himācalaḥ //
english: He was bestrewn with handfuls of fried paddy thrown over his body by the beautiful hands of village-women, that made him appear like the Himalaya covered over with snow.

sanskrit: āvarjayanvipragaṇānpariśṛṇvanprajāśiṣaḥ / ālokayandigantāṃśca paricakrāma jāṅgalān //
english: He dismissed the Brahmans with honor, and went on hearing the benedictions of the people, and taking a full view of the landscape around him until he proceeded towards the forest.

sanskrit: athārabhya svakāttasmātkramātkośalamaṇḍalāt / snānadānatapodhyānapūrvakaṃ sa dadarśa ha //
english: He went on distributing alms after making his holy ablutions and performing his devotion and meditation, as he gradually passed the limits of Kosala after starting from his palace.

sanskrit: nadītīrāṇi puṇyāni vanānyāyatanāni ca / jaṅgalāni janānteṣu taṭānyabdhimahībhṛtām //
english: He went about seeing the many rivers and their banks, visiting the shrines of gods, sacred forests and deserts far and remote from the resorts of men, as also the hills, seas and their shores.

sanskrit: mandākinīmindunibhāṃ kālindīṃ cotpalāmalām / sarasvatīṃ śatadrūṃ ca candrabhāgāmirāvatīm //
english: He saw the Mandakini bright as the moon, the Kalindi, clear as the lotus, and also the following rivers, Sarasvati, Satadru, Chandrabhaga and Iravati.

sanskrit: veṇīṃ ca kṛṣṇaveṇīṃ ca nirvindhyāṃ sarayūṃ tathā / carmaṇvatīṃ vitastāṃ ca vipāśāṃ bāhudāmapi //
english: Also Veni, Krishnaveni, Nirvindhya, Saraju, Charmanvati, Vitasta, Vipasa and Bahudaka.

sanskrit: prayāgaṃ naimiṣaṃ caiva dharmāraṇyaṃ gayāṃ tathā / vārāṇasīṃ śrīgiriṃ ca kedāraṃ puṣkaraṃ tathā //
english: He saw also the (holy places of) Prayaga, the Naimisha, the Dharmaranya, Gya, Varanasi, Srigiri, Kedara and Pushkara.

sanskrit: mānasaṃ ca kramasarastathaivottaramānasam / vaḍavāvadanaṃ caiva tīrthavṛndaṃ sa sādaram //
english: He saw the Manasa and the northern Mansaravara lakes, and many fiery lakes and springs, the Bada, the Vindhya range and the sea.

sanskrit: agnitīrthaṃ mahātīrthamindradyumnasarastathā / sarāṃsi saritaścaiva tathā nadahradāvalīm //
english: He saw the fiery pool of Jwalamukhi, the great shrine of Jagannatha, the fountain of Indradumna and many other reservoirs, rivers and lakes.

sanskrit: svāminaṃ kārtikeyaṃ ca śālagrāmaṃ hariṃ tathā / sthānāni ca catuḥṣaṣṭiṃ hareratha harasya ca //
english: He visited the shrine of Kartikeya and the Gandak river of Salagramas, and also the sixty four shrines sacred to Hari and Hara.

sanskrit: nānāścaryavicitrāṇi caturabdhitaṭāni ca / vindhyamandarakuñjāṃśca kulaśailasthalāni ca //
english: He saw various wonders, the coasts of the four seas, the Vindhya range, the groves of Hara, and the boundary hills and level lands.

sanskrit: rājarṣīṇāṃ ca mahatāṃ brahmarṣīṇāṃ tathaiva ca / devānāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ ce pāvanānāśramāñchubhān //
english: He visited the places of the great Rajarshis and the Brahmarshis, and went wherever there was any auspicious sanctuary of the gods and Brahmans.

sanskrit: bhūyobhūyaḥ sa babhrāma bhrātṛbhyāṃ saha mānadaḥ / caturṣvapi diganteṣu sarvāneva mahītaṭān //
english: Thus they all honouring Rama, travelled far and wide in company with his two brothers, and traversed all the four quarters on the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: amarakinnaramānavamānitaḥ samavalokya mahīmakhilāmimām / upayayau svagṛhaṃ raghunandano vihṛtadik śivalokamiveśvaraḥ //
english: Honoured by the gods, Kinnaras and by men, and having seen all the places on earth, the descendant of Raghu returned home, like Siva when he returns to the Sivaloka.

sanskrit: śrīvālmīkiruvāca / rāmaḥ puṣpāñjalivrātairvikīrṇaḥ puravāsibhiḥ / praviveśa gṛhaṃ śrīmāñjayanto viṣṭapaṃ yathā //
english: Rama strewn over with handfuls of flowers by the citizens (surrounding him) entered the palace, as when the beauteous Jayanta (son of Indra) enters his celestial abode.

sanskrit: praṇanāmātha pitaraṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ bhrātṛbāndhavān / brāhmaṇānkulavṛddhāṃśca rāghavaḥ prathamāgataḥ //
english: On his first arrival he bent himself in reverence before his father, before Vasishtha, before his brothers, his friends, the Brahmanas and the elderly members of the family.

sanskrit: suhṛdbhirbhrātṛbhiścaiva pitrā dvijagaṇena ca / muhurāliṅgitācāro rāghavo na mamau mudā //
english: Repeatedly embraced as he was by friends, by his father, mothers and by the Brahmanas, the son of Raghu bowed down his head to them with joy.

sanskrit: tasmingṛhe dāśaratheḥ priyaprakathanairmithaḥ / jughūrṇurmadhurairāśā mṛduvaṃśastanairiva //
english: The assembled people after their familiar conversation with Rama in the palace, strolled about on all sides highly delighted with his speech, resembling the music of a flute.

sanskrit: babhūvātha dinānyaṣṭau rāmāgamana utsavaḥ / sukhaṃ mattajanonmuktakalakolāhalākulaḥ //
english: Thus eight days were passed in festive mirth consequent to the arrival of Rama, and shouts of joy were sent forth by the elated multitude.

sanskrit: uvāsa sa sukhaṃ gehe tataḥ prabhṛti rāghavaḥ / varṇayanvividhākārāndeśācārānitastataḥ //
english: Thenceforth Raghava continued to dwell happily at home, with relating to his friends, the different customs and manners of the countries (he visited) on all sides.

sanskrit: prātarutthāya rāmo'sau kṛtvā saṃdhyāṃ yathāvidhi / sabhāsaṃsthaṃ dadarśendrasamaṃ svapitaraṃ tathā //
english: He rose early in the morning and performed his morning service according to law. He then visited his father seated as Indra in his Council.

sanskrit: kathābhiḥ suvicitrābhiḥ sa vasiṣṭhādibhiḥ saha / sthitvā dinacaturbhāgaṃ jñānagarbhābhirādṛtaḥ //
english: He next passed a fourth part of the day in company with Vasishtha and other sages, and was greatly edified by their conversations which were full of instruction.

sanskrit: jagāma pitrānujñāto mahatyā senayāvṛtaḥ / varāhamahiṣākīrṇaṃ vanamākheṭakecchayā //
english: He used also to go out for sport under orders of his father; and surrounded by a large number of troops, to forests full of (wild) boars and buffaloes.

sanskrit: tata āgatya sadane kṛtvā snānādikaṃ kramam / samitrabāndhavo bhuktvā nināya sasuhṛnniśām //
english: Then after returning home and performing his bath and other rites with his friends, he took his meal with them, and passed the night in company with his beloved companions.

sanskrit: evaṃprāyadinācāro bhrātṛbhyāṃ saha rāghavaḥ / āgatya tīrthayātrāyāḥ samuvāsa piturgṛhe //
english: In these and similar practices did he pass his days with his brothers at his father's house, after his return from the pilgrimage.

sanskrit: nṛpatisaṃvyavahāramanojñayā sujanacetasi candrikayānayā / parinināya dināni sa ceṣṭayā stutasudhārasapeśalayā'nagha //
english: Oh sinless (Bharadwaja), with his conduct becoming a prince, Rama passed his days with giving delight to the good men that surrounded him, in the manner of the moon that gladdens mankind with his soothing ambrosial beams.

sanskrit: śrīvālmīkiruvāca / athonaṣoḍaśe varṣe vartamāne raghūdvahe / rāmānuyāyini tathā śatrughne lakṣmaṇe'pi ca //
english: Valmiki said:—Afterwards Rama attained the fifteenth year of his age, and so also Satrughna and Lakshmana who followed Rama (in birth), attained also the same age.

sanskrit: bharate saṃsthite nityaṃ mātāmahagṛhe sukham / pālayatyavaniṃ rājñi yathāvadakhilābhimām //
english: Bharata continued to dwell with joy at the house of his maternal grandfather, and the king (Dasaratha) ruled the whole earth as usual.

sanskrit: janyatrārthaṃ ca putrāṇāṃ pratyahaṃ saha mantribhiḥ / kṛtamantre mahāprājñe tajjñe daśarathe nṛpe //
english: The most wise king Dasaratha (now) consulted his ministers day after day about the marriage of his sons.

sanskrit: kṛtāyāṃ tīrthayātrāyāṃ rāmo nijagṛhe sthitaḥ / jagāmānudinaṃ kārśyaṃ śaradīvāmalaṃ saraḥ //
english: But as Rama remained at home since his return from pilgrimage, he began to decay day by day as the translucent lake in autumn.

sanskrit: kumārasya viśālākṣaṃ pāṇḍutāṃ mukhamādade / pākaphulladalaṃ śuklaṃ sālimālamivāmbujam //
english: His blooming face with its out-stretched eyes, assumed by degrees a paleness like that of the withering petals of the white lotus beset by a swarm of bees.

sanskrit: kapolatalasaṃlīnapāṇiḥ padmāsanasthitaḥ / cintāparavaśastūṣṇīmavyāpāro babhūva ha //
english: He sat silent and motionless in the posture of his folded legs (Padmasana), and remained absorbed in thought with his palm placed under his cheek and neck.

sanskrit: kṛśāṅgaścintayā yuktaḥ khedī paramadurmanāḥ / novāca kasyacitkiṃcillipikarmārpitopamaḥ //
english: Being emaciated in person, and growing thoughtful, sad and distracted in his mind, he remained speechless as a mute picture in painting.

sanskrit: khedātparijanenāsau prārthyamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ / cakārāhnikamācāraṃ parimlānamukhāmbujaḥ //
english: On being repeatedly requested by the anxious inmates of the family to perform his daily rites, he discharged them with a melancholy countenance,

sanskrit: evaṃguṇaviśiṣṭaṃ taṃ rāmaṃ guṇagaṇākaram / ālokya bhrātarāvasya tāmevāyayaturdaśām //
english: Seeing the accomplished rama said:—the mine of merits in such a plight, all his brothers likewise were reduced to the same condition with him.

sanskrit: tathā teṣu tanūjeṣu khedavatsu kṛśeṣu ca / sapatnīko mahīpālaścintāvivaśatāṃ yayau //
english: The king of the earth observing all his three sons thus dejected and lean, gave way to anxiety together with all his queens.

sanskrit: kā te putra ghanā cintetyevaṃ rāmaṃ punaḥ punaḥ / apṛcchatsnigdhayā vācā naivākathayadasya saḥ //
english: Dasaratha asked Rama repeatedly and in a gentle voice (to tell him) what his anxiety was, and what was the cause of his thoughtfulness; but he returned no answer to it.

sanskrit: na kiṃcittāta me duḥkhamityuktvā pituraṅkagaḥ / rāmo rājīvapatrākṣastūṣṇīmeva sma tiṣṭhati //
english: Then being taken up in his father's lap, the lotus-eyed Rama replied, that he had no anxiety whatever, and held his silence.

sanskrit: tato daśaratho rājā rāmaḥ kiṃ khedavāniti / apṛcchatsarvakāryajñaṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ vadatāṃ varam //
english: Afterwards the king Dasaratha asked Vasishtha, the best of speakers and well informed in all matters, as to the cause why Rama was so sorrowful.

sanskrit: ityuktaścintayitvā sa vasiṣṭhamuninā nṛpaḥ / astyatra kāraṇaṃ śrīmanmā rājanduḥkhamastu te //
english: "The sage Vasishtha thought over the matter (for a while), and then said, ""there is Oh king! a cause of Rama's sadness, but you need not be anxious about it.  "

sanskrit: kopaṃ viṣādakalanāṃ vitataṃ ca harṣaṃ nālpena kāraṇavaśena vahanti santaḥ / sargeṇa saṃhṛtijavena vinā jagatyāṃ bhūtāni bhūpa na mahānti vikāravanti //
english: Wise men Oh king! never entertain the fluctuations of anger or grief, or a lengthened delight from frivolous causes, just as the great elements of the world do not change their states (of inertness) unless it were for the sake of (some new) production.

sanskrit: śrīvālmīkiruvāca / ityukte munināthena saṃdehavati pārthive / khedavatyāsthite maunaṃ kiṃcitkālapratīkṣaṇe //
english: The king was thrown into sorrow and suspense at these words of the prince of sages (Vasishtha); but kept his silence for sometime, and waited.

sanskrit: parikhinnāsu sarvāsu rājñīṣu nṛpasadmasu / sthitāsu sāvadhānāsu rāmaceṣṭāsu sarvataḥ //
english: (Meanwhile) the queens of the palace, kept themselves watchful of the movements of Rama with anxious carefulness.

sanskrit: etasminneva kāle tu viśvāmitra iti śrutaḥ / maharṣirabhyagāddraṣṭuṃ tamayodhyānarādhipam //
english: At this very time the famous Viswamitra, the great sage came to visit the king of men at Ayodhya.

sanskrit: tasya yajño'tha rakṣobhistathā vilulupe kila / māyāvīryabalonmattairdharmakāryasya dhīmataḥ //
english: The intelligent and wise seer had his sacrificial rites disturbed by the Rakshasas, who were deceitfully powerful and giddy with their strength.

sanskrit: rakṣārthaṃ tasya yajñasya draṣṭumaicchatsa pārthivam / nahi śaknotyavighnena samāptuṃ sa muniḥ kratum //
english: It was for the security of his sacrifice that the sage waited on the king, because he was unable to accomplish it in peace.

sanskrit: tatasteṣāṃ vināśārthamudyatastapasāṃ nithiḥ / viśvāmitro mahātejā ayodhyāmabhyagātpurīm //
english: It was also for the purpose of their destruction, that the illustrious Viswamitra, who was the gem of austere devotion had come to the city of Ayodhya.

sanskrit: sa rājño darśanākāṅkṣī dvārādhyakṣānuvāca ha / śīghramākhyāta māṃ prāptaṃ kauśikaṃ gādhinaḥ sutam //
english: Desirous of seeing the king, he spoke to the guards at the gate, to report the arrival of Kausika the son of Gadhi to the king with despatch.

sanskrit: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā dvāsthā rājagṛhaṃ yayuḥ / saṃbhrāntamanasaḥ sarve tena vākyena coditāḥ //
english: On hearing these words, the guards were struck with fear in their minds, and ran as they were bid to the palace of the king.

sanskrit: te gatvā rājasadanaṃ viśvāmitramṛṣiṃ tataḥ / prāptamāvedayāmāsuḥ pratīhārāḥ patestadā //
english: Coming to the Royal abode, the door-keepers informed the chief-warder of the arrival of Viswamitra the royal sage.

sanskrit: athāsthānagataṃ bhūpaṃ rājamaṇḍalamālinam / samupetya tvarāyukto yāṣṭīko'sau vyajijñapat //
english: The staff-bearer immediately proceeded to the presence of the king, seated among the princes and chiefs (under him) in the Court house, and gave his report saying:—

sanskrit: deva dvāri mahātejā bālabhāskarabhāsuraḥ / jvālāruṇajaṭājūṭaḥ pumāñchrīmānavasthitaḥ //
english: "Please your majestic, there is waiting at the door a mighty personage of majestic appearance, bright as the morning sun, with his pendant locks of hair (red and ruddy) as sunbeams.

sanskrit: sabhāsurapatākāntaṃ sāśvebhapuruṣāyudham / kṛtavāṃstaṃ pradeśaṃ yastejobhiḥ kīrṇakāñcanam //
english: The brilliancy of his person has brightened the place from the top-most flag down to the ground, and made the horses, men and armory shine as with a golden hue.

sanskrit: vīkṣyamāṇe tu yāṣṭīke nivedayati rājani / viśvāmitro muniḥ prāpta ityanuddhatayā girā //
english: No sooner had the warder appeared (before the king), and with hurried words announced the arrival of the sage Viswamitra:

sanskrit: iti yāṣṭīkavacanamākarṇya nṛpasattamaḥ / sa samantrī sasāmantaḥ prottasthau hemaviṣṭarāt //
english: Than the best of kings as he heard the herald say so, rose at once from his throne of gold with all the ministers and chiefs that surrounded him.

sanskrit: padātireva sahasā rājñāṃ vṛndena mālitaḥ / vasiṣṭhavāmadevābhyāṃ saha sāmantasaṃstutaḥ //
english: He walked immediately on foot with the staff of princes and chiefs by whom he was held in honour and regard, and in company with Vasishtha and Vamadeva.

sanskrit: jagāma tatra yatrāsau viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ / dadarśa muniśārdūlaṃ dvārabhūmāvavasthitam //
english: He went to the spot where the great sage was waiting, and saw Viswamitra the chief of sages standing at the gateway.

sanskrit: kenāpi kāraṇenorvītalamarkamupāgatam / brāhmeṇa tejasākrāntaṃ kṣātreṇa ca mahaujasā //
english: His priestly prowess joined with his military valour, made him appear as the sun descended on earth on some account.

sanskrit: jarājaraṭhayā nityaṃ tapaḥprasararūkṣayā / jaṭāvalyā vṛtaskandhaṃ sasaṃdhyābhramivācalam //
english: He was hoary with old age, rough-skinned by the practice of austerities, and covered down to his shoulders by red-bright braids of hair, resembling the evening clouds over topping a mountain brow.

sanskrit: upaśāntaṃ ca kāntaṃ ca dīptamapratighāti ca / nibhṛtaṃ corjitākāraṃ dadhānaṃ bhāsvaraṃ vapuḥ //
english: He was mild looking and engaging in his appearance, but at the same time as brilliant as the orb of the sun. He was neither assuming nor repulsive, but possessed of an ineffable gravity and majesty in his person.

sanskrit: peśalenātibhīmena prasannenākulena ca / gambhīreṇātipūrṇena tejasā rañjitaprabham //
english: He was attractive yet formidable (in his look), clear yet vast (in his mind), deep and full (in knowledge), and shining.

sanskrit: anantajīvitadaśāsakhīmekāmaninditām / dhārayantaṃ kare ślakṣṇāṃ kuṇḍīmamlānamānasam //
english: His life time had no limit, nor his mind any bound to it, nor had age impaired his understanding. He held the ascetics pot in one hand, that went (through life) as his only faithful companion.

sanskrit: karuṇākrāntacetattavātprasannairmadhurākṣaraiḥ / vīkṣaṇairamṛteneva saṃsiñcantamimāḥ prajāḥ //
english: The compassionateness of his mind, added to the sweet complacency of his speech and looks, pleased the people as if they were actually served with nectar drops, or sprinkled over with ambrosial dews.

sanskrit: yuktayajñopavītāṅga dhavalapronnatasruvam / anantaṃ vismayaṃ cāntaḥ prayacchantamivekṣituḥ //
english: His body decorated by the sacred thread, and his white prominent eyebrows, made him appear as a wonder to the eyes of his beholders.

sanskrit: sunimālokya bhūpālo dūrādevānatākṛtiḥ / praṇanāma galanmaulimaṇimānitabhūtalam //
english: On seeing the sage, the lord of earth lowly bent himself at a distance, and then bowed down to him (so low), that the ground was decorated by the gems pendant upon his crown.

sanskrit: munirapyavanīnāthaṃ bhāsvāniva śatakratum / tatrābhivādayāṃcakre madhurodārayā girā //
english: The sage also in his turn greeted the Lord of the earth on the spot with sweet and kind words, like the sun greeting the lord of the gods.

sanskrit: tato vasiṣṭhapramukhāḥ sarva eva dvijātayaḥ / svāgatādikrameṇainaṃ pūjayāmāsurādṛtāḥ //
english: Afterwards the assembled Brahmans (of the court) headed by Vasishtha, honoured him with their welcomes.

sanskrit: daśaratha uvāca / aśaṅkitopanītena bhāsvatā darśanena te / sādho svanugṛhītāḥ smo raviṇevāmbujākarāḥ //
english: The king said:—we are as highly favoured, Oh holy sage! by thine unexpected appearance and thy glorious sight, as a bed of lotuses at the sight of the luminous sun.  "

sanskrit: yadanādi yadakṣuṇṇaṃ yadapāyavivarjitam / tadānandasukhaṃ prāptaṃ mayā tvaddarśanānmune //
english: Oh sage, I have felt at thine appearance the happiness which knows no bounds, and which has no diminution in it.

sanskrit: adya vartāmahe nūnaṃ dhanyānāṃ dhuri dharmataḥ / bhavadāgamanasyeme yadvayaṃ lakṣyamāgatāḥ //
english: This day we must be placed at the front rank of the fortunate, as we have become the object of thine advent.

sanskrit: evaṃ prakathayanto'tra rājāno'tha maharṣayaḥ / āsaneṣu sabhāsthānamāsādya samupāviśan //
english: With these and similar conversations that went on among the princes and the sages, they proceeded to the court-hall where they took their respective seats.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā mālitaṃ lakṣmyā bhītastamṛṣisattamam / prahṛṣṭavadano rājā svayamarghyaṃ nyavedayat //
english: The king finding the best of sages (Viswamitra) so very prosperous in his devotion, felt some hesitation to offer him the arghya (honorarium) himself with his cheerful countenance.

sanskrit: sa rājñaḥ pratigṛhyārghyaṃ śāstradṛṣṭena karmaṇā / pradakṣiṇaṃ prakurvantaṃ rājānaṃ paryapūjayat //
english: He (the sage) accepted the arghya offered him by the king, and hailed him during his act of turning round (the sage), according to the rules of Sastra.

sanskrit: sa rājñā pūjitastena prahṛṣṭavadanastadā / kuśalaṃ cāvyayaṃ caiva paryapṛcchannarādhipam //
english: Thus honoured by the king, he with a cheerful countenance asked the Lord of men about the good health (of himself and family), and the fulness of his finance.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhena samāgamya prahasya munipuṃgavaḥ / yathārhaṃ cārcayitvainaṃ papracchānāmayaṃ tataḥ //
english: Then coming in contact with Vasishtha, the great sage saluted him as he deserved with a smile, and asked him about his health.

sanskrit: kṣaṇaṃ yathārhamanyonyaṃ pūjayitvā sametya ca / te sarve hṛṣṭamanaso mahārājaniveśane //
english: After their interview and exchange of due courtesies had lasted for a while to the satisfaction of all in the royal assembly;

sanskrit: yathocitāsanagatā mithaḥ saṃvṛddhatejasaḥ / paraspareṇa papracchuḥ sarve'nāmayamādarāt //
english: They both took their respective seats; when every one (in the court) respectfully greeted the sage of exalted prowess.

sanskrit: upaviṣṭāya tasmai sa viśvāmitrāya dhīmate / pādyamarghyaṃ ca gāṃ caiva bhūyobhūyo nyavedayat //
english: After the sapient sage (Viswamitra) was seated, they made various offerings of padya, arghya and kine to him.

sanskrit: arcayitvā tu vidhivadviśvāmitramabhāṣata / prāñjaliḥ prayato vākyamidaṃ prītamanā nṛpaḥ //
english: Having honoured Viswamitra in due form, the lord of men condescended to address him with a gladdest mind and in submissive terms, with his palms folded over each other.

sanskrit: yathā'mṛtasya saṃprāptiryathā varṣamavarṣake / yathāndhasyekṣaṇaprāptirbhavadāgamanaṃ tathā //
english: "He said, ""Sir, your coming here is as grateful to me as the obtaining of nectar by one, as a rainfall after a drought, and as the gaining of sight by the blind.  "

sanskrit: yatheṣṭadārasaṃparkātputrajanmā'prajāvataḥ / svapnadṛṣṭārthalābhaśca bhavadāgamanaṃ tathā //
english: Again it is as delightful to me as the getting of a son by a childless man in his beloved wife, and coming in possession of a treasure in a dream.

sanskrit: yathepsitena saṃyoga iṣṭasyāgamanaṃ yathā / praṇaṣṭasya yathā lābho bhavadāgamanaṃ tathā //
english: Your advent is no less pleasing to me than one's meeting with the object of his wishes, the arrival of a friend, and the recovery of thing that was given for lost.

sanskrit: yathā harṣo nabhogatyā mṛtasya punarāgamāt / tathā tvadāgamādbrahmansvāgataṃ te mahāmune //
english: It gives me the joy that is derived from the sight of a deceased friend suddenly returning by the way of the sky. It is thus Oh Brahman, I welcome your visit to me.

sanskrit: brahmalokanivāso hi kasya na prītimāvahet / mune tavāgamastadvatsatyameva bravīmi te //
english: Who is there that is not glad to live in the heaven (Brahma-loka)? I feel myself as happy Oh sage! at your advent, and this I tell you truly.

sanskrit: kaśca te paramaḥ kāmaḥ kiṃ ca te karavāṇyaham / pātrabhūto'si me vipra prāptaḥ paramadhārmikaḥ //
english: (Now tell me) what is your best pleasure, and what I may do for you; O Vipra, that are the best of the virtuous, and most properly deserving of my services.

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ rājarṣiśabdena tapasā dyotitaprabhaḥ / brahmarṣitvamanuprāptaḥ pūjyo'si bhagavanmayā //
english: Formerly had you been famed under the title of Rajarshi (or royal sage); but since, made glorious by dint of your asceticism, you have been promoted to the rank of a Brahmarshi (or Brahman sage). Wherefore you are truly the object of my worship.

sanskrit: gaṅgājalābhiṣekeṇa yathā prītirbhavenmama / tathā tvaddarśanātprītirantaḥ śītayatīva mām //
english: I am so glad at your sight that it soothes my inmost soul, in the same manner as an ablution in Ganga's stream cheers the mind.

sanskrit: vigatecchābhayakrodho vītarāgo nirāmayaḥ / idamatyadbhutaṃ brahmanyadbhavānmāmupāgataḥ //
english: Free as you are from fears and desires, from wrath and passions and the feelings of pleasure, pain and disease, it is very wonderful, Oh Brahman, that you should have recourse to me.

sanskrit: śubhakṣetragataṃ cāhamātmānamapakalmaṣam / candrabimba ivonmagnaṃ vedavedyavidāṃvara //
english: I consider myself as situated at a holy sanctuary, and absolved from all my sins, or as merged in the lunar sphere (by your presence), Oh! best of the learned in the truths of the Vedas.

sanskrit: sākṣādiva brahmaṇo me tavābhyāgamanaṃ matam / pūto'smyanugṛhītaśca tavābhyāgamanānmune //
english: I understand your appearance as that of Brahma himself before me, and I confess myself, O sage! to be purified and favoured by your advent.

sanskrit: tvadāgamanapuṇyena sādho yadanurañjitam / adya me saphalaṃ janma jīvitaṃ tatsujīvitam //
english: I am indeed so gratified at your arrival, that I deem myself fortunate in this birth, and that I have not lived in vain but led a truly good life.

sanskrit: tvāmihābhyāgataṃ dṛṣṭvā pratipūjya praṇamya ca / ātmanyeva namāmyantardṛṣṭvenduṃ jaladhiryathā //
english: My heart cannot contain within itself, but overflows (with joy) like the sea at the sight of the moon, since I beheld your person here and made my respectful obeisance to you.

sanskrit: yatkāryaṃ yena vārthena prāpto'si munipuṅgava / kṛtamityeva tadviddhi mānyo'sīti sadā mama //
english: Whatever is your commission, and whatsoever may be the object, O greatest of sages! which has brought you hither, know it as already granted (by me); for your commands are always to be obeyed by me.

sanskrit: svakārye na vimarśaṃ tvaṃ kartumarhasi kauśika / bhagavannāstyadeyaṃ me tvayi yatpratipadyate //
english: You need not hesitate to communicate to me your best, O progeny of Kausika, there is nothing, with me which is to be kept from you, if you should ask for it.

sanskrit: kāryasya na vicāraṃ tvaṃ kartumarhasi dharmataḥ / kartā cāhamaśeṣaṃ te daivataṃ paramaṃ bhavān //
english: You need not dubitate about my performance of the act. I tell it solemnly that I will execute your behest to the last item, as I take you in the light of a superior divinity.

sanskrit: idamatimadhuraṃ niśamya vākyaṃ śrutisukhamātmavidā vinītamuktam / prathitaguṇayaśāguṇairviśiṣṭaṃ munivṛṣabhaḥ paramaṃ jagāma harṣam //
english: Upon hearing these sweet words (of the king), which were pleasing to the ears, and delivered with a humility worthy of one knowing himself, the far famed and meritorious chief of the sages felt highly gratified in himself.

sanskrit: śrīvālmīkiruvāca / tacchrutvā rājasiṃhasya vākyamadbhutavistaram / hṛṣṭaromā mahātejā viśvāmitro'bhyabhāṣata //
english: After the illustrious Viswamitra had heard the aforesaid unusually lengthy speech of the lion among kings, his hairs stood erect with joy, and he said.

sanskrit: sadṛśaṃ rājaśārdūla tavaivaitanmahītale / mahāvaṃśaprasūtasya vasiṣṭhavaśavartinaḥ //
