english: This speech is worthy of thee, O best of kings on earth, and one descended from a royal race, and guided by the sage Vasishtha himself.

sanskrit: yattu me hṛdgataṃ vākyaṃ tasya kāryavinirṇayam / kuru tvaṃ rājaśārdūla dharmaṃ samanupālaya //
english: Consider well O king about the performance of the act which I have in mind, and support (the cause of) virtue.

sanskrit: ahaṃ dharmaṃ samātiṣṭhe siddhayarthaṃ puruṣarṣabha / tasya vighnakarā ghorā rākṣasā mama saṃsthitāḥ //
english: I am employed, O chief of men, in religious acts for attainment of my consummation, whereto the horrible Rakshasas have become my great obstructions.

sanskrit: yadā yadā tu yajñena yaje'haṃ vibudhavrajān / tadā tadā tu me yajñaṃ vinighnanti niśācarāḥ //
english: Whenever I betake myself to offer sacrifices (to the gods) at any place, instantly do these nocturnal demons appear to destroy my sacrificial rites.

sanskrit: bahuśo vihite tasminmayā rākṣasanāyakāḥ / akiraṃste mahīṃ yāge māṃsena rudhireṇa ca //
english: The chiefs of the Rakshasas fling heaps of flesh and blood on the sacrificial ground (before me), on very many occasions that I commence my ceremonies.

sanskrit: avadhūte tathābhūte tasminyāgakadambake / kṛtaśramo nirutsāhastasmāddeśādupāgataḥ //
english: Being thus obstructed in my sacrificial duties, I now come to thee from that spot and with a broken spirit, after having laboured in vain.

sanskrit: na ca me krodhamutsraṣṭuṃ buddhirbhavati pārthiva / tathābhūtaṃ hi tatkarma na śāpastasya vidyate //
english: I have no mind O king, to give vent to my anger by imprecations, which have no room in my conduct.

sanskrit: īdṛśī yajñadīkṣā sā mama tasminmahākratau / tvatprasādādavighnena prāpayeyaṃ mahāphalam //
english: Such being the sacrificial law, I expect to gain its great object in peace by thy favor.

sanskrit: trātumarhasi māmārtaṃ śaraṇārthinamāgatam / arthināṃ yannirāśatvaṃ sattame'bhibhavo hi saḥ //
english: Being thus oppressed I have recourse to thy protection, and thou shouldst protect me (from wrongs);otherwise it is an insult to solicitors to be put to disappointment by the best of men.

sanskrit: tavāsti tanayaḥ śrīmāndṛptaśārdūlavikramaḥ / mahendrasadṛśo vīrye rāmo rakṣovidāraṇaḥ //
english: Thou hast a son, the beauteous Rama, powerful as the fierce tiger, and strong as the great Indra himself. He it is who is able to destroy the Rakshasas.

sanskrit: taṃ putraṃ rājaśārdūla rāmaṃ satyaparākramam / kākapakṣadharaṃ śūraṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ me dātumarhasi //
english: Now mayst thou deliver to me that Rama thy eldest son, having his youthful locks of hair like the sable plumage of a crow, but possessing the true valour of a hero.

sanskrit: śakto hyeṣa mayā gupto divyena svena tejasā / rākṣasā ye'pakartārasteṣāṃ mūrdhavinigrahe //
english: Protected under my sacred authority, he will be able by his personal prowess, to sever the heads of the malicious Rakshasas.

sanskrit: śreyaścāsya kariṣyāmi bahurūpamanantakam / trayāṇāmapi lokānāṃ yena pūjyo bhaviṣyati //
english: I will do him an infinity of good services, whereby he will in the end become adored by the inhabitants of the three worlds.

sanskrit: na ca te rāmamāsādya sthātuṃ śaktā niśācarāḥ / kruddhaṃ kesariṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā vaneraṇa ivaiṇakāḥ //
english: The night-wandering Rakshasas cannot abide in the field before Rama, but must fly like stags in the wilderness before the furious lion.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ na cānyaḥ kākutsthādyoddhumutsahate pumān / ṛte kesariṇaḥ kruddhānmattānāṃ kariṇāmiva //
english: No other man than Rama can make bold to fight with the Rakshasas; as no animal other than the furious lion can stand to fight with the wild elephants.

sanskrit: vīryotsiktā hi te pāpāḥ kālakūṭopamā raṇe / kharadūṣaṇayorbhṛtyāḥ kṛtāntāḥ kupitā iva //
english: Elated with their strength these vicious beings have become (as deadly) as poisoned shafts in fighting, and being delegates of Khara and Dushana, they are as furious as death itself.

sanskrit: rāmasya rājaśārdūla sahiṣyante na sāyakān / anāratagatā dhārā jaladasyeva pāṃsavaḥ //
english: They cannot, Oh thou tiger among kings! be able to sustain the arrows of Rama, but must set down like the flying dust under the ceaseless showers of his arrows.

sanskrit: na ca putrakṛtaṃ snehaṃ kartumarhasi pārthiva / na tadasti jagatyasminyanna deyaṃ mahātmanām //
english: Let not paternal affection prevail over thee O king, (to withhold thy son), as there is nothing in this world, which the high-minded will refuse to part with.

sanskrit: hanta nūnaṃ vijānāmi hatāṃstānviddhirākṣasān / nahyasmadādayaḥ prājñāḥ saṃdigdhe saṃpravṛttayaḥ //
english: I know it for certain, and so shouldst thou know also, that the Rakshasas must be destroyed by him; and (believe me) that wise men like ourselves will never undertake to engage in an uncertainty.

sanskrit: ahaṃ vedmi mahātmānaṃ rāmaṃ rājīvalocanam / vasiṣṭhaśca mahātejā ye cānye dīrghadarśinaḥ //
english: I well know the great soul of the lotus-eyed Rama, and so does the illustrious Vasishtha, and all other far-seeing.

sanskrit: yadi dharmo mahattvaṃ ca yaśaste manasi sthitam / tanmahyaṃ samabhipretamātmajaṃ dātumarhasi //
english: Should the sense of greatness, duty and renown, have a seat in thy soul, thou shouldst deliver my desired object—thy son to me.

sanskrit: daśarātraśca me yajño yasminrāmeṇa rākṣasāḥ / hantavyā vighnakartāro mama yajñasya vairiṇaḥ //
english: It will take me ten nights to perform the rites of my sacrifice, at which Rama shall have to stay with me and kill the Rakshasas, who are obnoxious to my rites and enemies of the sacrifice.

sanskrit: atrāpyanujñāṃ kākutstha dadatāṃ tava mantriṇaḥ / vasiṣṭhapramukhāḥ sarve tena rāmaṃ visarjaya //
english: Let the ministers, Oh Kakutstha! headed by Vasishtha join to give their assent (to it), and deliver thy Rama to me.

sanskrit: nātyeti kālaḥ kālajña yathāyaṃ mama rāghava / tathā kuruṣva bhadraṃ te mā ca śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ //
english: Thou O son of Raghu, that knowest the times (of religious observances) must not allow my time to slip, so do as I may have Rama. Be blest and give not way to sorrow.

sanskrit: kāryamaṇvapi kāle tu kṛtametyupakāratām / mahadapyupakāro'pi riktatāmetyakālataḥ //
english: Even the smallest service appears to be much if done in good time, and the best service is of no avail if done out of season.

sanskrit: ityevamuktvā dharmātmā dharmārthasahitaṃ vacaḥ / virarāma mahātejā viśvāmitro munīśvaraḥ //
english: The illustrious and holy chief of the sages Viswamitra, paused after saying these words fraught with a virtuous and useful intention.

sanskrit: śrutvā vaco munivarasya mahānubhāvastūṣṇīmatiṣṭhadupapannapadaṃ sa vaktum / no yuktiyuktakathanena vinaiti toṣaṃ dhīmānapūritamano'bhimataśca lokaḥ //
english: Hearing these words of the great sage, the magnanimous king held his silence for some time, with a view to prepare a fitting answer; because no man of sense is ever satisfied with talking unreasonably either before others or to himself.

sanskrit: aṣṭamaḥ sargaḥ vālmīkiruvāca / tacchrutvā rājaśārdūlo viśvāmitrasya bhāṣitam / muhūrtamāsīnniśceṣṭaḥ sadainyaṃ cedamabravīt //
english: Valmiki added:—On hearing these words of Viswamitra, the tiger among kings remained speechless for a moment, and then besought him in the lowliness of his spirit.

sanskrit: ūnaṣoḍaśavarṣo'yaṃ rāmo rājīvalocanaḥ / na yuddhayogyatāmasya paśyāmi saha rākṣasaiḥ //
english: Rama my lotus-eyed boy is only of fifteen years of age. I do not see he is a match for the Rakshasas.

sanskrit: iyamakṣauhiṇī pūrṇā yasyāḥ patirahaṃ prabho / tayā parivṛto yuddhaṃ dāsyāmi piśitāśinām //
english: Here is a full akshauhini legion of my soldiers; of whom, Oh my Lord! I am the sole commander; surrounded by them I will offer battle to the Rakshasas cannibals.

sanskrit: ime hi śūrā vikrāntā bhṛtyā mantraviśāradāḥ / ahaṃ caiṣāṃ dhanuṣpāṇirgoptā samaramūrdhani //
english: Here are my brave generals who are well disciplined in warfare; I will be their leader in the height of war with my bow in hand.

sanskrit: ebhiḥ sahaiva vīrāṇāṃ mahendramahatāmapi / dadāmi yuddhaṃ mattānāṃ kariṇāmiva kesarī //
english: Accompanied with these, I can offer fight to the enemies of the gods, and to the great Indra himself, in the same manner as the lion withstands the wild elephants.

sanskrit: bālo rāmastvanīkeṣu na jānāti balābalam / antaḥpurādṛte dṛṣṭā nānenānyā raṇāvaniḥ //
english: Rama is but a boy who has no knowledge of the strength of our forces, and whose experience has scarcely stretched to the battle field beyond the inner apartments.

sanskrit: na śastraiḥ paramairyukto na ca yuddhaviśāradaḥ / navāstraiḥ śūrakoṭīnāṃ tajjñaḥ samarabhūmiṣu //
english: He is not well trained in arms, nor is he skilled in warfare. He does not know to fight with a foe, arrayed in the order of battle.

sanskrit: kevalaṃ puṣpakhaṇḍeṣu nagaropavaneṣu ca / udyānavanakuñjeṣu sadaiva pariśīlanam //
english: He only knows how to walk about in the gardens of this city and amidst the arbours and pleasant groves.

sanskrit: vihartumeṣa jānāti saha rājakumārakaiḥ / kīrṇapuṣpopahārāsu svakāsvajirabhūmiṣu //
english: He only knows how to play with his brother princes, in the flowery parks set apart for his play within the precincts of the palace.

sanskrit: adya tvatitarāṃ brahmanmama bhāgyaviparyayāt / himeneva hi padmābhaḥ saṃpanno hariṇaḥ kṛśaḥ //
english: Now a days, Oh Brahman! he has become by a sad reverse of my fortune, as lean and pale as the withering lotus under the dews.

sanskrit: nāttumannāni śaknoti na vihartuṃ gṛhāvanim / antaḥkhedaparītātmā tūṣṇīṃ tiṣṭhati kevalam //
english: He has no taste for his food, nor can he walk from one room to another, but remains ever silent and slow brooding over his inward grief and melancholy.

sanskrit: sadāraḥ sahabhṛtyo'haṃ tatkṛte munināyaka / śaradīva payovāho nūnaṃ niḥsāratāṃ gataḥ //
english: In my great anxiety about him, O chief of sages, I have been, with my family and dependants, deprived of the gist of our bodies, and become as empty clouds of autumn.

sanskrit: īdṛśo'sau suto bāla ādhinā'tha vaśīkṛtaḥ / kathaṃ dadāmi taṃ tubhyaṃ yoddhuṃ saha niśācaraiḥ //
english: Can my boy, so young as he is, and thus subjected to distemper, be fit to fight at all, and again with those marauders who rove about at nights.

sanskrit: api bālāṅganāsaṅgādapi sādho sudhārasāt / rājyādapi sukhāyaiva putrasneho mahāmate //
english: Oh thou high-minded sage! it is one's affection for his son that affords him far greater pleasure than his possession of a kingdom, or his connection with beauteous females, or even his relish for the juice of nectar.

sanskrit: ye durantā mahārambhāstriṣu lokeṣu khedadāḥ / putrasnehena santo'pi kurvate tānasaṃśayam //
english: It is from paternal affection that good people (engage to) perform the hardest duties and austerities of religion, and any thing which is painful in the three worlds.

sanskrit: asavo'tha dhanaṃ dārāstyajyante mānavaiḥ sukham / na putro muniśārdūla svabhāvo hyeṣa jantuṣu //
english: Men are even prepared under certain circumstances to sacrifice their own lives, riches and wives; but they can never sacrifice their children: this is the nature with all living beings.

sanskrit: rākṣasāḥ krūrakarmāṇaḥ kūṭayuddhaviśāradāḥ / rāmastānyodhayatvitthaṃ yuktirevātiduḥsahā //
english: The Rakshasas are very cruel in their actions and fight deceitful warfares: so that Rama should fight them, is an idea which is very painful to me.

sanskrit: viprayukto hi rāmeṇa muhūrtamapi notsahe / jīvituṃ jīvitākāṃkṣī ca rāmaṃ netumarhasi //
english: I that have a desire to live, cannot dare to live for a moment in separation from Rama; therefore thou shouldst not take him away.

sanskrit: navavarṣasahasrāṇi mama jātasya kauśika / duḥkhenotpāditāstvete catvāraḥ putrakā mayā //
english: I have O Kausika! passed nine thousand rains in my lifetime, ere these four boys were born to me after much austerity.

sanskrit: pradhānabhūtasteṣveva rāmaḥ kamalalocanaḥ / taṃ vineha trayo'pyanye dhārayanti na jīvitam //
english: The lotus-eyed Rama is the eldest of these without whom the three others can hardly bear to live.

sanskrit: sa eva rāmo bhavatā nīyate rākṣasānprati / yadi tatputrahīnaṃ tvaṃ mṛtamevāśu viddhi mām //
english: This Rama is going to be conveyed by thee against the Rakshasas; but when I am deprived of that son, know me certainly for dead.

sanskrit: caturṇāmātmajānāṃ hi prītiratraiva me parā / jyeṣṭhaṃ dharmamayaṃ tasmānna rāmaṃ netumarhasi //
english: Of my four sons he is the one in whom rests my greatest love. Therefore do not take away Rama—my eldest and most virtuous son from me.

sanskrit: niśācarabalaṃ hantuṃ mune yadi tavepsitam / caturaṅgasamāyuktaṃ mayā saha balaṃ naya //
english: If thy intention Oh sage, is to destroy the force of night wanderers, take me there accompanied by the four kinds (elephants, horse, chariots and foot soldiers) of mine army.

sanskrit: kiṃvīryā rākṣasāste tu kasya putrāḥ kathaṃ ca te / kiyatpramāṇāḥ ke caiva iti varṇaya me sphuṭam //
english: Describe to me clearly what these Rakshasas are, how strong they are, whose sons they be and what their size and figure.

sanskrit: kathaṃ tena prakartavyaṃ teṣāṃ rāmeṇa rakṣasām / māmakairbālakairbrahmanmayā vā kūṭayodhinām //
english: Tell me the way in which the Rakshasas are to be destroyed by Rama or my boys or by myself, when they are known to be treacherous in warfare.

sanskrit: sarvaṃ me śaṃsa bhagavanyathā teṣāṃ mahāraṇe / sthātavyaṃ duṣṭabhāgyānāṃ vīryotsiktā hi rākṣasāḥ //
english: Tell me all these, Oh great sage! that I can calculate the possibility of our making a stand against the fiercely disposed Rakshasas in the open field, when they are certainly so very powerful.

sanskrit: śrūyate hi mahāvīryo rāvaṇo nāma rākṣasaḥ / sākṣādvaiśravaṇabhrātā putro viśravaso muneḥ //
english: The Rakshasa named Ravana is heard as being very powerful, he is brother of Kuvera himself, and is the son of the sage Visravas.

sanskrit: sa cettava makhe vighnaṃ karoti kila durmatiḥ / tatsaṃgrāme na śaktāḥ smo vayaṃ tasya durātmanaḥ //
english: If it is he, the evil minded Ravana, that stands in the way of thy rites, we are unable to contend with that pest.

sanskrit: kāle kāle pṛthagbrahmanbhūrivīryavibhūtayaḥ / bhūteṣvabhyudayaṃ yānti pralīyante ca kālataḥ //
english: Power and prosperity in all their flourish come within the reach of the living at times, but they disappear at others.

sanskrit: adyāsmiṃstu vayaṃ kāle rāvaṇādiṣu śatruṣu / na samarthāḥ puraḥ sthātuṃ niyatereṣa niścayaḥ //
english: Now a days we are no match for such foes as Ravana and some others. Such is the decree of destiny.

sanskrit: tasmātprasādaṃ dharmajña kuru tvaṃ mama putrake / mama caivālpabhāgyasya bhavānhi paradaivatam //
english: Therefore, O thou, that art acquainted with law, do this favour to my son, (as not to take him away); unlucky as I am, it is thou that art the arbiter of my fate.

sanskrit: devadānavagandharvā yakṣāḥ patagapannagāḥ / na śaktā rāvaṇaṃ yoddhuṃ kiṃ punaḥ puruṣā yudhi //
english: The gods, and Asuras, the Gandharvas and Yakshas, the huge beasts, birds and serpents are unable to fight with Ravana: what are we human beings in arms to him.

sanskrit: mahāvīryavatāṃ vīryamādatte yudhi rākṣasaḥ / tena sārdhaṃ na śaktāḥ sma saṃyuge tasya bālakaiḥ //
english: That Rakshasa holds the prowess of the most powerful, we cannot afford to fight with him, nor even with his children.

sanskrit: ayamanyatamaḥ kālaḥ pelavīkṛtasajjanaḥ / rāghavo'pi gato dainyaṃ yato vārdhakajarjaraḥ //
english: This is a peculiar age in which good people are made powerless; I am moreover disabled by old age and want that spirit (that I was expected to possess) derived as I am from (the most powerful) race of the Raghus.

sanskrit: athavā lavaṇaṃ brahmanyajñaghnaṃ taṃ madhoḥ sutam / kathayatvasuraprakhyaṃ naiva mokṣyāmi putrakam //
english: Tell me O Brahmana! if it is Lavan the son of Madhu (the notorious Asura) that disturbs the sacrificial rites; in that case also I will not part with my son.

sanskrit: sundopasundayoścaiva putrau vaivasvatopamau / yajñavighnakarau brūhi na te dāsyāmi putrakam //
english: If it be the two sons of Sunda and Upasunda terrible as they are like the sons of the sun, that disturb your sacrifice, in that case also I will not give my son to thee.

sanskrit: atha neṣyasi cedbrahmaṃstaddhato'smyahameva te / anyathā tu na paśyāmi śāśvataṃ jayamātmanaḥ //
english: But after all, O Brahman, shouldest thou snatch him from me (by dint of the supernatural power that thou possessest), then I am also dead and gone with him. I do not see any other chance of a lasting success of thy devotion.

sanskrit: ityuktvā mṛdu vacanaṃ raghūdvaho'sau kallole munimatasaṃśaye nimagnaḥ / nājñāsītkṣaṇamapi niścayaṃ mahātmā prodvīcāviva jaladhau sa muhyamānaḥ //
english: Saying these gentle words, the descendant of Raghu was drowned in the sea of suspense with regard to the demand of the sage, but being unable to arrive at a conclusion, the great king was carried away by the current of his thoughts as one by the high waves of the sea.

sanskrit: vālmīkiruvāca / tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya snehaparyākulekṣaṇam / samanyuḥ kauśiko vākyaṃ pratyuvāca mahīpatim //
english: Valmiki said:—On hearing this speech of the king with his piteous look and eyes full of tears, the son of Kausika became highly incensed and replied.

sanskrit: kariṣyāmīti saṃśrutya pratijñāṃ hātumarhasi / sa bhavānkesarī bhūtvā mṛgatāmiva vāñchasi //
english: Thou art about to break thy promise after pledging thyself to its performance, and thus wishest to behave as a deer after having been a lion.

sanskrit: rāghavāṇāmayukto'yaṃ kulasyāsya viparyayaḥ / na kadācana jāyante śītāṃśoruṣṇaraśmayaḥ //
english: This is unbecoming of the race of Raghu, it is acting contrary (to the rules) of this great family. Hot rays must not proceed from the cool beamed moon.

sanskrit: yadi tvaṃ na kṣamo rājangamiṣyāmi yathāgatam / hīnapratijña kākutstha sukhī bhava sabāndhavaḥ //
english: If thou art so impotent Oh king! let me return as I came. Thou promise-breaking Kakustha live happily with thy friends.

sanskrit: vālmīkiruvāca / tasminkopaparīte'tha viśvāmitre mahātmani / cacāla vasudhā kṛtsnā surāṃśca bhayamāviśat //
english: As the high spirited Viswamitra now moved with ire, the earth trembled under him, and the gods were filled with fear.

sanskrit: krodhābhibhūtaṃ vijñāya jaganmitraṃ mahāmunim / dhṛtimānsuvrato dhīmānvasiṣṭho vākyamabravīt //
english: Vasishtha the meek and wise and observant of his vows, perceiving the great sage and friend of the world thus influenced by ire, gave vent to his speech.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca / ikṣvākūṇāṃ kule jātaḥ sākṣāddharma ivāparaḥ / bhavāndaśarathaḥ śrīmāṃstrailokyaguṇabhūṣitaḥ //
english: Oh king that art born of the race of the Ikshakus, and art a form of virtue itself, and called Dasaratha the fortunate, and art adorned with all the good qualities known in the three worlds.

sanskrit: dhṛtimānsuvrato bhūtvā na dharmaṃ hātumarhasi / triṣu lokeṣu vikhyāto dharmeṇa yaśasā yutaḥ //
english: Being famed for thy meekness and strictness to thy vows, and renowned in all three worlds for thy virtues and fame, thou canst not break thy plighted faith.

sanskrit: svadharmaṃ pratipadyasva na dharmaṃ hātumarhasi / munestribhuvaneśasya vacanaṃ kartumarhasi //
english: Preserve thy virtue and think not to break thy faith, comply with the request of the sage who is honoured in all the three worlds.

sanskrit: kariṣyāmīti saṃśrutya tatte rājannakurvataḥ / iṣṭāpūrtaṃ hareddharmaṃ tasmādrāmaṃ visarjaya //
english: Saying, thou wilt do it, if thou retract thy promise, thou losest the object of thy yet unfulfilled desires. Therefore part with Rama from thee.

sanskrit: ikṣvākuvaṃśajāto'pi svayaṃ daśaratho'pi san / na pālayasi cedvākyaṃ ko'paraḥ pālayiṣyati //
english: Descended from the race of Ikshaku, and being Dasaratha thyself, if thou failest to perform thy promise, who else on earth will ever keep his word?

sanskrit: yuṣmadādipraṇītena vyavahāreṇa jantavaḥ / maryādāṃ na vimuñcanti tāṃ na hātuṃ tvamarhasi //
english: It is in pursuance of the conduct of great men like thee, that low people even do not dare to transgress the bounds of their duty, how then dost thou wish to violate it thyself?

sanskrit: guptaṃ puruṣasiṃhena jvalanenāmṛtaṃ yathā / kṛtāstramakṛtāstraṃ vā nainaṃ śakṣyanti rākṣasāḥ //
english: Guarded by this lion-like man (Viswamitra) in the manner of ambrosia by fire, no Rakshasa will have power to prevail over Rama, whether he be accoutered and armed or not.

sanskrit: eṣa vigrahavāndharma epa vīryavatāṃ varaḥ / eṣa buddhyā'dhiko loke tapasāṃ ca parāyaṇam //
english: Behold him here as the personification of virtue, the mightiest of the mighty, and superior to all in the world in his intelligence, and devotedness to asceticism.

sanskrit: eṣo'straṃ vividhaṃ vetti trailokye sacarācare / naitadanyaḥ pumānvetti na ca vetsyati kaścana //
english: He is skilled in all warlike arms that are known in the three worlds, no other man knows them so well nor shall ever be able to master them like him.

sanskrit: na devā narṣayaḥ kecinnāsurā na ca rākṣasāḥ / na nāgā yakṣagandharvāḥ sametāḥ sadṛśā muneḥ //
english: Among the Gods, the Sages, the Asuras, the Rakshasas, the Nagas, the Yakshas and Gandharvas, there is none equal to him.

sanskrit: astramasmai kṛśāśvena paraiḥ paramadurjayam / kauśikāya purā dattaṃ yadā rājyaṃ samanvagāt //
english: In bygone days when this son of Kaushika used to rule over his realm, he was furnished with all the arms by Krisaswa, and which no enemy can baffle.

sanskrit: te hi putrāḥ kṛśāśvasya prajāpatisutopamāḥ / enamanvacaranvīrā dīptimanto mahaujasaḥ //
english: These arms were the progeny of Krisaswa, and were equally radiant and powerful as the progeny of the Prajapati, and followed him.

sanskrit: jayā ca suprabhā caiva dākṣāyaṇyau sumadhyame / tayostu yānyapatyāni śataṃ paramadurjayam //
english: Now Daksha (the patriarch) had two beauteous daughters Jaya and Supraja (alias Vijaya), who had a hundred offspring (as personifications of the implements, that are invincible in war.

sanskrit: pañcāśataṃ sutāñjajñe jayā labdhavarā purā / vadhārthaṃ surasainyānāṃ te kṣamāḥ kāmacāriṇaḥ //
english: Of these the favoured Jaya has given birth to fifty sons of old, who are implacable agents of the destruction of Asura forces.

sanskrit: suprabhā janayāmāsa putrānpañcāśataṃ parān / saṃgharṣānnāma durdharṣāndurākārānvalīyasaḥ //
english: In like manner, Supraja gave birth to fifty sons of very superior qualities, who are very powerful and terrible in their appearance, and indomitably aggressive.

sanskrit: evaṃvīryo mahātejā viśvāmitro jaganmuniḥ / na rāmagamane buddhiṃ viklavāṃ kartumarhasi //
english: Thus Viswamitra is strengthened and grown powerful (by means of these). He is acknowledged as a sage in the three worlds, Thou therefore must not think otherwise than deliver Rama to him.

sanskrit: asminmahāsattvatame munīndre sthite samīpe purūṣasya sādho / prāpte'pi mṛtyāvamaratvameti mā dīnatāṃ gaccha yathā vimūḍhaḥ //
english: This mighty and virtuous man and prince of sages being nigh, any one even at the point of death in his presence, is sure to attain his immortality (on earth): therefore be not disheartened like an insensible man.

sanskrit: daśamaḥ sargaḥ vālmīkiruvāca / tathā vasiṣṭhe bruvati rājā daśarathaḥ sutam / saṃprahṛṣṭamanā rāmamājuhāva salakṣmaṇam //
english: Valmiki related:—After Vasishtha had done saying in this manner, king Dasaratha was glad to send for Rama with Lakshmana, and said:

sanskrit: daśaratha uvāca / pratihāra mahābāhuṃ rāmaṃ satyaparākramam / salakṣmaṇamavighnena puṇyārthaṃ śīghramānaya //
english: Go you chamberlain, and bring here quickly the truly mighty and long armed Rama with Lakshmana, for the meritorious purpose of removing the impediments.

sanskrit: iti rājñā visṛṣṭo'sau gatvāntaḥpuramandiram / muhūrtamātreṇāgatya samuvāca mahīpatim //
english: Thus sent by the king he went to the inner apartment, and coming back in a moment informed the king.

sanskrit: deva dordalitāśeṣaripo rāmaḥ svamandire / vimanāḥ saṃsthito rātrau ṣaṭpadaḥ kamale yathā //
english: Oh sire! Rama, whose arms have crushed all his foes, remains rapt in thoughts in his room like the bee closed in the lotus at night.

sanskrit: āgacchāmi kṣaṇeneti vakti dhyāyati caikataḥ / na kasyacicca nikaṭe sthātumicchati khinnadhīḥ //
english: He said, he is coming in a moment, but is so abstracted in his lonely meditation that he likes no body to be near him.

sanskrit: ityuktastena bhūpālastaṃ rāmānucaraṃ janam / sarvamāśvāsayāmāsa papraccha ca yathākramam //
english: Thus acquainted by the chamberlain, the king called one of the attendants of Rama to him, and having given him every assurance, asked him to relate the particulars.

sanskrit: kathaṃ kīdṛgvidho rāma iti pṛṣṭo mahībhṛtā / rāmabhṛtyajanaḥ khinno vākyamāha mahīpatim //
english: On being asked by the king how Rama had come to that state, the attendant thus replied to him in a sorrowful mood.

sanskrit: dehayaṣṭimimāṃ deva dhārayanta ime vayam / khinnāḥ khede parimlānatanau rāme sute tava //
english: Sir, we have also become as lean as sticks in our persons, in sorrow for the fading away of your son Rama in his body.

sanskrit: rāmo rājīvapatrākṣo yataḥprabhṛti cāgataḥ / saviprastīrthayātrāyāstataḥprabhṛti durmanāḥ //
english: The lotus-eyed Rama appears dejected ever since he has come back from his pilgrimage in company with the Brahmanas.

sanskrit: yatnaprārthanayāsmākaṃ nijavyāpāramāhnikam / so'yamāmlānavadanaḥ karoti na karoti vā //
english: When besought by us with importunity to perform his daily rites, he sometimes discharges them with a placid countenance, and wholly dispenses with them at others.

sanskrit: snānadevārcanādānabhojanādiṣu durmanāḥ / prārthito'pi hi nātṛpteraśnātyaśanamīśvaraḥ //
english: He is averse, Oh Lord! to bathing, to worshipping the gods, to the distribution of alms, and to his meals also; and even when importuned by us he does not take his food with a good relish.

sanskrit: lolāntaḥpuranārībhiḥ kṛtadolābhiraṅgaṇe / naca krīḍati līlābhirdhārābhiriva cātakaḥ //
english: He no longer suffers himself to be rocked in the swinging cradles by the playful girls of the harem, nor does he divert himself under the showering fountains like the chataka.

sanskrit: māṇikyamukulaprotā keyūrakaṭakāvaliḥ / nānandayati taṃ rājandyauḥ pātaviṣayaṃ yathā //
english: No ornaments beset with the bud-shaped rubies, no bracelets nor necklace, Oh king, can please him now, in the same manner as nothing in heaven can please its inhabitants who expect their fall from it.

sanskrit: krīḍadvadhūvilokeṣu vahatkusumavāyuṣu / latāvalayageheṣu bhavatyativiṣādavān //
english: He is sorrowful even while sitting in the arbours of creepers, regaled by flowery breezes, and amidst the looks of damsels playing around him.

sanskrit: yaddravyamucitaṃ svādu peśalaṃ cittahāri ca / bāṣpapūrṇekṣaṇa iva tenaiva parikhidyate //
english: Whatever thing Oh king! is good and sweet, elegant and pleasing, to the soul, he looks at them with sorrowful eyes, like one whose eyes are already satiate with viewing them heaped up in piles.

sanskrit: kimimā duḥkhadāyinyaḥ prasphurantīḥ purāṅganāḥ / iti nṛttavilāseṣu kāminīḥ parinindati //
english: "He would speak ill of the girls that would dance merrily before him, and exclaim out saying, ""why should these ladies of the harem flutter about in this way causing grief in me.""  "

sanskrit: bhojanaṃ śayanaṃ yānaṃ vilāsaṃ snānamāsanam / unmattaceṣṭita iva nābhinandatyaninditam //
english: His doings are like those of a madman, who takes no delight at his food or rest, his vehicles or seats, his baths and other pleasures, however excellent they be.

sanskrit: kiṃ saṃpadā kiṃ vipadā kiṃ gehena kimiṅgitaiḥ / sarvamevāsadityuktvā tūṣṇīmeko'vatiṣṭhate //
english: As regards prosperity or adversity, his habitation or any other desirable things, he says of them to be all unreal, and then holds his silence.

sanskrit: nodeti parihāseṣu na bhogeṣu nimajjati / na ca tiṣṭhati kāryeṣu maunamevāvalambate //
english: He cannot be excited to pleasantry nor tempted to taste of pleasures; he attends to no business, but remains in silence.

sanskrit: vilolālakavallaryo helāvalitalocanāḥ / nānandayanti taṃ nāryo mṛgyo vanataruṃ yathā //
english: No woman with her loosened locks and tresses, and the negligent glances of her eyes, can please him any more than the playful fawn can please the trees in the forest.

sanskrit: ekānteṣu diganteṣu tīreṣu vipineṣu ca / ratimāyātyaraṇyeṣu vikrīta iva jantuṣu //
english: Like a man sold among savages, he takes delight in lonely places, in remotest skirts, in the banks (of rivers) and wild deserts.

sanskrit: vastrapānāśanādānaparāṅmukhatayā tayā / parivrāḍdharmiṇaṃ bhūya so'nuyāti tapasvinam //
english: His aversion to clothing and conveyance, food and presents, bespeaks O king! that he is following the line of life led by wandering ascetics.

sanskrit: eka eva vasandeśe janaśūnye janeśvara / na hasatyekayā buddhyā na gāyati na roditi //
english: He lives alone, Oh lord of men! in a lonely place, and neither laughs nor sings nor cries aloud from a sense of their indifference to him.

sanskrit: baddhapadmāsanaḥ śūnyamanā vāmakarasthale / kapolatalamādhāya kevalaṃ paritiṣṭhati //
english: Seated in the posture of folded legs (Padmasana), he stays with a distracted mind, reclining his cheek on his left palm.

sanskrit: nābhimānamupādatte na ca vāñchati rājatām / nodeti nāstamāyāti sukhaduḥkhānuvṛttiṣu //
english: He assumes no pride to himself nor wishes for the dignity of sovereignty; he is neither elated with joy nor depressed by grief or pain.

sanskrit: na vidmaḥ kimasau yāti kiṃ karoti kimīhate / kiṃ dhyāyati kimāyāti kathaṃ kimanudhāvati //
english: We do not know where he goes, what he does, what he desires, what he meditates upon, whence and when he comes and what he follows.

sanskrit: pratyahaṃ kṛśatāmeti pratyahaṃ yāti pāṇḍutām / virāgaṃ pratyahaṃ yāti śaradanta iva drumaḥ //
english: He is getting lean every day, growing pale day by day, and like a tree at the end of autumn, he is becoming discoloured day after day.

sanskrit: anuyātau tathaivaitau rājañchatrughnalakṣmaṇau / tādṛśāveva tasyaiva pratibimbāviva sthitau //
english: Satrughna and Lakshmana are, Oh king! the followers of all his habits, and resemble his very shadows.

sanskrit: bhṛtyai rājabhirambābhiḥ saṃpṛṣṭo'pi punaḥ punaḥ / uktvā na kiṃcideveti tūṣṇīmāste nirīhitaḥ //
english: Being repeatedly asked by his servants, his brother-princes and his mothers, (as to the cause of his dementedness), he says he has none, and then resumes his taciturnity and indifference.

sanskrit: āpātamātrahṛdyeṣu mā bhogeṣu manaḥ kṛthāḥ / iti pārśvagataṃ bhavyamanuśāsti suhṛjjanam //
english: "He would lecture his companions and friends saying, ""do not set your mind to sensual enjoyments which are only pleasing for the time being.""  "

sanskrit: nānāvibhavaramyāsu strīṣu goṣṭhīgatāsu ca / purasthitamivāsneho nāśamevānupaśyati //
english: He has no affection for the richly adorned women of the harem, but rather looks upon them as the cause of destruction presented before him.

sanskrit: nītamāyuranāyāsapadaprāptivivarjitaiḥ / ceṣṭitairiti kākalyā bhūyobhūyaḥ pragāyati //
english: He often chaunts in plaintive notes, how his life is being spent in vain cares, estranged from those of the easily attainable state of.

sanskrit: samrāḍbhaveti pārśvasthaṃ vadantamanujīvinam / pralapantamivonmattaṃ hasatyanyamanā muniḥ //
english: Should some dependant courtier speak of his being an emperor (one day), he smiles at him as upon a raving madman, and then remains silent as one distracted in his mind.

sanskrit: na proktamākarṇayati īkṣate na purogatam / karotyavajñāṃ sarvatra susametyāpi vastuni //
english: He does not pay heed to what is said to him, nor does he look at any thing presented before him. He hates to look upon things even the most charming.

sanskrit: apyākāśasarojinyā apyākāśamahāvane / itthametanmana iti vismayo'sya na jāyate //
english: As it is chimerical to suppose the existence of an etherial lake, and lotus growing in the same, so it is false to believe the reality of the mind and its conceptions. Saying so Rama marvels at nothing.

sanskrit: kāntāmadhyagatasyāpi mano'sya madaneṣavaḥ / na bhedayanti durbhedyaṃ dhārā iva mahopalam //
english: Even when sitting amidst beauteous maids, the darts of cupid fail to pierce his impenetrable heart, as showers of rain the (unimpregnable) rock.

sanskrit: āpadāmekamāvāsamabhivāñchasi kiṃ dhanam / anuśiṣyeti sarvasvamarthine saṃprayacchati //
english: "That ""no sensible man should ever wish for riches which are but the seats of dangers""; making this his motto, Rama gives away all that he has to beggars.  "

sanskrit: iyamāpadiyaṃ saṃpadityevaṃ kalpanāmayaḥ / manaso'bhyudito moha iti ślokānpragāyati //
english: "He sings some verses to this effect that ""it is an error to call one thing as prosperity and the other adversity, when they are both but imaginations of the mind"".  "

sanskrit: hā hato'hamanātho'hamityākrandaparo'pi san / na jano yāti vairāgyaṃ citramityeva vaktyasau //
english: "He repeats some words to this purport that, ""though it is the general cry, ""O I am gone, I am helpless grown,"" yet it is a wonder, that no body should betake himself to utter indifference.""  "

sanskrit: raghukānanaśālena rāmeṇa ripughātinā / bhṛśamitthaṃ sthitenaiva vayaṃ khedamupāgatāḥ //
english: That Rama, the destroyer of enemies, the great Sala (oak) that is grown in the garden of Raghu, should get into such a state of mind is what causes grief in us.

sanskrit: na vidmaḥ kiṃ mahābāho tasya tādṛśacetasaḥ / kurmaḥ kamalapatrākṣa gatiratra hi no bhavān //
english: We do not know, Oh great armed and lotus-eyed king! what to do with him in this state of his mind. We hope only in thee.

sanskrit: rājānamathavā vipramupadeṣṭāramagrataḥ / hasatyajñamivāvyagraḥ so'vadhīrayati prabho //
english: He laughs to scorn the counsels of the princes and Brahmans before him, and spurns them as if they were fools.

sanskrit: yadevedamidaṃ sphāraṃ jagannāma yadutthitam / naitadvastu nacaivāhamiti nirṇīya saṃsthitaḥ //
english: He remains inactive with the conviction, that the world which appears to our view is a vanity, and the idea of self is also a vanity.

sanskrit: nārau nātmani no mitre na rājye na ca mātari / na saṃpadā na vipadā tasyāsthā na vibho bahiḥ //
english: He has no respect for foes or friends, for himself or his kingdom, mother or riches, nor does he pay any regard to prosperity or adversity.

sanskrit: nirastāstho nirāśo'sau nirīho'sau nirāspadaḥ / na mūḍho na ca mukto'sau tena tapyāmahe bhṛśam //
english: He is altogether quiescent, without any desire or effort, and devoid of a mainstay; he is neither captivated by any thing nor freed from worldly thoughts. These are the reasons which afflict us most.

sanskrit: kiṃ dhanena kimambābhiḥ kiṃ rājyena kimīhayā / iti niścayavānantaḥ prāṇatyāgaparaḥ sthitaḥ //
english: "He says, ""what have we to do with riches, with our mothers, with this kingdom and all our activities."" Under these impressions, he is about to give up his life.  "

sanskrit: bhoge'pyāyuṣi rājyeṣu mitre pitari mātari / paramudvegamāyātaścātako'vagrahe yathā //
english: As the chataka (swallow) grows restless at the obstruction of rains (by hurricanes), so has Rama become impatient (under the restraint) of his father and mother, his friends and kingdom, his enjoyments and even his own life.

sanskrit: iti toke samāyātāṃ śākhāprasaraśālinīm / āpattāmalamuddhartuṃ samudetu dayāparaḥ //
english: Now in compassion on thy son, incline to root out this chagrin which like a noxious creeper has been spreading its branches.

sanskrit: tasya tādṛksvabhāvasya samagravibhavānvitam / saṃsārajālamābhogi prabho prativiṣāyate //
english: For notwithstanding his possession of all affluence, he looks upon the enjoyments of the world as his poison under such a disposition of his mind.

sanskrit: īdṛśaḥ syānmahāsattvaḥ ka ivāsminmahītale / prakṛte vyavahāre taṃ yo niveśayituṃ kṣamaḥ //
english: Where is that potent person in this earth, who can restore him to proper conduct.

sanskrit: manasi mohamapāsya mahāmanāḥ sakalamārtitamaḥ kila sādhutām / saphalatāṃ nayatīha tamo haran dinakaro bhuvi bhāskaratāmiva //
english: Who is there, that like the sun removing the darkness of the world by his rays, will remove the errors that have been the cause of grief in Rama's mind, and thereby make his generosity effectual in his case.

sanskrit: viśvāmitra uvāca / evaṃ cettanmahāprājñā bhavanto raghunandanam / ihānayantu tvaritā hariṇaṃ hariṇā iva //
english: Viswamitra said:—If such is the case, you who are intelligent, may go at once, and persuade that progeny of Raghu to come hither; as they do one deer by others.

sanskrit: eṣa moho raghupaternāpadbhyo na ca rāgataḥ / vivekavairāgyavato bodha eva mahodayaḥ //
english: This stupor of Rama is not caused by any (external) accident or (inward) affection; it is I think the development of that superior intellect which rises from the right reasoning of dispassionate men.

sanskrit: ihāyātu kṣaṇādrāma iha caiva vayaṃ kṣaṇāt / mohaṃ tasyāpaneṣyāmo māruto'drerghanaṃ yathā //
english: Let Rama come here for a while, and here shall we in a moment dispel the delusion (of his mind), as the wind drives away the clouds from the mountain-tops.

sanskrit: etasminmārjite yuktyā mohe sa raghunandanaḥ / viśrāntimeṣyati pade tasminvayamivottame //
english: After his hebetude is removed by my reasoning, he shall be enabled to repose in that happy state of mind, to which we have arrived.

sanskrit: satyatāṃ muditāṃ prajñāṃ viśrāntimapatāpatām / pīnatāṃ varavarṇatvaṃ pītāmṛta ivaiṣyati //
english: He shall not only attain to pure truth and a clear understanding of uninterrupted tranquility, but secure to himself a plumpness and beauteousness of his figure and complexion, as one derives from a potion of ambrosia.

sanskrit: nijāṃ ca prakṛtāmeva vyavahāraparamparām / paripūrṇamanā mānya ācariṣyatyakhaṇḍitam //
english: He will then attend with all his heart to the full discharge of the proper course of his duties without remission, which will redound to his honour.

sanskrit: bhaviṣyati mahāsattvo jñātalokaparāvaraḥ / sukhaduḥkhadaśāhīnaḥ samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ //
english: He will become strong with a knowledge of both worlds, and his exemption from the states of pleasure and pain, and then he will look upon gold and stones with an indifferent eye.

sanskrit: ityukte munināthena rājā saṃpūrṇamānasaḥ / prāhiṇodrāmamānetuṃ bhūyo dūtaparamparām //
english: After the chief of the sages had spoken in this manner, the king resumed the firmness of his mind, and sent heralds after heralds to bring Rama to him.

sanskrit: etāvatātha kālena rāmo nijagṛhāsanāt / pituḥ sakāśamāgantumutthito'rka ivācalāt //
english: By this very time Rama was preparing to rise from his seat in the palace to come over to his father, in the manner that the sun rises from the mountain in the east.

sanskrit: vṛtaḥ katipayairbhṛtyairbhrātṛbhyāṃ ca jagāma ha / tatpuṇyaṃ svapituḥ sthānaṃ svargaṃ surapateriva //
english: Surrounded by a few of his servants, he came with his two brothers to the hallowed hall of his father, resembling the heaven of the king of gods.

sanskrit: dūrādeva dadarśāsau rāmo daśarathaṃ tadā / vṛtaṃ rājasamūhena devaugheneva vāsavam //
english: He saw at a distance his kingly sire seated amidst the assemblage of princes, as Indra surrounded by the gods.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhaviśvāmitrābhyāṃ sevitaṃ pārśvayordvayoḥ / sarvaśāstrārthatajjñena mantrivṛndena mālitam //
english: He was accompanied on either side by the sages Vasishtha and Viswamitra, and respectfully attended by his staff of ministers, all well versed in the interpretation of all Sastras.

sanskrit: cārucāmarahastābhiḥ kāntābhiḥ samupāsitam / kakubbhiriva mūrtābhiḥ saṃsthitābhiryathocitam //
english: He was fanned by charming damsels, waving the fine chowry flappers in their hands, and equalling in beauty the goddesses presiding over the quarters of heaven.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhaviśvāmitrādyāstathā daśarathādayaḥ / dadṛśū rāghavaṃ dūrādupāyāntaṃ guhopamam //
english: Vasishtha, Viswamitra and the other sages, with Dasaratha and his chiefs, saw Rama coming at a distance as beautiful as Skanda himself.

sanskrit: sattvāvaṣṭabdhagarbheṇa śalyeneva himācalam / śritaṃ sakalasevyena gambhīreṇa sphuṭena ca //
english: He appeared by his qualities of mildness and gravity to resemble the mount Himalaya (with his cooling frost and firmness), and was esteemed by all for the depth and clearness.

sanskrit: saumyaṃ samaṃ śubhākāraṃ vinayodāramānasam / kāntopaśāntavapuṣaṃ parasyārthasya bhājanam //
english: He was handsome and well proportioned (in his features), auspicious in his look, but humble and magnanimous in his mind. With loveliness and mildness of his person, he was possessed of all manly prowess.

sanskrit: samudyadyauvanārambhaṃ vṛddhopaśamaśobhanam / anudvignamanānandaṃ pūrṇaprāyamanoratham //
english: He was just developed to youth, yet he was as majestic as an elderly man. He was neither morose nor merry, but seemed to be fully satisfied with himself, as if he had obtained all the objects of his desire.

sanskrit: vicāritajagadyātraṃ pavitraguṇagocaram / mahāsattvaikalobhena guṇairiva samāśritam //
english: He was a good judge of the world, and possessed of all holy virtues. The purity of his mind was the attraction for all the virtues which met in him.

sanskrit: udāramāryamāpūrṇamantaḥkaraṇakoṭaram / avikṣubhitayā vṛttyā darśayantamanuttamam //
english: The receptacle of his mind was filled by his magnanimity and honourable virtues, and the candour of his conduct showed him in the light of perfection.

sanskrit: evaṅguṇagaṇākīrṇo dūrādeva raghūdvahaḥ / parimeyasmitācchācchasvahārāmbarapallavaḥ //
english: Endowed with these various virtues and decorated by his necklace and fine apparel, Rama the support of Raghu's race, approached (his father) with a smiling countenance.

sanskrit: praṇanāma calaccārucūḍāmaṇimarīcinā / śirasā vasudhākampaloladevācalaśriyā //
english: He bowed his head to his father with the sparkling gems trembling in his locks, and imparting to his head the graceful appearance of the mountain Sumeru shaken by an earth-quake.

sanskrit: evaṃ munīndre bruvati pituḥ pādābhivandanam / kartumabhyājagāmātha rāmaḥ kamalalocanaḥ //
english: The lotus-eyed Rama came up to salute the feet of his father, when the lord of the sages (Viswamitra) was speaking with him.

sanskrit: prathamaṃ pitaraṃ paścānmunī mānyaikamānitau / tato viprāṃstato bandhūṃstato gurugaṇānsuhṛt //
english: First of all Rama saluted his father, and then the two honorable sages, he next saluted the Brahmanas, and then his relations, and lastly his elders and well wishing friends.

sanskrit: jagrāha ca tato dṛṣṭyā manāṅmūrdhnā tathā girā / rājalokena vihitāṃ tāṃ praṇāmaparamparām //
english: He then received and returned the salutations of the chiefs and princes, bowing to him with graceful motion of their heads and respectful addresses.

sanskrit: vihitāśīrmunibhyāṃ tu rāmaḥ susamamānasaḥ / āsasāda pituḥ puṇyaṃ samīpaṃ surasundaraḥ //
english: Rama of god-like beauty and equanimity of mind, approached the sacred presence of his father, with the blessings of the two sages.

sanskrit: pādābhivandanaparaṃ tamathāsau mahīpatiḥ / śirasyabhyāliliṅgāśu cucumba ca punaḥpunaḥ //
english: During the act of his saluting the feet of his father, the lord of the earth repeatedly kissed his head and face, and embraced him with fondness.

sanskrit: śatrughnaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ caiva tathaiva paravīrahā / āliliṅga ghanasneho rājahaṃso'mbuje yathā //
english: At the same time, he the destroyer of his enemies, embraced Lakshmana and Satrughna, with as intense an affection as the swan embracing the lotus flowers.

sanskrit: utsaṅge putra tiṣṭheti vadatyatha mahīpatau / bhūmau parijanāstīrṇe soṃ'śuke'tha nyavikṣata //
english: Be you seated my son upon my lap, said the king to Rama, who however, took his seat on a fine piece of cloth spread on the floor by his servants.

sanskrit: rājovāca / putra prāptavivekastvaṃ kalyāṇānāṃ ca bhājanam / jaḍavajjīrṇayā buddhyā khedāyātmā na dīyatām //
english: "The king said ""O my son and receptacle of blessings, you have attained the age of discretion, so put not yourself to that state of self-mortification, as the dull-headed do from their crazy understandings.  "

sanskrit: vṛddhavipraguruproktaṃ tvādṛśenānutiṣṭhatā / padamāsādyate puṇyaṃ na mohamanudhāvatā //
english: Know that it is by following the course of his elders, guides and Brahmanas, that one attains to meritoriousness, and not by his persistence in error.

sanskrit: tāvadevā''pado dūre tiṣṭhanti paripelavāḥ / yāvadeva na mohasya prasaraḥ putra dīyate //
english: "So long will the train of our misfortunes lie at a distance, as we do not allow the seeds of error to have access to us.""  "

sanskrit: śrīvasiṣṭha uvāca / rājaputra mahābāho śūrastvaṃ vijitāstvayā / durucchedā durārambhā apyamī viṣayārayaḥ //
english: Vasishtha said, Oh strong armed prince! you are truly heroic to have conquered your worldly appetites, which are at once as difficult to be eradicated as they are fierce in their action.

sanskrit: kimatajjña ivājñānāṃ yogye vyāmohasāgare / vinimajjasi kallolabahule jāḍyaśālini //
english: Why do you allow yourself like the unlearned, to be drowned in this rolling sea of errors, causing such dull inactivity in you?

sanskrit: viśvāmitra uvāca calannīlotpalavyūhasamalocanalolatām / brūhi cetaḥkṛtāṃ tyaktvā hetunā kena muhyasi //
english: "Viswamitra said ""why are your eyes so unsteady (with doubts) as the tremulous clusters of blue lotuses. You ought to do away with this unsteadiness, and tell us what is that grief (which rankles) in your mind.  "

sanskrit: kiṃniṣṭhāḥ ke ca te kena kiyantaḥ kāraṇena te / ādhayaḥ pravilumpanti mano gehamivākhavaḥ //
english: What are these thoughts, and what are their names and natures, their number and causes, that infest your mind like its maladies (in the same manner) as the mice undermine a fabric.

sanskrit: manye nānucitānāṃ tvamādhīnāṃ padamuttamam / āpatsu cā'prayojyaṃ te nihīnā api cādhayaḥ //
english: I am disposed to think, that you are not the person to be troubled with those evils and distempers, to which the base and vile alone are subject.

sanskrit: yathābhimatamāśu tvaṃ brūhi prāpsyasi cānagha / sarvameva punaryena bhetsyante tvāṃ tu nādhayaḥ //
english: Tell me the craving of your heart, O sinless Rama! and they will be requited in a manner, as will prevent their recurrence to you.

sanskrit: ityuktamasya sumate raghuvaṃśaketurākarṇya vākyamucitārthavilāsagarbham / tatyāja khedamabhigarjati vārivāhe barhī yathā tvanumitābhimatārthasiddhiḥ //
english: Rama said:—the standard of Raghu's race having listened to the reasonable and graceful speech of the good-intentioned sage, shook off his sorrowing, like the peacock at the roaring of a cloud, in the hope of gaining his object.

sanskrit: vālmīkiruvāca / iti pṛṣṭo munīndreṇa samāśvasya ca rāghavaḥ / uvāca vacanaṃ cāru paripūrṇārthamantharam //
english: Valmiki related:—Being thus asked with soothing words by the chief of the sages, Rama made his answer in a soft and graceful speech replete with good sense.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / bhagavanbhavatā pṛṣṭo yathāvadadhunā'khilam / kathayāmyahamajño'pi ko laṅghayati sadvacaḥ //
english: Rama said, Oh venerable sage! I will tell thee in truth, untutored though I am, all the particulars as asked by thee; for who would disobey the bidding of the wise?

sanskrit: ahaṃ tāvadayaṃ jāto nije'sminpitṛsadmani / krameṇa vṛddhiṃ saṃprāptaḥ prāptavidyaśca saṃsthitaḥ //
english: Since I was born in this mansion of my father I have all along remained, grown up and received my education.

sanskrit: tataḥ sadācāraparo bhūtvāhaṃ munināyaka / vihṛtastīrthayātrārthamurvīmambudhimekhalām //
english: Then O leader of sages! being desirous to learn good usages (of mankind), I set out to travel to holy places all over this sea-girt earth.

sanskrit: etāvatātha kālena saṃsārāsthāmimāṃ haran / samudbhūto manasi me vicāraḥ so'yamīdṛśaḥ //
english: It was by this time that there arose a train of reflections in my mind of the following nature which shook my confidence in worldly objects.

sanskrit: vivekena parītātmā tenāhaṃ tadanu svayam / bhoganīrasayā buddhyā pravicāritavānidam //
english: My mind was employed in the discrimination of the nature of things which led me gradually to discard all thoughts of sensual enjoyments.

sanskrit: kiṃnāmedaṃ bata sukhaṃ yeyaṃ saṃsārasaṃtatiḥ / jāyate mṛtaye loko mriyate jananāya ca //
english: What are these worldly pleasures good for, (thought I), and what means the multiplication (of our species) on earth? Men are born to die, and they die to be born again.

sanskrit: asthirāḥ sarva eveme sacarācaraceṣṭitāḥ / āpadāṃ patayaḥ pāpā bhāvā vibhavabhūmayaḥ //
english: There is no stability in the tendencies of beings whether movable or immovable. They all tend to vice, decay and danger; and all our possessions are the grounds of our penury.

sanskrit: ayaḥśalākāsadṛśāḥ parasparamasaṅginaḥ / śliṣyante kevalaṃ bhāvā manaḥkalpanayā svayā //
english: All objects (of sense) are detached from each other as iron rods or needles from one another; it is imagination alone which attaches them to our minds.

sanskrit: manaḥsamāyattamidaṃ jagadābhogi dṛśyate / manaścāsadivābhāti kena sma parimohitāḥ //
english: It is the mind that pictures the existence of the world as a reality, but the deceptiveness of the mind (being known) we are safe from such deception.

sanskrit: asataiva vayaṃ kaṣṭaṃ vikṛṣṭā mūḍhabuddhayaḥ / mṛgatṛṣṇāmbhasā dūre vane mugdhamṛgā iva //
english: If the world is an unreality, it is a pity that ignorant men should be allured by it, like the deer tempted by a distant mirage (appearing) as water.

sanskrit: na kenacicca vikrītā vikrītā iva saṃsthitāḥ / bata mūḍhā vayaṃ sarve jānānā api śāmbaram //
english: We are sold by none (to any one) and yet we remain as if enslaved to the world; and knowing this well, we are spellbound to riches, as it were by the magic wand of Sambara.

sanskrit: kimeteṣu prapañceṣu bhogā nāma sudurbhagāḥ / mudhaiva hi vayaṃ mohātsaṃsthitā baddhabhāvanāḥ //
english: What are the enjoyments in this quintessence (of the world) but misery; and yet we are foolishly caught in its thoughts, as if clogged in honey.

sanskrit: ā jñātaṃ bahukālena vyarthameva vayaṃ vane / mohe nipatitā mugdhāḥ śvabhre mugdhā mṛgā iva //
english: Ah! I perceive after long that we have insensibly fallen into errors, like senseless stags falling into caverns in the wilderness.

sanskrit: kiṃ me rājyena kiṃ bhogaiḥ ko'haṃ kimidamāgatam / yanmithyaivāstu tanmithyā kasya nāma kimāgatam //
english: Of what use is royalty and these enjoyments to me? What am I and whence are all these things? They are but vanities, and let them continue as such without any good or loss to any body.

sanskrit: evaṃ vimṛśato brahmansarveṣveva tato mama / bhāveṣvaratirāyātā pathikasya maruṣviva //
english: Reasoning in this manner Oh Brahman, I came to be disgusted with the world, like a traveller in (his journey through) a desert.

sanskrit: tadetadbhagavanbrūhi kimidaṃ pariṇaśyati / kimidaṃ jāyate bhūyaḥ kimidaṃ parivardhate //
english: Now tell me, O venerable sir! whether this world is advancing to its dissolution, or continued reproduction, or is it in course of its endless progression?

sanskrit: jarāmaraṇamāpacca jananaṃ saṃpadastathā / āvirbhāvatirobhāvairvivardhante punaḥpunaḥ //
english: If there is any progress here, it is that of the appearance and disappearance of old age and decease, of prosperity and adversity by turns.

sanskrit: bhogaistaireva taireva tucchairvayamamī kila / paśya jarjaratāṃ nītā vātairiva giridrumāḥ //
english: Behold how the variety of our trifling enjoyments hastens our decay, they are like hurricanes shattering the mountain trees.

sanskrit: acetanā iva janāḥ pavanaiḥ prāṇanāmabhiḥ / dhvanantaḥ saṃsthitā vyarthaṃ yathā kīcakaveṇavaḥ //
english: Men continue in vain to breathe their vital breath as hollow-bamboo wind-pipes having no sense.

sanskrit: śāmyatīdaṃ kathaṃ duḥkhamiti tapto'smi cintayā / jaraddruma ivogreṇa koṭarasthena vahninā //
english: How is (human) misery to be alleviated, is the (only) thought that consumes me like wild fire in the hollow of a withered tree.

sanskrit: saṃsāraduḥkhapāṣāṇanīrandhrahṛdayo'pyaham / nijalokabhayādeva galadvāṣpaṃ na rodimi //
english: The weight of worldly miseries sits heavy on my heart as a rock, and obstructs my lungs to breathe out. I have a mind to weep, but am prevented from shedding my tears for fear of my people.

sanskrit: śūnyā manmukhavṛttīstāḥ śuṣkarodananīrasāḥ / viveka eva hṛtsaṃstho mamaikānteṣu paśyati //
english: My tearless weeping and speechless mouth, give no indication of my inward sorrow to any body, except my consciousness the silent witness in my solitude.

sanskrit: bhṛśaṃ muhyāmi saṃsmṛtya bhāvābhāvamayīṃ sthitim / dāridryeṇeva subhago dūre saṃsāraceṣṭayā //
english: I wait to think on the positive and negative states (of worldly bliss), as a ruined man bewails to reflect on his former state of affluence.

sanskrit: mohayanti manovṛttiṃ khaṇḍayanti guṇāvalim / duḥkhajālaṃ prayacchanti vipralambhaparāḥ śriyaḥ //
english: I take prosperity to be a seducing cheat, for its deluding the mind, impairing the good qualities (of men), and spreading the net of our miseries.

sanskrit: cintānicayacakrāṇi nānandāya dhanāni me / saṃprasūtakalatrāṇi gṛhāṇyugrāpadāmiva //
english: To me, like one fallen into great difficulties, no riches, offspring, consorts or home afford any delight, but they seem to be (so many sources of) misery.

sanskrit: vividhadoṣadaśāparicintanairvitatabhaṅgurakāraṇakalpitaiḥ / mama na nirvṛtimeti mano mune nigaḍitasya yathā vanadantinaḥ //
english: I, like a wild elephant in chains, find no rest in my mind, by reflecting on the various evils of the world, and by thinking on the causes of our frailties.

sanskrit: khalāḥ kālekāle niśi niśitamohaikamihikāgatāloke loke viṣayaśatacaurāḥ sucaturāḥ / pravṛttāḥ prodyuktā diśidiśi vivekaikaharaṇe raṇe śaktāsteṣāṃ ka iva viduṣaḥprojjhya subhaṭāḥ //
english: There are wicked passions prying at all times, under the dark mist of the night of our ignorance; and there are hundreds of objects, which like so many cunning rogues, are about all men in broad day-light, and lurking on all sides to rob us of our reason. What mighty champions can we delegate (now) to fight with these than our knowledge of truth?

sanskrit: trayodaśaḥ sargaḥ śrīrāma uvāca / iyamasminsthitodārā saṃsāre parikalpitā / śrīrmune parimohāya sāpi nūnaṃ kadarthadā //
english: Rama said:—It is opulence, Oh sage! that is reckoned a blessing here; it is even she that is the cause of our troubles and errors.

sanskrit: ullāsabahulānantakallolānalamākulān / jaḍānpravahati sphārānprāvṛṣīva taraṅgiṇī //
english: She bears away as a river in the rainy season, all high-spirited simpletons overpowered by its current.

sanskrit: cintāduhitaro bahvayo bhūridurlalitaidhitāḥ / cañcalāḥ prabhavantyasyāstaraṅgāḥ sarito yathā //
english: Her daughters are anxieties fostered by many a malpractice, like the waves of a stream raised by the winds.

sanskrit: eṣā hi padamekatra na nibadhnāti durbhagā / dagdhevāniyatācāramitaścetaśca dhāvati //
english: She can never stand steady on her legs any where, but like a wretched woman who has burnt her feet, she limps from one place to another.

sanskrit: janayantī paraṃ dāhaṃ parāmṛṣṭāṅgikā satī / vināśameva dhatte'ntardīpalekheva kajjalam //
english: Fortune like a lamp both burns and blackens its possessor, until it is extinguished by its own inflammation.

sanskrit: guṇāguṇavicāreṇa vinaiva kila pārśvagam / rājaprakṛtivanmūḍhā durārūḍhā'valambate //
english: She is unapproachable as princes and fools, and likewise as favourable as they to her adherents, without scanning their merits or faults.

sanskrit: karmaṇā tenatenaiṣā vistāramanugacchati / doṣāśīviṣavegasya yatkṣīraṃ vistarāyate //
english: She begets only evils in them by their various acts (of profligacy), as good milk given to serpents, serves but to increase the poignancy of their poison.

sanskrit: tāvacchītamṛdusparśāḥ pare sve ca jane janāḥ / vātyayeva himaṃ yāvacchriyā na paruṣīkṛtāḥ //
english: Men (by nature) are gentle and kind hearted to friends and strangers, until they are hardheartened by their riches, which like blasts of wind, serve to stiffen (the liquid) frost.

sanskrit: prājñāḥ śūrāḥ kṛtajñāśca peśalā mṛdavaśca ye / pāṃsumuṣṭyeva maṇayaḥ śriyā te malinīkṛtāḥ //
english: As brilliant gems are soiled by dust, so are the learned, the brave, the grateful, the mild and gentle, corrupted by riches.

sanskrit: na śrīḥ sukhāya bhagavanduḥkhāyaiva hi vardhate / guptā vināśanaṃ dhatte mṛtiṃ viṣalatā yathā //
english: Riches do not conduce to one's happiness, but redound to his woe and destruction, as the plant aconite when fostered, hides in itself the fatal poison.

sanskrit: śrīmānajananindyaśca śūraścāpyavikatthanaḥ / samadṛṣṭiḥ prabhuścaiva durlabhāḥ puruṣāstrayaḥ //
english: A rich man without blemish, a brave man devoid of vanity, and a master wanting partiality, are the three rarities on earth.

sanskrit: eṣā hi viṣamā duḥkhabhogināṃ gahanā guhā / ghanamohagajendrāṇāṃ vindhyaśailamahātaṭī //
english: The rich are as inaccessible as the dark cavern of a dragon, and as unapproachable as the deep wilderness of the Vindhya mountain inhabited by fierce elephants.

sanskrit: satkāryapadmarajanī duḥkhakairavacandrikā / sudṛṣṭidīpikāvātyā kallolaughataraṅgiṇī //
english: Riches like the shadow of night, overcast the good qualities of men, and like moon-beams brings to bloom the buds of their misery. They blow away the brightness of a fair prospect as a hurricane, and resemble a sea with huge surges.

sanskrit: saṃbhramābhrādipadavī viṣādaviṣavardhinī / kedārikā vikalpānāṃ khedāyabhayabhoginī //
english: They bring upon us a cloud of fear and error, increase the poison of despondence and regret, and are like the dreadful snakes in the field of our choice.

sanskrit: himaṃ vairāgyavallīnāṃ vikārolūkayāminī / rāhudaṃṣṭrā vivekendoḥ saujanyāmbhojacandrikā //
english: Fortune is (as a killing) frost to the bondsmen of asceticism, and as the night to the owls of libertinism; she is an eclipse to the moonlight of reason, and as moonbeams to the bloom of the lilies of folly.

sanskrit: indrāyudhavadālolanānārāgamanoharā / lolā taḍidivotpannadhvaṃsinī ca jaḍāśrayā //
english: She is as transitory as the Iris, and alike pleasant to view by the play of her colours; she is as fickle as the lightning, which vanishes no sooner it appears to sight. Hence none but the ignorant have reliance in her.

sanskrit: cāpalāvajitāraṇya nakulī nakulīnajā / vipralambhanatātparyajitogramṛgatṛṣṇikā //
english: She is as unsteady as a well born damsel following a base-born man to the words; and like a (deceptive) mirage that tempts the run-aways to fall to it as the doe.

sanskrit: laharīvaikarūpeṇa padaṃ kṣaṇamakurvatī / calā dīpaśikhevātidurjñeyagatigocarā //
english: Unsteady as the wave, she is never steady in any place; (but is ever wavering to all sides) like the flickering flame of a lamp. So her leaning is known to nobody.

sanskrit: siṃhīva vigrahavyagrakarīndrakulapothinī / khaḍgadhāreva śiśirā tīkṣṇatīkṣṇāśayāśrayā //
english: She like the lioness is ever prompt in fighting, and like the leader of elephants favourable to her partizans. She is as sharp as the blade of a sword (to cut off all obstacles), and is the patroness of sharp-witted sharpers.

sanskrit: nānayāpahṛtārthinyā durādhiparilīnayā / paśyāmyabhavyayā lakṣmyā kiṃcidduḥkhādṛte sukham //
english: I see no felicity in uncivil prosperity, which is full of treachery, and replete with every kind of danger and trouble.

sanskrit: dūreṇotsāritā'lakṣmyā punareva samādarāt / aho batāśliṣyatīva nirlajjā durjanā sadā //
english: It is pity that prosperity, like a shameless wench will again lay hold on a man, after being abandoned by him in his association with (her rival) Poverty.

sanskrit: manoramā karṣati cittavṛttiṃ kadarthasādhyā kṣaṇabhaṅgurā ca / vyālāvalīgātravivṛttadehā śvabhrotthitā puṣpalateva lakṣmīḥ //
english: What is she with all her loveliness and attraction of human hearts, but momentary thing obtained by all manner of evil means, and resembling at best a flower shrub, growing out of a cave inhabited by a snake, and beset by reptiles all about its stem.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / āyuḥ pallavakoṇāgralambāmbukaṇabhaṅguram / unmattamiva saṃtyajya yātyakāṇḍe śarīrakam //
english: Human life is as frail as a pendant drop of water trembling on the tip of a leaflet; and as irrepressible as a raving madman, that breaks loose from its bodily imprisonment out of its proper season.

sanskrit: viṣayāśīviṣāsaṅgaparijarjaracetasām / aprauḍhātmavivekānāmāyurāyāsakāraṇam //
english: Again the lives of those whose minds are infected by the poison of worldly affairs, and who are incapable of judging for themselves, are (varily) but causes of their torment.

sanskrit: ye tu vijñātavijñeyā viśrāntā vitate pade / bhāvābhāvasamāśvāsamāyusteṣāṃ sukhāyate //
english: Those knowing the knowable, and resting in the all-pervading spirit, and acquiescing alike to their wants and gains, enjoy lives of perfect tranquility.

sanskrit: vayaṃ parimitākārapariniṣṭhitaniścayāḥ / saṃsārābhrataḍitpuñje mune nāyuṣi nirvṛtāḥ //
english: We that have certain belief of our being but limited beings, can have no enjoyment in our transient lives, which are but flashes of lightnings amidst the cloudy sky of the world.

sanskrit: yujyate veṣṭanaṃ vāyorākāśasya ca khaṇḍanam / grathanaṃ ca taraṅgāṇāmāsthā nāyuṣi yujyate //
english: It is as impossible to keep the winds in confinement, to tear asunder the sky to pieces, and wreathe the waves to a chaplet, as to place any reliance in our lives.

sanskrit: pelavaṃ śaradīvābhramasneha iva dīpakaḥ / taraṅgaka ivālolaṃ gatamevopalakṣyate //
english: Fast as the fleeting clouds in autumn, and short as the light of an oilless lamp, our lives appear to pass away as evanescent as the rolling waves in the sea.

sanskrit: taraṅgaṃ pratibimbenduṃ taḍitpuñjaṃ nabhombujam / grahītumāsthāṃ badhnāmi na tvāyuṣi hatasthitau //
english: Rather attempt to lay hold on the shadow of the moon in the waves, the fleeting lightenings in the sky, and the ideal lotus blossoms in the ether, than ever place any reliance upon this unsteady life.

sanskrit: aviśrāntamanāḥ śūnyamāyurātatamīhate / duḥkhāyaiva vimūḍho'ntargarbhamaśvatarī yathā //
english: Men of restless minds, desiring to prolong their useless and toilsome lives, resemble the she-mule conceiving by a horse.

sanskrit: saṃsārasaṃsṛtāvasyāṃ pheno'sminsargasāgare / kāyavallayāmbhaso brahmañjīvitaṃ me na rocate //
english: This world (Sansara) is as a whirlpool amidst the ocean of creation, and every individual body is as (evanescent) as a foam or froth or bubble, which can give me no relish in this life.

sanskrit: prāpyaṃ saṃprāpyate yena bhūyo yena na śocyate / parāyā nirvṛteḥ sthānaṃ yattajjīvitamucyate //
english: That is called true living, which gains what is worth gaining, which has no cause of sorrow or remorse, and which is a state of transcendental tranquility.

sanskrit: taravo'pi hi jīvanti jīvanti mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ / sa jīvati mano yasya mananena na jīvati //
english: There is a vegetable life in plants, and an animal life in beasts, and birds: man leads a thinking life, but true life is above (the succession of) thoughts.

sanskrit: jātāsta eva jagati jantavaḥ sādhujīvitāḥ / ye punarneha jāyante śeṣā jaraṭhagardabhāḥ //
english: All those living beings are said to have lived well in this earth, who being once born herein have no more to return to it. The rest are no better than old asses.

sanskrit: bhāro'vivekinaḥ śāstraṃ bhāro jñānaṃ ca rāgiṇaḥ / aśāntasya mano bhāro bhāro'nātmavido vapuḥ //
english: Knowledge is an encumbrance to the unthinking, and wisdom is cumbersome to the passionate; intellect—is a heavy load to the restless, and the body is a ponderous burden to one ignorant of his soul.

sanskrit: rūpamāyurmano buddhirahaṃkārastathehitam / bhāro bhāradharasyeva sarvaṃ duḥkhāya durdhiyaḥ //
english: A goodly person possessed of life, mind, intellect and self-consciousness and its occupations, is of no avail to the unwise, but seem to be his over-loadings as those upon a porter.

sanskrit: aviśrāntamanāpūrṇamāpadāṃ paramāspadam / nīḍaṃ rogavihaṅgānāmāyurāyāsanaṃ dṛḍham //
english: The discontented mind is the great arena of all evils, and the nestling place of diseases which alight upon it like birds of the air: such a life is the abode of toil and misery.

sanskrit: pratyahaṃ khedamutsṛjya śanairalamanāratam / ākhuneva jaracchubhraṃ kālena vinihanyate //
english: As a house is slowly dilapidated by the mice continually burrowing under it, so is the body of the living gradually corroded by the (pernicious) teeth of time boring within it.

sanskrit: śarīrabilaviśrāntairviṣadāhapradāyibhiḥ / rogairāpīyate raudrairvyālairiva vanānilaḥ //
english: Deadly diseases bred within the body, feed upon our vital breath, as poisonous snakes born in caves of the woods consume the meadow air.

sanskrit: prasnuvānairavicchedaṃ tucchairantaravāsibhiḥ / duḥkhairāvṛścyate krūrairghuṇairiva jaraddrumaḥ //
english: As the withered tree is perforated by minutest worms residing in them, so are our bodies continually wasted by many inborn diseases and noxious secretions.

sanskrit: nūnaṃ nigaraṇāyāśu ghanagardhamanāratam / ākhurmārjārakeṇeva maraṇenāvalokyate //
english: Death is incessantly staring and growling at our face, as a cat looks and purrs at the mouse in order to devour it.

sanskrit: gandhādiguṇagarbhiṇyā śūnyayā'śaktiveśyayā / annaṃ mahāśaneneva jarayā parijīryate //
english: Old age wastes us as soon as a glutton digests his food;and it reduces one to weakness as an old harlot, by no other charm than her paint and perfumes.

sanskrit: dinaiḥ katipayaireva parijñāya gatādaram / durjanaḥ sujaneneva yauvanenāvamucyate //
english: Youth forsakes us as soon, as a good man abandons his wicked friend in disgust, after his foibles come to be known to him in a few days.

sanskrit: vināśasuhṛdā nityaṃ jarāmaraṇabandhunā / rūpaṃ khiṅgavareṇeva kṛtāntenābhilaṣyate //
english: Death the lover of destruction, and friend of old age and ruin, likes the sensual man, as a lecher likes a beauty.

sanskrit: sthiratayā sukhabhāsitayā tayā satatamujjñitamuttamaphalgu ca / jagati nāsti tathā guṇavarjitaṃ maraṇabhājanamāyuridaṃ yathā //
english: Thus there is nothing so worthless in the world as this life, which is devoid of every good quality and ever subject to death, unless it is attended by the permanent felicity of emancipation.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / mudhaivābhyutthito mohānmudhaiva parivardhate / mithyāmayena bhīto'smi durahaṃkāraśatruṇā //
english: Rama continued:—Egoism springs from false conceit, and it is vanity (or vain glory) which fosters it; I am much afraid of this baneful egotism which is an enemy.

sanskrit: ahaṃkāravaśādeva doṣakośakadarthatām / dadāti dīnadīnānāṃ saṃsāro vividhākṛtiḥ //
english: It is under the influence of egotism that all men in this diversified world, and even the very poorest of them, fall into the dungeon of evils, and misdeeds.

sanskrit: ahaṃkāravaśādāpadahaṃkārāhurādhayaḥ / ahaṃkāravaśādīhā tvahaṃkāro mamāmayaḥ //
english: All accidents, anxieties, troubles and wicked exertions proceed from egoism or self-confidence; hence I deem egoism as a disease.

sanskrit: tamahaṃkāramāśritya paramaṃ ciravairiṇam / na bhuje na pibāmyambhaḥ kimu bhogānbhuje mune //
english: Being subject to that everlasting arch-enemy—the cynic egoism, I have refrained from my food and drink. What other enjoyment is there for me to partake of?

sanskrit: saṃsārarajanī dīrghā māyā manasi mohinī / tato'haṃkāradoṣeṇa kirāteneva vāgurā //
english: This world resembles a long continuous night, in which our egoism like a hunter, spreads the snare of affections.

sanskrit: yāni duḥkhāni dīrghāṇi viṣamāṇi mahānti ca / ahaṃkārātprasūtāni tānyagātkhadirā iva //
english: All our great and intolerable miseries, growing as rank as the thorny plants of the catechu, are but results of our egoism.

sanskrit: śamendusaiṃhikeyāsyaṃ guṇapadmahimāśanim / sāmyameghaśaratkālamahaṃkāraṃ tyajāmyaham //
english: It overcasts the equanimity of mind as an eclipse overshadows the moon; it destroys our virtues as a frost destroys the lotus flowers; it dispels the peace of men as the autumn drives away the clouds. I must therefore get rid of this egoistic feeling.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ rāmo na me vāñchā bhāveṣu na ca me manaḥ / śānta āsitumicchāmi svātmanīva jino yathā //
english: I am not Rama the prince, I have no desire nor should I wish for affluence; but I wish to have the peace of my mind and remain as the self-satisfied old sage Jina.

sanskrit: ahaṃkāravaśādyadyanmayā bhuktaṃ hutaṃ kṛtam / sarvaṃ tattadavastveva vastvahaṃkārariktatā //
english: All that I have eaten, done or offered in sacrifice under the influence of egoism, have gone for nothing; it is the absence of egoism which (I call) to be real good.

sanskrit: ahamityasti cedbrahmannahamāpadi duḥkhitaḥ / nāsti cetsukhitastasmādanahaṃkāritā varam //
english: So long, O Brahman! as there is (the feeling of) egoism in one, he is subject to sorrow at his difficulties; but being devoid of it, he becomes happy; hence it is better to be without it.

sanskrit: ahaṃkāraṃ parityajya mune śāntamanastayā / avatiṣṭhe gatodvego bhogaugho bhaṅgurāspadaḥ //
english: I am free from anxiety, O sage! ever since I have got the tranquility of my mind after giving up my (sense of) egoism; and known the transitoriness of all enjoyments.

sanskrit: brahmanyāvadahaṃkāravāridaḥ parijṛmbhate / tāvadvikāsamāyāti tṛṣṇākuṭajamañjarī //
english: As long, O Brahman! as the cloud of egoism overspreads (the region of our minds), so long our desires expand themselves like the buds of kurchi plants.

sanskrit: ahaṃkāraghane śānte tṛṣṇā navataḍillatā / śāntadīpaśikhāvṛttyā kvāpi yātyatisatvaram //
english: But when the cloud of egoism is dispersed, the lightning of avarice vanishes away, just as the lamp being extinguished, its light immediately disappears.

sanskrit: ahaṃkāramahāvindhye manomattamahāgajaḥ / visphūrjati ghanāsphoṭaiḥ stanitairiva vāridaḥ //
english: The mind vaunts with egoism, like a furious elephant in the Vindhyan hills, when it hears the thunder-claps in the clouds.

sanskrit: iha dehamahāraṇye ghanāhaṃkārakesarī / yo'yamullasati sphārastenedaṃ jagadātatam //
english: Again egoism residing like a lion in the vast forest of all human bodies, ranges about at large throughout the whole extent of this earth.

sanskrit: tṛṣṇātantulavaprotā bahujanmaparamparā / ahaṃkārograkhiṅgena kaṇṭhe muktāvalī kṛtā //
english: The self-conceited are decorated with a string of pearls about their necks, of which avarice forms the thread, and repeated births—the pearls.

sanskrit: putramitrakalatrāditantramantravivarjitam / prasāritamaneneha mune'haṃkāravairiṇā //
english: Our inveterate enemy of egoism, has (like a magician) spread about us the enchantments of our wives, friends and children, whose spells it is hard to break.

sanskrit: pramārjite'hamityasminpade svayamapi drutam / pramārjitā bhavantyete sarva eva durādhayaḥ //
english: As soon as the (impression of the) word (ego) is effaced from the mind, all our anxieties and troubles are wiped out of it.

sanskrit: ahamityambude śānte śanaiśca śamaśātinī / manogaganasaṃmohamihikā kvāpi gacchati //
english: The cloud of egoism being dispelled from the sky of our minds, the mist of error which it spreads to destroy our peace, will be dispersed also.

sanskrit: nirahaṃkāravṛtterme maurkhyācchokena sīdataḥ / yatkiṃciducitaṃ brahmaṃstadākhyātumihārhasi //
english: I have given up my (sense of) egoism, yet is my mind stupified with sorrow by my ignorance. Tell me, O Brahman! what thou thinkest right for me under these circumstances.

sanskrit: sarvāpadāṃ nilayamadhruvamantarasthamunmuktamuttamaguṇena na saṃśrayāmi / yatnādahaṃkṛtipadaṃ parito'tiduḥkhaṃ śeṣeṇa māṃ samanuśādhi mahānubhāva //
english: I have with much ado given up this egoism, and like no more to resort to this source of all evils and perturbation. It retains its seat in the breast for our annoyance only, and without benefiting us by any good quality of its own. Direct me now, you men of great understandings!

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / doṣairjarjaratāṃ yāti satkāryādāryasevanāt / vātāntaḥpicchalavavaccetaścalati cañcalam //
english: Our minds are infested by evil passions and faults, and fluctuate in their observance of duty and service to superiors, as the plumes of a peacock fluttering at the breeze.

sanskrit: itaścetaśca suvyagraṃ vyarthamevābhidhāvati / dūrāddūrataraṃ dīnaṃ grāme kauleyako yathā //
english: They rove about at random with ardour and without rest from one place to another, like the poor village dog running afar and wide in quest of food.

sanskrit: na prāpnoti kvacitkiṃcitprāptairapi mahādhanaiḥ / nāntaḥ saṃpūrṇatāmeti karaṇḍaka ivāmbubhiḥ //
english: It seldom finds any thing any where, and happening even to get a good store some where, it is as little content with it as a wicker vessel filled with water.

sanskrit: nityameva mune śūnyaṃ kadāśāvāgurāvṛtam / na mano nivṛtiṃ yāti mṛgo yūthādiva cyutaḥ //
english: The vacant mind, Oh sage! is ever entrapped in its evil desires, and is never at rest with itself; but roves at large as a stray deer separated from its herd.

sanskrit: taraṅgataralāṃ vṛttiṃ dadhadālūnaśīrṇatām / parityajya kṣaṇamapi hṛdaye yāti na sthitim //
english: Human mind is of the nature of the unsteady wave, and as light as the minutest particle. It can therefore have no rest in spite of (the fickleness and levity of) its nature.

sanskrit: mano mananavikṣubdhaṃ diśo daśa vidhāvati / mandarāhananoddhūtaṃ kṣīrārṇavapayo yathā //
english: Disturbed by its thoughts, the mind is tossed in all directions, like the waters of the milk-white ocean when churned by the Mandara mountain.

sanskrit: kallolakalitāvartaṃ māyāmakaramālitam / na niroddhuṃ samartho'smi manomayamahārṇavam //
english: I can not curb my mind, resembling the vast ocean (in its course), and running with its huge surges (of the passions), with whirlpools (of error), and beset by the whales of delusion.

sanskrit: bhogadūrvāṅkurākāṅkṣī śvabhrapātamacintayan / manohariṇako brahmandūraṃ viparidhāvati //
english: Our minds run afar, O Brahman! after sensual enjoyments, like the deer running towards the tender blades of grass, and unmindful of falling into the pits.

sanskrit: na kadācana me cetaḥ svāmālūnaviśīrṇatām / tyajatyākulayā vṛttyā cañcalatvamivārṇavaḥ //
english: The mind can never get rid of its wavering state owing to the habitual fickleness of its nature, resembling the restlessness of the sea.

sanskrit: cetaścañcalayā vṛttyā cintānicayacañcuram / dhṛtiṃ badhnāti naikatra pañjare kesarī yathā //
english: The mind with its natural fickleness and restless thoughts, finds no repose at any place, as a lion (has no rest) in his prison-house.

sanskrit: mano moharathārūḍhaṃ śarīrātsamatāsukham / haratyapahatodvegaṃ haṃsaḥ kṣīramivāmbhasaḥ //
english: The mind seated in the car of delusion, absorbs the sweet, peaceful and undisturbed rest of the body, like the gander sucking up pure milk from amidst the water.

sanskrit: analpakalpanātalpe vilīnāścittavṛttayaḥ / munīndra na prabudhyante tena tapye'hamākulaḥ //
english: O chief of sages! I grieve much to find the faculties of the mind lying dormant upon the bed of imaginary delights, from which it is hard to waken them.

sanskrit: kroḍīkṛtadṛḍhagranthitṛṣṇāsūtre sthitātmanā / vihago jālakeneva brahmanbaddho'smi cetasā //
english: I am caught, O Brahman! like a bird in the net by the knots (of my egoism), and held fast in it by the thread of my avarice.

sanskrit: saṃtatāmarṣadhūmena cintājvālākulena ca / vahnineva tṛṇaṃ śuṣkaṃ mune dagdho'smi cetasā //
english: I burn in my mind, O sage, like the dried hay on fire, by the flame of my anxieties and under the spreading fumes of my impatience.

sanskrit: krūreṇa jaḍatāṃ yātastṛṣṇābhāryānugāminā / śavaṃ kauleyakeneva brahmanmukto'smi cetasā //
english: I am devoured, O Brahman! like a clod of cold meat, by the cruelty and greediness of my heart, as a carcase is swallowed by a hungry dog and its greedy mate.

sanskrit: taraṅgataralāsphālavṛttinā jaḍarūpiṇā / taṭavṛkṣa ivaughena brahmannīto'smi cetasā //
english: I am borne away, O sage! by the current of my heart, as a tree on the bank is carried away by the waters and waves beating upon it.

sanskrit: avāntaranipātāya śūnye vā bhramaṇāya ca / tṛṇaṃ caṇḍānileneva dūre nīto'smi cetasā //
english: I am led afar by my (greedy) mind, like a straw carried off by the hurricane, either to flutter in the air or fall upon the ground.

sanskrit: saṃsārajaladherasmānnityamuttaraṇonmukhaḥ / setuneva payaḥpūro rodhito'smi kucetasā //
english: My earthly mindedness has put a stop to my desire of crossing over the ocean of the world, as an embankment stops the course of the waters.

sanskrit: pātālādgacchatā pṛthvīṃ pṛthvyāḥ pātālagāminā / kūpakāṣṭhaṃ kudāmneva veṣṭito'smi kucetasā //
english: I am lifted up and let down again by the baseness of my heart, like a log of wood tied to a rope dragging it in and out of a well.

sanskrit: mithyaiva sphārarūpeṇa vicārādviśarāruṇā / bālo vetālakeneva gṛhīto'smi kucetasā //
english: As a child is seized by the false apparition of a demon, so I find myself in the grasp of my wicked mind, representing falsities as true.

sanskrit: vahneruṣṇataraḥ śailādapi kaṣṭatarakramaḥ / vajrādapi dṛḍho brahmandurnigrahamanograhaḥ //
english: It is hard to repress the mind, which is hotter than fire, more inaccessible than a hill, and stronger than a thunder bolt.

sanskrit: cetaḥ patati kāryeṣu vihagaḥ svāmiṣeṣviva / kṣaṇena viratiṃ yāti bālaḥ krīḍanakādiva //
english: The mind is attracted to its objects as a bird to its prey, and has no respite for a moment as a boy from his play.

sanskrit: jaḍaprakṛtirālolo vitatāvartavṛttimān / mano'bdhirahitavyālo dūraṃ nayati tāta mām //
english: My mind resembling the sea both in its dullness as well as restlessness, in its extent and fulness with whirlpools and dragons, keeps me far from advancing towards it.

sanskrit: apyabdhipānānmahataḥ sumerūnmūlanādapi / api vahnyaśanātsādho viṣamaścittanigrahaḥ //
english: It is more difficult to subdue the mind than to drink off the ocean, or to upset the Sumeru mountain. It is ever harder than the hardest thing.

sanskrit: cittaṃ kāraṇamarthānāṃ tasminsati jagattrayam / tasminkṣīṇe jagatkṣīṇaṃ taccikitsyaṃ prayatnataḥ //
english: The mind is the cause of all exertions, and the sensorium of the three worlds. Its weakness weakens all worldliness, and requires to be cured with care.

sanskrit: cittādimāni sukhaduḥkhaśatāni nūnamabhyāgatānyagavarādiva kānanāni / tasminvivekavaśatastanutāṃ prayāte manye mune nipuṇameva galanti tāni //
english: It is the mind from which arise our pains and pleasures by hundreds, as the woods growing in groups upon a hill; but no sooner is the scythe of reason applied to them, than they fall off one by one.

sanskrit: sakalaguṇajayāśā yatra baddhā mahadbhistamarimiha vijetuṃ cittamabhyutthito'ham / vigataratitayāntarnābhinandāmi lakṣmīṃ jaḍamalinavilāsāṃ meghalekhāmivenduḥ //
english: I am ready to subdue my mind which is my greatest enemy in this world, for the purpose of mastering all the virtues, which the learned say depend upon it.
