english: Further : 'O Agni, take thou upon thyself the office of Hotri, take thou upon thyself the part of messenger!' for Agni is both Hotri and messenger to the gods: hence he thereby says, 'know thou both (offices) which thou art (holding) for the gods!'--'May earth and heaven guard thee! Guard thou earth and heaven!' there is nothing obscure in this.--'Indra, by this butter-oblation, may be the maker of good offering (svishtakrit) for the gods! Svâhâ!' Indra, indeed, is the deity of sacrifice; therefore he says 'Indra, by this butter-oblation . .

sanskrit: athāsaṃsparśayantsrucau paryetya /
english: . .' Having then returned (to his former position behind the altar), without letting the two offering-spoons touch each other, he mixes (some of the butter left in the guhû) with (that in) the dhruvâ.

sanskrit: dhruvayā samanakti śiro vai yajñasyottara āghāra ātmā vai dhruvā tadātmanyevaitaciraḥ pratidadhāti śiro vai yajñasyottara āghāraḥ śrīrvai śiraḥ śrīrhi vai śirastasmādyo 'rdhasya śreṣṭho bhavatyasāvamuṣyārdhasya śira ityāhuḥ //
english: Now the second libation (which he has just offered) is the head of the sacrifice, and the dhruvâ is its body : hence he thereby replaces the head on the body. And the second libation, moreover, is the head of the sacrifice, and the head (siras) represents excellence (srî), for the head does indeed represent excellence: hence, of one who is the most excellent (sreshtha) of a community, people say that he is 'the head of that community.'

sanskrit: yajamāna eva dhruvāmanu /
english: The sacrificer, assuredly, stands behind the dhruvâ, and he who means evil to him stands behind the upabhrit .

sanskrit: yo 'smā arātīyati sa upabhṛtamanu sa yaddhopabhṛtā samaṇjyādyo yajamānāyārātīyati tasmiṃcriyaṃ dadhyāttadyajamāna evaitacriyaṃ dadhāti tasmāddhruvayā samanakti //
english: Hence if he were to mix (the butter remaining in the guhû) with (that in) the upabhrit, he would bestow excellence on him who means evil to the sacrificer; but in this, way he bestows that excellence on the sacrificer himself: for this reason he mixes (the butter in the gull with (that in) the dhruvâ.

sanskrit: sa samanakti / saṃ jyotiṣā jyotiriti jyotirvā itarasyāmājyam bhavati jyotiritarasyāṃ te hyetadubhe jyotiṣī saṃgacete tasmādevaṃ samanakti //
english: He mixes it, with the text , 'Light with light!' for light (lustre), indeed, is the butter in the one (spoon) and light also is that in the other. Thereby these two lights unite with each other, and for this reason he mixes (the butter) in this manner.

sanskrit: athāto manasaścaiva vācaśca / ahambhadra uditam manaśca ha vai vākcāhambhadra ūdāte //
english: Now a dispute once took place between Mind and Speech as to which was the better of the two.

sanskrit: taddha mana uvāca /
english: Both Mind and Speech said, 'I am excellent!'

sanskrit: ahameva tvacreyo 'smi na vai mayā tvaṃ kiṃ canānabhigataṃ vadasi sā yanmama tvaṃ kṛtānukarānuvartmāsyahameva tvacreyo 'smīti //
english: Mind said, 'Surely I am better than thou, for thou dost not speak anything that is not understood by me; and since thou art only an imitator of what is done by me and a follower in my wake, I am surely better than thou!'

sanskrit: ahameva tvacreyasyasmi yadvai tvaṃ vetthāhaṃ tadvijñapayāmyahaṃ saṃjñapayāmīti //
english: Speech said, 'Surely I am better than thou, for what thou knowest I make known, I communicate.'

sanskrit: te prajāpatiṃ pratipraśnameyatuḥ /
english: They went to appeal to Pragâpati for his decision.

sanskrit: sa prajāpatirmanasa evānūvāca mana eva tvacreyo manaso vai tvaṃ kṛtānukarānuvartmāsi śreyaso vai pāpīyāṅkṛtānukaro 'nuvartmā bhavatīti //
english: He, Pragâpati, decided in favour of Mind, saying (to Speech), 'Mind is indeed better than thou, for thou art an imitator of its deeds and a follower in its wake; and inferior, surely, is he who imitates his better's deeds and follows in his wake.'

sanskrit: sā ha vākparoktā visiṣmiye /
english: Then Speech (vâk, fem.) being thus gainsaid, was dismayed and miscarried.

sanskrit: tasyai garbhaḥ papāta sā ha vākprajāpatimuvācāhavyavāḍevāhaṃ tubhyam bhūyāsaṃ yāṃ mā parāvoca iti tasmādyatkiṃ ca prājāpatyaṃ yajñe kriyata upāṃśveva tatkriyate havyavāḍhi vākprajāpataya āsīt //
english: She, Speech, then said to Pragâpati, 'May I never be thy oblation-bearer, I whom thou hast gainsaid!' Hence whatever at the sacrifice is performed for Pragâpati, that is performed in a low voice; for speech would not act as oblation-bearer for Pragâpati.

sanskrit: taddhaitaddevāḥ / retaścarmanvā yasminvā babhrustaddha smapṛcantyatreva tyāditi tato triḥ sambabhūva tasmādapyātreyyā yoṣitainasvyetasyai hi yoṣāyai vāco devatāyā ete sambhūtāḥ //
english: That germ (retas) the gods then brought away in a skin or in some (vessel). They asked: 'Is it here (atra)?' and therefore it developed into Atri. For the same reason one becomes guilty by (intercourse) with a woman who has just miscarried (âtreyî); for it is from that woman, from the goddess Speech, that these (germs) originate .

sanskrit: sa vai pravarāyāśrāvayati /
english: He (the Adhvaryu) now utters his call for the Pravara (choosing of the Hotri) .

sanskrit: tadyatpravarāyāśrāvayati yajño vā āśrāvaṇaṃ yajñamabhivyāhṛtyātha hotāram pravṛṇā iti tasmātpravarāyāśrāvayati //
english: The reason why he utters his call, is that the (Adhvaryu's) call isthe sacrifice: 'having bespoke the sacrifice, I will choose the Hotri,' thus (he thinks, and) for this reason he utters his call for the Pravara.

sanskrit: sa yadvānārabhy a yajñamadhvaryurāśrāvayedvepano vā ha syādanyāṃ vārttimārcet //
english: He utters his call after taking the fuel-band; for if the Adhvaryu were to utter his call without taking hold of the sacrifice, he would either be unsteady or meet with some other ailment.

sanskrit: vede stīrṇāyai barhirabhipadyāśrāvayantīdhmasya vā śakalamapacidyābhipadyāśrāvayantīdaṃ vai kiṃcidyajñasyedaṃ yajñamabhipadyāśrāvayāma iti vadantastadu tathā na kuryādetadvai kiṃcidyajñasya yairidhmaḥ saṃnaddho bhavatyagniṃ sammṛjanti tadveva khalu yajñamabhipadyāśrāvayati tasmādidhmasaṃnahanānyevābhipadyāśrāvayet //
english: Here now some utter the call after taking sacrificial grass (barhis) from the covered altar, or they utter the call after cutting off and taking a chip of fire-wood, arguing, 'this, surely, is something belonging to the sacrifice; after taking hold of this, the sacrifice, we will utter the call.' Let him, however, not do this; for that also wherewith the firewood was tied together and wherewith they sweep the fire is, doubtless, something belonging to the sacrifice; and thus indeed he utters his call after taking hold of the sacrifice: for this reason let him utter the call after taking the fuel-band.

sanskrit: ya eva devānāṃ hotā tamevāgre pravṛṇite 'gnimeva tadagnaye caivaitaddevebhyaśca nihnute yadahāgre 'gnim pravṛṇīte tadagnaye nihnute 'tha yo devānāṃ hotā tamagre pravṛṇīte tadudevebhyo nihnute //
english: Having uttered the call, he in the first place chooses him who is the Hotri of the gods, that is, Agni. Thereby he propitiates both Agni and the gods: for by first choosing Agni, he propitiates Agni;and by first choosing him who is the Hotri of the gods, he propitiates the gods.

sanskrit: agnirdevo daivyo hotetyagnirhi devānāṃ hotā tasmādāhāgnirdevo daivyo hoteti tadagnaye caiva devebhyaśca nihnute yadahāgre 'gnimāha tadagnaye nihnute 'tha yo devānāṃhotā tamagra āha tadu devebhyo nihnute // devānyakṣadvidvāṃścikitvāniti / eṣa vai devānanuvidvānyadagniḥ sa enānanuvidvānanuṣṭhyā yakṣadityevaitadāha //
english: He says, 'Agni, the god, the divine Hotri--,' for Agni is indeed the Hotri of the gods, therefore he says 'Agni, the god, the divine Hotri:' thereby he propitiates both Agni and the gods; for by his first mentioning Agni he propitiates Agni; and by his first mentioning him who is the Hotri of the gods, he propitiates the gods. 'May he worship, knowing the gods , he the thoughtful one,'--for he, Agni, indeed, knows the gods well: hence, he thereby says 'may he who knows them well worship (them) in due form!

sanskrit: manuṣvadbharatavaditi / manurha vā agre yajñeneje tadanukṛtyemāḥ prajā yajante tasmādāha manuṣvaditi manoryajña ityu vā āhustasmādvevāha manuṣvaditi //
english: 'Like as Manu (did), like as Bharata;'--Manu, indeed, worshipped with sacrifice in olden times, and doing as he did these descendants of his now sacrifice: therefore he says 'like as Manu.' Or, say they, (it means) 'at the sacrifice of Manu,' and therefore he says 'as (he did) with Manu.'

sanskrit: bharatavaditi / eṣa hi devebhyo havyam bharati tasmādbharato 'gnirityāhureṣa u vā imāḥ prajāḥ prāṇo bhūtvā bibharti tasmādvevāha bharatavaditi //
english: 'Like as (with) Bharata,'--for, say they, he bears (bhar) the oblation to the gods, hence Bharata (the bearer) is Agni; or, say they, he, having become the breath, supports (bhar) these creatures, and therefore he says 'like as Bharata.'

sanskrit: athārṣeyam pravṛṇīte /
english: He then chooses (Agni as) the ancestral (Hotri).

sanskrit: ṛṣibhyaścaivainametaddevebhyaśca nivedayatyayam mahāvīryo yo yajñam prāpaditi tasmādārṣeyam pravṛṇīte //
english: He thus introduces him both to the (ancestral) rishis and to the gods (as if he were saying), 'he is of mighty strength who obtained the sacrifice!' for this reason he chooses (him as) the ancestral one.

sanskrit: parastādarvākpravṛṇīte /
english: He chooses from the remote end (of the sacrificer's ancestral line) downwards; for it is from theremote end downwards that a race is propagated.

sanskrit: parastāddhyarvācyaḥ prajāḥ prajāyante jyāyasaspataya u caivaitannihnuta idaṃ hi pitaivāgre 'tha putro 'tha pautrastasmātparastādarvākpravṛṇite //
english: Thereby he also propitiates the lord of seniority; for here among men the father comes first, then the son, and then the grandson: this is the reason why he chooses from the remote end downwards.

sanskrit: sa ārṣeyamuktvāha / brahmaṇvaditi brahma hyagnistasmādāha brahmaṇvadityā ca vakṣaditi tadyā evaitaddevatā āvoḍhavā āha tā evaitadāhā ca vakṣaditi //
english: Having named the ancestral, he says, 'Like as, Brahman;'--for Agni is the Brahman (the Veda, or the sacerdotium), and therefore he says 'like as Brahman;'--'may he bring (the gods) hither!' what deities he bids him bring hither, those he refers to in saying 'may he bring (them) hither.'

sanskrit: brāhmaṇā asya yajñasya prāvitāra iti / ete vai brāhmaṇā yajñasyaprāvitāro ye 'nūcānā ete hyenaṃ tanvata eta enaṃ janayanti tadu tebhyo nihnute tasmādāha brāhmaṇā asya yajñasya prāvitāra iti //
english: 'The Brâhmanas (priests) are the guardians of this sacrifice;' for guardians of the sacrifice, indeed, are those Brâhmanas who are versed in the sacred writ, because they spread it, they originate it: these he thereby propitiates; and for this reason he says, 'the Brâhmanas are the guardians of the sacrifice.'

sanskrit: asau mānuṣa iti / tadimam mānuṣaṃ hotāraṃ pravṛṇīte hotā haiṣa purāthaitarhi hotā //
english: is the man,' thereby he chooses this man for his Hotri; heretofore he was not a Hotri, but now he is a Hotri.

sanskrit: sa pravṛto hotā / japati devatā upadhāvati yathānuṣṭhyā devebhyo vaṣaṭkuryādyathānuṣṭhyā devebhyo havyaṃ vahedyathā na hvaledevaṃ devatā upadhāvati //
english: The chosen Hotri mutters,--has recourse to the deities: in order that he may give the vashat-call to the gods in its proper order, that he may convey the oblation to the gods in its proper order, that he may not stumble, he has thus recourse to the deities.

sanskrit: tatra japati etatattvā deva savitarvṛṇata iti tatsavitāram prasavāyopadhāvati sa hi devānām prasavitāgniṃ hotrāyeti tadagnaye caivaitaddevebhyaśca nihnute yadahāgre 'gnimāha tadagnaye nihnute 'tha yo devānāṃ hotā tamagra āha tadu devebhyo nihnute //
english: He mutters on this occasion , 'Thee, O divine Savitri, they now choose,'--thereby he has recourse to Savitri for his impulsion (prasava), for Savitri is the impeller (prasavitri) of the gods;--'(thee who art) Agni, for the Hotriship,' thereby hepropitiates both Agni and the gods; for by first naming Agni, he propitiates Agni; and by first naming him who is the Hotri of the gods, he propitiates the gods.

sanskrit: saha pitrā vaiśvānareṇeti / sam\vatsaro vai pitā vaiśvānaraḥ prajāpatistatsaṃvatsarāyaivaitatprajāpataye nihnute 'gne pūṣanbṛhaspate pra ca vada pra ca yajetyanuvakṣyanvā etadyakṣyanbhavati tadaitābhya evaitaddevatābhyo nihnute yūyamanubrūta yūyaṃ yajateti //
english: 'Together with father Vaisvânara,'--for the father Vaisvânara ('common to all men'), doubtless, is the year, is Pragâpati (lord of creatures); hence he thereby propitiates the year and thus Pragâpati.--'O Agni! O Pûshan! O Brihaspati! speak forth and offer up sacrifice (pra-yag)!'--he (the Hotri), namely, will have to recite the anuvâkyâs and the yâgyâs ; he therefore now propitiates those gods: do ye recite, 'do ye offer!' thus (he thereby says).

sanskrit: vasūnāṃ rātau syāma / rudrāṇāmurvyāyāṃ svādityā aditaye syāmānehasa ityete vai trayā devā yadvasavo rudrā ādityā eteṣāmabhiguptau syāmetyevaitadāha //
english: 'May we partake of the bounty of the Vasus, of the wide sway of the Rudras! may we be beloved of the Âdityas for the sake of (aditi) security from injury, free from obstruction!'--these, to wit, the Vasus, Rudras, and Âdityas, namely, are three (classes of) gods: 'may we enjoy their protection' he thereby says.

sanskrit: juṣṭāmadya devebhyo vācamudyāsamiti / juṣṭamadya devebhyo 'nūcyāsamityevaitadāha taddhi samṛddhaṃ yo juṣṭaṃ devebhyo 'nubravat //
english: 'May I this day utter speech that is agreeable to the gods;'--by this he means to say 'may I this day recite what is agreeable to the gods,' for auspicious it is when one recites what is agreeable to the gods.

sanskrit: juṣṭām brahmabhya iti / juṣṭamadya brāhmaṇebhyo 'nūcyāsamityevaitadāha taddhi samṛddham yo juṣṭam brāhmaṇebhyo 'nubravat //
english: 'Agreeable to the Brahmans,'--by this he means to say 'may I this day recite what is agreeable to the Brâhmanas (priests);' for auspicious it is when one recites what is agreeable to the Brâhmanas.

sanskrit: juṣṭāṃ narāśaṃsāyeti / prajā vai narastatsarvābhyaḥ prajābhya āha taddhi samṛddhaṃ yaśca veda yaśca na sādhvanvavocatsādhvanvavocadityeva visṛjyante yadadya hotṛvarye jihmaṃcakṣuḥ parāpatat agniṣṭatpunarābhriyājjātavedā vicarṣaṇiriti yathā yānagre 'gnīnhotrāya prāvṛṇata te prādhanvannevaṃ yanme 'tra pravareṇāmāyi tanme punarāpyāyayetyevaitadāha tatho hāsyaitatpunarāpyāyate // athādhvaryuṃ cāgnīdhaṃ ca sammṛśati /
english: 'Agreeable to Narâsamsa ,'--man (nara), namely, is a creature: hence he says this for all the creatures; thereby it is auspicious, and whether or not he knows (forms of speech that are agreeable), they are uttered (and received with applause), 'well he has recited! well he has recited!'--'What at the Hotri choice may escape the crooked eye this day, that may Agni bring back here, he, the knower of beings (gâtavedas), the nimble one (vikarshani)!'--by this he means to say, 'even as those (three) Agnis, whom they first chose for the Hotriship, passed away , (but thou, the fourth Agni, wast then obtained,) so do thou make good for me whatever mistake may have been committed at my election!' and it is accordingly made good for him.

sanskrit: mano vā adhvaryurvāgghotā tanmanaścaivaitadvācaṃ ca saṃdadhāti // tatra japati /
english: He now touches the Adhvaryu and the Âgnîdhra: for the Adhvaryu is the mind, and the Hotri is, speech: thus he thereby brings mind and speech together.

sanskrit: ṣaṇmorvīraṃhasaspāntvagniśca pṛthivī cāpaśca vājaścāhaśca rātriścetyetā mā devatā ārttergopāyantvityevaitadāha tasyo hi na hvalāsti yametā devatā ārttergopāyeyuḥ //
english: At the same time he mutters , 'From anguish may the six spaces protect me, fire, earth, water, wind, day, and night !'--'may these deities protectme from disease!' thus he thereby says; for he whom these deities protect from disease, will not stumble (or fail).

sanskrit: atha hotṛṣadanamupāvartate / sa hotṛṣadanādekaṃ tṛṇaṃ nirasyati nirastaḥ parāvasuriti purāvasurha vai nāmāsurāṇāṃ hotā sa tamevaitaddhotṛṣadanānnirasyati //
english: "He steps beside the Hotri's seat, takes one stalk of (reed) grass from the Hotri's seat and casts it outside (the sacrificial ground), with the formula, 'Ejected is the wealth-clutcher (parâvasu, lit. ""off-wealth"")!' Formerly, namely, the Hotri of the Asuras was one Parâvasu by name: him he thereby ejects from the Hotri's seat."

sanskrit: atha hotṛṣadana upaviśati /
english: He then sits down on the Hotri's seat, with the formula, 'I here sit down on the seat of the wealth-bestower (arvâvasu, lit.

sanskrit: idamahamarvāvasoḥ sadane sīdāmītyarvāvasurvai nāma devānāṃ hotā tasyaivaitatsadane sīdati //
english: hither-wealth)!' for one Arvâvasu by name was the Hotri of the gods , and on his seat he accordingly sits down.

sanskrit: tatra japati viśvakarmastanūpā asi mā mo doṣiṣṭam mā mā hiṃsiṣṭameṣa vāṃ loka ityudaṅṅejatyantarā vā etadāhavaniyaṃ ca gārhapatyaṃ cāste tadu tābhyāṃ nihnute mā mo doṣiṣṭam mā mā hiṃsiṣṭamiti tathā hainametau na hiṃstaḥ //
english: At the same time he mutters, 'O All-maker, thou art the protector of lives! do not ye two (fires) scorch me away (from this) , injure me not! thisis your sphere;' with this he moves slightly northwards: by this (mantra, he indicates that) he sits midway between the Âhavanîya and the Gârhapatya, and thus he propitiates these two; and in accordance with what he says, 'do not scorch me away from this! injure me not!' they do not injure him.

sanskrit: viśve devāḥ śāstana mā yatheha hotā vṛto manavai yanniṣadya pra me brūta bhāgadheyaṃ yathā vo yena pathā havyamā vo vahānīti yathā yebhyaḥ pakvaṃ syāttānbrūyādvanu mā śāsta yathā va āhariṣyāmi yathā vaḥ parivekṣyāmītyevamevaitaddeveṣu praśāsanamicate 'nu mā śāsta yathā vo 'nuṣṭhyā vaṣaṭkuryāmanuṣṭyā havyaṃ vaheyamiti tasmādevaṃ japati //
english: He then mutters whilst looking at the (Âhavanîya) fire, 'All ye gods, instruct me, how and what I am to mind while seated here as the chosen Hotri! declare my share (of the sacrificial duties), how and by what road I am to convey the oblation to you!'--for as one says to those for whom food has been cooked, 'order me how I am to bring if you, how I am to serve it up for you!' in like manner he is desirous of directions regarding the gods, and for this reason he mutters thus, 'instruct me how I may utter the Vashat-call for you in its proper order, how I may bring you the oblation in its proper order!'

sanskrit: agnirhotā vettvagnerhotramiti agniridaṃ hotā vettvityevaitadāhāgnerhotramiti tasyo hi hotraṃ vettu prāvitramiti yajño vai prāvitraṃ vettu yajñamityevaitadāha sādhu te yajamāna devateti sādhu te yajamāna devatā yasya te 'gnirhotetyevaitadāha ghṛtavatīmadhvaryo srucamāsyasveti tadadhvaryu prasauti sa yadekāmivāha //
english: [The Hotri continues], 'May Agni, the priest (hotri), know (undertake) Agni's priestly duty (hautram),'--thereby he says 'may Agni, as Hotri, know this!' 'Agni's priestly duty' he says, because it is his duty that he must know;--'that means of salvation ,'--the means of salvation, assuredly, is the sacrifice: 'may he know the sacrifice' is what he thereby says.--'Favourable to thee, O Sacrificer, isthe deity!' by this he says 'favourable is the deity to thee, O Sacrificer, whose Hotri is Agni !'--'Take up the spoon, O Adhvaryu, full of butter!' thereby he urges on the Adhvaryu.

sanskrit: yajamāna eva juhūmanu /
english: The reason why he mentions one (spoon) only (is this).

sanskrit: yo smā arātīyati sa upabhṛtamanu sa yaddve iva brūyādyajamānāya dviṣantam bhrātṛvyam pratyudyāminaṃ kuryādattaiva juhūmanvādya upabhṛtamanu sa yaddve iva brūyādattra ādyam pratyudyāminaṃ kuryāttasmādekāmivaivāha //
english: The Sacrificer, doubtless, stands behind the guhû, and he, who means evil to him, stands behind the upabhrit; and if he were to speak of two (spoons), he would cause the spiteful enemy to countervail the Sacrificer. Behind the guhû stands the eater, and behind the upabhrit the one to be eaten; and if he were to speak of two (spoons), he would make the one to be eaten countervail the eater.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ cīraṃ vasānāyāṃ nāthavatyāmanāthavat| pracukrośa janaḥ sarvo dhik tvāṃ daśarathaṃ tviti ||
english: "When Şītā, having a husband although seeming as if she had none, was putting on the ascetic guise, the people got into a wrath and exclaimed, “O Dasaratha, fie on you!"""

sanskrit: tena tatra praṇādena duḥkhitaḥ sa mahīpatiḥ| ciccheda jīvite śraddhāṃ dharme yaśasi cātmanaḥ|| sa niḥśvasyoṣṇamaikṣvākastāṃ bhāryāmidamabravīt| kaikeyi kuśacīreṇa na sītā gantumarhati||
english: Aggrieved at the uproar that arose there in consequence, the lord of earth banished from his heart all regard for life, virtue, and fame. And sighing hot, that descendant of Ikşvāku spoke to that wife of his, saying, O Kaikeyi, Sītā deserves not to go in a Kuća dress.

sanskrit: sukumārī ca bālā ca satataṃ ca sukhocitā| neyaṃ vanasya yogyeti satyamāha gururmama ||
english: Tender, and youthful, and worthy of happiness, she is by no means capable of living in the forest. My spiritual guide has spoken the truth.

sanskrit: iyaṃ hi kasyāpi karoti kiṃcit tapasvinī rājavarasya putrī| yā cīramāsādya vanasya madhye jātā visaṃjñā śramaṇīva kācit||
english: Whom has this one injured that, being the daughter of the foremost of kings, she like a female ascetic, wearing a meagre garb in the presence of all, will (repair to the woods and) remain there like a beggar destitute of everything?

sanskrit: cīrāṇyapāsyājjanakasya kanyā neyaṃ pratijñā mama dattapūrvā| yathāsukhaṃ gacchatu rājaputrī vanaṃ samagrā saha sarvaratnaiḥ||
english: Let Janaka's daughter leave off her ascetic guise. This is not the promise that I had made to you before. Let the princess go to the forest in comfort, furnished with all sorts of gems.

sanskrit: ajīvanāheṇa mayā nṛśaṃsā kṛtā pratijñā niyamena tāvat| tvayā hi bālyāt pratipannametat tanmā dahed veṇumivātmapuṣpam||
english: My sands run out; by me has this cruel promise been made with an oath. But this (exile of Sītä) has been thought of by you through your ignorance. Let it not, however, consume you like a bamboo flower destroying the bamboo.

sanskrit: rāmeṇa yadi te pāpe kiṃcitkṛtamaśobhanam| apakāraḥ ka iha te vaidehyā darśito'dhame||
english: If, O wicked woman, Rāma has happened to do you something unbeautiful, what wrong, O base wretch, has Vaidehi done you in the world?

sanskrit: mṛgīvotphullanayanā mṛduśīlā manasvinī| apakāraṃ kamiva te karoti janakātmajā||
english: Of eyes expanded like those of a doe, endued with a mild temperament, and virtuous, what harm has Janaka's daughter done you.

sanskrit: nanu paryāptamevaṃ te pāpe rāmavivāsanam| kimebhiḥ kṛpaṇairbhūyaḥ pātakairapi te kṛtaiḥ||
english: Surely, O nefarious one, the banishment of Ráma is enough for you. Why then do you bend your mind to perpetrate these atrocious sins?

sanskrit: pratijñātaṃ mayā tāvat tvayoktaṃ devi śṛṇvatā| rāmaṃ yadabhiṣekāya tvamihāgatamabravīḥ||
english: O noble dame, having heard you asking for the banishment of Rāma, who had at first been intended by me for being installed, and who came here afterwards, I had promised you (his exile alone.)

sanskrit: tattvetat samatikramya nirayaṃ gantumicchasi| maithilīmapi yā hi tvamīkṣase cīravāsinīm||
english: But since, going beyond that promise of mine, you behold Mithala's daughter dressed in mendicant garb, surely you wish to find your way to hell.

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvantaṃ pitaraṃ rāmaḥ samprasthito vanam| avākśirasamāsīnamidaṃ vacanamabravīt||
english: Thus commissioned to the forest, Räma who was seated sealing his lips, said.

sanskrit: iyaṃ dhārmika kausalyā mama mātā yaśasvinī| vṛddhā cākṣudraśīlā ca na ca tvāṃ deva garhate|| mayā vihīnāṃ varada prapannāṃ śokasāgaram| adṛṣṭapūrvavyasanāṃ bhūyaḥ sammantumarhasi ||
english: O righteous one, this my mother is aged and famous and of lofty spirit. May she not meet with improper treatment at your hands! It behoves you, O bestower of boons, to show greater honour to her when she shall be deprived of me and be plunged into a sea of grief and afflicted with unprecedented woe.

sanskrit: putraśokaṃ yathā nachet tvayā pūjyena pūjitā| māṃ hi saṃcintayantī sā tvayi jīvet tapasvinī|| imāṃ mahendropama jātagardhinī tathā vidhātuṃ jananī mamārhasi| yathā vanasthe mayi śokakarśitā na jīvitaṃ nyasya yamakṣayaṃ vrajet||
english: O you comparable to the mighty Indra, you should so behove with my mother smitten with my separation, that exercised by grief in consequence of my residence in the forest, she may not, renouncing life, repair to the mansions of Yama.

sanskrit: munervacanamaklībaṃ śrutvā naravarātmajaḥ| rāghavaḥ prāñjalirbhūtvā pratyuvāca dṛḍhavrataḥ||
english: Hearing those bold words of the ascetic, the son of that foremost of men, Rāghava firm in his vows, with clasped hands answered.

sanskrit: piturvacananirdeśāt piturvacanagauravāt| vacanaṃ kauśikasyeti kartavyamaviśaṅkayā|| anuśiṣṭo'smyayodhyāyāṃ gurumadhye mahātmanā| pitrā daśarathenāhaṃ nāvajñeyaṃ hi tadvacaḥ||
english: In accordance with the desire of my sire, and in order to glorify it, I ought fearlessly to do even as Kusika's son says. And having been desired to that end while at Ayodhyā by that high-souled one, my father Dasaratha, in the midst of the spiritual guides, I ought not to pass by your words.

sanskrit: so'haṃ piturvacaḥ śrutvā śāsanād brahmavādinaḥ| kariṣyāmi na saṃdehastāṭakāvadhamuttamam||
english: Therefore, commanded by that upholder of the Veda, I, agreeably to my father's mandate, will, without doubt, bring about that welcome event-the death of Tataka.

sanskrit: gobrāhmaṇahitārthāya deśasya ca hitāya ca| tava caivāprameyasya vacanaṃ kartumudyataḥ||
english: And in the interests of Brāhmaṇas, kine, and celestials, I am ready to act as desired by you of immeasurable energy.

sanskrit: evamuktvā dhanurmadhye baddhvā muṣṭimariṃdamaḥ| jyāghoṣamakarot tīvra diśaḥ śabdena nādayan || tena śabdena vivastāstāṭakāvanavāsinaḥ| tāṭakā ca susaṃkruddhā tena śabdena mohitā||
english: Having said this, that repressor of foes, with clenched fist, twanged his bow-string, filling the ten cardinal points with the sounds. And at those sounds, the dwellers in Tāțakā's forest were filled with perturbation, and Tātakā also amazed at those sounds, became exceedingly wroth.

sanskrit: taṃ śabdamabhinidhyāya rākṣasī krodhamūrchitā| śrutvā cābhyadravat kruddhā yatra śabdo viniḥsṛtaḥ||
english: And rendered almost insensible by anger, that Räksasī furiously rushed in a main towards the spot whence had come the report.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā rāghavaḥ kruddhāṃ vikṛtāṃ vikṛtānanām| pramāmenātivṛddhāṃ ca lakṣmaṇaṃ so'bhyabhāṣata||
english: And beholding that frightful one of hideous visage and colossal proportions, transported with rage, Raghu's descendant spoke to Laksmana,9

sanskrit: paśya lakṣmaṇa yakṣiṇyā bhairavaṃ dāruṇaṃ vapuḥ| bhidyeran darśanādasyā bhīrūṇāṃ hṛdayāni ca||
english: Behold, O Laksmana, the terrible and hideous body of yonder Yakṣiṇī! The sight of her strike terror into the hearts of even the brave.

sanskrit: etāṃ paśya durādharṣāṃ māyābalasamanvitām| vinivṛttāṃ karomyadya hṛtakarṇānanāsikām||
english: Mark! This irrepressible one, possessing all the resources of illusion, will I oppose, and deprive her of ears and nose.

sanskrit: na hyenāmutsahe hantuṃ strīsvabhāvena rakṣitām| vīryaṃ cāsyā gatiṃ caiva hanyāmiti hi me matiḥ||
english: But I dare not slay her, she being protected by virtue of her feminineness. I intend only to oppose her course, and deprive her of her prowess.

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇe rāme tu tāṭakā krodhamūrcchitā| udyamya bāhuṃ garjantī rāmamevābhyadhāvata||
english: As Rāma was speaking thus, Tāțakā, deprived of sense through ire, uttering roars, with uplifted arms rushed against him.

sanskrit: viśvāmitrastu brahmarṣihu~kāreṇābhibhaya̭ tām| svasti rāghavayorastu jayaṃ caivābhyabhāṣata||
english: And thereat the Brahmarsi, Visvāmitra, uttering a roar, upbraided her, and said, Svasti!* May victory attend the descendants of Raghu! *A particle of benediction, indeclinable.

sanskrit: uddhanvānā rajo ghoraṃ tāṭakā rāghavāvubhau| rajomeghena mahatā muhūrtaṃ sā vyamohayat||
english: And raising thick clouds of dust, Tāțakā instantly bewildered both the descendants of Raghu.

sanskrit: tato māyāṃ samāṃsthāya śilāvarṣeṇa rāghavau| avākirat sumahatāṃ tataścakrodha rāghavaḥ||
english: And then by help of illusion, she began to pour upon them a mighty shower of crags. And thereat Raghu's descendant was wroth.

sanskrit: śilāvarṣaṃ mahat tasyāḥ śaravarṣeṇa rāghavaḥ| prativāryopadhāvantyāḥ karau ciccheda patribhiḥ||
english: And resisting that mighty shower of crags by vollies of shafts, Rāghava with arrows cut off her hands.

sanskrit: tataśchinnabhujāṃ śrāntāmabhyāśe parigarjatīm| saumitrirakarot krodhāddhatakarṇāgranāsikām||
english: And with the fore-parts of her arms lopped off, as she was roaring before them, Sumitra's son waxing wroth deprived her of her ears and nose.

sanskrit: kāmarūpadharā sā tu kṛtvā rūpāṇyanekaśaḥ| antardhānaṃ gatā yakṣī mohayantī svamāyayā||
english: Thereupon that one capable of assuming forms at will, began to assume various shapes; and to vanish from sight, bewildering her antagonists with her illusory displays.

sanskrit: aśmavarṣaṃ vimuñcantī bhairavaṃ vicacāra sā| tatastāvaśmavarṣeṇa kīryamāṇau samantataḥ|| dṛṣṭvā gādhisutaḥ śrīmānidaṃ vacanamabravīt| alaṃ te ghṛṇayā rāma pāpaiṣā duṣṭvāriṇī|| yajñavighnakarī yakṣī purā vardheta māyayā| vadhyatāṃ tāvadevaiṣā purā saṃdhyā pravartate|| rakṣāṃsi saṃdhyākāle tu durdharṣāṇi bhavanti hi|
english: Terribly ranging the field, the Yakṣī showered crags upon her antagonists. And beholding them enveloped on all sides by that craggy downpour, the auspicious son of Gadhi spoke these words-O Rāma, renounce your antipathy. This one of wicked ways is exceedingly impious. And this sacrifice-disturbing Yakși will, by virtue of her power of illusion, come to increase more and more in energy. Do you, therefore, against the arrival of dusk, slay her! The Rākṣasas are incapable of being controlled when evening sets in.

sanskrit: ityuktaḥ sa tu tāṃ yakṣīmaśmavṛṣṭayābhivarṣiṇīm || darśayaśabdavedhitvaṃ tāṃ rurodha sa sāyakaiḥ|
english: Thus addressed, Rāma, displaying his skill in aiming by sounds, enveloped with arrows that Yakṣī showering crags.

sanskrit: sā ruddhā bāṇajālena māyābalasamanvitā|| abhidudrāva kākutsthaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ ca vineduṣī| tāmāpatantī vegena vikrāntāmaśanīmiva || śareṇorasi vivyādha sā papāta mamāra ca|
english: Being thus hemmed in with a network of shafts, she possessed of the powers of illusion, rushed against Kākutstha and Lakşmaņa, uttering terrible roars. And as that Yaksi, in prowess like to a thunder-bolt, was rushing on, Rāma pierced her chest with arrows, and thereat she dropped down and died.

sanskrit: tāṃ hatāṃ bhīmasaṃkāśāṃ dṛṣṭvā surapatistadā|| sādhu sādhviti kākutsthaṃ surāścāpyabhipūjayan|
english: Upon seeing that grim-visaged one slain, the lord of the celestials together with the celestials themselves honouring Kākutstha, exclaimed Well, Well!.

sanskrit: uvāca paramaprītaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ purandaraḥ|| surāśca sarve saṃhṛṣṭā viśvāmitramathābruvan|
english: And exceedingly pleased, the thousand-eyed Purandara, together with the delighted deities, said to Viśvāmitra.

sanskrit: mune kauśika bhadraṃ te sendrāḥ sarve marudgaṇāḥ|| toṣitāḥ karmaṇānena snehaṃ darśaya rāghave| prajāpateḥ kṛśāśvasya putrān satyaparākramān|| tapobalabhṛto brahman rāghavāya nivedaya|
english: O ascetic, O Kusika's son, good betide you! all the Maruts with Indra at their head, have been gratified with this act (of Rāma's). Do you, O Brāhmaṇa, confer upon Raghu's descendant the sons of Prajāpati Kțśāśva, of true prowess, and charged with ascetic energy.

sanskrit: pātrabhūtaśca te brahmastavānugamane rataḥ|| kartavyaṃ sumahat karma surāṇāṃ rājasūnunā|
english: And ever following you, he, O Brāhmaṇa, is fit to receive them of you. And this son of the king is to accomplish a mighty task in the interests of the celestials.

sanskrit: evamuktvā surāḥ sarve jagmurhaṣṭā vihāyasam|| viśvāmitraṃ pūjayantastataḥ saṃdhyā pravartate|
english: Saying this, the deities, having paid homage to Viśvāmitra, joyfully entered the celestial regions.

sanskrit: tato munivaraḥ prītastāṭakāvadhatoṣitaḥ|32|| mūrdhni rāmamupāghrāya idaṃ vacanamabravīt|
english: And now came evening on, when that best of ascetics, gratified at the destruction of Tāțakā, smelt Rāma's crown and said these words,

sanskrit: ihādya rajanī rāma vasāma śubhadarśana || śvaḥ prabhāte gamiṣyāmastadāśramapadaṃ mama|
english: Here, O Rāma of gracious presence, shall we pass the night; and morrow morning, went to that hermitage of mine.

sanskrit: viśvāmitravacaḥ śrutvā hṛṣṭo daśarathātmajaḥ|| uvāsa rajanī tatra tāṭakāyā vane sukham|
english: Hearing Visvāmitra's words, Dasaratha's son, glad at heart, happily passed that night in the forest of Tāțakā.

sanskrit: muktaśāpaṃ vanaṃ tacca tasminneva tadāhani| ramaṇīyaṃ vibabhrāja yathā caitrarathaṃ vanam||
english: And being thus freed from all disturbances, from that day forth that forest appeared charming, even like to the forest of Caitraratha.

sanskrit: nihatya to yakṣasutāṃ sa rāmaḥ praśasyamānaḥ surasiddhasaṃghaiḥ| uvāsa tasmin muninā sahaiva prabhātavelāṃ pratibodhyamānaḥ||
english: Having thus slain the Yakşa's daughter, Rāma, eulogised by celestials and Siddhas, spent there that night with the saint, being awakened by the latter at the break of day.

sanskrit: ṛṣyamūkāt sa dharmātmā kiṣkindhāṃ lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ| jagāma saha sugrīvo vālivikramapālitām|| samudyamya mahaccāpaṃ rāmaḥ kāñcanabhūṣitam| śarāṃścādityasaṃkāśān gṛhītvā raṇasādhakān||
english: Thereupon the high-souled Rāma, along with Sugrīva, proceeded from the mount Rșyamuka to Kiskindha, maintained by Vali's prowess, raising up his gold crested mighty bow and taking his battle arrows like to Aditya.

sanskrit: agratastu yayau tasya rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ| sugrīvaḥ saṃhatagrīvo lakṣmaṇasya mahābalaḥ||
english: The mighty Sugrīva, bending low, proceeded before the high-souled Rama and Laksmana.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhato hanumān vīro nalo nīlaśca vīryavān| tāraścaiva mahātejā hariyūthapayūthapaḥ||
english: They were followed by the heroic Hanumān, the mighty Nala and Neela, and the highly powerful Tārā, the leader of the monkey herd.

sanskrit: te vīkṣamāṇā vṛkṣāṃśca puṣpabhārāvalambinaḥ| prasannāmbuvahāścaiva saritaḥ sāgaraṃgamāḥ|| kandarāṇi ca śailāṃśca nirdarāṇi guhāstathā| śikharāṇi ca mukhyāni darīśca priyadarśanāḥ||
english: They beheld as they proceeded, trees, lowered down with the weight of flowers, rivers of clear water flowing to the ocean, mountain hollows, hills, caves, cavities, and principal peaks and charming rills.

sanskrit: vaidūryavimalaistoyaiḥ padyaiścākośakuḍmalaiḥ| śobhitān sajalān mārge taṭākāṃścāvalokayan|| kāraṇḍaiḥ sārasaiha~sairvañjulairjalakukkuṭaiḥ| cakravākaistathā cānyaiḥ śakunaiḥ pratināditān||
english: They. beheld on their way, pools filled with water clear as Baidurya and beautified with lotuses-full blown and buds, and resounded with the cries of Kārandhabas, swans, geese, Banculas, water-fowls, Cakravākas, and various other birds.

sanskrit: mṛduśaṣpāṅkurāhārānnirbhayān vanagocarān| carataḥ sarvataḥ paśyan sthalīṣu hariṇān sthitān||
english: They surveyed all around in the forest-land, deer ranging fearlessly at large and grazing on tender grass.

sanskrit: taṭākavairiṇaścāpi śukladantavibhūṣitān| ghorānekacarānvanyān dviradān kūlaghātinaḥ|| mattān giritaṭotkṛṣṭān parvatāniva jaṅgamān| vānarān dviradaprakhyān mahīreṇusamukṣitān || vane vanacarāṃścānyān khecarāṃśca vihaṃgamān| paśyantastvaritā jagmuḥ sugrīvavaśavartinaḥ||
english: They beheld frightful wild elephants having white teeth, ranging alone-the destroyers of river banks and enemies of pools. And observing many an infuriated monkey like to elephants, resembling so many moveable mountains riving the mountainous expanses crusted with dust, and many other wild beasts and birds the followers of Sugrīva wended their way.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu gacchatāṃ tatra tvaritaṃ raghunandanaḥ| dumaṣaṇḍavanaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmaḥ sugrīvamabravīt||
english: They proceeding quickly, Rama, the descendant of Raghu, beholding the forest filled with trees, spoke to Sugrīva, saying.

sanskrit: eṣa megha ivākāśe vṛkṣaṣaṇḍaḥ prakāśate| meghasaṃghātavipulaḥ paryantakadalīvṛtaḥ|| kimetajjñātumicchāmi sakhe kautūhalaṃ mama| kautūhalāpanayanaṃ kartumicchāmyahaṃ tvayā||
english: These trees skirted by plantain groves, dense as a collection of clouds, appear as clouds in the sky. Great is my curiosity, O friend, to learn what are these. 'And I wish to have my curiosity removed by you.

sanskrit: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ| gacchannevācacakṣe'tha sugrīvastanmahad vanam||
english: Hearing the words of the high-souled Rāghava, Sugrīva began to describe that great forest.

sanskrit: etad rāghava vistīrṇamāśramaṃ śramanāśanam| udyānavanasampannaṃ svādumūlaphalodakam|| atra saptajanā nāma munayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ| saptavāsannadhaḥśīrṣā niyataṃ jalaśāyinaḥ|| saptarātre kṛtāhārā vāyunācalavāsinaḥ| divaṃ varṣaśatairyātāḥ saptabhiḥ sakalevarāḥ||
english: In this extensive asylum, O Rāghava, removing the toil (of the travellers) filled with gardens and trees and abounding in delicious fruits, roots and water, dwelt seven Saints, having control over their senses. Those seven Saints, dwelling on the mountain, passed days and nights in water with their heads down and after seven nights used to live upon air. In this wise, passing seven hundred years they repaired bodily to heaven.

sanskrit: teṣāmetatprabhāveṇa dumaprākārasaṃvṛtam| āśramaṃ sudurādharṣamapi sendraiḥ surāsuraiḥ||
english: By virtue of their asceticism, this asylum is walled by trees and incapable of being conquered even by Indra, the celestials and the Asuras.

sanskrit: pakṣiṇo varjayantyetat tathānye vanacāriṇaḥ| viśanti mohād ye'pyatra na nivartanti te punaḥ||
english: Birds or other wild animals do not enter this asylum; whoever entereth this by mistake never returneth.

sanskrit: vibhūṣaṇaravāścātra śrūyante sakalākṣarāḥ| tūryagītasvanaścāpi gandho divyaśca rāghava ||
english: There is audible, O Rāghava, the sound of the dressing of Apsarās, their sweet-winged accents and that of their music and drums; and herçin pervadeth the celestial fragrance.

sanskrit: tretāgnayo'pi dīpyante dhūmo hyeṣa pradṛśyate| veṣṭayanniva vṛkṣāgrān kapotāṅgāruṇo ghanaḥ||
english: Here burneth the fire Tretā; and the smoke and cloud sable like to the wings of a pigeon envelope the tops of the trees.

sanskrit: ete vṛkṣāḥ prakāśante dhūmasaṃsaktamastakāḥ| meghajālapraticchannā vaidūryagirayo yathā ||
english: And there appear the trees, having their tops saturated with smoke and cloaked with clouds, like to so many Baidurya hills.

sanskrit: kuru praṇāmaṃ dharmātmasteṣāmuddiśya rāghava| lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā prayataḥ saṃhatāñjaliḥ||
english: Do you, O Rāghava, O virtuous-souled one, make obeisance to them along with your brother Lakṣmaṇa, with concentrated heart and folded palms.

sanskrit: praṇamanti hi ye teṣāmṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām| na teṣāmaśubhaṃ kiṃciccharīre rāma vidyate||
english: There resteth no sin in their persons, O Rāma, who bow to those self-controlled Saints.

sanskrit: tato rāmaḥ saha bhrātrā lakṣmaṇena kṛtāñjaliḥ| samuddiśya mahātmānastānṛṣīnabhyavādayat||
english: Thereupon Rāma, along with his younger brother Lakşmaņa, made obeisance to those high-souled ones.

sanskrit: abhivādya ca dharmātmā rāmo bhrātā ca lakṣmaṇaḥ| sugrīvo vānarāścaiva jagmuḥ saṃhaṣṭamānasāḥ||
english: Having paid homage (to the sacred memory of those great ones) the virtuous-souled Rāma his (younger) brother Laksmana, Sugriva and other monkeys, proceeded with delighted hearts.

sanskrit: te gatvā dūramadhvānaṃ tasmāt saptajanāśramāt| daddaśustāṃ durādharṣāṃ kiṣkindhāṃ vālipālitām||
english: And wending a distant way from that hermitage of the seven great ones, they beheld Kişkindhä, hard to conquer and occupied by Vali.

sanskrit: tatastu rāmānujarāmavānarāḥ pragṛhya śastrāṇyuditogratejasaḥ| purī sureśātmajavīryapālitāṃ vadhāya śatroḥ punarāgatāstviha||
english: Thereupon, Rāma, his younger brother and the monkeys taking their weapons, entered, to encompass the destruction of their enemies, the city (of Kişkindhā) reared by the prowess of Indra's son.

sanskrit: sā tathoktā tu vaidehī nirbhayā śokakarśitā| tṛṇamantarataḥ kṛtvā rāvaṇaṃ pratyabhāṣata||
english: Having been thus addressed, Vaidehī unaffected by fear, although exercised with grief, placing a blade of grass between herself and Rāvana, answered him.

sanskrit: rājā daśaratho nāma dharmaseturivācalaḥ| satyasaṃdhaḥ parijñāto yasya putraḥ sa rāghavaḥ|| nāmo nāma sa dharmātmā triṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ| dīrghabāhurviśālākṣo daivataṃ sa patirmama ||
english: There was a king named Dasaratha, the bridge of righteousness, like to a mountain, ever bearing regard towards the truth, and renowned among men, whose son is Rāghava. He is named Rāma, and is righteous-souled and celebrated over the three worlds. he is long-armed, of expansive eyes, like to a celestial—he is my husband.

sanskrit: ikṣvākūṇāṃ kule jātaḥ siṃhaskandho mahādyutiḥ| lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā yaste prāṇān vadhiṣyati|| pratyakṣaṃ yadyahaṃ tasya tvayā vai dharṣitā balāt| śayitā tvaṃ hataḥ saṃkhye janasthāne yathā kharaḥ||
english: Born in the race of the Ikşvākus, the has the shoulders of a lion and is possessed of exceeding effulgence-the same that along with his brother, Laksmana, shall take your life. If you had wronged me forcibly in his presence, you would have slain in battle in Janasthāna even as Khara.

sanskrit: ya ete rākṣasāḥ proktā ghorarūpā mahābalāḥ| rāghave nirviṣāḥ sarve suparṇe pannagā yathā||
english: All the mighty Rākşasas of grim visages, whom you have extolled (before me), shall be deprived of their venom before Rāma, as serpents are before Suparna,

sanskrit: tasya jyāvipramuktāste kharāḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇāḥ| śarīraṃ vidhamiṣyanti gaṅgākūlamivormayaḥ|7||
english: The shafts decorated with gold shot by the bow-string of Rāghava, shall pierce their bodies, as the waves of the Ganga (beat against) her banks.

sanskrit: asurairvā surairvā tvaṃ yadyavadhyo'si rāvaṇa| utpādya sumahad vairaṃ jīvaṃstasya na mokṣyase ||
english: Although, O Rāvana, you may be incapable of being slain either by the gods or the Asuras, yet having roused the high hostility of Rāghava, you will not be able to liberate your life.

sanskrit: sa te jīvitaśeṣasya rāghavo'ntakaro balī| paśoḍūṃpagatasyeva jīvitaṃ tava durlabham||
english: The strong Rāghava will compass the end of what remains of your life. Like the life of a beast tied to the sacrificial stake, your own is incapable of being reclaimed.

sanskrit: yadi paśyet sa rāmastvaṃ roṣadīptena cakṣuṣā| rakṣastvamadya nirdagdho yathā rudreṇa manmathaḥ||
english: Should Rāma look at you with eyes aglow with anger, you, O Raksasa, would be consumed even as Manmatha was by, Rudra.

sanskrit: yaścandraṃ nabhaso bhūmau pātayennāśayeta vā| sāgaraṃ śoṣayed vāpi sa sītāṃ mocayediha||
english: He who is able to bring down the Moon or destroy him, and to drink up the ocean dry, will surely liberate Sītā from here.

sanskrit: gatāsustvaṃ gataśrīko gatasattvo gatendriyaḥ| laṅkā vaidhavyasaṃyuktā tvatkṛtena bhaviṣyati ||
english: Your days are numbered, and auspiciousness has bidden you adieu. You are shorn of strength, and your senses have been dulled. And it is owing to you that Larkā shall be subject to widowhood.

sanskrit: na te pāpamidaṃ karma sukhodakaṃ bhaviṣyati| yāhaṃ nītā vinābhāvaṃ patipārdhvāt tvayā balāt||
english: That you by force have for naught carried me away from the side of my husband-this sinful act can never conduce to your felicity.

sanskrit: sa hi devarasaṃyukto mama bhartā mahādyutiḥ| nirbhayo vīryamāśritya śūnye vasati daṇḍake||
english: That exceedingly effulgent lord of mine along with my husband's younger brother, summoning up their energy, is fearlessly dwelling in the vacant Dandaka.

sanskrit: sa te vīryaṃ balaṃ darpamutsekaṃ ca tathāvidham| vyapaneṣyati gātrebhyaḥ śaravarṣeṇa saṃyuge||
english: By means of an arrowy shower in conflict, he will take your prowess and strength, your hauteur and wickedness out of your person,

sanskrit: yadā vināśo bhūtānāṃ dṛśyate kālacoditaḥ| tadā kārye pramādyanti narāḥ kālavaśaṃ gatāḥ||
english: When urged by the Destroyer, the destruction of creatures is perceptible, then, coming under the sway of the Destroyer, men become careless in their actions.

sanskrit: māṃ pradhṛṣya sa te kālaḥ prāpto'yaṃ rākṣasādhama| ātmano rākṣasānāṃ ca vadhāyāntaḥpurasya ca||
english: Having outraged me, you, O worst of Rāks asas your time come; for compassing your own destruction as well as that of the Rākşasas and those dwelling in your inner apartment.

sanskrit: na śakyā yajñamadhyasthā vediḥ srugbhāṇḍamaṇḍitā| dvijātimantrasampūtā caṇḍālenāvamarditum||
english: A Candāla cannot tread the dais reared the midst of a sacrifice beauteous with ladies, and vessels, and sanctified by the twice-born ones.

sanskrit: tathāhaṃ dharmanityasya dharmapatnī dṛḍhavratā| tvayā spraṣṭuṃ na śakyāhaṃ rākṣasādhama pāpinā||
english: So I, the religiously wedded wife of that one, ever intent on virtue, and (always) firm in my vows, is incapable, you vilest of Raksasas, of being touched by you, a sinner.

sanskrit: krīḍantī rājahaṃsena padmaṣaṇḍeṣu nityaśaḥ| haṃsī sā tṛṇamadhyasthaṃ kathaṃ drakṣyeta madgukam||
english: How can the female that has always ‘sported with her mate amidst lotuses, cast her eyes on a shag staying among rushes.

sanskrit: idaṃ śarīraṃ ni:saṃjñaṃ bandha vā ghātayasva vā| nedaṃ śarīraṃ rakṣyaṃ me jīvitaṃ vāpi rākṣasa ||
english: Do you either bind or destroy this body deprived of sensation. This body will I not protect, nor yet this life, O Rāvana;

sanskrit: na tu śakyamapakrośaṃ pṛthivyāṃ dātumātmanaḥ| evamuktvā tu vaidehī krodhāt suparuṣaṃ vacaḥ||
english: And I shall not be able to bring blame on myself in this world. having said these harsh words in wrath, Videha's daughter, Janaki, did not there again say anything to Rāvaņa.

sanskrit: rāvaṇaṃ jānakī tatra punarnovāca kiṃcana| sītāyā vacanaṃ śrutvā paruṣaṃ romaharṣaṇam|| pratyuvāca tataḥ sītāṃ bhayasaṃdarśanaṃ vacaḥ|
english: Hearing Sita's words, harsh and calculated to make one's down stand on end, Rāvana answered her in words tending to excite one's apprehension,

sanskrit: śṛṇumaithili madvākyaṃ māsān dvādaśa bhāmini || kālenānena nābhyeṣi yadi māṃ cāruhāsini| tatastvāṃ prātarāśārthaṃ sūdāśchetsyanti leśaśaḥ||
english: Hear, O Maithili, my words. O damsel if, O you of sweet smiles, within this time you do not turn yourself to me, the cooks shall cut you off in pieces to serve my morning mcal.

sanskrit: ityuktvā paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ rāvaṇaḥ śatrurāvaṇaḥ| rākṣasīśca tataḥ kruddha idaṃ vacanamabravīt||
english: Having herself spoken thus, Ravana-challenger of foes-growing exceedingly wroth, addressed the Rākşasis in these words,

sanskrit: śīghrameva hi rākṣasyo virūpā ghoradarśanāḥ| darpamasyāpaneṣyantu māṃsaśoṇitabhojanāḥ||
english: You frightful Rākşasīs terrible to behold, subsisting on flesh and gore, do you at once crush her pride.

sanskrit: vacanādeva tāstasya sughorā ghoradarśanāḥ| kṛtaprāñjalayo bhūtvā maithilī paryavārayan||
english: As soon as he had said this, those frightful and terrible Rākṣasīs with joined hands encircled Maithili.

sanskrit: sa tāḥ provāca rājāsau rāvaṇo ghoradarśanāḥ| pracalya caraṇotkarṣairdārayanniva medinīm||
english: Then the grim-visaged king Ravana, as if riving the earth by his tread, proceeding a pace or two, said,

sanskrit: aśokavanikāmadhye maithilī nīyatāmiti| tatreyaṃ rakṣyatāṃ gūḍhaṃ yuṣmābhiḥ parivāritā|| tatraināṃ tarjanaioraiḥ punaḥ sāntvaiśca maithilīm| ānayadhvaṃ vaśaṃ sarvā vanyāṃ gajavadhūmiva ||
english: Do you take Maithilī to the wood of Asokas. There surrounding her, do you secretly guard her; and there (sometimes) by storming, and (at other) by means of soft speech, do you all strive to bring Mithila's daughter, like a wild female elephant, under your sway.

sanskrit: iti pratisamādiṣṭā rākṣasyo rāvaṇena tāḥ| aśokavanikāṃ jagmurmaithilī parigṛhya tu|| sarvakāmaphalairvṛkṣairnānāpuṣpaphalairvṛtām| sarvakālamadaiścāpi dvijaiḥ samupasevitām||
english: Thus commanded by Rāvana, those Rākşasis taking Maithili along with them, went to the Asoka wood, abounding with trees granting every desire, and filled with various kinds of fruits and flowers, and frequented by fowls fraught with juices at all seasons.

sanskrit: sā tu śokaparitāṅgī maithilī janakātmajā| rākṣasīvaśamāpannā vyāghrīṇāṃ hariṇī yathā||
english: And as a doe comes under the subjection of tigresses, Janaka's daughter, Maithili, her frame worked up with grief, came under the sway of the Raksasis.

sanskrit: śokena mahatā trastā maithilī janakātmajā| na śarma labhate bhīruḥ pāśabaddhā mṛgī yathā||
english: And like a female deer fast bound by a trap, Janaka's timid daughter Maithilī, agitated by the mighty grief, did not attain respite.

sanskrit: na vindate tatra tu śarma maithilī virūpanetrābhiratīva tarjitā| patiṃ smarantī dayitaṃ ca devaraṃ vicetanābhūd bhayaśokapīḍitā ||
english: And greatly up-braided by the fierce eyes (of the Raksasis), Maithili did not know repose; and, afflicted with grief and fear, she, remembering her beloved lord along with Lakşmaņa swooned away.

sanskrit: itaḥ paraṃ prakṣipto'yaṃ sargaḥ|| praveśitāyāṃ sītāyāṃ laṅkāṃ prati pitāmaha| tadā provāca devendra parituṣṭaṃ śatakratum||
english: Having been thus addressed, Vaidehi unaffected by fear, although exercised with grief, placing a blade of grass between herself and Ravana, answered him.

sanskrit: trailokyasya hitārthāya rakṣasāmahitāya ca| laṅkāṃ praveśitā sītā rāvaṇena durātmanā ||
english: On Sītā having entered Lankā, the great father addressed the gratified Devendra of an hundred sacrifices, For bringing about the weal of the three worlds, and the woe of the Rākşasas, Sītā has been taken into Lankā by the wickedminded, Rāvaņa.

sanskrit: pativratā mahābhāgā nityaṃ caiva sustraidhitā| apaśyantī ca bhatauraṃ paśyantī rākṣasījanam|| rākṣasībhiḥ parivṛtā bhartṛdarśanalālasā|
english: Devoted to her husband, the exalted lady always brought up in happiness, not seeing her husband, and seeing (on the other hand) environed by numbers of Räkşasīs,-is hungering after the sight of her lord.

sanskrit: niviṣṭā hi purī laṅkā tīre nadanadīpateḥ|| kathaṃ jñāsyati tāṃ rāmastatrasthāṃ tāmaninditām|
english: The city of Lankā is situated on the shores of the lord of rivers and streams. How can Rāma get a knowledge of that blameless one, staying there?

sanskrit: duḥśaṃ saṃcintayanitī sā bahuśaḥ paridurlabhā || prāṇayātrāmakurrāṇā prāṇāṃstyakṣyatyasaṃśayam| sa bhūyaḥ saṃśayo jātaḥ sītāyāḥ prāṇasaṃkṣaye||
english: Brooding over the various ills she has undergone, that exceedingly rare damsel is passing her days. Surely she will resign her existence. Great is the doubt that has arisen as to Sītā putting a period to her existence.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ śīghramito gatvā sītāṃ paśya śubhānanām| praviśya nagarī laṅkāṃ prayaccha haviruttamam||
english: Having yourself from here, do you see the fair-faced Sītā. having entered the city of Lankā, Offer excellent clarified butter.

sanskrit: evamukto'tha devendraḥ purī rāvaṇapālitām| āgacchannidrayā sārdha bhagavān pākaśāsanaḥ||
english: Thus addressed by the reverend chastiser of Pāka, Devendra in company with sleep, approached the city ruled by Rāvana.

sanskrit: nidrāṃ covāca gaccha tvaṃ rākṣasān sampramohaya| sā tathoktā maghavatā devī paramaharṣitā|| devakāryārthasiddhayarthaṃ prāmohayata rākṣasān |
english: He then addressed sleep, saying. Go you; and stupefy the Räksasas. Thus accosted by Maghavat, that goddess, exceedingly delighted, for securing success to the work of the celestials, covered the Rākşasas with stupor.

sanskrit: etasminnantare devaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ śacīpatiḥ|| āsamāda vanasthāṃ tāṃ vacanaṃ cedamabravīt |
english: In the meanwhile, that god, the thousand-eyed lord of Śacī went to (Sītā) staying in the woods, and spoke to her these words,

sanskrit: devarājo'smi bhadraṃ te iha cāsmi śucismite|| ahaṃ tvāṃ kāryaniddadhyarthaṃ rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ| sāhāyyaṃ kalpayiṣyāmi mā śuco janakātmaje ||
english: I am the sovereign of the celestials. Good betide you! I am here, O you of luminous smiles! For securing success to the work of the magnanimous Rāghava, I will lend my aid to you. Do not, Odaughter of Janaka, grieve.

sanskrit: matprasādāt samudraṃ sa tariṣyati balaiḥ saha| mayaiveha ca rākṣasyo māyāya mohitāḥ śubhe||
english: Through my grace, he shall along with his forces cross over the ocean. And, O excellent wench, I have by my supernal power, stupified the Raksasis.

sanskrit: tasmādannamidaṃ sīte haviṣyānnahaṃ svayam| sa tvāṃ saṃgṛhya vaidehi āgataḥ saha nidrayā|14||
english: And, O Sita, for this reason, I along with sleep, taking these rice, rice boiled in clarified butter, have, O Vaidehi, corne to you.

sanskrit: etadatsyasi maddhastānna tvāṃ vādhiṣyate śubhe| kṣudhā tṛṣā ca rambhoru varṣāṇāmayutairapi||
english: If you partake of these from my hand, you shall never O beauteous one, be afflicted either with hunger or thirst, O you of thighs resembling rambhā (trunks), for years.

sanskrit: evamuktā tu devendramuvāca pariśaṅkitā| kathaṃ jānāmi devendraṃ tvāmihasthaṃ khajāpatim||
english: Thus addressed, Sītā, alarmed, said, How can I know you for Devendra, Saci's husband, staying here?

sanskrit: devaliṅgāni dṛṣṭāni rāmalakṣmaṇasaṃnidhau| tāni darśaya devendra yadi tvaṃ devarāṭ svayam||
english: By the side of Rāma and Lakşmaņa, I had beheld the signs of the celestials. If, O Devendra, you are yourself the sovereign of the celestials, show those to me.

sanskrit: sītāyā vacanaṃ śrutvā tathā cakre śacīpatiḥ| gṛthivīṃ nāspṛśat padbhyāmanimeṣekṣaṇāni ca|| arajo'mbaradhārī ca namlīnakusumastathā| taṃ jñātvā lakṣṇaiḥ sītā vāsavaṃ pariharṣitā ||
english: Hearing Sītā's words, the lord of Saçī did accordingly. he did not touch the earth with his feet, and his eyes remained winkless. he bloomed in youth, and the blossoms did not fade on his attire. Thereupon knowing him for Vāsava, Sītā was overjoyed.

sanskrit: uvāca vākyaṃ rudatī bhagavan rāghavaṃ prati| kaha bhrātrā mahābāhurdiṣṭayaḥ me śrutimāgataḥ||
english: And weeping, she spoke regarding Rāghava, By luck it is that I had heard of that mightyarmed one along with his brother.

sanskrit: yathā me śvaśuro rājā yathā ca mithilādhipaḥ| sathā tvamadya paśyāmi sanātho me patistvayā||
english: As is my father-in-law, the king, as is the master of Mithilā, so are you (to me), you whom I behold to-day; my husband has now found a protector.

sanskrit: tavājñayā ca devendra payobhūtamidaṃ haviḥ| aśiṣyāmi tvayā dattaṃ raghūṇāṃ kulavarghanam||
english: And by your command, O Devendra, will I partake of this pāyasa cooked with milk, which has been offered to me, and which shall enhance (the prosperity) of our race.

sanskrit: indrahastād gṛhītvā tat pāyasaṃ sā śucismitā| nyavedayata bharne sā lakṣmaṇāya ca maithilī||
english: Thereupon taking the pāyasa from Indra's hands, that Maithilī of luminous smiles (mentally) offered it to her husband as well as Laksmana.

sanskrit: yadi jīvati me bhartā saha bhrātrā mahābalaḥ| idamastu tayorbhaktyā tadāśnāt svayam||
english: If my mighty lord live along with his brother, let this through my reverence for them, be theirs. She then partook of the pāyasa herself.

sanskrit: itīva tat prāśya havirvarānanā jahau kṣudhāduḥkhasamudbhavaṃ ca tam| indrāt pravṛttimupalabhya jānakī kākutsthayoḥ prītamanā babhūva ||
english: Having thus eaten it, that one of excellent countenance, had her hunger and rising sorrow removed; and attaining a mental tendency from Indra, Janaki grew glad with reference to the Kakutsthas.

sanskrit: sa cāpi śakrastridivālayaṃ tadā prīto yayau rāghavakāryasiddhaye| āmantrya sītāṃ sa tato mahātmā jagāma nidrāsahitaḥ svamālayam||
english: And Sakra also for bringing about the success of Rāghava's work, with a pleased mind, went to the abode of celestials. And greeting Sītā again and again, that high-souled celestial, in company with sleep went back to his own abode.

sanskrit: tataḥ śūrpaṇakhāṃ dṛṣṭvā bruvantī paruṣaṃ vacaḥ| amātyamadhye saṃkruddhaḥ paripapraccha rāvaṇaḥ||
english: Seeing Śūrpanakhā speak harsh words in the midst of the courtiers, Ravana, being enraged, asked her.

sanskrit: kaśca rāmaḥ kathaṃvīryaḥ kiṃrūpaḥ kiṃparākramaḥ| kimarthe daṇḍakāraṇyaṃ praviṣṭaśca sudustaram||
english: Who is Rāma? And what is his prowess? And what his form? And what his power? And why had he entered the forest of Dandaka, difficult to range?

sanskrit: āyughaṃ kiṃ ca rāmasya yena te rākṣasā hatāḥ| kharaśca nihataḥ saṃkhye dūṣaṇastriśirāstathā||
english: And what Rāma's weapons, by means of which he had slain the Rākşasas?. And Khara has been slain in battle, and Dūşaņa and Trisirā.

sanskrit: tattvaṃ brūhi manojñāṅgi kena tvaṃ ca virūpitā | ityuktā rākṣasendreṇa rākṣasī krodhamūrchitā ||
english: Do you, O you of a pleasing person, tell me the truth. And who had deformed you?

sanskrit: tato rāmaṃ yathānyāyamākhyātumupacakrame| dīrghabāhurviśālākṣaścīrakṛṣṇājināmbaraḥ|| kandarpasamarūpaśca rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ|
english: Thus addressed by the lord of the Rākṣasas, the Raksasi, transported with rage, commenced to duly narrate all about Rāma. Rāma the son of Dasaratha is long-armed, of expansive eyes, clad in bark and dark deer-skin, and like Kandarpa in grace.

sanskrit: śakracāpanibhaṃ cāpaṃ vikṛṣya kanakāṅgadam|| dīptān tripati nārācān saniva mahāviṣān |
english: And drawing a bow resembling that of Sakra, decked with golden rings, he discharges blazing nāracas, like to serpents of virulent poison.

sanskrit: nādadānaṃ śarān ghorān vimuñcantaṃ mahābalam|7|| na kārmukaṃ vikarṣantaṃ rāmaṃ paśyāmi saṃyuge| hanyamānaṃ tu tatsainyaṃ paśyāmi śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ|| indreṇevottamaṃ sasyamāhataṃ tvaśmavṛṣṭibhiḥ| rakṣasāṃ bhīmavīryāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi caturdaśa|| nihatāni śaraistīkṣṇaistenaikena padātinā| ardhādhikamuhūrtena kharaśca sahadūṣaṇaḥ|| ṛṣīṇāmabhayaṃ dattaṃ kṛtakṣemāśca daṇḍakāḥ|| ekā kathaṃcitmuktāhaṃ paribhūya mahātmanā | strīvadhaṃ śaṅkamānena rāmeṇa viditātmanā|| bhrātā cāsya mahātejā guṇatastulyavikramaḥ|
english: I do not see in the field, Rāma drawing his bow: I only see the host being slaughtered by a shower of shafts. And as Indra destroys (a field of) goodly crops, by pouring down hail stones, fourteen thousand Räksasas of dreadful prowess, as well as Khara and Duşaņa were in a little over a moment slain with sharp shafts by Rāma alone fighting on foot. And he had reassured the saints, and after having been deformed, I alone from fear of slaying a woman, have been let off by the high-souled Rāma knowing self.

sanskrit: anuraktaśca bhaktaśca lakṣmaṇo nāma vīryavān|| amarṣī durjayo jetā vikrānto buddhimān balī| rāmasya dakṣiṇo bāhunityaṃ prāṇo bahiścaraḥ||
english: His brother is endued with mighty energy, and in merit, is of equal prowess, and he is devoted to his brother, and bear him regard; the puissant one is named Laksmana. And wrathful and invincible and victorious, and powerful, and intelligent and mighty, (he) is Rāma's right-arı-his life ranging externally.

sanskrit: rāmasya tu viśālākṣī pūrṇendusadṛśānanā| dharmapatnī priyā nityaṃ bhartuḥ priyahite ratā||
english: And Rāma's virtuously wedded beloved wife having expansive eyes, and a face resembling the full-moon, is ever to the welfare of her lord.

sanskrit: sā sukeśī sunāsorū: surūpā ca yaśasvinī| devateva vanasyāsya rājate śrīrivāparā||
english: And that fair-haired, fair-nosed, and fairthighed illustrious one possessed of beauty, grace the forest like a goddess, as if a goddess of wealth herself.

sanskrit: taptakāñcanavarṇābhā raktatuṅganakhī śubhā| sītā nāma varārohā vaidehī tanumadhyamā||
english: Of the lustre of burnished gold, with her finger nails reddish and projecting, and graceful, that surpassingly lovely wench is named Sītā—the slender-waisted daughter of Videha.

sanskrit: naiva devī na gandharvī na yakṣī na ca kiṃnarī| tathārūpā mayā nārī dṛṣṭapūrvā mahītale||
english: And neither a goddess, nor a Gandharvi, nor a Yaksi, nor a Kinnari, had I seen before on earth, possessed of such beauty.

sanskrit: yasya sītā bhaved bhāryā yaṃ ca hṛṣṭā pariṣvajet| abhijīvet sa sarveṣu lokeṣvapi puraṃdarāt||
english: He that shall have Sītā for his spouse, and who shall be warmly embraced by her, shall live longer in the world than the Lord of celestials himself.

sanskrit: sā suśīlā vapuḥślādhyā rūpeṇāpratimā bhuvi| tavānurūpā bhāryā sā tvaṃ ca tasyāḥ patirvaraḥ||
english: That good-natured girl, unparalleled on earth in loveliness, who can well pride herself on her person, is a worthy wife for you, and you too are a fit husband for her.

sanskrit: tāṃ tu vistīrṇajaghanāṃ pīnottuṅgapayodharām| bhāryārthe tu tavānetumudyatāhaṃ varānanām|| virūpitāsmi krūreṇa lakṣmaṇena mahābhuja|
english: It is to bring over for you that one of spacious hips, and a high and well-developed bust, that I had put forth my endeavours. But, O mightyarmed one I have been disfigured by the wicked Laksmana.

sanskrit: tāṃ tu dṛṣṭvādya vaidehī pūrṇacandranibhānanām|| manmathasya śarāṇāṃ ca tvaṃ vidheyo bhaviṣyasi|
english: As soon as you have seen Vaidehi having a countenance resembling the full moon, you shall be afflicted with the shafts of Cupid.

sanskrit: yadi tasyāmabhiprāyo bhāryātve tava jāyate| śīghramudbhiyatāṃ pādo jayārthamiha dakṣiṇaḥ||
english: If it is your purpose to have her for your wife, at once stretch forth your right leg. for attaining success.

sanskrit: rocate yati te vākyaṃ mamaitad rākṣaseśvara| kriyatāṃ nirviśaṅkena vacanaṃ mama rāvaṇa ||
english: If, O lord of Raksasas, you relish my speech, do you then, O Ravana, without fear, do as I tell you.

sanskrit: vijñāyaiṣāmaśaktiṃ ca kriyatāṃ ca mahābala| sītā tavānavadyāṅgī bhāryātve rākṣaseśvara||
english: Understanding their incapacity, do you, O lord of Rākṣasas, for making her your wife, by force carry away the frail Sītā of a blameless person.

sanskrit: hatāñjanasthānagatān niśācarān| kharaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā nihataṃ ca dūṣaṇaṃ tvamadya kṛtyaṃ pratipattumarhasi||
english: Hearing that Rāma by means of straight coursing shafts, has slain the Rākşasas that had gone to Janasthāna, and seeing Khara and Düşaņa, killed, do you ascertaining your course, adopt it.

sanskrit: tamagnimiva saṃśāntamambuhīnamivārṇavam| gataprabhamivādityaṃ svargasthaṃ prekṣya bhūmipam|| kausalyā bāṣpapūrṇākṣī vividhaṃ śokakarśitā| upagṛhya śiro rājñaḥ kaikeyī pratyabhāṣata ||
english: Seeing the king had ascended heaven, like to a fire that has cooled, or an ocean deprived of its waters, or the sun shorn of his splendour, Kausalyā afflicted with woe, taking on her lap the head of the king, with tears in her eyes, said.

sanskrit: sakāmā bhava kaikeyi bhukṣva rājyamakaṇṭakam| tyaktvā rājānamekānā nṛśaṃse duṣṭacāriṇi || vihāya māṃ gato rāmo bhartā ca svargato mama| vipathe sārthahīneva nāhaṃ jīvitumutsahe||
english: O Kaikeyī, attain you your wished: do you enjoy this kingdom rid of your thorn. O cruel one, O you of wicked ways, you that forsaking the king had set your heart (on having your son crowned), Rāma had gone away, forsaking me; and now my lord has ascended heaven. I can no longer bear to live, like one left lone in a wilderness by her companions.

sanskrit: bhartāraṃ tu parityajya kā strī daivatamātmanaḥ| icchejjīvitumanyatra kaikeyyāstyaktadharmaṇaḥ||
english: What other woman except Kaikeyi lost to righteousness, having lost her deity, her lord, wishes to carry on existence in another's kingdom?

sanskrit: na lubdho budhyate doṣān kiṃpākamiva bhakṣayan| kubjānimittaṃ kaikeyyā rāghavāṇāṃ kulaṃ hatam|| aniyoge niyuktena rājñā rāmaṃ vivāsitam| sabhārya janakaḥ śrutvā paritapsyatyahaṃ yathā|7||
english: As a covetous person taking poison (through anger or some other passion), does not consider himself guilty, (so Kaikeyī) having done this evil through Manthara's incitement, does not bring her guilt home to her mind. It is through the instrumentality of the humpbacked woman that this race of the Rāghavas has been destroyed by Kaikeyi. Hearing that the king being made to do an unrighteous action, has banished Rāma together with his wife, king Janaka will be filled with grief as I have been.

sanskrit: sa māmanāthāṃ vidhavāṃ nādya jānāti dhārmikaḥ| rāmaḥ kamalapatrākṣo jīvanāśamito gataḥ||
english: That virtuous one does not know that to-day I have become helpless and been widowed. Răma of eyes resembling lotus-petals has living been removed from my sight.

sanskrit: videharājasya sutā tathā cārutapasvinī| duḥkhasyānucitā duḥkhaṃ vane paryudvijiṣyati||
english: The fair daughter of Videha's king unworthy of hardship, in ascetic guise is leading a life of trouble and terror in the woods.

sanskrit: nadatāṃ bhīmaghoṣāṇāṃ niśāsu mṛgapakṣiṇām| niśamyamānā saṃtrastā rāghavaṃ saṃśrayiṣyati||
english: Hearing at night the dreadful roars of birds and beasts crying, she exceedingly frightened takes shelter with Rāghava.

sanskrit: vṛddhaścaivālpaputraśca vedehīmanucintayan| so'pi śokasamāviṣṭo nūnaṃ tyakṣyati jīvitam|| sāhamacaiva diṣṭāntaṃ gamiṣyāmi pativratā| idaṃ śarīramāliṅgaya pravekṣyāmi hutāśanam||
english: Old and having an only daughter, he revolving in his mind thoughts of Vaidehi, shall, smitten with grief, surely renounce his life. I ever faithful to my lord will die this very day, embracing this body; I will enter fire.

sanskrit: tāṃ tataḥ sampariṣvajya vilapantī tapasvinīm| vyapaninyuḥ suduḥkhātā kausalyāṃ vyāvahārikāḥ||
english: As embracing the (dead) body, that unfortunate lady was bewailing, the courtiers had the distressed (queen) removed from there.

sanskrit: tailadroṇyāṃ tadāmātyāḥ saṃveśya jagatīpatim| rājñaḥ sarvāṇyathādiṣṭāścakruḥ karmāṇyanantaram||
english: Then placing the corpse of the king in a (capacious) pan with oil, the courtiers performed the mourning rites of the monarch.

sanskrit: na tu saṃkālanaṃ rājño vinā putreṇa mantriṇaḥ| sarvajñāḥ kartumīṣuste tato rakṣanti bhūmipam|| tailadroṇyāṃ śāyitaṃ taṃ sacivaistu narādhipam| hā mṛto'yamiti jñātvā striyastāḥ paryadevayan||
english: But well versed in everything, the counsellors, in the absence of his son, did not perform the funeral obsequies of the king; and therefore they placed his body stretched in the pan of oil. Alas! at length concluding it for certain that the king was dead, the ladies burst out into lamentaions.

sanskrit: bāhūnucchritya kṛpaṇā netraprasravaṇairmukhaiḥ| rudatyaḥ śokasaṃtaptāḥ kṛpaṇaṃ paryadevayan||
english: And raising their arms, with tears trickling down their faces, they in dire affliction and extremely exercised with grief, lamented.

sanskrit: hā mahārāja rāmeṇa saṃtataṃ priyavādinā| vihīnāḥ satyasaṃdhena kimarthaṃ vijahāsi naḥ||
english: O monarch, why do you forsake us, who have been already deprived of Rāma ever speaking fair and firm in promise?

sanskrit: kaikeyyā duṣṭabhāvāyā rāghaveṇa vivarjitāḥ| kathaṃ sapatnyā vatsyāmaḥ samīpe vidhavā vayam||
english: Renounced by Rāma, how shall we, rendered widows, stay with the wicked Kaikeyi, co-wife with us?

sanskrit: sa hi nāthaḥ sa cāsmākaṃ tava ca prabhurātmavān| vanaṃ rāmo gataḥ śrīmān vihāya nṛpatiśriyam||
english: That one of free soul is our master, as he is the lord of yourself. Rāma has gone to the woods, forsaking regal dignity.

sanskrit: tvayā tena ca vīreṇa vinā vyasanamohitāḥ| kathaṃ vayaṃ nivatsyāmaḥ kaikeyyā ca vidūṣitāḥ||
english: Deprived of you as well as that hero, and overwhelmed with misfortune, how shall we live reprimanded by Kaikeyi?

sanskrit: yayā ca rājā rāmaśca lakṣmaṇaśca mahābalaḥ| sītayā saha saṃtyaktāḥ sā kamanyaṃ na hāsyati ||
english: She that has renounced the king, Rāma, and Lakşmaņa along with Sītā, whom can such a one not renounce?

sanskrit: tā bāṣpeṇa ca saṃvītāḥ śokena vipulena ca| vyaceṣṭanta nirānandā rāghavasya varastriyaḥ||
english: Thus with tears in their eyes, the wives of that descendant of Raghu, joyless and convulsed with a huge passion, displayed signs of sorrow.

sanskrit: niśā nakṣatrahīneva strīva bhartṛvivarjitā| purī nārājatāyodhyā hīnā rājñā mahātmanā|| bāṣpaparyākulajanā hāhābhūtakulāṅganā| śūnyacatvaraveśmāntā na babhrāja yathāpuram||
english: Like a night without stars, like a fair one forsaken by her husband, the city of Ayodhyā without the magnanimous monarch did not appear delightful as it had done before, with the populace filled with tears, the ladies uttering exclamations of distress, and the terraces and courts deserted.

sanskrit: gate tu śokāt tridivaṃ narādhipe mahītalasthāsu nṛpāṅganāsu ca| nivṛttacāraḥ sahasā gato raviḥ pravṛttacārā rajanī hyupasthitā||
english: On the lord of men having ascended heaven from grief, and the wives of the king remaining on the earth, the sun, his journey done, set, and the night began her course.

sanskrit: nārocayaste suhṛdaḥ samāgatāḥ| itīva tasmiśayane nyaveśayan vicintya rājānamacintyadarśanam||
english: The idea of consuming the king's corpse in the absence of his son did not recommended itself to the assembled. adherents (of the departed). Thinking this, they in that way laid the king endowed with an inconceivably dignified presence.

sanskrit: gataprabhā dyauriva bhāskaraṃ vinā vyapetanakṣatragaṇeva śarvarī| purī babhāse rahitā mahātmanā kaṇṭhāsrakaṇṭhākulamārgacatvarā ||
english: And with her terraces overflowing with tears that flooded the throats of the mourners, the city appeared like the welkin without its splendour in the absence of the sun, or the night with the stars enveloped.

sanskrit: narāśca nāryaśca sametya saṃghaśo vigarhamāṇā bharatasya mātaram| tadā nagā~ naradevasaṃkṣaye babhūvurārtā na ca śarma lebhire||
english: And on on the demise of that illustrious personage, in the city men and women in multitudes, censuring Bharata's mother, became extremely distressed, and did not attain peace of mind.

sanskrit: sa evaṃ bruvatī sītāṃ dharmajñā dharmavatsalaḥ| na netuṃ kurute buddhiṃ vane duḥkhāni cintayan||
english: That lover of virtue, thinking of the miseries of the forest, resolved no to take Sītā with him, who was versed in religious lore's and had spoken thus.

sanskrit: sāntvayitvā tatastāṃ tu bāṣpadūṣitalocanām| nivartanārthe dharmātmā vākyametaduvāca ha||
english: And consoling her whose eyes were stained with tears, that virtuous-souled one spoke to her the following words with a view to prevent her from going.

sanskrit: sīte mahākulīnāsi dharme ca niratā sadā| ihācarasva dharmaṃ tvaṃ yathā me manasaḥ sukham||
english: Oh Sītā, you are born of an illustrious family and ever intent on the performance of religious deeds; do you practise virtue here as it may conduce to the happiness of my mind.

sanskrit: sīte yathā tvāṃ vakṣyāmi tathā kāryaṃ tvayābale| vane doṣā hi bahavo vasatastān nibodha me||
english: Oh Sītā, Oh you of the weaker sex, Do you act up to my counsels; there are evils enough in the forest, do you learn them from me who am about to dwell in it.

sanskrit: sīte vimucyatāmeṣā vanavāsakṛtā matiḥ| bahudoṣaṃ hi kāntāraṃ vanamityabhidhīyate||
english: Renounce therefore, Oh Sītă, your intention of flying as an exile to the forest, which for its impenetrableness is said to abound in evils.

sanskrit: hitabuddhyā khalu vaco mayaitadabhidhīyate| sadā sukhaṃ na jānāmi duḥkhameva sadā vanam||
english: It is for your welfare that I give utterance to these words; happiness there is none, it is always covered with miseries.

sanskrit: girinirjharasambhūtā girinirdarivāsinām| siṃhānāṃ ninadā duḥkhāḥ śrotuṃ duḥkhamatovanam||
english: The roarings of the lions living in the caves of mountains, swelling with the sounds of the water-falls, produce a very painful impression upon the ears; so the wood is full of misery.

sanskrit: krīḍamānāśca visrabdhāmattāḥ śūnye tathā mṛgāḥ| dṛṣṭvā samabhivartante sīte duḥkhamato vanam||
english: Animals, all maddened, sporting in solitude, seeing (man), approach to attack him; so the wood is full of misery.

sanskrit: sagrāhāḥ saritaścaiva paṅkavatyastu dustarāḥ| mattairapi gajairnityamato duḥkhataraṃ vanam ||
english: The rivers are full of crocodiles, sharks, and other fearful animals, muddy and impassable and always infested with infuriated elephants; so the wood is full of misery.

sanskrit: latākaṇṭakasaṃkīrṇāḥ kṛkavākūpanāditāḥ| nirapāśca suduḥkhāśca mārgā duḥkhamato vanam||
english: There the wayfarers are covered with creepers and thorns they are void of drinking water ever resounded with the noise of the wild fowls, so the wood is full of misery.

sanskrit: supyate parṇaśayyāsu svayaṃbhagnāsu bhūtale| rātriṣu śramakhinnena tasmād duḥkhamato vanam||
english: Being exhausted with the toil of the day, the dwellers of the wood have to sleep in night on the bed made of leaves fallen from the trees on the surface of the ground; so the wood is full of misery.

sanskrit: ahorātraṃ ca saṃtoṣaḥ kartavyo niyatātmanā| phalairvṛkṣāvapatitaiḥ sīte duḥkhamato vanam||
english: With the (supply of) fruits that have fallen from the trees man of self discipline must content himself morning and evening; so the wood, O Sītă, is full of misery.

sanskrit: upavāsaśca kartavyo yathā prāṇena maithili| jaṭābhāraśca kartavyo valkalāmbaradhāraṇam|| devatānāṃ pitṛṇāṃ ca kartavyaṃ vidhipūrvakam| prāptānāmatithīnāṃ ca nityaśaḥ pratipūjanam|| kāryastrirabhiṣekaśca kāle kāle ca nityaśaḥ| caratāṃ niyamenaiva tasmād duḥkhataraṃ vanam||
english: One has to fast, O Maithili, according to his might, to wear matted hair and bark, to adore the deities and his ancestors according to due rites, every day to serve the guests that come to him, and observing the rules of asceticism, to bathe every day thrice, namely, in the morning, in the mid-day and in the evening; so the wood is full of misery.

sanskrit: upahāraśca kartavyaḥ kusumaiḥ svayamāhataiḥ| ārṣeṇa vidhinā vedyāṃ sīte duḥkhamato vanam||
english: One has to offer presents of flowers collected by his ownself to the altars, O Sītā, according to the rites of the ascetics; so the wood is full of misery.

sanskrit: yathālabdhena kartavyaḥ saṃtoṣastena maithili| yatāhārairvanacaraiḥ sīte duḥkhamato vanam||
english: Those that dwell in the forest will have to remain content, having practised moderation in food, O Maithill, with whatever edibles are attainable in the forest; so the wood is full of misery.

sanskrit: atīva vātastimiraṃ bubhukṣā cāsti nityaśaḥ| bhayāni ca mahāntyatra ato du:khataraṃ vanam||
english: There are always violent winds, darkness hunger, and great fear; so the wood is full of misery.

sanskrit: sarīsṛpāśca bahavo bahurūpāśca bhāmini| caranti pathi te dāttato duḥkhataraṃ vanam||
english: Reptiles, many and of various kinds, creep there on the path, O excellent lady, with haughtiness; so the wood is full of misery.

sanskrit: nadīnilayanāḥ sarpā nadīkuṭilagāminaḥ| tiṣṭhantyāvṛtya panthānamato duḥkhataraṃ vanam||
english: And snakes living in the rivers and of crooked course like them, always await the wayfarers, hindering the passers-by: so the wood is full of misery.

sanskrit: pataṅgā vṛścikāḥ kīṭā daṃśāśca maśakaiḥ saha| bādhante nityamabale sarvaṃ duḥkhamato vanam||
english: Birds, scorpions, insects mosquito's and wild gnats, always disturb the dwellers, O fair one' of the weaker sex; so the wood is full misery.

sanskrit: dumāḥ kaṇṭakinaścaiva kuśāḥ kāśāśca bhāmini| vane vyākulaśākhāgrāstena duḥkhamato vanam||
english: There are trees full of thorns, having their branches moving to and fro, and the kusa and kāsa grasses with thorny blades constantly undulating; so the wood is full misery.

sanskrit: kāyakleśāśca bahavo bhayāni vividhāni ca| araṇyavāse vasato duḥkhameva sadā vanam|| krodhalobhau vimoktavyau kartavyā tapase matiḥ| na bhetavyaṃ ca bhetavye duḥkhaṃ nityamato vanam||
english: There are various physical afflictions and divers fears and great misery consequent upon living in the forest. Anger and desires are to be renounced, the heart is to be set on ascetic austerities, fear in the fearful objects is to be cast off; so the wood is full of misery.

sanskrit: tadalaṃ te vanaṃ gatvā kṣemaṃ nahi vanaṃ tava| vimṛśaniva paśyāmi bahudoṣakaraṃ vanam||
english: You should not therefore go to the forest, it forebodes no good to you. Weighing well, have I concluded that the forest abounds in innumerable evils.

sanskrit: vanaṃ tu netuṃ na kṛtā matiryadā babhūva rāmeṇa tadā mahātmanā| na tasya sītā vacanaṃ cakāra taṃ tato'bravīd rāmamidaṃ suduḥkhitā||
english: While the high-souled Rāma, resolved thus not to take Sītā with him to the forest, she, greatly sorry, did not accept his words and spoke to him in the following way.

sanskrit: sumālinaṃ hataṃ dṛṣṭvā vasunā bhasmasātkṛtam| svasainyaṃ vidrutaṃ cāpi lakṣayitvāditaṃ suraiḥ|| tataḥ sa balavānkruddho rāvaṇasya sutastadā| nivartya rākṣasānsanmeighanādo vyavasthitaḥ||
english: Beholding Sumali slain and reduced to ashes by Vasu and being assailed by the deities the Räksasa host fled into diverse directions. And collecting all the Rākşasas stood there the highly powerful Meghanāda, enraged, the son of Ravana.

sanskrit: sa rathena mahārheṇa kāmagena mahārathaḥ| abhidudrāva senāṃ tāṃ vanānyagniriva jvalan||
english: Like to flaming fire approaching towards forest that great car-warrior encountered the enemies in a precious car coursing at will.

sanskrit: tataḥ praviśatastasya vividhāyudhadhāriṇaḥ| vidudruvurdiśaḥ sarvā darśanādeva devatāḥ||
english: As soon as he, armed with various weapons, entered the field the celestials, at his very sight. And away to all directions.

sanskrit: na babhūva tadā kaścidyuyutsorasya saṃmukhe| sarvānāviddhya vitrastāṃstataḥ śakro'bravītsurān||5
english: None could stand before him, well-versed in war-fare. Thereupon beholding the deities terrified and pierced with shafts, Indra, the king of gods, said.

sanskrit: na bhetavyaṃ na gantavyaṃ nivartadhvaṃ raṇe surāḥ| eṣa gacchati putro me yuddhārthamaparājitaḥ||
english: Be not afraid, O you celestials; do not fly away; come back to the battle; this my son, who has never been vanquished, goes to battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ śakrasuto devo jayanta iti viśrutaḥ| rathenādbhutakalpena saṅgrāme so'bhyavartata|7||
english: Thereupon Sakra's son, known as divine Jayanta, proceeded towards the field of action by a wondrous car.

sanskrit: tataste tridaśāḥ sarve parivārya śacīsutam| rāvaṇasya sutaṃ yuddhe samāsādya prajanire|||||
english: Having encircled Saci's son and encountered Rāvana's son, the deities began to assail him.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ yuddhaṃ samabhavatsadṛśaṃ devarakṣasām| mahendrasya ca putrasya rākṣasendrasutasya ca ||
english: The encounter between Mahendra's son Jayanta and Rāvana's son Meghanāda was like one between gods and demons.

sanskrit: tato mātaliputrasya gomukhasya sa rāvaṇiḥ| sāratheḥ pātayāmāsa śarānkanakabhūṣaṇān||
english: Thereupon Rāvana's son began to assail, with shafts feathered in gold, his (Jayanta's) charioteer Gomukha, Mātali's son.

sanskrit: śacīsutaścāpi tathā jayantastasya sārathim| taṃ cāpi rāvaṇiḥ kruddhaḥ samantātpratyavidhyatā || sa hi krodhasamāviṣṭo balī visphāritekṣaṇaḥ| rāvaṇiḥ śakratanayaṃ śaravarṣairavākirat||
english: Sacīs son too, enraged, assailed on all sides, Rāvana's son and his charioteer. And the powerful Rāvani, stricken with ire and with eyes expanded, covered Sakra's son with arrows.

sanskrit: tato nānāpraharaṇāñchitadhārānsahasraśaḥ| pātayāmāsa saṃkruddhaḥ surasainyeṣu rāvaṇiḥ|| śataghnīmusalaprāsagadākhaṅgaparaśvadhān| mahānti giriśṛṅgāṇi pātayāmāsa rāvaṇiḥ||
