english: Thereupon Rāvana's son struck the celestial host with thousands of huge mountain summits, Śataghnīs, maces, Prāsas, Prāsas, clubs, daggers, Paraśus and various other sharp pointed weapons.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravyathitā lokāḥ saṃjajñe ca tamastataḥ| tasya rāvaṇaputrasya śatrusainyāni nighnataḥ||
english: Rāvana's son thus striking Indra's army the quarters were enshrouded with darkness by his illusory power.

sanskrit: tatastadaivatabalaṃ samantāttaṃ śacīsutam| bahuprakāramasvasthamabhavaccharapīḍitam||
english: Being overpowered with arrows on all sides the celestial army, leaving aside Jayanta, became restless.

sanskrit: nābhyajānanta cānyonyaṃ rakṣo vā devatāthavā| tatra tatra viparyastaṃ samantātparidhāvata ||
english: The deities or the Rākşasas, they could not recognise one another. And being distressed they ran about on all sides.

sanskrit: devā devānijaghnuste rākṣasānrākṣasāstathā| saṃmūḍhāstamasā channā vyadravanapare tathā||
english: Being enveloped with darkness and having their senses bewildered the celestials killed their own kith and the Rākṣasas their own men, and others fled away.

sanskrit: etasminnantare vīraḥ pulomā nāma vīryavān| daityendrastena saṃgṛhya śacīputro'pavāhitaḥ||
english: In the interim a heroic and powerful Daityachief, Pulomā, be name, taking ſacī's son disappeared.

sanskrit: saṃgṛhya taṃ tu dauhitraṃ praviṣṭaḥ sāgaraṃ tadā| āryakaḥ sa hi tasyāsītpulomā yena sā śacī||20
english: Taking his own grand-son he entered into the ocean, Puloma was his grand-father for by him Śaci was begotten.

sanskrit: jñātvā praṇāśaṃ tu tadā jayantasyātha devatāḥ| aprahṛṣṭāstataḥ sarvā vyathitāḥ saṃpradudruvuḥ||
english: Thinking that Jayanta was slain all the deities greatly sorry and distressed fled away on all sides.

sanskrit: rāvaṇistvatha saṃkruddho balaiḥ parivṛtaḥ svakaiḥ| abhyadhāvata devāṃstānmumoca ca mahāsvanam||
english: Thereupon Rāvana's son, enraged and encircled by his own powerful followers, pursued the celestials emitting loud cries.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā praṇāśaṃ putrasya daivateṣu ca vidvatan| mātaliṃ cāha deveśo rathaḥ samupanīyatām||
english: "Not beholding his son and observing the flight of the deities the king of the celestials said to Mātali, “Bring the car."""

sanskrit: sa tu divyā mahābhīmaḥ sajja eva mahārathaḥ| upasthito mātalinā bāhyamāno mahājavaḥ||
english: By Mātali was brought, the celestial, highly dreadful, huge and quick-coursing chariot, that was ready.

sanskrit: tato meghā rathe tasmiṃstaḍittvanto mahābalāḥ| agrato vāyucapalā neduḥ paramaniḥsvanāḥ||
english: (And he having) ascended the car, the huge clouds, with lightening, being driven by winds, began to emit forth loud mutterings before the chariot.

sanskrit: nānāvādyāni vādyanta gandharvāśca samāhitāḥ| nanṛtuścāpsaraḥsaṅghā niryāte tridaśeśvare||
english: The Gandharvas began to play on various instruments and the Apsarās began to dance.

sanskrit: rudrairvasubhirādityairaśvibhyāṃ samarudgaṇaiḥ| vṛto nānāpraharaṇairniryayau tridaśādhipaḥ||
english: Taking up various weapons, Indra, the king of divinities, set out for the field of action, in the company of Rudras, Vasus, Adityas, the two Asvins and Maruts.

sanskrit: nirgacchatastu śakrasya paruṣaḥ pavano vavau| bhāskaro niṣprabhaścaiva maholkāśca prapedire||
english: He, having set out for battle, the winds began to blow high, the sun was divested of its brilliance and the huge fire-brands began to send out flames.

sanskrit: etasminnantare śūro daśagrīvaḥ pratāpavān| āruroha rathaṃ divyaṃ nirmitaṃ viśvakarmaṇā|29|| pannagaiḥ sumahākāyairveṣṭitaṃ lomaharṣaṇaiḥ| yeṣāṃ niḥśvāsavātena pradīptamiva saṃyuge||
english: In the interval the heroic and the highly powerful Daśagrīva ascended the celestial car, constructed by the Architect of the deities, encircled by the huge-bodied serpents capable of making down erect and by whose breath the battle-field was ablaze.

sanskrit: daityainiśācaraiścaiva sa rathaḥ parivāritaḥ| samarābhimukho divyo mahendraṃ so'bhyavartata||
english: Surrounded by demons and night-rangers and with the celestial car he encountered Mahendra in the battle-field.

sanskrit: putraṃ taṃ vārayitvā tu svayameva vyavasthitaḥ| so'pi yuddhādviniṣkramya rāvaṇiḥ samupāviśat||
english: Having desisted his son he himself stood there. And having coming out from the field of action Ravana's son too stood silent.

sanskrit: tato yuddhaṃ pravṛttaṃ tu surāṇāṃ rākṣasaiḥ saha| śastrāṇi varṣatāṃ teṣāṃ meghanāmiva saṃyuge||
english: Thereupon there arose an encounter between the Räkşasas and the deities and there began a downpour of weapons in the conflict like clouds.

sanskrit: kumbhakarṇastu duṣṭātmā nānāpraharaṇodyataḥ| nājñāyata tadā rājanyuddhaṃ kenābhyapadyata||
english: The vicious-souled Kumbhakarņa armed with various weapons came you, but he did not know,* O king, with whom the conflict was going on. *For he was asleep till then so he was not acquainted with the particulars war-fare. He used to sleep for six months at a time.

sanskrit: dantaiḥ pādairbhujairhastaiḥ śaktitomaramudgaraiḥ| yena tenaiva saṃkruddhastāḍayāmāsa devatāḥ||
english: And by him enraged, the celestials were assailed with his teeth, feet, arms, hands, Saktis, Tomaras and clubs or any weapon whatsoever.

sanskrit: sa tu rudairmahāghoraiḥ saṃgamyātha niśācaraḥ| prayuddhastaiśca saṃgrāme kṣataḥ śastrairnirantaram||
english: Thereupon the night-ranger engaged with the highly powerful Rudra and was wounded, in the conflict, with incessant strokes of weapons.

sanskrit: tatastadrākṣasaṃ sainyaṃ prayuddhaṃ samarudgaṇaiḥ| raṇe vidrāvitaṃ sarvaṃ nānāpraharaṇaistadā||
english: Thereupon the Rākşasas army began to fight with Maruts and they were overwhelmed in the encounter with the stroke of various weapons.

sanskrit: kecidvinihatāḥ kṛttāśceṣṭanti sma mahītale| vāhaneṣvavasaktāśca sthitā evapāre raṇe|| rathānāgānkharāṣṭrānpannagāṃsturagāṃstathā| śiśumārānvarāhāṃśca piśācavadanānapi|| tānsamāliṅgaya bāhubhyāṃ viṣṭabdhāḥ kecidutthitāḥ| devaistu śastrasaṃbhinnā manire ca niśācarāḥ|| citrakarma ivābhāti sarveṣāṃ raṇasaṃplavaḥ| nihatānāṃ prasuptānāṃ rākṣasānāṃ mahībale||
english: Some fell down on earth of their carriers in the battle. And they all stood there in a halfsensible mood, some holding the car, some elephants, some asses, some boars, some Piśācamouthed animals and some embracing the Pannagas. And other night-rangers, having their bodies sundered by the deities gave up their being. The Rakşasas being slain and lying down on earth the action appeared wondrous like a painting.

sanskrit: śoṇitodakaniṣpandā kākagṛdhrasamākulā| pravṛttā saṃyugamukhe śastragrāhavatī nadī||
english: There issued out in the battle-field a river from weapons, having blood for its silent waters and infested with crows and vultures.

sanskrit: etasminnantare kruddho daśagrīvaḥ pratāpavān| nirīkṣya tu balaṃ sarvaṃ daivatairvinipātitam|| sa taṃ prativigāhyāśu pravṛddhaṃ sainyasāgaram| tridaśānsamare nighnaśakramevābhyavartata||
english: Having beheld his own army slain by the deities the highly powerful Daśänana, enraged beholding the army slain by gods, entered the ocean of celestial army and slaying the deities in the conflict confronted Sakra.

sanskrit: tataḥ śakro mahaccāpaṃ visphārya sumahāsvanam| yasya visphāranirghoṣaiḥ stananti sma diśo daśa||45
english: Thereupon Śakra took up his huge bow by the twang where-of the ten quarters were filled.

sanskrit: tadvikṛṣya mahaccāpamindro rāvaṇamūrdhani| pātayāmāsa sa śarānpāvakādityavarcasaḥ||
english: Having unstrung his huge bow Indra struck Răvaņa, on his head, with arrows resembling the flame of fire and the rays of the sun.

sanskrit: tathaiva ca mahābāhurdaśagrīvo niśācaraḥ| śakraṃ kārmukavibhraṣṭaiḥ śaravarṣairavākirat||
english: And the Rākşasa-chief Daśānana, having long arms, also assailed Indra with hundreds of shafts discharged off his bow.

sanskrit: prayudhyatoratha tayorbāṇavaṣaiḥ samantataḥ| nājñāyata tadā kiṃcitsarvaṃ hi tamasā vṛtam||
english: They having been thus engaged with each other with the downpour of dreadful shafts, all the quarters were filled with darkness and in consequence thereof nothing was visible.

sanskrit: atadarha mahārājaṃ śayānamatathocitam| yayātimiva puṇyānte devalokāt paricyutam|| anartharūpāsiddhārthā hyabhītā bhayadarśinī| punarākārayāmāsa tameva varamaṅganā||
english: Then as the mighty king was lying down in this unbeseeming and improper guise, like Yayāti dropped from the celestial, that lady, personating the ruin of the race, not fearing public odium, who had discerned danger from Rāma to Bharata, not having attained her wish, again addressed the monarch, concerning the boon he had promised to her.

sanskrit: tvaṃ katthase mahārāja satyavādī dṛḍhavrataḥ| mama cedaṃ varaṃ kasmād vidhārayitumicchasi||
english: You describe yourself, O mighty monarch, as speaking the truth and firm in vow. Why then do you hesitate to confer this boon on me?

sanskrit: evamuktastu kaikeyyā rājā daśarathastadā| pratyuvāca tataḥ kruddho muhūrtaṃ vihvalaniva||
english: Thus addressed by Kaikeyi king Dasaratha, remaining stupefied for a while thus answered her in wrath.

sanskrit: mṛte mayi gate rāme vanaṃ manujapuṅgave| hantānārye mamāmitre sakāmā sukhinī bhava||
english: O ignoble one! O enemy of mine! On my being dead and that chief of men, Rāma, repairing to the woods, do you, yours wish attained, become happy.

sanskrit: svarge'pi khalu rāmasya kuśalaṃ daivatairaham| pratyādeśādabhihitaṃ dhārayiṣye kathaṃ bata||
english: When in heaven, questioning me as to Rāma's welfare, the celestials, learning of his banishment to the woods, will tax me on this score, how shall I also bear that reproach of theirs?

sanskrit: kaikeyyāḥ priyakāmena rāmaḥ pravrājito vanam| yadi satyaṃ bravīmyetat tadasatyaṃ bhaviṣyati||
english: If I shall truthfully say I have sent Rāma to the woods for compassing Kaikeyi's pleasure, that will count for a falsehood.

sanskrit: aputreṇa mayā putraḥ śrameṇa mahatā mahān| rāmo labdho mahātejāḥ sa kathaṃ tyajyate mayā||
english: Sonless first, I have obtained the exceedingly energetic and mighty Rāma by great pain, how can I then renounce him?

sanskrit: śūraśca kṛtavidyaśca jitakrodhaḥ kṣamāparaḥ| kathaṃ kamalapatrākṣo mayā rāmo vivāsyate||||
english: How shall I banish Rāma having eyes resembling lotus' petals, who is heroic, and accomplished and of subdued anger, and forgiving.

sanskrit: kathamindīvaraśyāmaṃ dīrghabāhuṃ mahābalam| abhirāmamahaṃ rāmaṃ sthāpayiṣyāmi daṇḍakān||
english: How shall I dismiss to Dandaka the charming Rāma of dark blue hue like that of a blue lotus, possessed of mighty arms, and having great strength?

sanskrit: sukhānāmucitasyaiva duḥkhairanucitasya ca| duḥkhaṃ nāmānupaśyeyaṃ kathaṃ rāmasya dhīmataḥ||
english: How shall I behold the intelligent Rāma in evil plight, who has never known suffering, and has always enjoyed felicity?

sanskrit: yadi duḥkhamakṛtvā tu mama saṃkramaṇaṃ bhavet| aduḥkhārhasya rāmasya tataḥ sukhamavāpnuyām||
english: If without inflicting injury upon Rāma, I meet with death, I shall then attain happiness.

sanskrit: nṛśaṃse pāpasaṃkalpe rāmaṃ satyaparākramam| kiṃ vipriyeṇa kaikeyi priyaṃ yojayase mama||
english: O cruel Kaikeyi, O you of evil purpose, why do you do this wrong to my beloved Rāma having truth for prowess? If I banish Rāma, an unparalleled obloquy will surely darken (my fair fame).

sanskrit: akīrtiratulā loke dhruvaṃ paribhaviṣyati| tathā vilapatastasya paribhramitacetasaḥ|| astamabhyāgamat sūryo rajanī cābhyavartata|
english: As king Dasaratha was bewailing thus with a heart wrought up with grief, the sun set and night came on.

sanskrit: sā triyāmā tadārtasya candramaṇḍalamaṇḍitā|| rājño vilapamānasya na vyabhāpata śarvarī|
english: But although crested with the lunar disc, the night failed to bring comfort to the king, distressed, and indulging in grief.

sanskrit: sadaivoṣṇaṃ viniḥśvasya vṛddho daśaratho nṛpaḥ|| vilalāpāvid duḥkhaṃ gaganāsaktalocanaḥ|
english: Then the old king Dasaratha, with his eyes fixed at the sky, sighing hot, lamented in this strain.

sanskrit: tato rājā na prabhātaṃ tvayecchāmi niśe nakṣatrabhūṣite|| kriyatāṃ me dayā bhadre mayāyaṃ racito'ñjaliḥ|
english: O night studded with stars, I beseech you, let not the morning appear. Do you, O gentle one, do me this kindness. I do thus clasp my hands (by way of supplication.)

sanskrit: athavā gamyatāṃ śīghraṃ nāhamicchāmi nighṛṇām|| nṛśaṃsāṃ kekayoṃ draṣṭuṃ yatkṛte vyasanaṃ mama |
english: Or do you speedily repair for I do not wish to see the hated and relentless Kaikeyi, who has brought this calamity upon me.

sanskrit: evamuktvā kaikeyīṃ saṃyatāñjaliḥ|| prasādayāmāsa punaḥ kaikeyī rājadharmavit|
english: Having spoken thus, the kind conversant with the duties of Sovereigns again endeavoured to propitiate Kaikeyī, saying.

sanskrit: sādhuvṛttasya dīnasya tvadgatasya gatāyuṣaḥ|| prasādaḥ kriyatāṃ bhadre devi rājño viśeṣataḥ|
english: O noble dame, do you show favour to me, who am of honest ways, who am distressed, who have made myself yours, who have finished his life, and who, in especial, am your king.

sanskrit: śūnye na khalu suśroṇi mayedaṃ samudāhṛtam|| kuru sādhuprasādaṃ me bāle sahṛdayā hyasi|
english: That I have spoken you thus was because, O you of shapely hips, I had been deprived of my senses (through grief). O girl, do you show your favour to me, be generous, be propitious.

sanskrit: prasīda devī rāmo me tvaddattaṃ rājyamavyayam|| labhatāmasitāpāne yaśaḥ paramavāpsyasi|
english: Let my Rāma obtain the kingdom in fact conferred by you. Thereupon, O you having the outer corner of your eyes of dark blue hue, you will attain high fame (among men.)

sanskrit: mama rāmasya lokasya guruṇāṃ bharatasya ca| priyametad guruśroṇi kuru cārumukhekṣaṇe||
english: O you of well-developed hips, do you do this act of benefit to me and Ráma and the people and the superiors, and Bharata.

sanskrit: viśuddhabhāvasya hi duṣṭabhāvā dīnasya tāmrāśrukalasya rājñaḥ| śrutvā vicitraṃ karuṇaṃ vilāpaṃ bharturnuśaṃsā na cakāra vākyam||
english: Having heard the exceedingly piteous words of her husband, the king of pure sentiment, who was distressed, with his eye rendered coppery and flowing with tears, that wicked minded and merciless woman spoke not.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā punareva mūrcchitaḥ priyāmatuṣṭāṃ pratikūlabhāṣiṇīm| samīkṣya putrasya vivāsanaṃ prati kṣitau visaṃjño nipapāta duḥkhitaḥ||
english: Thereat seeing that his favourite dissatisfied wife persisted in urging the banishment of his son, the king struck with grief, again fell down to the earth, senseless.

sanskrit: itīva rājño vyathitasya sā niśā jagāma ghoraṃ śvasato manasvinaḥ| vibodhyamānaḥ pratibodhanaṃ tadā nivārayāmāsa sa rājasattamaḥ||
english: As the wise king afflicted with sorrow was sighing hot and hard, the night passed away Then as the eulogists attempted to sung his praises for awakening him, he prohibited them to do so.

sanskrit: tathā tu karuṇaṃ tasya dvijasya paridevanam| śuśrāva rāghavaḥ sarvaṃ duḥkhaśokasamanvitam|| sa duḥkhena ca saṃtapto mantriṇastānupāhvayat| vasiṣṭhaṃ vāmadevaṃ ca bhrātṛ̭śca saha naigamān||
english: Hearing those sorrowful words of the Brāhmaṇa, Rāma was greatly sorry and sent for Vasistha, Vamadeva, his brothers, citizens and councillors.

sanskrit: tato dvijā vasiṣṭhena sārdhamaṣṭau praveśitāḥ| rājānaṃ devasaṃkāśaṃ vardhasveti tato'bruvan||
english: There upon having entered the apartment in the company of Vasiştha, eight Brāhmaṇas blessed the king Rāma, resembling a celestial, saying 'may victory crown you.'

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeyo'tha maudgalyo vāmadevaśca kāśyapaḥ| kātyāyano'tha jābāligautamo nāradastathā|| ete dvijarṣabhāḥ sarve āsaneṣūpaveśitāḥ| maharṣīnsamanuprāptānabhivādya kṛtāñjaliḥ|| mantriṇo naigamāścaiva yathārhamanukūlitāḥ| teṣāṃ samupaviṣṭānāṃ sarveṣāṃ dīptatejasām|| rāghavaḥ sarvamācaṣṭe dvijo'yamuparodhati|
english: Markandeya, Maudgalya, Vamadeva, Kashyapa, Katyayana, Javali, Gautama, and Nārada, these eight leading Brāhmaṇas having takes their seats, Rāma with folded hands, saluted them. And he showed due civilities towards his minister, citizens, Rșis and all others. There upon all the highly effulgent Rșis being accommodated with seats Råma narrated duly before them the account of the Brāhmaṇa and said. This Brāhmaṇa is waiting at the Palace-gate.

sanskrit: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā rājño dīnasya nāradaḥ|| pratyuvāca śubhaṃ vākyamṛṣīṇāṃ saṃnidhau svayam|
english: Hearing those words of the poorly king, Narada, in the presence of all other Rsis, replied.

sanskrit: śṛṇu rājanyathākāle prāpto bālasya saṃkṣayaḥ|| śrutvā kartavyatāṃ rājankuruṣvaraghunandana|
english: Hear, o king, why this boy has met with untimely death. And hearing this, O descendant or Raghu, do you settle what you think proper.

sanskrit: purā kṛtayuge rājanbrāhmaṇā vai tapasvinaḥ|||| abrāhmaṇastadā rājanna tapasvī kathaṃcana|
english: O king, in the golden age, only the Brahmanas used to engage in asceticism. At that age save the Brāhmaṇas no other caste used to lead the life of an anchoret.

sanskrit: tasminyuge prajvalite brahmabhūte tvanāvṛte|| amṛtyavastadā sarve jajñire dīrghadarśinaḥ|
english: And for this, the Brāhmaṇas were the highest caste, effulgent in asceticism, asceticism, shorn shorn of ignorance, above death and conversant with three ages.

sanskrit: tatastretāyugaṃ nāma mānavānāṃ vapuṣmatām|| kṣatriyā yatra jāyante pūrveṇa tapasānvitāḥ| vīryeṇa tapasā caiva te'dhikāḥ pūrvajanmani|| mānavā ye mahātmānastatra tretāyuge yuge|
english: There upon at the end of the golden age, Brāhmaṇa's understanding became loose and the Tretā Yuga set in. At this age Kşatriyas, gifted with the power acquired by pristine asceticism, were born. And those men, intent upon austere penances, that were born in the Tretā age, were more powerful and greater devotees than those in the former age.

sanskrit: brahma kṣatraṃ ca tatsarvaṃ yatpūrvamavaraṃ ca yat|| yugayorubhayorāsītsamavīryasamanvitam|
english: In the golden age the Brāhmaṇas were more powerful than the Kșatriyas. But in the Tretā age the Brāhmaṇas and the Ksatriyas were equally powerful.

sanskrit: apaśyantastu te sarve viśeṣamadhikaṃ tataḥ|| sthāpanaṃ cakrire tatra cāturvarṇyasya saṃmatam|
english: Thus in the Tretā age, not beholding prominence of the Brāhmaṇas greater than that of the Kşatriyas, Manu and other religious leaders of the time composed the Sastra describing and setting in the four divisions of castes.

sanskrit: tasminyuge prajvalite dharmabhūte hyanāvṛte|| adharmaḥ pādamekaṃ tu pātayatpṛthivītale| adharmeṇa hi saṃyuktastejo mandaṃ bhaviṣyati||16
english: In this wise the Tretā age was prolific with virtues of the four Varņas, and many pious sacrifices and was shorn of iniquities. But being attacked a little with iniquity, one portion of sin appeared on earth. And growing impious people of sin appeared on earth. And growing impious people lost their strength.

sanskrit: āmiṣaṃ yacca pūrveṣāṃ rājasaṃ ca malaṃ bhṛśam| anṛtaṃ nāma tadbhūtaṃ kṣiptena pṛthivītale|| anṛtaṃ pātayitvā tu pādamekamadharmataḥ| tataḥ prāduṣkṛtaṃ pūrvamāyuṣaḥ pariniṣṭhitam||
english: And for houses and farms that were the property of the former age, people of the Tretā Yuga were possessed by envy, the outcome of the quality of darkness. And with the treading of impiety on earth during Tretā, the soiled sin of untruth appeared. And this iniquity stretching one footstep, the lease of people's lives, for sins, became limited.

sanskrit: pātite tvanṛte tasminadharmeṇa mahītale| śubhānyevācaraillokaḥ satyadharmaparāyaṇaḥ||
english: And the sin of untruth descending on earth, people, to a void the extinction of life in consequence thereof, became truthful and engaged in many pious observances.

sanskrit: tretāyuge ca vartante brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyāśca ye| tapo'tapyanta te sarve śuśrūṣāmapare janāḥ||
english: During the Tretă age the Brāhmaṇas and Kș atriyas engaged in austere penances and the Vaiśyas and Sūdras engaged in serving them.

sanskrit: svadharmaḥ paramasteṣāṃ vaiśyaśūdraṃ tadāgamat| pūjāṃ ca sarvavarṇānāṃ śūdrāścanurviśeṣataḥ||
english: And the greatest piety of the Vaiśyas and Śūdras at that time consisted of serving the Brāhmaṇas and Ksatriyas and specially for the Śūdras the highest religion was to serve people of all Varnas.

sanskrit: etasminnantare teṣāmadharme cānṛte ca ha| tataḥ pūrve punarvāsamagamannṛpasattama||
english: O foremost of kings, at the end of the Tretă age, Vaiśyas and Śūdras being fully overpowered by the sin of untruth, the Brāhmaṇas and the Kșatriyas also grew feeble.

sanskrit: tataḥ pādamadharmasya dvitīyamavatārayat| tato dvāparasaṃkhyā sā yugasya samajāyata||
english: And the second foot of impiety being ushered into the world the Dvāpara age set in.

sanskrit: tasmindvāparasaṃkhye tu vartamāne yugakṣaye| adharmaścānṛtaṃ caiva vavṛdhe puruṣarṣabha||
english: O foremost of men, during this age two legs of piety being cut off, impiety and untruth multiplies.

sanskrit: asmindvāparasaṃkhyāne tapo vaiśyānsamāviśat| tribhyo yugebhyastrīnvarṇānkramādvai tapa āviśat||
english: And in Yuga named Dvāpara the Vaisyas engaged in devout penances. In this wise in three ages the three Varnas gradually engaged in ascetic performances.

sanskrit: tribhyo yugebhyastrīnvarṇāndharmaśca pariniṣṭhitaḥ| na śūdro labhate dharma yugatastu nararṣabha||
english: The piety of asceticism by Yugas gradually became established in three Varmas, But, O foremost of men, in these three Yugas the Sūdras were not entitled to the virtues of devout penances.

sanskrit: hīnavarṇo nṛpaśreṣṭha tapyate sumahattapaḥ| bhaviṣyacchūdrayonyāṃ hi tapaścaryā kalau yuge||
english: O foremost of men, the degraded caste, the Śūdras, during your rege me, have engaged in austere penances. And in the Kali Yuga asceticism shall be established in the Sūdras.

sanskrit: adharmaḥ paramo rājandvāpare śūdrajanmanaḥ| sa vai viṣayaparyante tava rājanmahātapāḥ|| adya tapyati durbuddhistena bālavadho hyayam| yo hyadharmamakārya vā viṣaye pārthivasya tu||
english: O king, even in Davāpara, devout penances for Śūdras were considered as impiety, what to speak of the Tretāage. O king, one Śūdras, under the influence of vicious understanding, has begun devout penances within your kingdom. And for that reason this boy has met with death.

sanskrit: karoti cāśrīmūlaṃ tatpure vā durmatirnaraḥ| kṣipraṃ ca narakaṃ yāti sa ca rājā na saṃśayaḥ||
english: Calamity sets in that kingdom where a vicious-minded person commits an iniquity and that vicious wight and the king forsooth speedily repair to hell.

sanskrit: adhītasya ca taptasya karmaṇaḥ sukṛtasya ca| ṣaṣṭhaṃ bhajati bhāgaṃ tu prajā dharmeṇa pālayan||
english: The king, who piously govern his subjects, receive the sixth portion of there study asceticism and good actions.

sanskrit: ṣaḍbhāgasya ca bhoktāsau rakṣate na prajāḥ katham| sa tvaṃ puruṣaśārdūla mārgasva viṣayaṃ svakam|| duṣkṛtaṃ yatra paśyethāstatra yatnaṃ samācara|
english: While the king is entitled to the sixth portion of everything why should he not fully protect his subjects? Therefore, O chief of men, do you bring all informations of your kingdom. And be then studious to repress vices wherever you shall find them.

sanskrit: evaṃ ceddharmavṛddhiśca nṛṇāṃ cāyurvivardhanam| bhaviṣyati naraśreṣṭha bālasyāsya ca jīvitam||
english: And by that, O foremost of men, the piety of the subjects shall be increased, the lease of their life shall be prolonged and this boy shall regain his life.

sanskrit: tatastamakṣobhyabalaṃ laṅkādhipataye carāḥ| suvele rāghavaṃ śaile niviṣṭaṃ pratyavedayan||
english: Then the spies communicated to Lankā's lord news concerning Rāghava and his host stationed at the mount Suvela.

sanskrit: cārāṇāṃ rāvaṇaḥ śrutvā prāptaṃ rāmaṃ mahābalam| jātodvego'bhavatkicicchārdūlaṃ vākyamabravīt||
english: Hearing the words of the spies, that Rama, accompanied by a mighty army, had arrived (there), Rāvana was a little agitated and spoke to Sardula.

sanskrit: ayathāvacca te varṇo dīnaścāsi niśācara| nāsi kaccidamitrāṇāṃ kruddhānāṃ vaśamāgataḥ||
english: Your colour has changed its natural aspect, and O ranger of the night, you look poorly. Did not come under the control of the wrathful foes?

sanskrit: iti te nānuśiṣṭastu vācaṃ mandamudīrayan| tadā rākṣasaśārdūlaṃ śārdūlo bhayaviklavaḥ||
english: Thus ordered by him, then (Sārdula), bewildered by fear, addressed that tiger of a Raksasa, saying.

sanskrit: na te cārayituṃ śakyā rājanvānarapuṃgavāḥ| vikrāntā balavantaśca rāghaveṇa ca rakṣitāḥ||
english: Those powerful monkeys, o king, puissant, strong, and protected by Rāghava, are incapable of being ranged (by us). or

sanskrit: nāpi saṃbhāṣituṃ śakyāḥ saṃpraśno'tra na labhyate| sarvato rakṣyate panthā vānaraiḥ parvatopamaiḥ||
english: They cannot be conversed with interrogated. All around, the courses are kept by monkeys resembling hills.

sanskrit: praviṣṭamātre jñāto'haṃ bale tasminvicārite| balādṛhīto rakṣobhirbahudhāsmi vicāritaḥ||
english: As soon as I entered, and was scanning that host, I was discovered. And forcibly taken by the Rākşasa, I was pulled by them hither and thither.

sanskrit: jānubhirmuṣṭibhirdantaistalaiścābhihato bhṛśam| pariṇīto'smi haribhirbalamadhye amarṣaṇaiḥ||
english: And furiously assailed by the monkeys with thighs, clenched fists, teeth, and palms, I was dragged in the midst of the army by the enraged monkeys.

sanskrit: pariṇīya ca sarvatra nīto'haṃ rāmasaṃsadi| rudhirasrāvidīnāṅgo vihvalaścalitendriyaḥ||
english: And, after having been taken all about, I was (at length) taken before Rāma, bleeding, with my limbs showing sorry work, and my senses swimming and paralysed.

sanskrit: haribhirvadhyamānaśca yācamānaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ| rāghaveṇa paritrāto māmeti ca yadṛcchayā||
english: And, having been belaboured by the monkeys, I, on craving his kindness with joined hands, was, at his pleasure, rescued by Rāghava, with, Don't, don't!

sanskrit: eṣa śailaśilābhistu pūrayitvā mahārṇavam| dvāramāśritya laṅkāyā rāmastiṣṭhati sāyudhaḥ||11
english: Having filled up the deep with rocks and crags, Rāma equipped with weapons, stay, occupying the gate of Lanka.

sanskrit: garuḍavyūhamāsthāya sarvato haribhirvṛtaḥ| māṃ visṛjya mahātejā laṅkāmevātivartate||
english: And, letting me off, that one of suspassing vigour, surrounded by monkeys, and, arranging his forces in the Garuda fashion, advance upon Lanka.

sanskrit: purā prākāramāyāti kṣipramekataraṃ kuru| sītāṃ vāpi prayacchāśu yuddhaṃ vāpi pradīyatām||
english: He draw nigh to the wall. Therefore, do one of these things in preference to the other, either render back Sītā, or give him battle.

sanskrit: manasā tattadā prekṣya tacchutvā rākṣasādhipaḥ| śārdūlaṃ sumahadvākyamathovāca sa rāvaṇaḥ||
english: Hearing this, Ravana, lord of Raksasas, then reflecting in his mind, spoke to Sārdula these pregnant words.

sanskrit: yadi māṃ pratiyuddhyante devagandharvadānavāḥ| naiva sītā pradāsyāmi sarvalokabhayādapi||
english: Even if the gods, Gandharvas, and Dānavas should array themselves against me, Sītā I shall not give, from fear of all creatures.

sanskrit: evamuktvā mahātejā rāvaṇaḥ punarabravīt| caritā bhavatā senā ke'tra śūrāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ||
english: Having said this, that exceedingly energetic one again said,You have ranged this army. Who here among the monkeys are heroic?

sanskrit: kiṃprabhāḥ kīdṛśāḥ saumya vānarā ye durāsadāḥ| kasya putrāśca pautrāśca tattvamākhyāhi suvrata||
english: O amiable one, what is their potency? And what are those monkeys that are hard to approach, like? And, O you of fair vows, whose sons and grandsons are they? Truly relate all this (to me).

sanskrit: tathātra pratipatsyāpi jñātvā teṣāṃ balābalam| avaśyaṃ khalu saṃkhyānaṃ kartavyaṃ yuddhamicchatā||18
english: Having ascertained their strength and weakness, I shall in this matter adopt my course. Those who wish for fight, certainly take account of all this.

sanskrit: athaivamuktaḥ śārdūlo rāvaṇenottamaścaraḥ| idaṃ vacanamārebhe vaktuṃ rāvaṇasaṃnidhau||
english: Thus addressed by Rāvana, Sārdula—best of spies-thus began to speak in the presence of Ravana.

sanskrit: atharbharajasaḥ putro yudhi rājansudurjayaḥ| gadgadasyātha putro'tra jāmbavāniti viśrutaḥ||
english: O king, that unconquerable one in fight, Jāmbavān, is well known as the son Gadgada, king of bears.

sanskrit: gadgadasyātha putro'nyo guruputraḥ śatakratoḥ| kadanaṃ yasya putreṇa kṛtamekena rakṣasām||
english: The other son of Gadgada is the son of Śakra's preceptor. By which son, single-handed, was done immense oppression to the Rākṣasa.

sanskrit: suṣeṇaścātra dharmātmā putro dharmasya vīryavān| saumyaḥ somātmajaścātra rājandadhimukhaḥ kapiḥ||
english: The righteous and puissant Sușeņa is the son of Dharma. And the mild monkey, Dadhimukha, O king, is the son of Soma. 1. Righteousness. 2. Moon.

sanskrit: sumukho durmukhaścātra vegadarśī ca vānaraḥ| mṛtyurvānararūpeṇa nūnaṃ sṛṣṭaḥ svayaṃbhuvā||
english: "And Sumukha, Durmukha and the monkey, vegadarcin (resembling) Death himself, were for certain begot by the Self-create in the shape of a monkey.* *Another meaning is, “The monkey, Vegadarsi who is death himself in the shape of a monkey."" But I give the acceptable sense."

sanskrit: putro hutavahasyātra nīlaḥ senāpatiḥ svayam| anilasya tu putro'tra hanūmāniti viśrutaḥ||
english: Nīla himself is the son of the bearer of sacrificial oblations;* and Hanumán is famed as the son of the Wind-god. * Fire.

sanskrit: naptā śakrasya durdharṣo balavānaṅgado yuvā| maindaśca dvividaścobhau balināvaśvisaṃbhavau||
english: The irrepressible and youthful Angada is the grandson of Śakra. And the lusty Mainda and Dvivida are sprung from Aśvi.

sanskrit: putrā vaivasvatasyātha pañca kālāntakopamāḥ| gajo gavākṣo gavayaḥ śarabho gandhamādanaḥ||
english: And five are the sons of Vaivasvata, resembling the Reaper himself, Gaya, Gavāks a, gavaya, Sarabha and Gandhamādana.

sanskrit: daśa vānarakoṭyaśca śūrāṇāṃ yuddhakākṣiṇām| śrīmatāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ śeṣa nākhyātumutsahe||
english: But I can not enumerate the rest, ten koțis of heroic monkeys-all sons of deities—burning for battle.

sanskrit: putro daśarathasyaiṣa siṃhasaṃhanano yuvā| dūṣaṇo nihato yena svaraśca triśirāstathā||
english: And this is Dasaratha's son—this you resembling a lion, who slew Düşana and Khara and Triſiras.

sanskrit: nāsti rāmasya sadṛśo vikrame bhuvi kaścana| virādho nihato yena kabandhaścāntakopamaḥ||
english: There breathes none on Earth that is like to Rāma in prowess, by whom was slain Virādha and Kabandha, resembling the Destroyer.

sanskrit: vaktuṃ na śakto rāmasya guṇānkaścinnaraḥ kṣitau| janasthānagatā yena tāvanto rākṣasā hatāḥ||
english: No person can on earth describe the virtues of Rāma; by whom have been slain all those Rākşasas that had gone to Janasthāna.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇaścātra dharmātmā mātaṅgānāmivarṣabhaḥ| yasya bāṇapathaṃ prāpya na jīvedapi vāsavaḥ||
english: Here also is the virtuous Lakşmaņa, like to the foremost of elephants, coming in the way of whose shafts, even Vasava does not live.

sanskrit: śveto jyotirmukhaścātra bhāskarasyātmasaṃbhavau| varuṇasyātha putro'tha hemakūṭaḥ plavaṃgamaḥ||
english: And here are ſveta and Jyotirmukha, sprung from Vāskara's self; and the monkey Hemakūta is the son of Varuna.

sanskrit: viśvakarmasuto vīro nalaḥ plavagasattamaḥ| vikrānto vegavānatra vasuputraḥ sa durdharaḥ||
english: The heroic Nalabest of monkeys, is the son of Viśvakarmă. And powerful and impetuous, Durdhara is the son of Vasu.

sanskrit: rākṣasānāṃ variṣṭhaśca tava bhrātā vibhīṣaṇaḥ| pratigṛhya purīṃ laṅkāṃ rāghavasya hite rataḥ||
english: That foremost of Rāksasas, Vibhisana, your brother, engaged in the welfare of Raghava, has laid seige to Lankā.

sanskrit: iti sarvaṃ samākhyātaṃ tathā vai vānaraṃ balam| suvele'dhiṣṭhitaṃ śaile śeṣakārye bhavāngatiḥ||
english: Thus have I described to you the entire monkey host stationed in mount Suvela. As for what remain to be done, you are the master.

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā kuśanābhasya dhīmataḥ| śirobhiścaraṇo spṛṣṭvā kanyāśatamabhāṣata||
english: Hearing those words of the intelligent Kusanābha, his hundred daughters touching his feet with their heads, said,

sanskrit: vāyuḥ sarvātmako rājan pradharṣayitumicchati| aśubhaṃ mārgamāsthāya na dharmaṃ pratyavekṣate||
english: O king, that life of all, the Air, was desirous of overcoming us, having recourse to an improper way; nor did he regard morality.

sanskrit: pitṛmatyaḥ sma bhadraṃ te svacchande na vayaṃ sthitāḥ| pitaraṃ no vṛṇīṣva tvaṃ yadi no dāsyate tava||
english: We have a father, good betide you; and we live at ease. Do you ask our father about it, if he consent conferring us on you.

sanskrit: tena pāpānubandhena vacanaṃ na pratīcchatā| evaṃ bruvantyaḥ sarvāḥ sma vāyunābhihatā bhṛśam||
english: But that wicked wight did not listen to our words; and as we were saying this, were we roughly handled by him.'

sanskrit: tāsāṃ tu vacanaṃ śrutvā rājā paramadhārmikaḥ| pratyuvāca mahātejāḥ kanyāśatamanuttamam||
english: Hearing those words of theirs, the highly pious and puissant king addressed his hundred beautiful daughters, saying

sanskrit: kṣāntaṃ kṣamāvatāṃ putryaḥ kartavyaṃ sumahat kṛtam| aikamatyamupāgamya kulaṃ cāvekṣitaṃ mama||
english: You have displayed a signal example of that forgiveness which is fit to be followed by the forbearing; and that you have unanimously regarded the honour of my house, also conduces to your praise.

sanskrit: alaṃkāro hi nārīṇāṃ kṣamā tu puruṣasya vā| duṣkaraṃ tacca vai kṣāntaṃ tridaśeṣu viśeṣataḥ|| yādṛśī vaḥ kṣamā putryaḥ sarvāsāmaviśeṣataḥ|
english: Alike to men and women, forbearance is an ornament. And difficult it is for one to exercise that forbearance, specially in respect of the celestials. And may every descendant of mine possess forbearance like to yours!

sanskrit: kṣamā dānaṃ kṣamā satyaṃ kṣamā yajñāśca putrikāḥ| kṣamā yaśaḥ kṣamā dharmaḥ kṣamāyāṃ viṣṭhitaṃ jagat|
english: Forbearance is charity; forbearance is truth; forbearance, O daughters, is sacrifice; forbearance is fame; forbearance is virtue, you, the universe is established in forbearance;

sanskrit: visṛjya kanyāḥ kākutstha rājā tridaśavikramaḥ|| mantrajño mantrayāmāsa pradānaṃ saha mantribhiḥ| deśe kāle ca kartavyaṃ sadṛśe pratipādanam||
english: Then dismissing his daughters, the king endowed with the prowess of celestials, and versed in counsel, began to consult with his counsellors about the bestowal of his daughters, in respect of time and place and person and equability of lineage.

sanskrit: etasminneva kāle tu cūlī nāma mahādyutiḥ| ūrdhvaretāḥ śubhācāro brāhmaṃ tapa upāgamat||
english: It came to pass that at this time, an ascetic named Culi, highly effulgent, with his vital fluid under control, and of pure practices, was performing Brāhma austerities.

sanskrit: tapasyantamṛṣiṃ tatra gandharvī paryupāsate| somadā nāma bhadraṃ te ūrmilātanayā tadā ||
english: And as the saint was engaged in austerities, good betide you, Urmila's daughter named Somada-a Gandharvi-ministered to him.

sanskrit: sā ca taṃ praṇatā bhūtvā śuśrūṣaṇaparāyaṇā| uvāsa kāle dharmiṣṭhā tasyāstuṣṭo'bhavad guruḥ||
english: And in all humility that virtuous one for a definite period was engaged in ministering to him. And thereat, her spiritual guide was gratified with her.

sanskrit: sa ca tāṃ kālayogena provāca raghunandana| parituṣṭo'smi bhadraṃ te kiṃ kami tava priyam||
english: And, O descendant of Raghu, once he said to her, I am gratified, good betide you! What good shall I render you?

sanskrit: parituṣṭaṃ muniṃ jñātvā gandharvī madhurasvaram| uvāca paramaprītā vākyajñā vākyakovidam||
english: Thereupon, concluding that the ascetic was gratified, the Gandharvi, cognizant of words, exceedingly delighted, sweetly addressed that one versed in speech.

sanskrit: lakṣmyā samudito brāhmayā brahmabhūto mahātapāḥ| brāhmaṇa tapasā yuktaṃ putramicchāmi dhārmikam||
english: You are furnished with the Brāhma marks, art sprung from Brahmă, and art of mighty austerities. I desire of you a righteous son endowed with the Brāhma ascetic virtues.

sanskrit: apatiścāsmi bhadraṃ te bhāryā cāsmi na kasyacit| brāhmaṇopagatāyāśca dātumarhasi me sutam||
english: I am without a husband, good betide you, and I am no one's wife. Upon me who is your servant you should confer such a son by help of Brāhma means.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ prasanno brahmarṣirdadau brāhmamanuttamam| brahmadatta iti khyātaṃ mānasaṃ cūlinaḥ sutam||
english: Thereupon, well pleased with her, Cūlina conferred upon her an excellent Brāhma mindbegotten son, named Brahmadatta,

sanskrit: sa rājā brahmadattastu purīmadhyavasat tadā| kāmpilyāṃ parayā lakṣmyā devarājo yathā divam||
english: And that king, Brahmadatta, founded the flourishing city of Kampilya, even as the sovereign of the celestials founded the celestial regions.

sanskrit: sa buddhiṃ kṛtavān rājā kuśanābhaḥ sudhārmikaḥ| brahmadattāya kākutstha dātuṃ kanyāśataṃ tadā||
english: And, O Kākutstha, the righteous king Kusanābha finally decided on conferring his hundred daughters upon Brahmadatta.

sanskrit: tamāhūya mahātejā brahmadattaṃ mahīpatiḥ| dadau kanyāśataṃ rājā sugrīvenāntarātmanā ||
english: And inviting Brahmadatta, that highly energetic lord of earth, with a glad heart conferred his hundred daughters upon him.

sanskrit: yathākramaṃ tadā pāṇiṃ jagrāha raghunandana| brahmadatto mahīpālastāsāṃ devapatiryathā ||
english: And O descendant of Raghu, king Brahmadatta resembling the lord himself of the celestials, by turns received their hands in marriage.

sanskrit: spṛṣṭamātre tadā pāṇau vikubjā vigatajvarāḥ| yuktaṃ paramayā lakṣmyā babhau kanyāśataṃ tadā||
english: And as soon as he touched them, the hundred daughters were cured of their crookedness, and became free from anguish, and were endowed with pre-eminent beauty.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā vāyunā muktāḥ kuśanābho mahīpatiḥ| babhūva paramaprīto harṣaṃ lebhe punaḥ punaḥ||
english: And upon beholding them delivered from (the tyranny of) the Air, the monarch Kušanābha became exceedingly delighted, and rejoiced again and again.

sanskrit: kṛtodvāhaṃ tu rājānaṃ brahmadattaṃ mahīpatim| sadāraṃ preṣayāmāsa sopādhyāyagaṇaṃ tadā||
english: And he dismissed that lord of earth, king Brahmadatta, in company with his consorts and the priests.

sanskrit: somadāpi sutaṃ dṛṣṭvā putrasya sadṛśīṃ kriyām| yathānyāyaṃ ca gandhavīṃ snuṣāstāḥ pratyanandata| spṛṣṭvā ca tāḥ kanyāḥ kuśanābhaṃ praśasya ca||
english: And the Gandharvī Somadā rejoiced exceedingly at the completion of the nuptials of her son; and embracing her daughters-in-law again and again, and extolling her son, she expressed the fullness of her joy. And he dismissed that lord of earth, king Brahmadatta, in company with his consorts and the priests.

sanskrit: somadāpi sutaṃ dṛṣṭvā putrasya sadṛśīṃ kriyām| yathānyāyaṃ ca gandhavīṃ snuṣāstāḥ pratyanandata| spṛṣṭvā ca tāḥ kanyāḥ kuśanābhaṃ praśasya ca||
english: And the Gandharvī Somadā rejoiced exceedingly at the completion of the nuptials of her son; and embracing her daughters-in-law again and again, and extolling her son, she expressed the fullness of her joy.

sanskrit: atha tāṃ rajanīṃ tatra kṛtārthoṃ rāmalakṣmaṇau| uṣaturmuditau vīrau prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā||
english: Those heroes, Rāma and Laksmana, their interest secured, with glad hearts passed that night there.

sanskrit: prabhātāyāṃ tu śarvaryāṃ kṛtapaurvāhnikakriyau| viśvāmitramṛṣīṃścānyān sahitāvabhijagmatuḥ||
english: And when the night had passed away and the morning come, they together appeared before the saint, Visvāmitra, and the rest.

sanskrit: abhivādya muniśreṣṭhaṃ jvalantamiva pāvakam| ūcatuḥ paramodāraṃ vākyaṃ madhurabhāṣiṇau||
english: And having saluted that foremost of ascetics resembling flaming fire, your addressed him in gentle and honied accents.

sanskrit: imau sma muniśārdūla kiṃkarau samupāgatau| ājñāpaya muniśreṣṭha śāsanaṃ karavāva kim||
english: These servants of yours, O best of ascetics, have come before you. Do you command, O chief of anchorites, what command of your are we to execute

sanskrit: evamukte tayorvākye sarvaṃ eka maharṣayaḥ| viśvāmitraṃ puraskṛtya rāmaṃ vacanamabruvan|5||
english: Thus addressed by them the Maharșis with Viśvāmitra at their head spoke to Rāma, saying,

sanskrit: maithilasya naraśreṣṭha janakasya bhaviṣyati| yajñaḥ paramadharmiṣṭhastatra yāsyāmahe vayam||
english: A highly meritorious sacrifice, O foremost of men, is to be celebrated by Mithila's lord, Janaka. Thither shall we repair.

sanskrit: tvaṃ caiva naraśārdūla sahāsmābhirgamiṣyasi| adbhutaṃ ca dhanūratnaṃ tatra tvaṃ draṣṭumarhasi ||
english: And you, O tiger among men, men, must accompany us, and there behold a wonderful jewel of a bow.

sanskrit: taddhi pūrvaṃ naraśreṣṭha dattaṃ sadasi daivataiḥ| aprameyabalaṃ ghoraṃ makhe paramabhāsvaram||
english: And formerly this bow of immeasurable energy, and dreadful, and exceedingly effulgent at the sacrifice, had been conferred in court by the celestials (on king Devarata.)8

sanskrit: nāsya devā na gandharvā nāsurā na ca rākṣasāḥ| kartumāropaṇaṃ śaktā na kathaṃcana mānuṣāḥ||
english: And neither gods nor Gandharvas, neither Asuras nor Rākşasas nor men, can fix the string upon it.

sanskrit: dhanuṣastasya vīryaṃ hi jijñāsanto mahīkṣitaḥ| na śekurāropayituṃ rājaputrā mahābalāḥ||
english: And desirous of being acquainted with the prowess of this bow, many kings and princes came; but they in spite of their mighty strength, failed in stringing it.

sanskrit: taddhanurnaraśārdūla maithilasya mahātmanaḥ| tatra drakṣyasi kākutstha yajñaṃ ca paramādbhutam||
english: There, O Kākutstha, you will behold that bow belonging to the high-souled king of Mithila, as well as his exceedingly wonderful sacrifice..

sanskrit: taddhi yajñaphalaṃ tena maithilenottamaṃ dhanuḥ| yācitaṃ naraśārdūla sunābhaṃ sarvadaivataiḥ||
english: That rare bow, O foremost of men, furnished with an excellent device for griping it, had been solicited by Mithila's lord as the fruit of his sacrifice; and the celestials conferred it upon him.

sanskrit: āyāgabhūtaṃ nṛpatestasya veśmani rāghava| arcitaṃ vividhairgandhaidhūpaiścāgurugandhibhiḥ||
english: Now, O descendant of Raghu, in the residence of the king, the bow is worshipped like a deity with agaru dhüpa, and various other incenses.

sanskrit: evamuktvā munivaraḥ prasthānamakarot tadā| sarṣisaṅghaḥ sakākutstha āmantrya vanadevatāḥ||
english: This having been said, that foremost of ascetics, in company with Kākutstha and the saints, departed.

sanskrit: svasti vo'stu gamiṣyāmi siddhaḥ siddhāśramādaham| uttare jāhnavītīre himavantaṃ śiloccayam||
english: And on the eve of setting out, he addressed the sylvan deities, saying, Luck! I will, with my desire obtained, go from forth this Siddhāśrama to the Himavat mountain on the north of the Jahnavi.

sanskrit: ityuktvā muniśārdūlaḥ kauśikaḥ sa tapodhanaḥ| uttarāṃ diśamuddiśya prasthātumupacakrame||
english: Having said this, that tiger-like ascetic, Kusika's son, along with other anchorets having asceticism for their wealth, set out in a northerly direction.

sanskrit: taṃ vrajantaṃ munivaramanvagādanusāriṇām| śakaṭīśatamātraṃ tu prayāṇe brahmavādinām||
english: And as that best of ascetics proceeded, he was followed by Brāhmaṇas, unholding the Veda, carrying the sacrificial necessaries on an hundred cars.

sanskrit: mṛgapakṣigaṇāścaiva siddhāśramanivāsinaḥ| anujagmurmahātmānaṃ viśvāmitraṃ tapodhanam||
english: And birds and beasts dwelling in Siddhāśrama followed the high-souled Viśvāmitra having asceticism for wealth.

sanskrit: nivartayāmāsa tataḥ sarṣisaṅghaḥ sa pakṣiṇaḥ| te gatvā dūramadhvānaṃ lambamāne divākare|| vāsaṃ cakrurmunigaṇāḥ śoṇākūle samāhitāḥ| te'staṃ gate dinakare snātvā hutahutāśanāḥ|| viśvāmitraṃ puraskṛtya niṣeduramitaujasaḥ| rāmo'pi sahasaumitrirmunīstānabhipūjya ca|| jagrato niṣasādātha viśvāmitrasya dhīmataḥ|
english: Having proceeded a long way, when the sun was sioping down, the ascetics rested on the banks of the Soņa. And when the maker of day had set, having bathed and offered oblations to the fire those ascetics of immeasurable energy, placing Viśvāmitra in their front, sat them down. And Rāma also together with Sumitrā's son, having paid homage to those ascetics, sat him down before the intelligent Viśvāmitra.

sanskrit: atha rāmo mahātejā viśvāmitraṃ tapodhanam|| papraccha muniśārdūlaṃ kautūhalasamanvitam| bhagavan ko nvayaṃ deśaḥ samṛddhavanaśobhitaḥ|| śrotumicchāmi bhadraṃ te vaktumarhasi tattvataḥ|
english: Then Rama of exceeding energy, influenced by curiosity, asked that foremost of ascetics, Viśvāmitra, having asceticism for his wealth, saying, 'O worshipful one, what country is this, graced with luxuriant woods? I am desirous of hearing this Good betide you, it behove you to tell me this truly.

sanskrit: nodito rāmavākyena kathayāmāsa suvrataḥ| tasya deśasya nikhilamṛṣimadhye mahātapāḥ||
english: Thus addressed by Rāma, that one of high austerities and excellent vows began in the midst of the saints to describe the opulence of that region.

sanskrit: tadapriyamamitraghno vacanaṃ maraṇopamam| śrutvā na vivyathe rāmaḥ kaikeyī cedamabravīt|||
english: Hearing these unpleasant words like to death, Rama, the destroyer of foes, was not pained, and spoke thus to Kaikeyī.

sanskrit: evamastu gamiṣyāmi vanaṃ vastumahaṃ tvitaḥ| jaṭācīradharo rājñaḥ pratijñāmanupālayan||
english: Be it what you say; carrying out the promise of the king, I shall repair to the forest from this place wearing bark and matted hair.

sanskrit: idaṃ tu jñātumicchāmi kimarthaṃ māṃ mahīpatiḥ| nābhinandati durdharṣo yathāpūrvabhariṃdamaḥ||
english: Now I want to know only why that lord of the earth, invincible and the conqueror of foes, does not receive me in the same way as he used to do on previous occasions.

sanskrit: manyurna ca tvayā kāryo devi brūmi tavāgrataḥ| yāsyāmi bhava suprītā vanaṃ cīrajaṭādharaḥ||
english: be not angry, Oh worshipful one, I speak before you, be you propitiated well, and I shall go to the forest wearing bark and matted hair.

sanskrit: hitena guruṇā pitrā kṛtajñena nṛpeṇa ca| niyujyamāno visrabdhaḥ kiṃ na kuryāāhaṃ priyam||
english: What is there that I cannot perform, considering it good without suspicion, if I am ordered so by my well-wisher, spiritual leader, father and king, who acknowledges your service (rendered in time of danger).* *The epithet Krtajñena may as well as be rendered into general terms; such as 'who acknowledges services rendered to him.' Here in translation I have followed the commentator who has restricted it to the special sense suitable to the occasion.

sanskrit: alīkaṃ mānasaṃ tvekaṃ hṛdayaṃ dahate mama| svayaṃ yannāha māṃ rājā bharatasyābhiṣecanam||
english: But this one sorrow burns my heart, why king did not tell me personally of the installation of Bharata.

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi sītāṃ rājyaṃ ca prāṇāniṣṭān dhanāni ca | hṛṣṭo bhrātre svayaṃ dadyāṃ bharatāya pracoditaḥ|| kiṃ punarmanujendreṇa svayaṃ pitrā pracoditaḥ| tava ca priyakāmārthaṃ pratijñāmanupālayan||
english: What of the command of the king, my father, I shall even at your mandate joyfully make over to Bharata, my kingdom, Sītā, wealth and even my life, thereby satisfying you, and fulfilling my promise.

sanskrit: tathāśvāsaya hrīmantaṃ kiṃtvidaṃ yanmahīpatiḥ| vasudhāsaktanayano mandamaśrūṇi muñcati ||
english: Do you now console the bashful king; why has he, with his eyes steadily fixed on the ground, been shedding tears slowly?

sanskrit: gacchantu caivānayituṃ dūtāḥ śīghrajavairhayaiḥ| bharataṃ mātulakulādadyaiva nṛpaśāsanāt||
english: Let messengers, with fast going steeds go today at the command of the king to fetch Bharata from his maternal uncle's house.

sanskrit: daṇḍakāraṇyameṣo'haṃ gacchāmyeva hi satvaraḥ| avicārya piturvākyaṃ samā vastuṃ caturdaśa||
english: I shall, not even judging the propriety of my father's words, speedily repair to the forest of Dandaka for fourteen years.

sanskrit: sā hṛṣṭā tasya tad vākyaṃ śrutvā rāmasya kaikayī| prasthānaṃ śraddadhānā sā tvarayāmāsa rāghavam||
english: Hearing those words of Rāma, Kaikeyi was pleased, and being certain about his departure, hurried on Raghava.

sanskrit: yāsyanti dūtāḥ śīghrajavairhayaiḥ| bharataṃ mātulakulādihāvartayutaṃ narāḥ||
english: Let it be that messengers with fast going steeds shall go to bring Bharata from his maternal uncle's residence.

sanskrit: evaṃ bhavatu tava tvahaṃ kṣamaṃ manye notsukasya vilambanam| rāma tasmāditaḥ śīghraṃ vanaṃ tvaṃ gantumarhasi ||
english: I do not think it proper for you, O Rāma, to delay, when you are so anxious; it behoves you therefore to depart from this place speedily to the forest.

sanskrit: vrīḍānvitaḥ svayaṃ yacca nṛpastvāṃ nābhibhāṣate| naitat kiṃcinnaraśreṣṭha manyureṣo'panīyatām||
english: The king being abashed, does not himself address you, there is nothing else than this. Do you, Oh best of men, dispel this wretchedness of his.

sanskrit: yāvattvaṃ na vanaṃ yātaḥ purādasmādatitvaram| pitā tāvannate rāma snāsyate bhokṣyate'pi vā||
english: As long as you shall not hurriedly depart from his presence, Oh Rāma, your father shall not bathe, or eat anything.

sanskrit: dhikkaṣṭamiti niḥśvasya rājā śokapariplutaḥ| mūrcchito nyapatat tasmin paryaṅke hemabhūṣite||
english: 'Oh fie!' 'what affliction' sobbing hard with these words, the monarch, filled with sorrow, swooned away and fell down upon the sofa, embellished with gold.

sanskrit: rāmo'pyutthāppa rājānaṃ kaikeyyābhipracoditaḥ| kaśayeva hato vājī vanaṃ gantuṃ kṛtatvaraḥ||
english: Raising the king up, Rāma, being directed by Kaikeyī, began to hurry on his departure to the forest, like to a steed struck sharp with a whip.

sanskrit: tadapriyamanāyā vacanaṃ dāruṇodayam| śrutvā gatavyatho rāmaḥ kaikeyīṃ vākyamabravīt||
english: Hearing those cruel and unpleasant words of the wicked Kaikeyi, Rama, not being distressed, began to address her with the following words.

sanskrit: nāhamarthaparo devi lokamāvastumutsahe| viddhi māmṛṣibhistulyaṃ vimalaṃ dharmamāsthitam ||
english: Oh worshipful one, being addicted to wealth do I not long for living in this world; like to Rșis, know me, to be well established in pure religion.

sanskrit: yat tatra bhavataḥ kiṃcicchakyaṃ kartuṃ priyaṃ mayā| prāṇānapi parityajya sarvathā kṛtameva tat||
english: If I can, even at the sacrifice of my own life, satisfy my worshipful father, rest assured it is to be done first in all manner.

sanskrit: na hyato dharmacaraṇaṃ kiṃcidasti mahattaram| yathā pitari śuśrūṣā tasya vā vacanakriyā||
english: There is no virtue greater than the serving of the father and carrying out his words.

sanskrit: anukto'pyatrabhavatā bhavatyā vacanādaham| vane vatsyāmi vijane varṣāṇīha caturdaśa||
english: Even though not commanded by him, I shall, for your words, live in a solitary forest for fourteen years.

sanskrit: na nyūnaṃ mayi kaikeyi kiṃcidāśaṃsase guṇān | yad rājānamavocastvaṃ mameśvaratarā satī ||
english: Oh Kaikeyī, certain it is that you are not acquainted with my foremost virtues, inasmuch as possessing full authority to rule me, you have requested the monarch for this.

sanskrit: yāvanmātaramāpṛcche sītāṃ jānunayāmyaham| tato'dyaiva gamiṣyāmi daṇḍakānāṃ mahad vanam||
english: Excuse me until I ask my mother, and comfort Sītā; even this very day shall I wend my way to the great forest of Dandaka.

sanskrit: bharataḥ pālayed rājyaṃ śuśrūṣecca pituryathā| tathā bhavatyā kartavyaṃ sa hi dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ||
english: If behoves you to do that by which Bharata may govern the kingdom and tend our father, for this is the virtue eternal.

sanskrit: rāmasya tu vacaḥ śrutvā bhṛśaṃ duḥkhagataḥ pitā| śokādaśaknuvan vaktuṃ praruroda mahāsvanam||
english: Hearing these words of Rāma, his father, greatly afflicted and incapable of speaking anything on account of sorrow, began to cry aloud.

sanskrit: vanditvā caraṇau rājño visaṃjñasya pitustadā| kaikeyyāścāpyanā yā niṣpapāta mahādyutiḥ||
english: Worshipping the feet of the king lying insensible, and those of vicious Kaikeyi, that greatly effulgent one went out.

sanskrit: sa rāmaḥ pitaraṃ kṛtvā kaikeyīṃ ca pradakṣiṇam| niṣkramyāntaḥpurāt tasmāt svaṃ dadarśa suhajjanam||
english: And reverentially going round his father and Kaikeyi, and issuing out of the female apartment, Rāma saw his own friends and relatives.

sanskrit: taṃ bāṣpaparipūrṇākṣaḥ pṛṣṭhato'nujagāma ha| lakṣmaṇaḥ paramakruddhaḥ sumitrānandavardhanaḥ||
english: Then followed him Lakşmaņa, the enhance of Sumitra's joy, greatly angry and with his eyes full of tears.

sanskrit: ābhiṣecanikaṃ bhāṇḍaṃ kṛtvā rāmaḥ pradakṣiṇam| śanairjagāma sāpekṣo dṛṣṭiṃ tatrāvicālayan||
english: Going round with reverence the house of installation full of necessary articles, not turning away from it his wistful look, Rāma began to proceed slowly.

sanskrit: na cāsya mahatīṃ lakṣmī rājyanāśo'pakarṣati| lokakāntasya kāntatvācchītaraśmeriva kṣayaḥ||
english: Loss of kingdom could not diminish the great beauty of that beloved of the people on account of its everlasting pleasantness, like to the wane of the moon.

sanskrit: na vanaṃ gantukāmasya tyajataśca vasuṃdharām| sarvalokātigasyeva lakṣyate cittavikriyā||
english: There was manifest in his no change of mind, who was about to fly as an exile to the forest and leave the world, like to one emancipated while yet living.

sanskrit: pratiṣidhya śubhaṃ chatraṃ vyajane ca svalaṃkṛte| visarjayitvā svajanaṃ rathaṃ paurāṃstathā janān|| dhārayan manasā du:khamindriyāṇi nigṛhya ca| praviveśātmavān veśma māturapriyaśaṃsivān||
english: Leaving aside the excellent umbrella and well adorned chowries, forsaking his relatives, chariot, citizens and other people, calmly bearing the affliction in mind and not manifesting the outward signs of sorrow, Rāma, with a view to communicate this unpleasant news to his mother, entered her abode.

sanskrit: sarvo'pyabhijanaḥ śrīmāñśrīmataḥ satyavādinaḥ| nālakṣayata rāmasya kaṃcidākāramānane||
english: All persons, who were present there and who adorned themselves on account of the installation, did not perceive any sign of mental agony on the face of Rāma.

sanskrit: ucitaṃ ca mahābāhurna jahau harṣamātmavān| śāradaḥ samudīrṇāṃśuścandrasteja ivātmajam||
english: Like to the rays of the fully brilliant autumnal moon, that hero of mighty arms, having control over himself, did not forsake his native cheerfulness.

sanskrit: vācā madhurayā rāmaḥ sarvaṃ sammānayañjanam| mātuḥ samīpaṃ dharmātmā praviveśa mahāyaśāḥ||
english: The pious Rāma, having high fame, entered into the presence of his mother, manifesting great regards for the people with sweet speech.

sanskrit: taṃ guṇaiḥ samatāṃ prāpto bhrātā vipulavikramaḥ| saumitriranuvavrāja dhārayan duḥkhamātmajam||
english: Then followed him, the son of Sumitrā, of mighty prowess, of equal accomplishments with his brother, and bearing the mental sorrow. Rāma, entering the abode of his mother.

sanskrit: praviśya veśmātibhṛśaṃ mudā yutaṃ samīkṣya tāṃ cārthavipattimāgatām| na caiva rāmo'tra jagāma vikriyāṃ suhṛjjanasyātmavipattiśaṅkayā||
english: Saw it filled with all sorts of amusements; and even though his mind was not agitated with any mental disturbance seeing the impending calamity of loss of wealth, he was anxious lest the lives of his dear relatives mighty be in danger.

sanskrit: kharaṃ tu virathaṃ rāmo gadāpāṇimavasthitam| mṛdupūrvaṃ mahātejāḥ paruṣaṃ vākyamabravīt||
english: And to Khara deprived of his car standing with a mace in his hand, that exceedingly energetic one, Rāma, precluding his speech with mildness, spoke.

sanskrit: gajāśvarathasambādhe bale mahati tiṣṭhatā| kṛtaṃ te dāruṇaṃ karma sarvalokajugupsitam|| udvejanīyo bhūtānāṃ nṛśaṃsaḥ pāpakarmakṛt| trayāṇāmapi lokānāmīśvaro'pi sa tiṣṭhati || karma lokaviruddhaṃ tu kurvāṇaṃ kṣaṇadācara| tīkṣṇaṃ sarvajano hanti saṣa duṣṭamivāgatam||
english: Backed by this mighty host abounding in elephants and horses and cars, you have done an exceedingly wicked deed, execrated by all the worlds. Even if one happen to be the lord of the three worlds, one given to troubling creatures, and who is cruel and engaged in wicked acts, can not exist. All persons destroy, like a snake that has intruded itself, him that dose cruel deeds, hostile to the interests of every one.

sanskrit: lobhāt pāpāni kurvāṇaḥ kāmād vā yo na budhyate| hṛṣṭaḥ paśyati tasyāntaṃ brāhmaṇī karakādiva||
english: People delightedly behold the end of him that doing an action either from covetousness or desire, dose not like a Brāhmaṇi swallowing a Karakā, see the consequence thereof.

sanskrit: vasato daṇḍakāraṇye tāpasān dharmacāriṇaḥ| kiṃ nu hatvā mahābhāgān phalaṃ prāpsyasi rākṣasa||
english: What, O Rākṣasa, do you gain by slaughtering exceedingly pious ascetics engaged in righteous acts, living in the forest of Dandaka?

sanskrit: na ciraṃ pāpakarmāṇaḥ krūrā lokajugupsitāḥ| aiśvaryaṃ prāpya tiṣṭhanti śīrṇamūlā iva drumāḥ|7||
english: Like to trees whose roots have been reduced, cruel persons, execrated of men, who perpetrate iniquitous acts, do not exist long.

sanskrit: avaśyaṃ labhate kartā phalaṃ pāpasya karmaṇaḥ| ghoraṃ paryāgate kāle drumaḥ puṣpamivārtavam ||
english: As a tree puts forth blossoms in season, the doer of sinful deeds, at the hour (of repentance) inevitably reaps their fruit in the shape of dreadful anguish (of the spirit).

sanskrit: na cirāt prāpyate loke pāpānāṃ karmaṇāṃ phalam| saviṣāṇāmivānnānāṃ bhuktānāṃ kṣaṇadācara||
english: O ranger of night, as the effect of having taken rice mixed with poison, appears without delay, even so also people readily reap the fruit of their own acts.

sanskrit: pāpamācaratāṃ ghoraṃ lokasyāpriyamicchatām| ahamāsādito rājñā prāṇān hantuṃ niśācara ||
english: O ranger of the night, it is to take the lives of the perpetrators of dreadful sins, who wish ill to men, that I the king have come.

sanskrit: adya bhitvā mayā muktāḥ śarāḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇāḥ| vidāryātipatiṣyanti valmīkamiva pannagāḥ||
english: Today the gold-decked arrows discharged by ine, piercing (your body), shall enter into the carth, cleaving it, like serpents falling into an ant-hill.

sanskrit: ye tvayā daṇḍakāraṇye bhakṣitā dharmacāriṇaḥ| tānadya nihataḥ saṃkhye sasainyo'nugamiṣyasi ||
english: Slain in battle, you shall in company with your army, follow those people practising piety, whom you have devoured in the Dandaka forest.

sanskrit: adya tvāṃ nihataṃ bāṇaiḥ paśyantu paramarṣayaḥ| nirayasthaṃ vimānasthā ye tvayā nihatāḥ purā||
english: Today let those great saints, who had formerly been slain by you, stationed in the sky, behold you slain (in turn) with my arrows, and inhabiting hell.

sanskrit: praharasva yathākāmaṃ kuru yatnaṃ kulādhama| adya te pātayiṣyāmi śirastālaphalaṃ yathā||
english: Do you strike as you like. And youl that are of an odious race, do you put forth your energy. Today I will bring down your head, even as a palm falls to the ground.

sanskrit: evamuktastu rāmeṇa kruddhaḥ saṃraktalocanaḥ| pratyuvāca tato rāmaṃ prahasan krodhamūcchitaḥ||
english: Thus addressed by Rāma, Khara enraged and beyond himself with passion, with eyes reddened, replied.

sanskrit: prākṛtān rākṣasān hatvā yuddhe daśarathātmaja| ātmanā kathamātmānamapraśasyaṃ praśaṃsasi||
english: O son of Dasaratha, why having slain inferior Rākṣasas in battle, do you praise yourself without reason?

sanskrit: vikrāntā balavanto vā ye bhavanti nararṣabhāḥ| kathayanti na te kiṃcit tejasā cātigarvitāḥ||
english: Those foremost of men that are puissant and powerful, do not, inflated with their energy, mouth (their own consequence).

sanskrit: prākṛtāstvakṛtātmāno loke kṣatriyapāṃsanāḥ| nirarthakaṃ vikatthante yathā rāma vikatthase ||
english: It is the mean-minded Kșatriyas of impure hearts that magnify themselves among men, even as you, O Rama,do.

sanskrit: kulaṃ vapadiśan vīraḥ samare ko'bhidhāsyati| mṛtyukāle tu samprāpte svayamaprastave stavam||
english: What hero, when the hour of his death has approached, publishes in the field his own lofty lineage and sings his own hymn.

sanskrit: sarvathā tu laghutvaṃ te katthanena vidarśitam| suvarṇapratirūpeṇa tapteneva kuśāgninā||
english: As brass wearing the semblance of gold, displays its own defect on being heated*, with a fire lit with Kusa, so you have betrayed your own lightness by this speech of yours. i.c. becomes dusky, (Ramanuja).

sanskrit: na tu māmiha tiṣṭhantaṃ paśyasi tvaṃ gadādharam| dharādharamivākampyaṃ parvataṃ dhātubhiścitam||
english: You do not see me staying here mace in hand, like a moveless mountain dyed in metals, bearing mobile and immobile things.

sanskrit: paryāpto'haṃ gadāpāṇirhantuṃ prāṇān raṇe tava| trayāṇāmapi lokānāṃ pāśahasta ivāntakaḥ||
english: I can, mace in hand, deprive you and the three worlds to boot clean of your lives, like the very Destroyer with the noose in his hand.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ bahvapi vaktavyaṃ tvayi vakṣyāmi na tvaham| astaṃ prāpnoti savitā yuddhavighnastato bhavet||
english: But I will not parley much with you as much as I could wish: the sun is going to set, and our fight shall be interrupted.

sanskrit: caturdaśa sahasrāṇi rākṣasānāṃ hatāni te| tvadvināśāt karomyadya teṣāmathupramārjanam||
english: Fourteen thousand Räksasas have been slaughtered by you. I will for their deaths wipe their tears to-day.

sanskrit: ityuktvā paramakruddhaḥ sa gadāṃ paramāṅgadām| kharaścikṣepa rāmāya pradīptāmaśani yathā ||
english: Saying this Khara, highly enraged, hurled his mace+ provided with golden rings at Rāma, like to the blazing thunderbolt. Another reading is, plaited with gold.

sanskrit: kharabāhupramuktā sā pradīptā mahatī gadā| bhasmavṛkṣāṃśca gulmāṃśca kṛtvāgāt tatsamīpataḥ||
english: Thereat, reducing to ashes trees and shrubs, that mighty flaming mace, discharged by Khara's arm, fell before Rama.

sanskrit: tāmāpatantī mahatī mṛtyupāśopamāṃ gadām| antarikṣagatī rāmaściccheda bahudhā śaraiḥ||
english: And Rāma severed in many fragments that mighty mace, resembling the noose of Death, as ascending the welkin, it was coming down.

sanskrit: sā viśīrṇā śarairbhinnā papāta dharaṇītale| gadā mantrauṣadhibalaiālīva vinipātitā||
english: Thereupon, like a she-serpent brought down by force of incantations, the mace fell to the earth shattered and riven.

sanskrit: tathā tu taṃ samādiśya bhrātaraṃ raghunandanaḥ| babandhāsiṃ mahātejā jāmbūnadamayatsarum||
english: Having thus directed his brother, the highly energetic son of Raghu equipped himself with his gold-hilted scimitar.

sanskrit: tatastrivinataṃ cāpamādāyātmavibhūṣaṇam| ābadhya ca kapālau dvau jagāmodagravikramaḥ||
english: And girding himself with his bow bent at three places, which served him ornament,—as well as a couple of quivers, that one of fierce energy sallied out.

sanskrit: taṃ vanyarājo rājendramāpatantaṃ nirīkṣya vai| babhūvāntarhitastrāsāt punaḥ saṃdarśane'bhavat||
english: Seeing that foremost of monarchs approach, that best of beasts from fear disappeared; and then again showed himself. as an

sanskrit: baddhāsirdhanurādāya pradudrāva yato mṛgaḥ| taṃ sma paśyati rūpeṇa dyotayantamivāgrataḥ|| avekṣyāvekṣya dhāvantaṃ dhanuṣpāṇirmahāvane| ativṛttamivotpātāllobhayānaṃ kadācana|| śaṅkitaṃ tu samudmāstamutpatantamivāmbaram| dṛśyamānamadṛśyaṃ ca vanoddeśeṣu keṣucit|| chinnābhairiva saṃvītaṃ śāradaṃ candramaṇḍalam| muhūrtādeva dadṛśe muhurdūrāt prakāśate||
english: Thereat girt with the bow and sword, (Rāma) rushed where the deer was; and beheld him illumining all before him with his beauty, and bow in hand (Rāma beheld) him in that vast forest, darting away after gazing at him,-and sometimes seeming to have got beyond arrow range, and at others tempting Rāma (by his vicinity). And sometimes influenced by fear and bewildered, (the deer) seemed to course the welkin; and in the forest now he became visible and now vanished from sight. And like the autumual lunar disc enveloped by indented clouds, he momentarily showed himself, and anon discovered himself at a distance.

sanskrit: darśanādarśanenaiva so'pākarṣata rāghavam| sa dūramāśramasyāsya mārīco mṛgatāṃ gataḥ||
english: And Mārica wearing the shape of a deer, showing himself and disappearing from sight, drew Rāghava a long way from the hermitage.

sanskrit: āsīt kruddhastu kākutstho vivaśastena mohitaḥ| athāvatasthe suśrāntaśchāyāmāśritya śābale||
english: Thereat Rāma, eagerly anxious to secure the deer, being foiled by the deer, and in consequence growing enraged, wearied out, rested under a shadow, on a sward.

sanskrit: sa tamunmādayāmāsa mṛgarūpo niśācaraḥ| mṛgaiḥ parivṛto'thānyairadūrāt pratyadṛśyata||
english: And that ranger of the night, wearing the form of a deer, maddening Rāma, discovered himself (again) at a distance surrounded by (other) deer,

sanskrit: grahītukāmaṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ punarevābhyadhāvata| tatkṣaṇādeva saṃtrāsāt punarantarhito'bhavat||
english: And Rama desirous of taking (the beast), seeing him again, set off at speed. At the very moment the deer disappeared from fear,

sanskrit: punareva tato dūrād vṛkṣakhaṇḍād viniḥsṛtaḥ| dṛṣṭvā rāmo mahātejāstaṃ hantuṃ kṛtaniścayaḥ|| bhūyastu śaramuddhatya kupitastatra rāghavaḥ| sūryaraśmipratīkāśaṃ jvalantamarimardanam || saṃdhāya sudṛḍhe cāpe vikṛṣya balavadabalī| tameva mṛgamuddiśya śvasantamiva pannagam|| mumoca jvalitaṃ dīptamastraṃ brahmavinirmitam|
english: And again showed himself at a distance behind a tree. And seeing him, the exceedingly energetic and strong Rāghava, determined to slay him, growing wroth, taking out a flaming shaft, resembling the rays of the sun, powerfully drew his bow, and firmly setting the shaft, and aiming it at the deer, let go the blazing and burning weapon forged by Brahmā, resembling a flaiming serpent.

sanskrit: śarīraṃ mṛgarūpasya vinirbhidya śarottamaḥ|| mārīcasyaiva hṛdayaṃ bibhedāśanisaṃnibhaḥ|
english: And that best of arrows, like to a thunderbolt, deeply pierced the breast of Mārīca, wearing the shape of a deer.

sanskrit: tālamītramathotplutya nyapatat sa bhṛśāturaḥ|| vyanadad bhairavaṃ nādaṃ dharaṇyāmalpajīvitaḥ|
english: Thereat bounding up high as a palmyra palm, that one whose saws had almost run out, uttered terrible sounds, lying on the earth.

sanskrit: mriyamāṇastu mārīco jahau tāṃ kṛtrimā tanum|| smṛtvā tadvacanaṃ rakṣo dadhyau kena tu lakṣmaṇam| iha prasthāpayet sītā tāṃ śūnye rāvaṇo haret||
english: And while on the point of death, Mārīca renounced his counterfeit shape. And remembering the words of Rāvana, the Rākşasa reflected, by what means can Sītā send away Lakşmaņa, and Rāvana carry off Sītā staying in solitude?

sanskrit: sa prāptakālamājñāya cakāra ca tataḥ svanam| sadṛśaṃ rāghavasyeva hā sīte lakṣmaṇeti ca || tena marmaṇi nirviddhaṃ śareṇānupamena hi| mṛgarūpaṃ tu tat tyaktvā rākṣasaṃ rūpamāsthitaḥ||
english: And pierced to the marrow by that peerless shaft, Marica, renouncing his deer form, resumed his Rākşasa lineaments; and giving up his life attaining a huge person, considering the time had come (for availing himself of the advice tendered by Rāvana), began to cry with the voice of Rāghava, Ah Sita! Ah Laksmana!

sanskrit: cakre sa sumahākāyo mārīco jīvitaṃ tyajan| taṃ dṛṣṭvā patitaṃ bhūmau rākṣasaṃ bhīmadarśanam|| rāmo rudhirasiktāṅga ceṣṭamānaṃ mahītale| jagāma manasā sītāṃ lakṣmaṇasya vacaḥ smaran ||
english: And seeing that grim-visaged Rākşasa lying low on the ground, with his person bathed in blood, and rolling hither and thither, Rāma proceeded towards the asylum thinking of Sītā and revolving within himself Laksmana's words.

sanskrit: mārīcasya tu māyaiṣā pūrvoktaṃ lakṣmaṇena tu| tat tathā hyabhavaccādya mārīco'yaṃ mayā hataḥ||
english: While returning he thought Mārīca aside Lakş mana said before that this was Mārica's illusion! His words have been verified now. Truly have I killed Mārīca.

sanskrit: hā sīte lakṣmaṇetyevamākruśya tu mahāsvanam| mamāra rākṣasaḥ so'yaṃ śrutvā sītā kathaṃ bhavet||
english: Mārīca has given up his ghost exclaiming aloud Ah! Sītā, Ah! Laksmana. I do not know what shall Sītā do hearing the cry? And what shall the mighty-armed Laksmana do?

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇaśca mahābāhuḥ kāmavasthāṃ gamiṣyati| iti saṃcintya dharmātmā rāmo hṛṣṭatanūrūhaḥ|| tatra rāmaṃ bhayaṃ tīvramāviveśa viṣādajam| rākṣasaṃ mṛgarūpaṃ taṃ hatvā śrutvā ca tatsvanam||
english: While pondering thus the hairs of the virtuous-souled Rāma stood on their end. Killing that Räkşasa assuming the shape of a deer and hearing his terrible cry Rāma was overwhelmed with fear arising out of sorrow.

sanskrit: nihatya pṛṣataṃ cānyaṃ māṃsamādāya rāghavaḥ| tvaramāṇo janasthānaṃ sasārābhisukhaṃ tadā||
english: Thereupon killing a deer and taking its flesh he hastened towards Janasthāna.

sanskrit: tāṃ tu pārśve sthitāṃ prahvāṃ rāmaḥ saṃmekṣya maithilīm| hṛdayāntargataṃ bhāvaṃ vyāhartumupacakrame||
english: Beholding Maithili standing humbly by him, Räma began to give vent to his pent-up feelings.

sanskrit: eṣāsi nirjitā bhadre śatru jitvā raṇājire| pauruṣāt yadanuṣṭheyaṃ mayaitadupapāditam||
english: O gentle one, destroying all the enemies in the arena of battle I have subdued your enemy-I have done all that can be accomplished by manliness.

sanskrit: gato'smyantamamarṣasya dharṣaṇā saṃpramārjitā| avamānaśca śatruśca yugapatrihatau mayā||
english: I have reached the other end of my anger, rubbed off (the insult) for my spouse being taken away by the enemy and have killed simultaneously my disgrace and enemy.

sanskrit: adya me pauruṣaṃ dṛṣṭamadya me saphalaḥ śramaḥ| adya tīrṇapratijño'haṃ prabhavāmyadya cātmanaḥ||
english: My manliness has been displayed today, my laboúr has been crowned with success and today I have fulfilled my promise by my own prowess.

sanskrit: yā tvaṃ virahitā nītā calacittena rakṣasā| daivasaṃpādito doṣo mānuṣeṇa mayā jitaḥ||
english: That accidental misfortune, under the influence where of you were carried away by the fickle-minded Räksasa in my absence, has been subdued today by me, a man.

sanskrit: saṃprāptamavamānaṃ yastejasā na pramārjati| kastasya pauruṣeṇārtho mahatāpyalpacetasaḥ||
english: What is the use of his manliness, who when insulted, cannot remove it? Even if he be a great man he may be called mean.

sanskrit: laṅghanaṃ ca samudrasya laṅkāyāścāpi mardanam| saphalaṃ tasya ca ślāghyamadya karma hanūmataḥ||
english: The praise-worthy works of Hanumān-the crossing of the deep and the devastation of Lankā, have been crowned with success today.

sanskrit: yuddhe vikramataścaiva hitaṃ mantrayatastayā| sugrīvasya sasainyasya saphalo'dya pariśramaḥ||
english: The labour of Sugrīva with his army, who displayed valour in the encounter and gave me good counsels, has borne fruit today.

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇasya ca tathā saphalo'dya pariśramaḥ| viguṇaṃ bhrātaraṃ tyaktvā yo māṃ svayamupasthitaḥ||||
english: Today also the labour of Vibhişaņa has borne fruit-who renouncing his brother, devoid of all good Qualities, came to my side.

sanskrit: ityevaṃ vadataḥ śrutvā sītā rāmasya tadvacaḥ| mṛgīvotphullanayanā babhūvāśrupariplutā ||
english: Hearing those words of Rāma, Sītā began to look wistfully like a hind, with eyes full of tears.

sanskrit: paśyatastāṃ tu rāmasya samīpe hṛdayapriyām| janavādabhayādrājño babhūva hṛdayaṃ dvidhā ||
english: Beholding his beloved spouse near him and afraid of popular ignominy his heart was broken into two.

sanskrit: sītāmutpalapatrākṣī nīlakuñcitamūrdhajām| avadadvai varārohāṃ madhye vānararakṣasām||
english: Thereupon he spoke to the exquisitely beautiful Sītā, in the midst of the monkeys and Räkşasas, having eyes resembling lotus petals and black and curling hairs, saying.

sanskrit: yatkartavyaṃ manuṣyeṇa dharṣaṇāṃ pratimārjatā| tatkṛtaṃ rāvaṇaṃ hatvā mayedaṃ mānakāṅkṣiṇā|| nirjitā jīvalokasya tapasā bhāvitātmanā| agastyena durādharṣā muninā dakṣiṇeva dik ||
english: As the southern quarter, incapable of being got at by the people, was conquered by the selfcontrolled great ascetic Agasty, so for you slaying Ravana, I (always) anxious to have honour, have removed my insult-as is the duty of a man.

sanskrit: viditaścāstu bhadraṃ te yo'yaṃ raṇapariśramaḥ| sutīrṇaḥ suhṛdāṃ vīryānna tvadarthaṃ mayā kṛtaḥ||
english: May good betide you-do you know that all my labour in the battle-field, backed by the prowess of my friends, is for you.

sanskrit: rakṣatā tu mayā vṛttamapavādaṃ ca sarvataḥ| prakhyātasyātmavaṃśasya nyaṅgaṃ ca parimārjatā||
english: To uphold the dignity of my well-known family, to remove the ignominy consequent upon your being stolen away as well as to wipe off my own insult I have encompassed this.

sanskrit: prāptacāritrasaṃdehā mama pratimukhe sthitā| dīpo netrāturasyeva pratikūlāsi me dṛḍhā ||
english: I have suspected your character; you, (Therefore) standing before me, are distressing me like to a lamp before one who is subject to an eye-desease.

sanskrit: tadgaccha tvānujāne'dya yatheṣṭaṃ janakātmaje| etā daśa diśo bhadre kāryamasti na me tvayā||
english: Do you therefore proceed, O daughter of king Janaka, wherever you like to one of these ten quarters. I permit you, O gentle one. I have nothing to do with you.

sanskrit: kaḥ pumāṃstu kule jātaḥ striyaṃ paragṛhoṣitām| tejasvī punarādadyātsuhṛllobhena cetasā ||
english: What powerful man, born in a high family, take back his wife considering her as friend out of lust, who has lived long in another's house?

sanskrit: rāvaṇāṅkaparikliṣṭāṃ dṛṣṭāṃ duṣṭena cakṣuṣā| kathaṃ tvāṃ punarādadyāṃ kulaṃ vyapadiśanmahat||
english: You were taken by Rāvana on his lap, beheld by him with sinful eyes; how can I, taking you back, bring disgrace upon my great family?

sanskrit: yadartha nirjitā me tvaṃ so'yamāsādito mayā| nāsti me tvayyabhiṣvaṅgo yatheṣṭaṃ gamyatāmiti ||
english: The object, with which I have gained you back, has been accomplished. I have got no attachment for you-do you go wherever you wish, O gentle one.

sanskrit: tadadya vyāhṛtaṃ bhadre mayaitatkṛtabuddhinā| lakṣmaṇe vātha bharate kuru buddhiṃ yathāsukham|| śatrughne vātha sugrīve rākṣase vā vibhīṣaṇe| niveśaya manaḥ sīte yathā vā sukhamātmanā||
english: I speak these to you impelled by my sense of duty. If you wish you may live with Laksmana, Bharatga or Satrughna or with Sugrīva or Räkş asa Vibhisana. Do you settle, O Sita, where you may find your own pleasure.

sanskrit: nahi tvāṃ rāvaṇo dṛṣṭvā divyarūpāṃ manoramām| marṣayatyaciraṃ sīte svagṛhe paryavasthitām||
english: O Sita, (I do not think) Ravana has overlooked you, who lived in his house, beholding you so graceful and beautiful.

sanskrit: tataḥ priyāhaśravaṇā tadapriyaṃ priyādupaśrutya cirasya māninī| mumoca bāṣpaṃ rudatī tadā bhṛśaṃ gajendrahastābhihateva vallarī||
english: Thereupon hearing those unpleasant words from her beloved (husband) Sītā, always sensitive and who had never heard such unpleasant words, trembling like a creeper torn by the trunk of an elephant, began to weep shedding tears profusely.

sanskrit: tadā vṛtravadhaṃ sarvamakhilena sa lakṣmaṇaḥ| kathayitvā naraśreṣṭhaḥ kathāśeṣa pracakrame|| tato hate mahāvīrye vṛtre devabhayaṃkare| brahmahatyāvṛtaḥ śakraḥ saṃjñāṃ lebhe na vṛtrahā||
english: Having thus described at length and finished the story of Vſtra's destruction Lakşmaņa said:-The mighty Vţtra, the terror of the deities, being slain, and the slayer Indra being assailed by the sin of Brahmanicide, was bewildered and at a loss to ascertain his duty.

sanskrit: so'ntamāśritya lokānāṃ naṣṭasaṃjño vicetanaḥ| kālaṃ tatrāvasatkaṃcidveṣṭamāna ivoragaḥ||
english: Being at his wit's end he repaired to the other side of the Lokāloka mountain and remained there for some time like a coiled serpent.

sanskrit: atha naṣṭe sahasrākṣe udvignamabhavajjagat| bhūmiśca dhvastasaṃkāśā niḥsnehā śuṣkakānanā|| niḥsrotasaste sarve tu hṛdāśca saritastathā| saṃkṣobhaścaiva sattvānāmanāvṛṣṭikṛto'bhavat||
english: And again in consequence of Indra's separation, the whole world was agitated, the forests grew dried and the earth was devoid of water. On account of the rivers being dried up and want of rain all creatures grew impatient.

sanskrit: kṣīyamāṇe tu loke'sminsaṃbhrāntanasaḥ surāḥ| yaduktaṃ viṣṇunā pūrvaṃ taṃ yajñaṃ samupānayan||
english: In this wise, the celestials being stricken with anxiety, according to the previous command of Visnu, engaged in celebrating the sacrifice.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarve suragaṇāḥ sopādhyāyāḥ saharṣibhiḥ| taṃ deśaṃ samupājagmuryavendro bhayamohitaḥ|| te tu dṛṣṭvā sahasrākṣamāvṛtaṃ brahmahatyayā| taṃ puraskṛtya deveśamaśvamedhaṃ pracakrire||
english: With Rșis and Rtvikas they fearfully approached Purandra; and beholding him assailed by the sin of Brahmanicide, they with him, at their head, engaged in celebrating a horse-sacrifice.

sanskrit: tato'śvamedhaḥ suhānmahendrasya mahātmanaḥ| vavṛte brahmahatyāyāḥ pāvanārthaṃ nareśvara || tato yajñe samāpte tu brahmahatyā mahātmanaḥ| abhigamyābravīdvākyaṃ kva me sthānaṃ vidhāsyatha|| te tāmūcustato devāstuṣṭāḥ prītisamanvitāḥ| caturdhā vibhajātmānamātmanaiva durāsade||
english: After the sacrifice the sin issued out of Indra's person and addressing the high-souled deities said: Do you all ascertain, where I shall go now. There upon highly pleased the deities replied: Do you divide yourself into four portions.

sanskrit: devānāṃ bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā brahmahatyā mahātmanām| saṃdadhau sthānamanyatra varayāmāsa durvasā || ekenāṃśena vatsyāmi pūrṇodāsu nadīṣu vai| caturo vārṣikānmāsāndarpaghnī kāmacāriṇī||
english: Hearing the words of the high-souled celestials she divided herself into four parts and wishing for a separate habitation said:-By one portion, I shall at my pleasure, live in rivers full of water during rains and shall obstruct people from going there.

sanskrit: bhūmyāmahaṃ sarvakālamekenāṃśena sarvadā| vasiṣyāmi na saṃdehaḥ satyenaitadbravīmi vaḥ|| | yo'yamaṃśastṛtīyo me strīṣu yauvanaśāliṣu| trirātraṃ darpapūrṇāsu vasiṣye darpaghātinī|| hantāro brāhmaṇānye tu mṛṣāpūrvamadūṣakān| tāṃścaturthena bhāgena saṃśrayiṣye sarurṣabhāḥ||
english: By my second portion I shall live perpetually on lands as Uşara;* I tell you the truth. By my third portion I shall for three nights every month live in youthful women proud of their youth-So that men might not live with them. And by my fourth portion I shall enter into the persons of those who shall slay innocent Bråhmaņas. *(A spot with saline soil.)

sanskrit: pratyūcustāṃ tato devā yathā vadasi durvase| tathā bhavatu tatsarvaṃ sādhayasva yadīpsitam||
english: Hearing those words the deities said What you have said shall be carried out. Do what you wish.

sanskrit: tataḥ prītyānvitā devāḥ sahasrākṣaṃ vavandire| vijvaraḥ pūtapāpmā ca vāsavaḥ samapadyata ||
english: There upon the celestials, delighted, adored their Chief divested of sins and crowned with victory.

sanskrit: praśāntaṃ ca jagatsarvaṃ sahasrākṣe pratiṣṭhite| yajñaṃ cādbhutasaṃkāśaṃ tadā śakro'bhyapūjayat||
english: And Väsava being installed again on the throne, the whole universe was at rest. There upon Indra worshipped Vişnu in the shape of that wonderful sacrifice.

sanskrit: īdṛśo hyaśvamedhasya prasādo raghunandana| yajasva sumahābhāga hayamedhena pārthiva ||
english: O descendant of Raghu, such is the power of a horse-sacrifice. O honourable king, therefore, you may perform this sacrifice.

sanskrit: iti lakṣmaṇavākyamuttamaṃ nṛpatiratīva manoharaṃ mahātmā| paritoṣamavāpa hṛṣṭacetāḥ sa niśamyendrasamānavikramaujāḥ||
english: Hearing the charming words of Lakşmaņa, the energetic and high-souled king, Rāma, powerful like Indra, was greatly delighted.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya tato'strāṇi prahṛṣṭavadanaḥ śuciḥ| gacchanneva ca kākutstho viśvāmitramathābravīt||
english: Having accepted those weapons with purity, Käkutstha while proceeding, with a complacent countenance spoke these words to sage Visvāmitra,-

sanskrit: gṛhītāstro'smi bhagavan durādharṣaḥ surairapi| astrāṇāṃ tvahamicchāmi saṃhārān munipuṅgava||
english: O adorable one, I have received these weapons, incapable of being repressed even by the celestials themselves. Now, O best of ascetics, I would acquire a knowledge of with drawing them.

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvati kākutsthe viśvāmitro mahātapāḥ| saṃhārān vyājahārātha dhṛtimān suvrataḥ śuciḥ||
