english: Upon Kākutstha's representing this, Viśvāmitra of high austerities, endowed with patience, of excellent vows, and pure in spirit, communicated to him the mantras for restraining the weapons.

sanskrit: satyavantaṃ satyakīrtiṃ dhṛṣṭaṃ rabhasameva ca| pratihārataraṃ nāma parāṅmukhamavāṅmukham|| lakṣyālakṣyāvimau caiva dṛḍhanābhasunābhako| daśākṣaśatavaktrau ca daśaśīrṣaśatodarau|| padmanābhamahānābhau dundunābhasvanābhako| jyotiṣa śakunaṃ caiva nairāsyavimalāvubhau || yaugaṃdharavinidrau ca daityapramathanau tathā| śucibāhurmahābāhuniṣkalivirucastathā| sārcimālī dhṛtimālī vṛttimān rucirastathā|| pitryaḥ saumanasaścaiva vidhūtamakarāvubhau| paravīraṃ ratiṃ caiva dhanadhānyau ca rāghava|| kāmarūpaṃ kāmaruciṃ mohamāvaraṇaṃ tathā| jṛmbhakaṃ sarpanāthaṃ ca panthānavaruṇau tathā|| kṛśāśvatanayān rāma bhāsvarān kāmarūpiṇaḥ| pratīccha mama bhadraṃ te pātrabhūto'si rāghava||
english: Do you, O Rāma, accept Satyavat, and Satyakirti, Dhrsta, Rabhasa, Pratihāratara, Paranmukha, Avanmukha, and also Laksya, a Alakṣya, Dędhanabha, Sunābha, Sunabha, Dasaksa, Satavaktra, Dasasirsa, Satodara, Padmanabha, Mahanabha, Indunābha, Svanābha, Jyotisa, Sakuna, Nairasya, Vimala, Yaugandhara, Vinidra, and the two Daityapramathanas, and Śucibāhu, Mahābāhu, Niskali, Viruca, Arcimāli, Dhrtimali, Vrttimān, Rucira, Pitrya, Saumansa, Vidhuta, Makara, Karavīra, Rati, Dhana, and Dhānya, O Rāghava, and Kāmarūpa, Kāmaruci, Moha, Avarana and Jrmbhaka, Sarpanātha, Panthāna, and Varuņa-these sons of Kļśāśva, O Rāma, effulgent, and assuming shapes at will. And, good betide you, O descendant of Raghu, you are worthy to receive these weapons.

sanskrit: bāḍhamityeva kākutsthaḥ prahaṣṭenāntarātmanā | divyabhāsvaradehāśca mūrtimantaḥ sukhapradāḥ|| kecidaṅgārasadṛśāḥ kecit dhūmopamāstathā| candrārkasadṛśāḥ kecit prahvāñjalipuṭāstathā|| rāmaṃ prāñjalayo bhūtvābruvan madhurabhāṣiṇaḥ| ime sma naraśārdūla śādhi kiṃ karavāma te||
english: Thereupon, Kākutstha with heart overflowing with delight, said,-So be it! And those weapons were furnished with celestial and shining persons, and endowed with visible shapes, and capable of conferring happiness. And some of them were like (live) coals; and some comparable to smoke; and some were like to the Sun or the Moon. And with folded hands, they spoke to Rāma in honied accents; O chief of men, here we are! Do you command as to what we are to do on your behalf.

sanskrit: gamyatāmiti tānāha yatheyaṃ raghunandanaḥ| mānasāḥ kāryakāleṣu sāhāyyaṃ me kariṣyatha ||
english: Then the descendant of Raghu answered, saying, Repair whither soever you will! Recurring to my memory, do you in time of need, render me assistance!

sanskrit: atha te rāmāmantrya kṛtvā cāpi pradakṣiṇam| evamastviti kākutsthamuktvā jagmuryathāgatam|| sa ca tān rāghavo jñātvā viśvāmitraṃ mahāmunim| gacchannevātha madhuraṃ ślakṣṇaṃ vacanamabravīt|| kimetanmeghasaṃkāśaṃ parvatasyāvidūrataḥ| vṛkṣakhaṇḍamito bhāti paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me||
english: Thereupon paying homage to Rāma, and having gone round him, they replied to Kākutstha, What is yonder wood hard by the hill, appearing like clouds? Great is my curiosity.

sanskrit: darśanīyaṃ mṛgākīrṇaṃ manoharamatīva ca| nānāprakāraiḥ śakunairvalgubhāṣairalaṃkṛtam||
english: It is pleasing to the sight, and abounds in beasts, and is exceedingly romantic, and is adorned with various birds singing sweetly.

sanskrit: niḥsṛtāḥ smo muniśreṣṭha kāntārād romaharṣaṇāt| anayā tvavagacchāmi deśasya sukhavattayā||
english: Now, O foremost of ascetics, we have come out of a wilderness capable of making one's hair stand on end. And from the pleasantness attaching to this place, I have come to a conclusion.

sanskrit: sarvaṃ me śaṃsa bhagavan kasyāśramapadaṃ tvidam| samprāptā yatra te pāpā brahmaghnā duṣṭacāriṇaḥ|| tava yajñasya vighnāya durātmāno mahāmune| bhagavaṃstasya ko deśa: sā yatra tava yājñikī|| rakṣitavyā kriyā brahman mayā vadhyāśca rākṣasāḥ| etat sarvaṃ muniśreṣṭha śrotumicchāmyahaṃ prabho||
english: Tell me, O reverend sir, whose hermitage is this? Have we, O eminent ascetic, reached that spot where dwell those wicked minded wretches of impious deeds, given to slaughtering Brāhmaṇas, who disturb your sacrifice? Where, O adorable one, is that hermitage, repairing to which, O Brahmana, I am to protect your sacrificial rites, and to slay the Raksasas? All this, O foremost of ascetics, I desire to hear, O lord.

sanskrit: visṛjya tu suhṛdvarga buddhyā niścitya rāghavaḥ| samīpe dvā:sthamāsīnamidaṃ vacanamabravīt||
english: Having sent away his friends and determined what to do, Rāma, the delight of the Råghus, commanded the warder, who was seated hard by, saying.

sanskrit: śīghramānaya saumitri lakṣmaṇaṃ śubhalakṣaṇam| bharataṃ ca mahābhāgaṃ śatrughnamaparājitam||
english: Do you bring in no time, Lakşmaņa, a son of Sumitrā, gifted with auspicious marks, alongwith great Bharata and the irrepressible Šatrughna.

sanskrit: rāmasya vacanaṃ śrutvā dvā:stho mūrdhni kṛtāñjaliḥ| lakṣmaṇasya gṛhaṃ gatvā praviveśānivāritaḥ||
english: Hearing the words of Rāma and placing his folded palms on his head the warder reached house of Lakşmaņa and unobstructed entered therein.

sanskrit: uvāca sumahātmānaṃ vardhayitvā kṛtāñjaliḥ| draṣṭumicchati rājā tvāṃ gamyatāṃ tatra mā ciram||
english: "And having saluted him, with folded palms he said to the high-souled Laksmana and:-""The King wishes to behold you-do you soon go there."

sanskrit: bāḍhamityeva saumitriḥ kṛtvā rāghavaśāsanam| prādravadrathamāruhya rāghavasya niveśanam||
english: Thereupon being apprised of Rāghava's command and saying 'so be it.' Saumitri ascended his car and went speedily towards Rāma's abode.

sanskrit: prayāntaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā dvā:stho bharatamantikāt| uvāca bharataṃ tatra vardhayitvā kṛtāñjaliḥ|| vinayāvanato bhūtvā rājā tvāṃ draṣṭumicchati|
english: "Having beheld Lakşmana's departure the warder humbly went to Bharata and having blessed him with folded hands said: “The King wishes to see you."""

sanskrit: bharatastu vacaḥ śrutvā dvāḥsthādrāmasamīritam|| utpapātāsanāttūrṇaṃ padbhyāmeva mahābalaḥ|
english: Hearing of the command of Rāma from the warder, the highly powerful Bharata at once got up from his seat and proceeded on foot.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā prayāntaṃ bharataṃ tvaramāṇaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ|| śatrughnabhavanaṃ gatvā tato vākyamuvāca ha|
english: Seeing Bharata's departure the warder speedily went to the mansion of Satrughna and with folded hands said.

sanskrit: ehyāgaccha raghuśreṣṭha rājā tvāṃ draṣṭumicchati|| gato hi lakṣmaṇaḥ pūrvaṃ bharataśca mahāyaśāḥ|
english: """Do you come, O foremost Raghus, the King wish to behold you.” Lakşmaņa and Bharata are also there."

sanskrit: śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tasya śatrughnaḥ paramāsanāt|| śirasā vandya dharaṇī prayayau yatra rāghavaḥ|
english: Hearing the words of the warder Satrughna lowered his head and rising up speedily proceeded to Rama.

sanskrit: dvāḥsthastvāgamya rāmāya sarvāneva kṛtāñjaliḥ|| nivedayāmāsa tathā bhrātṛnsvānsamupasthitān|
english: Thereupon returning, the warder, with folded। hands, communicated to Rama, the arrivals of his brothers.

sanskrit: kumārānāgatāñchrutvā cintāvyākulitendriyaḥ|| avāṅmukho dīnamanā dvāḥsthaṃ vacanamabravīt| praveśaya kumārāṃstvaṃ matsamīpaṃ tvarānvitaḥ|| eteṣu jīvitaṃ mahyamete prāṇāḥ priyā mama|
english: So long Rāma was engaged poorly in anxious meditation with his crown bent downwards. Informed of the princes' arrival he commanded the warder, “Do you soon bring the princes here. My life depends upon them. They are my dearest life.

sanskrit: ājñaptāstu narendreṇa kumārāḥ śuklavāsasaḥ|| prahvāḥ prāñjalayo bhūtvā viviśuste samāhitāḥ|
english: Having obtained Rāma's command, the princes, clothed in white raiment, entered there, with folded palms and quiescent mind.

sanskrit: Vimalakīrtinirdeśa
english: The Teaching of Vimalakīrti

sanskrit: namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisatvebhyaḥ //
english: Reverence to all the buddhas, bodhisattvas, noble disciples, and pratyekabuddhas, in the past, the present, and the future.

sanskrit: Vkn  evaṃ mayā śrutam /
english: Thus did I hear on a single occasion.

sanskrit: ekasmin samaye bhagavān vaiśālyāṃ viharati sma, āmrapālīvane mahatā bhikṣusamghena sārdham aṣṭābhir bhikṣusahasraiḥ,
english: The Lord Buddha was in residence in the garden of Āmrapālī, in the city of Vaiśālī, attended by a great gathering. Of bhikṣus there were eight thousand, all arhats.

sanskrit: Vkn  sarvair arhadbhiḥ kṣīṇāsravair niḥkleśair vaśībhūtaiḥ suvimuktacittaiḥ suvimuktaprajñair
english: They were free from impurities and afflictions, and all had attained selfmastery. Their minds were entirely liberated by perfect knowledge.

sanskrit: ājāneyair mahānāgaiḥ kṛtakṛtyaiḥ kṛtakaraṇīyair apahṛtabhārair anuprāptasvakārthaiḥ
english: They had accomplished their work, done what they had to do, cast off their burdens, attained their goals, and totally destroyed the bonds of existence.

sanskrit: parikṣīṇabhavasamyojanaiḥ samyagājñāsuvimuktacittaiḥ sarvacetovaśiparamapāramiprāptaiḥ,
english: Their true knowledge had made their minds entirely free. They all had attained the utmost perfection of every form of control over their minds.

sanskrit: Vkn  dvātriṃśatā ca bodhisatvasahasrair abhijñānābhijñātaiḥ sarvair mahābhijñāparikarmaniryātaiḥ,
english: Of bodhisattvas there were thirtytwo thousand, great spiritual heroes who were universally acclaimed.

sanskrit: buddhādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhitaiḥ,
english: They were dedicated through the penetrating activity of their great superknowledges and were sustained by the grace of the Buddha.

sanskrit: saddharmanagarapālaiḥ, saddharmaparigrāhakaiḥ, mahāsiṃhanādanādibhiḥ, daśadigvighuṣṭaśabdaiḥ,
english: Guardians of the city of Dharma, they upheld the true doctrine, and their great teachings resounded like the lion’s roar throughout the ten directions.

sanskrit: sarvasatvānadhyeṣitakalyāṇamitraiḥ,
english: Without having to be asked, they were the natural spiritual benefactors of all living beings.

sanskrit: triratnavaṃśānupacchetṛbhiḥ, nihatamārapratyarthikaiḥ, sarvaparapravādyanabhibhūtaiḥ,
english: They maintained unbroken the succession of the Three Jewels, conquering devils and foes and overwhelming all critics.

sanskrit: smṛtisamādhidhāraṇīsaṃpannaiḥ, sarvanivaraṇaparyutthānavigataiḥ,
english: Their mindfulness, intelligence, realization, meditation, retention, and eloquence all were perfected.

sanskrit: anāvaraṇavimokṣapratiṣṭhitaiḥ, anācchedyapratibhānaiḥ,
english: They were free of all obscurations and emotional involvements, living in liberation without impediment.

sanskrit: dānadamaniyamasaṃyamaśīlakṣāntivīryadhyānaprajñopāyaniryātaiḥ, anupalambhānutpattikadharmakṣāntisamanvāgataiḥ,
english: They were totally dedicated through the transcendences of generosity subdued, unwavering, and sincere morality tolerance effort meditation wisdom skill in liberative art commitment and gnosis. They had attained the intuitive tolerance of the ultimate incomprehensibility and unborn nature of all things.

sanskrit: avaivartikadharmacakrapravartakaiḥ,
english: They turned the irreversible wheel of the Dharma.

sanskrit: alakṣaṇamudrāmudritaiḥ,
english: They were stamped with the insignia of signlessness.

sanskrit: sarvasatvendriyajñānakuśalaiḥ,
english: They were expert in knowing the spiritual faculties of all living beings.

sanskrit: sarvaparṣadanabhibhūtavaiśāradyavikrāmibhiḥ,
english: They were brave with the confidence that overawes all assemblies.

sanskrit: mahāpuṇyajñānasaṃbhāropacitaiḥ, lakṣaṇānuvyañjanasamalaṃkṛtakāyaiḥ, paramarūpadhāribhiḥ, apagatabhūṣaṇaiḥ,
english: They had gathered the great stores of merit and of wisdom, and their bodies, beautiful without ornaments, were adorned with all the auspicious signs and marks.

sanskrit: meruśikharābhyudgatayaśaḥkīrtisamudgataiḥ,
english: They were exalted in fame and glory, like the lofty summit of Mount Sumeru.

sanskrit: dṛḍhavajrādhyāśayābhedyabuddhadharmaprasādapratilabdhaiḥ, dharmaratnavikaraṇāmṛtajalasaṃpravarṣakaiḥ,
english: Their high resolve as hard as diamond, unbreakable in their faith in the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, they showered forth the rain of ambrosia that is released by the light rays of the jewel of the Dharma, which shines everywhere.

sanskrit: sarvasatvarutaravitasvarāṅgaghoṣaviśuddhasvaraiḥ,
english: Their voices were perfect in diction and resonance, and versatile in speaking all languages.

sanskrit: gambhīradharmapratītyāvatārāntānantadṛṣṭivāsanānusaṃdhisamucchinnaiḥ, vigatabhayasiṃhopamanādibhiḥ,
english: They had penetrated the profound principle of relativity and had destroyed the persistence of the instinctual mental habits underlying all convictions concerning finitude and infinitude. They spoke fearlessly, like lions, sounding the thunder of the magnificent teaching.

sanskrit: tulyātulyasamatikrāntaiḥ,
english: Unequaled, they surpassed all measure.

sanskrit: dharmaratnaprajñāsamudānītamahāsārthavāhaiḥ ṛjusūkṣmamṛdudurdṛśaduranubodhasarvadharmakuśalaiḥ,
english: They were the best captains for the voyage of discovery of the treasures of the Dharma, the stores of merit and wisdom. They were expert in the way of the Dharma, which is straight, peaceful, subtle, gentle, hard to see, and difficult to realize.

sanskrit: āgatisatvāśayamatimanupraviṣṭajñānaviṣayibhiḥ,
english: They were endowed with the wisdom that is able to understand the thoughts of living beings, as well as their comings and goings.

sanskrit: asamasamabuddhajñānābhiṣekābhiṣiktaiḥ,
english: They had been consecrated with the anointment of the peerless gnosis of the Buddha.

sanskrit: daśabalavaiśāradyāveṇikabuddhadharmādhyāśayagataiḥ sarvāpāyadurgativinipātotkṣiptaparikhaiḥ, saṃcintyabhavagatyupapattisaṃdarśayitṛbhiḥ,
english: With their high resolve, they approached the ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, and the eighteen special qualities of the Buddha. They had crossed the terrifying abyss of the bad migrations, and yet they assumed reincarnation voluntarily in all migrations for the sake of disciplining living beings.

sanskrit: mahāvaidyarājaiḥ, sarvasatvavinayavidhijñaiḥ, yathārhadharmabhaiṣajyaprayogaprayuktaiḥ,
english: Great Kings of medicine, understanding all the sicknesses of passions, they could apply the medicine of the Dharma appropriately.

sanskrit: anantaguṇākarasamanvāgataiḥ, anantabuddhakṣetraguṇavyūhasamalaṃkṛtaiḥ,
english: They were inexhaustible mines of limitless virtues, and they glorified innumerable buddhafields with the splendor of these virtues.

sanskrit: amoghaśravaṇadarśanaiḥ,
english: They conferred great benefit when seen, heard, or even approached.

sanskrit: amoghapadavikramaiḥ, aparimitakalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraguṇaparikīrtanāparyantaguṇaughaiḥ /
english: Were one to extol them for innumerable hundreds of thousands of myriads of eons, one still could not exhaust their mighty flood of virtues.

sanskrit: sumatinā ca, sujātena ca,
english: These bodhisattvas were named

sanskrit: padmaśrīgarbheṇa ca, padmavyūhena ca, avalokiteśvareṇa ca, mahāsthāmaprāptena ca, brahmajālinā ca,
english: Samadarśin, Sama­viṣama­darśin, Samādhi­vikurvaṇa­rāja, Dharmeśvara, Dharmaketu, Prabhāketu, Prabhāvyūha, Ratnavyūha, Mahāvyūha, Pratibhāna­kūṭa, Ratnakūṭa, Ratnapāṇi, Ratna­mudrā­hasta, Nityotkṣipta­hasta, Nityotpalakṛta­hasta, Nityotkaṇṭhita, Nitya­prahasita­pramuditendriya, Prāmodyarāja, Devarāja, Praṇidhi­prayāta­prāpta, Prati­saṃvit­praṇāda­prāpta, Gaganagañja, Ratnolkā­dhārin, Ratnavīra, Ratnananda, Ratnaśrī, Indrajāla, Jālinīprabha, Anārambaṇa­dhyāyin, Prajñākūta, Ratnajaha, Mārapramardin, Vidyuddeva, Vikurvaṇarāja, Lakṣaṇa­kūṭa­samatikrānta, Siṃha­ghoṣābhigarjita­śvara, Śaila­śikhara­saṃghaṭṭana­rāja, Gandhahastin, Gaja­gandha­hastin, Satatodyukta, Anikṣiptadhura, Sumati, Sujāta, Padmaśrī­garbha, Padmavyūha, Avalokiteśvara, Mahā­sthāma­prāpta, Brahmajāla, Ratnayaṣṭin, Mārajit, Kṣetralaṃkṛta, Maṇi­ratnacchattra, Suvarnacūḍa, Maṇicūḍa, Maitreya, Mañjuśrī­kumāra­bhūta, and so forth, with the remainder of the thirtytwo thousand.

sanskrit: Vkn  daśabhiś ca brahmasahasrair jaṭibrahmapramukhaiḥ, anekāc caturmahādvīpakāl lokadhātor abhyāgatair bhagavato darśanāyai vandanāyai paryupāsanāyai dharmaśravaṇāya ca /
english: There were also gathered there ten thousand Brahmās, at their head Brahmā Śikhin, who had come from the Aśoka universe with its four sectors to see, venerate, and serve the Buddha and to hear the Dharma from his own mouth.

sanskrit: dvādaśa ca śakrasahasrāṇy anyānyebhyaś caturmahādvīpakebhyo 'bhyāgatāni tatraiva parṣadi saṃnipatitāny abhūvan /
english: There were twelve thousand Śakras from various foursector universes. And there were other powerful gods

sanskrit: tathānye 'pi maheśākhyamaheśākhyāḥ śakrabrahmalokapāladevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragās tatraiva parṣadi saṃnipatitā abhūvan saṃnisaṇṇāḥ /
english: Brahmās, Śakras, Lokapālas, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas.

sanskrit: tathā catasraḥ parṣado bhikṣubhiksūṇyupāsakopāsikāś copasaṃkrāntā abhūvan /
english: Finally, there was the fourfold community, consisting of bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, laymen, and laywomen.

sanskrit: Vkn  tatra bhagavān anekaśatasahasrayā parṣadā parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto dharmaṃ deśayati sma /
english: The Lord Buddha, thus surrounded and venerated by these multitudes of many hundreds of thousands of living beings, sat upon a majestic lionthrone and began to teach the Dharma.

sanskrit: sumerur iva parvatarājaḥ sāgaramadhyād abhyudgataḥ sarvaparṣadam abhibhūya bhāsate tapati virocate śrīgarbhe siṃhāsane niṣaṇnaḥ /
english: Dominating all the multitudes, just as Sumeru, the king of mountains, looms high over the oceans, the Lord Buddha shone, radiated, and glittered as he sat upon his magnificent lionthrone.

sanskrit: Vkn  atha ratnākaro bodhisatvo licchavikumāraḥ sārdhaṃ pañcamātrair licchavikumāraśataiḥ saptaratnamayāni cchatrāṇi gṛhītvā vaiśālyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ niṣkramya yenāmrapālīvanaṃ
english: Thereupon, the Licchavi bodhisattva Ratnākara, with five hundred Licchavi youths, each holding a precious parasol made of seven different kinds of jewels, came forth from the city of Vaiśālī and presented himself at the grove of Āmrapālī.

sanskrit: upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavantaṃ saptakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya yathā parigṛhītais taiś chatrair bhagavantam abhicchādayati sma /
english: Each approached the Buddha, bowed at his feet, circumambulated him clockwise seven times, laid down his precious parasol in offering, and withdrew to one side.

sanskrit: Vkn  samantaraniḥsṛṣṭāni ca tāni ratnacchatrāṇy atha tāvad eva buddhānubhāvenaikaṃ mahāratnacchatraṃ saṃsthitam / tena ca mahāratnacchatreṇāyaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātuḥ sarvaḥ saṃchāditaḥ saṃdṛśyate sma / yaś cāsmiṃs trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātāv āyāmavistāraḥ,
english: As soon as all these precious parasols had been laid down, suddenly, by the miraculous power of the Lord, they were transformed into a single precious canopy so great that it formed a covering for this entire billionworld galaxy. The surface of the entire billionworld galaxy was reflected in the interior of the great precious canopy, where the total content of this galaxy could be seen

sanskrit: ye 'pīha trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau mahāsamudrā vā sarastaḍāgāni vā nadīkunadyaḥ sravantyo vā pravahanti, tā api sarvās tasminn evaikamahāratnacchatre saṃdṛśyante sma / yāny apīha trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sūryācandramasāṃ vimānāni tārārūpāṇi vā devabhavanāni vā nāgabhavanāni vā yakṣabhavanāni vā gandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragabhavanāni vā cāturmahārājabhavanāni vā grāmanagaranigamarāṣṭrarājadhānyo vā,
english: limitless mansions of suns, moons, and stellar bodies the realms of the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, as well as the realms of the four Mahārājas the king of mountains, Mount Sumeru Mount Himavat, Mount Mucilinda, Mount Mahāmucilinda, Mount Gandhamādana, Mount Ratnaparvata, Mount Kālaparvata, Mount Cakravāḍa, and Mount Mahācakravāḍa all the great oceans, rivers, bays, torrents, streams, brooks, and springs and finally, all the villages, suburbs, cities, capitals, provinces, and wildernesses.

sanskrit: tāny api sarvāṇi tasminn evaikamahāratnacchatre saṃdṛśyante sma /
english: All this could be clearly seen by everyone.

sanskrit: yāpi ca daśadiśi loke buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ dharmadeśanā pravartate, sāpi tasmād evaikamahāratnacchatrān niścarantī śrūyate sma /
english: And the voices of all the buddhas of the ten directions could be heard proclaiming their teachings of the Dharma in all the worlds, the sounds reverberating in the space beneath the great precious canopy.

sanskrit: Vkn  tatra sā sarvā parṣad āścaryaprāptā bhagavato 'ntikād idam evaṃrūpaṃ mahāprātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā tuṣṭodagrāttamanāḥ pramuditā prītisaumanasyajātā tathāgataṃ namasyatī sthitānimiṣaṃ prekṣamāṇā /
english: At this vision of the magnificent miracle effected by the supernatural power of the Lord Buddha, the entire host was ecstatic, enraptured, astonished, delighted, satisfied, and filled with awe and pleasure. They all bowed down to the Tathāgata, withdrew to one side with palms pressed together, and gazed upon him with fixed attention.

sanskrit: Vkn  atha khalu ratnākaro licchavikumāro bhagavato 'ntikād idam evaṃrūpaṃ mahāprātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvaikāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena
english: The young Licchavi Ratnākara knelt with his right knee on the ground, raised his hands, palms pressed together in salute of the Buddha, and praised him with the following hymn “Pure are your eyes, broad and beautiful, like the petals of a blue lotus.

sanskrit: śubhaśuddhakamalavarapatraviśālanetra śuddhāśayā śamathapāramitāgraprāpta / śubhakarmasaṃcaya viśālaguṇāprameya vandāmi tvāṃ śramaṇaśāntipathapraṇetum // //
english: Pure is your thought, having discovered the supreme transcendence of all trances. Immeasurable is the ocean of your virtues, the accumulation of your good deeds. You affirm the path of peace. O Great Ascetic, obeisance to you!

sanskrit: paśyatha ṛddhi puruṣarṣabhanāyakasya saṃdṛśyate sugatakṣetravaraprakāśāḥ /
english: “Leader, bull of men, we behold the revelation of your miracle. The superb and radiant fields of the sugatas appear before us,

sanskrit: amṛtaṃgamā ca varadharmakathā udārā sā sarva śrūyati ito gaganatalātaḥ // //
english: And your extensive spiritual teachings that lead to immortality Make themselves heard throughout the whole reach of space.

sanskrit: dharmeṇa te jitam idaṃ varadharmarājyaṃ dharmaṃ dhanaṃ ca dadase jagato jitāre /
english: “DharmaKing, you rule with the Dharma your supreme Dharmakingdom, And thereby bestow the treasures of the Dharma upon all living beings.

sanskrit: dharmaprabhedakuśalaṃ paramārthadarśin dharmeśvaraṃ śirasi vandami dharmarājam // //
english: Expert in the deep analysis of things, you teach their ultimate meaning. Sovereign Lord of Dharma, obeisance to you!

sanskrit: na ca nāma asti na ca nāsti giraṃ prabhāṣi hetuṃ pratītya imi saṃbhavi sarvadharmāḥ /
english: “All these things arise dependently, from causes, Yet they are neither existent nor nonexistent.

sanskrit: naivātra ātmana ca kāraku vedako vā na ca karmu naśyati śubham aśubhaṃ ca kiṃcit // //
english: Therein is neither ego, nor experiencer, nor doer, Yet no action, good or evil, loses its effects. Such is your teaching.

sanskrit: māras tvayāstu vijitas sabalo munīndraḥ prāptā śivā amṛtaśāntavarāgrabodhiḥ /
english: “O Śākyamuni, conquering the powerful host of Māra, You found peace, immortality, and the happiness of that supreme enlightenment

sanskrit: yasminn avedita na cittamanaḥpracārā sarvakutīrthikagaṇāś ca na yānti gāhaṃ // //
english: That is not realized by any among the outsiders, Though they arrest their feeling, thought, and mental processes.

sanskrit: cakraṃ ca te triparivarti bahuprakāraṃ prāvartitaṃ praśamanaṃ prakṛtīviśuddham / pratyakṣa devamanujādbhutadharmarājā ratnāni trīṇi upadarśita tatra kāle // //
english: “O Wonderful King of Dharma, you turned the wheel of Dharma before men and gods, With its threefold revolution, its manifold aspects, Its extreme peace, and its purity of nature And thereby the Three Jewels were revealed.

sanskrit: ye tubhya dharmaratanena vinīta samyak teṣām akalpana punaḥ satate praśāntā /
english: “Those who are well disciplined by your precious Dharma Are free of vain imaginings and always deeply peaceful.

sanskrit: vaidyottamaṃ maraṇajātijarāntakāriṃ śirasā nato 'smi guṇasāgaram aprameyam // //
english: Supreme doctor, you put an end to birth, decay, sickness, and death. Immeasurable ocean of virtue, we bow to you!

sanskrit: satkārasatkṛta na vedhasi merukalpa duḥśīlaśīlavati tulyagatādhimaitrī /
english: “Like Mount Sumeru, you are unmoved by honor or scorn. You love moral beings and immoral beings equally.

sanskrit: gaganaprakāśamanase samatāvihārī ko nāma satvaratane 'smi na kuryu pūjām // //
english: Poised in equanimity, your mind is like the sky. Who would not honor such a precious jewel of a being?

sanskrit: samāgatā te janatā mahāmune mukham udīkṣanti prasannamānasā /
english: “Great Sage, in all these multitudes gathered here, Who look upon your countenance with hearts sincere in faith,

sanskrit: sarve ca paśyanti jinaṃ purastāj jinasya āveṇikabuddhalakṣaṇam // //
english: Each being beholds the Victor, as if just before him. This is a special quality of the Buddha.

sanskrit: ekāṃ ca vācaṃ bhagavān pramuñcase nānārutaṃ ca pariṣad vijānati /
english: “Although the Lord speaks with but one voice, Those present perceive that same voice differently,

sanskrit: yathāsvakaṃ cārtha vijānate jano jinasya āveṇikabuddhalakṣaṇam // //
english: And each understands in his own language according to his own needs. This is a special quality of the Buddha.

sanskrit: ekāya vācāya udīritāya vāsesi eke apare nividyasi /
english: “From the leader’s act of speaking in a single voice, Some merely develop an instinct for the teaching, some gain realization,

sanskrit: ākāṅkṣatāṃ kāṅkṣa śamesir nāyako jinasya āveṇikabuddhalakṣaṇam // //
english: Some find pacification of all their doubts. This is a special quality of the Buddha.

sanskrit: vandāmi tvāṃ daśabala satyavikramaṃ vandāmi tvām abhayagataṃ viśāradam /
english: “We bow to you who command the force of leadership and the ten powers! We bow to you who are dauntless, knowing no fear!

sanskrit: dharmeṣu āveṇikaniścayaṃ gataṃ vandāmi tvāṃ sarvajagatpraṇāyakam // //
english: We bow to you, leader of all living beings, Who fully manifests the special qualities!

sanskrit: vandāmi samyojanabandhanacchidaṃ vandāmi tvāṃ pāragataṃ sthale sthitam /
english: “We bow to you who have cut the bondage of all fetters! We bow to you who, having gone beyond, stand on firm ground!

sanskrit: vandāmi khinnasya janasya tārakaṃ vandāmi saṃsāragatāv aniśritam // //
english: We bow to you who save the suffering beings! We bow to you who do not remain in the migrations!

sanskrit: satvair samādhānagataṃ gatīgatam gatīṣu sarvāsu vimuktamānasam /
english: “You associate with living beings by frequenting their migrations, Yet your mind is liberated from all migrations.

sanskrit: jaleruhaṃ vā salile na lipyase niṣevitā te munipadma śūnyatā // //
english: Just as the lotus, born of mud, is not tainted thereby,

sanskrit: vibhāvitā sarvanimitta sarvaśo na te kahiṃcit praṇidhāna vidyate /
english: “You nullify all signs in all things everywhere. You are not subject to any wish for anything at all.

sanskrit: acintiyaṃ buddhamahānubhāvaṃ vande 'ham ākāśasamam aniśritam // //
english: The miraculous power of the buddhas is inconceivable. We bow to you, who stand nowhere, like infinite space.”

sanskrit: Vkn  atha ratnākaro licchavikumāro bhagavantam ābhir gāthābhir abhiṣṭutya bhagavantam etad avocat imāni bhagavan pañcamātrāṇi licchavikumāraśatāni sarvāṇy anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau saṃprasthitāni / tāni cemāni buddhakṣetrapariśuddhiṃ paripṛcchanti ḥ katamā bodhisatvānāṃ buddhakṣetrapariśuddhir iti /
english: Then, the young Licchavi Ratnākara, having celebrated the Buddha with these verses, further addressed him, “Lord, these five hundred young Licchavis are truly on their way to unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, and they have asked what is the bodhisattvas’ purification of the buddhafield. Please, Lord, explain to them the bodhisattvas’ purification of the buddhafield!”

sanskrit: evam ukte bhagavān ratnākarāya licchavikumārāya sādhukāram adāt
english: Upon this request, the Buddha gave his approval to the young Licchavi Ratnākara.

sanskrit: sādhu sādhu kumāra /
english: “Good, good, young man!

sanskrit: sādhu khalu punas tvaṃ kumāra yas tvaṃ buddhakṣetrapariśuddhim ārabhya tathāgataṃ paripṛcchasi /
english: Your question to the Tathāgata about the purification of the buddhafield is indeed good.

sanskrit: tena hi kumāra śṛṇu sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru /
english: Therefore, young man, listen well and remember!

sanskrit: bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te yathā bodhisatvānāṃ buddhakṣetrapariśuddhim ārabhya /
english: I will explain to you the purification of the buddhafield of the bodhisattvas.”

sanskrit: sādhu bhagavann iti ratnākaro licchavikumāras tāni ca pañcamātrāṇi licchavikumāraśatāni bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣuḥ /
english: “Very good, Lord,” replied Ratnākara and the five hundred young Licchavis, and they set themselves to listen.

sanskrit: bhagavāṃs teṣām etad avocat Vkn  satvakṣetraṃ kulaputra bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram /
english: The Buddha said, “Noble son, a buddhafield of bodhisattvas is a field of living beings.

sanskrit: tat kasya hetoḥ /
english: Why so?

sanskrit: yāvantaṃ bodhisatvaḥ satveṣūpacayaṃ karoti tāvad buddhakṣetraṃ parigṛhṇāti /
english: A bodhisattva embraces a buddhafield to the same extent that he causes the development of living beings.

sanskrit: yādṛśaḥ satvānāṃ vinayo bhavati tādṛśaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ parigṛhnāti /
english: He embraces a buddhafield to the same extent that living beings become disciplined.

sanskrit: yādṛśena buddhakṣetrāvatāreṇa satvā buddhajñānam avataranti tādṛśaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ parigṛhnāti / yādṛśena buddhakṣetrāvatāreṇa satvānām āryākārāṇīndriyāṇy utpadyante tādṛśaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ parigṛhṇāti /
english: He embraces a buddhafield to the same extent that, through entrance into a buddhafield, living beings are introduced to the buddhagnosis. He embraces a buddhafield to the same extent that, through entrance into that buddhafield, living beings increase their noble spiritual faculties.

sanskrit: tat kasya hetoḥ /
english: Why so?

sanskrit: satvārthanirjātaṃ hi kulaputra bodhisatvānāṃ buddhakṣetram /
english: ‌Noble son, a buddhafield of bodhisattvas springs from the aims of living beings.

sanskrit: tadyathā ratnākara yādṛśam icched ākāśaṃ māpayituṃ tādṛśaṃ māpayeta, na cākāśaṃ śakyate māpayituṃ nāpy alaṃkartum /
english: “For example, Ratnākara, should one wish to build in empty space, one might go ahead in spite of the fact that it is not possible to build or to adorn anything in empty space.

sanskrit: evam eva ratnākara ākāśasamān sarvadharmāñ jñātvā / yādṛśam icched bodhisatvaḥ satvaparipākāya buddhakṣetraṃ māpayituṃ tādṛśaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ māpayati, na ca buddhakṣetrākāśatā śakyaṃ māpayituṃ nāpy alaṃkartum /
english: In just the same way, should a bodhisattva, who knows full well that all things are like empty space, wish to build a buddhafield in order to develop living beings, he might go ahead, in spite of the fact that it is not possible to build or to adorn a buddhafield in empty space.

sanskrit: Vkn  api ca ratnākara, āśayakṣetraṃ bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram,
english: “Yet, Ratnākara, a bodhisattva’s buddhafield is a field of positive thought.

sanskrit: tasya bodhiprāptasyāśaṭhā amāyāvinaḥ satvā buddhakṣetra upapadyante /
english: When he attains enlightenment, living beings free of hypocrisy and deceit will be born in his buddhafield.

sanskrit: adhyāśayakṣetraṃ kulaputra bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram,
english: “‌Noble son, a bodhisattva’s buddhafield is a field of high resolve.

sanskrit: tasya bodhiprāptasya sarvakuśalasaṃbhāropacitāḥ satvā buddhakṣetre saṃbhavanti /
english: When he attains enlightenment, living beings who have harvested the two stores and have planted the roots of virtue will be born in his buddhafield.

sanskrit: prayogakṣetraṃ bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram,
english: “A bodhisattva’s buddhafield is a field of virtuous application.

sanskrit: tasya bodhiprāptasya sarvakuśaladharmopasthitāḥ satvās tatra buddhakṣetra upapadyante /
english: When he attains enlightenment, living beings who live by all virtuous principles will be born in his buddhafield.

sanskrit: udāro bodhisatvasya bodhicittotpādo buddhakṣetram,
english: “A bodhisattva’s buddhafield is the magnificence of the conception of the spirit of enlightenment.

sanskrit: tasya bodhiprāptasya mahāyānasaṃprasthitāḥ satvās tatra buddhakṣetre saṃbhavanti /
english: When he attains enlightenment, living beings who are actually participating in the Mahāyāna will be born in his buddhafield.

sanskrit: dānakṣetraṃ bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram,
english: “A bodhisattva’s buddhafield is a field of generosity.

sanskrit: tasya bodhiprāptasya sarvaparityāginaḥ satvās tatra buddhakṣetre saṃbhavanti /
english: When he attains enlightenment, living beings who give away all their possessions will be born in his buddhafield.

sanskrit: śīlakṣetraṃ bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram,
english: “A bodhisattva’s buddhafield is a field of morality.

sanskrit: tasya bodhiprāptasya sarvābhiprāyasaṃpannā daśakuśalakarmapathasaṃrakṣakāḥ satvās tatra buddhakṣetre saṃbhavanti /
english: When he attains enlightenment, living beings who follow the path of the ten virtues with positive thoughts will be born in his buddhafield.

sanskrit: kṣāntikṣetraṃ kulaputra bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram,
english: “A bodhisattva’s buddhafield is a field of tolerance.

sanskrit: tasya bodhiprāptasya dvātriṃśallakṣanālaṃkṛtāḥ kṣāntidamaśamathapāramiprāptāḥ satvā buddhakṣetre saṃbhavanti /
english: When he attains enlightenment, living beings with the transcendences of tolerance, discipline, and the superior trancehence beautiful with the thirtytwo auspicious signswill be born in his buddhafield.

sanskrit: vīryakṣetraṃ bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram,
english: “A bodhisattva’s buddhafield is a field of effort.

sanskrit: tasya bodhiprāptasya sarvakuśalaparyeṣṭiṣv ārabdhavīryāḥ satvā buddhakṣetre saṃbhavanti /
english: When he attains enlightenment, living beings who devote their efforts to virtue will be born in his buddhafield.

sanskrit: dhyānakṣetraṃ bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram,
english: “A bodhisattva’s buddhafield is a field of meditation.

sanskrit: tasya bodhiprāptasya smṛtisaṃprajanyasamāhitāḥ satvā buddhakṣetre saṃbhavanti /
english: When he attains enlightenment, living beings who are evenly balanced through mindfulness and awareness will be born in his buddhafield.

sanskrit: prajñākṣetraṃ bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram,
english: “A bodhisattva’s buddhafield is a field of wisdom.

sanskrit: tasya bodhiprāptasya samyaktvaniyatāḥ satvā buddhakṣetre saṃbhavanti /
english: When he attains enlightenment, living beings who are destined for the ultimate will be born in his buddhafield.

sanskrit: catvāry apramāṇāni ca bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram,
english: “A bodhisattva’s buddhafield consists of the four immeasurables.

sanskrit: tasya bodhiprāptasya maitrīkaruṇāmuditopekṣāvihārinaḥ satvā buddhakṣetre saṃbhavanti /
english: When he attains enlightenment, living beings who live by love, compassion, joy, and impartiality will be born in his buddhafield.

sanskrit: catvāri saṃgrahavastūni kulaputra bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram,
english: “A bodhisattva’s buddhafield consists of the four means of unification.

sanskrit: tasya bodhiprāptasya sarvavimuktisaṃgṛhītāḥ satvā buddhakṣetre saṃbhavanti /
english: When he attains enlightenment, living beings who are held together by all the liberations will be born in his buddhafield.

sanskrit: upāyakauśalyaṃ bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram,
english: “A bodhisattva’s buddhafield is skill in liberative art.

sanskrit: tasya bodhiprāptasya sarvopāyamīmāṃsākuśalāḥ satvā buddhakṣetre saṃbhavanti /
english: When he attains enlightenment, living beings skilled in all liberative arts and activities will be born in his buddhafield.

sanskrit: saptatriṃśadbodhipakṣā dharmā bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram,
english: “A bodhisattva’s buddhafield consists of the thirtyseven aids to enlightenment.

sanskrit: tasya bodhiprāptasya samyaksmṛtyupasthānasamyakprahāṇarddhipādendriyabalabodhyaṅgamārgavidhijñāḥ satvā buddhakṣetre saṃbhavanti /
english: Living beings who devote their efforts to the four foci of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of magical power, the five spiritual faculties, the five strengths, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eight branches of the holy path will be born in his buddhafield.

sanskrit: pariṇāmanācittaṃ bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram,
english: “A bodhisattva’s buddhafield is his mind of total dedication.

sanskrit: tasya bodhiprāptasya sarvaguṇālaṃkāraṃ buddhakṣetraṃ dṛśyate /
english: When he attains enlightenment, the ornaments of all virtues will appear in his buddhafield.

sanskrit: aṣṭākṣaṇapraśamadeśanā kulaputra bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram,
english: “A bodhisattva’s buddhafield is the doctrine that eradicates the eight adversities.

sanskrit: tasya bodhiprāptasya sarvāpāyasamucchinnam aṣṭākṣaṇavigataṃ buddhakṣetraṃ saṃbhavanti /
english: When he attains enlightenment, the three bad migrations will cease, and there will be no such thing as the eight adversities in his buddhafield.

sanskrit: svayaṃ śikṣāpadeṣu vartamānā parāpattyacodanatā bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram,
english: “A bodhisattva’s buddhafield consists of his personal observance of the basic precepts and his restraint in blaming others for their transgressions.

sanskrit: tasya bodhiprāptasyāpattiśabdo 'pi buddhakṣetre na saṃbhavati /
english: When he attains enlightenment, even the word ‘crime’ will never be mentioned in his buddhafield.

sanskrit: daśakuśalakarmapathapariśuddhiḥ kulaputra bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetram,
english: “A bodhisattva’s buddhafield is the purity of the path of the ten virtues.

sanskrit: tasya bodhiprāptasya niyatāyuṣo mahābhogā brahmacāriṇaḥ satyānuparivartinyā vācālaṃkṛtā madhuravacanā abhinnaparṣado bhinnasaṃdhānakuśalā īrṣyāvigatā avyāpannacittāḥ samyagdṛṣṭisamanvāgatāḥ satvā buddhakṣetre saṃbhavanti /
english: When he attains enlightenment, living beings who are secure in long life, great in wealth, chaste in conduct, enhanced by true speech, softspoken, free of divisive intrigues and adroit in reconciling factions, enlightening in their conversations, free of envy, free of malice, and endowed with perfect views will be born in his buddhafield.

sanskrit: Vkn  iti hi kulaputra, yāvanto bodhisatvasya prayogās tāvanta āśayāḥ /
english: “Thus, noble son, just as is the bodhisattva’s production of the spirit of enlightenment, so is his positive thought.

sanskrit: yāvanta āśayās tāvanto 'dhyāśayāḥ /
english: And just as is his positive thought, so is his virtuous application.

sanskrit: yāvanto 'dhyāśayās tāvantyo nidhyaptayaḥ / yāvantyo nidhyaptayas tāvantyaḥ pratipattayaḥ / yāvantyaḥ pratipattayas tāvantyaḥ pariṇāmanāḥ / yāvantyaḥ pariṇāmanās tāvanta upāyāḥ / yāvanta upāyās tāvantyaḥ kṣetrapariśuddhayaḥ /
english: “His virtuous application is tantamount to his high resolve his high resolve is tantamount to his determination his determination is tantamount to his practice his practice is tantamount to his total dedication his total dedication is tantamount to his liberative art his liberative art is tantamount to his development of living beings and his development of living beings is tantamount to the purity of his buddhafield.

sanskrit: yādṛśī kṣetrapariśuddhis tādṛśī satvapariśuddhiḥ / yādṛśī satvapariśuddhis tādṛśī jñānapariśuddhiḥ / yādṛśī jñānapariśuddhis tādṛśī deśanāpariśuddhiḥ / yādṛśī deśanāpariśuddhis tādṛśī jñānapratipattipariśuddhiḥ / yādṛśī jñānapratipattipariśuddhis tādṛśī svacittapariśuddhiḥ /
english: “The purity of his buddhafield reflects the purity of living beings the purity of the living beings reflects the purity of his gnosis the purity of his gnosis reflects the purity of his doctrine the purity of his doctrine reflects the purity of his transcendental practice and the purity of his transcendental practice reflects the purity of his own mind.”

sanskrit: Vkn  atha buddhānubhāvenāyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasyaitad abhavat
english: Thereupon, magically influenced by the Buddha, the venerable Śāriputra had this thought

sanskrit: yadi yādṛśī cittapariśuddhis tādṛśī bodhisatvasya buddhakṣetrapariśuddhiḥ saṃbhavati, tan mā āhaiva bhagavataḥ śākyamuner bodhisatvacaryāṃ carataś cittam apariśuddhaṃ yenedaṃ buddhakṣetram evam apariśuddhaṃ saṃdṛśyate /
english: “If the buddhafield is pure only to the extent that the mind of the bodhisattva is pure, then, when Śākyamuni Buddha was engaged in the career of the bodhisattva, his mind must have been impure. Otherwise, how could this buddhafield appear to be so impure?”

sanskrit: atha khalu bhagavān āyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasya cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkam ājñāyāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram etad avocat
english: The Buddha, aware of venerable Śāriputra’s thoughts, said to him, “What do you think, Śāriputra?

sanskrit: śāriputra mā āhaiva sūryācandramasāv apariśuddhau yaj jātyandho na paśyati /
english: Is it because the sun and moon are impure that those blind from birth do not see them?” Śāriputra replied, “No, Lord.

sanskrit: āha no hīdaṃ bhagavan jātyandhāparādha eṣa na sūryacandramasoḥ /
english: It is not so. The fault lies with those blind from birth, and not with the sun and moon.”

sanskrit: āha evam eva śāriputra satvānām ajñānāparādha eṣa yas tathāgatasya buddhakṣetraguṇālaṃkāravyūhaṃ kecit satvā na paśyanti,
english: The Buddha declared, “In the same way, Śāriputra, the fact that some living beings do not behold the splendid display of virtues of the buddhafield of the Tathāgata is due to their own ignorance.

sanskrit: na tatra tathāgatasyāparādhaḥ /
english: It is not the fault of the Tathāgata.

sanskrit: pariśuddhaṃ hi śāriputra tathāgatasya buddhakṣetraṃ yūyaṃ punar idaṃ na paśyatha /
english: Śāriputra, the buddhafield of the Tathāgata is pure, but you do not see it.”

sanskrit: Vkn  atha khalu jaṭī brahmā sthaviraṃ śāriputram etad avocat mā bhadantaśāriputra tathāgatasyāpariśuddhaṃ buddhakṣetram idaṃ vyāhārṣīt /
english: Then, the Brahmā Śikhin said to the venerable Śāriputra, “Reverend Śāriputra, do not say that the buddhafield of the Tathāgata is impure.

sanskrit: pariśuddhaṃ hi bhadantaśāriputra bhagavato buddhakṣetram /
english: Reverend Śāriputra, the buddhafield of the Tathāgata is pure.

sanskrit: īdṛśān vayaṃ buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhān bhagavataḥ śākyamuneḥ paśyāmaḥ /
english: I see the splendid expanse of the buddhafield of the Lord Śākyamuni as equal to the splendor of, for example, the abodes of the highest deities.”

sanskrit: atha khalu sthaviraḥ śāriputro jaṭinaṃ brahmāṇam etad avocat vayaṃ punar brahmann imāṃ mahāpṛthivīm utkūlanikūlāṃ kaṇṭakaprapātagiriśekharaśvabhragūthoḍigallapratipūrṇāṃ paśyāmaḥ /
english: Then the venerable Śāriputra said to the Brahmā Śikhin, “As for me, O Brahmā, I see this great earth, with its highs and lows, its thorns, its precipices, its peaks, and its abysses, as if it were entirely filled with ordure.”

sanskrit: nūnaṃ bhadantaśāriputrasyotkūlanikūlaṃ cittam apariśuddhabuddhajñānāśayaṃ yenedṛśaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ paśyasi /
english: Brahmā Śikhin replied, “The fact that you see such a buddhafield as this as if it were so impure, reverend Śāriputra, is a sure sign that there are highs and lows in your mind and that your positive thought in regard to the buddhagnosis is not pure either.

sanskrit: ye punas te bhadantaśāriputra bodhisatvāḥ sarvasatvasamacittāḥ pariśuddhabuddhajñānāśayās ta imaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ pariśuddhaṃ paśyanti /
english: Reverend Śāriputra, those whose minds are impartial toward all living beings and whose positive thoughts toward the buddhagnosis are pure see this buddhafield as perfectly pure.”

sanskrit: atha khalu tasmin samaye 'yaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātur anekaratnaśatasahasrasaṃcito 'nekaratnaśatasahasrapratyarpitaḥ saṃsthito 'bhūt tadyathāpi nāma ratnavyūhasya tathāgatasyānantaguṇaratnavyūho lokadhātus tādṛśo 'yaṃ lokadhātuḥ saṃdṛśyate sma /
english: Thereupon the Lord touched the ground of this billionworld galactic universe with his big toe, and suddenly it was transformed into a huge mass of precious jewels, a magnificent array of many hundreds of thousands of clusters of precious gems, until it resembled the universe of the Tathāgata Ratnavyūha, called Ananta­guṇa­ratna­vyūha.

sanskrit: tatra sā sarvāvatī parṣad āścaryaprāptā ratnapadmaniṣaṇnam ātmānaṃ saṃjānīte sma /
english: Everyone in the entire assembly was filled with wonder, each perceiving himself seated on a throne of jeweled lotuses.

sanskrit: Vkn  tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram āmantrayate sma paśyasi tvaṃ śāriputra imān buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhān /
english: Then, the Buddha said to the venerable Śāriputra, “Śāriputra, do you see this splendor of the virtues of the buddhafield?” Śāriputra replied, “I see it, Lord!

sanskrit: āha paśyāmi bhagavan adṛṣṭāśrutapūrvā ime vyūhāḥ saṃdṛśyante /
english: Here before me is a display of splendor such as I never before heard of or beheld!”

sanskrit: āha īdṛśaṃ mama śāriputra sadā buddhakṣetram / hīnasatvaparipākāya tu tathāgata evaṃ bahudoṣaduṣṭaṃ buddhakṣetram upadarśayati /
english: The Buddha said, “Śāriputra, this buddhafield is always thus pure, but the Tathāgata makes it appear to be spoiled by many faults, in order to bring about the maturity of inferior living beings.

sanskrit: tadyathā śāriputra devaputrāṇām ekapātryāṃ bhuñjānānāṃ yathā puṇyopacayaviśeṣeṇa sudhādevabhojanam upatiṣṭhataḥ,
english: For example, Śāriputra, the gods of the Trayastriṃśa heaven all take their food from a single precious vessel, yet the nectar that nourishes each one differs according to the differences of the merits each has accumulated.

sanskrit: evam eva śāriputra ekabuddhakṣetropapannā yathā cittapariśuddhyā satvā buddhānāṃ buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhān paśyanti /
english: Just so, Śāriputra, living beings born in the same buddhafield see the splendor of the virtues of the buddhafields of the buddhas according to their own degrees of purity.”

sanskrit: Vkn  asmin khalu punar buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhālaṃkāre saṃdarśyamāne caturaśīteḥ prāṇisahasrāṇām anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpannāni yāni ca tāni ratnākareṇa licchavikumāreṇa sārdhaṃ pañca licchavikumāraśatāny āgatāni teṣām apy ānulomikyāḥ kṣānteḥ pratilaṃbho 'bhūt /
english: When this splendor of the beauty of the virtues of the buddhafield shone forth, eightyfour thousand beings conceived the spirit of unexcelled perfect enlightenment, and the five hundred Licchavi youths who had accompanied the young Licchavi Ratnākara all attained the conformative tolerance of ultimate birthlessness.

sanskrit: Vkn  atha bhagavān punar eva tām ṛddhiṃ pratisaṃharati sma / tataḥ punar evedaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ tatsvabhāvam eva saṃvṛtam,
english: Then, the Lord withdrew his miraculous power and at once the buddhafield was restored to its usual appearance.

sanskrit: tatra śrāvakayānikānāṃ devamanuṣyāṇām ḥ anityā bateme sarvasaṃskārā iti viditvā dvātriṃśatā prāṇisahasrāṇāṃ virajovigatamalaṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣur viśuddham /
english: Then, both men and gods who subscribed to the Disciple Vehicle thought, “Alas! All constructed things are impermanent.” Thereby, thirtytwo thousand living beings purified their immaculate, undistorted Dharmaeye in regard to all things.

sanskrit: aṣṭānāṃ ca bhikṣusahasrāṇām anupādāyāsravebhyaś cittāni vimuktāni /
english: The eight thousand bhikṣus were liberated from their mental defilements, attaining the state of nongrasping.

sanskrit: caturaśīteś ca prāṇisahasrāṇām udārabuddhadharmādhimuktānāṃ Ō viṭhapanapratyupasthānalakṣaṇāḥ sarvadharmā iti viditvānuttarasyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpannāni // // buddhakṣetrapariśuddhinidānaparivartaḥ prathamaḥ //
english: And the eightyfour thousand living beings who were devoted to the grandeur of the buddhafield, having understood that all things are by nature but magical creations, all conceived in their own minds the spirit of unexcelled, totally perfect enlightenment. Inconceivable Skill in Liberative Art

sanskrit: Vkn  tena khalu punaḥ samayena vaiśālyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ vimalakīrtir nāma licchaviḥ prativasati sma /
english: At that time, there lived in the great city of Vaiśālī a certain Licchavi, Vimalakīrti by name.

sanskrit: pūrvajinakṛtādhikāraḥ, avaropitakuśalamūlaḥ, bahubuddhaparyupāsitaḥ,
english: Having served the ancient buddhas, he had generated the roots of virtue by honoring them and making offerings to them.

sanskrit: pratilabdhakṣāntikaḥ, labdhapratibhānaḥ,
english: He had attained tolerance as well as eloquence.

sanskrit: mahābhijñāvikrīḍitaḥ,
english: He played with the great superknowledges.

sanskrit: dhāraṇīpratilabdhaḥ, vaiśāradyaprāptaḥ, nihatamārapratyarthikaḥ,
english: He had attained the power of retention and the fearlessnesses. He had conquered all demons and opponents.

sanskrit: gambhīradharmanayasupraviṣṭaḥ,
english: He had penetrated the profound way of the Dharma.

sanskrit: prajñāpāramitānirjātaḥ,
english: He was liberated through the transcendence of wisdom.

sanskrit: pratibhānasamanvāgataḥ, satvāśayacaritakuśalaḥ, indriyaparāparajñānaniryātaḥ,
english: Having integrated his realization with skill in liberative art, he was expert in knowing the thoughts and actions of living beings.

sanskrit: yathāpratyarhadharmadeśakaḥ,
english: Knowing the strength or weakness of their faculties, and being gifted with unrivaled eloquence, he taught the Dharma appropriately to each.

sanskrit: kṛtaniścayaḥ kṛtaśrama iha mahāyāne, suparīkṣitakarmakārī,
english: Having applied himself energetically to the Mahāyāna, he understood it and accomplished his tasks with great finesse.

sanskrit: buddheryāpathapratiṣṭhitaḥ, sāgaravarabuddhyanupraviṣṭaḥ,
english: He lived with the deportment of a buddha, and his superior intelligence was as wide as an ocean.

sanskrit: sarvabuddhastutastomitapraśaṃsitaḥ, sarvaśakrabrahmalokapālanamaskṛtaḥ,
english: He was praised, honored, and commended by all the buddhas and was respected by Śakra, Brahmā, and all the Lokapālas.

sanskrit: sa satvaparipākāyopāyakauśalyena vaiśālyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ prativasati sma /
english: In order to develop living beings with his skill in liberative art, he lived in the great city of Vaiśālī.

sanskrit: Vkn  akṣayabhogo daridrānāthasatvasaṃgrahāya /
english: His wealth was inexhaustible for the purpose of sustaining the poor and the helpless.

sanskrit: pariśuddhaśīlo duḥśīlasaṃgrahāya /
english: He observed a pure morality in order to protect the immoral.

sanskrit: kṣamadamaprāpto duṣṭapraduṣṭavyāpannakrudhacittānāṃ satvānāṃ saṃgrahāya /
english: He maintained tolerance and selfcontrol in order to reconcile beings who were angry, cruel, violent, and brutal.

sanskrit: uttaptavīryaḥ kusīdānāṃ satvānāṃ saṃgrahāya /
english: He blazed with energy in order to inspire people who were lazy.

sanskrit: dhyānasmṛtisamādhisthito vibhrāntacittānāṃ satvānāṃ saṃgrahāya /
english: He maintained concentration, mindfulness, and meditation in order to sustain the mentally troubled.

sanskrit: prajñāniścayaprāpto duḥprajñānāṃ satvānāṃ saṃgrahāya /
english: He attained decisive wisdom in order to sustain the foolish.

sanskrit: Vkn  avadātavastradhārī śramaṇeryāpathasaṃpannaḥ /
english: He wore the white clothes of the layman, yet lived impeccably like a religious devotee.

sanskrit: gṛhavāsasthitaḥ kāmadhāturūpadhātvārūpyadhātvasaṃsṛṣṭaḥ /
english: He lived at home, but remained aloof from the realm of desire, the realm of pure matter, and the immaterial realm.

sanskrit: bhāryāputradārāṃś ca saṃdarśayati, sadā ca brahmacārī /
english: He had a son, a wife, and female attendants, yet always maintained continence.

sanskrit: sadā ca vivekacārī / ābharaṇavibhūṣitaś ca saṃdṛśyate, sadā ca lakṣaṇaparicchinnaḥ /
english: He appeared to be adorned with ornaments, yet always was endowed with the auspicious signs and marks.

sanskrit: annapānabhojanajīvaḥ saṃdṛśyate, sadā ca dhyānāhāraḥ /
english: He seemed to eat and drink, yet always took nourishment from the taste of meditation.

sanskrit: dyūtakrīḍāsaktacittāṃś ca satvān paripācayati, sadā cāpramādacārī / sarvapāṣaṇḍapratyeṣakaś ca /
english: He made his appearance at the fields of sports and in the casinos, but his aim was always to mature those people who were attached to games and gambling.

sanskrit: buddhe cābhedyāśayaḥ /
english: He visited the fashionable outsider teachers, yet always kept unswerving loyalty to the Buddha.

sanskrit: sarvalaukikalokottaraśāstravidhijñaś ca / sadā ca dharmārāmaratirataḥ /
english: He understood the mundane and transcendental sciences and esoteric practices, yet always took pleasure in the delights of the Dharma.

sanskrit: sarvasaṃgaṇikāsu ca saṃdṛśyate, sarvatra cāgrapūjitaḥ /
english: He mixed in all crowds, yet was respected as foremost of all.

sanskrit: Vkn  dharmavādī ca vṛddhamadhyadahrasahāyakaś ca lokānuvartanāya / sarvavyavahārodyuktaś ca na ca lābhabhogābhilāṣī /
english: In order to be in harmony with people, he associated with elders, with those of middle age, and with the young, yet always spoke in harmony with the Dharma. He engaged in all sorts of businesses, yet had no interest in profit or possessions.

sanskrit: sarvacatvaraśrṅgāṭakeṣu ca saṃdṛśyate sarvasatvavainayikatāyai / rājakāryānupraviṣṭaś ca satvārakṣāyai /
english: To educate living beings, he would appear at crossroads and on street corners, and to protect them he participated in government.

sanskrit: sarvadharmaśravaṇasāṃkathyeṣu ca saṃdṛśyate hīnayānavicchandanāya mahāyāne samādāpanatayā /
english: To turn people away from the Individual Vehicle and to engage them in the Mahāyāna, he appeared among listeners and teachers of the Dharma.

sanskrit: sarvalipiśālāsu copasaṃkrāmati dārakaparipācanāya /
english: To develop children, he visited all the schools.

sanskrit: sarvagaṇikākulāni ca praviśati kāmadoṣasaṃdarśanāya /
english: To demonstrate the evils of desire, he even entered the brothels.

sanskrit: sarvakallavālagṛhāṇi ca praviśati smṛtisaṃprajanyopasthāpanāya /
english: To establish drunkards in correct mindfulness, he entered all the drinkinghouses.

sanskrit: Vkn  śreṣṭhiṣu ca śreṣṭhisaṃmataḥ śreṣṭhadharmārocanatāyai /
english: He was honored as the merchant among merchants because he demonstrated the priority of the Dharma.

sanskrit: gṛhapatiṣu ca gṛhapatisaṃmataḥ sarvagrāhodgrahaparicchedāya / kṣatriyeṣu ca kṣatriyasaṃmataḥ kṣāntisauratyabalapratiṣṭhāpanāya /
english: He was honored as the landlord among landlords because he renounced the aggressiveness of ownership. He was honored as the warrior among warriors because he cultivated endurance, determination, and fortitude.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇeṣu ca brāhmaṇasaṃmato mānamadadarpanirghātanāya /
english: He was honored as the brahmin among brahmins because he suppressed pride, vanity, and arrogance.

sanskrit: āmātyeṣu cāmātyasaṃmataḥ sarvarājakāryasahadharmamyojanāya /
english: He was honored as the official among officials because he regulated the functions of government according to the Dharma.

sanskrit: kumāreṣu ca kumārasaṃmato rājabhogaiśvaryābhilāṣavinivartanāya / antaḥpureṣu ca kāñcukīyasaṃmataḥ strīkumārikāparipācanāya /
english: He was honored as the prince of princes because he reversed their attachment to royal pleasures and sovereign power. He was honored as a chamberlain in the royal harem because he brought the young ladies to spiritual maturity.

sanskrit: Vkn  prākṛtajanānuvartakaś ca sāmānyapuṇyaviśiṣṭādhyālaṃbanāya /
english: He was compatible with ordinary people because he appreciated the excellence of ordinary merits.

sanskrit: śakreṣu ca śakrasaṃmata aiśvaryānityatvasaṃdarśanāyau /
english: He was honored as the Śakra among Śakras because he showed them the temporality of their lordship.

sanskrit: brahmasu ca brahmasaṃmato viśeṣajñānasaṃdarśanāya /
english: He was honored as the Brahmā among Brahmās because he showed them the special excellence of gnosis.

sanskrit: lokapāleṣu ca lokapālasaṃmataḥ sarvasatvaparipālanāya /
english: He was honored as the Lokapāla among Lokapālas because he fostered the development of all living beings.

sanskrit: iti hi vimalakīrtir licchavir evam apramāṇopāyakauśalajñānasamanvāgato vaiśālyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ prativasati sma /
english: Thus lived the Licchavi Vimalakīrti in the great city of Vaiśālī, endowed with an infinite knowledge of skill in liberative arts.

sanskrit: Vkn  sa upāyakauśalyena glānam ātmānam upadarśayati sma /
english: At that time, out of this very skill in liberative art, Vimalakīrti manifested himself as if sick.

sanskrit: tasya glānasya vaiśālyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ rājarājamahāmātrāmātyakumārapāriṣadyā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ śreṣṭhinaigamajānapadās tadanyāni ca bahūni prāṇisahasrāṇi glānaparipṛcchakāny upasaṃkrāmanti sma /
english: To inquire after his health, the king, the officials, the lords, the youths, the brahmins, the householders, the businessmen, the townfolk, the countryfolk, and thousands of other living beings came forth from the great city of Vaiśālī and called on the invalid.

sanskrit: Vkn  teṣām upasaṃkrāntānāṃ vimalakīrtir licchaviḥ / imam eva cāturmahābhautikaṃ kāyam ārabhya dharmaṃ deśayati sma
english: When they arrived, Vimalakīrti taught them the Dharma, beginning his discourse from the actuality of the four main elements

sanskrit: evam anityo 'yaṃ mārṣāḥ kāyaḥ / evam adhruvaḥ,
english: “Friends, this body is so impermanent, fragile, unworthy of confidence, and feeble.

sanskrit: evaṃ durbalaḥ, evam asāraḥ / evaṃ jarjaraḥ, evam itvaraḥ, evaṃ duḥkhaḥ,
english: It is so insubstantial, perishable, shortlived, painful, filled with diseases, and subject to changes.

sanskrit: evaṃ bahurogabhājano 'yaṃ mārṣāḥ kāyaḥ / tatra paṇḍitena niśrayo na kartavyaḥ /
english: Thus, my friends, as this body is only a vessel of many sicknesses, wise men do not rely on it.

sanskrit: Vkn  phenapiṇḍopamo 'yaṃ mārṣāḥ kāyo 'parimardanakṣamaḥ / budbudopamo 'yaṃ kāyo 'cirasthitikaḥ / marīcyupamo 'yaṃ kāyaḥ kleśatṛṣṇāsaṃbhūtaḥ /
english: This body is like a ball of foam, unable to bear any pressure. It is like a water bubble, not remaining very long. It is like a mirage, born from the appetites of the passions.

sanskrit: kadalīskandhopamo 'yaṃ kāyo 'sārakatvāt / yantrabhūto batāyaṃ kāyo 'sthisnāyuvinibaddhaḥ /
english: It is like the trunk of the plantain tree, having no core. This body is like a machine, a nexus of bones and tendons.

sanskrit: māyopamo 'yaṃ kāyo viparyāsasaṃbhūtaḥ / svapnopamo 'yaṃ kāyo vitathadarśanaḥ /
english: It is like a magical illusion, consisting of falsifications. It is like a dream, being an unreal vision.

sanskrit: pratibhāsopamo 'yaṃ kāyaḥ pūrvakarmapratibhāsatayā saṃdṛśyate /
english: It is like a reflection, being the image of former actions.

sanskrit: pratiśrutkopamo 'yaṃ kāyaḥ pratyayādhīnatvāt /
english: It is like an echo, being dependent on conditioning.

sanskrit: meghopamo 'yaiḥ kāyaś cittākulavigamalakṣaṇaḥ / vidyutsadṛśo 'yaṃ kāyaḥ kṣaṇabhaṅgayukto 'navasthitaḥ /
english: It is like a cloud, being characterized by turbulence and dissolution. It is like a flash of lightning, being unstable, and decaying every moment.

sanskrit: asvāmiko 'yaṃ kāyo nānāpratyayasaṃbhūtaḥ /
english: The body is ownerless, being the product of a variety of conditions.

sanskrit: anātmo 'yaṃ kāyo 'psadṛśaḥ / nirjīvo 'yaṃ kāyas tejaḥsadṛśaḥ / niṣpudgalo 'yaṃ kāyo vāyusadṛśaḥ /
english: “This body is inert, like the earth selfless, like water lifeless, like fire impersonal, like the wind and nonsubstantial, like space.

sanskrit: niḥsvabhāvo 'yaṃ kāya ākāśasadṛśaḥ /
english: This body is unreal, being a collocation of the four main elements.

sanskrit: śūnyo 'yaṃ kāya ātmātmīyavigataḥ /
english: It is void, not existing as self or as selfpossessed.

sanskrit: jaḍo 'yaṃ kāyas tṛṇakāṣṭhakuḍyaloṣṭapratibhāsasadṛśaḥ /
english: It is inanimate, being like grass, trees, walls, clods of earth, and illusions.

sanskrit: niśceṣṭo 'yaṃ kāyo vātayantrayukto vartate /
english: It is insensate, being driven like a windmill.

sanskrit: rikto 'yaṃ kāyo 'śucipūtisaṃcayaḥ / tuccho 'yaṃ kāya ucchādanaparimardanavikiraṇavidhvansanadharmā /
english: It is filthy, being an agglomeration of pus and excrement. It is false, being fated to be broken and destroyed, in spite of being anointed and massaged.

sanskrit: upadruto 'yaṃ kāyaś caturuttaraiś caturbhī rogaśataiḥ / jīrṇodapānasadṛśo 'yaṃ kāyaḥ sadā jarābhibhūtaḥ /
english: It is afflicted by the four hundred and four diseases. It is like an ancient well, constantly overwhelmed by old age.

sanskrit: paryantasthāyī batāyaṃ kāyo maraṇaparyavasānaḥ /
english: Its duration is never certaincertain only is its end in death.

sanskrit: vadhakāśīviṣaśūnyagrāmopamo 'yaṃ kāyaḥ skandhadhātvāyatanaparigṛhītaḥ /
english: This body is a combination of aggregates, elements, and sensemedia, which are comparable to murderers, poisonous snakes, and an empty town, respectively. Therefore, you should be repelled by such a body.

sanskrit: tatra yuṣmābhir evaṃrūpe kāye nirvidvirāga utpādayitavyas tathāgatakāye ca spṛhotpādayitavyā /
english: You should despair of it and should arouse your admiration for the body of the Tathāgata.

sanskrit: Vkn  dharmakāyo hi mārṣāḥ tathāgatakāyo dānanirjātaḥ śīlanirjātaḥ samādhinirjātaḥ prajñānirjāto vimuktinirjāto vimuktijñānadarśananirjātaḥ
english: The body of a tathāgata is born of the stores of merit and wisdom. It is born of morality, of concentration, of wisdom, of the liberations, and of the knowledge and vision of liberation. It is born of love, compassion, joy, and impartiality.

sanskrit: maitrīkaruṇāmuditopekṣānirjātaḥ /
english: It is born of charity, discipline, and selfcontrol.

sanskrit: dānadamasaṃyamanirjātaḥ kṣāntisauratyanirjāto dṛḍhavīryakuśalamūlanirjāto dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattinirjātaḥ śrutaprajñopāyanirjātaḥ /
english: It is born of patience and gentleness. It is born of the roots of virtue planted by solid efforts. It is born of the concentrations, the liberations, the meditations, and the absorptions. It is born of learning, wisdom, and liberative art.

sanskrit: saptatriṃśadbodhipakṣyanirjātaḥ śamathavidarśanānirjāto daśabalanirjātaś caturvaiśāradyanirjātaḥ / aṣṭādaśāveṇikabuddhadharmanirjātaḥ sarvapāramitānirjātaḥ /
english: It is born of the thirtyseven aids to enlightenment. It is born of mental quiescence and transcendental analysis. It is born of the ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, and the eighteen special qualities. It is born of all the transcendences.

sanskrit: abhijñāvidyānirjātaḥ sarvākuśaladharmaprahāṇāya nirjātaḥ sarvakuśaladharmaparigrahanirjātaḥ satyanirjāto bhūtanirjāto 'pramādanirjātaḥ /
english: It is born from sciences and superknowledges. It is born of the abandonment of all evil qualities, and of the gathering of all good qualities. It is born of truth. It is born of reality. It is born of conscious awareness.

sanskrit: apramāṇaśubhakarmanirjāto mārṣās tathāgatakāyas tatra yuṣmābhiḥ spṛhā kartavyā /
english: “Friends, the body of a tathāgata is born of innumerable good works.

sanskrit: sarvasatvānāṃ ca sarvakleśavyādhiprahāṇāyānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpādayitavyāni /
english: Toward such a body you should turn your aspirations, and, in order to eliminate the sicknesses of the passions of all living beings, you should conceive the spirit of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.”

sanskrit: Vkn  evaṃ vimalakīrtir licchavis tathā saṃnipatitānāṃ teṣāṃ glānaparipṛcchakānāṃ tathā tathā dharmaṃ deśayati yad bahūni satvaśatasahasrāṇy anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau
english: While the Licchavi Vimalakīrti thus taught the Dharma to those who had come to inquire about his sickness, many hundreds of thousands of living beings conceived the spirit of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

sanskrit: acintyopāyakauśalyaparivarto nāma dvitīyaḥ //
english: The Disciples’ and the Bodhisattvas’ Reluctance to Visit Vimalakīrti

sanskrit: Vkn  atha vimalakīrter licchaver etad abhavat ahaṃ ca glāna ābādhiko mañcasamārūḍhaḥ, na ca māṃ tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ samanvāharati, na ca me glānaparipṛcchakaṃ kaṃcit preṣayaty anukaṃpām upādāya /
english: Then, the Licchavi Vimalakīrti thought to himself, “I am sick, lying on my bed in pain, yet the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly accomplished Buddha, does not consider me or take pity upon me, and sends no one to inquire after my illness.”

sanskrit: Vkn  samanvāhṛtaś ca bhagavatā vimalakīrtir licchaviḥ / atha bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram āmantrayate sma gaccha tvaṃ śāriputra vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
english: The Lord knew this thought in the mind of Vimalakīrti and said to the venerable Śāriputra, “Śāriputra, go to inquire after the illness of the Licchavi Vimalakīrti.”

sanskrit: evam ukta āyuṣmāñ śāriputro bhagavantam etad avocat nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: Thus addressed, the venerable Śāriputra answered the Buddha, “Lord, I am indeed reluctant to go to ask the Licchavi Vimalakīrti about his illness.

sanskrit: ekasmin samaye 'nyatamasmin vṛkṣamūle pratisaṃlīno 'bhūvam / vimalakīrtiś ca licchavir yena tad vṛkṣamūlaṃ tenopasaṃkramya mām etad avocat Vkn  na bhadantaśāriputra evaṃ pratisaṃlayanaṃ saṃlātavyaṃ yathā tvaṃ pratisaṃlīnaḥ /
english: I remember one day, when I was sitting at the foot of a tree in the forest, absorbed in contemplation, the Licchavi Vimalakīrti came to the foot of that tree and said to me, ‘Reverend Śāriputra, this is not the way to absorb yourself in contemplation.

sanskrit: api tu tathā pratisaṃlīyaś ca yathā traidhātuke na kāyaś cittaṃ vā saṃdṛśyate /
english: You should absorb yourself in contemplation so that neither body nor mind appear anywhere in the three realms.

sanskrit: tathā pratisaṃlīyaś ca yathā nirodhāc ca na vyuttiṣṭhasi sarveryāpatheṣu ca saṃdṛśyase /
english: You should absorb yourself in contemplation in such a way that you can manifest all ordinary behavior without forsaking cessation.

sanskrit: tathā pratisaṃlīyaś ca yathā te na cādhyātmaṃ cittam avasthitaṃ bhaven na bahirdhopavicaret /
english: You should absorb yourself in contemplation so that the mind neither settles within nor moves without toward external forms.

sanskrit: tathā pratisaṃlīyaś ca yathā sarvadṛṣṭigatebhyaś ca na calasi saptatriṃśatsu ca bodhipakṣyeṣu dharmeṣu saṃdṛśyase /
english: You should absorb yourself in contemplation in such a way that the thirtyseven aids to enlightenment are manifest without deviation toward any convictions.

sanskrit: tathā pratisaṃlīyaś ca yathā saṃsārāvacarāṃś ca kleśān na prajahāsi nirvāṇasamavasaraṇaś ca bhavasi /
english: You should absorb yourself in contemplation in such a way that you are released in liberation without abandoning the passions that are the province of the world.

sanskrit: ye bhadantaśāriputra evaṃ pratisaṃlayanaṃ pratisaṃlīyante teṣāṃ bhagavān pratisaṃlayanam anujānāti /
english: “ ‘Reverend Śāriputra, those who absorb themselves in contemplation in such a way are declared by the Lord to be truly absorbed in contemplation.’

sanskrit: Vkn  so 'haṃ bhagavan etāṃ śrutvā tūṣṇīm evābhūvam /
english: “Lord, when I heard this teaching, I was unable to reply and remained silent.

sanskrit: tan nāham utsahe tasya kulaputrasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: Therefore, I am reluctant to go to ask that good man about his sickness.”

sanskrit: Vkn  tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanam āmantrayate sma gaccha tvaṃ maudgalyāyana vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
english: The Buddha then said to the venerable Mahā­maudgalyāyana, “Maudgalyāyana, go to the Licchavi Vimalakīrti to inquire about his illness.”

sanskrit: maudgalyāyano 'py āha nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: Maudgalyāyana replied, “Lord, I am indeed reluctant to go to the Licchavi Vimalakīrti to inquire about his illness.

sanskrit: abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan ekasmin samaye vaiśālyāṃ mahānagaryām anyatamasmin vīthīmukhe gṛhapatibhyo dharmaṃ deśayāmi / tatra māṃ vimalakīrtir licchavir upasaṃkrāmyaivam āha
english: I remember one day when I was teaching the Dharma to the householders in a square in the great city of Vaiśālī, and the Licchavi Vimalakīrti came along and said to me, ‘Reverend Maudgalyāyana, that is not the way to teach the Dharma to the householders in their white clothes.

sanskrit: api tu tathā bhadantamaudgalyāyana dharmo deśayitavyo yathaiva sa dharmaḥ / dharmo hi bhadantamaudgalyāyana asatvaḥ satvarajovigataḥ,
english: The Dharma must be taught according to reality. “ ‘Reverend Maudgalyāyana, the Dharma is without a living being, because it is free of the dust of living beings.

sanskrit: nairātmyo rāgarajovigataḥ,
english: It is selfless, because it is free of the dust of desire.

sanskrit: nirjīvo jāticyutivigataḥ,
english: It is lifeless, because it is free of birth and death.

sanskrit: niṣpudgalaḥ pūrvāntāparāntaparicchinnaḥ,
english: It is without a person, because it dispenses with past origins and future destinies.

sanskrit: śānta upaśāntalakṣaṇaḥ,
english: “ ‘The Dharma is peace and pacification, because it is free of desire.

sanskrit: virāgo 'nārambaṇagatikaḥ, anakṣaraḥ sarvavākyacchedaḥ, anudāhāraḥ sarvormivigataḥ,
english: It does not become an object, because it is free of words and letters it is inexpressible, and it transcends all movement of mind.

sanskrit: sarvatrānugata ākāśasamasadṛśaḥ,
english: “ ‘The Dharma is omnipresent, because it is like infinite space.

sanskrit: avarṇaliṅgasaṃsthānaḥ sarvapracāravigataḥ,
english: It is without color, mark, or shape, because it is free of all process.

sanskrit: amamo mamakāravigataḥ,
english: It is without the concept of “mine,” because it is free of the habitual notion of possession.

sanskrit: avijñaptiś cittamanovijñānavigataḥ, asadṛśo niṣpratipakṣatvāt,
english: It is without ideation, because it is free of mind, thought, or consciousness.

sanskrit: hetuvilakṣaṇaḥ pratyayāsamāropaḥ,
english: It is without presumption of conditionality, because it does not conform to causes.

sanskrit: dharmadhātusamavasaraṇaḥ sarvadharmasamāhitaḥ, tathatānugato 'nanugamanayogena, bhūtakoṭipratiṣṭhito 'tyantācalitatvāt,
english: “ ‘It permeates evenly all things, because all are included in the ultimate realm. It conforms to reality by means of the process of nonconformity. It abides at the realitylimit, for it is utterly without fluctuation.

sanskrit: acalitaḥ ṣaḍviṣayāniśritatvāt,
english: It is immovable, because it is independent of the six objects of sense.

sanskrit: na kvacid gamanāgamano 'navasthitatvāt,
english: It is without coming and going, for it never stands still.

sanskrit: śūnyatāsamāhita ānimittaprabhāvito 'praṇihitalakṣaṇaḥ, ūhāpohavigataḥ,
english: It is comprised by voidness, it is remarkable through signlessness, and because of wishlessness it is free of presumption and repudiation.

sanskrit: anutkṣepo 'prakṣepaḥ, utpādabhaṅgavigataḥ,
english: It is without establishment and rejection, without birth or destruction.

sanskrit: anālayaś cakṣuḥśrotraghrāṇajihvākāyamanaḥpathasamatikrāntaḥ,
english: It is without any fundamental consciousness, transcending the range of eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and thought.

sanskrit: anunnato 'navanataḥ,
english: It is without highness and lowness.

sanskrit: sthito 'neñjyaṃ prāptaḥ, sarvapracāravigataḥ /
english: It abides without movement or activity.

sanskrit: Vkn  īdṛśasya bhadantamahāmaudgalyāyana dharmasya kīdṛśī deśanā /
english: “ ‘Reverend Mahā­maudgalyāyana, how could there be a teaching in regard to such a Dharma?

sanskrit: dharmadeśaneti bhadantamahāmaudgalyāyana samāropapadam etat / ye 'pi śṛṇvanti te 'pi samāropenaiva śṛṇvanti /
english: Reverend Mahā­maudgalyāyana, even the expression “to teach the Dharma” is presumptuous, and those who listen to it listen to presumption.

sanskrit: yatra bhadantamaudgalyāyana asamāropapadaṃ na tatra deśyate na śrūyate na vijñāyate /
english: Reverend Maudgalyāyana, where there are no presumptuous words, there is no teacher of the Dharma, no one to listen, and no one to understand.

sanskrit: tadyathā māyāpuruṣo māyāpuruṣebhyo dharmaṃ deśayati /
english: It is as if an illusory person were to teach the Dharma to illusory people.

sanskrit: Vkn  evaṃ hi cittāvasthānena dharmo deśayitavyaḥ /
english: “ ‘Therefore, you should teach the Dharma by keeping your mind on this.

sanskrit: satvendriyakuśalena ca te bhavitavyam,
english: You should be adept in regard to the spiritual faculties of living beings.

sanskrit: sudṛṣṭaprajñādarśanena mahākaruṇāmukhībhūtena mahāyānasaṃvarṇakena buddhekṛtajñena śuddhāśayena dharmaniruktividhijñena, triratnavaṃśānupacchedāya ca te dharmo deśayitavyaḥ /
english: By means of the correct vision of the wisdomeye, manifesting the great compassion, acknowledging the benevolent activity of the Buddha, purifying your intentions, and understanding the definitive expressions of the Dharma, you should teach the Dharma in order that the continuity of the Three Jewels may never be interrupted.’

sanskrit: Vkn  tena bhagavan tathā tathā dharmo deśito yathā tato gṛhapatiparsado 'ṣṭānāṃ gṛhapatiśatānām anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpannāni ahaṃ ca niṣpratibhāno 'bhūvam /
english: “Lord, when Vimalakīrti had discoursed thus, eight hundred householders in the crowd conceived the spirit of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, and I myself was speechless.

sanskrit: tan nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: Therefore, Lord, I am indeed reluctant to go to this good man to inquire about his illness.”

sanskrit: Vkn  tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ mahākāśyapam āmantrayate sma gaccha tvaṃ mahākāśyapa vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ / mahākāśyapo 'py āha
english: The Buddha then said to the venerable Mahākāśyapa, “Mahākāśyapa, you go to the Licchavi Vimalakīrti to inquire about his illness.”

sanskrit: nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: “Lord, I am indeed reluctant to go to the Licchavi Vimalakīrti to inquire about his illness.

sanskrit: tatra māṃ vimalakirtir licchavir upasaṃkramyaivam āha Vkn  prādeśikī bhadantamahākāśyapasya karuṇāmaitrī, yan mahākulāny utsṛjya daridrakulāny upasaṃkrāmasi / api tu bhadantamahākāśyapa dharmasamatāpratiṣṭhitena te bhavitavyam / sarvadā sarvasatvasamanvāhāreṇa piṇḍapātaḥ paryeṣṭavyaḥ /
english: I remember one day, when I was in the street of the poor begging for my food, the Licchavi Vimalakīrti came along and said to me, ‘Reverend Mahākāśyapa, to avoid the houses of the wealthy, and to favor the houses of the poorthis is partiality in benevolence. Reverend Mahākāśyapa, you should dwell on the fact of the equality of things, and you should seek alms with consideration for all living beings at all times.

sanskrit: anāhāreṇa cāhāraḥ paryeṣṭavyaḥ / parapiṇḍagrāhāpanayāya ca te piṇḍāya caritavyam /
english: You should beg your food in awareness of the ultimate nonexistence of food. You should seek alms for the sake of eliminating the materialism of others.

sanskrit: śūnyagrāmādhiṣṭhitena ca grāmaḥ praveṣṭavyaḥ / naranārīparipākāya ca te nagaraṃ praveṣṭavyam /
english: When you enter a town, you should keep in mind its actual voidness, yet you should proceed through it in order to develop men and women.

sanskrit: buddhakulakulīnena ca te kulāny upasaṃkramitavyāni /
english: You should enter homes as if entering the family of the Buddha.

sanskrit: Vkn  apratigrahaṇatayā ca piṇḍapātaḥ pratigrāhyaḥ /
english: You should accept alms by not taking anything.

sanskrit: jātyandhasamatayā ca rūpāṇi draṣṭavyāni / pratiśrutakopamatayā ca śabdāḥ śrotavyāḥ / vātasamatayā ca gandhā ghrātavyāḥ / avijñaptito rasā āsvādayitavyāḥ / jñānāsparśanatayā ca sparśāḥ spraṣṭavyāḥ /
english: You should see form like a man blind from birth, hear sounds as if they were echoes, smell scents as if they were like wind, experience tastes without any discrimination, touch tangible objects without there being in gnosis any contact, and know things with the consciousness of an illusory creature.

sanskrit: yo 'svabhāvo 'parabhāvaś ca tad anujjvalitam /
english: That which is without a state of being self and a state of being other does not burn.

sanskrit: yad anujjvalitaṃ tan na śāmyati /
english: And what does not burn will not be extinguished.

sanskrit: Vkn  yadi sthaviro mahākāśyapo 'ṣṭau ca mithyātvāni samatikrāmet, aṣṭau ca vimokṣān samāpadyeta, mithyāsamatayā ca samyaktvasamatām avataret, ekena ca piṇḍapātena sarvasatvān pratipādayet, sarvabuddhān sarvāryāṃś ca pratipādya paścād ātmanā paribhuñjīta,
english: “ ‘Elder Mahākāśyapa, if, equipoised in the eight liberations without transcending the eight perverse paths, you can enter the sameness of reality by means of the sameness of perversity, and if you can make a gift to all living beings and an offering to all the noble ones and buddhas out of even a single measure of alms, then you yourself may eat.

sanskrit: tathā ca paribhuñjīta yathā na saṃkleśo na vigatakleśaḥ, paribhuñjīta na samāhito na vyutthitaḥ, na saṃsārasthito na nirvāṇasthitaḥ paribhuñjīta /
english: Thus, when you eat, after offering, you should be neither affected by afflictions nor free of afflictions, neither involved in concentration nor free of concentration, neither living in the world nor abiding in liberation.

sanskrit: ye ca bhadantāya piṇḍapātaṃ dadati te teṣāṃ nālpaphalaṃ na mahāphalaiḥ bhavet /
english: Furthermore, those who give such alms, reverend, have neither great merit nor small merit, neither gain nor loss.

sanskrit: buddhagatisamavasaraṇāya ca bhaveta na śrāvakagatisamavasaraṇāya /
english: They should follow the way of the buddhas, not the way of the disciples.

sanskrit: evaṃ sthaviro mahākāśyapo 'moghaṃ rāṣṭrapiṇḍaṃ paribhuñjīta /
english: Only in this way, Elder Mahākāśyapa, is the practice of eating by alms meaningful.’

sanskrit: Vkn  so 'haṃ bhagavan imaṃ dharmanirdeśaṃ śrutvāścaryaprāptaḥ sarvabodhisatvān namasyāmi /
english: “Lord, when I heard this teaching, I was astonished and thought, ‘Reverence to all bodhisattvas!

sanskrit: ko 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittaṃ notpādayet / tataḥ prabhṛti me na kaścit satvaḥ śrāvakayāne pratyekabuddhayāne vā samādāpitapūrvo 'nyatra mahāyānāt /
english: If a lay bodhisattva may be endowed with such eloquence, who is there who would not conceive the spirit of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment?’ From that time forth, I no longer recommend the vehicles of the disciples and of the solitary sages but recommend the Mahāyāna.

sanskrit: tan nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya kulaputrasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: And thus, Lord, I am reluctant to go to this good man to inquire about his illness.”

sanskrit: Vkn  tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ subhūtim āmantrayate sma gaccha tvaṃ subhūte vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
english: The Buddha then said to the venerable Subhūti, “Subhūti, go to the Licchavi Vimalakīrti to inquire about his illness.”

sanskrit: subhūtir apy āha nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: Subhūti replied, “Lord, I am indeed reluctant to go to this good man to inquire about his illness.
