sanskrit: abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan ekasmin samaye vaiśālyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ piṇḍāya carāmi / vimalakīrter licchaver niveśanaṃ piṇḍāya praviṣṭaḥ / tasya me vimalakīrtir licchaviḥ pātraṃ gṛhītvā praṇītena bhojanena pratipūryaivam āha Vkn  sacet tvaṃ bhadantasubhūte āmiṣasamatayā sarvadharmasamatām anugataḥ sarvadharmasamatayā ca buddhadharmasamatām anugata eva,
english: My Lord, I remember one day, when I went to beg my food at the house of the Licchavi Vimalakīrti in the great city of Vaiśālī, he took my bowl and filled it with some excellent food and said to me, ‘Reverend Subhūti, take this food if you understand the sameness of all things through the sameness of material objects, and if you understand the sameness of the qualities of the Buddha through the sameness of all things.

sanskrit: na ca te 'vidyā bhavatṛṣṇā ca samudghātitā na ca vidyāvimuktī utpādite / ānantaryasamatayā ca te samādhivimuktiḥ / na cāsi mukto na baddhaḥ / na ca te catvāry āryasatyāni dṛṣṭāni na ca na dṛṣṭasatyaḥ / na prāptaphalo na pṛthagjanasamavasaraṇaḥ /
english: Take this food if, without abandoning desire, hatred, and folly, you can avoid association with them if you can follow the path of the single way without ever disturbing the egoistic views if, neither conquering ignorance and the craving for existence, nor producing knowledge and liberation, your liberation being the same as the equality of the uninterruptible sins, you are neither liberated nor bound if you do not see the four noble truths, yet are not one who “has not seen the truth” if you are also neither “one who has attained fruition,” nor “an ordinary person,” while not having eliminated the qualities of “an ordinary person” if you are not a noble one, and not a nonnoble one and if, though you are in the presence of all things, you are free of any notion of “all things.”

sanskrit: Vkn  na ca te śāstā dṛṣṭo na dharmaḥ śruto na saṃghaḥ paryupāsitaḥ / ye ca te ṣaṭ śāstāras tadyathā pūraṇaḥ kāśyapaḥ, maskarī gośālīputraḥ, saṃjayo vairāṣṭrikaputraḥ, kakudaḥ kātyāyanaḥ,
english: “ ‘Take this food, reverend Subhūti, if, without seeing the Buddha, hearing the Dharma, or serving the Saṅgha, you undertake the religious life under the six outsider mastersnamely, Purāṇa Kāśyapa, Māskārin Gośāli­putra, Saṃjāyin Vairaṭi­putra, Kakuda Kātyāyana, Ajita Keśakambala, and Nirgrantha Jñāti­putra, and follow the ways they prescribe.

sanskrit: te ca bhadantasya śāstāras tāṃś ca niśritya pravrajito yadgāminas te ṣaṭ śāstāras tadgāmy evāryasubhūtiḥ, Vkn  sarvadṛṣṭigateṣu cāryaman antargato na cāntamadhyaprāptaḥ, aṣṭākṣaṇasamavasaraṇaś cāsi na cāsi lakṣaṇam anuprāptaḥ, saṃkleśena cāsi samo 'vyavadānam adhigataḥ, yā ca sarvasatvānām araṇā sā bhadantasyāpy araṇā,
english: “ ‘Take this food, reverend Subhūti, if, entertaining all false views, you find neither extremes nor middle if, bound up in the eight adversities, you do not obtain favorable conditions if, assimilating the passions, you do not attain purification if the dispassion of all living beings is your dispassion, reverend if those who make offerings to you are not thereby purified if those who offer you food, reverend, still fall into the three bad migrations if you associate with all māras if you entertain all passions if the nature of passions is the nature of a reverend if you have hostile feelings toward all living beings if you despise all the buddhas if you criticize all the teachings of the Buddha if you do not rely on the saṅgha and finally, if you never enter ultimate liberation.’

sanskrit: Vkn  tasya me bhagavan imaṃ dharmanirdeśaṃ śrutvāndhakāraprāptā diśo 'bhūvan ḥ tat kim asmai nirdiśāmi, katham vā pratipadya iti /
english: “Lord, when I heard these words of the Licchavi Vimalakīrti, I wondered what I should say and what I should do, but I was totally in the dark.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ tat pātram utsṛjya tato gṛhān niṣkramiṣyāmīti / vimalakīrtir Iicchavir mām evam āha mā bhadantasubhūte akṣarebhya uttrasīḥ,
english: Leaving the bowl, I was about to leave the house when the Licchavi Vimalakīrti said to me, ‘Reverend Subhūti, do not fear these words, and pick up your bowl.

sanskrit: tat kiṃ manyase bhadantasubhūte,
english: What do you think, reverend Subhūti?

sanskrit: yadi tathāgatanirmita evam ucyeta kaccit sa uttraset / so 'ham avocam
english: If it were an incarnation created by the Tathāgata who spoke thus to you, would you be afraid?’

sanskrit: no hīdaṃ kulaputra / sa mām evam āha nirmitamāyāsvabhāvebhyo bhadantasubhūte sarvadharmebhyo nottrasitavyam /
english: “I answered, ‘No indeed, noble sir!’ He then said, ‘Reverend Subhūti, the nature of all things is like illusion, like a magical incarnation.

sanskrit: tat kasmād dhetoḥ /
english: So you should not fear them.

sanskrit: sarvāṇi hi tāni vacanāni tatsvabhāvāni, evaṃ paṇḍitā akṣareṣu na sajjanti na tebhya uttrasyanti /
english: All words also have that nature, and thus the wise are not attached to words, nor do they fear them.

sanskrit: sarvāṇi tāny akṣarāṇy anakṣarāṇi sthāpayitvā vimuktiṃ vimuktilakṣaṇāṃś ca sarvadharmān /
english: All language does not ultimately exist, except as liberation. The nature of all things is liberation.’

sanskrit: Vkn  iha nirdeśe nirdiśyamāne dvayor devaputraśatayor virajo vigatamalaṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣur viśuddham, pañcānāṃ ca devaputraśatānām ānulomikyāḥ kṣānteḥ pratilambho 'bhūt /
english: “When Vimalakīrti had discoursed in this way, two hundred gods obtained the pure doctrinal vision in regard to all things, without obscurity or defilement, and five hundred gods obtained the conformative tolerance.

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca niṣpratibhāno 'bhūvam,
english: As for me, I was speechless and unable to respond to him.

sanskrit: tan nāham utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: Therefore, Lord, I am reluctant to go to this good man to inquire about his illness.”

sanskrit: Vkn  atha khalu bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ pūrṇaṃ maitrāyaṇīputram āmantrayate sma gaccha tvaṃ pūrṇa vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
english: The Buddha then said to the venerable Pūrṇa­maitrāyaṇī­putra, “Pūrṇa, go to the Licchavi Vimalakīrti to inquire about his illness.”

sanskrit: pūrṇo 'py āha nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: Pūrṇa replied, “Lord, I am indeed reluctant to go to this good man to inquire about his illness.

sanskrit: abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan ekasmin samaye vanasyānyatamasmin pṛthivīpradeśa ādikarmikāṇāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ dharmaṃ deśayāmi / tatra vimalakīrtir licchavir upasaṃkramya mām evam āha Vkn  samāpadya bhadantapūrṇa eteṣāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ cittaṃ vyavalokya dharmaṃ deśaya /
english: Lord, I remember one day, when I was teaching the Dharma to some young monks in the great forest, the Licchavi Vimalakīrti came there and said to me, ‘Reverend Pūrṇa, first concentrate yourself, regard the minds of these young bhikṣus, and then teach them the Dharma!

sanskrit: mā mahāratnabhājaneṣu prati kulmāṣān prākṣaipsīḥ /
english: Do not put rotten food into a jeweled bowl!

sanskrit: jāniṣva tāvat kimāśayā ete bhikṣava iti / mā vaiḍūryaratnaṃ kācamaṇikaiḥ samānīkārṣīḥ /
english: First understand the inclinations of these monks, and do not confuse priceless sapphires with glass beads!

sanskrit: mā bhadantapūrṇa apratyavekṣyā satvendriyeṣu prādeśikendriyatvam upasaṃhārṣīḥ / mā akṣatāṃ kṣiṇuṣva / mā mahāmārgam avatartukāmān bhandarathyāṃ praveśaya / mā mahāsāgaraṃ goṣpade praveśaya / mā sūryaprabhāṃ khadyotakair nirvartaya /
english: “ ‘Reverend Pūrṇa, without examining the spiritual faculties of living beings, do not presume upon the onesidedness of their faculties do not wound those who are without wounds do not impose a narrow path upon those who aspire to a great path do not try to pour the great ocean into the hoofprint of an ox do not try to put Mount Sumeru into a grain of mustard do not confuse the brilliance of the sun with the light of a glowworm and do not expose those who admire the roar of a lion to the howl of a jackal!

sanskrit: api bhadantapūrṇa sarve hy ete bhikṣavo mahāyānasaṃprasthitā amuṣitabodhicittāḥ /
english: “ ‘Reverend Pūrṇa, all these monks were formerly engaged in the Mahāyāna but have forgotten the spirit of enlightenment.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ bhadantapūrṇa mā śrāvakayānam upadarśaya /
english: So do not instruct them in the Disciple Vehicle.

sanskrit: kaṣṭaṃ hi śrāvakayānam / jātyandhā iva me śrāvakāḥ pratibhānti satvendriyavimātratājñāne /
english: The Disciple Vehicle is not ultimately valid, and you disciples are like men blind from birth, in regard to recognition of the degrees of the spiritual faculties of living beings.’

sanskrit: Vkn  atha vimalakīrtir licchavis tasyāṃ velāyāṃ tathārūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpadyate sma / yathā te bhikṣavo 'nekavidhaṃ pūrvenivāsam anusmaraṇti sma / te pañcabuddhaśataparyupāsitakuśalamūlāḥ samyaksaṃbodhaye,
english: “At that moment, the Licchavi Vimalakīrti entered into such a concentration that those monks were caused to remember their various former lives, in which they had produced the roots of virtue by serving five hundred buddhas for the sake of perfect enlightenment.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tad bodhicittam āmukhībhūtam / te tasya satpuruṣasya pādau śirobhiḥ praṇamya tatraiva niṣaṇṇāḥ prāñjalayo bhūtvā,
english: As soon as their own spirits of enlightenment had become clear to them, they bowed at the feet of that good man and pressed their palms together in reverence.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tādṛśī dharmadeśanā kṛtā yathāvaivartikāḥ saṃvṛttā anuttarasyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau /
english: He taught them the Dharma, and they all attained the stage of irreversibility from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

sanskrit: Vkn  tan nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: These disciples are not expert in discerning the superiority and inferiority of the spiritual faculties of living beings, and they are not always in a state of concentration like the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly accomplished Buddha.’ Therefore, Lord, I am reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his health.”

sanskrit: Vkn  tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ kātyāyanam āmantrayate sma gaccha tvaṃ kātyāyana vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
english: The Buddha then said to the venerable Mahākātyāyana, “Kātyāyana, go to the Licchavi Vimalakīrti to inquire about his illness.”

sanskrit: kātyāyano 'py āha nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: Kātyāyana replied, “Lord, I am indeed reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.

sanskrit: abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan bhagavatā saṃkṣiptena bhikṣūṇām avavādo dattaḥ / teṣāṃ sūtrapadaviniścayāya dharmaṃ deśayāmi, yad idam anityārthaṃ duḥkhārtham anātmārthaṃ śāntārtham / tatra vimalakīrtir licchavir upasaṃkramya mām evam āha
english: Lord, I remember one day when, after the Lord had given some brief instruction to the monks, I was defining the expressions of that discourse by teaching the meaning of impermanence, suffering, selflessness, and peace, the Licchavi Vimalakīrti came there and said to me, ‘Reverend Mahākātyāyana, do not teach an ultimate reality endowed with activity, production, and destruction!

sanskrit: yo bhadantamahākātyāyana atyantatayā na jāto na janiṣyati notpanno na niruddho na nirotsyate 'yam anityārthaḥ /
english: Reverend Mahākātyāyana, nothing was ever destroyed, is destroyed, or will ever be destroyed.

sanskrit: yaḥ pañcānāṃ skandhānāṃ śūnyatānugamānutpādānirodhārtho 'yaṃ duḥkhārthaḥ / yad ātmānātmayor advayatvam ayam anātmārthaḥ / yo 'svabhāvo 'parabhāvas tad anujjvalitam, yad anujvalitaṃ na tac chāmyati, yo 'tyantopaśamo 'yaṃ śāntārthaḥ /
english: Such is the meaning of “impermanence.” The meaning of the realization of birthlessness, through the realization of the voidness of the five aggregates, is the meaning of “suffering.” The fact of the nonduality of self and selflessness is the meaning of “selflessness.” That which has no intrinsic substance and no other sort of substance does not burn, and what does not burn is not extinguished such lack of extinction is the meaning of “peace.” ’

sanskrit: Vkn  asmin khalu punar nirdeśe nirdiśyamāne teṣāṃ bhikṣūṇām anupādāyāsravebhyaś cittāni vimuktāni /
english: “When he had discoursed thus, the minds of the monks were liberated from their defilements and entered a state of nongrasping.

sanskrit: tan nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: Therefore, Lord, I am reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.”

sanskrit: Vkn  tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam aniruddham āmantrayate sma gaccha tvam aniruddha vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ / aniruddho 'py āha
english: The Buddha then said to the venerable Aniruddha, “Aniruddha, go to the Licchavi Vimalakīrti to inquire about his illness.”

sanskrit: nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: “My Lord, I am indeed reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.

sanskrit: Vkn  abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan anyatamasmiṃś caṅkrame caṅkramāmi / tatra śubhavyūho nāma brahmā daśabhir brahmasahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ taṃ pradeśam avabhāsya yenāhaṃ tenopasaṃkramya mama pādau śirasābhivandyaikānte sthitvā mām etad avocat kiyad āyuṣmān aniruddho divyena cakṣuṣā paśyati /
english: I remember, Lord, one day when I was taking a walk, the great Brahmā named Śubhavyūha and the ten thousand other Brahmās who accompanied him illuminated the place with their radiance and, having bowed their heads at my feet, withdrew to one side and asked me, ‘Reverend Aniruddha, you have been proclaimed by the Buddha to be the foremost among those who possess the divine eye.

sanskrit: ahaṃ mārṣa imaṃ triṃ sāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātuṃ bhagavataḥ śākyamuner buddhakṣetraṃ tad yathāpi nāma karatale nyastam āmalakaphalam evaṃ paśyāmi / Vkn  iyaṃ ca kathā pravṛttā vimalakīrtiś ca licchavis taṃ pradeśam upasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya mama pādau śirasā vanditvaivam āha kiṃ bhadantāniruddha divyaṃ cakṣur abhisaṃskāralakṣaṇam utānabhisaṃskāralakṣaṇam /
english: To what distance does the divine vision of the venerable Aniruddha extend?’ I answered, ‘Friends, I see the entire billionworld galactic universe of the Lord Śākyamuni just as plainly as a man of ordinary vision sees a myrobalan nut on the palm of his hand.’ When I had said these words, the Licchavi Vimalakīrti came there and, having bowed his head at my feet, said to me, ‘Reverend Aniruddha, is your divine eye compounded in nature? Or is it uncompounded in nature?

sanskrit: yady abhisaṃskāralakṣaṇaṃ tad bāhyaiḥ pañcābhijñaiḥ samam,
english: If it is compounded in nature, it is the same as the superknowledges of the outsiders.

sanskrit: athānabhisaṃskāralakṣaṇaṃ anabhisaṃskāro 'saṃskṛtas tena na śakyaṃ draṣṭum / tat kathaṃ sthaviraḥ paśyati /
english: If it is uncompounded in nature, then it is not constructed and, as such, is incapable of seeing. Then, how do you see, O elder?’

sanskrit: so 'haṃ tūṣṇīm abhūvam / Vkn  sa ca brahmā tasya satpuruṣasyemaṃ nirdeśaṃ śrutvāścaryaprāptas taṃ namaskṛtyaitad avocat
english: “At these words, I became speechless, and Brahmā also was amazed to hear this teaching from that good man.

sanskrit: ke loke divyacakṣuṣaḥ /
english: Having bowed to him, he said, ‘Who then, in the world, possesses the divine eye?’

sanskrit: āha buddhā bhagavanto loke divyacakṣuṣo ye samāhitāvasthāṃ ca na vijahati sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇi ca paśyanti / na ca dvayaprabhāvitāḥ /
english: “Vimalakīrti answered, ‘In the world, it is the buddhas who have the divine eye. They see all the buddhafields without even leaving their state of concentration and without being affected by duality.’

sanskrit: Vkn  atha sa brahmemaṃ nirdeśaṃ śrutvā daśasahasraparivāro 'dhyāśayenānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittam utpādayati sma /
english: “Having heard these words, the ten thousand Brahmās were inspired with high resolve and conceived the spirit of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

sanskrit: sa māṃ vanditvā taṃ ca satpuruṣam abhivādya tatraivāntarhitaḥ /
english: Having paid homage and respect both to me and to that good man, they disappeared.

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca niṣpratibhāno 'bhūvam / tan nāham utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: As for me, I remained speechless, and therefore I am reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.”

sanskrit: Vkn  tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam upālim āmantrayate sma gaccha tvam upāle vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
english: The Buddha then said to the venerable Upāli, “Upāli, go to the Licchavi Vimalakīrti to inquire about his illness.”

sanskrit: upālir apy āha nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: Upāli replied, “Lord, I am indeed reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.

sanskrit: abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan anyatamau dvau bhikṣū āpattim āpannau, tau bhagavataḥ paryapatrapamāṇau bhagavantaṃ nopasaṃkrāmataḥ / tau yenāhaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntāv upasaṃkrāmya mām etad avocatām /
english: Lord, I remember that one day there were two monks who had committed some infraction and were too ashamed to appear before the Lord, so they came to me and said, ‘Reverend Upāli, we have both committed an infraction but are too ashamed to appear before the Buddha.

sanskrit: tāv āvāṃ paryapatrapamāṇau bhagavantam upasaṃkramituṃ notsahāvahe /
english: Venerable Upāli, kindly remove our anxieties by absolving us of these infractions.’

sanskrit: Vkn  so 'haṃ bhagavaṃs tau bhikṣū dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayāmi / vimalakīrtiś ca licchavis taṃ pradeśam anuprāptaḥ sa mām etad avocat mā bhadantopāle etau bhikṣū āgāḍhīkārṣīḥ,
english: “Lord, while I was giving those two monks some religious discourse, the Licchavi Vimalakīrti came there and said to me, ‘Reverend Upāli, do not aggravate further the sins of these two monks.

sanskrit: vinodayānayor āpattim, mā āvilīkārṣīḥ /
english: Without perplexing them, relieve their remorse.

sanskrit: na hi bhadantopāle āpattir adhyātmapratiṣṭhitā na bahirdhāsaṃkrānto nobhayam antareṇopalabhyate /
english: Reverend Upāli, sin is not to be apprehended within, or without, or between the two.

sanskrit: uktaṃ hi bhagavatā cittasaṃkleśāt satvāḥ saṃkliśyante cittavyavadānād viśudhyante /
english: The Buddha has said, “Living beings are afflicted by the passions of thought, and they are purified by the purification of thought.”

sanskrit: cittaṃ ca bhadantopāle nādhyātmapratiṣṭhitaṃ na bahirdhā nobhayam antareṇopalabhyate /
english: “ ‘Reverend Upāli, the mind is neither within nor without, nor is it to be apprehended between the two.

sanskrit: yathā cittaṃ tathāpattiḥ, yathāpattis tathā sarvadharmāḥ,
english: Sin is just the same as the mind, and all things are just the same as sin.

sanskrit: tathatāṃ na vyativartante /
english: They do not escape this same reality.

sanskrit: yā bhadantopāle cittasya prakṛtir yayā cittaprakṛtyā bhadantasya cittaṃ vimuktam, kiṃ jātu sā cittaprakṛtiḥ saṃkliṣṭā /
english: “ ‘Reverend Upāli, this nature of the mind, by virtue of which your mind, reverend, is liberateddoes it ever become afflicted?’

sanskrit: āha no hidam /
english: “ ‘Never,’ I replied.

sanskrit: āha tatprakṛtikāni bhadantopāle sarvasatvānāṃ cittāni /
english: “ ‘Reverend Upāli, the minds of all living beings have that very nature.

sanskrit: Vkn  saṃkalpo bhadantopāle kleśaḥ / akalpāvikalpā ca prakṛtiḥ / viparyāsaḥ saṃkleśaḥ, aviparyastā ca prakṛtiḥ /
english: Reverend Upāli, conceptualization is total affliction, and not conceptualizing and not discriminating is their true nature. Misapprehension is total affliction, and nonmisapprehension is their true nature.

sanskrit: ātmasamāropaḥ saṃkleśaḥ, nairātmyā ca prakṛtiḥ /
english: The presumption of self is total affliction, and selflessness is their true nature.

sanskrit: utpannabhagnānavasthitā bhadantopāle sarvadharmā māyāmeghavidyutsadṛśāḥ / nirapekṣāḥ sarvadharmāḥ kṣaṇam api nāvatiṣṭhante / svapnamarīcisadṛśāḥ sarvadharmā vitathadarśanāḥ / dakacandrapratibimbasadṛśāḥ sarvadharmāś cittaparikalpenotpadyante /
english: Reverend Upāli, all things are without production, destruction, and duration, like magical illusions, clouds, and lightning all things are evanescent, not remaining even for an instant all things are like dreams, hallucinations, and unreal visions all things are like the reflection of the moon in water and like a mirrorimage they are born of mental construction.

sanskrit: ye tv evaṃ jānanti te vinayadharā ity ucyante / ya evaṃ vinītās te suvinītāḥ /
english: Those who know this are called the true upholders of the discipline, and those disciplined in that way are indeed well disciplined.’ ”

sanskrit: Vkn  atha tau bhikṣu etad avocatām prajñādharo vinayadharo 'yam upāsakaḥ /
english: “Then the two monks said, ‘This householder is extremely well endowed with wisdom.

sanskrit: na tv ayaṃ bhadantopālir yo bhagavatā vinayadharāṇām agro nirdiṣṭaḥ /
english: The reverend Upāli, who was proclaimed by the Lord as the foremost of the upholders of the discipline, is not his equal.’

sanskrit: tāv aham evaṃ vadāmi mā bhikṣū atra gṛhapatisaṃjñām utpādayatām /
english: “I then said to the two monks, ‘Do not entertain the notion that he is a mere householder!

sanskrit: tathāgataṃ sthāpayitvā nāsti kaścic chrāvako vā bodhisatvo vā, ya etasya pratibhānam ācchindyāt / tādṛśa etasya prajñālokaḥ /
english: With the exception of the Tathāgata himself, there is no disciple or bodhisattva capable of competing with his eloquence or rivaling the brilliance of his wisdom.’

sanskrit: Vkn  atha tau bhikṣū vinītakaukṛtyāv adhyāśayena tatraivānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittam utpāditavantau,
english: “Thereupon, the two monks, delivered from their anxieties and inspired with a high resolve, conceived the spirit of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

sanskrit: taṃ ca satpuruṣam abhivandyaivam āhatuḥ
english: Bowing down to that good man, they made the wish

sanskrit: sarvasatvā īdṛśasya pratibhānasya lābhino bhavantu / tan nāham utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: ‘May all living beings attain eloquence such as this!’ Therefore, I am reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.”

sanskrit: Vkn  tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ rāhulam āmantrayate sma gaccha tvaṃ rāhula vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
english: The Buddha then said to the venerable Rāhula, “Rāhula, go to the Licchavi Vimalakīrti to inquire about his illness.”

sanskrit: rāhulo 'py āha nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: Rāhula replied, “Lord, I am indeed reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.

sanskrit: abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan ekasmin samaye saṃbahulā licchavikumārakā yenāhaṃ tenopasaṃkramya mām etad avocan tvaṃ rāhula tasya bhagavataḥ putraś cakravartirājyam utsṛjya pravrajitaḥ,
english: Lord, I remember that one day many young Licchavi gentlemen came to the place where I was and said to me, ‘Reverend Rāhula, you are the son of the Lord, and, having renounced a kingdom of a universal monarch, you have left the world.

sanskrit: tatra ke te pravrajyāyā guṇānuśaṃsāḥ /
english: What are the virtues and benefits you saw in leaving the world?’

sanskrit: teṣām ahaṃ yathārūpaṃ pravrajyāyā guṇānuśaṃsā nirdiśāmi, vimalakīrtir licchavir yenāhaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / sa mām abhivandyaitad avocat Vkn  na bhadantarāhula evaṃ pravrajyāyā guṇānuśaṃsā nirdeṣṭavyā yathā tvaṃ nirdiśasi /
english: “As I was teaching them properly the benefits and virtues of renouncing the world, the Licchavi Vimalakīrti came there and, having greeted me, said, ‘Reverend Rāhula, you should not teach the benefits and virtues of renunciation in the way that you do.

sanskrit: nirguṇā niranuśaṃsā hi pravrajyā /
english: Renunciation is itself the very absence of virtues and benefits.

sanskrit: yatra bhadantarāhula saṃskṛtapravṛttis tatra guṇānuśaṃsā / pravrajyā cāsaṃskṛtā, asaṃskṛte ca na guṇā nānuśāṃsā /
english: Reverend Rāhula, one may speak of benefits and virtues in regard to compounded things, but renunciation is uncompounded, and there can be no question of benefits and virtues in regard to the uncompounded.

sanskrit: pravrajyā bhadantarāhula arūpiṇi rūpavigatā, panthā nirvāṇasya,
english: It is free of the extreme views of beginning and end. It is the path of liberation.

sanskrit: praśaṃsitā paṇḍitaiḥ, parigṛhītāryaiḥ, parājayaḥ sarvamārāṇām,
english: It is praised by the wise, embraced by the noble ones, and causes the defeat of all māras.

sanskrit: pañcagatyuttāraṇī, pañcacakṣuviśodhanī, pañcabalapratilambhā, pañcendriyapratiṣṭhā,
english: It liberates from the five states of existence, purifies the five eyes, cultivates the five powers, and supports the five spiritual faculties.

sanskrit: pareṣām anupaghātaḥ, pāpadharmāsaṃsṛṣṭā,
english: Renunciation is totally harmless to others and is not adulterated with evil things.

sanskrit: paratīrthyapramardanī, prajñaptisamatikrāntā,
english: It disciplines the outsiders, transcending all denominations.

sanskrit: paṅke saṃkramaḥ, amamā mamakāravigatā, aparigrahā, anupādānā, anākulā,
english: It is the bridge over the swamp of desire, without grasping, and free of the habits of “I” and “mine.” It is without attachment and without disturbance, eliminating all commotion.

sanskrit: ākulaprahīṇā, svacittadarśanī paracittasaṃrakṣaṇī, śamathānukūlā,
english: It disciplines one’s own mind and protects the minds of others. It favors mental quiescence and stimulates transcendental analysis.

sanskrit: sarvato 'navadyā / iyam ucyate pravrajyā /
english: It is irreproachable in all respects and so is called renunciation.

sanskrit: ya evaṃ pravrajitās te supravrajitāḥ / Vkn  pravrajata yūyaṃ kumārakāḥ svākhyāte dharmavinaye /
english: Those who leave the mundane in this way are called “truly renunciant.” Young men, renounce the world in the light of this clear teaching!

sanskrit: durlabho hi buddhotpādaḥ,
english: The appearance of the Buddha is extremely rare.

sanskrit: durlabhā kṣaṇasaṃpat, durlabho manuṣyapratilambhaḥ /
english: Human life endowed with leisure and opportunity is very hard to obtain. To be a human being is very precious.’

sanskrit: te kumārakā evam āhuḥ śrutam asmābhir gṛhapate, na tathāgato 'navasṛṣṭaṃ mātāpitṛbhyāṃ pravrājayatīti /
english: “The young men complained, ‘But, householder, we have heard the Tathāgata declare that one should not renounce the world without the permission of one’s parents.’

sanskrit: sa tān āha utpādayata yūyaṃ kumārakāḥ anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittam / pratipattyā ca saṃpādayata,
english: “Vimalakīrti answered, ‘Young men, you should cultivate yourselves intensively to conceive the spirit of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

sanskrit: saiva yuṣmākaṃ bhaviṣyati pravrajyā sopasaṃpat /
english: That in itself will be your renunciation and high ordination!’

sanskrit: Vkn  tatra dvātriṃśatā licchavikumārair anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpāditāni /
english: “Thereupon, thirtytwo of the Licchavi youths conceived the spirit of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

sanskrit: tan nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: Therefore, Lord, I am reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.”

sanskrit: Vkn  tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate sma gaccha tvam ānanda vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
english: The Buddha then said to the venerable Ānanda, “Ānanda, go to the Licchavi Vimalakīrti to inquire about his illness.”

sanskrit: ānanda āha nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: Ānanda replied, “Lord, I am indeed reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.

sanskrit: tatra ca kṣīreṇa kṛtyam āsīt / so 'ham anyatamasmin brāhmaṇamahāśālasya gṛhamūle pātraṃ gṛhītvā sthitaḥ / vimalakīrtir licchavis taṃ pradeśam anuprāptaḥ / sa māṃ vanditvaivam āha Vkn  kiṃ bhadantānanda kālyam eva pātram ādāyāsmin gṛhadvārasamīpe tiṣṭhasi /
english: Lord, I remember one day when the body of the Lord manifested some indisposition and he required some milk I took the bowl and went to the door of the mansion of a great brahmin family. The Licchavi Vimalakīrti came there, and, having saluted me, said, ‘Reverend Ānanda, what are you doing on the threshold of this house with your bowl in your hand so early in the morning?’

sanskrit: tam enam aham etad avocam bhagavato gṛhapate kāyasya kaścid evābādhaḥ /
english: “I replied, ‘The body of the Lord manifests some indisposition, and he needs some milk.

sanskrit: tat paryeṣāmi /
english: Therefore, I have come to fetch some.’

sanskrit: sa mām evam āha alaṃ bhadantānanda mā evaṃ vocaḥ /
english: “Vimalakīrti then said to me, ‘Reverend Ānanda, do not say such a thing!

sanskrit: vajrasaṃhatano hi bhadantānanda tathāgatakāyaḥ sarvākuśalavāsanāprahīṇaḥ sarvamahaujaskakuśaladharmasamanvāgataḥ /
english: Reverend Ānanda, the body of the Tathāgata is tough as a diamond, having eliminated all the instinctual traces of evil and being endowed with all goodness.

sanskrit: kutas tasya vyādhiḥ kuta upadravaḥ /
english: How could disease or discomfort affect such a body?

sanskrit: Vkn  tūṣṇīṃbhūto bhadantānanda gaccha / mā bhagavantam abhyācakṣva /
english: “ ‘Reverend Ānanda, go in silence, and do not belittle the Lord.

sanskrit: mā kasyacid bhūya evaṃ vocaḥ /
english: Do not say such things to others.

sanskrit: mā mahaujaskā devaputrā anyabuddhakṣetrasaṃnipatitāś ca bodhisatvāḥ śroṣyanti /
english: It would not be good for the powerful gods or for the bodhisattvas coming from the various buddhafields to hear such words.

sanskrit: rājñas tāvad bhadantānanda cakravartina itvarakuśalamūlasamanvāgatasya vyādhir na saṃvidyate /
english: “ ‘Reverend Ānanda, a universal monarch, who is endowed only with a small root of virtue, is free of diseases.

sanskrit: kutas tasya bhagavato 'pramāṇakuśalasamanvāgatasya vyādhir bhaviṣyati /
english: How then could the Lord, who has an infinite root of virtue, have any disease?

sanskrit: nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate /
english: It is impossible.

sanskrit: gaccha gaccha bhadantānanda / mā mām adhyapatrāpaya, mā anyatīrthikacarakaparivrājakanigranthājīvāḥ śroṣyanti,
english: “ ‘Reverend Ānanda, do not bring shame upon us, but go in silence, lest the outsider sectarians should hear your words.

sanskrit: mā teṣām evaṃ bhaviṣyati /
english: They would say, “For shame!

sanskrit: kīdṛśo bata ayam eṣāṃ śāstā yaḥ svayam eva tāvad ātmānaṃ glānaṃ na śaknoti paritrātum,
english: The teacher of these people cannot even cure his own sicknesses.

sanskrit: tataḥ pracchannaṃ bhadantānanda gaccha śīghram / mā kaścic chṛṇuyāt /
english: How then can he cure the sicknesses of others?” Reverend Ānanda, go then discreetly so that no one observes you.

sanskrit: Vkn  api tu bhadantānanda dharmakāyās tathāgatā nāmiṣakāyāḥ /
english: “ ‘Reverend Ānanda, the tathāgatas have the body of the Dharmanot a body that is sustained by material food.

sanskrit: lokottarakāyās tathāgatāḥ sarvalokadharmasamatikrāntāḥ /
english: The tathāgatas have a transcendental body that has transcended all mundane qualities.

sanskrit: anābādhas tathāgatasya kāyaḥ sarvāsravavinivṛtaḥ / asaṃskṛtas tathāgatasya kāyaḥ sarvasaṃkhyāvigataḥ /
english: There is no injury to the body of a tathāgata, as it is rid of all defilements. The body of a tathāgata is uncompounded and free of all formative activity.

sanskrit: tasya bhadanto vyādhim icchatīty ayuktam asadṛśam /
english: Reverend Ānanda, to believe there can be illness in such a body is irrational and unseemly!’

sanskrit: Vkn  tasya me bhagavan mahadapatrāpyaṃ jātam / mā me bhagavato 'ntikād duḥśrutaṃ durgṛhītaṃ vā kṛtam iti /
english: “When I had heard these words, I wondered if I had previously misheard and misunderstood the Buddha, and I was very much ashamed.

sanskrit: so 'ham antarīkṣāc chabdam aśrauṣam /
english: Then I heard a voice from the sky

sanskrit: evam etad ānanda yathā gṛhapatir nirdiśati /
english: ‘Ānanda! The householder speaks to you truly.

sanskrit: atha ca punaḥ pañcakaṣāye bhagavān utpannaḥ, tenānarthalūhadaridracaryayā satvā vinetavyāḥ /
english: Nevertheless, since the Buddha has appeared during the time of the five corruptions, he disciplines living beings by acting lowly and humble.

sanskrit: tad gaccha tvam ānanda kṣīraṃ gṛhītvā, mā paryapatrapaś ceti /
english: Therefore, Ānanda, do not be ashamed, and go and get the milk!’

sanskrit: Vkn  īdṛśā bhagavan vimalakīrter licchaveḥ praśnavyākaraṇanirdeśāḥ / tan nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya kulaputrasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: “Lord, such was my conversation with the Licchavi Vimalakīrti, and therefore I am reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.”

sanskrit: Vkn  evaṃ tāni pañcamātrāṇi śrāvakaśatāny anutsahamānāni bhagavate nivedayanti / ye ca tair vimalakīrtinā licchavinā sārdhaṃ kathāsaṃlāpāḥ kṛtās tān sarvān bhagavate nivedayanti sma /
english: In the same way, the rest of the five hundred disciples were reluctant to go to the Licchavi Vimalakīrti, and each told the Buddha his own adventure, recounting all his conversations with the Licchavi Vimalakīrti.

sanskrit: Vkn  tatra bhagavān maitreyaṃ bodhisatvam āmantrayate sma gaccha tvaṃ maitreya vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
english: The Buddha then said to the bodhisattva Maitreya, “Maitreya, go to the Licchavi Vimalakīrti to inquire about his illness.”

sanskrit: maitreyo 'py āha nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: Maitreya replied, “Lord, I am indeed reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.

sanskrit: abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan ekasmin samaye saṃtuṣitena devaputreṇa sārdhaṃ tuṣitakāyikaiś ca devaputraiḥ sārdhaṃ dharmyāṃ kathāṃ kathayāmi yad idaṃ bodhisatvānāṃ mahāsatvānām avivartyāṃ bhūmim ārabhya /
english: Lord, I remember that one day I was engaged in a conversation with the gods of the Tuṣita heaven, the god Saṃtuṣita and his retinue, about the stage of nonregression of the great bodhisattvas.

sanskrit: tatra ca vimalakīrtir licchavis taṃ pradeśam upasaṃkrāntaḥ / sa mām etad avocata
english: At that time, the Licchavi Vimalakīrti came there and addressed me as follows

sanskrit: Vkn  tvaṃ maitreya ekajātipratibaddho bhagavatā vyākṛto 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau /
english: “ ‘Maitreya, the Buddha has prophesied that only one more birth stands between you and unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

sanskrit: tat katamayāsi maitreya jātyāu vyākṛtaḥ,
english: What kind of birth does this prophecy concern, Maitreya?

sanskrit: kim atītayā vānāgatayota pratyutpannayā /
english: Is it past? Is it future? Or is it present?

sanskrit: tatra yātītā jātiḥ sā kṣīṇā,
english: If it is a past birth, it is already finished.

sanskrit: yāpy anāgatā sāpy asaṃprāptā, pratyutpannāyāḥ sthitir nāsti jāteḥ /
english: If it is a future birth, it will never arrive. If it is a present birth, it does not abide.

sanskrit: yathoktaṃ bhagavatā tathā hi tvaṃ bhikṣaḥ kṣaṇe kṣaṇe jāyase jīryasi mriyase cyavase upapadyase ceti /
english: For the Buddha has declared, “Bhikṣus, in a single moment, you are born, you age, you die, you transmigrate, and you are reborn.”

sanskrit: ajātitaś ca niyāmāvakrāntiḥ / na cājātir vyākriyate / nāpy ajātir abhisaṃbudhyate /
english: But birthlessness applies to the stage of destiny for the ultimate, in which there is neither prophecy nor attainment of perfect enlightenment.

sanskrit: Vkn  tat kathaṃ tvaṃ maitreya vyākṛtas tathatotpādena tathatānirodhena vā /
english: “ ‘Therefore, Maitreya, is your reality from birth? Or is it from cessation?

sanskrit: na ca tathatotpadyate na nirudhyate, na nirotsyate / yā ca sarvasatvānāṃ tathatā, yā ca sarvadharmāṇāṃ tathatā,
english: Your reality as prophesied is not born and does not cease, nor will it be born nor will it cease. Furthermore, your reality is just the same as the reality of all living beings, the reality of all things, and the reality of all the holy ones.

sanskrit: evaṃ yadi tvaṃ vyākṛtaḥ sarvasatvā api vyākṛtā bhavanti /
english: If your enlightenment can be prophesied in such a way, so can that of all living beings.

sanskrit: na hi tathatā dvayaprabhāvitā nānātvaprabhāvitā /
english: Because reality does not consist of duality or of diversity.

sanskrit: tad yadā maitreyo bodhim abhisaṃbhotsyate, sarvasatvā api tasmin samaye tādṛśīm eva bodhim abhisaṃbhotsyante /
english: Maitreya, whenever you attain buddhahood, which is the perfection of enlightenment, at the same time all living beings will also attain buddhahood.

sanskrit: sarvasatvānubodho hi bodhiḥ /
english: Enlightenment consists of the realizations of all living beings.

sanskrit: yadā ca maitreyaḥ parinirvāsyati, sarvasatvā api tadā parinirvāsyanti /
english: Maitreya, at the moment when you attain ultimate liberation, all living beings will also attain ultimate liberation.

sanskrit: na hy aparinirvṛtānāṃ sarvasatvānāṃ tathāgatāḥ parinirvānti /
english: The tathāgatas do not enter ultimate liberation until all living beings have entered ultimate liberation.

sanskrit: parinirvṛtāni te satvāni paśyanti nirvāṇaprakṛtikāni /
english: For, since all living beings are utterly liberated, the tathāgatas see them as having the nature of ultimate liberation.

sanskrit: tasmād iha maitreya mā etān devaputrān ullāpaya mā visaṃvādaya /
english: “ ‘Therefore, Maitreya, do not fool and delude these deities!

sanskrit: Vkn  na bodhau kaścit pratiṣṭhate, na nivartate /
english: No one abides in, or regresses from, enlightenment.

sanskrit: api tu khalu punar maitreya yaiṣāṃ devaputrāṇāṃ bodhiparikalpanadṛṣṭis tām etām utsarjaya /
english: Maitreya, you should introduce these deities to the repudiation of all discriminative constructions concerning enlightenment.

sanskrit: na hi bodhiḥ kāyenābhisaṃbudhyate, na cittena /
english: “ ‘Enlightenment is perfectly realized neither by the body nor by the mind.

sanskrit: vyupaśamo bodhiḥ sarvanimittānām,
english: Enlightenment is the eradication of all marks.

sanskrit: asamāropo bodhiḥ sarvārambaṇānām, apracāro bodhiḥ sarvamanaskārāṇām,
english: Enlightenment is free of presumptions concerning all objects. Enlightenment is free of the functioning of all intentional thoughts.

sanskrit: paricchedo bodhiḥ sarvadṛṣṭigatānām, vigamo bodhiḥ sarvaparikalpānām, visaṃyogo bodhiḥ sarveñjitamanyasyanditānām,
english: Enlightenment is the annihilation of all convictions. Enlightenment is free from all discriminative constructions. Enlightenment is free from all vacillation, mentation, and agitation.

sanskrit: anadhiṣṭhānaṃ bodhiḥ sarvapraṇidhānānām, asaṅgapraveśo bodhiḥ sarvodgrahavigatā,
english: Enlightenment is not involved in any commitments. Enlightenment is the arrival at detachment, through freedom from all habitual attitudes.

sanskrit: sthitā bodhir dharmadhātusthāne, anugatā bodhis tathatāyām, pratiṣṭhitā bodhir bhūtakoṭyām,
english: The ground of enlightenment is the ultimate realm. Enlightenment is realization of reality. Enlightenment abides at the realitylimit.

sanskrit: advayā bodhir manodharmavigatā /
english: Enlightenment is without duality, since therein are no minds and no things.

sanskrit: samā bodhir ākāśasamatayā,
english: Enlightenment is equality, since it is equal to infinite space.

sanskrit: asaṃskṛtā bodhir utpādabhaṅgasthityanyathātvavigatā,
english: “ ‘Enlightenment is unconstructed, because it is neither born nor destroyed, neither abides nor undergoes any transformation.

sanskrit: parijñā bodhiḥ sarvasatvacittacaritāśayānām,
english: Enlightenment is the complete knowledge of the thoughts, deeds, and inclinations of all living beings.

sanskrit: advārā bodhir āyatanānām,
english: Enlightenment is not a door for the sensemedia.

sanskrit: asaṃsṛṣṭā bodhiḥ sarvavāsanānusaṃdhikleśavigatā,
english: Enlightenment is unadulterated, since it is free of the afflictions of the instinctually driven succession of lives.

sanskrit: na deśasthā na pradeśasthā bodhiḥ sthānāsthānavigatā,
english: Enlightenment is neither somewhere nor nowhere, abiding in no location or dimension.

sanskrit: tathatāpratiṣṭhitā bodhiḥ sarvato 'dṛśyā /
english: Enlightenment, not being contained in anything, does not stand in reality.

sanskrit: nāmadheyamātraṃ bodhis tac ca nāma nirīhakam,
english: Enlightenment is merely a name and even that name is motionless.

sanskrit: nirātmikā bodhir āyūhaniryūhavigatā, anākulā bodhiḥ prakṛtipariśuddhā,
english: Enlightenment, free of abstention and undertaking, is energyless. There is no agitation in enlightenment, as it is utterly pure by nature.

sanskrit: prakāśā bodhiḥ svabhāvapariśuddhā,
english: Enlightenment is radiance, pure in essence.

sanskrit: anudgrahā bodhir adhyālambanavigatā, nirnānātvā bodhiḥ sarvadharmasamatāvabodhatvāt,
english: Enlightenment is without subjectivity and completely without object. Enlightenment, which penetrates the equality of all things, is undifferentiated.

sanskrit: anupamā bodhir upamopanyāsavigatāḥ,
english: Enlightenment, which is not shown by any example, is incomparable.

sanskrit: sūkṣmā bodhir duranubodhatvāt,
english: Enlightenment is subtle, since it is extremely difficult to realize.

sanskrit: sarvatrānugatā bodhir ākāśasvabhāvatvāt /
english: Enlightenment is allpervasive, as it has the nature of infinite space.

sanskrit: sā na śakyā kāyena vācā cittenābhisaṃboddhum /
english: Enlightenment cannot be realized, either physically or mentally.

sanskrit: Vkn  iha bhagavan nirdeśe nirdiśyamāne tataḥ pariṣado dvayor devaputraśatayor anutpattikeṣu dharmeṣu kṣāntipratilambho 'bhūt /
english: “Lord, when Vimalakīrti had discoursed thus, two hundred of the deities in that assembly attained the tolerance of the birthlessness of things.

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca niṣpratibhāno 'bhūvam /
english: As for me, Lord, I was rendered speechless.

sanskrit: tan nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: Therefore, I am reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.”

sanskrit: Vkn  tatra bhagavān prabhāvyūhaṃ licchavikumāram āmantrayate sma gaccha tvaṃ satpuruṣa vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
english: The Buddha then said to the young Licchavi Prabhāvyūha, “Prabhāvyūha, go to the Licchavi Vimalakīrti to inquire about his illness.”

sanskrit: prabhāvyūho 'py āha nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: Prabhāvyūha replied, “Lord, I am indeed reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.

sanskrit: ekasmin samaye bhagavan vaiśālyā mahānagaryā niṣkramāmi / vimalakīrtiś ca licchaviḥ praviśati /
english: Lord, I remember one day, when I was going out of the great city of Vaiśālī, I met the Licchavi Vimalakīrti coming in.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ tam abhivādyaivam avocam
english: He greeted me, and I then addressed him

sanskrit: kutas tvaṃ gṛhapate āgacchasīti / sa mām evam āha āgacchāmi bodhimaṇḍād iti / tam aham etad avocam bodhimaṇḍa iti kasyaitan nāma /
english: ‘Householder, where do you come from?’ He replied, ‘I come from the seat of enlightenment.’ I then inquired, ‘What is meant by “seat of enlightenment”?’ He then spoke the following words to me

sanskrit: Vkn  bodhimaṇḍa iti kulaputra āśayamaṇḍa eṣo 'kṛtrimatayā,
english: ‘Noble son, the seat of enlightenment is the seat of positive thought because it is without artificiality.

sanskrit: prayogamaṇḍa eṣa ārambhottāraṇatayā, adhyāśayamaṇḍa eṣa viśeṣādhigamatayā,
english: It is the seat of effort, because it releases energetic activities. It is the seat of high resolve, because its insight is superior.

sanskrit: bodhicittamaṇḍa eṣo 'saṃpramoṣanatayā,
english: It is the seat of the great spirit of enlightenment, because it does not neglect anything.

sanskrit: Vkn  dānamaṇḍa eṣa vipākāpratikāṅkṣaṇatayā,
english: “ ‘It is the seat of generosity, because it has no expectation of reward.

sanskrit: śīlamaṇḍa eṣa praṇidhānaparipūraṇatayā, kṣāntimaṇḍa eṣa sarvasatvāpratihatacittatayā,
english: It is the seat of morality, because it fulfills all commitments. It is the seat of tolerance, because it is free of anger toward any living being.

sanskrit: vīryamaṇḍa eṣo 'vinivartanatayā,
english: It is the seat of effort, because it does not turn back.

sanskrit: dhyānamaṇḍa eṣa cittakarmaṇyatayā,
english: It is the seat of meditation, because it generates fitness of mind.

sanskrit: prajñāmaṇḍa eṣa pratyakṣadarśitayā,
english: It is the seat of wisdom, because it sees everything directly.

sanskrit: Vkn  maitrīmaṇḍa eṣa sarvasatvasamacittatayā, karuṇāmaṇḍa eṣa khedasahiṣṇutayā,
english: “ ‘It is the seat of love, because it is equal to all living beings. It is the seat of compassion, because it tolerates all injuries.

sanskrit: muditāmaṇḍa eṣa dharmārāmaratiratatayā,
english: It is the seat of joy, because it is joyfully devoted to the bliss of the Dharma.

sanskrit: upekṣāmaṇḍa eṣo 'nunayapratighaprahāṇatayā,
english: It is the seat of equanimity, because it abandons affection and aversion.

sanskrit: Vkn  abhijñāmaṇḍa eṣa ṣaḍabhijñatayā,
english: “ ‘It is the seat of paranormal perception, because it has the six superknowledges.

sanskrit: vimokṣamaṇḍa eṣo 'kalpanatayā,
english: It is the seat of liberation, because it does not intellectualize.

sanskrit: upāyamaṇḍa eṣa satvaparipācanatayā, saṃgrahavastumaṇḍa eṣa sarvasatvasaṃgrahanatayā,
english: It is the seat of liberative art, because it develops living beings. It is the seat of the means of unification, because it brings together living beings.

sanskrit: śrutamaṇḍa eṣa pratipattisārakatvāt,
english: It is the seat of learning, because it makes practice of the essence.

sanskrit: nidhyaptimaṇḍa eṣa yoniśaḥpratyavekṣaṇatayā,
english: It is the seat of decisiveness, because of its precise discrimination.

sanskrit: bodhipakṣyadharmamaṇḍa eṣa saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtotsarjanatayā,
english: It is the seat of the aids to enlightenment, because it eliminates the duality of the compounded and the uncompounded.

sanskrit: satyamaṇḍa eṣa sarvalokāvisaṃvādanatayā,
english: It is the seat of truth, because it does not deceive anyone.

sanskrit: pratītyasamutpādamaṇḍa eṣo 'vidyāsravakṣayatayā yāvaj jarāmaraṇāsravakṣayatayā, sarvakleśapraśamanamaṇḍa eṣa yathābhūtābhisaṃbodhanatayā,
english: “ ‘It is the seat of interdependent origination, because it proceeds from the exhaustion of ignorance to the exhaustion of old age and death. It is the seat of eradication of all afflictions, because it is perfectly enlightened about the nature of reality.

sanskrit: Vkn  sarvasatvamaṇḍa eṣa satvāsvabhāvatayā,
english: It is the seat of all living beings, because all living beings are without intrinsic identity.

sanskrit: sarvadharmamaṇḍa eṣa śūnyatābhisaṃbodhanatayā,
english: It is the seat of all things, because it is perfectly enlightened with regard to voidness.

sanskrit: sarvamāranirghātanamaṇḍa eso 'calanatayā,
english: “ ‘It is the seat of the conquest of all devils, because it never flinches.

sanskrit: traidhātukamaṇḍa eṣa prasthānavigamanatayā,
english: It is the seat of the triple world, because it is free of involvement.

sanskrit: siṃhanādanadanavīryamaṇḍa eṣo 'bhītānutrāsanatayā,
english: It is the seat of the heroism that sounds the lion’s roar, because it is free of fear and trembling.

sanskrit: balavaiśāradyāveṇikasarvabuddhadharmamaṇḍa esa sarvato 'nupākruṣṭatvāt,
english: It is the seat of the strengths, the fearlessnesses, and all the special qualities of the Buddha, because it is irreproachable in all respects.

sanskrit: aśeṣa śakti pracitāt pradhānāt eva kevalāt | kārya bhedāḥ pravarttante tad rūpāḥ eva bhāvataḥ ||
english: It is out of prakṛti (primordial matter) itself alone, as equipped with all potencies, that the various products evolve, really having their essence in that same matter.”

sanskrit: aśeṣa śakti pracitāt pradhānāt eva kevalāt | kārya bhedāḥ pravarttante tad rūpāḥ eva bhāvataḥ ||
english: It is out of prakṛti (primordial matter) itself alone, as equipped with all potencies, that the various products evolve, really having their essence in that same matter.”

sanskrit: yadi tu asat bhavet kāryam kāraṇa ātmani śaktitaḥ  | kartum tat na eva śakyeta nairupyāt viyat abja vat ||
english: If the effect were non-existent, potentially, in the form of the cause,—then it could not be produced; because it would have no form at all, being like the sky-lotus.”

sanskrit: kasmāt ca niyatāni eva śāli bīja ādi bhedataḥ | upādānāni gṛhṇanti tulye asattve aparam na tu ||
english: How is it that people have recourse to only specific causes, in the shape of such diverse things as the paddy-seed and the like, and not any other,—even though the nonexistence (of the desired effect or product) is equal (everywhere)?”

sanskrit: sarvam ca sarvatas bhāvāt bhavet utpatti dharmakam | tādātmya vigamasya iha sarvasmin aviśeṣataḥ ||
english: Everything likely to be produced would be produced from everything; because the negation of co-essentiality is equally present in everything.”

sanskrit: śaktīnām niyamāt eṣām na evam iti api anuttaram  | śakyam eva yatas kāryam śaktāḥ kurvanti hetavaḥ ||
english: Because the potencies of these things are restricted in their scope, therefore it is not as has been urged; hence it does not answer our argument. because potent causes produce only such effect as is amenable to their potency.”

sanskrit: akārya atiśayam yat tu nīrūpam avikāri ca | vikṛtau ātma hāni āpteḥ tat kriyeta katham nu taiḥ ||
english: That to which no peculiarity can be attributed, which is eormless and unmodipiable,—how could such a thing be produced by causes,—when any modification would involve the loss of its very essence?”

sanskrit: kāryasya evam ayogāt ca kim kurvat kāraṇam bhavet | tatas kāraṇa bhāvaḥ api bīja ādeḥ na vikalpate ||
english: Thus the effect being impossible, what would that be by producing which anything would be a cause? as a consequence, it cannot be possible to admit the causal character of even such things as the seed and the like.”

sanskrit: sukha ādi anvitam etat ca vyaktam vyaktam samīkṣyate | prasāda tāpa dainya ādi kāryasya iha upalabdhitaḥ ||
english: All that is Manifest is clearly known to be homogeneous with Pleasure and the rest, from the fact of the Effect being found to be the product of Satisfaction, Irritation and Dejection, etc.”

sanskrit: tatas tad maya sambhūtam tad jāti anvaya darśanāt | kuṭa ādi bhedavat tat ca pradhānam iti kāpilāḥ ||
english: Thus, the whole (manifest) must be taken as having emanated from something made up of the said (pleasure, etc,),—because the said generic character is found present in it,—just as in the case of the jar and other things; and this something is primordial matter”,—so say the followers of Kapila

sanskrit: tat atra sudhiyaḥ prāhuḥ tulyā satve api codanā | yat tasyām uttaram vaḥ syāt tat tulyam sudhiyām api ||
english: In answer to this, the wise ones hectare that the argument that has been urged (by the sāṃkhya against the doctrine that the effect is non-existent prior to its production) is equally applicable to the doctrine of the existence of the effect. and the answer that you would have to that argument would equally aptly be the answer of the wise ones also

sanskrit: yadi dadhi ādayaḥ santi dugdha ādi ātmasu sarvathā | teṣām satām kim utpādyam hetu ādi sadṛśa ātmanām ||
english: If the curd and other effects are already wholly existent in the essence of (their causes) milk and the rest,—then, inasmuch as they would be exactly like the cause, etc. in their essence, what of theirs would be there that would have to be produced? A) The said effect cannot be produced by the cause,—because it already exists,—like the cause and the spirit

sanskrit: hetu janyam na tat kāryam sattātaḥ hetu vitti vat | atas na abhimataḥ hetuḥ asādhya tvāt parātma vat ||
english: B) Thus also what is postulated cannot be the cause,—because there is nothing that can be brought about by it,—just like the other thing

sanskrit: atha asti atiśayaḥ kaścid abhivyakti ādi lakṣaṇaḥ | yam hetavaḥ prakurvāṇāḥ na yānti vacanīya tām ||
english: It might be urged that “there is some peculiar feature, something in the shape of manifestation and the like,—by producing which, causes might cease to be defamed (as futile)”

sanskrit: prāk āsīt yadi asau evam na kiṃcid dattam uttaram | no ced saḥ asat katham tebhyaḥ prādurbhāvam samaśnute ||
english: If this (peculiar feature) existed previously, then the objection is not answered; if, however, it did not exist previously, then, being- non-existent, how could it be produced out of the causes?

sanskrit: na atas sādhyam samasti iti na upādāna parigrahaḥ | niyatāt api naḥ janma na ca śaktiḥ na ca kriyā ||
english: For the same reason, if there is nothing to be produced, there would be no ‘recourse to the cause’,—nor would there be any production out of even a specific cause,—nor would there be any ‘efficiency’, nor any ‘operation’ (of the cause)

sanskrit: sarva ātmanā ca niṣpatteḥ na kāryam iha kiṃcana | kāraṇa vyapadeśaḥ api tasmāt na eva upapadyate ||
english: Inasmuch as every effect, is already there in its entirety, there can be nothing ‘to be produced’ (an effect); consequently, the very name ‘cause’ cannot be logical

sanskrit: sarvam ca sādhanam vṛttam viparyāsa nivartakam  | niścaya utpādakam ca idam na tathā yukti saṅgatam ||
english: All Means (of Cognition), when operative, serve to set aside Wrong Cognition and to produce Definitely Certain Cognition; this would not be compatible with reason (under the Sāṃkhya theory)

sanskrit: na sandeha viparyāsau nivartyau sarvadā sthiteḥ  | na api niścaya janma asti tatas eva vṛthak akhilam ||
english: The doubt and the misconception cannot be set aside, as they would be always there. nor is the producing op definitely certain cognition possible, for the very same reason. hence all that has been said is futile

sanskrit: athā api niścayaḥ abhūtaḥ samutpadyeta sādhanāt | nanu tena eva sarve amī bhaveyuḥ vyabhicāriṇaḥ ||
english: If, on the other hand, (it be held that) the definite cognition that would be produced would be one that has not been there,—then, this one instance (of the effect being non-existent) would invalidate all those reasons (that have been set forth by the sāṃkhya)

sanskrit: avyaktaḥ vyakti bhāktebhyaḥ iti ced vyaktiḥ asya kā | na rūpa atiśaya utpattiḥ avibhāgāt asaṅgateḥ ||
english: If it be held that—“the effect, which has been unmanifested (latent, in the cause), acquires manifestation through the causes”,—then (the question is) what is this manifestation of the effect?—it cannot consist in'the appearance (production) of a peculiarity in its nature; because of non-differentiation and non-connection

sanskrit: na tad viṣaya saṃvittiḥ na upalambha āvṛti kṣayaḥ | nitya tvāt upalambhasya dvitīyasya api asaṃbhavāt ||
english: The ‘Manifestation’ of the Effect cannot consist in its Apprehension; nor in the removal of what was obstructing its Apprehension; because the Apprehension is a constant factor, and also because there is no possibility of a second (Apprehension)

sanskrit: traiguṇyasya avibhede api na sarvam sarva kārakam | yadvat tadvat asatve api na sarvam sarva kārakam ||
english: Just as (under the sāṃkhya theory),—even though, on the ground of all things being constituted by the Three Attributes, there is no differentiation among them, and yet everything (Cause) does not produce everything (Effect),—in the same manner, even though the Effect is non-existent (before the Causal Operation), everything cannot produce everything

sanskrit: avadhīnām aniṣpatteḥ niyatāḥ te na śaktayaḥ | satve tu niyamaḥ tāsām yuktaḥ sa avadhikaḥ na nu ||
english: Inasmuch as the presence of limits would re impossible for you, the potencies cannot be restricted. on the view of their being existent, on the other hand, their restriction would be right and proper as pertaining to the limits.”

sanskrit: na evam teṣām aniṣpattyā mā abhūt śabdaḥ tathā aparam | sarva upādhi viviktasya vastu rūpasya na kṣatiḥ ||
english: It is not so; it may be that, on account of the absence of ‘limits’, there can be no such subsequent assertion as held by us. but there is no harm done to the nature of the thing itself which is entirely free from all restrictive adjuncts

sanskrit: na nāma rūpam vastūnām vikalpāḥ vācakāḥ ca yat | viśva kalpāḥ pravarttante yathā abhyāsam abhedini ||
english: The name of things is not their ‘essence’ (nature, form); because all kinds of ‘conception’ and ‘verbal expression’ proceed through habit, with reference to the undifferentiated (immaculate) entity

sanskrit: utpādaḥ vastu bhāvaḥ tu saḥ asatā na satā tathā  | sambadhyate kalpikayā kevalam tu asatā dhiyā ||
english: In reality, the ‘production’ (or a thing) consists in its becoming a thing; this ‘production’ cannot be related to what is existent, or with what is non-existent; it is related only to a conceptual idea which is purely nonexistent

sanskrit: yat idam vastunaḥ rūpam eka anantaram īkṣyate | prāk āsīt na iti tat bījam prāk bhūte tu idam asti na ||
english: The basis (of the said conception) lies in the fact that the form of a thing perceived in immediate sequence to another thing did not exist before. if the said thing had existed previously, then this basis would not be there (for the said assumption)

sanskrit: kṣīra ādiṣu ca dadhi ādi śakti rūpeṇa yat matam | kā śaktiḥ tatra dadhi ādi yadi dṛśyeta dugdha vat ||
english: It has been held that the curd and other effects subsist in the milk and other causes, in the form of latent potency; now what is this ‘potency’? if it is the same as the curd and other effects,—then this also would be perceived like the milk itself

sanskrit: anyat ced katham anyasya bhāve abhaktyā anyat ucyate | nahi satvasya sadbhāvaḥ sadbhāvaḥ duḥkha mohayoḥ ||
english: If it is something different (from the effect), then the existence of one thing cannot be spoken of as that of another, except figuratively. (for example) the existence of the (attribute of) ‘harmony’ is not spoken of as the existence of ‘pain’ and ‘delusion

sanskrit: sattva ādi anugatam vyaktam na siddham naḥ kathaṃcana | āntara tvāt sukha ādīnām vyakta tvāt tad sva saṃvidaḥ ||
english: The ‘manifest’ is not admitted by us in any way whatsoever as homogeneous with (made up of) pleasure and the rest; because pleasure and the rest are ‘internal’, ‘subjective’; and that these are so is manifest from their own clear cognition

sanskrit: ekatra eva ca śabda ādau bhāvanā jāti bhedataḥ | saṅga ādayaḥ saṃbhavinaḥ lakṣyante niyatāḥ sphuṭam ||
english: On account of the diversity of habit and nature, all possible attachment and the rest are clearly found to be restricted to each single object, like sound and the rest

sanskrit: eka vastu anupāti tve citrā saṃvid prasajyate | adṛṣṭa ādi vaśāt no ced na syāt vastu anuyāyinī ||
english: Being in keeping with one and the same object, the consciousness would be variegated in character.—if it be urged that “it is not so because of destiny and such other forces”,—then the consciousness would not be in keeping with the object at all

sanskrit: tri ākāram vastunaḥ rūpam eka ākārāḥ ca tad vidaḥ | tāḥ katham tatra yujyante bhāvinyaḥ tad vilakṣaṇāḥ ||
english: The form of the object itself is three-formed, and the cognitions (of men) are one-formed;—how can these latter be really possible with reference to the object,—being entirely different from it in character?

sanskrit: prasāda udvega varaṇāni ekasmin puṃsi yoginām | jāyante na ca tad rūpaḥ pumān abhimataḥ paraiḥ ||
english: For the followers of yoga, ‘satisfaction’, ‘dissatisfaction’ and ‘delusion’ are produced in the same spirit; and yet the other party do not hold the spirit to be of the essence of those

sanskrit: siddhe api triguṇe vyakte na pradhānam prasidhyati | ekam tad kāraṇam nityam na eka jāti anvitam hi tat ||
english: Even though the ‘manifest’ be accepted as ‘consisting of three attributes’,—primordial matter does not become established as the one eternal cause of that (manifest); because that ‘manifest’ is not imbued with any single generic character

sanskrit: ayaḥ śalākā kalpāḥ hi krama saṅgata mūrtayaḥ | dṛśyante vyaktayaḥ sarvāḥ kalpanā miśrita ātmikāḥ ||
english: All ‘manifested things’ are found to be like iron-bars; as having their forms associated with an order of sequence and their essence mixed up with fancies

sanskrit: mṛd vikāra ādayaḥ bhedāḥ na eka jāti anvitāḥ tathā  | siddhāḥ na eka nimittāḥ ca mṛd piṇḍa ādeḥ vibhedataḥ ||
english: So also the various products of clay and other things are not recognised as imbued with any single generic character,—nor as the effects of any single cause; as all such things as the ‘lump of clay’ are diverse

sanskrit: caitanya ādi anvita tve api na eka pūrva tvam iṣyate | puruṣāṇām amukhyam ced tat iha api samam na kim ||
english: In the case of ‘spirits’, even though they are endowed with ‘sentience’ and other qualities, they are not regarded (by the sāṃkhya) as preceded (produced) by a single entity (as their cause).—it might be said that “the said qualities are attributed (to the spirits) only secondarily (indirectly, figuratively)”;—then why cannot the same be the case in regard to the matter under discussion also?

sanskrit: pradhāna hetu abhāve api tatas sarvam prakalpate | śakteḥ bhedena vaicitryam kārya kāraṇa tā ādikam ||
english: Thus, even in the absence of a cause in the shape of ‘primordial matter’, all diversity relating to effects and causes and other things becomes explicable, on the basis of the diversity of potencies

sanskrit: pradhāna hetu abhāve api tatas sarvam prakalpate | śakteḥ bhedena vaicitryam kārya kāraṇa tā ādikam ||
english: Thus, even in the absence of a cause in the shape of ‘primordial matter’, all diversity relating to effects and causes and other things becomes explicable, on the basis of the diversity of potencies

sanskrit: sarva utpattimatām īśam anye hetum pracakṣate | na acetanam sva kāryāṇi kila prārabhate svayam ||
english: Other philosophers declare the ‘lord’ to be the cause of all things produced; on the ground that no insentient thing, by itself, can produce its effects

sanskrit: sarva utpattimatām īśam anye hetum pracakṣate | na acetanam sva kāryāṇi kila prārabhate svayam ||
english: Other philosophers declare the ‘lord’ to be the cause of all things produced; on the ground that no insentient thing, by itself, can produce its effects

sanskrit: yat sva ārambhaka avayava saṃniveśa viśeṣa vat | buddhimat hetu gamyam tat tat yathā kalaśa ādikam || dvi indriya grāhyam agrāhyam vivāda padam īdṛśam  | buddhimat pūrvakam tena vaidharmyaiṇa aṇavaḥ matāḥ ||
english: A) that which is characterised by a peculiar arrangement of its own component parts is subject to a cause that is endowed with intelligence,—for instance, the jar and other objects.—the thing in dispute,—which is perceptible by means of two sense-organs and also imperceptible,—must be preceded (and produced) by a cause endowed with intelligence,—atoms supplying the corroborative instance ‘per dissimilarity’.”

sanskrit: tattva ādīnām upādānam cetanāvat adhiṣṭhitam | rūpa ādimat tvāt tantu ādi yathā dṛṣṭam sva kārya kṛt ||
english: B) the material cause of the body and other things is controlled by an intelligent being,—because they are endowed with colour and other qualities,—like the yarn and such things which have been seen to bring about their effects (only when controlled by the intelligent weaver).”

sanskrit: dharma adharma aṇavaḥ sarve cetanāvat adhiṣṭhitāḥ  | sva kārya ārambhakāḥ sthitvā pravṛtteḥ turi tantu vat ||
english: In the producing of their effects, all such causes as merit, demerit and atoms are controlled by an intelligent being,—because they operate intermittently,—like the shuttle and the yarn.”

sanskrit: sarga ādau vyavahāraḥ ca puṃsām anya upadeśa jaḥ | niyata tvāt prabuddhānām kumāra vyavahāra vat ||
english: At the beginning of creation, usage among men must have been due to the teaching of other persons;—when they become subsequently awakened to consciousness, it is found to be restricted to particular things,—like the usage of little boys.”

sanskrit: mahābhūta ādikam vyaktam buddhimat hetu adhiṣṭhitam | yāti sarvasya lokasya sukha duḥsva nimitta tām || acetana tva kārya tva vināśi tva ādi hetutaḥ | vāsi ādi vat atas spaṣṭam tasya sarvam pratīyate ||
english: The manifested world, consisting of the primary elemental substances and the rest, becomes the source of pleasure and pain to all people, only when controlled by an intelligent cause,—because it is insentient, itself a product, evanescent and so forth,—like the axe and other things; thus everything is clearly believed to be his.”

sanskrit: sarva kartṛ tva siddhau ca sarvajña tvam ayatnataḥ | siddham asya yatas kartā kārya rūpa ādi vedakaḥ ||
english: The fact of his being the creator of all things having been established, his omniscience is proved without effort; because the creator must be one who knows the form and all other details regarding what he has created.”

sanskrit: vimateḥ āspadam vastu pratyakṣam kasya cit sphuṭam | vastu sattva ādi hetubhyaḥ sukha duḥkha ādi bhedavat ||
english: The thing under dispute must clearly be perceptible to some one,—because or such reasons as being a thing, being existent and so forth:—just like the diversities of pleasure, pain, etc.—[and this some one is god].”

sanskrit: tat atra asiddha tā hetoḥ prathame sādhane yatas  | sanniveśaḥ na yoga ākhyaḥ siddhaḥ na avayavī tathā  ||
english: The first argument (propounded by the naiyāyika) is open to the fallacy of being ‘unproven, inadmissible’; because the existence of any such ‘arrangement’ as ‘conjunction’ is not proven, nor that of the ‘composite

sanskrit: dṛśya tvena abhyupetasya dvayasya anupalambhanāt | sādhana ananvitam ca idam udāharaṇam api atas ||
english: Because both the facts that have been assumed (and put forward) are such as are not actually apprehended; and for the same reason the corroborative instance also that has been cited has no connection with the probans cited

sanskrit: cakṣuḥ sparśana vijñānam bhinna ābham upajāyate | eka ālambana tā na asti tayoḥ gandha ādi vitti vat ||
english: Visual cognition and tactile cognition always appear differently; they cannot therefore have one and the same substratum,—just like the cognition of odour and other things

sanskrit: tad sāmarthya samudbhūta kalpanā anugata ātmakam | pratisandhāna vijñānam samudāyam vyavasyati || jala anala ādi na eva idam dvi indriya grāhyam asti atas  | āśraya asiddha tā asiddheḥ yathā abhihita dharmiṇaḥ ||
english: As a matter of fact, what brings about the joint cognition (involved in recognition) is the fact that recognition consists in an assumption arising out of the potencies of the two cognitions concerned.—thus, such things as water, fire and the like are not ‘perceptible by two sense-organs ’; and hence the probans (of the naiyāyika) is found to have its substratum ‘unproven, inadmissible’, as is indicated by the ‘ un-proven ’ character of the object itself

sanskrit: sanniveśa viśiṣṭa tvam yādṛś devakula ādiṣu | karttari anupalabdhe api yad dṛṣṭau buddhimat gatiḥ || tādṛś eva yat īkṣyeta tanvak ādiṣu dharmiṣu | yuktam tad sādhanāt asmāt yathā abhīṣṭasya sādhanam ||
english: In the case of temples and such things, the presence of a peculiar arrangement (of component parts) is distinctly perceived,—from which perception follows the cognition (inferential) of an intelligent builder,—even when no such builder is actually seen; if, in the case of such objects as the body, the mountain and the like, a similar peculiar arrangement of parts were distinctly perceived, then it would be correct to deduce from this perception as the reason, the conclusion that is desired (by the Naiyāyika)

sanskrit: anvaya vyatirekābhyām yat kāryam yasya niścitam  | niścayaḥ tasya tad dṛṣṭau iti nyāyaḥ vyavasthitaḥ  || saṃniveśa viśeṣaḥ tu na eva amīṣu tathāvidhaḥ | tanu taru ādi bhedeṣu śabdaḥ eva tu kevalaḥ || tādṛśaḥ procyamānaḥ tu sandigdha vyatireka tām | āsādayati valmīke kumbhakāra kṛta ādiṣu ||
english: When a certain thing is definitely recognised, through affirmative and negative concomitance, as the effect of a certain cause, then, the perception of that effect must prove that cause;—such is the standing law.—the ‘peculiar arrangement of parts’ in such diverse things as the body, the mountain and the like however is not an effect of this kind; there is a mere assertion to that effect.—such a reason, when put forward, renders the conclusion open to doubt and denial, as it does when put forward for proving that ‘the anthill is the work of the potter

sanskrit: nanu jāti uttaram idam dharma bheda vikalpanāt | sāmānyam eva kārya ādi sādhanam pratipāditam ||
english: What has been put forward (by you) is only a ‘futile rejoinder’, as it is based upon the assumption op a particular character; while what has been put forward (by us, the naiyāyika) is only the general character of ‘effects’.”

sanskrit: a tad rūpa parāvṛttam vastu mātram anitya tām | tādātmyat sādhayati eṣa na nyāyaḥ asti iha sādhane ||
english: In the example of futile rejoinder cited] the mere thing (effect in general), as excluded from all that is not that thing (not-effect), does really prove non-eternality, on account of its being of the same essence as that. but as regards the probans under discussion, there is no reason for it at all

sanskrit: dhūma ātmā dhavalaḥ dṛṣṭaḥ pāvaka avyabhicāravān | sita abhidheya tā mātrāt na himāt api tad gatiḥ ||
english: As a matter of fact, the smoke that has been seen to be invariably concomitant with fire is white; and yet the mention of mere ‘whiteness’ could not prove the existence of fire; if it did, then that existence could be inferred even from the ‘snow’

sanskrit: sāmānya pratibandhe tu viśeṣa āśrayaṇī yadā | codanā kriyate tatra jāti uttaram udāhṛtam ||
english: When the invariable concomitance (premiss) is stated in the general form, and the objection urged against it is on the basis of a particular aspect of it,—then this is said to be a futile rejoinder

sanskrit: go śabda vācya tā mātrāt diś ādīnām viṣāṇi tā  | saṃsiddhyet anyathā hi eṣa nyāyaḥ na āśrīyate yadi ||
english: The mere character of ‘being denoted by the term go’ (as a general character) might prove the ‘presence of horns’ in the quarters and other things (which are all denoted by the term ‘go’),—ip the reasoning were not adopted in a different form

sanskrit: yadi tu pratibandhaḥ asmin pramāṇe na upapadyate | tat atra yuktitaḥ siddhe na vivādaḥ asti kasyacid ||
english: If it were proved by some valid means of cognition that there is an invariable concomitance between the probans and the probandum (cited by the naiyāyika), then, the conclusion would be fully established by reasoning, and no one could have anything to say against it

sanskrit: kintu nitya eka sarvajña nitya buddhi samāśrayaḥ | sādhya vaikalyataḥ avyāpteḥ na siddhim upagacchati ||
english: But the existence of a being who is eternal, one, and the substratum of eternal all-embracing consciousness,—can never be proved; as the invariable concomitance (premiss) that may be cited would be devoid of the probandum

sanskrit: tathā hi saudha sopāna gopura aṭṭālaka ādayaḥ | aneka anitya vijñāna pūrvaka tvena niścitāḥ ||
english: For instance, all such products as houses, steps, gateways, towers and the like are definitely known to have been made by makers who have been many, and with fleeting ideas

sanskrit: atas eva ayam iṣṭasya vighāta kṛt api icya ṣya te | aneka anitya vijñāna pūrvaka tva prasādhanāt ||
english: For the same reason, the probans is also detrimental to what is desired; inasmuch as what it establishes is [a cause] that is many, and the substratum of fleeting ideas

sanskrit: buddhimat hetu mātre hi pratibandhaḥ tvayā uditaḥ | dvitīye punar asmābhiḥ vispaṣṭam abhidhīyate ||
english: The invariable concomitance that has been asserted by you is only with reference to the probandum in the form of ‘the character of having an intelligent cause’; and we are going to assert it clearly with reference to a second (different, contrary) probandum

sanskrit: krama akrama virodhena nityāḥ no kārya kāriṇaḥ | viṣayāṇām krami tvena tad jñāneṣu api ca kramaḥ ||
english: For us, eternal things cannot produce any effects, because ‘consecutive’ and ‘concurrent’ action are mutually contradictory; and if objects are consecutive, there must be the same consecutiveness in their cognitions also

sanskrit: krama bhāvi īśvara jñānam krami vijñeya saṅgateḥ | devadatta ādi vijñānam yathā jvālā ādi gocaram ||
english: God’s cognition must be consecutive, because it is related to consecutive cognisable things;—just like the cognition of devadatta and other persons, relating to flame and other things

sanskrit: aṇu saṃhati mātram ca ghaṭāt yasmābhiḥ iṣyate | tad kārakaḥ kulāla ādiḥ aṇūnām eva kārakaḥ || na vyāvṛttaḥ tatas dharmaḥ sādhya tvena abhivāñchitaḥ | aṇu udāharaṇāt asmāt vaidharmyeṇa prakāśitāt ||
english: The jar and other things are regarded by us as mere aggregates of atoms; and the potter and other men who make those things are only makers of the atoms; hence the character that you mean to prove (i.e. your probandum) is not excluded (absent) erom the atom which has been cited (by you) as a corroborative instance per dissimilarity

sanskrit: buddhimat pūrvaka tvam ca sāmānyena yadi iṣyate | tatra na eva vivādaḥ naḥ vaiśvarūpyam hi karma jam ||
english: If the character of ‘being produced by an intelligent cause’ is meant to be proved only in a general form, then we have no dispute with you; as all diversity is due to actions

sanskrit: nitya eka buddhi pūrva tva sādhane sādhya śūnya tā | vyabhicāraḥ ca saudha ādeḥ bahubhiḥ karaṇa īkṣaṇāt ||
english: If what you seek to prove is the fact that the world is created by a cause who is one and whose consciousness is eternal,—then there is absence of the probandum (in the instance); and it is ‘inconclusive’ also, since such things as the house and the like are found to be made by several makers

sanskrit: etat eva yathāyogyam avaśiṣṭeṣu hetuṣu | yojyam dūṣaṇam anyat ca kiñcid mātram prakāśyate ||
english: Against the other reasonings (of the theist) also, this same criticism may be urged mutatis mutandis; some other criticism also is now being briefly set forth

sanskrit: sthitvā pravṛttiḥ aṇu ādeḥ na siddhā kṣaṇa bhaṅgataḥ | vyabhicāraḥ ca tena eva tasya api krama vṛtti tā ||
english: Intermittent action’ of atoms and other causes is not proven (admitted); as there is ‘perpetual flux’, all things are undergoing destruction every moment; it is also ‘inconclusive’ in reference to that same (god), as hls activity also is consecutive (hence intermittent)

sanskrit: pralaye lupta vijñāna smṛtayaḥ puruṣāḥ na naḥ | ābhāsvara ādi sambhūteḥ tatas eva iha saṃbhavāt ||
english: According to us, at dissolution, persons do not continue to remain with all consciousness and memory completely lost; because they are born in effulgent regions, and from these latter they are born again in this world

sanskrit: vimukhasya upadeṣṭṛ tvam śraddhā gamyam param yadi | vaimukhyam vitanu tvena dharma adharma vivekataḥ ||
english: Then again, the ‘teachership’ of a mouthless person can only be a matter of blind faith; god’s ‘mouthlessness’ is proved by his having no body, on account of the absence in him of merit and demerit

sanskrit: anumāna virodhaḥ ca vyāpteḥ sarvatra sādhane | na viruddhena dharmeṇa vyāptiḥ hetoḥ prakalpate ||
english: In all the arguments, the invariable concomitance (premiss) is contrary to inference; and there can be no invariable concomitance of the probans on the basis of a contrary (false) character

sanskrit: na īśvaraḥ janminām hetuḥ utpatti vikala tvataḥ  | gagana ambhoja vat sarvam anyathā yugapad bhavet ||
english: God cannot be the cause of born things,—because he is hlmsele devoid of birth,—like the ‘sky-lotus’, otherwise, all things would come into existence simultaneously

sanskrit: ye vā krameṇa jāyante te na eva īśvara hetukāḥ  | yathā ukta sādhana udbhūtāḥ jaḍānām pratyayāḥ iva || teṣām api tad udbhūtau viphalā sādhana abhidhā | nitya tvāt acikitsyasya nā eva sā sahakāriṇī ||
english: Things that are born consecutively cannot have cod for their cause,—just like the notions of foolish persons arising from the said reasonings (of the theist).—if those (notions) also are produced by cod, then the adducing of proofs (in support of them) should be useless; because of (his) eternality; and as he would be beyond remedy, the said statement could render no help

sanskrit: yeṣu satsu bhavat dṛṣṭam asatsu na kadāca | tasya anya hetu tā klṛptau anavasthā katham na te ||
english: When you have seen that a certain thing exists only when certain other things exist, and never when these do not exist,—then, if you assume a cause for the former, other than these latter,—how can you avoid falling into an infinite regress?

sanskrit: kartṛ tva pratiṣedhāt ca sarvajña tvam nirākṛtam | boddhavyam tad balena eva sarvajña tva upapādanāt ||
english: By the refutation of god’s creatorship, his omniscience also is understood to be set aside by the same; as it is on the strength of ‘creatorship’ that the argument for ‘omniscience’ has been based

sanskrit: yathā ukta doṣa duṣṭāni mā abhūvan sādhanāni vā | tathā api kartuḥ na eka tvam vyabhicāra upadarśanāt || eka kartuḥ asiddhau ca sarvajña tvam kim āśrayam |
english: Your reasonings may not be beset with the defects urged above; and yet the creator cannot be one, because the falsity of such a proposition has been shown above; and when the oneness of the creator is not proved, wherein could ‘omniscience’ subsist?a)

sanskrit: prakṛti īśvarayoḥ evam hetu tva pratiṣedhanāt | pratyekam sahitam kartṛ na ubhayam janminām idam ||
english: The doctrines of ‘god’ or ‘primordial matter’ severally being the cause (of the world) having been refuted,—it follows that these two together cannot be the ‘maher’ of things produced

sanskrit: prakṛti īśvarayoḥ evam hetu tva pratiṣedhanāt | pratyekam sahitam kartṛ na ubhayam janminām idam ||
english: The doctrines of ‘god’ or ‘primordial matter’ severally being the cause (of the world) having been refuted,—it follows that these two together cannot be the ‘maher’ of things produced

sanskrit: sāhityam sahakāri tvāt etayoḥ kalpyate ca yat | tat syāt atiśaya ādhānāt eka artha kriyayā api vā || na yuktā kalpanā ādyasya nirvikāra tayā tayoḥ | na dvitīyasya kāryāṇām yaugapadya prasaṅgataḥ ||
english: As for their ‘association’ assumed on the basis op their acting jointly,—this could be due either (a) to the creation op some peculiarity, or (b) to their serving a common purpose. (a) The former op these assumptions cannot be right, as both are ‘unmodifiable’; (b) nor is the latter acceptable; as that would lead to the absurdity op all products coming into existence simultaneously

sanskrit: atha ucyate pradhānasya trirūpa tvam vyavasthitam  | tatra ayam rajasā yuktaḥ sarga hetuḥ maheśvaraḥ || udbhūta vṛtti sattvam tu yadā saṃśrayate punar | tadā sarvasya lokasya sthiteḥ yāti nimitta tām  || udbhūta śakti rūpeṇa tamasā yujyate yadā | pralayam sarva jagataḥ tadā kila karoti ayam || rajaḥ sattva ādi rūpa ādi tat evam sahakāriṇaḥ | krameṇa eva asya vartante kāryāṇām na ākramaḥ tatas
